He is forced to immediately cancel his channel and abort his trade, or stay and get stunned, leaving him open to a massive Hextech Ray and Siphon Power burst.

summary: Kennen uses E (Lightning Rush) to easily dodge Mordekaiser's E (Death's Grasp) pull, allowing him to safely poke with Q (Thundering Shuriken).
howToPlay: To survive, never cast Death's Grasp unless Kennen has already wasted Lightning Rush to clear minions or trade. Position yourself deep inside your own minion wave to block his Thundering Shuriken pathing. If he steps past your wave to harass, use Obliterate on isolated minions to push back, and rely heavily on the shield from Indestructible to absorb his Electrical Surge damage. If he locks you in Slicing Maelstrom, use Realm of Death to isolate him.
laneImpact: You will constantly find yourself pushed under turret, absorbing poke while trying to secure minions. If you step up to contest the wave, Kennen will chip away at your health bar, forcing early recalls and giving him a massive gold lead through turret plates. Since you cannot easily lock him down, he maintains complete control over the wave state and can comfortably rotate.
why: This matchup is dictated by Kennen's superior mobility. Whenever you attempt to pull him in with Death's Grasp, he can reactively activate Lightning Rush to easily dash out of the hand's hitbox. Once your primary crowd control is on cooldown, Kennen can freely position forward to harass you with Thundering Shuriken and stack Mark of the Storm without any fear of your retaliation.

summary: Taliyah's Unraveled Earth (E) punishes Aurora's dash mechanics on Across the Veil (W) and Between Worlds (R).
howToPlay: Focus on farming from a safe distance using Twofold Hex and avoid forward dashes. You must hold Across the Veil strictly for defensive purposes, using it only after Unraveled Earth has expired or if she mispositions. Utilize the minor self-knockback on The Weirding to disengage without activating her ground traps. Only activate Between Worlds if you can guarantee you won't be forced to jump directly onto her active boulder field.
laneImpact: Taliyah dictates the wave state because your threat of engagement is heavily suppressed. She can freely clear minions with Threaded Volley while keeping you at bay. If you get chunked trying to trigger Spirit Abjuration, you will lose mid priority. This allows her to easily roam to side lanes using Rock Surfing and Weaver's Wall while you are trapped under your turret.
why: The core difficulty of this matchup lies in how Unraveled Earth neutralizes your mobility. Whenever you attempt to reposition with Across the Veil or blink across your ultimate zone during Between Worlds, you will trigger Taliyah's minefield. This interaction turns your vital defensive and offensive dashes into self-destructive triggers, leaving you heavily damaged and vulnerable to her subsequent spell rotations.

summary: Corki's Valkyrie allows him to match Ezreal's Arcane Shift safety, turning the lane into a pure skillshot battle between Missile Barrage and Mystic Shot.
howToPlay: To win this duel, you must hold Arcane Shift strictly for defensive purposes, specifically to dodge his Special Delivery or a deadly Missile Barrage "Big One". Never use it forward, as his Valkyrie will let him disengage or punish you instantly. Position yourself diagonally to the minion wave; this angles your Mystic Shot around his cover while keeping you safe from the splash damage of his Phosphorus Bomb.
laneImpact: The laning phase turns into a war of attrition where neither marksman can easily dive or force a decisive engage. You will find yourself constantly fighting for wave control, trying to hide behind your minions to block his Gatling Gun and Phosphorus Bomb while attempting to thread Mystic Shot through the gaps. Trading health relies entirely on who lands their ultimate projectiles first once you both reach level 5.
why: This lane is a constant exchange of long-range fire where safety is guaranteed but victory is earned through accuracy. Whenever you try to reposition or escape with Arcane Shift, Corki can easily match your safety with Valkyrie. This cancels out your usual mobility advantage, leaving both of you to trade blows in a relentless battle of skillshots, pitting your Mystic Shot against his Missile Barrage.

summary: Poppy can reactively block Skarner's E (Ixtal's Impact) charge with her W (Steadfast Presence), preventing his engage and wall-stun.
howToPlay: To survive this matchup, never lead with Ixtal's Impact when Poppy is nearby. Instead, walk up and use the slow from Shattered Earth / Upheaval or the shield from Seismic Bastion to bait out her Steadfast Presence first. Keep your distance from terrain to prevent her Heroic Charge stun. Once her defensive barrier expires, you can safely unleash Impale to drag her or her allies into your team, turning the fight on your terms.
laneImpact: In the jungle, this interaction severely limits your map pressure and skirmishing power. Attempting to gank lanes defended by Poppy becomes highly risky, as she can effortlessly peel you off her carries. During river skirmishes, you are forced to play defensively, knowing that she can also turn the tables by using Heroic Charge to slam you into the very walls you tried to navigate with your charge.
why: Poppy holds a massive advantage because her Steadfast Presence directly shuts down your primary initiation tool. Whenever you attempt to line up Ixtal's Impact for a crucial wall-stun, she can reactively trigger her protective barrier. This immediately halts your charge, damages you, and leaves you grounded, completely neutralizing your ability to force fights or peel for your allies.

summary: Jayce's early Shock Blast combined with To the Skies! deals far more burst damage than Corki can handle before getting items.
howToPlay: Prioritize safety by farming from maximum range using Phosphorus Bomb, and eventually, Missile Barrage. Keep Valkyrie ready solely as a defensive tool; if Jayce lunges forward with To the Skies!, immediately cast it backward to break the engage. Never trade auto-attacks when his Thundering Blow gate is active. If you get chunked, accept losing some gold, stay in experience range, and wait for your Package delivery to impact the map rather than force fights in mid.
laneImpact: This damage disparity forces you to yield early wave control. Jayce can easily crash waves and poke you under turret with Shock Blast. You will find yourself constantly pushed back, burning through mana to thin waves with Phosphorus Bomb. This conceded priority prevents you from helping your jungler contest early river skirmishes, locking you in mid lane while you struggle to maintain high health for potential Special Delivery packages.
why: Jayce's dual-form versatility via Transform Mercury Cannon gives him an overwhelming early burst advantage. His accelerated Shock Blast chunks your health from afar, and if you step up, he can transition to hammer form to execute a lethal dive with To the Skies!. Your early Phosphorus Bomb and Gatling Gun simply cannot match this raw damage output before you acquire your first major item spikes, leaving you vulnerable to quick trades.

summary: Jax's Counter Strike does not dodge your H-28G Evolution Turret laser beams, allowing you to shred him if he uses Leap Strike to engage.
howToPlay: Survival requires disciplined patience. Never use Leap Strike forward unless Heimerdinger has already wasted his CH-2 Electron Storm Grenade. Instead, walk up to safely disarm isolated H-28G Evolution Turret units using Empower for quick resets, saving Counter Strike purely to mitigate minion damage or retreat. If he activates UPGRADE!!!, immediately retreat using Leap Strike on a friendly minion or ward to escape his massive damage zone.
laneImpact: Heimerdinger will comfortably park his H-28G Evolution Turret trio in the lane, forcing you under tower. Because you cannot reliably trade with Leap Strike, you are forced to concede early priority. Every attempt to clear his machines exposes you to CH-2 Electron Storm Grenade, which leads to heavy poke from Hextech Micro-Rockets. Your tower will constantly take chip damage while you struggle to stack Relentless Assault.
why: This matchup hinges on a critical interaction: while Jax's Counter Strike dodges standard attacks, it does not block the charged laser beams from Heimerdinger's H-28G Evolution Turret. If you blindly initiate with Leap Strike, Heimerdinger can easily trigger these lasers by landing Hextech Micro-Rockets or CH-2 Electron Storm Grenade, melting your health bar instantly while you are locked in your engage animation.

summary: Ezreal can use Arcane Shift to dodge Yunara's Arc of Ruin, but must be careful of her high DPS once she activates Transcend One's Self.
howToPlay: To win this skill matchup, never use Arcane Shift offensively unless Yunara's Arc of Ruin is already on cooldown. Always position yourself behind your minions to block her basic trades, but keep enough distance to react when she rushes forward. If she activates Transcend One's Self, immediately back off and use Trueshot Barrage from a safe distance to clear the incoming wave, stalling out her trance duration before looking to re-engage with your own poke.
laneImpact: During the laning phase, this dynamic creates a constantly shifting pressure wave. When Yunara has her Transcend One's Self unavailable, you can confidently push the wave and fish for Essence Flux followed by Mystic Shot combos to force her under tower. However, if she triggers her trance, her enhanced Cultivation of Spirit can melt your health bar if you stand in auto-attack range, forcing you to play defensively.
why: This matchup is a high-stakes duel between Ezreal's long-range poking abilities and Yunara's mobility and DPS. The lane is defined by how you manage your safety net. While you can easily poke her down from afar using Mystic Shot, Yunara's trade potential skyrockets when she activates Transcend One's Self. Your Arcane Shift is your ultimate tool to completely negate her Arc of Ruin projectile, turning her main catch tool into a wasted cooldown.

summary: Maokai's Bramble Smash can knock Alistar back mid-Headbutt, and his Sap Magic passive keeps him sustained against Alistar's burst trades.
howToPlay: To survive, stand parallel to your ADC outside of brush vision to bait out Sapling Toss without taking damage. Never initiate with Headbutt unless you see Maokai waste Bramble Smash on the wave. If Maokai initiates on your carry with Twisted Advance, do not chase him; instead, use Headbutt to peel the enemy marksman away, then activate Trample to stun Maokai, letting Triumphant Roar slowly stabilize your health under your tower.
laneImpact: This interaction forces you into a passive role where your threat level is neutralized. Maokai can freely control the brushes with Sapling Toss, slowly chipping away at your health bar and pushing your ADC off the wave. You cannot easily engage to contest this pressure, because entering his range risks getting locked down by Twisted Advance and swept into Nature's Grasp, leaving you bleeding health and forcing disadvantageous recalls.
why: Maokai counters your primary engage tool. Whenever you attempt to initiate with Headbutt, a reactive Maokai can use Bramble Smash to knock you back mid-charge, completely cancelling your Pulverize follow-up. Furthermore, if you do manage to trigger short trades, Maokai relies on Sap Magic to constantly heal up, rendering your high-cooldown Triumphant Roar sustain insufficient to win this battle of attrition.

summary: Tristana can use Rocket Jump to aggressively follow Corki's Valkyrie retreat after fully stacking her Explosive Charge on him.
howToPlay: To execute this, always wait for Corki to use Phosphorus Bomb to farm before stepping forward. Once he mispositions, jump in with Rocket Jump to slow him, immediately apply Explosive Charge, and activate Rapid Fire. Do not use your ultimate, Buster Shot, too early; hold it to execute or push him back into your wave if he tries to dodge with Valkyrie. If he has Special Delivery active, play back and avoid direct engagements until his fiery trail disappears.
laneImpact: This interaction dictates a highly aggressive lane phase where Corki is forced to play defensively. Tristana's passive, Draw a Bead, paired with Explosive Charge passive explosions, naturally pushes the wave, forcing Corki under his turret where he struggles to farm without burning mana on Phosphorus Bomb. Tristana can easily chip away at the turret plates or dive Corki the moment his escape tool is down, securing early gold.
why: Tristana dominates this matchup by capitalizing on Corki's fragile escape option. While Corki relies on Valkyrie to disengage from trades, his long cooldown leaves him vulnerable. When Tristana attaches Explosive Charge and activates Rapid Fire, she quickly stacks the bomb. If Corki panics and slides away, Tristana can immediately match his flight with Rocket Jump, detonating the charges mid-air or upon landing to secure a lethal burst.

summary: Orianna can abuse Command: Attack and Command: Dissonance to poke Akali down early, forcing Akali to play defensively until she unlocks Perfect Execution.
howToPlay: To survive, let the wave bounce toward you and use Twilight Shroud to safely harvest minions under turret while avoiding her basic attacks. Do not waste Shuriken Flip defensively; save it to react when she mispositions her ball. Once you reach level five, wait for Orianna to miss Command: Attack, then immediately launch Perfect Execution to gap-close, bypassing her Command: Shockwave by dashing behind her to burst her down before she can reactivate her shield.
laneImpact: This constant harassment forces you to concede early minion priority, pushing you under your turret. If you take too much damage trying to trigger Assassin's Mark or clear minions with Five Point Strike, you will be forced into an early recall, losing gold and experience. Orianna will safely farm, shield herself with Command: Protect if you attempt to trade, and maintain superior wave control while threatening you with her ranged basic attacks.
why: Orianna dominates the early game by constantly positioning her ball to zone you. Her ability to repeatedly spam Command: Attack combined with Command: Dissonance creates a persistent hazard zone that chips away at your health whenever you attempt to step up. Because you are a melee champion, you cannot easily retaliate, forcing you to endure this oppressive ranged pressure until you unlock your ultimate, Perfect Execution.

summary: When Zed casts Death Mark (R), Galio can charge Shield of Durand (W) to immediately taunt Zed upon re-emergence and reduce his burst damage.
howToPlay: Always hold Shield of Durand when Zed has Death Mark available. When he marks you, immediately start charging Shield of Durand to mitigate his initial burst, releasing it the millisecond he reappears behind you to trigger the taunt. While he is taunted, chain Justice Punch backwards to knock him up and escape his shadow's range, preventing him from landing Shadow Slash or maximizing his mark's pop damage. If you miss the taunt timing, immediately walk laterally to dodge his shurikens.
laneImpact: Before level five, your Winds of War and Colossal Smash give you superior wave clear, forcing Zed to use Razor Shuriken to farm under turret. But if you waste Justice Punch aggressively, he will punish you with Living Shadow and Shadow Slash. Once ultimates are active, you cannot blindly roam with Hero's Entrance without first shoving the wave, otherwise Zed will quickly destroy your turret or follow your rotation.
why: This matchup is a pure test of reflexes centered on Zed's ultimate. Because Zed deals physical damage, Galio's passive magic shield from Shield of Durand is useless here. However, the physical damage reduction from channeling Shield of Durand when Zed casts Death Mark, followed by an instant taunt when he reappears, completely shuts down his burst window before he can trigger Contempt for the Weak or land multiple Razor Shuriken strikes.

summary: If Leona lands Zenith Blade on Nami, she can lock her down before Nami can cast Aqua Prison to peel.
howToPlay: Establish yourself inside the lane brushes to hide your pathing. Hold Zenith Blade to make Nami move predictably, then strike the moment she steps forward to attempt an Ebb and Flow bounce. Always activate Eclipse mid-air to absorb any delayed counter-poke. If Nami attempts a defensive Tidal Wave, counter her instantly by dropping Solar Flare directly on her head to extend the crowd control chain.
laneImpact: This threat forces Nami to play defensively, limiting her ability to step up and poke with Ebb and Flow or empower her carry with Tidecaller's Blessing. You can control the lane brushes easily, creating immense zone pressure. Consequently, the enemy duo is forced to concede wave control, allowing your lane to stack waves and safely dive or secure deep vision while Nami struggles to sustain under her tower.
why: Nami relies heavily on her Aqua Prison to interrupt incoming engage, but Leona completely bypasses this defense. Once you land Zenith Blade directly onto Nami, the travel time puts you in immediate melee range to instantly chain Shield of Daybreak. This rapid lockdown prevents Nami from casting her bubble or escaping with her Surging Tides passive, leaving her fragile health pool completely exposed to your burst.

summary: Yunara's Kanmei's Steps allows her to dodge Volley and close the distance to unleash her high-damage Cultivation of Spirit.
howToPlay: Never throw Volley unless Yunara has already activated Kanmei's Steps or is locked in her attack animation. Stand deep behind your caster minions so she must draw minion aggro to reach you. If she initiates with Transcend One's Self, do not try to trade back; immediately fire Enchanted Crystal Arrow to stun her and disengage. Use Hawkshot to spot her support's positioning, ensuring you aren't pincered when farming under tower.
laneImpact: You cannot freely contest the wave because stepping up to apply Frost Shot exposes you to her quick engagements. If she activates Transcend One's Self, her upgraded Untouchable Shadow dash will instantly close any safe distance you try to keep. This constant threat forces you to concede early priority, leading to bleed-out plate damage, while she easily matches your waveclear using her bouncing attacks.
why: Yunara's mobility makes this matchup incredibly difficult. Your main tool for spacing and poke, Volley, is easily bypassed when she uses Kanmei's Steps to dodge the arrows and close the gap. Once she is on top of you, her Cultivation of Spirit provides an overwhelming burst of attack speed and ricocheting damage that out-trades Ranger's Focus before you can even stack it up.

summary: Jarvan IV can repeatedly trap Kayle with Cataclysm before level 5, forcing her to burn Flash or die before she unlocks Divine Judgment.
howToPlay: Start the lane by landing Dragon Strike to poke while preparing the wave. Save your Demacian Standard combo for when she steps up to last-hit with Starfire Spellblade. The moment you are one minion away from level five, prep your engage. Use the Demacian Standard and Dragon Strike combo to close the gap, immediately trigger Golden Aegis to slow her, and slam Cataclysm the instant you level up. If she plays too safely, freeze the wave to deny experience.
laneImpact: This matchup demands aggressive wave control to secure that crucial level advantage. You must use Martial Cadence to push early, preventing Kayle from using Celestial Blessing to sustain or safely scale. By forcing her under turret, you deny her the ability to contest your fast level five. Once you achieve this lead, her lane is effectively ruined as she is forced to play extremely far back, sacrificing gold and map pressure.
why: The lane revolves around the race to level five. Since Kayle relies on Divine Ascent and Starfire Spellblade to farm safely from a distance early on, your early threat with Dragon Strike and Demacian Standard is massive. The deciding moment occurs when you secure level five first. Trapping her in Cataclysm before she can unlock Divine Judgment leaves her with no response, forcing an immediate Flash or guaranteeing a fatal first blood.

summary: Brand's Conflagration easily spreads through Heimerdinger's H-28G Evolution Turrets, turning his own defenses into vectors for Brand's burn.
howToPlay: Space your H-28G Evolution Turret placements far apart to prevent a single Conflagration from chaining across your entire line. Never stand in a direct vector between your creations and the minion wave. Hold your CH-2 Electron Storm Grenade strictly to interrupt Brand if he steps forward to cast Pillar of Flame. If he clears your setup, fall back, farm safely from range using Hextech Micro-Rockets, and do not waste UPGRADE!!! on a giant turret that he will instantly melt.
laneImpact: You cannot safely stand near your H-28G Evolution Turret cluster, ruining your Hextech Affinity speed boosts. Brand effortlessly clears your mechanical setup using Pillar of Flame and Conflagration, turning every attempt at establishing wave control into a free poke opportunity for him. This constant health bleed forces early recalls, stripping away your mid-lane priority and letting Brand roam or safely bounce Pyroclasm off your turrets to kill you under your own tower.
why: Your H-28G Evolution Turret setup normally secures your lane, but against Brand, it becomes your greatest liability. His Conflagration spreads instantly from your turrets directly to you or your minion wave. This lets him apply Blaze passively without even aiming his skillshots, turning your static mechanical nest into a deadly network of cascading explosions that easily setups Sear to stun you.

summary: Neither jungler has hard CC to interrupt the other, turning the matchup into a pure farming race where Shyvana prioritizes dragons while Mundo scales for teamfights.
howToPlay: Do not try to force early ganks that waste your tempo. Instead, track her Fury and keep lanes warded to spot her heading to Drakes. When Shyvana commits her Dragon's Descent onto an objective, do not contest blindly if you lack numbers; instead, use Infected Bonesaw to steal her opposite jungle camps or secure the Rift Herald. In late-game teamfights, use Maximum Dosage and Blunt Force Trauma to out-tank her damage while blocking her pathing.
laneImpact: This farming speed directly shapes map pressure. Shyvana will constantly look to secure early Elemental Drakes to power up her Dragon's Descent and stack her passive. If you ignore her, she will melt objectives with Flame Breath. However, Dr. Mundo's safety with Heart Zapper and Maximum Dosage means you can counter-jungle her aggressively, turning the map into a split-map farm fest where neutral objectives are traded.
why: Since neither champion possesses hard crowd control in their base kits to stop the other, this match becomes a direct PvE farming duel. Shyvana uses Burnout and Twin Bite to clear camps rapidly and stack Fury of the Dragonborn, while Dr. Mundo matches her speed using Blunt Force Trauma and Infected Bonesaw. It is a straight race to reach peak item spikes without direct disruption.

summary: Cho'Gath must use Rupture to disengage whenever Darius attempts to pull him in with Apprehend.
howToPlay: Never initiate trades. Keep your distance and hold Rupture exclusively as a defensive tool for when Apprehend is cast. If Darius pulls you, immediately cast Rupture at your feet, follow up with Feral Scream to silence his Decimate, and walk away. Only use Feast to secure minion stacks safely under your tower until you outscale his raw damage. If you miss your knockup, immediately walk toward his inner handle during Decimate to minimize his healing.
laneImpact: You must concede early wave control, as Darius will freeze and look to zone you with Apprehend. Every CS you take with Vorpal Spikes carries the risk of a deadly pull. Your health bar will constantly fluctuate, forcing you to rely on Carnivore to heal back up under your turret. If you waste Rupture to secure distant minions, Darius will instantly force an all-in, turning the lane into a nightmare.
why: Darius thrives on prolonged skirmishes where Hemorrhage can reach five stacks, leading to an execution via Noxian Guillotine. If Darius catches you with Apprehend, he immediately setups Decimate and Crippling Strike. Cho'Gath cannot win these extended duels. Your entire survival hinges on cast-timing Rupture directly on top of yourself the moment Apprehend pulls you, interrupting his follow-up and allowing you to retreat.

summary: Lillia's passive Dream-Laden Bough deals max health damage that melts Mundo, while her high movement speed makes it impossible for him to land Infected Bonesaw.
howToPlay: Your survival hinges on keeping your distance and tracking her Blooming Blows stacks. Never engage when she has max speed; instead, hold Infected Bonesaw until she commits her dash with Watch Out! Eep!, which briefly locks her in place. If she hits you with Swirlseed and prepares Lilting Lullaby, immediately fall back toward a wall so your passive, Goes Where He Pleases, can drop its canister safely.
laneImpact: This dynamic completely strips away your early jungle pressure. Since you cannot reliably hit Infected Bonesaw, Lillia can easily contest your camps or counter-gank you with Swirlseed and Watch Out! Eep!. If she catches you in the river, she will kite you indefinitely, forcing you to back early, which leaves your lanes completely vulnerable to her high-tempo ganks.
why: Lillia is a nightmare matchup in the jungle because her Dream-Laden Bough deals percentage maximum health magic damage, directly countering your massive health pool. Furthermore, the passive movement speed she gains from Blooming Blows makes her incredibly swift, allowing her to easily dodge your Infected Bonesaw. You cannot lock her down or trade effectively when she can constantly dance around your cleaver throws.

summary: Grand Entrance has a brief delay, allowing Morgana to easily react with Black Shield or interrupt him with Dark Binding.
howToPlay: Position yourself slightly parallel to your carry to ensure your Black Shield is always within casting range when Rakan steps up. Never throw Dark Binding blindly; hold it specifically to punish his Grand Entrance trajectory or to stop him when he rushes forward with The Quickness. If he tries to flank with his ultimate, trigger Soul Shackles immediately to stun him as he attempts to use Battle Dance to escape back to safety.
laneImpact: This matchup turns Rakan into a passive protector rather than an active playmaker. Since he cannot safely cast Grand Entrance without being punished, your duo enjoys total control over the lane's pace. You can freely poke with Tormented Shadow to wear down his Fey Feathers shield and punish his ADC. Rakan is forced to waste Battle Dance defensively, draining his mana while you safely command the space around the minion waves.
why: Rakan relies entirely on diving forward to initiate skirmishes, but his predictable movement plays directly into your hands. Because Grand Entrance features a brief, highly visible delay before the knock-up triggers, you have more than enough time to react. You can either protect his target with Black Shield to completely absorb the crowd control or intercept his dash mid-air with Dark Binding, neutralizing his primary engage tool entirely.

summary: Yasuo's Wind Wall cannot block any of your melee abilities, allowing you to freely land Cunning Sweep and Lacerate through his wall.
howToPlay: Position yourself away from your own low-health minions to limit Yasuo's Sweeping Blade escape routes, forcing him to fight you directly. Always hold Repudiation to absorb his third Steel Tempest tornado or his ultimate, Last Breath, negating his crowd control. If he manages to poke you down from a distance, use your Drakehound's Step dashes to slip into the brush to break his vision, then close the gap with Public Execution to finish him.
laneImpact: Yasuo will constantly try to charge Steel Tempest on the wave to threaten you with a tornado. When he has his third strike ready, his threat zone expands, forcing you to use Drakehound's Step defensively. However, because his Wind Wall cannot mitigate Lacerate or Cunning Sweep, he cannot easily disengage or freeze the wave against you, turning every minion wave into a volatile zone where single missteps lead to lethal trades.
why: This matchup is a high-speed duel of pure movement. While Yasuo relies on Sweeping Blade to dance through minions, your Drakehound's Step allows you to match his dashes step for step. Crucially, his Wind Wall is completely useless against you. Because all your primary damage tools—Cunning Sweep and Lacerate—are melee strikes rather than projectiles, you can ignore his defensive barrier entirely and strike him down right through it.

summary: Braum can block Pyke's Bone Skewer with Unbreakable, but Pyke's Death from Below executes through Braum's defensive shields.
howToPlay: Always position yourself parallel to your carry to block Bone Skewer with Unbreakable, but never stand directly on top of them to avoid Pyke stunning both of you with Phantom Undertow. Hold Unbreakable strictly for his hook; if you waste it, he will engage. When Pyke casts Death from Below, use Stand Behind Me to jump out of the 'X' indicator to a minion or your ally, or interrupt his follow-up with Glacial Fissure.
laneImpact: You cannot play aggressively or step past the minion wave to land Winter's Bite. Pyke's Ghostwater Dive forces you to play defensively under tower, as a single successful hook-stun chain via Phantom Undertow puts your ADC directly into execute range. Consequently, you will constantly lose priority, allowing Pyke to freely roam the map while you are stuck safely clearing waves and shielding under-tower poke.
why: Pyke's high-lethality kit turns this lane into a deadly dance. While your Unbreakable can completely intercept his Bone Skewer to protect your carry, this defensive layer loses all value once your health drops. If either of you falls below the threshold, Pyke's Death from Below completely bypasses Unbreakable and Stand Behind Me's resistances, executing you instantly. This makes your shield a double-edged sword that can trap you into giving resets.

summary: Jhin can punish Jinx's lack of mobility by trapping her with Captive Audience and securing a root with Deadly Flourish.
howToPlay: To survive, prioritize minigun form on Switcheroo! to match his push without wasting mana. Always stand behind your own minion wave to block Deadly Flourish, but stay far enough from low-health minions to avoid Dancing Grenade bounces. If he steps up with his fourth Whisper shot, back off and use Zap! to slow his advance. If you get rooted, immediately drop Flame Chompers! directly on his path to cut off his follow-up attack.
laneImpact: This constant threat of CC forces you to play defensively under your turret, where Jhin can bounce Dancing Grenade off low-health minions to poke you. You will struggle to maintain wave control, as clearing waves with Switcheroo! rockets drains your mana too fast. This allows Jhin to crash waves, secure easy recall timings, and constantly chip away at your tower while threatening you with Curtain Call if your health drops too low.
why: Jhin thrives in this lane because Jinx lacks any natural dash or escape to dodge his setups. If you step onto a hidden Captive Audience trap, the slow makes you an incredibly easy target for his Deadly Flourish. This long-range root setup allows him to safely unload Whisper fourth-shot critical damage or bounce a lethal Dancing Grenade without you being able to trade back effectively during the early skirmishes.

summary: Neither jungler has hard CC to interrupt the other, turning the matchup into a pure farming race where Shyvana prioritizes dragons while Mundo scales for teamfights.
howToPlay: Maximize your clear speed by resetting your auto-attacks with Twin Bite inside your Burnout aura. Do not waste time chasing him; his passive Goes Where He Pleases makes early skirmishes fruitless. Instead, track his pathing and rush the first dragon the moment Dragon's Descent is active. If Dr. Mundo contests, use Flame Breath to shred his high health pool, but prioritize the objective's health bar to secure your vital Fury of the Dragonborn stacks.
laneImpact: Because ganks are hard to force without reliable CC, lanes on both sides receive very little early pressure. The jungle remains quiet until Epic Monsters spawn. You will find yourself constantly tracking his position to steal away camps with Flame Breath while he attempts to out-sustain you. If you fail to secure the first drake, you fall behind in stacks, shifting the pressure entirely onto your laners to survive his mid-game teamfight scaling.
why: This matchup is a pure speed-clearing contest because neither of you possesses the hard crowd control required to lock down or interrupt the other. Dr. Mundo relies on Infected Bonesaw for slow and Heart Zapper for sustain, while you use Burnout and Twin Bite to tear through camps. Without CC to force errors, you both powerfarm, but your passive Fury of the Dragonborn demands you secure elemental dragons to scale.

summary: Ryze can instantly interrupt your Astral Flight with a point-and-click Rune Prison root.
howToPlay: Never initiate trades with Astral Flight while Rune Prison is available. Instead, bait him into using his root by standing just outside its short range while using Singularity to farm. Once Rune Prison is on cooldown, you have a brief window to channel Breath of Light safely. If Ryze attempts to rotate with Realm Warp, prepare to drop Falling Star on his portal destination to instantly stun him upon arrival.
laneImpact: This interaction severely limits your ability to trade or clear waves aggressively. You cannot use Astral Flight to fly over minions for a quick Breath of Light spray without risking an immediate grounding. If Ryze freezes the wave or uses Realm Warp to reposition, you are forced to play defensively near your tower, delaying your passive scaling and reducing your map pressure.
why: Ryze's point-and-click Rune Prison is the ultimate counter to your Astral Flight. While you attempt to reposition or escape, his instant root immediately stops your flight mid-air, leaving you stationary and vulnerable to his Spell Flux and Overload burst. Because Ryze scales exceptionally well with Arcane Mastery, letting him disrupt your main defensive and mobility tool makes it hard to safely gather Stardust from Singularity.

summary: Kog'Maw can abuse his massive range advantage from Bio-Arcane Barrage to poke Vayne down whenever she steps up to last-hit, as she lacks waveclear or long-range tools.
howToPlay: Your primary objective is to watch Kog'Maw's glowing green visual effect that signals Bio-Arcane Barrage is active. The moment he activates it, immediately step back and concede CS if necessary. Only look for a quick Tumble trade once his buff ends and goes on cooldown. Keep Condemn ready to push him away if he attempts to chase you down with Void Ooze while his range is enhanced, ensuring you stay alive.
laneImpact: This range mismatch forces you to play perpetually under your turret. Kog'Maw will easily slow-push waves while chipping away at your health bar with Void Ooze to slow you down if you step up. You will find yourself bleeding health, making early recalls inevitable. This gives Kog'Maw free plate gold and pressure, delaying your crucial scaling spikes while keeping you trapped defending your tower.
why: Kog'Maw completely controls the lane's pacing because of Bio-Arcane Barrage. When this ability is active, his basic attacks outrange Vayne's short reach, allowing him to punish every single CS she attempts. Since Vayne relies entirely on single-target autos and has no long-range abilities or waveclear like Tumble to contest him safely, she is forced to take heavy damage just to secure minions while he safely scales.

summary: Jayce can use Thundering Blow to knock Aatrox away if Aatrox attempts to close the distance with Umbral Dash.
howToPlay: To survive, you must bait out Thundering Blow before committing. Position yourself safely near the brush to drop minion aggro and farm primarily with the tip of The Darkin Blade. Never use Umbral Dash forward unless he has already wasted his knockback in hammer form. If he jumps on you with To the Skies!, use Infernal Chains to pull him in after he tries to disengage, allowing you to activate World Ender and turn the trade.
laneImpact: This knockback interaction forces you into a defensive posture, making it extremely difficult to contest the wave early on. You are constantly shoved under your turret, losing priority and bleeding health trying to farm. Because you cannot reliably land Infernal Chains without being pushed away, your trade potential is non-existent, which translates into zero pressure on his tower and allows Jayce to freely roam.
why: Jayce dictates this matchup by abusing his range advantage. He constantly pokes you down from afar, and any attempt to retaliate is instantly shut down. The moment you try to close the distance using your Umbral Dash to land The Darkin Blade, Jayce simply switches forms and uses Thundering Blow to knock you back, completely resetting the fight and leaving you vulnerable to his ranged follow-up.

summary: Jax can use Leap Strike to close the gap on Kindred, and Counter Strike blocks her Mounting Dread third-strike execution.
howToPlay: Never initiate a fight by blindly jumping in; instead, walk up or flank from a bush, saving Leap Strike to follow her after she uses Dance of Arrows. Hold your Counter Strike specifically for when she applies Mounting Dread, activating it right before her third hit to deny the execute. If she deploys Lamb's Respite, stand inside the circle with her, charge your attacks, and time Empower to strike the very millisecond her ultimate expires.
laneImpact: This matchup advantage shifts the jungle pressure heavily in your favor, allowing you to aggressively contest her Mark of the Kindred spawns. Because she cannot safely trade with you 1v1, you can invade her camps and force her out of the river. She is forced to play defensively, delaying her marks and severely limiting her scaling while you secure early map control.
why: Jax completely shuts down Kindred's kiting potential by neutralizing her primary self-peel and burst tool. When she tries to distance herself, Leap Strike instantly closes the distance. More importantly, when she attempts to execute you with Mounting Dread, activating Counter Strike blocks the basic attacks required to trigger that critical third-strike damage, leaving her vulnerable and stripped of her main defensive threat.

summary: Garen must activate Courage to absorb the damage and reduce the stun duration of Renekton's Ruthless Predator.
howToPlay: Watch Renekton's fury bar closely; when it glows red, expect him to dash in. Do not waste Decisive Strike early; instead, hold it to cleanse the slow from Slice and Dice or to silence him before he can activate Dominus. If he manages to stun you without your Courage active, immediately retreat, let Perseverance restore your health pool, and do not contest the wave until your shield is fully available again.
laneImpact: When you successfully block his stun, Renekton is left vulnerable with extremely long recovery windows. This allows you to aggressively push the wave with Judgment while his Cull the Meek is insufficient to match your clear. If you fail to time your shield, you will be forced under turret, bleeding gold while your passive Perseverance slowly ticks. Winning these trades dictates who controls the top alcove and prevents Renekton from roaming.
why: This matchup is a pure test of reflexes centered on Renekton's Ruthless Predator. If the crocodile catches you with his stun, especially when fueled by Reign of Anger, he will chunk your health bar and dash away safely using Slice and Dice. However, Garen possesses the perfect response: activating Courage right as the stun lands. Mitigating that burst and reducing the stun's duration completely neutralizes Renekton's trading power, turning an even lane into your favor.

summary: Galio's innate magic resistance scaling and Shield of Durand (W) shield mitigate Mel's magic damage poke, allowing him to easily clear waves with Winds of War (Q).
howToPlay: Stand directly inside the minion wave to bait Mel into aiming her skillshots at you, letting your Shield of Durand shield absorb the brunt of the magic damage. Simultaneously, aim Winds of War to clip both her and the caster minions. If she steps past her melee minions to contest you, immediately punish her with Justice Punch followed by Colossal Smash. Save Hero's Entrance for skirmishes near the river once you have pushed her deep under tower.
laneImpact: This match-up quickly turns into a one-sided shoving contest where you dictate the tempo. By constantly shoving Mel under her turret with Winds of War and Colossal Smash, you force her to waste her high-cooldown control spells on farming rather than trading. She is pinned to her lane, losing any ability to contest neutral objectives or match your map-wide rotations when you activate Hero's Entrance.
why: Mel relies on continuous magic damage to zone out her opponents, but your innate magic resistance scaling combined with the passive magic shield from Shield of Durand completely neutralizes her poke. She cannot chunk your health pool down before running out of mana. This defensive safety net allows you to step up aggressively and deploy Winds of War to demolish minion waves without fearing her retaliatory spellcasts.

summary: Teemo's Blinding Dart prevents Kai'Sa's basic attacks from landing, stopping her from popping her Second Skin plasma stacks.
howToPlay: Never waste Blinding Dart on minion farm; hold it until Kai'Sa charges forward with Supercharge or tries to hit you with Void Seeker. If she misses her void projectile, immediately step past her minions to force a short trade. Place Noxious Trap mushrooms along the side brush paths to catch her if she attempts to escape. If she targets you with Killer Instinct, drop a trap directly at your feet and blind her immediately.
laneImpact: Because Kai'Sa cannot safely stack plasma, she is forced to concede priority. You can easily slow-push waves using Toxic Shot to poke her under turret. If she attempts to thin the wave with Icathian Rain, she isolates herself, making her an easy target. This constant pressure denies her farm and forces early recalls, keeping her from evolving her abilities and preventing her from roaming with Killer Instinct.
why: Teemo dominates this mid matchup because Kai'Sa relies entirely on landing consecutive auto-attacks to trigger the burst from her passive, Second Skin. By using Blinding Dart right as she attempts to trade, you completely negate her offensive threat. While blinded, she cannot stack plasma or detonate it, turning her Icathian Rain into isolated, non-lethal magic damage while your Toxic Shot continuously drains her health.

summary: Orianna can constantly harass Ahri with Command: Attack, but she is highly vulnerable to a Spirit Rush engage if she mispositions her Ball.
howToPlay: Never stand in a direct line between Orianna and her ball. Position yourself laterally to force her to choose between hitting you or clearing the wave. The moment she throws Command: Attack too far behind your caster minions, immediately trigger Spirit Rush forward to bypass her zone. With her ball out of position, she cannot quickly use Command: Shockwave on herself, leaving her wide open to a clean Charm and Fox-Fire burst.
laneImpact: You will find yourself constantly pushed toward your tower, forced to use Orb of Deception just to secure minions from a safe distance. Every mistake in your positioning leads to heavy health loss, forcing you to rely on Essence Theft to sustain through her poke. This constant pressure limits your ability to roam, locking you in lane until you can find an opening to punish her ball placement.
why: Orianna dominates the early game by constantly repositioning her ball with Command: Attack, forcing you to step back to avoid Command: Dissonance. Because her ranged auto-attacks from Clockwork Windup hurt, you cannot easily trade back. However, the tide turns when she moves her ball too far forward. Without Command: Protect immediately available to shield her, Orianna becomes completely defenseless against a sudden Spirit Rush dash.

summary: Aurora can use the stealth from Across the Veil (W) to stall out the duration of Zed's Death Mark (R).
howToPlay: Never cast Across the Veil proactively to trade. If Zed initiates with Living Shadow to poke, use The Weirding to slow him and step back. When he commits with Death Mark, wait for the brief delay of his reappearance, then immediately trigger Across the Veil to jump away and become invisible. If he tries to follow your outline, immediately cast Between Worlds to leap to the opposite border, completely wasting his ultimate window before turning back with Twofold Hex for a counter-kill.
laneImpact: Before level five, Aurora holds a range advantage, using Twofold Hex and The Weirding to poke Zed while he tries to farm with Razor Shuriken. However, once both ultimates are available, the lane completely freezes in terms of raw aggression. Zed cannot safely dive with Living Shadow because if he uses his shadows aggressively, Aurora can trap him inside Between Worlds or safely disengage, turning the lane into a battle of baiting out high-value cooldowns.
why: This matchup is a chess game of evasive mechanics where Zed's burst relies heavily on his ultimate. When Zed commits with Death Mark, Aurora has the perfect defensive tool in Across the Veil. By entering stealth immediately after he reappears, she denies him the target visibility required to land Razor Shuriken and Shadow Slash, neutralizing the damage amplification before the mark detonates.

summary: Using Shuriken Flip (E) or Perfect Execution (R) to dash behind Sett when he casts Haymaker (W) completely avoids his true damage shield blast.
howToPlay: Never initiate a full trade with Shuriken Flip; instead, use your movement speed from Assassin's Mark and Five Point Strike to bait Sett into activating his grit. Keep your cursor positioned behind Sett to immediately react with Shuriken Flip or Perfect Execution the millisecond his Haymaker animation begins. If you misplay and get stunned by Facebreaker before executing this, immediately drop Twilight Shroud to break his targeting and stall out his temporary shield.
laneImpact: Sett is forced into a defensive posture, unable to safely contest waves with Knuckle Down or force trades. Since his primary burst threat is neutralized, you can freely poke him with Five Point Strike and trigger Assassin's Mark from the safety of Twilight Shroud. This pressure secures you easy wave control, enabling you to crash waves at will, threaten dive setups with your high mobility, or roam to assist your jungler.
why: This favorable matchup hinges entirely on Akali's ability to completely negate Sett's main defensive and offensive tool, Haymaker. While Sett relies on trading heavy blows to build grit and unleash a massive true damage shield blast, Akali possesses the perfect mobility tools to bypass it. By saving Shuriken Flip or Perfect Execution to dash directly behind him during his Haymaker cast, you render his core ability completely useless while continuing your assault.

summary: Morgana can reactively cast Black Shield to block Ahri's Charm, neutralizing Ahri's pick potential in skirmishes.
howToPlay: To survive, you must bait out Black Shield before committing. Use Fox-Fire to gain movement speed and position aggressively, threatening a fake engage. If she holds her shield, do not throw Charm; instead, focus on farming with Orb of Deception. When she misses Dark Binding, you have a short window to pressure her. If she catches you with Soul Shackles, immediately use Spirit Rush to dash out of its tether range before the stun triggers.
laneImpact: Laning becomes a tedious war of attrition. Morgana will constantly shove the wave using Tormented Shadow, forcing you to use Orb of Deception defensively for waveclear rather than poke. If you get caught by Dark Binding while trying to match her push, she will drop Tormented Shadow underneath you for massive damage. This limits your roam timers, keeping you locked in mid-lane and unable to utilize Spirit Rush to map-play.
why: This matchup is dictated by how Black Shield completely negates your pick potential. Whenever you attempt to set up a burst combo with Charm, Morgana can reactively absorb the crowd control and the initial magic damage. Without the damage amplification from Charm, your Orb of Deception and Fox-Fire fail to threaten her health bar, while her passive Soul Siphon allows her to easily sustain through any minor poke you land.

summary: Garen must use Decisive Strike to run away and kite Tryndamere once Undying Rage is activated.
howToPlay: When Tryndamere commits, activate Courage immediately to absorb his high-crit damage. The absolute golden rule of this matchup is to save Decisive Strike for his ultimate. Once he triggers Undying Rage, do not try to fight him; immediately activate Decisive Strike to cleanse the slow from Mocking Shout, gain movement speed, and run away. Kite him out for those five seconds, then turn back to finish him.
laneImpact: Tryndamere will constantly push to stack Battle Fury, forcing you to defend your turret. You cannot let him hit the wave for free, so you must contest his lane control with Judgment. However, overextending is fatal; if he catches you with your abilities on cooldown, he will chase you down the long lane using Spinning Slash and Mocking Shout, turning a simple trade into a deadly pursuit.
why: This duel is a constant battle of attrition where your passive healing from Perseverance matches his Bloodlust sustain. You win short trades with quick bursts, but Tryndamere excels in extended fights once his Battle Fury is fully stacked. The lane hinges entirely on how you manage his ultimate window; executing him with Demacian Justice is impossible while Undying Rage is active, turning the matchup into a precise dance of baiting and disengaging.

summary: Ornn can use the Unstoppable status of Bellows Breath to completely negate the pull of Sett's Facebreaker or the suppression of The Show Stopper.
howToPlay: Never initiate trades with Searing Charge; save it strictly to escape after Sett wastes his pull. Keep Bellows Breath ready specifically for when Sett lunges forward to cast Facebreaker or starts the animation for The Show Stopper. If you successfully block his crowd control, immediately disengage while his Haymaker grit decays. If Sett manages to ult you, wait out his shield before attempting a counter-engage with Call of the Forge God from safety.
laneImpact: This matchup forces you to play defensively near your tower. If Sett freezes, you cannot contest with basic attacks due to Pit Grit's passive healing. Every time you try to secure minions with Volcanic Rupture, you risk Sett using Knuckle Down to close the gap. If he grabs you with Facebreaker while your defensive tools are offline, he easily sets up a massive Haymaker shield, forcing an early recall.
why: Sett dominates short trades with Knuckle Down and Pit Grit, but Ornn can completely neutralize Sett's primary engage tools. By timing Bellows Breath perfectly, you become Unstoppable, completely negating the displacement of Facebreaker or the suppression from The Show Stopper. If you fail this timing, Sett will drag you into a losing brawl where his true damage from Haymaker melts your tank stats.

summary: Amumu must save Curse of the Sad Mummy to lock down Viego the moment he attempts to possess a soul via Sovereign's Domination.
howToPlay: Do not rush to claim a soul with Sovereign's Domination immediately if Amumu is lurking nearby with his ultimate ready. Instead, use Harrowed Path along walls to scout and bait out Bandage Toss. Charge Spectral Maw from the fog of war to disrupt his channels or pin him down. If he holds Curse of the Sad Mummy, delay your possession, staying on the outskirts of the fight, and use Heartbreaker to execute other targets first.
laneImpact: In the jungle, Amumu clears quickly using Despair and Tantrum, matching your speed but preferring 5v5 skirmishes. If you get caught by Bandage Toss in the river, you risk getting locked down before you can set up your Harrowed Path. This pressure forces you to fight in tight corridors where your camouflage is effective, or wait out the initial engage so you don't get focused down first during major objective contests.
why: This jungle matchup revolves around Viego's ability to chain resets versus Amumu's teamfight disruption. The central clash occurs when Viego tries to trigger Sovereign's Domination. If Viego attempts to possess a fallen enemy, Amumu can easily time Curse of the Sad Mummy to lock him down mid-animation. However, if Amumu wastes his ultimate early, Viego's Blade of the Ruined King and Heartbreaker will shred through the mummy's tankiness during skirmishes.

summary: Bard can cast Cosmic Binding to stun Leona against the wall or her own ADC when she engages with Zenith Blade.
howToPlay: Never throw Cosmic Binding proactively unless Leona's Zenith Blade is on cooldown. Stand near walls to bait her engage, but always keep an angle clear to land your stun immediately when she pulls herself to you. If she locks down your marksman instead, target her ADC with Tempered Fate to stop their follow-up damage, then drop a Caretaker’s Shrine behind your partner to help them safely retreat.
laneImpact: Whichever support misuses their primary tool loses complete control of the bush line. If Leona misses Zenith Blade, she becomes a walking target, allowing you to poke her down with Traveler’s Call empowered attacks. However, if you waste Cosmic Binding, your ADC has to retreat immediately, conceding wave priority and allowing Leona to zone you away from your Caretaker’s Shrine packs under the turret.
why: The lane revolves entirely around Leona's engage versus Bard's counter-disengage. When Leona launches forward with Zenith Blade, her linear path makes her incredibly vulnerable to a well-timed Cosmic Binding. Because she lands directly on top of her target, you can easily stun her against nearby terrain or her approaching marksman, neutralizing her Shield of Daybreak threat before she can lock anyone down.

summary: Twitch's Spray and Pray turns him into a rapid-fire physical damage source, causing him to instantly melt himself against Rammus's Defensive Ball Curl.
howToPlay: Your primary rule is to hold Powerball until Twitch reveals his position from Ambush. Once he appears, roll directly into his path, activate Frenzying Taunt to force his focus onto you, and immediately follow up with Defensive Ball Curl. If he activates Spray and Pray, position yourself directly in front of your squishy allies. Block his piercing bolts with your shell so he melts his own health bar against your spikes.
laneImpact: Twitch is completely locked out of contesting neutral objectives or invading your jungle. His stealth from Ambush becomes useless for aggressive skirmishing because you can instantly react to his appearance. If he tries to open fire on your lanes, your map-wide pressure allows you to counter-gank, shut down his momentum, and prevent him from safely stacking Deadly Venom or executing allies with Contaminate.
why: Twitch relies entirely on rapid-fire physical auto-attacks to stack his Deadly Venom. However, when he unleashes Spray and Pray, his increased attack speed and piercing bolts turn into a self-destructive trap. By activating Defensive Ball Curl, you reflect massive damage back to him with every single hit he lands, boosted by your Rolling Armordillo passive, forcing the rat to quickly obliterate his own health bar.

summary: Brand can easily land his Sear stun on you if you stand still to channel Breath of Light.
howToPlay: Never activate Breath of Light while Brand has his Sear available unless you are safely flying sideways with Astral Flight. Bait out his Pillar of Flame first by stepping forward and immediately back. Once he misses or wastes Sear on a minion, immediately drop Singularity to trap him and channel your fire. If he initiates with Pyroclasm, immediately fly away with Astral Flight to prevent the fireballs from bouncing back to you.
laneImpact: The lane oscillates between rapid wave clearing and punishing trades. If you mindlessly use Singularity and Breath of Light to stack Cosmic Creator, Brand will walk up to chunk you. Every time you get stunned, you lose significant health, forcing early recalls that cost you tower plating and delay your scaling. Missing his skillshots, however, gives you free reign to push him under tower.
why: This matchup revolves entirely around your immobility during Breath of Light. Because you must stand still to channel your main source of damage, Brand has an incredibly easy time landing Sear to stun you, provided he has already applied Blaze via Pillar of Flame or Conflagration. This instantly interrupts your channel, leaving you completely vulnerable to his full burst trade.

summary: Equinox instantly silences Morgana, preventing her from casting Black Shield to protect herself or her ally during trades.
howToPlay: To survive this lane, you must bait out Equinox without committing your own spells first. Walk forward to feign an incoming Dark Binding, then immediately step back to force Soraka to waste her silence. Once her silence zone disappears, you have a brief opening to safely protect your marksman with Black Shield and look for a Dark Binding catch. If she refuses to cast her zone first, refuse any aggressive trade.
laneImpact: This constant threat turns short trades heavily in her favor. Whenever your marksman takes damage, you cannot reliably protect them if Equinox is active. Soraka easily negates your Tormented Shadow poke by keeping her lane partner healthy with Astral Infusion and Wish, slowly draining your mana while forcing your duo to concede wave priority and take unfavorable early recalls.
why: Soraka completely shuts down your defensive utility due to an asymmetric casting window. Whenever you attempt to react with Black Shield or fish for a Dark Binding, Soraka can instantly drop Equinox under you. This instant silence prevents you from activating Black Shield in time to block incoming crowd control or damage for your ally, while she safely out-sustains any trade using Astral Infusion and Starcall.

summary: K'Sante can use Path Maker to block the knockup from Jarvan's E-Q, or use All Out to smash Jarvan through his own Cataclysm wall.
howToPlay: Play this lane with extreme discipline by baiting his defensive tools. Never lead with your Demacian Standard and Dragon Strike combo; instead, farm using the extra range of Dragon Strike and trigger Martial Cadence only when he wastes Path Maker. If he activates All Out, immediately use Golden Aegis for the slow and walk away. Save your Cataclysm until after he has committed his dashes, ensuring he cannot easily reposition you through a wall.
laneImpact: Because your main engage is so easily countered, you cannot easily force short, aggressive trades. K'Santé will zone you with Ntofo Strikes, threatening a third-stack knockup if you step up to farm. If you try to push the wave, he can slide in with Footwork to shield himself and drag out the skirmish, slowly wearing down your Golden Aegis and forcing you into unfavorable recall timings.
why: K'Santé holds all the tools to neutralize your primary initiation. The moment you commit to a Demacian Standard and Dragon Strike combo, he can reactively channel Path Maker to completely shrug off the knockup while reducing your damage. Furthermore, relying on Cataclysm to trap him often backfires, as he can use All Out to shatter your arena, displacing you through the terrain while shredding your tankiness.

summary: Maokai can use the untargetability of Twisted Advance to dodge Zenith Blade, turning the engage back on Leona.
howToPlay: To win this, you must hold Zenith Blade and bait Maokai into initiating. Walk up aggressively with Shield of Daybreak active to force his Twisted Advance. Once he commits and lands, use Eclipse to absorb his Bramble Smash follow-up, then immediately lock him down. If you must engage, wait until he uses Sap Magic to heal or when you see his Twisted Advance is on cooldown, giving you a clean window to land Solar Flare.
laneImpact: Neither support can blindly fish for engages without risking a devastating counter-attack. When Maokai uses Sapling Toss to control the bushes, you cannot easily step up to threaten with Shield of Daybreak. This turns the lane into a tense standoff where the wave bounces back and forth, and any early health leads depend entirely on who baits out the other's defensive tools first.
why: This matchup revolves around the clash between Leona's Zenith Blade and Maokai's Twisted Advance. If you initiate with Zenith Blade, Maokai can activate Twisted Advance on your ally or you during your dash. Because he becomes untargetable during Twisted Advance, he completely negates your root, repositioning himself to peel your target or counter-engage on your vulnerable carry with Bramble Smash.

summary: Using Shuriken Flip (E) or Perfect Execution (R) to dash behind Sett when he casts Haymaker (W) completely avoids his true damage shield blast.
howToPlay: To survive, never cast Haymaker reactively while she has her dashes available. Instead, prioritize landing a stunned Facebreaker by pulling her alongside a minion before releasing your true damage blast; this brief stun window prevents her from using Shuriken Flip or Perfect Execution to escape behind you. If she shrouds, walk away immediately toward your tower to force her to chase you outside her safety zone, keeping Knuckle Down ready to punish her.
laneImpact: This interaction forces you into a defensive posture where securing wave control is extremely difficult. Standard trades become highly risky; if she bait-forces your Haymaker and dashes behind you, you lose the trade catastrophically and are forced to retreat under tower. You cannot easily pressure her with Facebreaker because Twilight Shroud lets her safely stall out your defensive windows.
why: Akali holds the upper hand because her high mobility completely neutralizes your main retaliatory tool. The moment you channel Haymaker to turn her burst into a shield and true damage, she can instantly react with Shuriken Flip or Perfect Execution. By dashing directly behind you, she effortlessly escapes the central blast zone, leaving you completely vulnerable with an empty Grit bar and no defensive shield.

summary: Braum's Unbreakable can absorb Karma's Mantra-boosted Inner Flame, preventing the explosive AoE damage from hitting his ADC.
howToPlay: Position yourself slightly ahead of your carry to bait her *Inner Flame*, but never waste *Unbreakable* on unempowered poke. Wait specifically for the purple glow of her *Mantra* to activate before raising your shield. If she manages to catch you with *Focused Resolve*, quickly use *Stand Behind Me* on your ally to break the distance, or counter her approach with *Glacial Fissure* to disrupt her movement.
laneImpact: When *Unbreakable* is available, you deny Karma's ability to easily push the wave and chunk your health under turret. However, if she baits out your shield, her *Inspire* allows her to easily kite your attempts to engage. Missing this defensive window results in your duo being shoved in, bleeding health, and losing control of the bushes where she can freely land *Focused Resolve*.
why: This matchup is a pure test of reflexes and positioning, centered on how you manage Karma's poke. While she attempts to bully your marksman with *Inner Flame*, your *Unbreakable* is the ultimate countermeasure. It can completely absorb the projectile of her *Mantra*-empowered *Inner Flame*, swallowing the initial hit and preventing the devastating secondary explosion from splashing onto your carry.

summary: Wukong can cast Warrior Trickster to leave a clone right as Zed lands from Death Mark, absorbing his burst and leaving him vulnerable to a Cyclone knock-up.
howToPlay: Never initiate a duel with Warrior Trickster; keep it strictly reserved as your defensive reaction to Death Mark. The instant Zed reappears behind you, press Warrior Trickster to leave the decoy, then immediately activate Cyclone to knock him up as he tries to escape. If he swaps places with his Living Shadow, use Nimbus Strike to close the gap, reducing his armor with Golden Staff to finish him off.
laneImpact: This interaction dictates the entire jungle tempo, stripping Zed of his ability to contest Epic Monsters or Scuttle Crabs. Knowing he cannot execute you, Zed is forced into passive farming or desperate cross-map ganks. You can aggressively invade his camps, force early skirmishes, and secure objective priority because any direct 1v1 encounter in the river heavily favors your high-impact teamfight tools.
why: Wukong completely neutralizes Zed's assassination potential thanks to the decoy mechanic of Warrior Trickster. The moment Zed commits his Death Mark, you can deploy your clone to absorb his initial burst and Razor Shuriken strikes. Furthermore, the bonus armor from Stone Skin makes you naturally too tanky for his physical damage, leaving Zed completely vulnerable once his shadow cooldowns are spent.

summary: Annie must use Pyromania-charged stuns to interrupt Ryze's Spell Flux combos before he can spread damage to the wave.
howToPlay: Sit constantly at three or four Pyromania charges to keep Ryze second-guessing his positioning. When he approaches the wave to cast Spell Flux, activate Molten Shield for the sudden movement speed and stun charge, then immediately tag him with Disintegrate or Incinerate. Never waste your stun on low-value poke; hold it specifically to freeze him in place when he tries to spread his damage. If he gets a push lead, use Molten Shield to mitigate his bounced Overload damage.
laneImpact: Failing to disrupt his rhythm allows Ryze to rapidly shove you under turret using Spell Flux spreads, forcing you to waste mana farming with Disintegrate. This pressure keeps you trapped in lane while he roams. However, when you successfully threaten him with Pyromania, the lane remains static. He cannot safely step up to spread his runes, which completely stalls his ability to secure early priority or rotate with Realm Warp.
why: This matchup is a pure race for mid lane priority, decided by how you handle Ryze's wave clear. Ryze relies on marking minions with Spell Flux to bounce Overload damage across the wave and onto you. To stop this engine, you must use your Pyromania-charged stuns. Interrupting his spell rotations before he can spread his marks neutralizes his pushing power, keeping the lane completely even.

summary: Ahri must hold her Charm to interrupt Aurora's dash or catch her immediately as she exits Across the Veil.
howToPlay: To win, never initiate trades with Across the Veil while Ahri has Charm available. Instead, use the threat of Twofold Hex to bait her into throwing it. If she misses, immediately activate Between Worlds to lock her down, using the border teleports to dodge her Orb of Deception return damage. If you do get charmed, use The Weirding immediately upon recovery to slow her Spirit Rush chase and retreat safely.
laneImpact: Wave control becomes a tense standoff. Ahri uses Orb of Deception to push and heal with Essence Theft, while you must match her with Twofold Hex. Neither of you can safely commit to an all-out dive because Between Worlds and Spirit Rush offer too much safety. A single missed Charm or a mistimed Across the Veil immediately shifts the lane pressure, forcing the loser under tower or back to base.
why: This matchup is a pure duel of movement where Aurora's stealth and Ahri's crowd control collide. The lane's outcome hinges entirely on how Ahri uses Charm. She will actively hold it to intercept you mid-dash during Across the Veil or time it precisely to hit you the moment your brief invisibility ends. If she lands this, your Spirit Abjuration trade setup completely collapses.

summary: Sivir can easily react to Ezreal's highly telegraphed Mystic Shot with her Spell Shield, gaining mana while constantly shoving him under tower with Ricochet.
howToPlay: To survive, you must discipline your trigger finger. Never lead with Mystic Shot; instead, try to bait her Spell Shield by marking her with Essence Flux, then holding your actual trigger. If she misplays her shield, that is your cue to trade. Use Arcane Shift exclusively as a defensive tool to reposition away from the return path of her Boomerang Blade. Focus on matching her push as much as possible with basic attacks to prevent your tower from falling too early.
laneImpact: This matchup quickly devolves into a constant struggle under your own turret. Sivir's relentless wave clearance with Ricochet and Boomerang Blade keeps you pinned, making it impossible to establish lane priority. Because you are constantly clearing large waves, you cannot find clean angles to land Essence Flux or retaliate. This continuous pressure drains your mana pool and chip-damages your turret, leaving you unable to assist in early River skirmishes.
why: Sivir completely neutralizes your primary poke tool because the projectile speed of Mystic Shot makes it incredibly easy for her to react with Spell Shield. Instead of softening her up, your missed skillshots actively benefit her by triggering her heal and passive movement speed. Meanwhile, she can constantly activate Ricochet to bounce physical damage through your minion wave, forcing you to farm backward while she remains entirely safe.

summary: Fizz can use Playful / Trickster to become untargetable, easily dodging your Falling Star and landing on top of you.
howToPlay: To survive, you must never cast Falling Star or Singularity offensively; keep them locked until Fizz commits his Playful. If he initiates with Urchin Strike, drop Singularity directly on yourself and prepare Astral Flight to fly backward immediately towards your turret. Never try to trade back with Breath of Light while his untargetable jump is available. If he lands Chum the Waters, immediately fly away to safety before the shark erupts.
laneImpact: This interaction turns the laning phase into a passive survival challenge. You cannot walk up to collect Cosmic Creator stacks on the wave because Fizz will punish you with Chum the Waters. He will freeze the minions or dive you under your own turret, forcing you to forfeit early priority and gold. This pressure prevents you from helping your jungler, giving Fizz free reign to roam.
why: Fizz's Playful completely negates your primary defensive tool and ultimate, Falling Star. If you attempt to stun him or zone him out when he dives you, he simply hops into his untargetable state, rendering your impact useless. Once he bypasses your ultimate and lands directly on top of you, his Urchin Strike and Rending Wave will quickly shred your health bar before you can even channel Breath of Light.

summary: Thresh can use Flay (E) to interrupt Rell's crash down engage, completely neutralizing her primary teamfight initiation.
howToPlay: To survive and make plays, you must bait out Flay before committing your main leap. Use Full Tilt to speed up and threaten a flip, or walk up to shatter the shield of his Dark Passage with Shattering Strike. If he wastes Flay, that is your immediate green light to cast Ferromancy: Crashdown or Magnet Storm. If caught by Death Sentence, rely on Break the Mold defenses to survive while waiting for his sweep to go on cooldown.
laneImpact: Because Thresh can deny Ferromancy: Crashdown, you cannot freely contest the wave or force early trades. If you try to engage, a simple Flay followed by Death Sentence will turn the fight into a disaster. Your ADC will be forced to play defensively, giving up bush control to Thresh. You'll often find yourselves pushed under tower, where Thresh can fish for hooks or use Dark Passage to bring his jungler in safely.
why: Thresh holds all the cards in this engage dynamic because his Flay acts as a hard stop to your primary initiation tool, Ferromancy: Crashdown. If you attempt to jump in, a reactive Thresh can easily sweep you out of the air, leaving you dismounted, slow, and highly vulnerable without having landed your knock-up. This interaction shifts the pressure entirely onto you, forcing you to play around his reaction time.

summary: Vladimir has no hard crowd control to interrupt your Breath of Light, allowing you to freely channel it whenever he steps up to farm.
howToPlay: Watch Vladimir's resource bar closely; when his Transfusion is fully charged and red, step back slightly to deny his empowered heal. Once that window passes, immediately drop Singularity on the wave to trap him, then fly forward with Astral Flight while channeling Breath of Light to punish his retreat. If he panics and uses Sanguine Pool, do not chase; wait for him to emerge, then finish the trade with your superior range.
laneImpact: You dictate the wave's tempo from the first minute. By placing Singularity directly on the minion wave, you force Vladimir to choose between taking heavy damage from Breath of Light or burning Sanguine Pool, which costs him a massive portion of his current health. This pressure secures you permanent push priority, letting you crash waves at will, secure easy recall timings, and safely stack your passive.
why: This matchup is highly advantageous because Vladimir lacks any form of hard crowd control to interrupt your Breath of Light. While he relies on Transfusion to sustain and farm, he cannot stop you from channeling your main damage source directly onto him. This structural vulnerability completely neutralizes his early pressure, allowing you to harvest Cosmic Creator stacks rapidly while matching his scaling threat without any threat of being cancelled.

summary: Jax's Counter Strike blocks Ambessa's passive-empowered basic attacks, severely cutting her damage output and energy regeneration.
howToPlay: To survive his invades, you must discipline your passive usage. When Jax engages with Leap Strike, immediately use the dash from Drakehound's Step to kite backwards or sideways, refusing to attack while Counter Strike is active. Hold Repudiation to absorb his stun damage and block the crowd control. Once his helicopter spin ends, you have a brief window to strike back with Cunning Sweep and Lacerate, using Public Execution to finish him off only after his defensive cooldown is spent.
laneImpact: In the jungle, this interaction makes early river skirmishes and neutral camps highly dangerous. Jax can aggressively invade your territory, using Leap Strike to close the gap and forcing you to retreat. If you attempt to contest him, a well-timed Counter Strike negates your retaliation, leaving you with depleted energy and forcing you to yield scuttle crabs or give up pressure on adjacent lanes.
why: This matchup hinges on how Jax's Counter Strike completely shuts down Drakehound's Step. Ambessa’s entire combat loop relies on landing her passive-empowered basic attacks to deal burst damage and recover vital energy. When Jax activates his evasion, your empowered strikes from Cunning Sweep and Lacerate do zero damage and fail to restore your energy, leaving you completely starved of resources while setup for his stun.

summary: Graves can use Quickdraw to distance himself from Cunning Sweep while stacking armor, making him difficult for Ambessa to burst down.
howToPlay: To survive and turn the tides, never initiate with Cunning Sweep. Instead, walk up or use Lacerate to force him to panic-cast Quickdraw first. Keep your Repudiation active to absorb his high-impact burst from End of the Line or the blinding effect of Smoke Screen. If you fight near walls, position yourself so his returning powder keg doesn't detonate instantly, then lock him down with Public Execution only after his armor stacks decay.
laneImpact: This dynamic makes early jungle skirmishes highly dangerous for you, especially around the Scuttle Crabs. If Graves intercepts your clear, he can deploy Smoke Screen to disrupt your Drakehound's Step targeting. He will slowly chip away at your health bar, forcing you to concede camp priority or risk a fatal duel where his Collateral Damage executes you after you have wasted your gap-closers.
why: Graves holds a clear advantage because his Quickdraw allows him to effortlessly dash out of your Cunning Sweep sweet spot. By doing so, he not only avoids the devastating secondary slam but also stacks True Grit armor, mitigating your physical burst. His ranged basic attacks from New Destiny let him kite you down easily while you struggle to stick to him without your passive dashes.

summary: Samira's Blade Whirl can block all shots from Akshan's Heroic Swing and Comeuppance, completely neutralizing his burst window.
howToPlay: Treat this lane as a test of patience. Never initiate with Heroic Swing; instead, use your Dirty Fighting passive and Avengerang to chip away at her health from maximum range. Force her to use Blade Whirl defensively to block a returning Avengerang or a minion wave push. Only when you see that circular barrier expire do you have a brief five-second window to swing in or channel Comeuppance before she can protect herself again.
laneImpact: Because you cannot reliably trade with Heroic Swing, you lose the ability to easily force Samira off the wave. She can safely farm to stack Daredevil Impulse, using Flair to poke you while keeping Blade Whirl ready to block your Avengerang or physical trades. If you attempt an aggressive swing, she can easily counter-engage with Wild Rush, using your lack of escape to trigger Inferno Trigger and dive your turret.
why: Your entire burst potential relies on the rapid firing of Heroic Swing and the execute damage from Comeuppance. However, Samira holds a massive mechanical advantage because her Blade Whirl completely deletes every single projectile from both of these abilities. This single interaction nullifies your aggressive mobility and your ultimate, turning what should be your primary kill windows into empty, vulnerable animations while she builds her Daredevil Impulse.

summary: Shyvana relies on Dragon's Descent to engage, which makes her a perfect target for Amumu's Curse of the Sad Mummy.
howToPlay: To win, avoid forced teamfights and focus on counter-jungling his camps to quickly stack Fury of the Dragonborn. During skirmishes, never be the first to engage. Hold Dragon's Descent until Amumu expends Bandage Toss or commits Curse of the Sad Mummy on your front line. Use the movement speed of Burnout to bait and dodge his skillshots, then counter-attack with Flame Breath once his crowd control is down.
