laneImpact: Laning is a constant tug-of-war for priority. Ekko uses Timewinder to shove, forcing you to match with Tormented Shadow to avoid being pinned under tower. Trades are explosive; if Ekko fails to stun you inside his Parallel Convergence, he cannot easily escape your Dark Binding counter-attack. However, missing your root allows him to dive freely, forcing early recalls or securing him mid priority to roam.
why: This skill matchup revolves around your ability to nullify Ekko's setup. While your Black Shield completely negates the stun from his Parallel Convergence, it does not protect you from his rapid damage profile. If Ekko bypasses your shield's magic absorption with the raw physical and magic burst of his Phase Dive and Timewinder, his Z-Drive Resonance will still tear through your health bar.

summary: Lux can easily land Light Binding on you while you are stationary during your Breath of Light channel.
howToPlay: Never cast Light Binding proactively when Aurelion Sol has his mobility ready. Instead, walk forward to bait his Breath of Light or wait for him to initiate Astral Flight. The moment he channels, throw your root directly along his travel path. If you miss, immediately retreat and use Prismatic Barrier to mitigate his return fire while hiding behind your minions to avoid his cosmic breath.
laneImpact: The lane dynamic revolves around Aurelion Sol trying to gather Stardust using Singularity while you look to punish his lock-in animations. If you miss your root, his Breath of Light quickly melts the minion wave, forcing you under turret and letting him scale safely. Successful trades keep his health too low to roam with Astral Flight, turning the lane into a tense zoning war.
why: This matchup is a pure test of positioning, dictated by how you exploit Aurelion Sol's vulnerability. Whenever he stands still or flies in a straight line to channel Breath of Light, he becomes a sitting duck. This stationary window gives you the perfect opportunity to hit a guaranteed Light Binding, opening him up to your full burst with Lucent Singularity and Final Spark.

summary: Kayn can dodge Diana's Moonfall pull and burst by timing Umbral Trespass just as she activates her ultimate.
howToPlay: To win this mental game, never initiate a skirmish with Moonfall. Instead, engage with Crescent Strike and Lunar Rush, then trigger Pale Cascade to shield his initial Reaping Slash damage. Force Kayn to panic and use Umbral Trespass defensively to avoid your basic attacks. Once he emerges from your body, that is your cue to immediately cast your ultimate to lock him down and finish him before he can slide away.
laneImpact: Because both of you clear camps incredibly fast using Pale Cascade and Reaping Slash, this matchup becomes a high-speed tempo battle. Neither jungler can easily force a direct duel without risking a counter-gank. Skirmishes around neutral objectives are decided entirely by who gets their transformation or ultimate spike first. If you waste your crowd control early, Kayn easily escapes through walls using Shadow Step.
why: This jungle matchup is a pure race of timing centered around your ultimate. While your standard Crescent Strike into Lunar Rush combo delivers fast burst, Kayn holds a massive defensive trump card. The moment you pull him in with Moonfall, he can reactively cast Umbral Trespass to infest you. This completely dodges your ultimate's damage and displacement, leaving you vulnerable while he waits inside you.

summary: Lux outranges Nami's Ebb and Flow with Lucent Singularity, but must dodge Aqua Prison to avoid being turned on during trades.
howToPlay: Maximize your spacing by casting Lucent Singularity at its absolute maximum range to deny Nami any chance of bouncing Ebb and Flow onto you. Never walk forward to trigger your Illumination passive with an auto-attack unless you have actively baited out and dodged her Aqua Prison. If she attempts to force an engagement using Tidal Wave, immediately retaliate with Light Binding to lock down her ADC and cushion the assault with Prismatic Barrier.
laneImpact: Every trade determines who controls the minion waves. When you successfully land Lucent Singularity while avoiding retaliatory poke, you force Nami to waste mana on Ebb and Flow heals rather than aggressive pushes. But if you get caught by Aqua Prison, Nami's Surging Tides will let her ADC collapse on you instantly, stripping away your lane priority and forcing a defensive recall.
why: This matchup is a pure battle of ranges and reflexes. You have a distinct advantage with Lucent Singularity, which easily outranges Nami's Ebb and Flow, letting you poke her safely. However, if you step up too predictably to pop Illumination, Nami can catch you with Aqua Prison. This bubble completely disables you, allowing her to heal back your damage and turn the trade.

summary: Zyra's Grasping Roots can catch Alistar as he walks up, and her Stranglethorns completely disrupts his teamfight engage.
howToPlay: To survive, never walk in a straight line toward Zyra; instead, position behind your minion wave to force her to choose between pushing or poking. Hold your Unbreakable Will specifically to cleanse the root from Grasping Roots or the knock-up from Stranglethorns if you get caught. If the lane becomes unplayable, stop trying to engage on her and look to flash-engage on the enemy ADC only when her plants are dormant.
laneImpact: This constant threat forces you to play defensively under your own turret. Zyra's Deadly Spines combined with Rampant Growth seeds constantly pushes the wave and chips away your health, making positive trades impossible. You're forced into early, unfavorable recalls, which deprives your marksman of protection and allows Zyra to secure deep river vision, leaving your mid laner vulnerable to unchecked rotations.
why: Zyra completely shuts down Alistar's proactive play. Whenever you try to walk forward to set up a Headbutt into Pulverize combo, Zyra can easily react with Grasping Roots to root you in place while her Garden of Thorns plants chew through your health. Even if you manage to dive in, her Stranglethorns creates a massive zone that knocks you up and completely ruins your team's follow-up.

summary: Kayle lacks any early crowd control or kill pressure, allowing you to safely stack Stardust with Singularity and outscale her mid-game impact.
howToPlay: Focus entirely on grouping the minion waves. Place Singularity on the caster minions as they arrive, then immediately melt them with Breath of Light to farm Stardust safely. If she steps forward to poke with Radiant Blast, do not panic; simply activate Astral Flight backward to reset your spacing. Never trade when her Divine Judgment is active; wait out its invulnerability before committing Falling Star.
laneImpact: This matchup turns the mid lane into a free-farming zone where you dictate the tempo. Kayle is forced to rely on Starfire Spellblade to secure individual last hits under her turret. By keeping the wave pushed with Singularity, you deny her any roaming potential and force her to burn mana on Celestial Blessing to sustain, securing your priority without sacrificing health.
why: Kayle's complete lack of early crowd control or burst threat removes any danger when you channel Breath of Light. Because her Divine Ascent keeps her weak and melee-range initially, she cannot contest your wave positioning. You can drop Singularity directly on the minions without fear of a Radiant Blast slow turning into a lethal chase, allowing you to accumulate Cosmic Creator stacks rapidly.

summary: Vladimir can cast Sanguine Pool when Zed initiates Death Mark, completely wasting Zed's ultimate cooldown.
howToPlay: Always hold Sanguine Pool specifically for Zed's Death Mark; never use it to dodge basic Razor Shuriken poke or to clear waves. Stand comfortably near your minions to bait his engage. If he steps forward and activates his ultimate, wait for his shadow to appear before pooling. If you mistakenly waste your pool, immediately retreat under your tower and use Crimson Pact's health pool to buffer his burst until it returns.
laneImpact: This interaction shifts all wave priority to your side. Since Zed cannot safely execute his all-in, he is forced to use Razor Shuriken and Living Shadow to farm from a distance, draining his energy and preventing him from roaming. You can freely slow-push waves, harass him under his turret with Tides of Blood, and build a massive gold lead while keeping him locked in the mid lane.
why: Vladimir completely dictates the pace of this matchup because of how Sanguine Pool interacts with Death Mark. The moment Zed commits his ultimate to dive or burst you, entering your pool makes you untargetable, entirely canceling the application of his mark and wasting his longest cooldown. Without his ultimate threat, Zed's melee nature makes him highly vulnerable to Transfusion poke every time he walks up to farm.

summary: Poppy's Steadfast Presence blocks Vayne's Tumble, meaning Vayne must hold her dash until Poppy's defensive aura expires.
howToPlay: Never activate Steadfast Presence proactively; wait until Vayne actually initiates the animation of Tumble or attempts to escape a trade. Use the extra range from Iron Ambassador to secure minions from a safe distance and pick up the buckler shield to absorb her basic attacks. If she mispositions near the alcove or terrain, punish her immediately with Heroic Charge to wall-stun her, then use Hammer Shock to chunk her down before she can cast Condemn.
laneImpact: The lane becomes a psychological standoff near the walls. Vayne will try to bait out your defensive aura with basic attacks to safely trigger Silver Bolts. If you waste your anti-dash, she can freely space you down with Final Hour and Tumble. However, as long as you hold your grounding field, she must farm cautiously, preventing her from aggressively pushing you under tower or securing easy plates.
why: This skill-reliant matchup revolves entirely around the interaction between your Steadfast Presence and Vayne's Tumble. Because your active aura grounds her and stops her short roll, Vayne is forced to play defensively and hold her mobility spell until your defensive shield dissipates. Without her quick repositioning tool, her reliance on Silver Bolts is severely hindered, allowing you to control the immediate space around you.

summary: Irelia can use Bladesurge to dash behind Pantheon when he casts Aegis Assault, bypassing his frontal damage immunity.
howToPlay: Never initiate trades with Aegis Assault. Instead, chip her down with quick taps of Comet Spear when she goes to last-hit. Hold Shield Vault to lock her down the moment she attempts to stack Ionian Fervor on low-health minions. If she casts Flawless Duet, step laterally to dodge the stun. Only activate Aegis Assault after she has exhausted her Bladesurge charges, ensuring she cannot easily reposition to your vulnerable back.
laneImpact: Every trade in this lane determines wave priority and dive potential. If you waste Aegis Assault, Irelia will immediately dash behind you, shred your health bar, and slow you with Vanguard's Edge to force a recall or secure a kill under tower. Conversely, interrupting her Bladesurge resets with a well-timed Shield Vault prevents her from stacking her passive, stopping her from crashing massive minion waves.
why: This skill matchup revolves around how you mitigate each other's burst. Your primary defense, Aegis Assault, is completely bypassed if Irelia uses the mobility of Bladesurge to dash directly behind you, rendering your frontal shield useless. Since her Ionian Fervor grants her massive basic attack damage once fully stacked, getting caught with your shield facing the wrong way during her onslaught means losing the trade instantly.

summary: Samira can completely block Enchanted Crystal Arrow with Blade Whirl, leaving you defenseless against her Wild Rush all-in.
howToPlay: Never initiate with Enchanted Crystal Arrow while her Blade Whirl is available. Instead, use Volley to poke from absolute maximum range and force her to play defensively. If she wastes her defensive circle, that is your twenty-second opening to strike. If she dashes in with Wild Rush, fire your ultimate point-blank only after her defensive spin ends, then activate Ranger's Focus to kite backward using the slow from Frost Shot.
laneImpact: Because she can erase your ultimate, you cannot play aggressively or hold the wave near her tower. You are forced to play defensively, as any extended trade where you use Volley can be negated. She will slow-push waves to force you under tower, knowing that if you try to retaliate, a quick Wild Rush over your front line will lead to a lethal dive or a forced recall.
why: This lane is dictated by a massive defensive mismatch. Your ultimate tool for self-peel and initiation, Enchanted Crystal Arrow, is completely neutralized by Samira's Blade Whirl. Once she deletes your arrow, you lose your primary crowd control, allowing her to immediately close the distance with Wild Rush. Without your stun, you cannot stop her from stacking Daredevil Impulse and tearing you apart with Inferno Trigger.

summary: Jax's Counter Strike blocks the damage and knockback of Devastating Charge, leaving Hecarim stunned and unable to stack Rampage.
howToPlay: Do not waste your Counter Strike early when clearing or starting a skirmish. Wait for the audio or visual cue of Hecarim's Devastating Charge running towards you. Activate it right before impact to stun him, then immediately follow up with Leap Strike and Empower to chunk his health. If he uses Onslaught of Shadows to escape or turn, activate Grandmaster-at-Arms to survive the fear duration and beat him down with your fully stacked Relentless Assault.
laneImpact: In the jungle, this interaction shifts the power dynamic heavily during skirmishes and crab contests. Hecarim relies on his fast clear and ganking speed, but he cannot contest you directly in the river. If he tries to invade or fight for objectives, your ability to deny his main engage tool forces him to play passively. You can easily invade his camps, knowing his dueling potential is completely crippled once his main cooldown is wasted.
why: Jax outscales Hecarim significantly, but the duel is won directly through a single interaction. When Hecarim attempts to engage with his high-speed Devastating Charge, Jax can activate Counter Strike. This entirely negates both the burst damage and the knockback of the charge. Without this initial impact, Hecarim cannot effectively build his Rampage stacks, leaving him vulnerable to Jax's superior sustained DPS.

summary: Morgana's Black Shield (E) completely negates the stun from CH-2 Electron Storm Grenade (E), preventing Heimerdinger's burst setup.
howToPlay: To break the stalemate, you must bait out Black Shield using raw damage before throwing your crowd control. Position your H-28G Evolution Turret units in a wider triangle rather than a tight cluster to prevent a single Tormented Shadow from melting them all. If she holds her shield, do not throw CH-2 Electron Storm Grenade; instead, use Hextech Micro-Rockets to chip her down. If the shield breaks, immediately unleash UPGRADE!!! for maximum burst.
laneImpact: This interaction creates a heavy lane stall where neither side can easily force a recall or dive. Morgana clears your H-28G Evolution Turret setups from afar using Tormented Shadow, while you easily match her push with your own mechanical army. Neither mid laner can reliably lock down the other, meaning the lane remains locked in a perpetual state of shoving waves back and forth with minimal kill pressure.
why: The neutral state of this matchup stems from how Black Shield nullifies your primary offensive threat. Whenever you attempt to set up a burst combo using CH-2 Electron Storm Grenade, Morgana can reactively absorb the stun. Without this crowd control, your H-28G Evolution Turret laser beams won't trigger automatically, reducing your offensive threat. Since Morgana recovers health via Soul Siphon, random poke without a stun setup fails to stick.

summary: Garen's Judgment shreds Shen's armor and pushes waves rapidly, punishing Shen whenever he leaves the lane with Stand United.
howToPlay: To survive, trigger Ki Barrier frequently by pulling your blade with Twilight Assault through him to slow his retreat. Save Shadow Dash to disengage the moment he starts spinning with Judgment, rather than using it to initiate trades. Only cast Stand United when your wave is fully pushed out or if the global play guarantees a massive objective cross-map to compensate for the guaranteed loss of your turret plates.
laneImpact: You are constantly forced into a defensive posture under your own turret because Garen's wave clear outmatches yours. Trading directly with him is dangerous; if he shreds your armor, his Demacian Justice becomes a lethal threat. The real punishment occurs when your teammates need aid. Channeling Stand United means conceding multiple plates or even your entire outer turret to Garen's relentless push.
why: The lane hinges on how Garen's Judgment interacts with your kit. While your Spirit's Refuge blocks his Decisive Strike silence, it does nothing to stop the spinning damage of Judgment. Furthermore, Judgment shreds your armor while rapidly clearing the wave. This means Garen can easily shove you under turret, and if you leave with Stand United, he will immediately demolish your tower.

summary: Braum's Unbreakable can block Galio's Winds of War, but it cannot stop the AoE taunt of Shield of Durand.
howToPlay: Focus your Winter's Bite on Galio's carry rather than Galio himself, as his Shield of Durand makes him too tanky to burst down. Save Stand Behind Me to quickly disengage your ally if Galio lands a Justice Punch. If he channels his taunt, do not use Unbreakable immediately; instead, hold it to block the inevitable Winds of War that follows his crowd control, ensuring your carry survives the burst.
laneImpact: Because both supports possess excellent defensive tools, outright kills are rare without external intervention. When Galio steps up with Justice Punch to initiate, you can counter-engage with Concussive Blows on his ADC. However, if he uses Shield of Durand to disrupt your passive stacking, the trade stalls out. This turns the lane into a slow battle of attrition where mistake-free positioning prevents dives under your tower.
why: This matchup is a pure contest of defensive disruption where your shield placement is tested against his area control. While your Unbreakable completely nullifies the damage from Galio's Winds of War, it is entirely useless against the magic damage reduction and massive area-of-effect taunt of Shield of Durand. This creates a tense standoff where both of you excel at protecting your ADCs, turning every skirmish into a battle of target focus.

summary: Mordekaiser can use Death's Grasp to pull Tryndamere away and kite out the duration of Undying Rage inside the Realm of Death.
howToPlay: Never initiate with Spinning Slash if Mordekaiser has Death's Grasp ready. Instead, walk up to trade, using Mocking Shout when he turns to retreat to lower his AD. Save Spinning Slash exclusively to close the gap after he attempts to pull you away during Undying Rage. If he drags you into the Realm of Death, hug the outer boundary to limit his kiting angles and force a close-quarters brawl where your critical strikes dominate.
laneImpact: Trades revolve around your positioning relative to your minion wave. If Mordekaiser misses Obliterate on you while hitting minions, he pushes the wave, giving you a chance to stack Battle Fury. If you get caught in the open, his Darkness Rise aura will burn your health down, forcing you to use Bloodlust early and giving up your pressure, which allows him to secure free recalls.
why: This matchup is a tight race of timing and positioning. When you trigger Undying Rage, Mordekaiser wants to drag you into his Realm of Death. Once inside, he uses Death's Grasp not to engage, but to pull you away, keeping you at a distance to waste your precious seconds of invulnerability. Your Battle Fury gives you the damage to melt him, but only if he cannot isolate and kite you.

summary: Wukong can use Warrior Trickster to absorb Viego's Spectral Maw stun, leaving Viego vulnerable to a Cyclone follow-up.
howToPlay: Never initiate a skirmish using Warrior Trickster. Instead, close the gap using Nimbus Strike and rely on basic attacks to force Viego's hand. Hold your clone until you see the charging animation of Spectral Maw. The moment he releases the projectile, press your decoy to block the stun, then immediately follow up with Cyclone to knock him up. If he manages to stun you first, delay your Cyclone until his passive marks fade.
laneImpact: In the jungle, this interaction dictates how early skirmishes around the Scuttle Crabs and Epic Monsters play out. Because you win the direct duel whenever your decoy is available, Viego is forced to play passively within his Harrowed Path mist. He cannot contest the river freely, meaning you easily secure early map priority and force him to rely on defensive farming.
why: Wukong dominates this jungle matchup because Warrior Trickster completely neutralizes Viego's only reliable crowd control, Spectral Maw. When Viego charges his mist dash to lock you down, dropping your decoy absorbs the projectile entirely. Lacking this crucial stun, Viego cannot safely land Heartbreaker or easily apply his Blade of the Ruined King marks, leaving him highly vulnerable to your high-damage counter-engagement.

summary: Aurora can easily bait out and dodge Lux's Light Binding (Q) using the brief stealth and leap of Across the Veil (W).
howToPlay: To survive, you must absolutely hoard Light Binding like a precious resource, never casting it proactively. Instead, use the slow from Lucent Singularity to harass her and control her movement. If Aurora attempts to close the gap with Across the Veil, retreat immediately under the safety of Prismatic Barrier to absorb the incoming burst. Only throw your root when she is locked in the casting animation of The Weirding or after she has already wasted her leap.
laneImpact: This interaction forces you onto the defensive, stripping away your ability to contest the minion wave directly. Knowing she can dodge your root, Aurora will aggressively zone you with Twofold Hex, aiming to trigger Spirit Abjuration. You are forced to farm from extreme range using Lucent Singularity, which drains your mana rapidly and prevents you from securing mid priority or assisting your jungler in the river.
why: The core of this matchup lies in how easily Aurora can bait and neutralize your primary self-defense. Whenever you throw out Light Binding, she can instantly react with Across the Veil, using the brief stealth and leap to completely bypass the projectile. Because Lux relies entirely on landing that root to set up her full burst, this single interactive tool allows Aurora to turn any trade in her favor.

summary: Zoe can easily fish for Sleepy Trouble Bubble through walls and follow up with a lethal Paddle Star! while Teemo is asleep.
howToPlay: Never stand in a straight line between the lane walls and the minion wave; always keep a thick wall of minions between you and Zoe to block Sleepy Trouble Bubble. Activate Move Quick immediately if you see her projectile coming to sidestep it. If you do get hit, quickly retreat toward your tower or into your own Noxious Trap field before sleeping, forcing Zoe to walk into a slow if she attempts to close the distance.
laneImpact: You are constantly forced into defensive, predictable farming near your turret. Zoe uses her superior range to pressure the wave, while you must constantly weave behind minions to block her bubble. This passive stance forfeits your midlane priority, meaning your jungler loses crucial support in the river, and Zoe can easily roam or secure spell fragments with Spell Thief.
why: Zoe outranges Teemo drastically, turning this midlane into a deadly zone. She relies on launching Sleepy Trouble Bubble from behind the jungle walls, catching you off guard. Once you are drowsy and eventually asleep, she easily redirects a long-range Paddle Star! combined with a More Sparkles! empowered auto-attack, chunking your health bar before you can even retaliate with Blinding Dart.

summary: Vladimir can use Sanguine Pool to dodge Ahri's Charm, neutralizing her burst while healing back any poke with Transfusion.
howToPlay: To survive this matchup, you must hold Charm as a defensive deterrent rather than using it to initiate. Force him to use Sanguine Pool by threatening him with Orb of Deception and Fox-Fire first. Keep the minion wave close to your side of the lane to deny him easy Transfusion targets. If he overextends without his pool, use Spirit Rush to quickly reposition and burst him down.
laneImpact: Since you cannot easily burst him, the lane devolves into a grueling test of wave management. If you blindly push with Orb of Deception, you feed his safe farming under tower. Meanwhile, taking short trades against his empowered Transfusion slowly chips away at your health, forcing bad recall timings and leaving your tower vulnerable while he scales into a massive threat.
why: Vladimir completely nullifies your kill pressure because any attempt to lock him down with Charm is met with Sanguine Pool, making him untargetable and wasting your crowd control. Even if you land Orb of Deception or Fox-Fire for trade damage, his Transfusion allows him to constantly drain your health and replenish his own, winning the battle of attrition.

summary: Master Yi can use Alpha Strike to dodge the knockup of Dragon Strike, but cannot escape Cataclysm without Flash.
howToPlay: When ganking or dueling Yi, do not lead with your Demacian Standard and Dragon Strike combo. Instead, walk up and slow him with Golden Aegis to force out his Alpha Strike. Once he reappears, immediately drop Cataclysm to trap him. If he tries to channel Meditate inside your arena, use your knockup combo to disrupt his healing and armor shred him for your team to finish off.
laneImpact: This interaction shifts the early skirmishes and jungle duels heavily in your favor. Yi cannot safely contest scuttle crabs or invade your camps because you can always threaten to lock him down. His ganking pressure is severely neutered since your ultimate forces him into static fights where his Highlander speed is useless, allowing your lanes to play aggressively knowing you can trap him.
why: Jarvan IV dominates Master Yi by forcing him into a deadly guessing game. While Yi can use the untargetability of Alpha Strike to completely bypass the knockup of Jarvan's Demacian Standard and Dragon Strike combo, he has absolutely no response to Cataclysm once his Flash is down. The impassable arena forces Yi to either waste Meditate defensively or die inside the ring.

summary: Galio's Shield of Durand (W) magic shield and damage reduction heavily mitigate Syndra's Unleashed Power (R) burst, allowing him to survive her full combo.
howToPlay: Focus on chipping away at him rather than looking for a single burst rotation. Only cast Unleashed Power when Shield of Durand is on its long cooldown or if he has already committed it to mitigate a trade. Hold Scatter the Weak to interrupt his Justice Punch mid-dash; reacting quickly to his forward movement is your primary defensive safety net. If he walks up to taunt you, use Force of Will to slow him down and safely walk backward.
laneImpact: You cannot easily threaten to solo-kill Galio, meaning he can confidently use Winds of War to contest your wave clear. If you use Scatter the Weak aggressively, he will immediately look to punish you with Justice Punch and Colossal Smash. Furthermore, your inability to burst him down allows him to roam freely with Hero's Entrance, forcing you to constantly decide between matching his high-pressure map rotations or securing plates.
why: Galio directly counters your burst-heavy identity. His passive magic shield from Shield of Durand absorbs your poke, while its active damage reduction completely neutralizes your Unleashed Power execution threshold. Even if you land a full stun combo with Dark Sphere and Scatter the Weak, he can channel his damage reduction to survive the final ultimate onslaught, leaving you vulnerable with your main damage tool on cooldown.

summary: Kayn uses Shadow Step to bypass Darius's jungle pressure, but Darius wins extended fights if he lands Decimate on Kayn's Reaping Slash.
howToPlay: Never initiate a fight by throwing out Apprehend blindly. Save this pull to drag Kayn back when he attempts to escape through a wall with Shadow Step or immediately after he finishes his Reaping Slash dash. When he infects you with Umbral Trespass, charge your Decimate the split-second he emerges to guarantee the outer-edge heal. Use Crippling Strike to reset your attacks and stack Hemorrhage before he can react.
laneImpact: Kayn's ability to slip through walls forces you to constantly secure your jungle entrances. He will attempt to steal your raptors or krugs and escape before you can react. If you catch him in your jungle without his terrain walk, you can trap him. Forcing an early Umbral Trespass or a clean kill drastically reduces his form transformation speed, keeping your lanes safe.
why: This jungle matchup is a constant test of tracking. Kayn relies on Shadow Step to phase through terrain, allowing him to bypass your direct pressure and steal camps. However, when forced into a direct duel, his Reaping Slash brings him right into your preferred range. If you manage to space correctly and strike him with the outer edge of Decimate during his dash, Hemorrhage will quickly overwhelm him.

summary: Pull Renekton with Apprehend when he tries to use his second Slice and Dice dash to escape after a short trade.
howToPlay: Never waste Apprehend to initiate. Walk up to last-hit and bait his forward dash. When Renekton strikes with Ruthless Predator and attempts to dash away using his second Slice and Dice, cast Apprehend to drag him back. Immediately follow up with Crippling Strike to slow him down, then spin with Decimate to heal while stacking Hemorrhage. If he activates Dominus, do not panic; stack your passive and execute him with Noxian Guillotine once he is low.
laneImpact: This dynamic forces Renekton to play incredibly passively, as he cannot safely step up to generate Fury with Reign of Anger. If he tries to thin the wave with Cull the Meek, he exposes himself to a deadly freeze. You can easily hold the wave near your tower, denying him the space needed to utilize Slice and Dice safely. Any attempt he makes to trade will cost him massive health bars or his Flash.
why: Renekton relies on quick, bursty trades by dashing in, stunning you, and dashing away. However, his power budget is heavily tied to his Fury-empowered Ruthless Predator and Cull the Meek. Once those are spent, he has no sustained damage. By interrupting his escape dash, Slice and Dice, with your Apprehend, you prevent him from retreating, forcing him into a prolonged brawl where your Hemorrhage stacks will easily overwhelm him.

summary: Wukong can use Warrior Trickster to spawn a clone, instantly breaking his isolation status and absorbing Kha'Zix's Taste Their Fear.
howToPlay: Never initiate a skirmish with Warrior Trickster; instead, use Nimbus Strike to close the gap and Golden Staff to shred his armor. Save your clone exclusively for the moment Kha'Zix uses Leap or tries to strike with Taste Their Fear. If he attempts to escape using Void Assault, immediately activate Cyclone to knock him out of his stealth or zone him away from your low-health allies, turning his sneaky retreats into easy multi-knockup setups.
laneImpact: Your safety in the jungle completely alters the early game dynamic, allowing you to contest both Scuttle Crabs and invade his camps without fearing his isolation damage. Because Kha'Zix cannot reliably burst you down, he is forced to concede river control and early neutral objectives. This security enables you to pressure his jungle camps safely, knowing that any face-to-face duel in the river will skew heavily in your favor.
why: This matchup heavily favors you because Warrior Trickster completely negates Kha'Zix's primary source of burst. By summoning your clone right as he leaps in, you instantly break your isolation status and force his Taste Their Fear to target the decoy or deal significantly reduced damage. Additionally, your Stone Skin passive actively stacks up armor during these sudden duels, rendering his physical lethality useless while you shred him in return.

summary: Annie can hold her Pyromania stun to instantly stop your Heroic Swing with a point-and-click Disintegrate.
howToPlay: Always sit on three Pyromania stacks, using Molten Shield to instantly prime the stun whenever Akshan steps forward. Never throw your stun raw at him while his Heroic Swing is up; instead, wait for him to attach his grapple to a wall, then cast Disintegrate mid-flight. If he plays passively to avoid this, force trades with Molten Shield's speed boost to land an Incinerate, saving Summon: Tibbers to crush him if he panics and tries to swing away.
laneImpact: This threat completely paralyzes Akshan's aggressive laning. He cannot freely use Heroic Swing to clear waves or trade, allowing you to easily manage the lane with Disintegrate last-hits. Since he cannot safely slide in to trigger Dirty Fighting's shield, you hold constant health priority. If he tries to roam using Going Rogue, your burst potential keeps him pinned under his own turret.
why: Annie dictates this lane because Akshan relies heavily on Heroic Swing for both mobility and trading power. By saving your Pyromania charge, you create an absolute zoning tool. If Akshan attempts to swing around a wall, a point-and-click Disintegrate instantly cancels his movement mid-air, leaving him completely vulnerable to a follow-up Incinerate and Summon: Tibbers burst.

summary: Camille can freely poke Nasus with Tactical Sweep and interrupt his farm, but must avoid long chases once hit by Wither.
howToPlay: Position yourself near your dying minions and charge Precision Protocol the moment Nasus approaches. If he targets you with Wither, immediately back off using the movement speed from Precision Protocol or buffer his slow by latching to a wall with Hookshot. Never chase him deep into his wave when slowed. If you accidentally push the wave, use Tactical Sweep to secure a fast crash, then reset to prevent him from freezing.
laneImpact: This matchup is won through strict wave control. By keeping the minions frozen near your turret, you force Nasus to walk up into the threat zone of Hookshot. Every time he steps forward to last-hit with Siphoning Strike, you can punish him. This prevents him from scaling, starves his passive sustain, and makes him vulnerable to dives with The Hextech Ultimatum if he drops too low under his own tower.
why: Camille dominates the early game because her Tactical Sweep constantly chips away at Nasus's health from safety, preventing him from freely stacking Siphoning Strike. Since Nasus relies on Soul Eater to sustain, keeping him away from the wave with your range advantage is key. Even if he tries to trade back, Adaptive Defenses absorbs his physical damage, rendering his retaliation useless unless he slows you with Wither to force an extended fight.

summary: Diana's Pale Cascade shield absorbs Akali's burst, allowing Diana to win extended trades with her passive.
howToPlay: To survive and win, you must discipline your trading patterns. Never commit your Shuriken Flip while Diana has her Pale Cascade available. Instead, bait her shield by walking up as if to strike, then immediately retreat. If she activates it, deploy Twilight Shroud to hide and let the shield decay naturally. Only execute your full Perfect Execution burst once her defensive orbs are gone and she cannot retaliate with her Moonsilver Blade passive.
laneImpact: This dynamic forces you into a defensive posture where you cannot freely contest the wave. If you step up to execute minions, Diana will look to clip you with Crescent Strike and initiate a heavy trade. You will often find yourself pushed under turret, forced to use Five Point Strike defensively to secure farm, which limits your roaming potential and delays your mid-game power spikes.
why: Diana dominates short trades because her Pale Cascade shield perfectly absorbs the initial burst of your Five Point Strike and Assassin's Mark combo. Once your energy is depleted and your shroud is down, she excels in extended duels. Her Moonsilver Blade passive grants her massive attack speed and extra magic damage on every third strike, allowing her to easily out-damage you if you linger in melee range.

summary: Miss Fortune's Make It Rain easily reveals or slows Twitch if he tries to use Ambush to escape or engage in lane.
howToPlay: Never cast Make It Rain mindlessly for simple wave clear. Keep this ability ready as your primary tool to respond to Twitch's displacement. If you see the poison indicator from Venom Cask or suspect he is preparing Ambush, drop your rain on his escape path. Once he is slowed and revealed, activate Strut to quickly close the gap and land an empowered auto-attack, forcing him to waste his summoner spells or die under a fully channeled Bullet Time.
laneImpact: You command complete control over the wave state from the very first level. By securing a push advantage with Love Tap, you force Twitch to farm under tower where your Double Up bounces off dying minions to chunk his health. He cannot walk up to thin the wave because a well-placed Make It Rain will leave him slowed and vulnerable to a devastating Bullet Time channel if he steps out of line.
why: Twitch relies on the stealth of Ambush to reposition or escape your harass, but your Make It Rain completely shuts this down. Because Make It Rain applies a massive, instant area-of-effect slow that ticks frequently, it renders his Ambush useless by revealing his position or delaying his stealth. This leaves the plague rat exposed to your heavy physical damage from Double Up and Love Tap before he can even retaliate with Contaminate.

summary: Sona's extremely low base health makes her an easy target for Pyke's Bone Skewer and Phantom Undertow combo before she can scale.
howToPlay: To survive, you must constantly position behind your minion wave to block Bone Skewer. Keep the bushes warded to track Ghostwater Dive. Never use Song of Celerity aggressively; save its movement speed boost to dodge incoming hooks. If Pyke misses Bone Skewer, you have a brief fifteen-second window to harass him with Hymn of Valor. Once he reaches level five, prepare to use Crescendo to interrupt his Phantom Undertow dash.
laneImpact: This threat forces Sona to play extremely defensively, conceding early lane pressure and bush control. Sona cannot safely walk up to poke with Hymn of Valor, as stepping past her minion wave exposes her to Bone Skewer. Consequently, your ADC will often be shoved under turret, facing dive pressure once Pyke unlocks Death from Below, while Pyke freely roams the map using Ghostwater Dive.
why: Sona's fragile health pool makes her incredibly vulnerable during the early levels. If Pyke lands Bone Skewer, the forced displacement combined with Phantom Undertow's follow-up stun will reliably burst Sona down before she can react. Even with Aria of Perseverance, Sona lacks the defensive stats to survive this physical damage onslaught, meaning any positioning error results in an immediate death.

summary: Vladimir can use Sanguine Pool to sink into the ground, dodging both the knockup of E-Q and the burst damage of Cataclysm.
howToPlay: Keep Sanguine Pool strictly on standby; never waste it for wave clear or casual trades. Only activate it the moment Jarvan IV commits to his Demacian Standard and Dragon Strike dive, or when he leaps into the air for Cataclysm. Once he misses his knockup, immediately retaliate with Transfusion and Tides of Blood. If his health is low, initiate your all-in by dropping Hemoplague to amplify your counter-offensive and secure an easy dive.
laneImpact: This interaction strips Jarvan IV of his lane dominance. He cannot poke you down with Dragon Strike because Transfusion easily recovers your health. Because he cannot lock you down with Cataclysm, his jungle setups fail, allowing you to freely control the wave. You will slowly bleed him out under his tower, turning the lane into a free scaling avenue where you easily build an insurmountable gold lead.
why: Vladimir naturally outscales Jarvan IV, but the matchup is truly decided by how easily Sanguine Pool shuts down the Demacian's engage. By timing this pool, you can completely phase through the knockup of the Demacian Standard and Dragon Strike combo, while also negating the burst damage of Cataclysm. Without these tools landing, Jarvan IV cannot match your late-game power.

summary: Aurora's slippery Across the Veil is completely neutralized by Annie's point-and-click Disintegrate stun.
howToPlay: To survive, track the swirling fire of Pyromania constantly. Only initiate short trades with Twofold Hex and The Weirding when she has zero or one stack, or immediately after she uses Disintegrate to last-hit a minion. If she holds her stun indefinitely, use The Weirding from maximum range to farm safely. If she triggers her stun on you, immediately drop Between Worlds to hop away and delay her Tibbers follow-up.
laneImpact: You are forced into a passive laning phase where trading is incredibly risky. You cannot safely trigger Spirit Abjuration because stepping forward to land Twofold Hex invites a Disintegrate stun. Annie will comfortably zone you, using Molten Shield to absorb your poke while threatening an all-in. If she freezes near her tower, you cannot walk up to break it without risking a lethal Summon: Tibbers combo.
why: This matchup is highly unfavorable because your main defensive tool, Across the Veil, cannot save you from Annie's targeted lockdown. When her Pyromania passive is fully charged, her Disintegrate becomes a point-and-click stun that ignores your brief invisibility entirely. Since Disintegrate is not a skillshot, you cannot outplay it with your mobility, leaving you completely exposed to an immediate follow-up from Incinerate or Summon: Tibbers.

summary: Aatrox must use Umbral Dash backwards to escape Darius's Decimate inner circle and prevent Hemorrhage stacks.
howToPlay: To win this positioning duel, never lead your trades with Decimate. Instead, walk up to threaten him with basic attacks and Crippling Strike. Force Aatrox to panic-cast Umbral Dash defensively to escape. The moment he commits his dash backward, immediately use Apprehend to drag him back into your melee range, ensuring your axe sweep connects perfectly. If you miss your pull while his dash is up, immediately retreat to avoid his sweetspots.
laneImpact: Neither juggernaut can easily freeze the wave without risking a lethal trade. If Aatrox baits out your Decimate and dashes away, he immediately gains lane priority, using Infernal Chains to lock you down for a full combo. Conversely, if you catch him mid-dash with Apprehend, you pull him into close quarters where your Crippling Strike guarantees five stacks, forcing him to surrender tower pressure or face Noxian Guillotine.
why: This matchup is a pure battle of micro-spacing where every trade hinges on a crucial movement interaction. Darius relies on hitting the outer edge of Decimate to sustain and quickly stack Hemorrhage. To deny this, Aatrox constantly holds Umbral Dash to slip backward out of your axe's reach. If he successfully dodges the blade, you lose both your healing and your passive momentum, leaving you vulnerable to The Darkin Blade counter-attacks.

summary: Draven's Stand Aside can interrupt Corki's Valkyrie mid-flight, leaving him stranded and exposed to massive Spinning Axe damage.
howToPlay: To survive, you must hold your Valkyrie strictly for defense, using it only after Draven has wasted Stand Aside or to dodge his global Whirling Death. Farm safely from afar using the long range of Missile Barrage once you hit level five. If he freezes the wave near his tower, do not walk up; instead, wait for the wave to bounce back, prioritizing experience over gold.
laneImpact: This constant threat forces you to concede early wave control, as stepping up to use Gatling Gun or Phosphorus Bomb invites a devastating trade. Draven will freeze the wave to deny you gold, or crash it to dive you with Whirling Death. You must accept losing minion gold under tower, focusing purely on surviving to prevent him from cashing in his League of Draven stacks.
why: Draven dominates this lane because his Stand Aside completely cancels Corki's Valkyrie mid-dash. If you attempt to escape his aggressive Spinning Axe trades, a well-timed displacement leaves you grounded and vulnerable. Without your primary mobility tool, Draven's Blood Rush allows him to run you down easily, turning your only defensive tool into a deadly trap.

summary: While Seraphine can match Taliyah's waveclear with High Note, she cannot match the map pressure generated by Weaver's Wall.
howToPlay: Never attempt to follow Taliyah blindly through the river when she activates Weaver's Wall, as she can easily turn and catch you with Seismic Shove into Unraveled Earth. Instead, hold your Beat Drop to safely clear remaining minions from a distance. The moment she roams, ping missing immediately, use your High Note echo to hard-shove the wave into her turret, and look to secure local plating.
laneImpact: The laning phase becomes a race against the clock. Since Taliyah wants to shove with Threaded Volley and roam, you are forced to constantly use Stage Presence boosted High Note casts to prevent her from locking you under turret. If you fail to match her push, she will disappear into the fog of war. This forces your side lanes to play terrified, costing your team map control.
why: Your High Note allows you to keep pace with Taliyah's Threaded Volley during wave clearing, but the fundamental issue lies in map mobility. While you can match her push, Rock Surfing gives her superior natural speed near walls. Once she unlocks Weaver's Wall, she can bypass your vision completely and influence side lanes instantly, a map-spanning threat your kit simply cannot mirror.

summary: Using Heroic Swing to circle around Brand lets you easily dodge his linear Sear stun while delivering high physical burst.
howToPlay: To convert this advantage, never initiate a trade blindly with Heroic Swing if Brand has his stun ready and minions are blocking your trajectory. Instead, bait his Pillar of Flame by walking forward, then immediately hook to a side wall to swing past his linear Sear. Fire your Avengerang through the wave to trigger Dirty Fighting for a shield, ensuring that even if a stray Conflagration bounces to you, the passive shield absorbs the burn damage.
laneImpact: Brand is forced to play extremely defensively, often wasting Pillar of Flame and Conflagration just to keep the minion wave from crashing. If he steps up to harass you with basic attacks, he risks getting run down. This wave pressure allows you to roam freely using Going Rogue to hunt down his jungler, while Brand remains trapped under his turret, terrified of getting caught in the river without his defensive stun.
why: This matchup leans heavily in Akshan's favor due to his ability to completely bypass Brand's self-peel. Brand relies on landing a linear Sear on a target already afflicted by Blaze to secure a stun. By activating Heroic Swing at an angle, you can effortlessly dodge this skillshot while swinging. The rapid physical damage from your grapple quickly shreds Brand's low base armor before his delayed Pillar of Flame can even detonate.

summary: Pantheon's Shield Vault provides an instant point-and-click stun that prevents Ekko from reacting with Phase Dive or Chronobreak.
howToPlay: When hunting Ekko in his jungle, always hold Shield Vault until he commits his movement. If he tries to slow you with Timewinder, walk around the returning projectile and gap-close. Use Mortal Will to empower your stun, preventing any window for him to cast Chronobreak when low. If he casts Parallel Convergence, immediately burst him down or use Aegis Assault to block his incoming damage while stepping out of the stun zone.
laneImpact: This interaction turns early river skirmishes and jungle invasions heavily in your favor. Knowing you can lock him down instantly prevents Ekko from contesting Scuttle Crabs or securing his own camps safely. He cannot risk trading health because your Comet Spear poke and immediate stun burst will force him out of the jungle or kill him before he can safely trigger his shield from Parallel Convergence.
why: Pantheon dominates this jungle matchup because his point-and-click crowd control completely neutralizes Ekko's slippery nature. The moment Ekko tries to engage or escape, your instant Shield Vault locks him in place before he can react with Phase Dive to dash away or activate Chronobreak to undo your burst. This immediate lockdown prevents him from triggering Z-Drive Resonance or escaping after a bad commit.

summary: Vladimir can use Sanguine Pool to dodge Mordekaiser's Death's Grasp or to pool under the cast animation of Realm of Death to cancel it.
howToPlay: Never initiate a trade with Death's Grasp while Sanguine Pool is off cooldown. Instead, walk forward and trigger Darkness Rise using basic attacks and isolated Obliterate strikes. Force him to waste his pool to escape your passive aura's burn. The moment he resurfaces, you have a twenty-second window where he is incredibly vulnerable. That is your cue to immediately pull him in and activate Realm of Death to secure the kill.
laneImpact: Because Vladimir has no resources, he will try to poke you down with Transfusion while you try to crash waves. If you blindly push with Obliterate, he will freeze near his turret, scaling safely through Crimson Pact. You must keep the wave in the middle of the lane. Letting him push allows you to threaten him with Death's Grasp, but pushing him under tower lets him safely regenerate health.
why: This lane is a pure battle of attrition where Vladimir heals constantly with Transfusion while you shield with Indestructible. The entire matchup hinges on Sanguine Pool. A skilled Vladimir will use it to slip away from your Death's Grasp, or worse, activate it during the cast animation of Realm of Death. If he pools under your ultimate's cast, your crucial duel is cancelled, leaving you without your stat-stealing advantage.

summary: Vex's Doom 'n Gloom passive marks you when you use Heroic Swing, allowing her to interrupt your swing with a fear.
howToPlay: Track Vex’s resource bar constantly. Your only safe trading windows open when she expends Doom 'n Gloom on the minion wave with Mistral Bolt or Looming Darkness. When her red bar is empty, you can quickly poke with Avengerang and your Dirty Fighting double-tap. Always hold Heroic Swing purely as a defensive tool to escape her Shadow Surge, rather than using it to initiate fights.
laneImpact: You lose the freedom to trade dynamically. Because Heroic Swing is too dangerous to cast, you are forced to farm passively using Avengerang from a distance. Vex easily dictates the wave state with Mistral Bolt, gaining priority to assist her jungler. If you attempt to roam using Going Rogue, she can quickly shove and punish your turret, or even intercept you with Shadow Surge.
why: This matchup is dictated by Vex's passive, Doom 'n Gloom. The moment you initiate Heroic Swing, her passive marks you, and any of her basic abilities like Personal Space or Mistral Bolt will instantly interrupt your flight with a fear. This completely neutralizes your main combat mobility and burst potential, turning your aggressive movement tool into a self-inflicted crowd control trap.

summary: Zed can use Death Mark to dodge Seraphine's Encore or Beat Drop, appearing right behind her for an easy burst kill.
howToPlay: Surviving requires an immediate shift toward defensive itemization, prioritizing early armor and the stasis active over raw ability power. Never initiate trades with Encore or Beat Drop; you must hold these abilities until Zed commits his Death Mark. When he ultimate-assaults you, activate Surround Sound to absorb the initial burst. Only cast your crowd control behind your own character model the exact millisecond he reappears, or immediately activate your stasis to neutralize his mark explosion.
laneImpact: From level three onward, Zed uses Living Shadow to project Razor Shuriken and Shadow Slash past your attack range, making safe farming difficult. You are forced to use High Note and Stage Presence passively from extreme range just to secure minions under your turret. This constant pressure deprives you of mid-lane priority, allowing Zed to freely roam the map while you are trapped defending your tower.
why: Zed completely dominates this matchup because his Death Mark provides the ultimate tool to bypass your self-peel. Whenever you attempt to lock him down with Encore or set up a defensive stun using Beat Drop, he can activate his ultimate to become untargetable, easily dodging your slow-moving projectiles. He then reappears directly behind you, unleashing Razor Shuriken and Shadow Slash to trigger Contempt for the Weak for a guaranteed kill.

summary: Seraphine must use Beat Drop to slow or root Rell mid-dash during her engage attempts, preventing her from reaching the ADC.
howToPlay: Maintain maximum distance and never waste Beat Drop trying to harass her in lane; save it exclusively to interrupt her forward momentum. When she misses her engage, punish her sluggish disengage immediately by proc'ing Stage Presence notes alongside High Note. If she does manage to lock down your ally, use Surround Sound instantly to mitigate the burst damage, and prepare to chain Encore to turn the fight under your turret.
laneImpact: Because of Rell's zoning threat, you cannot step up blindly to poke with High Note. The lane dynamic forces you to yield wave priority, playing defensively near your turret. Missing your crowd control means giving up complete control of the bush line, leading to forced early recalls and leaving your jungler vulnerable to invades without your rotation support.
why: This matchup is defined by your ability to disrupt Rell's heavy engage. Rell wants to dive straight onto your carry, and Seraphine's squishy nature means any successful initiation is lethal. Your primary defensive tool is Beat Drop. You must react instantly to her dash, using the projectile to slow or root her mid-air to shut down her crowd control chain before she can touch your marksman.

summary: Vladimir can use Sanguine Pool to dodge the initial impact and stun of Summon: Tibbers, wasting Annie's primary burst tool.
howToPlay: Never waste your Sanguine Pool offensively or for simple wave clear. You must hold it exclusively for when Annie has three or four charges of Pyromania active and moves forward. Watch her animation closely; the moment she casts Summon: Tibbers, activate your pool to dodge the bear and the stun. Immediately counter-attack with Hemoplague and a fully charged Tides of Blood while her main damage tool is on cooldown.
laneImpact: Before level five, you slowly chip away at her health using empowered Transfusion casts while she tries to farm with Disintegrate. Once ultimates are unlocked, the lane becomes a high-stakes waiting game. If Annie cannot land her stun, she cannot push you out of lane or secure priority. This allows you to comfortably sustain through her minor trades, matching her wave clear with Tides of Blood without risking a bad recall.
why: This lane is a pure test of reflexes and resource management. Annie wants to prep her Pyromania stun to drop a devastating Summon: Tibbers burst, while Vladimir relies on constant healing from Transfusion to shrug off her poke. The entire matchup hinges on a single interaction: using Sanguine Pool to completely dissolve Annie's ultimate cast, leaving her vulnerable with no burst threat while your Hemoplague ticks down.

summary: Maokai's Twisted Advance makes him untargetable, allowing him to dodge Cosmic Binding and lock Bard down easily.
howToPlay: To survive, never cast Cosmic Binding reactively when Maokai walks at you; instead, hold it until after he completes Twisted Advance, aiming it at the wall behind you to stun him post-dash. Place your Caretaker’s Shrine deep behind your turret to secure a safe retreat path. If he traps you with Nature's Grasp, use Tempered Fate on his incoming marksman rather than Maokai himself, buying time for your Magical Journey escape.
laneImpact: This interaction forces you to play extremely safe, giving up brush control because of his Sapling Toss. You cannot step up to harass with Traveler’s Call without risking a sudden lockup. If Maokai freezes the wave near his tower, any attempt to collect chimes or place a Caretaker’s Shrine leaves you vulnerable to a long-range Twisted Advance or a wide Nature's Grasp that secures an easy kill.
why: Maokai completely neutralizes your defensive tools because Twisted Advance grants him untargetability. When you try to peel him off with Cosmic Binding, a skilled Maokai will activate his root to bypass your projectile entirely and close the gap. Once he lands, Bramble Smash knocks you back into his team, leaving you unable to escape his follow-up crowd control.

summary: Force Kayle to use Divine Judgment early by stacking Hemorrhage quickly, then execute her once the shield expires.
howToPlay: Do not initiate fights by blindly throwing out Apprehend. Instead, walk up to her when she tries to farm, or catch her after she uses Celestial Blessing to flee. Apply Crippling Strike to slow her down, spin with the outer edge of Decimate, and stack Hemorrhage. When she panics and triggers Divine Judgment, do not press your ultimate. Wait out the golden shield, keep auto-attacking, and then execute her with Noxian Guillotine.
laneImpact: Because Kayle must play passive, you can easily freeze the wave near your turret. She will attempt to break freezes using Radiant Blast, but doing so exposes her to deadly run-downs. Keeping the minions on your side deprives her of gold, delays her scaling milestones, and allows you to trade heavily. Slow-pushing and diving her under her own tower becomes trivial once you establish health supremacy.
why: Darius holds a massive early advantage before Kayle unlocks the ranged power of her Divine Ascent. She relies on Starfire Spellblade to farm from safety, but cannot survive close-range brawls. Your goal is to apply Hemorrhage stacks rapidly. This immense damage pressure forces her to panic-cast Divine Judgment defensively. Once her invulnerability shield expires, she is completely defenseless against your Noxian Guillotine.

summary: Ambessa can use Repudiation to block the crowd control from Vi's Vault Breaker, turning the duel in her favor.
howToPlay: Do not waste Repudiation to block simple Relentless Force pokes; keep it exclusively for the moment Vi releases her Vault Breaker. If she tries to bait your shield by holding her charge, use Drakehound's Step to dash laterally out of her trajectory. When she reaches level five, expect her to initiate with Cease and Desist; respond immediately by casting Public Execution to match her unstoppable state and crush her during her recovery animation.
laneImpact: Since both of you clear camps at a similar pace, early river skirmishes for the Scuttle Crab or deep jungle invasions are incredibly volatile. If Vi misses or gets her Vault Breaker parried, she cannot easily trigger Denting Blows or stack Blast Shield. This forces her to play defensively or rely on her ultimate, Cease and Desist, which you can also outplay with a well-timed Public Execution to turn the fight.
why: This jungle duel hinges entirely on a single reactionary window. Vi relies on the charge of her Vault Breaker to initiate fights, strip your armor with Denting Blows, and lock you down. However, Ambessa possesses the perfect counter-tool with Repudiation. Timed correctly, your shield absorbs the impact and completely negates the knockback, turning her primary engagement tool into a massive retaliatory blast that swings the skirmish instantly.

summary: Janna can easily react to Rell's engage dash with a quick Howling Gale, canceling her jump mid-air and leaving her vulnerable.
howToPlay: To survive, you must play parallel to your carry and never project an obvious forward movement. Hold Ferromancy: Crashdown and use your physical presence as a zoning threat rather than an active tool. Wait for Janna to waste Howling Gale on wave clearance or a poke attempt before moving in. If she holds her tornado, wait for your jungler and use Full Tilt to close the gap on foot, forcing her Monsoon or flash before committing your jump.
laneImpact: This denial forces you into a passive state where you cannot contest the minion waves. Janna safely pokes you with Zephyr while her carry chips away at your health. If you try to force an engage, getting interrupted mid-air leads to massive counter-damage, forcing early recalls and leaving your carry to farm under tower. This pressure prevents you from roaming to secure river vision.
why: Your entire engage kit is completely shut down by a single reactive ability. Whenever you attempt to initiate with Ferromancy: Crashdown, Janna can instantly release Howling Gale to interrupt your leap mid-flight. Because your jump has a highly visible windup, a decent Janna will consistently knock you out of the air, leaving you dismounted, extremely slow, and completely exposed without landing your crowd control.

summary: Shyvana lacks early crowd control, allowing Darius to easily stack Hemorrhage and run her down if he catches her in her jungle.
howToPlay: Start by warding her raptors or blue buff to track her pathing. When you invade, wait for her to waste Burnout on camp clearing before engaging. Do not initiate with Apprehend; instead, walk up, slow her with Crippling Strike, and save your pull for when she attempts to flee. If she manages to turn with Flame Breath, use the outer edge of Decimate to heal through her damage and secure the execution with Noxian Guillotine.
laneImpact: This matchup turns the jungle into a relentless hunt where you dictate the tempo. Shyvana desperately wants to power-farm to stack Fury of the Dragonborn, but your constant invasion forces her to abandon her camps or die trying to defend them. By stealing her monsters, you delay her Dragon's Descent, neutralizing her teamfight presence while you secure early neutral objectives with the threat of your Noxian Guillotine.
why: Shyvana's early game is highly vulnerable due to her complete lack of crowd control. Since she cannot stop you from sticking to her, you can aggressively invade her camps. If you catch her, you easily apply five stacks of Hemorrhage. Her Burnout offers movement speed but no escape from Apprehend, meaning she cannot disengage once pulled in, ensuring you win any direct duel before she can stack Fury of the Dragonborn.

summary: Garen can use Decisive Strike to cleanse the slow from Gnar's Boomerang Throw and close the gap when Gnar's Hop is on cooldown.
howToPlay: Use the lane brushes to break Gnar's line of sight and minimize his free basic attacks. Never activate Decisive Strike before his Boomerang Throw actually hits you, or you will waste the cleanse. Once the projectile slows you, activate it immediately to break free. If Gnar has recently wasted Hop, charge in with Judgment. When he transforms, hold Courage to absorb the predictable stun from his Mega form's slam before executing him with Demacian Justice.
laneImpact: Expect to spend most of the early levels pushed under your turret, bleeding minions while Gnar harasses you. Your Perseverance is crucial here to heal back the damage from his hyper-aggressive attacks. If you fail to maintain your health bar, Gnar will easily dive you when he transforms into Mega Gnar using his Boulder Toss to smash you against the tower walls, completely shutting down your lane.
why: Gnar's constant shift between forms via Rage Gene makes this a grueling matchup where you are constantly poked from range in his Mini form. His Boomerang Throw applies a heavy slow to keep you at bay, but your Decisive Strike has the unique ability to purge this slow instantly. If you trigger this cleanse while his Hop is on cooldown, you can finally close the distance and trade.

summary: Master Yi can dodge Viego's Spectral Maw stun or Heartbreaker execute with a well-timed Alpha Strike, securing the 1v1 victory.
howToPlay: To survive and win the 1v1, never initiate with Spectral Maw. Instead, activate Harrowed Path near walls to gain attack speed, and use basic attacks enhanced by Blade of the Ruined King to force him to use Alpha Strike first. Once he reappears, immediately unleash Spectral Maw to lock him down, or execute him with Heartbreaker if his health is low. If he channels Meditate to stall, use your charged stun to interrupt him instantly.
laneImpact: This dynamic limits your freedom in the jungle. You cannot contest crabs or invade his camps safely without tracking his Alpha Strike. If you encounter him in the river, you are forced to play defensively, sacrificing early scuttle control. Failing to respect this matchup results in Master Yi getting early kills, which accelerates his Highlander resets and compromises your team's objective security.
why: Master Yi holds the upper hand in direct duels because his Alpha Strike allows him to seamlessly dodge both your Spectral Maw stun and your Heartbreaker execute. Since Viego relies on landing Spectral Maw to set up his Blade of the Ruined King burst and needs Heartbreaker to finish the kill, Master Yi can reactively disappear from the map to negate your entire combo while shredding you with Wuju Style true damage.

summary: Ezreal can instantly escape Miss Fortune's Bullet Time using Arcane Shift, but must avoid standing directly behind low-health minions to prevent Double Up bounces.
howToPlay: To win this, never stand in a direct line behind your low-health minions, forcing Miss Fortune to use Double Up directly on you rather than getting the empowered bounce. Always hold Arcane Shift when her Bullet Time is up; do not use it offensively unless she has already wasted her ultimate. If she catches you with Make It Rain, walk sideways immediately to avoid the slow, then retaliate with a quick Essence Flux and Mystic Shot combo.
laneImpact: The lane rhythm shifts constantly based on minion health. Miss Fortune will attempt to shove the wave with Make It Rain and fish for lethal Double Up bounces. This pressure forces you to trade from off-angles. If you get chunked, you lose the ability to safely stack Rising Spell Force on the wave. However, because you can easily escape her ultimate, she can rarely force a dive or a clean kill without heavy setup.
why: This matchup is a pure skill battle defined by how you manage spacing against her poke. Miss Fortune relies on Double Up bouncing off dying minions to chunk your health, while you want to land Mystic Shot and Essence Flux from safety. The critical tool in your kit is Arcane Shift, which allows you to completely negate the massive zoning threat of her Bullet Time by blinking out of its channel instantly.

summary: While Ambessa can block one instance of Bandage Toss with Repudiation, she cannot escape the massive area lockdown of Curse of the Sad Mummy.
howToPlay: To win the skirmishes, never initiate with Public Execution while his ultimate is available. Instead, use Drakehound's Step to dance around his melee range, baiting out Bandage Toss to trigger your Repudiation block. Once Curse of the Sad Mummy is expended on your frontline, immediately lock him down with Cunning Sweep and finish him off with Lacerate while staying spread from your allies.
laneImpact: In the river and during skirmishes, this interaction dictates who controls the pace. If you mistime your shield and get caught by Bandage Toss, the mummy will easily drag you into his team to unleash Curse of the Sad Mummy. This forces you to play defensively around neutral spawns, as a premature engage means getting locked down, while a successful block allows you to counter-engage with Public Execution.
why: This duel hinges on how you match your defensive reaction against the mummy's crowd control. Your Repudiation can perfectly absorb and negate one incoming Bandage Toss, stripping away his primary gap-closer and stun. However, you have no natural tool to bypass or escape the massive, instant radius of Curse of the Sad Mummy, which leaves you highly vulnerable to his continuous Despair and Tantrum damage if caught.

summary: Ziggs can disrupt your positioning and interrupt your channels from long range using Satchel Charge.
howToPlay: To survive and scale, never use *Astral Flight* aggressively unless Ziggs has already wasted his *Satchel Charge*. Keep your distance by clearing waves from behind your caster minions using *Singularity*, forcing him to choose between targeting you or the wave with *Bouncing Bomb*. If he attempts to zone you with *Hexplosive Minefield*, immediately drop *Singularity* on the opposing wave to match his clear speed, preventing him from utilizing his passive on your turret.
laneImpact: The laning phase becomes a high-stakes race for priority. If you let Ziggs shove you under turret, his *Short Fuse* and *Satchel Charge* will rapidly demolish your plating. However, stepping forward to contest the wave with *Singularity* exposes you to his *Hexplosive Minefield*. Every trade revolves around health versus mana efficiency; if you get forced to recall early, you lose critical stacking momentum while your mid turret crumbles.
why: This matchup is a constant artillery duel where wave positioning dictates who gets poked down. While Aurelion Sol wants to channel *Breath of Light* to collect *Cosmic Creator* stacks on minion waves, Ziggs excels at punishing stationary targets. His *Bouncing Bomb* easily chips away at your health from afar, but the true threat is *Satchel Charge*, which can instantly interrupt your channeled flight or damage, leaving you vulnerable and misplaced in the lane.

summary: If hit by Sleepy Trouble Bubble (E), Galio can pre-charge Shield of Durand (W) to reduce the incoming damage from Paddle Star! (Q) while asleep.
howToPlay: To survive Zoe's poke, position yourself away from the side walls to limit her Sleepy Trouble Bubble angles. Keep minion waves between you to block her bubble, but stay slightly to the side to avoid the splash radius of Paddle Star!. If the bubble connects, do not panic: immediately hold down Shield of Durand before the sleep kicks in. This mitigates her burst, allowing you to counter-attack with Justice Punch once you wake up.
laneImpact: Zoe's ability to fish for Sleepy Trouble Bubble through mid-lane walls forces you into a defensive posture. You cannot blindly rush her with Justice Punch, as she will easily counter-engage. Instead, the lane becomes a push war. By using Winds of War and Colossal Smash to match her wave clear, you prevent her from securing the priority needed to roam or collect active spells with Spell Thief.
why: This matchup centers on how you handle Zoe's crowd control. While her ranged basic attacks empowered by More Sparkles! harass you, her main threat is Sleepy Trouble Bubble. The lane remains even because of a specific defensive interaction: when you are hit by her bubble, you can immediately channel Shield of Durand. This active damage reduction remains active while you are asleep, absorbing the brunt of her incoming Paddle Star!.

summary: Vladimir can use Sanguine Pool to dodge Garen's Demacian Justice, making it crucial to silence him first with Decisive Strike.
howToPlay: Maintain a safe distance and never let Garen strike you with Decisive Strike for free. If you see him activate his speed boost, retreat immediately or charge Tides of Blood to slow him down. Hold your Sanguine Pool exclusively for his Demacian Justice; if he tries to silence you first to prevent this dodge, use your pool early to avoid the silence altogether. If you get caught off-guard, activate Hemoplague immediately to ensure massive healing.
laneImpact: This matchup turns into a battle of attrition where you easily choke Garen out of the wave. By repeatedly punishing his attempts to farm with Transfusion and Tides of Blood, you force him to use Courage defensively, draining his pressure. Since he cannot easily reach you without burning his movement speed, you command the wave state, forcing him into bad recall timings and securing early plate advantages.
why: Vladimir dominates this matchup because his ranged poke with Transfusion constantly disrupts Garen's health regeneration from Perseverance. While Garen relies on getting close to execute his rotation, Vladimir's safety net is absolute. The ultimate trump card is Sanguine Pool, which completely negates Garen's execution tool, Demacian Justice, provided Vladimir isn't silenced beforehand by Decisive Strike.

summary: Syndra can interrupt Ekko's Phase Dive mid-dash using Scatter the Weak, leaving him stranded and vulnerable to her burst.
howToPlay: To secure this advantage, never throw out Scatter the Weak mindlessly for wave clear. Always hold this knockback as a reactive tool for the exact moment Ekko initiates with Phase Dive. While waiting, harass him constantly using Dark Sphere and Force of Will whenever he steps up to last-hit. If he panics and uses Chronobreak to survive, track his clone's position to pre-cast another sphere at his landing spot.
laneImpact: This interaction completely strips Ekko of his laning agency. He is forced to forfeit wave control, relying solely on Timewinder from afar to secure minions. If he attempts to deploy Parallel Convergence to force a trade, you can easily zone him out. Because you constantly threaten to disrupt his dash, you maintain permanent priority, pinning him under tower and neutralizing his map pressure.
why: Syndra dictates this matchup by rendering Ekko's primary gap-closer useless. Because Ekko must rely on Phase Dive to get into melee range, he is entirely predictable. By timing Scatter the Weak to strike mid-dash, you cancel his forward momentum, knocking him back and leaving him stunned. Without his mobility, he cannot trigger Z-Drive Resonance, leaving him completely exposed to Dark Sphere and Force of Will.

summary: While Wither (W) severely slows your movement, it does not stop you from using Shuriken Flip (E) or Perfect Execution (R) to escape or reposition.
howToPlay: Never waste Shuriken Flip offensively unless Nasus has already squandered Wither or is extremely low. When he uses his slow to initiate, immediately react by casting Shuriken Flip backward or utilizing Perfect Execution to disengage, waiting out the slow's duration inside your Twilight Shroud. Once you push him under tower, immediately abandon the lane to look for skirmishes elsewhere, as trying to dive his Fury of the Sands is a guaranteed disaster.
laneImpact: As Nasus passively stacks Siphoning Strike under his turret, your kill pressure rapidly drops, especially once he unlocks Fury of the Sands. Staying top too long allows him to whittle down your health with Spirit Fire and trap you with Wither. This stalemate forces you to quickly clear waves with Five Point Strike and use those brief windows to impact the map before he threatens your tower.
why: Nasus naturally out-sustains your early harass using Soul Eater, turning this lane into a ticking clock. When he attempts to lock you down, his Wither drastically reduces your movement speed, making it nearly impossible to trigger your Assassin's Mark passive. However, this crippling slow does not prevent you from casting Shuriken Flip or Perfect Execution, meaning you retain complete control over your mobility to escape his Fury of the Sands.

summary: Syndra can use Scatter the Weak (E) to push Aurora away when she attempts to engage with Across the Veil (W).
howToPlay: To win this, bait out Scatter the Weak before committing. Walk up aggressively without using Across the Veil, using The Weirding to slow her and force a panicked reaction. Once she wastes her knockback, immediately activate Across the Veil to close the gap, trigger Spirit Abjuration, and trap her inside Between Worlds. If she holds her stun, focus entirely on farming with Twofold Hex and wait for her to misposition while trying to land Force of Will.
laneImpact: Because of this threat, you cannot freely jump in to trade health. The lane becomes a tense spacing game where you must use Twofold Hex to secure minions from a distance. If you waste your mobility, Syndra will immediately retaliate with Unleashed Power, forcing you to recall early and lose crucial waves. This neutralizes your ability to roam and pressure other lanes, locking both of you in a constant battle for mid priority.
why: This midlane duel revolves around a sharp burst trade where timing is everything. While you want to leap forward using Across the Veil to close the distance and trigger Spirit Abjuration, Syndra possesses the perfect tool to deny your aggression. Her Scatter the Weak can instantly knock you back mid-jump, completely neutralizing your stealth approach and leaving you vulnerable to a quick Dark Sphere and Force of Will follow-up.

summary: Jax's Counter Strike blocks Viego's Blade of the Ruined King passive double-strikes, severely limiting Viego's conqueror stacking and healing.
howToPlay: When contesting camps, hold Counter Strike until Viego commits to a fight by charging Spectral Maw or using his Blade of the Ruined King passive. Never waste your defensive stance early. Once he initiates, activate Counter Strike to absorb his double-strikes, then reset your attack timer using Empower to burst him down. If Viego attempts to retreat using Harrowed Path or Heartbreaker, save Leap Strike to close the distance and finish him off in his own zone.
laneImpact: This interaction turns the river and neutral camps into danger zones for Viego. Since you win straight duels, you can aggressively contest scuttle crabs and invade his camps. Viego is forced to clear cautiously, knowing that if you catch him in his Harrowed Path, his DPS is completely shut down. Your dominance in direct skirmishes limits his ability to secure early map pressure and secure neutral objectives.
why: Jax holds a decisive advantage in the jungle matchup because Counter Strike completely neutralizes Viego's main combat engine. When Viego uses Blade of the Ruined King to mark you, his subsequent passive double-strike basic attacks are entirely blocked by Counter Strike. This interaction denies Viego his primary source of healing and prevents him from rapidly building up his combat stacks during close-quarters skirmishes.

summary: Aatrox can interrupt Sion's Decimating Smash charge at any time using any of his three The Darkin Blade sweetspot knockups.
howToPlay: When Sion starts charging Decimating Smash, do not panic or run away. Instead, walk forward or use Umbral Dash to position your The Darkin Blade sweetspot directly on him to cancel his channel.
