If he tries to escape or slow you with Roar of the Slayer, use Infernal Chains to pull him back. Save your World Ender for when he attempts to flee with Unstoppable Onslaught or to match his raw health scaling in extended fights, ensuring you always keep a sweetspot ready.
laneImpact: This interaction completely strips Sion of his lane priority. Every time he tries to charge Decimating Smash to clear the wave or trade, you can step up and interrupt him. This denies his wave control, forcing him to farm under tower where you can harass him with The Darkin Blade and Infernal Chains. He cannot easily pop his Soul Furnace shield for damage because you can break it or pull him out of range.
why: Aatrox dominates this matchup because Sion's primary tool for waveclear and damage, Decimating Smash, requires him to stand still and channel. Any of your three The Darkin Blade sweetspot knockups instantly cancels his charge, putting it on a full cooldown and leaving him completely vulnerable. Since Sion has low mobility outside his ultimate, he cannot easily dodge your sweetspots while preparing his own attack.

summary: Syndra can pick up Heimerdinger's H-28G Evolution Turrets (Q) with Force of Will (W) and throw them to disable his zone control.
howToPlay: Never waste Force of Will on random minions; always hold it until Heimerdinger drops an H-28G Evolution Turret. Walk up confidently when his CH-2 Electron Storm Grenade is on cooldown, pick up his turret, and toss it onto his face. Follow up immediately with Dark Sphere and Scatter the Weak to stun him while he has no defensive zone. Once he is chunked, a quick Unleashed Power easily secures the kill on his fragile health pool.
laneImpact: Heimerdinger cannot establish his usual aggressive push or trap you under tower. By constantly displacing his H-28G Evolution Turret, you secure permanent wave priority without wasting mana on raw waveclear. You can crash waves at will, preventing him from ever using UPGRADE!!! safely to pressure your plating. This freedom allows you to secure early river vision and move first to assist your jungler.
why: This matchup is heavily tilted in your favor because Force of Will completely dismantles Heimerdinger's primary source of damage and lane control. Whenever he places an H-28G Evolution Turret, you can simply pick it up and throw it away or use it to clear his wave. This denies him his Hextech Affinity movement speed and leaves him incredibly vulnerable to your easy Dark Sphere and Scatter the Weak poke.

summary: Leona must engage on Sona early with Zenith Blade before Sona can scale and sustain through lane with Aria of Perseverance.
howToPlay: Actively occupy the lane bushes to hide your trajectory. The moment she steps up to cast Hymn of Valor, launch Zenith Blade directly at her, immediately activating Eclipse to mitigate any retaliatory damage while you apply Shield of Daybreak. If she plays excessively safe behind her minions, hold your ground near her tower and wait for your Solar Flare to stun her from range, preventing her from ever casting her defensive Crescendo.
laneImpact: This matchup creates immense pressure from level two onward. Sona is forced to play extremely far back, severely limiting her ability to poke with Hymn of Valor or stack her passive. If she steps up to assist her marksman, any aggressive forward movement exposes her to a lethal dive. You will control the brush easily, dictating when waves crash and forcing early recalls that ruin her scaling curve.
why: Sona lacks early defensive stats and relies heavily on Aria of Perseverance to recover from trades. However, before she can gather enough mana and levels to sustain her lane partner, Leona can easily bypass her poking tools like Hymn of Valor. Landing a single Zenith Blade allows you to lock her down instantly with Shield of Daybreak, triggering Sunlight marks that your ADC can easily detonate for an immediate kill.

summary: If Mordekaiser traps Kayn in the Realm of Death, Kayn can waste a massive portion of its duration using Umbral Trespass inside him.
howToPlay: To win these skirmishes, you must alter your ultimate timing. Never initiate with Realm of Death if Kayn has already damaged you, as he will immediately use it to dodge your burst. Instead, bait his escape tools first. Force him to burn Shadow Step to cross a wall or use Reaping Slash defensively. Once he is forced to activate Umbral Trespass early in the teamfight, that is your precise cue to pull him into your domain and crush him with Obliterate.
laneImpact: In the jungle, this interaction strips away your ability to easily secure neutral objectives through forced isolation. If you try to force a smite fight by banishing him, he simply buys time inside you while his team secures the objective or collapses. This forces you into passive farming routes, as you cannot confidently contest him in the river without a massive gold lead.
why: Duel-locking Kayn is highly deceptive because of how his kit interacts with your ultimate. When you drag him into the Realm of Death, Kayn can instantly retaliate by casting Umbral Trespass on you. This completely stalls out the duel, allowing him to hide inside your character model and waste almost the entire duration of your stolen stat window, rendering your main win condition useless.

summary: Tryndamere can delay Undying Rage until the final moment to completely negate the pop damage from Zed's Death Mark.
howToPlay: When Zed initiates with Death Mark, do not panic-activate Undying Rage immediately. Fight back using Battle Fury to stack damage, and only trigger your ultimate right before the mark detonates. If he tries to escape using Living Shadow, hold Spinning Slash to match his shadow-swap distance. Once he is out of energy and running away, use Mocking Shout to slow him down and secure the kill with your critical strikes.
laneImpact: In the jungle, this interaction strips Zed of his usual pressure during river skirmishes and objective contests. He cannot safely contest your camps or facecheck you, as he lacks the raw sustained damage to fight your Battle Fury once his burst is negated. You can aggressively invade his territory, knowing that any dueling attempt he makes will result in him wasting his cooldowns while you easily chase him down.
why: Tryndamere completely neutralizes Zed's assassination potential because Undying Rage acts as the ultimate counter to Death Mark. Zed relies on compounding damage with Razor Shuriken and Shadow Slash to trigger a lethal mark explosion. By holding Undying Rage until the absolute last millisecond before that final pop, you render his entire ultimate combo useless while maintaining full Battle Fury to shred him in return.

summary: Sona's lack of mobility makes her an easy target for Rakan's Grand Entrance, but failing to lock her down allows her Aria of Perseverance to out-sustain his poke.
howToPlay: Maintain maximum distance and never step parallel to your ADC to prevent Rakan from hitting both of you with Grand Entrance. Always keep Song of Celerity ready; the moment he starts his dash animation, activate it to sidestep the impact zone. If he does manage to close the gap, immediately cycle your Power Chord using Aria of Perseverance to reduce his target's damage output while preparing Crescendo to lock him down under your tower.
laneImpact: You cannot safely contest the brush because getting caught by Grand Entrance means death or burning critical summoner spells. Consequently, Rakan can easily zone you and secure bush control. This forces a defensive wave state near your tower. However, if you survive his initial dive attempt, your constant healing from Aria of Perseverance allows your ADC to win long-term health trades and slowly push him out of the lane.
why: Rakan's explosive engage relies on catching you off-guard with Grand Entrance, a task made easy by your complete lack of defensive dashes. If he lands this knock-up, his ADC can instantly burst you down. However, if Rakan misses or hesitates, your Aria of Perseverance completely nullifies any poke he attempts with Gleaming Quill. The lane is a constant test of whether he can successfully pin you down.

summary: Braum's Unbreakable shield cannot block Alistar's Pulverize knockup, but Braum's Concussive Blows make extended trades dangerous for Alistar.
howToPlay: To win this deadlock, play around the threat of your combo while staying near your own minions to block his Winter's Bite. Use Headbutt to push Braum away from your carry if he tries to stack Concussive Blows. Never commit with Trample unless his shield is down and you have immediate backup. If you do get caught in a stun, immediately activate Unbreakable Will to cleanse the crowd control and reduce incoming damage before retreating safely.
laneImpact: Because of this interaction, the lane dynamic remains slow and tense. You cannot easily dive or engage past their wave without risking a devastating counter-engage under tower. If Braum uses Stand Behind Me to reposition, he can easily setup Glacial Fissure to split you from your ADC. Trade health only when you can safely trigger Triumphant Roar to sustain, otherwise, any failed initiation leaves you vulnerable to a heavy slow.
why: This matchup is a pure test of positioning. While Braum can raise Unbreakable to absorb incoming projectiles, it does nothing to stop your Pulverize knockup from below. However, you cannot afford to overcommit. Linger too long in melee range, and his Concussive Blows passive will stack rapidly via his basic attacks and Winter's Bite, leading to a stun that completely swings the trade.

summary: Lee Sin can use Dragon's Rage to kick Hecarim away mid-charge during Devastating Charge, completely neutralizing his engage and damage.
howToPlay: To survive this matchup, you must map his starting camp and mirror his route in reverse to avoid direct 1v1 encounters. During teamfights, never lead with Devastating Charge directly into him; instead, wait for him to commit Sonic Wave or use Safeguard onto another target. If forced to engage, initiate with Onslaught of Shadows first to fear him, using the crowd control duration to safely land your knockback before he can react with Dragon's Rage.
laneImpact: Because Lee Sin possesses superior early-game dueling with Flurry and Sonic Wave, he will actively hunt you in your territory. If he tracks your pathing, he can invade and force skirmishes where your slower Rampage buildup cannot match his burst. This constant threat forces your laners to play defensively, as losing an early 2v2 to his high mobility ruins your map pressure before you can even unlock Onslaught of Shadows.
why: Lee Sin dominates this duel because his ultimate, Dragon's Rage, serves as a direct, hard counter to your primary engage. When you attempt to gank or initiate a skirmish using Devastating Charge, he can easily react by kicking you backward mid-dash. This completely cancels your momentum, wasting your main damage multiplier from Warpath and leaving you vulnerable without your crucial gap-closer.

summary: Wukong's Warrior Trickster (W) can decoy Nasus's Siphoning Strike (Q), but Wither (W) completely shuts down Wukong's ultimate DPS.
howToPlay: Play aggressively only when Wither is on cooldown. Initiate short trades with Golden Staff and Nimbus Strike, then immediately use Warrior Trickster to block Siphoning Strike and escape. Never commit your Cyclone while his slow is active; wait for him to waste Wither on a teammate during teamfights or bait it out before spinning. If he freezes the wave near his tower, call your jungler to break it or look to roam.
laneImpact: You cannot trade mindlessly because Nasus will just heal back up under his tower. If you push the wave too hard with Nimbus Strike, you freeze yourself out of gold while he safely stacks Siphoning Strike. This passive lane state limits your map pressure, forcing you to stay top to prevent him from taking your turret, as you cannot afford to leave him scaling uncontested.
why: Nasus outlasts you through the passive healing of Soul Eater, forcing a war of attrition you cannot win directly. While a well-timed Warrior Trickster can absorb a fully charged Siphoning Strike, his Wither remains your biggest hurdle. The massive attack speed and movement slow from Wither completely cripples your damage output, rendering your Cyclone spin ineffective if he uses it to disengage or fight back.

summary: Ashe's Enchanted Crystal Arrow is a reliable tool to stun Akshan mid-air during his Heroic Swing, stopping his engage instantly.
howToPlay: Position yourself near the center of the lane, far enough from the terrain to limit his Heroic Swing angles, but close enough to hit him with Volley whenever he tries to farm. Always hold onto Enchanted Crystal Arrow specifically for the moment he attaches his grapple to a wall. If he attempts to channel Comeuppance, immediately activate Ranger's Focus to shred his health bar while using your superior range to keep him from triggering his Dirty Fighting shield.
laneImpact: This interaction completely shifts the wave dynamic in your favor. Knowing you can cancel Heroic Swing prevents Akshan from aggressively clearing waves with Avengerang or looking for trades near the side walls. He is forced to play defensively behind his minions, allowing you to slow-push and stack waves. You can safely chip his tower plates or use Hawkshot to track his jungler without fearing a sudden, stealthy flank from Going Rogue.
why: Ashe naturally commands this lane because Akshan relies heavily on the predictable movement of Heroic Swing to close the distance. Since his trajectory is locked once he attaches to a wall, your Enchanted Crystal Arrow becomes an unavoidable shutdown tool. By interrupting his swing mid-air, you completely negate his primary burst and escape mechanism, leaving him stranded and vulnerable to your relentless Frost Shot slows.

summary: Lux's Light Binding can root Alistar mid-engage, but if she misses, she has no escape from his Headbutt-Pulverize combo.
howToPlay: Stand parallel to your minion wave to force her to choose between shoving or targeting you. Never walk straight at her; instead, bait her Light Binding by making sudden diagonal movements. If she misses, immediately trigger Headbutt into Pulverize. Should you get rooted beforehand, immediately activate Unbreakable Will to cleanse the crowd control, then use Trample to stun her or her carry as you retreat, preventing them from capitalizing on your mistake.
laneImpact: Lux will constantly use Lucent Singularity to shove the wave and chip your health, trying to force you under tower where headbutt angles are restricted. If you take too much poke early, you lose the health required to execute a dive or roam, locking you in lane. A single missed root from her completely shifts the pressure, turning her tower-sieging advantage into an immediate double kill for your marksman.
why: This matchup is a tense battle of spacing centered entirely on Lux's Light Binding. If you attempt to engage with your Headbutt-Pulverize combo while she has this root available, she can stop you mid-flight, leaving you stranded and vulnerable to Lucent Singularity and Illumination procs. However, the moment she wastes her Light Binding, she loses her only defensive tool, making her an easy target for your displacement.

summary: Mordekaiser's Realm of Death transports you to an alternate dimension, leaving all your pre-placed H-28G Evolution Turrets behind.
howToPlay: To survive, you must change how you manage your H-28G Evolution Turret charges. Never place all three on the map; always keep at least two charges in reserve. If Mordekaiser pulls you with Realm of Death, immediately drop an UPGRADE!!! empowered turret inside the death realm to fight back, and use CH-2 Electron Storm Grenade to stun him and kite. Maximize Hextech Affinity near your tower to dodge his Obliterate during the neutral phase.
laneImpact: Before level five, you can bully Mordekaiser, but once he unlocks his ultimate, your lane pressure completely evaporates. You can no longer safely push the wave or pressure his tower, as stepping past the river invites a Death's Grasp into an unavoidable Realm of Death. Any attempt to lock down a zone with H-28G Evolution Turret is instantly neutralized, forcing you into a defensive, low-resource playstyle under your own turret.
why: The entire matchup hinges on a devastating structural interaction: when Mordekaiser casts Realm of Death, he pulls you into his death realm but leaves all your pre-placed H-28G Evolution Turrets behind in the normal rift. Stripped of your primary zone control and DPS source, you are trapped in a tight space with a juggernaut who can easily run you down with Darkness Rise and Obliterate.

summary: Leona can engage immediately with Zenith Blade once Lux misses or wastes her Light Binding.
howToPlay: To survive, you must hold Light Binding strictly as a disengage tool. Never throw it proactively unless Leona's Zenith Blade is on cooldown. Use Lucent Singularity from maximum range to chip away at her health, and immediately cast Prismatic Barrier to mitigate her initial burst if she manages to hook you. If she misses her gap-closer, use that brief window to safely apply your Illumination passive before retreating.
laneImpact: Because of this threat, you cannot freely step up to trigger Illumination with basic attacks. Missing your root forces you and your carry to retreat under turret, forfeiting lane priority. Leona will use Eclipse to dive you or crash the wave, creating a massive zone of control where throwing Lucent Singularity carelessly results in an immediate, lethal all-in.
why: This matchup hinges entirely on the threat of your crowd control. If you miss or waste Light Binding, Leona will instantly lock you down with Zenith Blade. Without your root to halt her dash, she can easily chain Shield of Daybreak and Solar Flare, triggering Sunlight marks while using her Eclipse resistances to negate any retaliation from your Lucent Singularity.

summary: Yasuo's Wind Wall cannot block Mordekaiser's Obliterate or Darkness Rise aura, leaving him vulnerable once Mordekaiser closes the gap.
howToPlay: Pop his Way of the Wanderer shield with a simple basic attack or the edge of Obliterate before committing to a fight. Wait until he discharges his Steel Tempest tornado, then immediately cast Death's Grasp to pull him in. Once you lock him down, trigger Darkness Rise to burn through his health. If he manages to knock you up, activate Indestructible to absorb Last Breath's burst, and use Realm of Death to isolate him away from minions so he cannot dash.
laneImpact: You dominate the wave dynamic since Yasuo cannot hide behind his wind barrier to farm or trade safely. Every time he dashes forward with Sweeping Blade, he risks taking an unblockable Obliterate. This constant threat forces him to play defensively, giving you total control over the lane's push. You can easily chip away at his tower while keeping him trapped under his turret, starving his gold income.
why: This matchup heavily favors you because Yasuo's defensive centerpiece, Wind Wall, is completely useless against your main tools. It cannot block the overhead smash of Obliterate, nor can it stop the burning magic damage from your Darkness Rise aura. Once you close the distance, Yasuo is stripped of his primary projectile-blocking utility, forcing him into a pure stat check that his squishier skirmisher profile cannot win.

summary: A skilled Thresh can use Flay to interrupt Alistar's Headbutt mid-dash, completely denying the Headbutt-Pulverize combo.
howToPlay: To survive, you must play a patient baiting game. Never initiate with Headbutt unless you see Thresh waste Flay to clear waves or peel. When Flay is on cooldown, you have a brief fifteen-second window to strike. Alternatively, bypass his reaction time entirely by using Flash directly into Pulverize, then using Headbutt to push the target back into your tower, while keeping Unbreakable Will ready to cleanse his subsequent Death Sentence.
laneImpact: Because your main engage is neutralized, you lose the threat of a sudden engage, allowing Thresh to position aggressively and collect souls from Damnation. Your ADC will be forced under turret as Thresh's ranged basic attacks poke you down. If you attempt a desperate Headbutt that gets cancelled, Thresh will lock you down with The Box, resulting in massive health loss or a forced recall.
why: The entire matchup hinges on Thresh's ability to react to your engage. A competent Thresh will consistently use Flay to knock you out of your Headbutt dash before you can activate Pulverize. This mechanical denial leaves you stranded in the minion wave, stripped of your primary crowd control, and highly vulnerable to a counter-hook from Death Sentence while your cooldowns recover.

summary: Tristana can use Buster Shot to knock Akshan away mid-swing, or Rocket Jump to safety if he commits to an all-in.
howToPlay: Never initiate an all-in with Heroic Swing while her Buster Shot is available, as she will cancel your momentum and leave you stranded. Instead, use Avengerang to poke through the minion wave and trigger Dirty Fighting to win short trades. If she jumps on you with Rocket Jump, wait out her Rapid Fire duration, then utilize Going Rogue near the terrain to reposition and strike back once her explosive timer expires.
laneImpact: Trades are incredibly short and violent. If Tristana wastes her Rocket Jump forward to force a fight, you can punish her instantly with Avengerang and Heroic Swing. However, if she plays defensively, pushing her under turret becomes risky because Draw a Bead increases her range, making it easy for her to farm safely. The lane is decided by who successfully baits the opponent's main movement tool before committing.
why: This lane is a high-octane duel of instant bursts where timing is everything. Tristana wants to stack Explosive Charge quickly using Rapid Fire, but your Dirty Fighting shield can absorb a portion of this burst. However, your offensive threat relies heavily on Heroic Swing. Because Buster Shot can interrupt you mid-air and Rocket Jump allows her to disengage completely, you cannot blindly swing in without tracking her defensive tools.

summary: Wukong can use Warrior Trickster to leave a clone that absorbs your Infernal Chains and Q sweetspots.
howToPlay: To survive this matchup, never initiate with Infernal Chains. Instead, utilize your basic attacks and Deathbringer Stance to clear, and hold The Darkin Blade until he commits Warrior Trickster. If he jumps on you with Nimbus Strike, use Umbral Dash backwards to disengage his Cyclone ultimate. If you misplay and hit his clone with your main cooldowns, immediately retreat using World Ender's movement speed bonus rather than attempting to fight through his Stone Skin armor.
laneImpact: In the jungle, this interaction makes direct duels over Scuttle Crabs extremely hazardous. If Wukong baits your The Darkin Blade with his clone, he immediately counter-engages with Nimbus Strike and Golden Staff, winning the trade effortlessly. You lose the priority needed to contest early neutral camps, forcing you to concede pressure in your own jungle, which delays your World Ender power spike and leaves your laners exposed to his gank setups.
why: Wukong holds a massive advantage in the jungle skirmishes because Warrior Trickster completely neutralizes your primary combo. Whenever you attempt to set up your damage with Infernal Chains, he can deploy his clone to absorb the chain or block the sweetspots of The Darkin Blade. This interaction denies your healing from Deathbringer Stance and Umbral Dash, leaving you vulnerable to his armor-shredding Golden Staff and rapid physical burst.

summary: Darius can pull Talon with Apprehend mid-air during Assassin's Path to cancel his escape.
howToPlay: Position yourself closely to the terrain Talon is likely to hop over when contesting objectives. Never open a skirmish with Apprehend; instead, initiate with Crippling Strike to slow his movement, followed by Decimate. Save your hook exclusively for the moment he panics and activates Assassin's Path to vault away. If he tries to vanish using Shadow Assault, delay your actions slightly and prepare to pull him back the instant his silhouette approaches a wall.
laneImpact: In the jungle, this interaction strips Talon of his safety when contesting Scuttle Crabs or invading your camps. He cannot safely face-check or cross paths with you near walls, forcing him to take inefficient, longer pathings. If you catch him attempting to clear with Rake, your threat of pulling him mid-vault prevents him from securing neutral objectives, severely delaying his lethality spikes and bleeding his jungle pressure.
why: This matchup tilts heavily in your favor because you can completely deny Talon's signature mobility. While he relies on Assassin's Path to slip over walls and escape fights, your Apprehend acts as a hard stop. Snatching him out of his wall-vault animation leaves him stranded in melee range. Without his escape, he cannot survive a prolonged duel against Hemorrhage stacks, especially once you trigger Noxian Might.

howToPlay: Start with positioning: keep the wave closer to your tower and accept losing some “free” autos if they open an ult angle. Your goal isn’t killing him; it’s surviving without giving a kill window while keeping stable farm. Key timing: from level 5, treat his R as a permanent threat cooldown. If you lack jungle vision OR your jump is down, play as if the ult can happen anytime. Even when jump is up, reserve it to react to ult, not to take an aggressive trade. Decision-making: if lane becomes too risky, pivot to cross-map value. Instead of forcing damage onto Malphite, use any prio to secure objective fights, set deep vision, or rotate quickly — and if you don’t have prio, play safe and spam danger pings because your job becomes avoiding giving the fight start.
laneImpact: In lane you get a lose-lose pressure puzzle: if you push, you become gankable and give ult angles; if you don’t push, you lose Tristana top’s main value (tower pressure + prio). That often leads to freezes or forces you to play far back, breaking your tempo. From level 5 onward, every wave is a discipline check. One misstep (too close to wall, too close to his threat range) and you get engaged even with jump available. Malphite doesn’t need extended trades — one clean engage is enough. Midgame teamfights also become risky: Malphite makes your positioning fragile. Without vision, you’re no longer the bully — you’re a high-priority target that hands the enemy a fight start.
why: Malphite is a hard counter because he turns your natural advantage (range + push) into a trap: the more you step up to hit tower or take free autos, the more you expose yourself to an all-in you can’t reliably outplay. Your kit wants to harass and snowball plates; his kit wants one clean engage window. Tristana top also depends on safe auto windows. Malphite shrinks those windows through tankiness and simple trade patterns. Even if you “win” small pokes, his kill condition isn’t poke — it’s a timed engage when you don’t have enough HP or can’t hold your escape. As the game goes on, it gets worse: armor stacking + slows + teamfight engage. You can be ahead in gold yet still lose lane control because you can’t manage waves freely without offering his team a perfect entry.

summary: Teemo's short range and lack of waveclear make him an easy target for Seraphine's High Note and Beat Drop poke from complete safety.
howToPlay: To survive, prioritize freezing the minion wave just outside your turret range. Use *Move Quick* actively to dodge *Beat Drop*, as getting hit by its slow or root setup guarantees a devastating *High Note* follow-up. Hold your *Blinding Dart* to secure cannon minions safely from a distance instead of trading. Accept losing some gold; your main goal is staying healthy enough to absorb her wave pressure without dying.
laneImpact: You will constantly find yourself pushed under your own turret, losing health while struggling to last-hit. Seraphine easily neutralizes any passive play from *Guerrilla Warfare* by covering the lane with her wide area-of-effect spells. This constant pressure ruins your recall timings, chips away at your tower's health, and prevents you from placing defensive *Noxious Trap* setups, leaving you pinned down while she roams freely.
why: Seraphine completely outranges you, turning the mid lane into a firing range. Because Teemo relies on short-ranged basic attacks buffed by *Toxic Shot*, you must step up to farm. This positioning makes you highly vulnerable to Seraphine's *High Note* and *Beat Drop* poke, which she can cast from complete safety. Without any built-in waveclear, you cannot match her pushing power, forcing you to endure constant spell harass.

summary: Master Yi can stall out Tryndamere's Undying Rage by channeling Meditate for damage reduction or using Alpha Strike to become untargetable.
howToPlay: To win this duel, you must bait out his defensive tools before committing your ultimate. Never trigger Undying Rage while he still has Alpha Strike available to waste your precious seconds. If he begins to channel Meditate to stall your fury, do not blindly auto-attack him; instead, use this window to position yourself for a flanking Mocking Shout when he exits his channel, or prepare Spinning Slash to chase him down once his damage reduction ends.
laneImpact: Since neither jungler can easily force a successful duel without a massive lead, the early game revolves around clearing speed and counter-jungling. If you waste Spinning Slash to initiate an invade, you risk being ran down by Highlander and Wuju Style. A poorly timed skirmish costs your team neutral objectives, as whoever mismanages their ultimate-related cooldowns loses the pressure required to secure the map.
why: This jungle matchup is a direct race of farming efficiency and ultimate timing. While you possess incredible raw damage once Battle Fury is fully stacked, Master Yi has the perfect tools to neutralise your five seconds of invulnerability. He can completely stall out your Undying Rage by timing Alpha Strike to vanish from the map, or by channeling Meditate to absorb your critical strikes with massive damage reduction.

summary: Aurelion Sol must stand still to channel Breath of Light, making him an easy target for a full Heroic Swing rotation.
howToPlay: Watch for the exact moment he breathes fire. The second he activates Breath of Light, hook onto the side walls with Heroic Swing to circle behind him, completely dodging his narrow cone of damage while shredding his health bar. If he tries to escape using Astral Flight, follow his trajectory with your movement speed from Dirty Fighting. Should you draw tower aggro, drop back and use Going Rogue to disappear into the river, maintaining map control.
laneImpact: From level one, you dictate the lane's pace. If Aurelion Sol tries to stack his passive with Singularity, you can immediately punish him with Avengerang through the wave. He cannot contest the push or trade back effectively, forcing him to farm under tower or risk dying to an aggressive dive. This heavy early pressure completely stunts his scaling, delaying his powerful late-game upgrades.
why: Aurelion Sol's main damage tool, Breath of Light, forces him to stand completely still while channeling. This static positioning is the perfect invitation for Akshan to anchor Heroic Swing on a nearby wall and execute a full circling rotation around him. Because Aurelion Sol cannot easily dodge or interrupt this movement early on, Akshan's double-shot from Dirty Fighting and physical burst easily overwhelm the mage's fragile early game.

summary: Morgana's Black Shield blocks the knockup from Howling Gale and slow from Zephyr, but Janna can still use Monsoon to push Morgana away during Soul Shackles.
howToPlay: To break the stalemate, hold your Black Shield reactively rather than using it pre-emptively. Never cast Soul Shackles while Janna has Monsoon available unless you can bait her ultimate first or corner her against a wall. Position yourself parallel to your carry to split her Zephyr pressure. If she wastes her Howling Gale to poke, immediately step forward to fish for a Dark Binding, triggering your Soul Siphon healing to win the health trade.
laneImpact: Trade dynamics revolve entirely around shield timings and positioning. Janna will shield her ADC with Eye of the Storm to win brief auto-attack trades, while you must use Tormented Shadow to match her wave clear. Neither of you can easily force a kill. A missed Dark Binding allows Janna to poke safely, whereas a wasted Black Shield leaves your carry vulnerable to a fast Howling Gale trade.
why: This lane is a pure contest of utility and reflexes. Your Black Shield is the ultimate counter to Janna's primary tools, completely absorbing the slow from Zephyr and preventing the knockup of Howling Gale. However, this safety is bidirectional. When you try to engage with Soul Shackles, Janna can easily disrupt your ultimate's tether range by activating Monsoon, pushing you back before the stun can trigger.

summary: Darius's heavy slow from Crippling Strike severely reduces Hecarim's damage output from his passive Warpath.
howToPlay: Position yourself directly between Hecarim and his nearest escape path when contesting camps. Hold Apprehend to disrupt his Devastating Charge mid-flight, or to pull him back if he tries to leap away with Onslaught of Shadows. Once he is close, auto-attack and immediately reset with Crippling Strike to crush his movement speed and passive damage. Finish him with Noxian Guillotine once Hemorrhage is fully stacked, ensuring you hit the outer edge of Decimate to stay healthy during the duel.
laneImpact: This interaction gives you absolute dominance during early scuttle crab contests and jungle invasions. Since Hecarim relies on Spirit of Dread to sustain through fights, you can easily out-damage his healing by stacking Hemorrhage. Because he cannot safely duel you near camps, he is forced to concede priority, delaying his gold generation and preventing him from using Onslaught of Shadows to gank lanes with maximum momentum.
why: Darius dominates the jungle skirmishes because Hecarim relies on high movement speed to fuel his attack damage via Warpath. When Hecarim charges in with Devastating Charge, hitting him with Crippling Strike immediately neutralizes his momentum. This severe slow instantly tanks his bonus AD, leaving his Rampage sweeps incredibly weak. Without his speed-to-damage conversion, Hecarim cannot match your sustained damage in a direct duel.

summary: Bard can use Tempered Fate to freeze Nautilus's backline, preventing them from following up on his Depth Charge.
howToPlay: Stand consistently behind your minion wave to block Dredge Line, and place Caretaker’s Shrine far behind your tower to give your ADC a safe retreat path. Never use Tempered Fate aggressively. Instead, hold it specifically for the moment Nautilus casts Depth Charge. The second you see the depth charge tracking, aim your ultimate at the enemy follow-up. If Nautilus bypasses your wave, use Cosmic Binding on him and the nearest wall to stun him.
laneImpact: You will constantly be pushed under tower because trading into Titan's Wrath shield is highly inefficient. Stepping up to collect Traveler’s Call chimes exposes you to a Dredge Line that will force a summoner spell or a bad recall. This pressure restricts your map rotations, meaning you cannot roam freely without risking your ADC dying to a dive initiated by Riptide slow and crowd control.
why: Nautilus dominates the lane space because Dredge Line and Staggering Blow easily punish your fragile health pool. However, the matchup pivots entirely around Depth Charge. When Nautilus targets your ally with this ultimate, you can cast Tempered Fate on his backline. By freezing his follow-up damage dealers in stasis, you neutralize his dive and render his ultimate-led engage useless.

summary: Soraka's Equinox silences Braum instantly, preventing him from raising Unbreakable or jumping to safety with Stand Behind Me.
howToPlay: To survive, you must play a disciplined waiting game. Never initiate with Stand Behind Me while Equinox is available. Instead, bait this silence by posturing aggressively, then immediately step back. Once her zone is wasted and on cooldown, you have a brief window to strike. Use Winter's Bite to apply Concussive Blows and look for a fast trade, or safely deploy Glacial Fissure without fear of being interrupted mid-cast.
laneImpact: This interaction warps the lane into a grueling war of attrition where Soraka slowly neutralizes your health pool. Because she can constantly top up her ally with Astral Infusion and Starcall, any short trade you attempt becomes negative. If you get caught by Equinox during a skirmish, you cannot mitigate damage, forcing early recalls and leaving your carry exposed to heavy tower pressure and lost wave control.
why: Soraka directly counters your defensive agility. The moment you step up, her Equinox silences you instantly, which completely disables your ability to raise Unbreakable to shield your marksman or cast Stand Behind Me to leap back to safety. This instant disruption leaves you extremely vulnerable, unable to block incoming projectiles or reposition, turning your usually reliable peeling tools completely offline.

summary: Sona's Aria of Perseverance out-sustains Lulu's poke, allowing her to safely reach her superior late-game teamfighting scaling.
howToPlay: To exploit this, always monitor Lulu's cooldowns, specifically Whimsy. If she uses it on her ally for attack speed, she cannot polymorph you, which is your green light to walk up and poke. Keep your distance to avoid double-hit Glitterlance angles. If Lulu uses Wild Growth to turn a fight, do not panic; immediately counter with Crescendo to lock down her giant target, then use Song of Celerity to kite back until her ultimate's health buff expires.
laneImpact: In lane, this dynamic translates to a war of attrition that Lulu cannot win. When Lulu uses Help, Pix! aggressively to poke, she leaves herself or her ADC without a shield. This creates a massive window where you can trade back with Hymn of Valor and Power Chord. Lulu is forced to play defensively, losing wave control and failing to secure the early tower pressure her kit normally demands, letting you farm safely.
why: Sona's ability to nullify Lulu's early aggression dictates this matchup. While Lulu relies on Glitterlance and Help, Pix! to chip away at your carry's health, your Aria of Perseverance completely neutralizes this poke. Because Lulu lacks a natural hard-engage to punish you, her early lane pressure is wasted, allowing you to comfortably scale into a late-game powerhouse where your team-wide auras easily outclass her single-target utility.

summary: Use Repudiation to block the knockup from Ornn's Call of the Forge God or Searing Charge, negating his primary crowd control.
howToPlay: To execute this plan, never waste Repudiation aggressively; hold it strictly for his crowd control. When Ornn casts Call of the Forge God, wait for the return ram to strike before activating your shield, or trigger it the moment he charges a wall with Searing Charge. Use Cunning Sweep to poke him down, and always dash diagonally with Drakehound's Step to avoid the breath from Bellows Breath. If he attempts to escape, secure the kill with Public Execution.
laneImpact: This interaction forces Ornn into a defensive, passive lane state. He cannot safely contest the wave with Volcanic Rupture or trade with Bellows Breath because any forward movement allows you to dash in. When you block his crucial Searing Charge knockup, he is left without escape, allowing you to freeze the wave at will or crash giant waves to chip his turret plates while he sits helplessly under tower.
why: Ambessa dominates this matchup because her high mobility bypasses Ornn's predictable patterns. While Ornn relies on hitting Searing Charge against terrain or timing his Call of the Forge God to lock you down, your Repudiation acts as a perfect counter. By absorbing his knockups and shielding his burst, you strip the tank of his crowd control, leaving him vulnerable to extended trades where Drakehound's Step out-spaces his slow cooldowns.

summary: Poppy's Steadfast Presence completely blocks Vi's Vault Breaker dash, neutralizing her primary engage and leaving her vulnerable.
howToPlay: Discipline is your greatest weapon here. Never waste Steadfast Presence just for the bonus movement speed during a jungle clear or early in a fight. Keep your finger on the key and watch Vi closely; she must charge her punch before dashing, which gives you a clear visual cue. If she bypasses your field using her unstoppable Cease and Desist, wait out the knock-up animation, then immediately use Keeper's Verdict to knock her away and reset the fight.
laneImpact: This interaction transforms neutral objective contests and river skirmishes into a nightmare for Vi. She cannot safely secure Scuttle Crabs or contest Epic Monsters because your presence threatens a complete shutdown. Should she try to force an entry with her dash, your denial leaves her stranded in the river, making her an easy target for a wall-stun via Heroic Charge and subsequent burst from your teammates.
why: Your entire advantage in this jungle matchup hinges on a single, highly reactive interaction. Vi relies heavily on charging up Vault Breaker to initiate ganks, contest camps, or gap-close onto your allies. By activating Steadfast Presence the moment she releases her charge, you completely nullify her dash, knocking her down and grounding her. Without this crucial mobility tool, her damage output collapses.

summary: When Leona lands Zenith Blade, Galio can intercept the follow-up by charging Shield of Durand to taunt the enemy ADC.
howToPlay: Pivot your playstyle entirely toward protecting your ADC. Instead of diving forward with Zenith Blade, stand close to your carry and wait for Galio to initiate with Justice Punch. The moment he dashes, intercept him using Shield of Daybreak to lock him down, and activate Eclipse to absorb his burst. Save Solar Flare to disrupt his Hero's Entrance channel if he attempts to escape or rotate to a skirmish.
laneImpact: Because of this counter-engage threat, you cannot freely fish for standard lane-phase trades. Doing so results in chunked health bars and lost lane priority, forcing you under tower where Galio can poke with Winds of War. If you fall behind, Galio will safely secure roaming windows, using Hero's Entrance to impact the map while you are stuck trying to clear waves under tower with weak pushing power.
why: This matchup is dictated by Galio's ability to completely shut down your aggressive dives. Whenever you attempt to engage by landing Zenith Blade on either target, Galio can immediately channel Shield of Durand. The massive area-of-effect taunt interrupts your ADC's follow-up before they can proc your Sunlight marks, leaving you isolated deep in their range while absorbing Winds of War and Colossal Smash damage.

summary: Yasuo's Wind Wall completely blocks Corki's Missile Barrage and Phosphorus Bomb, neutralizing his poke in teamfights.
howToPlay: You must bait out Wind Wall before committing your Missile Barrage stacks. Use basic attacks to pop his Way of the Wanderer shield first, then throw a single Phosphorus Bomb to force his defensive wall. Once Wind Wall is on cooldown, you have a brief window to abuse Gatling Gun and your rocket spam. If he dashes forward with Sweeping Blade, immediately escape backward with Valkyrie, making sure you do not get knocked up by Steel Tempest.
laneImpact: In lane, Sweeping Blade allows Yasuo to close the gap easily, bypassing your range advantage. When you try to disengage with Valkyrie, he can often catch you with a stacked Steel Tempest tornado to trigger Last Breath. This constant threat forces you under your turret, as you cannot safely trade back once your Phosphorus Bomb is blocked, sacrificing mid lane priority and leaving your jungler without early backup.
why: Yasuo severely limits your impact because his Wind Wall acts as an absolute barrier to your primary damage sources. Both your Phosphorus Bomb and your Missile Barrage are completely absorbed by his wind barrier. This means your poke-heavy gameplay is entirely neutralized during teamfights and skirmishes, forcing you to play around the high cooldown of his defensive wall rather than freely outputting consistent magic damage from a distance.

summary: Nautilus can peel Pantheon's Shield Vault with Staggering Blow, but Pantheon's Aegis Assault can block Nautilus's initial burst.
howToPlay: When ganking his lane, do not lead with your empowered stun if he is looking at you. Instead, bait his hook or walk up to pressure him. If he stops your 'Shield Vault' with 'Staggering Blow', immediately channel 'Aegis Assault' facing his direction to soak 'Depth Charge' or 'Riptide'. Once his crowd control is spent, use the increased reach of 'Comet Spear' to execute him as he tries to retreat.
laneImpact: This interaction shifts map control heavily in your favor, allowing you to invade or gank without fearing his counter-engage. Because you win early skirmishes, you can force Nautilus to stay defensive near his turrets. Your superior mobility means you can time your roams to impact the side lanes long before he can drag his slow frame to assist his teammates, snowballing your lanes.
why: Your early pressure in the river dictates this matchup. While Nautilus can disrupt your initial engage by peeling 'Shield Vault' with a well-timed 'Staggering Blow' auto-attack, his threat ends there. By immediately raising 'Aegis Assault', you completely absorb his subsequent burst from 'Titan's Wrath' and 'Riptide'. You block his primary damage window, leaving him vulnerable to your sustained physical assault.

summary: Viktor can mitigate Jayce's poke with the shield from Siphon Power, turning the lane into a pure wave-clear and positioning battle.
howToPlay: Always hold Gravity Field specifically for when Jayce attempts to jump on you. If he switches weapon forms via Transform Mercury Cannon and leaps with To the Skies!, drop the trap directly on your own feet; this stops his combo and prevents him from knocking you back with Thundering Blow. Use Siphon Power's shield to absorb his ranged poke, and focus your Hextech Ray on clearing the caster minions first.
laneImpact: Since Viktor's shield prevents Jayce from securing easy health advantages, this matchup becomes a high-tempo pushing war. If you let Jayce push you under tower, he will chip your plating using Lightning Field in cannon form. However, matching his wave clear with Hextech Ray forces him to choose between using his mana to clear waves or trying to poke you, dragging the duel into a stale neutral state.
why: Jayce's long-range poke relies on shooting projectiles through his acceleration gate, but Viktor can systematically absorb that initial burst. By timing Siphon Power onto a minion just as the shockwave approaches, Viktor gains a shield that nullifies the impact. This neutralizes Jayce's ranged lane pressure, shifting the focus away from health bars and entirely onto how quickly each champion can clear waves with Hextech Ray and Jayce's melee tools.

summary: Camille must wait for Jayce to use Thundering Blow before committing to a full Hookshot engage, otherwise he will easily knock her away.
howToPlay: To win this, position yourself near the brush to break Jayce's vision and limit his ranged auto-attacks. Never cast the second dash of Hookshot unless you see him waste Thundering Blow or if you can bait it by perching on the wall without committing. If he knocks you away, immediately trigger Adaptive Defenses with a basic attack to absorb his incoming burst, then disengage using the movement speed from Precision Protocol.
laneImpact: Because of this mechanical standoff, the early waves require extreme patience. If you get chunked by his ranged attacks early, you will be forced under tower, losing all priority and allowing Jayce to pressure your jungler. You cannot simply crash waves at will. Trades are short and sharp; using Tactical Sweep to heal back his poke is essential to maintain enough health so he cannot dive you with To the Skies!.
why: This matchup is a pure contest of spacing and reaction times. Jayce wants to abuse his ranged form with Transform Mercury Cannon to poke you down, but his ultimate safety net against your Hookshot is Thundering Blow. If you grapple onto a wall, a competent Jayce will immediately knock you away mid-air, completely canceling your primary engage tool and leaving you vulnerable to a heavy ranged counter-attack.

summary: Mordekaiser's Realm of Death isolates Lee Sin: Safeguard still moves him, but the arena is far too cramped to escape through.
howToPlay: Position yourself aggressively between Lee Sin and his escape routes near jungle walls. Never initiate with Death's Grasp; instead, save it to pull him back if he attempts to run before you cast Realm of Death. When he lands Sonic Wave on you, activate Indestructible to absorb the incoming burst of his second activation, then immediately pull him into your ultimate. If he manages to kick you away with Dragon's Rage first, walk back to your camps and farm up.
laneImpact: This dynamic alters how you contest neutral monsters. Lee Sin cannot comfortably contest the Rift Scuttler or invade your jungle camps because stepping too close means risking a forced duel. If he attempts to steal a camp, your ability to isolate him prevents any quick escape over walls. This constant threat forces him to play passively, granting you uncontested pressure and making his early-game ganking presence much riskier to execute.
why: This jungle matchup turns heavily in your favor once you unlock your ultimate. Lee Sin relies on high mobility to escape, but your Realm of Death completely strips him of this option. Inside your realm, Safeguard still moves him but the arena is far too cramped to disengage through. Trapped in the duel, he is forced into a direct duel against your Darkness Rise aura where your magic damage simply melts his assassin defense.

summary: Vi can use Vault Breaker to escape Cataclysm or interrupt Jarvan's Dragon Strike knockup mid-air.
howToPlay: To survive, never lead with your Demacian Standard and Dragon Strike combo. Instead, walk up, slow her with Golden Aegis, and bait out her Vault Breaker first. Only drop your Cataclysm once she has used her dash, forcing her to flash or burn Cease and Desist defensively. If she targets an ally with her ultimate, use that exact window of her fixed trajectory to position your flag and knock her up the moment her unstoppable state ends.
laneImpact: In the jungle, this interaction severely limits your skirmishing power. You cannot safely contest scuttle crabs or objectives 1v1 because she shreds your armor via Denting Blows while ignoring your crowd control. Initiating ganks becomes a gamble; if she counters your gank, her ability to nullify Cataclysm means you cannot reliably trap her or protect your laners, giving her team massive map pressure and objective control.
why: This matchup is highly unfavorable because Vi has the perfect tools to dismantle your engage tools. When you attempt your signature Demacian Standard and Dragon Strike knockup, a well-timed Vault Breaker can stop you dead in your tracks mid-air. Furthermore, the arena created by your Cataclysm is easily bypassed, as Vi can simply charge through the physical barrier using Vault Breaker or ignore your lockdown entirely with Cease and Desist.

summary: Ornn can use Call of the Forge God to engage on Teemo from long range, as Teemo lacks any dashes to escape the knockup.
howToPlay: Let the wave crash and use Volcanic Rupture to safely last-hit from a distance. Save Searing Charge strictly for disengaging when Teemo tries to chase you down with Move Quick, rather than using it to trade. Once you unlock Call of the Forge God, call for your jungler and initiate from long range; Teemo's lack of mobility tools makes him incredibly vulnerable to your ram's knock-up, turning an oppressive lane into an easy kill.
laneImpact: The lane quickly becomes a war of attrition where you must concede early priority. Teemo will constantly push the wave, using Noxious Trap to secure the river and lane bushes. If you step up to contest minions with basic attacks, you will lose massive health. Your tower will constantly be under pressure, forcing you to craft items under turret using Living Forge to avoid bad recalls.
why: Teemo's constant harassment with Toxic Shot and Blinding Dart severely punishes your melee range, forcing you to play defensively. Since Ornn cannot easily close the gap early on without taking heavy damage, Teemo controls the spacing using Move Quick. However, because Teemo has no hard dashes to dodge skillshots, your Call of the Forge God acts as the ultimate equalizer, enabling long-range engages he cannot easily escape.

summary: Ziggs uses Bouncing Bomb to safely clear waves from afar, preventing Annie from ever finding an angle to engage directly.
howToPlay: Do not waste your mana trying to match his shove. Instead, use Molten Shield to absorb damage from Bouncing Bomb when stepping forward, and save your Pyromania charge. Your only window to strike is when he mispositions or uses Satchel Charge offensively; immediately activate Molten Shield for the movement speed burst, close the gap, and drop Summon: Tibbers. If he plays perfectly safe, accept the farm deficit and wait for your jungler to lock him down before committing.
laneImpact: This endless pressure forces you to constantly farm under your own turret using Disintegrate to conserve mana. You cannot easily match his wave clear, meaning Ziggs will frequently trap you in lane while threatening your turret with Satchel Charge. If you leave to help your jungler, you risk losing multiple plates, as his Hexplosive Minefield easily blocks your return path and delays your rotations.
why: Ziggs completely neutralizes your aggressive threat by using Bouncing Bomb to demolish minion waves from a safe distance, well outside the range of your Pyromania stun. Because he never needs to step up into the threat range of Disintegrate or Incinerate, you are left holding your stun charge with no targets to hit, while his Short Fuse passive guarantees he out-pokes you if you attempt to force an awkward trade.

summary: Nocturne can block Diana's Crescent Strike or Moonfall with Shroud of Darkness, negating her reset or her primary burst.
howToPlay: To win skirmishes, you must bait out Shroud of Darkness before committing your main damage. Initiate with basic attacks empowered by Moonsilver Blade or trigger Pale Cascade to crack his shield if he deploys it early. Never cast Moonfall while his spell shield is active. If he targets you with Unspeakable Horror, use Lunar Rush to dash to a nearby enemy minion or monster to break the fear tether before turning back to fight.
laneImpact: You cannot safely contest Nocturne in the river or duel him near camps. If he intercepts your ganks using Paranoia, his Unspeakable Horror will fear you before your Pale Cascade shield can absorb his Duskbringer-empowered auto-attacks. This forces you to play defensively, conceding early Scuttle Crabs and prioritizing safe, reactive farm rather than attempting aggressive invades, which slows down your ability to snowball.
why: Nocturne holds a massive advantage because his Shroud of Darkness completely neutralizes your offensive flow. If he blocks your Crescent Strike, you lose the Moonlight mark, preventing any Lunar Rush reset and leaving you stranded. Alternatively, he can reactively absorb the entire impact of your Moonfall, stripping away your primary burst tool while gaining a massive attack speed boost to shred you down.

summary: Rammus's Defensive Ball Curl severely punishes Ambessa's basic-attack-heavy passive, while Frenzying Taunt prevents her from using her dashes.
howToPlay: Rush physical defense immediately to scale your *Rolling Armordillo* passive and maximize *Defensive Ball Curl* damage. During skirmishes, do not initiate with *Frenzying Taunt* if her *Repudiation* shield is active, as it blocks crowd control. Instead, roll in with *Powerball*, wait out her defensive shield, then taunt her mid-dash to cancel her *Cunning Sweep* setup. If she jumps your backline with *Public Execution*, immediately peel with your ultimate, *Soaring Slam*.
laneImpact: This matchup secures you absolute dominance during river skirmishes and jungle invasions. Ambessa cannot comfortably contest Scuttle Crabs or secure objectives when you are nearby, as any duel ends in her self-destruction. Her ganking pressure is heavily mitigated because you can counter-gank and lock her down before she completes *Public Execution*, rendering her high-mobility assassin threat useless and forcing her to fall behind in gold.
why: Ambessa relies heavily on chaining abilities with *Drakehound's Step* to dash and land empowered basic attacks. Rammus completely neutralizes this flow. Activating *Defensive Ball Curl* turns her own high-frequency passive attacks into self-inflicted physical damage. Furthermore, applying *Frenzying Taunt* interrupts her mobility loop entirely, forcing her to auto-attack your spiked shell while preventing her from executing *Cunning Sweep* or escaping with her dashes.

summary: When Leona engages with Zenith Blade, Braum can use Stand Behind Me to protect his ADC and easily trigger Concussive Blows on her.
howToPlay: Position yourself slightly behind or parallel to your ADC to always keep them within the jump range of Stand Behind Me. Never waste Winter's Bite on poke; save it to instantly stack Concussive Blows on Leona the moment she lands her Zenith Blade. If she targets you instead, immediately raise Unbreakable facing her ADC to block the follow-up damage from Solar Flare while your ally turns the trade on the CC-locked Leona.
laneImpact: This dynamic strips Leona of her primary lane pressure. She cannot safely fish for Zenith Blade initiates because any successful hook results in her taking a massive chunk of damage. Your ADC can safely farm or even freeze the wave near your tower, knowing that Leona's engage will only trigger a deadly counter-strike. This forces her into passivity, preventing her from securing easy bush control or roaming to mid lane.
why: Braum naturally neutralizes Leona's aggressive tools. When Leona dives in with Zenith Blade, she places herself directly next to your carry, which is the perfect setup for Stand Behind Me. By jumping to your ally, you immediately gain defensive stats while positioning yourself to tag Leona with Concussive Blows. Since she must commit to her Shield of Daybreak stun, she cannot escape your passive's stun buildup, completely turning her engage attempt against her.

summary: Yasuo can completely nullify Ahri's burst and pick potential by blocking her Charm with his Wind Wall.
howToPlay: To survive, break his Way of the Wanderer shield with a simple basic attack before attempting any trade. Never cast Charm unless you have baited out his Wind Wall, which has a massive cooldown; instead, use Fox-Fire to gain movement speed and dodge his Steel Tempest tornadoes. If he dashes forward with Sweeping Blade, use Spirit Rush to reposition laterally, escaping his linear threat zone while keeping your distance until his wall expires.
laneImpact: You are forced into a defensive posture, as Yasuo easily clears waves using Steel Tempest and Sweeping Blade. If you throw Charm blindly, he will block it, dash through your minions, and force a lethal trade with Last Breath once he knocks you up. This constant threat forces you to save your mana and restrict your Orb of Deception solely to farming under or near your tower.
why: Yasuo controls the pace of this lane because his Wind Wall completely negates your primary setup tool, Charm, alongside your Orb of Deception. Since your entire burst relies on hitting that single projectile to amplify subsequent damage, his wall leaves you highly vulnerable. Furthermore, his Way of the Wanderer passive constantly absorbs your basic attack poke, making it incredibly difficult to chunk him down before he finds an engage angle.

summary: Jax can use Counter Strike to completely stall out Tryndamere's Undying Rage duration by blocking all of his basic attacks.
howToPlay: Survival depends on baiting out Counter Strike without committing your mobility. When Jax activates his dodge, immediately use Spinning Slash to retreat rather than fighting back. If he uses Leap Strike to follow, cast Mocking Shout to reduce his physical damage and slow his chase. Never activate Undying Rage while his dodge is available; instead, wait out the stun, and only use your ultimate to escape toward your tower or a wall you can dash over.
laneImpact: This interaction strips away your lane control, forcing you to play defensively under your turret. You cannot freely attack the wave to build Battle Fury because Jax will punish you with Leap Strike and Empower. Since trading is heavily skewed in his favor, you will constantly find yourself low on health, forcing early activations of Bloodlust just to stay in experience range, which completely kills your kill pressure.
why: Jax completely neutralizes your offensive pressure because Counter Strike blocks all basic attacks, which are your sole source of damage and Battle Fury generation. The matchup becomes incredibly oppressive once both of you have ultimates; when you activate Undying Rage to survive death, Jax simply uses Counter Strike to dodge your attacks for two seconds, running down your invulnerability timer and preventing you from healing with Bloodlust.

summary: Diana's Crescent Strike reveals Evelynn even if she is in Demon Shade, preventing her from escaping or setting up an ambush.
howToPlay: Actively track Evelynn's pathing and sweep high-traffic bushes. When she casts Allure on you, do not panic or retreat; instead, predict her approach angle and throw Crescent Strike to reveal her inside Demon Shade. Instantly follow up with Lunar Rush, activate Pale Cascade to absorb her initial Hate Spike damage, and pull her in with Moonfall. If she manages to slip away using Last Caress, immediately ping your team to seize the neutral objective she can no longer contest.
laneImpact: This interaction shifts the entire jungle dynamic in your favor. Knowing you can strip her stealth makes her jungle camps unsafe to farm. When she attempts to secure objectives or gank, you can aggressively counter-jungle and hunt her down. She cannot easily escape your burst with Last Caress if you force her to use it defensively early, rendering her unable to pressure your lanes effectively.
why: Diana completely shuts down Evelynn's stealth-based jungle pressure. The core of this matchup lies in Crescent Strike, which grants true sight on anything it hits. When Evelynn tries to stalk you or your teammates in Demon Shade, landing this crescent arc exposes her immediately. This negates her element of surprise, preventing her from comfortably cooking Allure, and opens her up to an immediate, lethal dive.

summary: Poppy's Steadfast Presence grounds and damages K'Santé whenever he attempts to use Footwork or Path Maker to reposition.
howToPlay: Position yourself parallel to the river and alcove walls to constantly threaten a wall-slam. Never initiate trades with Steadfast Presence; hold it strictly to react to his Footwork or Path Maker animations. If he goes All Out, don't panic. Immediately use the uncharged version of Keeper's Verdict to knock him airborne, neutralizing his stat-boosted aggression and allowing you to easily reposition or re-engage on your terms.
laneImpact: Because K'Santé cannot dash without being punished, you dictate the lane's tempo. He cannot easily stack Ntofo Strikes without exposing himself to a devastating wall-stun from Heroic Charge. This fear forces him to yield wave control, allowing you to crash waves at will, harass him under tower with Iron Ambassador passive bucklers, and secure early river priority to assist your jungler.
why: Poppy controls this matchup because Steadfast Presence completely neutralizes K'Santé's mobility tools. Whenever K'Santé attempts to reposition with Footwork or charge forward using Path Maker, your active barrier stops him in his tracks, dealing magic damage and grounding him. This converts his main defensive and positioning tools into self-sabotaging abilities, leaving him vulnerable and unable to escape your trading range.

summary: Garen should save Courage to mitigate Mordekaiser's isolated Obliterate damage during Realm of Death.
howToPlay: Pivot your build path toward early magic penetration to bypass his magic resistance. In combat, never cast Realm of Death while Garen still has Courage available, or use your isolated Obliterate first to bait his shield before trapping him. If he attempts to execute you with Demacian Justice, time your Indestructible at the absolute last microsecond to convert your stored damage into a massive shield that completely absorbs his ultimate's true damage.
laneImpact: Garen will try to neutralize your pressure by using Perseverance to heal up between waves. You must actively disrupt this by landing Obliterate to keep his passive offline. Because Garen lacks dash tools, a successful Death's Grasp guarantees an extended trade where your passive burns him down, forcing him to play defensively under tower or risk dying to Demacian Justice counters with Indestructible.
why: You hold a distinct advantage because Garen relies on short trades with Decisive Strike and Judgment, while your passive Darkness Rise excels in extended duels. The match hinges on how he uses Courage. Inside your Realm of Death, Garen is forced to hold Courage to block your isolated Obliterate strikes. If he wastes his shield early, your raw magic damage easily overcomes his natural tankiness.

summary: Draven can use Stand Aside to interrupt Tristana's Rocket Jump mid-air, leaving her stranded and vulnerable to his high DPS.
howToPlay: To survive, you must play defensively and strictly hold Rocket Jump as a reactive tool. Never initiate with it. Watch Draven's axes; if he drops a Spinning Axe or wastes Stand Aside trying to poke or push, you have a temporary window to retaliate. If he catches you with an aggressive engage, use Buster Shot to push him away instantly and disengage, relying on your passive Draw a Bead to safely farm from a distance as you scale.
laneImpact: Because of this airborne interruption, you cannot freely contest early waves. Draven easily secures lane priority with his high raw damage, forcing you to farm under turret. Any attempt to trade back with Rapid Fire feels underwhelming because you cannot commit to an all-in. If you get chunked while your escape is disabled, you will be forced into a bad recall, losing plates to his fast push.
why: This matchup is heavily dictated by Draven's ability to swat you out of the air. If you attempt an aggressive Rocket Jump, a skilled Draven will reactively cast Stand Aside mid-flight. This immediately cancels your leap's momentum, dropping you directly into his optimal range where his Spinning Axe and Blood Rush DPS will shred your health bar before you can stack Explosive Charge.

summary: Morgana's Black Shield (E) completely negates the stun from CH-2 Electron Storm Grenade (E), preventing Heimerdinger's burst setup.
howToPlay: Never waste Black Shield proactively; hold it exclusively for the moment you see his CH-2 Electron Storm Grenade in the air. Place Tormented Shadow directly on top of his H-28G Evolution Turret setups to drain their health from a safe distance, forcing him to waste mana replacing them. If he plays too far forward without his machines to protect him, throw Dark Binding to root him, then follow up with Soul Shackles to force his Flash or secure a kill.
laneImpact: Because both of you possess incredible wave-clearing tools, the lane naturally stalls out into a passive farming simulator. Heimerdinger will constantly push with H-28G Evolution Turret, but you can match his pressure instantly by dropping Tormented Shadow under his machines. Neither champion can easily dive or force a solo kill under tower. This neutralizes active map pressure, locking both mid laners in place while testing who can maintain perfect CS under constant pressure.
why: This matchup is a pure battle of attrition determined by your reaction time. Heimerdinger relies on landing CH-2 Electron Storm Grenade to trigger his H-28G Evolution Turret laser beams and maximize Hextech Micro-Rockets damage. By shielding yourself with Black Shield, you completely negate the stun. Without this crowd control, Heimerdinger cannot reliably lock you down for his turrets to shred your health bar, neutralizing his primary kill threat.

summary: Vladimir can use Sanguine Pool to evade Unleashed Power, so Syndra must force his pool out with basic Q-W-E combos first.
howToPlay: Never use Sanguine Pool to dodge a simple Dark Sphere or even Scatter the Weak unless you are at risk of dying. Instead, absorb her basic spells and heal back with your empowered Transfusion. Save your pool exclusively for the moment she casts Unleashed Power. Once she wastes her ultimate into your pool, you can immediately retaliate with Hemoplague and Tides of Blood to turn the fight in your favor.
laneImpact: You will spend the early levels absorbing pressure, relying on Transfusion to heal back her constant Dark Sphere poke. If she successfully baits your Sanguine Pool with a Force of Will slow, you lose a massive chunk of your current health and become incredibly vulnerable to a dive. This forces you to play defensively under turret, sacrificing early priority to secure your scaling.
why: Syndra outranges you and constantly threatens with her Dark Sphere and Scatter the Weak stun. However, this matchup hinges entirely on a specific interaction: your Sanguine Pool can completely dodge her Unleashed Power. Because of this, Syndra cannot simply burst you down; she must first poke you down and force you to panic-cast your pool using her basic combos before she can safely commit her ultimate.

summary: Zyra's Grasping Roots and Stranglethorns are ground-based spells that bypass Braum's Unbreakable shield entirely.
howToPlay: To survive, adopt a passive positioning rule: never stand directly parallel to your carry, or Grasping Roots will snare you both. Keep Stand Behind Me ready exclusively as an escape tool to leap backward to a caster minion when Stranglethorns is cast. Do not waste Unbreakable on her basic attacks; hold it to mitigate the rapid spitfire of her plants after she misses her root. Only look for a counter-engage with Glacial Fissure when your jungler arrives.
laneImpact: This mechanical loophole destroys your lane presence. Zyra easily establishes bush control using Garden of Thorns, spawning spitting plants that constantly block your Winter's Bite. You are forced to absorb poke under your own turret, losing health every time you try to step up. Because you cannot safely use Stand Behind Me to shield your carry from her root, your ADC is constantly zoned away from the minion wave.
why: Braum suffers immensely because his iconic defensive tool, Unbreakable, is utterly useless against Zyra's primary crowd control. Both Grasping Roots and her ultimate, Stranglethorns, are ground-based hazards. Since they erupt from beneath rather than traveling as standard projectiles, Unbreakable cannot intercept or block them. This mechanical bypass leaves Braum and his carry completely exposed to her plants and zone control without any reliable damage mitigation.

summary: Malphite's Ground Slam drastically reduces Jax's attack speed, while Seismic Shard prevents Jax from sticking to him even after using Leap Strike.
howToPlay: Focus entirely on survival and scaling. Pivot your build path toward magic defense and tenacity instead of raw offensive power. Never initiate trades with Leap Strike; instead, save it strictly to escape or jump to safety after he slows you with Seismic Shard. Only activate Counter Strike when his Thunderclap is active to block his empowered auto-attacks, then retreat immediately once his Ground Slam debuff hits you.
laneImpact: This interaction destroys your trading power. You cannot safely contest waves because Malphite can constantly poke you down, safely protected by his Granite Shield. Any attempt to force a prolonged trade will fail as your auto-attacks slow to a crawl under his debuff. This forces you under your own turret, bleeding farm and letting him roam freely with Unstoppable Force to impact the map while you struggle to clear.
why: Malphite completely shuts down your offensive engine. When you engage, his Ground Slam cripples your attack speed, neutralizing the scaling speed from Relentless Assault and the extra procs of Grandmaster-at-Arms. Even if you try to stick to him using Leap Strike, he uses Seismic Shard to steal your movement speed and walk away unharmed, leaving you vulnerable with no mobility left.

summary: Galio can taunt Aurora with Shield of Durand (W) when she attempts to use Across the Veil (W) or jump around with Between Worlds (R).
howToPlay: To secure your lead, never waste Shield of Durand to initiate randomly. Hold this ability specifically to intercept her movement paths when she activates Across the Veil or attempts to hop between the edges of Between Worlds. If she tries to disengage by pushing you away with The Weirding, immediately follow up with Justice Punch to close the gap, ensuring she cannot escape while her primary defensive tools are down.
laneImpact: In practice, this dynamic cripples Aurora's laning pressure. She cannot safely fish for trades with Twofold Hex because stepping forward risks a devastating counter-engage. By fast-clearing waves using Winds of War and Colossal Smash, you force her to defend her turret. This deprives her of roaming opportunities, neutralizing her impact on the map while you secure free priority.
why: This matchup favors Galio because his crowd control completely shuts down Aurora's elusive patterns. When she attempts to slip away using Across the Veil or leap across the borders of Between Worlds, charging Shield of Durand instantly disrupts her. Since the taunt is a large area-of-effect spell, her brief stealth and teleports cannot save her from being locked down and exposed mid-flight.

summary: Swinging with Heroic Swing over Taliyah's Unraveled Earth triggers the mines, dealing massive damage and interrupting your movement.
howToPlay: To survive, you must play as a passive marksman. Keep your distance and focus on farming with Avengerang, saving Heroic Swing exclusively as a defensive retreat after Taliyah has already wasted Unraveled Earth. If she holds her mines, never swing forward. When she roams with Weaver's Wall, do not try to follow her directly; instead, push the wave immediately and use Comeuppance to pressure her mid-lane tower.
laneImpact: Because you cannot use Heroic Swing aggressively, you lose the ability to force short health trades. Taliyah easily shoves the lane using Threaded Volley, forcing you under turret. If you try to match her push with Avengerang, you risk getting caught by Seismic Shove. This constant pressure prevents you from roaming to revive allies with Going Rogue, while Taliyah freely roams using Rock Surfing and Weaver's Wall.
why: This matchup is a structural nightmare for Akshan because your primary mobility tool, Heroic Swing, is completely neutralized by Taliyah. The moment you attempt to swing, she can reactively cast Unraveled Earth. Passing through her minefield instantly detonates the rocks, dealing devastating burst damage and stopping your movement mid-air, leaving you completely vulnerable to an easy Seismic Shove knockback.

summary: Jayce's Thundering Blow knockback is negated by Goes Where He Pleases, preventing him from disengaging when Mundo runs him down with Maximum Dosage.
howToPlay: Focus on farming with Infected Bonesaw and Blunt Force Trauma to secure lasthits safely while preserving your passive container. Do not engage actively until you have Maximum Dosage ready. Once you decide to fight, run directly at him to force him to waste Thundering Blow on your Goes Where He Pleases shield, then immediately activate Heart Zapper to absorb his remaining burst and finish him.
laneImpact: Jayce's range advantage is neutralized by holding the minion wave close to your turret. By keeping the wave frozen on your side, you deny him the long lane space he needs to poke you. If he overextends to break this freeze, he is entirely vulnerable. He must choose between losing farm or stepping up into a deadly chase where his hammer knockback cannot save him.
why: This matchup swings heavily in your favor because Jayce's primary tool for self-peel, Thundering Blow, is entirely neutralized by your passive, Goes Where He Pleases. When Jayce switches to hammer form to knock you away, your passive absorbs the displacement. This leaves him completely defenseless when you activate Maximum Dosage to run him down, turning his melee range transition into a death trap.

summary: Brand can easily land Pillar of Flame on Veigar when Veigar stops to last-hit with Baleful Strike.
howToPlay: Watch your own low-health minions closely. The exact millisecond Veigar steps forward and faces a minion to cast Baleful Strike, immediately drop Pillar of Flame on him. If he attempts to retaliate by trapping you inside Event Horizon, do not panic and run into the stun wall. Stand your ground inside the cage, dodge his delayed Dark Matter, and prepare to fire Sear to stun him the moment he tries to close the distance for a Primordial Burst.
laneImpact: Your ability to punish his last-hitting gives you absolute control over the minion waves. By constantly shoving him under turret with Conflagration and Pillar of Flame, you force him to burn mana farming instead of stacking. He will be too low on health to step up and trap you with Event Horizon, rendering him useless for his jungler and giving you free roam priority.
why: This matchup is heavily in your favor because Veigar must constantly pause his movement to cast Baleful Strike for his Phenomenal Evil Power stacks. This brief self-root is the perfect window to place Pillar of Flame right under his feet. Since his early waveclear is slow and predictable, you can easily force him to choose between losing gold or taking massive magic damage from your passive, Blaze.

summary: Olaf can activate Ragnarok to completely negate Sett's Facebreaker and The Show Stopper, but must dodge or flash the true damage center of Haymaker.
howToPlay: To survive, you must play around the duration of Ragnarok. Never initiate with The Show Stopper; instead, bait his ultimate by walking up with Knuckle Down, then immediately retreat. Hold Facebreaker specifically to disrupt his Undertow axes when his crowd control immunity is offline. If he triggers his ultimate, immediately charge your Haymaker grit, aiming the central line carefully to force his flash or punish his straightforward chase when he tries to finish you off.
