laneImpact: Once Olaf reaches level five, the lane dynamic shifts heavily in his favor, preventing you from ever freezing safely. If you attempt extended trades, Undertow slows you down, allowing him to run you down with Berserker Rage and Vicious Strikes. This constant threat forces you to concede wave priority, meaning you will often find yourself shoved under tower, slowly bleeding health while trying to farm under immense pressure.
why: Olaf holds a massive advantage because Ragnarok completely nullifies both your Facebreaker stun and your ultimate, The Show Stopper, stripping away your ability to peel or lock him down. Since his ultimate makes him immune to your crowd control, his only real threat is the true damage sweet spot of Haymaker. However, if he manages to flash or sidestep that central blast, your entire kit's high-impact threat is neutralized.

summary: Thresh can use Flay to interrupt Galio's Justice Punch mid-dash, preventing him from reaching the ADC.
howToPlay: To bypass this, never lead with Justice Punch from a distance where Thresh can see you coming. Instead, position yourself parallel to your ADC and use the brush to hide your windup. Force him to use Flay offensively first. If he misses a Death Sentence, walk up directly to threaten with Shield of Durand's taunt, and only use your dash to follow up once his sweep is on cooldown.
laneImpact: Because of this interaction, you cannot easily force trades. If you telegraph your Justice Punch, Thresh will deny you and immediately respond with Death Sentence or The Box to lock you down. This creates a tense standoff where both duos must play respectfully; any failed dash from you translates directly into massive health losses or a forced, early Shield of Durand to survive.
why: This lane is a pure skill matchup dictated by how Thresh responds to your engage. The primary bottleneck is his Flay, which can easily knock you out of Justice Punch mid-flight. If he reacts quickly enough, your main closing tool is completely cancelled, leaving you stranded while his ADC free-fires, turning your aggressive engage into a disastrous counter-engage.

summary: Varus can stop Kai'Sa's dive mid-flight by hitting her with Chain of Corruption as she uses Killer Instinct.
howToPlay: Always position yourself behind your own minion wave to dilute the missiles from her Icathian Rain. Keep a constant eye on her Void Seeker; if she lands it, be ready for her to engage. Crucially, never initiate trades with Chain of Corruption. Hold this ultimate specifically for her dive. The moment she activates Killer Instinct to dash toward you, fire your ultimate directly at her incoming path to root her mid-flight, then detonate your Blighted Quiver charges with a fully charged Piercing Arrow.
laneImpact: This range differential forces Kai'Sa to play defensively under her turret, bleeding gold. She cannot easily trigger her Second Skin passive without stepping into your wave-clear. Whenever you trigger Living Vengeance by killing minions, your increased attack speed lets you apply Blighted Quiver stacks effortlessly. Kai'Sa is forced to burn Supercharge defensively to dodge your skillshots or risk getting chunked out, losing all mid priority and lane control.
why: Varus naturally dictates this mid lane matchup through sheer range superiority. Your Piercing Arrow and Hail of Arrows easily outreach Kai'Sa's Icathian Rain, allowing you to poke her down from absolute safety. More importantly, her primary tool for closing the distance and bursting you, Killer Instinct, is completely countered by your ultimate. By casting Chain of Corruption directly into her incoming flight path, you stop her dive mid-air, leaving her isolated and vulnerable.

summary: Senna's basic attacks and Piercing Darkness are non-projectiles that completely bypass Braum's Unbreakable shield.
howToPlay: To survive, you must position defensively behind your minion wave, using Stand Behind Me to escape to a backline ally whenever Senna steps forward to trade. Never waste Unbreakable trying to block her basic attacks; instead, hold it strictly to mitigate incoming damage from her partner or to block Last Embrace if it's thrown at an ally behind you. If you get chunked too low, concede the outer turret rather than risking a dive, and wait to setup a counter-engage with Glacial Fissure under safer conditions.
laneImpact: Because your shield offers no safety, Senna dictates the wave's tempo from level one. She can freely poke you down under your own turret, generating massive gold and range advantages. If you step up to help clear or retaliate, she easily lands Last Embrace to root you. This constant health drain forces premature recalls, leaving your tower vulnerable and destroying your team's early dragon priority.
why: This matchup is exceptionally punishing because Senna fundamentally invalidates your primary defensive tool. Her basic attacks and Piercing Darkness are laser-like, non-projectile attacks. This means they completely bypass the damage reduction and blocking properties of your Unbreakable shield. Instead of absorbing the threat for your marksman, holding up your shield simply leaves you exposed to her relentless poke while she safely harvests souls.

summary: Lux can easily react to Lissandra's Glacial Path trajectory by throwing Light Binding at her destination, securing a full burst combo.
howToPlay: Maintain maximum distance, staying well outside the range of her Flash combined with Ring of Frost or Frozen Tomb. Always hold Light Binding as your primary self-peel tool; never throw it blindly. Instead, poke continuously with Lucent Singularity and pop the Illumination mark when safe. If she attempts to escape or engage with Glacial Path, aim your root at the very tip of the claw to secure an easy full-combo kill.
laneImpact: This interaction forces Lissandra into a defensive posture, preventing her from using Ice Shard to push waves safely. Since she cannot step up without taking heavy damage from Lucent Singularity, you command the mid lane's tempo. She cannot easily look for roams using Glacial Path because any aggressive movement towards the side brush is met with a zoning Lucent Singularity, keeping her trapped under her own turret.
why: You hold a massive range advantage that completely denies Lissandra's threat. Her only tool to engage or trade with you is Glacial Path, which has a highly visible and slow trajectory. Because you can easily track this claw, you can throw Light Binding directly at its destination. Once she teleports, she is immediately rooted, allowing you to follow up with Lucent Singularity and Final Spark before she can ever reach you.

summary: Yasuo's Wind Wall can completely block Syndra's Unleashed Power and her Scatter the Weak sphere projectiles, forcing her to bait his wall before committing.
howToPlay: To survive, break his Way of the Wanderer shield with basic attacks or a quick Dark Sphere before initiating any trade. Never commit your ultimate, Unleashed Power, while his defensive wall is available. Instead, use Force of Will to reposition spheres at unexpected angles, or fake an engage to force out his Wind Wall. Once that barrier disappears, you have a clear window where you can safely use Scatter the Weak to stun him and unleash your full combo.
laneImpact: This interaction forces you into a highly defensive posture where you cannot contest the wave freely. Yasuo will use Sweeping Blade through your minions to close the gap, aiming to pop your passive shield from Way of the Wanderer and bait your spells. If you panic and waste Scatter the Weak into his wall, he gains total lane control, zoning you from gold and threatening a fatal Last Breath combo.
why: Yasuo's Wind Wall is a massive hurdle in this lane because it completely deletes your primary damage threat and defensive tools. When you try to burst him down with Unleashed Power, a well-timed wall absorbs every single sphere. Furthermore, your crucial stun from Scatter the Weak is also blocked, leaving you completely vulnerable to his Sweeping Blade engage without any way to push him back.

summary: Viktor's Arcane Storm instantly interrupts your Death Lotus channel while dealing heavy magic damage.
howToPlay: Never use Arcane Storm proactively to poke. Keep it strictly in reserve for when she commits to Death Lotus. Place Gravity Field directly on top of her dropped Bouncing Blade daggers or onto yourself when she uses Shunpo to force an immediate stun. Trade with Siphon Power to absorb her initial daggers' damage, and continuously chip her down with Hextech Ray from max range. If she roams, push hard to deny her plates instead of blindly following her into unwarded areas.
laneImpact: This interaction completely strips Katarina of her kill pressure under your turret, allowing you to shove waves relentlessly with Hextech Ray. She cannot step up to clear without taking heavy poke, and her usual roam timings are delayed because she is constantly trapped under tower. Any attempt to engage with Shunpo onto a Bouncing Blade dagger is easily punished, turning her lane into a desperate search for scraps.
why: Viktor dominates this matchup because Arcane Storm acts as a hard stop to Katarina's ultimate. The moment she channels Death Lotus, you can instantly drop your storm to cancel her channel entirely while blasting her with massive magic damage. Since her main damage source is shut down immediately, her Shunpo resets and Voracity passive become useless, leaving her highly vulnerable after her initial engage.

summary: Olaf's Ragnarok makes him completely immune to your CH-2 Electron Storm Grenade stun, allowing him to run you down with Undertow.
howToPlay: To survive, you must play strictly near your outer tower, utilizing the bonus movement speed from Hextech Affinity to dodge Undertow axes. Never throw your CH-2 Electron Storm Grenade proactively; hold it to bait his ultimate early or to disengage when Ragnarok is down. If Olaf dives you with Ragnarok active, immediately deploy UPGRADE!!! combined with H-28G Evolution Turret to create a massive zone of damage that might force a trade.
laneImpact: This matchup forces you into an extremely passive stance under your own turret. You cannot safely contest waves or set up your H-28G Evolution Turret nest past the river. If you push, Olaf will simply freeze, activate Ragnarok, and chase you down the long top lane. This constant threat deprives you of lane priority, meaning you cannot assist with top-side skirmishes.
why: Facing Olaf is a structural nightmare because your primary self-defense tool, CH-2 Electron Storm Grenade, is completely neutralized once he activates Ragnarok. Without that stun, you cannot halt his advance. He can easily shrug off your crowd control, close the gap using the movement speed from his ultimate, and repeatedly slow you with Undertow while shredding your health bar.

summary: Gwen's Hallowed Mist completely negates your first two The Darkin Blade casts if she positions it correctly.
howToPlay: To survive, you must adjust your positioning during skirmishes. Never cast your initial The Darkin Blade strikes at maximum range while her Hallowed Mist is active. Instead, walk directly toward her to bait out Skip 'n Slash, then use Umbral Dash to close the distance and fight inside her circle. If you fail to enter her mist, retreat immediately and throw Infernal Chains to slow her pursuit until her zone dissipates.
laneImpact: This interaction destroys your ability to contest Scuttle Crabs or invade her jungle camps. Since you cannot lock her down inside her zone, she wins every duel. If your initial combo fails, she retaliates instantly using Snip Snip! and Needlework, driving you out of your own jungle. This forces you to concede early objective priority, leaving your laners exposed to her high-scaling ganks.
why: Gwen completely counters Aatrox in the jungle due to her Hallowed Mist. When you attempt to space her using the first two casts of The Darkin Blade, she deploys her mist to render herself completely untargetable from outside its zone. Because your initial Q strikes rely on medium-range sweetspots, they deal zero damage and fail to knock her up, leaving you vulnerable as she scales uncontrollably.

summary: Gwen can use Hallowed Mist to make herself immune to Diana's Crescent Strike from range, preventing Diana from getting her Lunar Rush reset.
howToPlay: To survive, never throw Crescent Strike from maximum range while her Hallowed Mist is available. Instead, position yourself to bait out her defensive zone by pathing closely, or wait until she commits her Skip 'n Slash forward. Once her mist fades, quickly execute your Crescent Strike into Lunar Rush combo. If caught inside her Hallowed Mist, immediately trigger Moonfall to disrupt her Snip Snip! and buy time for your Pale Cascade to absorb her initial burst before disengaging.
laneImpact: This interaction forces you to play defensively around neutral objectives and your own camps. You cannot safely contest scuttle crabs or early drakes if Gwen is present, as she can deploy Hallowed Mist to deny your initiation and then run you down with Skip 'n Slash. This limits your map pressure, forcing you to concede early skirmishes and rely on lanes to setup ganks instead of taking solo fights.
why: Gwen dominates this jungle duel because her Hallowed Mist completely nullifies your Crescent Strike from a distance. If you cannot land this projectile, you cannot apply the Moonlight mark required to reset Lunar Rush. Without your high-mobility resets, you are forced into a prolonged melee scrap where Gwen's passive A Thousand Cuts and rapid Snip Snip! shred your health and out-sustain your Pale Cascade shield.

summary: Braum can use Stand Behind Me to escape Rakan's Grand Entrance knockup, then counter-engage with Concussive Blows.
howToPlay: Position yourself slightly behind your marksman, ensuring there is always a clear line of sight to leap to them. Do not waste Stand Behind Me for armor stats; hold it strictly to dodge Grand Entrance. The instant Rakan dashes forward, press your W to jump back, then immediately hit him with Winter's Bite. If he tries to escape using Battle Dance, follow up with Glacial Fissure to cut off his retreat path and secure the stun.
laneImpact: This reaction-based dynamic shifts lane control heavily in your favor. Rakan cannot safely fish for trades with Gleaming Quill or commit to Grand Entrance without risking a deadly counter-engage. This fear keeps the enemy duo pinned under their turret, granting your ADC free farm. If Rakan tries to roam or use The Quickness to engage, your defensive mobility ensures your carry remains protected while you secure local lane priority.
why: Rakan relies on the sudden crowd control of Grand Entrance to dictate skirmishes, but Braum completely neutralizes this dive. By reacting to Rakan's jump with Stand Behind Me onto your ADC, you escape the knockup radius entirely. Once Rakan is stranded in your minion wave without his knockup, you can immediately retaliate with Winter's Bite and stack Concussive Blows, turning his aggressive initiation into a fatal trap.

summary: Red Kayn's passive healing and percentage health damage on Reaping Slash allow him to easily shred and outsustain Mundo in extended fights.
howToPlay: Shift your build focus immediately from pure health to anti-healing and armor to mitigate his healing. During skirmishes, save Heart Zapper's detonation for the exact moment Kayn exits you after Umbral Trespass to recover the burst damage he inflicts. If he invades your camps with Shadow Step, use the high damage of Blunt Force Trauma to quickly secure the monsters and retreat before a prolonged fight can begin.
laneImpact: In the early jungle rotations, you can contest camps using Infected Bonesaw to slow his clear and secure crabs. However, the moment Kayn gains his red form, the power dynamic shifts completely. You can no longer contest neutral objectives or defend your own jungle camps in direct duels, as he will use Shadow Step to initiate favorable fights and heal off your massive health pool.
why: Kayn's transformation via The Darkin Scythe creates a massive scaling gap that turns Mundo's high health pool against him. Once Kayn unlocks his red form, the percentage-health damage on Reaping Slash shreds your tankiness, while his passive healing easily outpaces the regeneration from Maximum Dosage and Heart Zapper in prolonged skirmishes.

summary: While Braum's Unbreakable blocks Cosmic Binding, Bard can use Tempered Fate to bypass the shield and freeze the enemies behind him.
howToPlay: To survive, never stand directly on top of your carry; split your positioning to force Bard to choose only one target for Tempered Fate. Hold Stand Behind Me specifically as an escape tool to leap out of the golden circular zone before it lands. If you or your ally get caught, prepare Glacial Fissure immediately to knock up incoming attackers the instant the stasis ends, preventing them from capitalizing on the freeze.
laneImpact: This dynamic makes contesting the wave incredibly dangerous. If you raise Unbreakable to block Cosmic Binding trades, you make yourself a stationary target for Tempered Fate. Bard can easily freeze you under your own turret, allowing his allies to ignore your defensive stats. This pressure forces you into a passive stance, giving Bard free reign to collect chimes with Traveler's Call and roam through walls using Magical Journey.
why: While your Unbreakable successfully absorbs Bard's incoming Cosmic Binding, his ultimate Tempered Fate completely bypasses this frontal defense. Because Tempered Fate is a ground-targeted area-of-effect stasis, it ignores your raised shield entirely. Bard can freeze you and your carry simultaneously, neutralizing your protective presence and setting up an easy follow-up stun against your allies once the golden stasis expires.

summary: Tempered Fate can freeze Sona to interrupt her Crescendo or catch her out before she can scale and sustain her team.
howToPlay: To secure your scaling advantage, never stand near walls to deny Bard easy stuns from Cosmic Binding. When teamfights erupt, do not lead the engage. Hold Crescendo and wait for Bard to cast Tempered Fate first. If you see the golden circle of his ultimate, immediately activate Song of Celerity to escape the radius. Only unleash your own ultimate once the stasis resolves to counter-engage and save your teammates.
laneImpact: During the laning phase, Bard will frequently leave his ADC to collect chimes for Traveler’s Call. You must punish these roams by playing aggressively with Hymn of Valor to force his partner off the wave. Although Bard's Caretaker’s Shrine provides some sustain, your consistent shielding ensures you win prolonged trades. Keep the wave pushed to punish his roams, but watch out for Magical Journey ganks from behind.
why: Sona naturally outscales Bard because her constant team-wide buffs from Aria of Perseverance and Hymn of Valor offer far superior late-game value compared to Bard's single-target Caretaker’s Shrine. However, this scaling advantage is gated by Bard's ability to shut her down using Tempered Fate. If Bard lands his ultimate to freeze Sona, he can completely interrupt her Crescendo or isolate her before her scaling-driven sustain can save her allies.

summary: Twilight Shroud (W) remains fully functional inside Mordekaiser's Realm of Death (R), allowing you to easily stall out the duration of his ultimate.
howToPlay: Always hold Twilight Shroud when Mordekaiser has his Realm of Death ready. If he pulls you in, immediately cast the shroud and run in circles to wait out the timer, using Assassin's Mark movement speed to avoid his Obliterate. Use Shuriken Flip to dodge Death's Grasp sideways rather than backward, ensuring you land behind him. If you mess up and cast your shroud too early, immediately disengage using Perfect Execution to dash over terrain or away from his Darkness Rise aura.
laneImpact: This interaction strips Mordekaiser of his primary kill threat, rendering his post-level-5 power spikes useless against you. He cannot pressure you under tower or force unfavorable recall timings because trying to lock you down with Death's Grasp or ultimate will only waste his resources. You control the lane tempo, easily dodging his Obliterate while farming safely and threatening high-damage trades whenever his shield from Indestructible is depleted.
why: Akali's high mobility completely counters Mordekaiser's slow, telegraphed skillshots. More importantly, when Mordekaiser pulls you into his Realm of Death, you can drop Twilight Shroud. Since the shroud transfers with you into his ultimate dimension, you can easily turn his 1v1 arena into a safe zone, completely stalling out his stat-stealing window while waiting for your Five Point Strike and Shuriken Flip cooldowns to reset.

summary: Caitlyn must avoid standing between Xayah and her feathers to prevent Bladecaller roots, while saving Ace in the Hole until after Xayah uses Featherstorm.
howToPlay: To win this matchup, always position diagonally relative to Xayah and the minion wave. This prevents her Clean Cuts from placing feathers directly behind you. When trading, if she activates Deadly Plumage, immediately fire 90 Caliber Net to back away and deny her extended damage. Crucially, hold your Ace in the Hole; never channel it until you have forced her to use Featherstorm defensively, ensuring your ultimate actually connects.
laneImpact: The threat of Bladecaller forces a cautious approach to wave control. You cannot easily lock Xayah under her turret with Yordle Snap Trap, as stepping up to harass exposes you to a quick root. When Xayah activates Deadly Plumage for a burst of speed and damage, you are forced to retreat, often using 90 Caliber Net to disengage. Consequently, securing early tower plates depends entirely on your lateral positioning.
why: This duel is defined by a delicate dance of ranges and angles. Caitlyn boasts superior base range to poke with basic attacks and Piltover Peacemaker, but Xayah counters this by scattering feathers with Clean Cuts and Double Daggers. The main threat is Bladecaller; if you stand between Xayah and her feathers, she can instantly root you. Additionally, your Ace in the Hole can be easily dodged by her Featherstorm untargetability.

summary: Using Rune Prison to root Sett when he activates Knuckle Down prevents him from closing the gap to land Facebreaker.
howToPlay: To survive this matchup, you must master bush control. Hide in the lane brushes to force Ryze to facecheck or waste his wards, preventing him from freely landing his basic attacks. Never initiate a trade with Knuckle Down if he has his root ready; instead, walk up naturally and save the speed boost to catch him after he wastes Rune Prison on a minion. If you get caught out of position, shield his burst with a well-timed Haymaker to absorb the damage.
laneImpact: Because you cannot easily retaliate, you will spend most of the early game pushed under your turret. Ryze will constantly bounce Spell Flux through your minions to chip away at your health. This constant pressure limits your ability to secure last hits without taking heavy damage, slowing down your gold acquisition. However, Ryze's reliance on mana means he cannot harass indefinitely before needing to use Realm Warp or a manual recall to replenish.
why: Sett struggles because Ryze commands the distance with ranged attacks. Whenever you attempt to close the gap by activating Knuckle Down for the movement speed boost, Ryze instantly shuts down your advance with Rune Prison. This targeted root freezes you in place, making it impossible to get close enough to pull him in with Facebreaker. You are left stranded while he unloads Spell Flux and Overload from safety.

summary: Nasus can use Spirit Fire to safely damage and clear your H-28G Evolution Turrets from a distance while stacking his Siphoning Strike.
howToPlay: To maintain your edge, never cluster your H-28G Evolution Turret setups; spread them out so a single Spirit Fire cannot damage multiple units. When Nasus steps up to last-hit with Siphoning Strike, immediately punish him with Hextech Micro-Rockets and CH-2 Electron Storm Grenade. If he activates Fury of the Sands and uses Wither to close the gap, immediately deploy UPGRADE!!! combined with your grenade to stun him and trigger your Hextech Affinity movement speed to kite away.
laneImpact: This dynamic forces a constant tug-of-war over wave position. If Nasus successfully zones your H-28G Evolution Turret placements with his AoE, he halts your push and gains a safe pocket to stack Siphoning Strike. However, if you force him to repeatedly use Spirit Fire on your turrets rather than the wave, his mana depletes rapidly, preventing him from sustaining with Soul Eater and leaving his tower vulnerable to your heavy AP siege.
why: Although you hold the absolute advantage as a ranged bully, Nasus combats your lane dominance using Spirit Fire to melt your H-28G Evolution Turret setups from a safe distance. This interaction allows him to neutralise your early pressure and comfortably stack Siphoning Strike under his tower. The matchup revolves around how quickly he can clear your machinery versus how fast you can punish his mana pool.

summary: Jax's Counter Strike reduces the damage of Rumble's Flamespitter by 25% as an AoE ability, but Jax still struggles against Rumble's constant magic damage poke.
howToPlay: Play defensively during the early levels and let the wave crash. Only engage with Leap Strike followed by Empower when Rumble has just depleted his heat or overextended. When he activates Flamespitter, immediately trigger Counter Strike to mitigate the 25% area damage, then use the stun to disengage safely rather than committing to an extended duel. If you are forced low, concede minions and wait for Grandmaster-at-Arms to burst him down in short trades.
laneImpact: Rumble easily dictates the wave pace early, forcing Jax to lose health for every minion. If you get shoved under tower, the constant threat of Flamespitter makes farming a nightmare. This pressure limits your map rotations, leaving your jungler without top priority. The lane is decided by how much health you preserve before unlocking Grandmaster-at-Arms, which represents your first real window to fight back.
why: Jax's Counter Strike reduces the AoE damage of Rumble's Flamespitter by 25%, but it does not block it entirely like basic attacks. Because Rumble deals persistent, non-targeted magic damage, Jax cannot simply dodge his way out of trades. Rumble's magic poke constantly chips away at Jax's health bar, making direct confrontations risky unless Jax can exploit Rumble's heat management windows.

summary: Aurora can easily dodge Brand's Pillar of Flame (W) using Across the Veil (W) and counter-engage.
howToPlay: To survive, you must hold Pillar of Flame as a deterrent rather than an initiation tool. Start your trades by spreading Blaze with Conflagration to threaten a stun. If Aurora aggressively jumps forward with Across the Veil, wait out her brief invisibility before throwing Sear to stun her. Once she is locked down, you can safely unleash Pillar of Flame and Pyroclasm to turn the trade in your favor.
laneImpact: Because you cannot throw Pillar of Flame blindly, you lose control of the minion waves. If you use it to clear, Aurora will immediately punish you with Twofold Hex. This constant threat of her Across the Veil forces you to play defensively near your turret. You will struggle to secure mid priority, meaning you cannot assist your jungler, while Aurora can comfortably roam using her high mobility.
why: Aurora's mobility completely disrupts your standard trading pattern. The moment you cast Pillar of Flame, she can instantly react with Across the Veil to leap away, turn invisible, and render your primary source of damage entirely useless. Once your key spell is wasted, she can safely close the gap to land Twofold Hex and trigger Spirit Abjuration, leaving you with no reliable way to trade back.

summary: Using Hookshot to interrupt Yone's Mortal Steel third cast or dodging Fate Sealed with Hextech Ultimatum decides the duel.
howToPlay: Keep a close eye on Yone's gathering wind. Never initiate with Hookshot when his Mortal Steel is fully charged; instead, hold onto the ability and hook onto a nearby wall, waiting to launch yourself the moment he initiates his dash to cancel his momentum. During post-level 5 duels, react to the red visual indicator of Fate Sealed by immediately casting The Hextech Ultimatum to become untargetable, landing safely to deliver an empowered Precision Protocol while his main escape is down.
laneImpact: The lane shifts constantly based on Mortal Steel stacks. When Yone has his tornado ready, Camille must play defensively, using Tactical Sweep to secure CS from safety. If you successfully interrupt his Q3 dash or dodge his ultimate, the trade immediately swings in your favor, allowing you to pressure his tower. Missing these crucial timings lets Yone abuse Soul Unbound to take free, risk-free trades and force you to recall early.
why: This matchup is a pure battle of reaction times and cooldown tracking. Camille's Adaptive Defenses provides a physical shield that mitigates Yone's early trades, but his mixed damage from Way of the Hunter can bypass it. The duel hinges entirely on neutralizing his key mobility: you must use Hookshot to knock Yone out of his Mortal Steel third cast, or buffer The Hextech Ultimatum to completely dodge the knockup from Fate Sealed.

summary: Olaf's Ragnarok makes him immune to the stun from Hookshot and the confinement of Hextech Ultimatum, allowing him to run Camille down.
howToPlay: To survive, use Tactical Sweep from maximum range to secure minions and slow his advance without committing. Never initiate with Hookshot when his ultimate is available; instead, cling to terrain and hold the dash exclusively as a disengage tool to escape over walls after Ragnarok expires. If he forces an all-in with Vicious Strikes, trigger your Adaptive Defenses shield with a quick Precision Protocol tap, then immediately retreat.
laneImpact: You cannot safely crash waves or freeze near his tower because any overextended position leaves you vulnerable to his slow. If Olaf lands Undertow, he can chain-axe you down the long lane. Since your The Hextech Ultimatum cannot trap him during his ultimate, you lose all kill pressure post-level five. This forces you to play defensively under your turret, sacrificing early priority.
why: Olaf's Ragnarok completely neutralizes Camille's primary tools for controlling the pace of a fight. While Camille wants to lock him down with The Hextech Ultimatum or escape using Hookshot, Olaf can activate his ultimate to ignore the confinement zone entirely and shrug off the wall-dive stun. This turns what should be a tactical skirmish into a pure stat check where his Berserker Rage and Reckless Swing will always overwhelm her.

summary: Kai'Sa can poke Galio down with Void Seeker (W) and physical damage from Icathian Rain (Q), making it difficult for him to walk up to last-hit.
howToPlay: To survive, let the wave crash and farm safely using Winds of War from behind your minions, which blocks her Void Seeker. Never use Justice Punch forward unless her Icathian Rain is on cooldown, as she can easily kite you with Supercharge. If you get chunked below half health, abandon the turret plates to recall immediately; chasing her with Hero's Entrance to side lanes is only viable after she commits her Killer Instinct.
laneImpact: Because of her poke, you will constantly find yourself pushed under turret, bleeding health whenever you try to thin the wave. This range denial prevents you from using Winds of War to contest wave priority safely. Since you cannot easily push, your ability to impact the map with Hero's Entrance is severely delayed, forcing you to choose between defending your tower plates or helping your jungler.
why: Kai'Sa exploits Galio's melee profile by punishing your attempts to farm with her ranged kit. Her Void Seeker snipes you from safety, while any attempt to walk up for a melee last-hit with Colossal Smash triggers isolated physical damage from Icathian Rain. This constant barrage makes your Shield of Durand magic passive less effective since her damage profile relies heavily on physical burst and Second Skin plasma stacks.

summary: Akshan can easily poke Akali down with his Dirty Fighting passive and Avengerang, forcing her to give up early minion waves.
howToPlay: Be patient and sacrifice early gold, using the outer tip of Five Point Strike only to secure dying minions from a safe distance. Preserve your Twilight Shroud to safely collect waves under your turret without taking free harass. Once you reach level five, wait for him to misplay his Heroic Swing. If he swings too close, land Shuriken Flip to close the gap, then unleash Perfect Execution to burst him down.
laneImpact: This constant range threat forces you to concede the first few waves, letting Akshan push you under your turret. Your health pool is your most valuable resource here; taking unnecessary damage to secure a single minion leads to a forced early recall. This gives Akshan free reign to roam with Going Rogue or chip away at your plating while you struggle to clear under tower.
why: Akshan dominates the early levels because his ranged auto-attacks trigger Dirty Fighting, granting him a protective shield and bonus movement speed. Whenever you try to approach the minion wave, he can easily line up Avengerang through the minions to extend its reach and shred your health bar. If you attempt a quick Five Point Strike poke, his passive shield nullifies your damage while he retaliates from safety.

summary: Malphite's Unstoppable Force can catch Corki mid-Valkyrie, setting up easy ganks for the enemy jungler.
howToPlay: To survive, always position yourself closer to your own turret than to his, keeping the wave near your side. Never use Valkyrie offensively; hold it strictly as a defensive tool, but only trigger it after you see him commit Unstoppable Force, or flash his ultimate entirely. If Malphite freezes the wave, use the long-range poke of Missile Barrage to break it safely from a distance instead of walking up.
laneImpact: This threat forces you into a highly defensive posture once Malphite reaches level five. You cannot aggressively push with Gatling Gun or poke with Phosphorus Bomb near his tower, as doing so leaves you too far up the lane. Every time your Valkyrie is baited or interrupted, you become a free target for the enemy jungler, forcing early recalls and costing you precious farm.
why: While Corki usually relies on Valkyrie to escape bad situations, Malphite completely neutralizes this safety net. The sheer speed of Unstoppable Force can intercept you right in the middle of your Valkyrie dash. Because Malphite is immune to crowd control during his ultimate, your package-enhanced Special Delivery cannot interrupt him either, leaving you extremely vulnerable to dive setups.

summary: Viktor can abuse Vladimir's weak early waveclear by constantly shoving with Hextech Ray (E) and using Siphon Power (Q) to shield against Transfusion (Q) trades.
howToPlay: Keep your distance when Vladimir's resource bar turns red, indicating his empowered Transfusion is ready. Instead of running, drop Gravity Field behind him if he tries to walk up, or simply step back until the bar depletes. Always hold Arcane Storm until he wastes Sanguine Pool, as his pool will easily dodge your ultimate's burst. If he pools to escape your pressure, immediately drop Gravity Field on his path to stun him as he emerges.
laneImpact: Constant shoving with Hextech Ray forces Vladimir to burn through his health pool using Tides of Blood under his turret. Since he is stuck farming defensively, he cannot roam or contest early river skirmishes. This priority grants you easy recall timings and total map freedom. If you maintain this pressure, Vladimir falls behind in CS and is forced into awkward, low-tempo backs.
why: Viktor dominates this matchup early because Vladimir lacks any tool to match the immediate waveclear of Hextech Ray. While Vladimir relies on Transfusion to sustain and slowly trade, Viktor can negate this exact pressure. By timing Siphon Power to absorb the incoming Transfusion damage, Viktor wins every short trade while keeping Vladimir trapped under tower, unable to heal back his own Tides of Blood costs.

summary: Ornn can use the unstoppable effect of Bellows Breath to block Mordekaiser's Death's Grasp pull or even cancel the cast of Realm of Death.
howToPlay: Never initiate with Searing Charge unless Mordekaiser has wasted his abilities. Keep Bellows Breath ready exclusively to react to his animations. When you see him raise his mace for Realm of Death or cast the claw of Death's Grasp, immediately use Bellows Breath to absorb the crowd control. If he misses these, use Volcanic Rupture to slow him, then escape. If trapped in his ultimate, focus on survival using Call of the Forge God to delay his assault.
laneImpact: Because Mordekaiser easily triggers Darkness Rise and shields with Indestructible, you cannot contest long trades. You are constantly pushed under tower, sacrificing early priority. If you fail to block Death's Grasp, you are forced into a disastrous trade. Post-level 5, your tower becomes your only safety, as stepping too far up invites Realm of Death, forcing you to play purely for defensive wave clear.
why: Mordekaiser naturally dominates Ornn due to his AP-based anti-tank profile. Darkness Rise shreds Ornn's health pool in extended fights, while Obliterate punishes CSing. However, this matchup pivots entirely on Ornn's Bellows Breath. The unstoppable frames can completely negate Death's Grasp or, with precise timing, cancel the cast of Realm of Death, preventing Mordekaiser from dragging you into his stat-stealing dimension.

summary: Skarner can use Impale to drag Kindred out of her own Lamb's Respite zone, leaving her vulnerable to being finished off.
howToPlay: When engaging, do not rush to use Impale immediately. Instead, initiate with Ixtal's Impact to stun her or slow her with Shattered Earth / Upheaval. Force Kindred to panic and deploy Lamb's Respite. The moment her zone appears, position yourself to immediately grab her with Impale and drag her outside the boundary. If she tries to kite with Dance of Arrows, use Seismic Bastion to absorb the damage and close the gap.
laneImpact: In the jungle, this interaction shifts the power dynamic during skirmishes around neutral objectives and Mark of the Kindred camps. Kindred cannot safely contest marks if you are nearby, as her usual safety net is neutralized. This allows you to aggressively invade her territory, secure crabs, and force early teamfights where her team cannot rely on her ultimate to survive your burst.
why: Skarner completely counters Kindred's ultimate utility because Impale acts as the perfect answer to Lamb's Respite. When Kindred attempts to save herself or her allies within her protective circle, Skarner can suppress and physically drag her out of the safe zone. This interaction denies her the final heal and leaves her completely exposed to immediate lethal damage, turning her primary defensive tool into a death trap.

summary: Lillia's high movement speed from Blooming Blows makes it easy to dodge Viego's Spectral Maw, allowing her to kite him indefinitely.
howToPlay: To survive this matchup, never lead with an unassisted Spectral Maw. Instead, use the camouflage of Harrowed Path hugging the jungle walls to approach unseen and close the distance. Hold your stun until she commits to her Watch Out! Eep! animation, which briefly locks her in place. If she manages to hit you with Swirlseed and prepares Lilting Lullaby, use the unstoppable frames of Heartbreaker to escape over a wall or reposition to safety before the sleep takes effect.
laneImpact: In the jungle, this interaction makes direct skirmishes near Scuttle Crabs or early neutral camps incredibly risky. If Lillia lands Swirlseed, she can slow you down, build her speed stacks, and force you out of your Harrowed Path camouflage. You will find yourself unable to force favorable trades, often giving up river priority and being forced to cede camps to avoid being put to sleep by Lilting Lullaby.
why: This matchup is defined by a severe mobility mismatch once combat begins. Lillia gains massive movement speed stacks from Blooming Blows, allowing her to easily react to and dodge your Spectral Maw charge. Without that crucial stun, Viego cannot close the gap or lock her down, leaving him entirely exposed to being run down and kited by her continuous magic damage.

summary: Ahri can buffer her Charm directly behind herself to instantly CC Zed as he emerges from his Death Mark.
howToPlay: Never throw Charm recklessly while Zed has Living Shadow available, as he can easily teleport to dodge it. Instead, poke with Orb of Deception and Fox-Fire. When he commits with Death Mark, wait for the exact moment he reappears behind you to cast Charm backward. If you miss, immediately use Spirit Rush to dash away, dodging his Razor Shuriken and Shadow Slash to survive his mark's explosion.
laneImpact: Before level five, you must abuse your ranged advantage with Orb of Deception to punish Zed whenever he uses Living Shadow to farm. If Zed wastes his shadow clone, he loses his escape tool, allowing you to play aggressively. However, if he manages to chunk your health, his Contempt for the Weak makes you an easy target under tower, forcing bad recalls that cost you mid lane priority.
why: This lane behaves as a pure skill duel centered on the timing of Zed's ultimate and Ahri's main crowd control. When Zed casts Death Mark, he always appears directly behind Ahri. This predictable spawn allows Ahri to buffer Charm behind her back, immediately interrupting Zed's burst setup and turning his aggressive dive into a lethal mistake, while Zed must bait this key cooldown first.

summary: Vi can interrupt Bountiful Harvest with Vault Breaker or Cease and Desist, forcing Fiddlesticks to delay his drain until her CC is spent.
howToPlay: Never waste both of your crowd control abilities simultaneously. If you initiate the fight by charging Vault Breaker to close the gap, absolutely hold Cease and Desist until Fiddlesticks starts channeling Bountiful Harvest. If he tries to peel you off with Terrify first, let the fear expire, activate Blast Shield to absorb his minor follow-up damage, and immediately crush his subsequent drain channel with your remaining knockup.
laneImpact: In the jungle, this interaction completely paralyzes Fiddlesticks' ability to contest objectives or secure crabs early. He cannot comfortably clear camps near you, knowing that a sudden Vault Breaker from a bush will cancel his heal and leave him defenseless. This pressure forces him to rely entirely on blind-spot Crowstorm ganks, giving you free rein to counter-jungle and secure early neutral epic monsters.
why: This matchup swings heavily in your favor because Vi possess two reliable ways to cancel Fiddlesticks' primary source of healing and damage. Whenever he channels Bountiful Harvest, you can instantly interrupt it using Vault Breaker or your unstoppable Cease and Desist. Without this continuous drain, Fiddlesticks lacks the raw tankiness to survive your rapid Denting Blows shred in isolated jungle skirmishes.

summary: Garen must disengage with Decisive Strike's movement speed before Volibear can land a second Frenzied Maul to heal.
howToPlay: Never initiate with Decisive Strike. Instead, wait for Volibear to commit with Thundering Smash. The moment he stuns you, immediately trigger Courage to mitigate his burst and Sky Splitter damage. As the stun expires, activate Decisive Strike to cleanse any lingering slow and sprint away before he can trigger his healing Frenzied Maul. If he manages to mark you anyway, abandon the wave immediately and retreat until the mark fades.
laneImpact: Volibear's constant lightning from The Relentless Storm naturally pushes the wave, forcing you under tower. Because you cannot contest extended trades, you will bleed health whenever you try to freeze. If he lands Sky Splitter to shield himself while slowing you, you are forced to use Courage defensively. This leaves you vulnerable to a dive with Stormbringer, which disables your tower and forces early, costly recalls.
why: Volibear dominates long trades because Frenzied Maul heals him when biting a marked target. While your Perseverance requires you to retreat to regenerate, Volibear sustains directly through combat. If you stay within his reach after he marks you, his second bite negates all damage from Judgment. Your survival hinges entirely on using Decisive Strike to break his slow and escape before he bites you a second time.

summary: Kassadin's Null Sphere grants him a magic damage shield that neutralizes Akali's early Five Point Strike poke.
howToPlay: To survive, refuse to trade while his Null Sphere is off cooldown. Let him push and focus on freezing the wave near your turret to farm safely. If he steps up to execute minions with Nether Blade, wait out his magic shield before committing to a Shuriken Flip counter-engage. Save your Twilight Shroud exclusively to drop target lock and wait out the silence when he jumps on you with Riftwalk. If you fail to hold the wave, prioritize roaming over forced, losing trades.
laneImpact: Since your Five Point Strike cannot pierce his magic shield, trading becomes highly inefficient. Kassadin can easily trade back with Nether Blade and Force Pulse while you are silenced, forcing you to play defensively. This shifts the wave control entirely in his favor, as you must use Twilight Shroud just to survive and last-hit under tower. You lose mid priority, leaving him free to recall safely or secure a resource advantage.
why: This matchup is dictated by Kassadin's passive-active defenses which neutralize Akali's early lane dominance. Whenever you attempt to poke or secure minions with Five Point Strike, Kassadin responds with Null Sphere, generating a magic shield that absorbs your damage while silencing you. Because your primary trading tool is constantly mitigated, you cannot punish his weak early game, allowing him to scale safely toward his explosive Riftwalk spikes.

summary: Using Shuriken Flip (E) to dodge Ornn's Searing Charge (E) knockup allows you to safely re-engage and poke him down with passive-enhanced attacks.
howToPlay: To win this tempo battle, never waste Shuriken Flip offensively unless Ornn's Searing Charge is on cooldown. Stand slightly away from his Volcanic Rupture pillar to bait his dash, then reactively flip backward. Once he misses, immediately reactivate the shuriken to close the gap, drop Twilight Shroud to block his Bellows Breath, and weave in and out of your Assassin's Mark circle. If you get hit by his knockup early, immediately disengage using Five Point Strike to slow him.
laneImpact: Missed knockups drastically alter the minion wave dynamics. If Ornn whiffs Searing Charge, he loses the threat required to secure the wave, allowing you to establish slow pushes and crash minions into his tower. However, if he lands his combo, he gains the health advantage needed to freeze near his turret, utilizing Living Forge to buy items without backing, which starves you of roam opportunities and lane priority.
why: This even matchup hinges on how you respond to Ornn's crowd control. When Ornn attempts to trigger a knockup by combining Volcanic Rupture with Searing Charge, your Shuriken Flip acts as the ultimate counter-mobility tool. By flipping away to avoid the collision, you negate his burst setup, leaving him vulnerable to being poked down by your Assassin's Mark-empowered attacks while his defensive cooldowns are offline.

summary: Easily dash out of Sion's Decimating Smash charge area using Drakehound's Step, leaving him completely vulnerable to your full combo.
howToPlay: To execute this perfectly, always hover within Sion's range and hold onto either Cunning Sweep or Lacerate. Avoid burning all your abilities at once; instead, wait for him to start anchoring his heavy strike before triggering Drakehound's Step to slide out of his path. If he attempts to escape or engage with Unstoppable Onslaught, time your Repudiation shield to absorb the impact, then immediately follow up with Public Execution to secure the kill.
laneImpact: This interaction grants you complete authority over wave states and trade pacing. Sion cannot safely channel Decimating Smash to clear minions without being severely punished. You can easily establish a slow push and dive or pressure his turret, as his desperate attempts to absorb your bursts with Soul Furnace will quickly deplete his mana pool, forcing him into terrible recall timings and loss of tower plates.
why: Ambessa dominates this matchup because her mobility completely neutralizes Sion's primary threat. The moment Sion begins channeling Decimating Smash, you can activate Drakehound's Step after casting Cunning Sweep or Lacerate to effortlessly dash out of the danger zone. By dodging his heavy knock-up, you strip him of his main crowd control and damage, leaving him entirely defenseless against your relentless counter-engage.

summary: Inside the Realm of Death, Lillia can easily use her high movement speed to dodge Mordekaiser's Obliterate and Death's Grasp.
howToPlay: Never initiate a fight by casting Realm of Death while Lillia already has maximum Blooming Blows stacks. Instead, save your Death's Grasp for the exact moment she locks herself into the leap animation of Watch Out! Eep!, which is her only predictable movement. If she misses this jump, activate Indestructible to absorb her passive burn damage, and only ultimate her once her movement speed stacks decay, trapping her in a tight corridor.
laneImpact: Because you cannot reliably lock Lillia down, contesting the Rift Scuttler or epic monsters becomes highly dangerous. If you try to force a duel in the river, her Swirlseed can slow you from afar, allowing her to dictate the engagement. You risk being constantly outpaced in your clear speed, and attempting to counter-gank her often results in her sleeping you with Lilting Lullaby before you can activate Indestructible.
why: Lillia's innate mobility turns your ultimate against you. Inside the Realm of Death, she easily stacks movement speed from Blooming Blows to dance around your slow skillshots. This makes landing Obliterate or catching her with Death's Grasp nearly impossible. If she applies Dream-Laden Bough and triggers Lilting Lullaby, she can easily put you to sleep, wasting your entire ultimate duration while keeping her distance.

summary: Katarina can use Shunpo to blink behind you, easily escaping your Singularity and dodging your Breath of Light angle.
howToPlay: To survive, never initiate trades with Singularity. Hold this zone and Breath of Light until she has already committed her Shunpo onto a dagger. If she unleashes Death Lotus, immediately use Astral Flight to fly backward to safety. When she disappears from the lane to roam, do not chase her blindly through unwarded paths; instead, ping your allies, gather Stardust safely, and push the wave hard to punish her absence.
laneImpact: You cannot safely contest the wave near her tower, as pushing too far exposes you to a sudden Shunpo engage. This pressure forces you to play defensively under tower, granting her the freedom to clear with Bouncing Blade and roam. If you try to follow her rotations through the river without vision, her burst can catch you in transit before you can escape with Astral Flight.
why: This matchup is dictated by how easily Katarina bypasses your zone control. Because Breath of Light forces you to face a single direction while channeling, Katarina can instantly react with Shunpo to blink behind you. This maneuver not only evades your primary damage stream but also allows her to step completely out of your Singularity radius, turning your static channel into an open invitation for her daggers.

summary: Ornn's passive scaling is strong, but his lack of early kill pressure allows Nasus to freely stack Siphoning Strike (Q) and sustain through trades with Soul Eater (P).
howToPlay: To survive, you must maintain a freeze on your side of the lane. Only use Volcanic Rupture to last-hit from a distance, never to harass. If Nasus slows you with Wither and activates Fury of the Sands, immediately time Bellows Breath to negate the movement speed reduction with its unstoppable state. Save Searing Charge solely as an escape tool toward your own tower, and use Call of the Forge God to disrupt his ultimate duration from safety.
laneImpact: Your lack of kill pressure means Nasus can comfortably freeze the wave near his tower. If you accidentally push using Bellows Breath, you hand him a safe zone to farm Siphoning Strike. Once he acquires Fury of the Sands, he will easily shrug off your crowd control, turn the lane into a split-push nightmare, and force you to defend your turret instead of helping your team.
why: While Living Forge ensures you scale incredibly well into the late game, you lack the early burst to punish Nasus's weak start. Any trade you force with Volcanic Rupture is quickly negated by his Soul Eater lifesteal. This allows him to freely stack Siphoning Strike on every minion wave, easily outscaling your raw tank stats without facing any real threat of dying in the early levels.

summary: Inside the Realm of Death, Xin Zhao's Crescent Guard cannot block Mordekaiser's damage because Morde is always considered inside the challenge circle.
howToPlay: To win the mid-game duels, never initiate with Death's Grasp; save it to pull Xin Zhao back if he tries to disengage after his Three Talon Strike knockup. Activate Indestructible right as his third strike launches you to absorb his burst. When contesting objectives, wait for him to jump onto your backline with Audacious Charge, then instantly cast Realm of Death to isolate him, rendering his defensive ultimate useless for his team.
laneImpact: Early on, you must concede crab priority if Xin Zhao contests with Audacious Charge and Wind Becomes Lightning. He will try to invade your camps to delay your level five. However, once you survive this initial pressure and secure your ultimate, his ability to secure neutral objectives collapses. He can no longer safely peel you off with Crescent Guard during smite fights, turning objective pits into death traps for him.
why: This matchup hinges on a scaling race where Xin Zhao dominates early skirmishes but falls off compared to your late-game presence. While his Determination and Three Talon Strike give him supreme early dueling, the dynamic shifts entirely once you unlock Realm of Death. Inside your ultimate, Xin Zhao's Crescent Guard becomes completely useless against you, as you are permanently inside his defense circle, allowing your AP damage to melt him.

summary: Using Blinding Dart when Tryndamere uses Spinning Slash to close the distance completely wastes his lethal critical strikes and Undying Rage duration.
howToPlay: Never waste Blinding Dart for poke. Keep it ready specifically for when he initiates with Spinning Slash. If he turns his back to activate Mocking Shout, use Move Quick to maintain your distance and chase kiting. If he triggers Undying Rage, do not panic; use your Noxious Trap slow to keep him at bay while the invincibility ticks down, ensuring you only strike with basic attacks when his blind wears off.
laneImpact: This matchup allows you to dictate the wave's positioning from level one. Since Tryndamere cannot safely stack Battle Fury without taking heavy damage from Toxic Shot, he is forced to use Bloodlust defensively to heal. This robs him of his lane pressure, forcing him under his turret where you can safely poke him and delay his power spikes while securing a massive gold advantage.
why: Teemo completely neutralizes Tryndamere's offensive threat because his entire damage output relies on basic attacks powered by Battle Fury. Whenever Tryndamere attempts to close the gap using Spinning Slash, a well-timed Blinding Dart completely shuts down his offensive window. He cannot land his critical strikes, rendering his high fury useless and entirely wasting the crucial seconds of his Undying Rage while you freely chip away at his health.

summary: Blocking Pantheon's Shield Vault with Shroud of Darkness denies his burst combo and leaves him vulnerable to Unspeakable Horror.
howToPlay: To win this, never lead with Shield Vault. Instead, walk up or use Comet Spear to bait his Shroud of Darkness first. If Nocturne panics and wastes his spell shield, you have a brief window to execute your full combo. If you get caught by Unspeakable Horror, channel Aegis Assault facing Nocturne right before the fear triggers to mitigate his incoming burst damage while you are unable to move.
laneImpact: Because Nocturne wins the direct duel if his spell shield is up, you lose the freedom to contest scuttle crabs and neutral objectives early. If you try to force a fight in the river, his Duskbringer trail gives him the speed to chase you down. During skirmishes, his Paranoia can completely shut down your Grand Starfall flank attempts by blinding you and counter-ganking before you can land.
why: This matchup is dictated by Nocturne's reaction speed with Shroud of Darkness. When you initiate with Shield Vault, a competent Nocturne will immediately deploy his spell shield, absorbing your stun and nullifying your Mortal Will-empowered burst. Deprived of your crowd control, you remain trapped in close quarters, making you an easy target for Unspeakable Horror's tether which will inevitably fear and kill you.

summary: Ahri can easily land a guaranteed Charm on Yone's original body when he is forced to snap back at the end of Soul Unbound.
howToPlay: Never throw Charm mindlessly during neutral play; hold it specifically for his Soul Unbound activation. When Yone initiates with his spirit form, track the physical clone left behind. Position yourself to have a clear line of sight to that clone. As the indicator circle on his tether shrinks, fire Charm directly at his original body. If he attempts to dive you with Fate Sealed, use Spirit Rush to dodge laterally, then retaliate instantly.
laneImpact: Every trade is dictated by the status of Yone's Mortal Steel. When he accumulates two stacks, you must yield wave priority and space backward to avoid the knock-up. If he wastes this tornado or misses his Soul Unbound engage, you immediately seize control, using Orb of Deception and Fox-Fire to shove him under tower or chunk his health bar before his defensive Spirit Cleave shield can absorb the damage.
why: This matchup is a high-stakes spacing duel governed entirely by the timer on Yone's Soul Unbound. While Yone uses Mortal Steel and his spirit form to close the gap and bypass your ranged advantage, his return point remains fixed. The entire lane revolves around this tether: the moment he snaps back to his original body, he is completely predictable, allowing you to buffer a guaranteed Charm onto his physical anchor.

summary: Galio can taunt Aurora with Shield of Durand (W) when she attempts to use Across the Veil (W) or jump around with Between Worlds (R).
howToPlay: To survive, you must bait out his defensive tools before committing. Never cast Across the Veil offensively; keep it strictly as a disengage tool for when he misses Justice Punch. When you deploy Between Worlds, wait until his Shield of Durand is on cooldown before you start teleporting between the boundaries. If he holds his taunt, content yourself with farming safely from range using Twofold Hex and slowing his approach with The Weirding.
laneImpact: Because of this threat, you cannot freely trade using Twofold Hex without risking a counter-engage. If you step forward, Galio can absorb your poke with his passive magic shield, clear the wave instantly using Winds of War, and slide in with Justice Punch. This forces you to play defensively under tower, bleeding priority and leaving you unable to match his global map pressure when he uses Hero's Entrance.
why: Galio is a natural anti-mage tank designed to shut down your mobile AP assassin kit. The primary danger lies in how Shield of Durand completely neutralizes your slippery tools. If you attempt to activate Across the Veil for a quick stealth reposition or try to bounce along the borders of Between Worlds, his wide area-of-effect taunt instantly cancels your momentum, dragging you into his devastating melee range.

summary: Garen can use Courage to block the shield-breaker damage of Urgot's Disdain and stay above the execute threshold of Fear Beyond Death.
howToPlay: Never initiate trades with Decisive Strike if Urgot has Corrosive Charge ready; instead, save it to instantly cleanse his slow. Keep your finger on Courage and trigger it only when you see the startup animation of Disdain. If you successfully block his flip, immediately counter-attack with Judgment to shred his armor, putting him in range for Demacian Justice. If you misstime your shield, immediately retreat to avoid his passive shotgun legs.
laneImpact: Trades are incredibly short and dictated by Urgot's ability cooldowns. If Urgot wastes Disdain, he loses his only escape and shield, allowing you to shove the wave safely or force him under turret with Judgment. Your passive Perseverance guarantees you can heal back any poke from Corrosive Charge, meaning Urgot must secure a full all-in to actually push you out of the lane.
why: This matchup is a pure test of reflexes centered on Urgot's dash. When Urgot charges with Disdain, his goal is to flip you and trigger Echoing Flames shotgun blasts. By timing Courage to absorb the knockup, you mitigate his burst and gain critical tenacity. This prevents him from lowering your health pool into the execution threshold of Fear Beyond Death, turning his primary offensive tool into a wasted cooldown.

summary: Vladimir lacks the hard CC to stop Corki's Valkyrie, allowing Corki to freely scale and shred him later with Gatling Gun.
howToPlay: Never use Valkyrie offensively unless Vladimir has already wasted his Sanguine Pool and is low on health. Instead, save it as your ultimate safety net. Walk up to trade only when his Transfusion indicator is white or yellow, and immediately back off when it turns red. If he tries to dive you with Hemoplague, drop your Special Delivery trail directly across his path to force him into a bad pool, then shred his armor with Gatling Gun while kiting backwards.
laneImpact: Since you do not fear his engage, you can dictate the wave's position. Keep the minions closer to your tower early to force Vladimir to walk up, making him vulnerable to your Phosphorus Bomb poke. Because his Transfusion sustain is predictable, you can easily time your push when his red bar is empty. This constant pressure forces him to use Sanguine Pool defensively under tower, destroying his health bar and giving you free roam timings.
why: Vladimir depends on wearing down opponents over time, but he has zero hard crowd control to interrupt your escape. Whenever he tries to pool forward or charge his Tides of Blood, you can effortlessly disengage with Valkyrie. This complete safety denies his kill pressure, allowing you to freely farm your core items. Once you scale, your Gatling Gun shreds his built-in health defenses during teamfights before he can even reach you.

summary: Zyra's plants from Rampant Growth (W) can block Heimerdinger's Hextech Micro-Rockets (W) while matching his lane push.
howToPlay: To bypass her botanical shields, stand parallel to the minion wave rather than directly behind your turrets. This lateral positioning gives your Hextech Micro-Rockets a clear angle around her Rampant Growth plants. Always hold your CH-2 Electron Storm Grenade until Zyra locks herself in her Deadly Spines casting animation. If she drops Stranglethorns to clear your nest, immediately deploy UPGRADE!!! followed by a super turret to reclaim your zone.
laneImpact: Expect a highly static lane where neither mage can easily push the other under tower. Since Zyra's plants contest your H-28G Evolution Turret range, the wave remains frozen in the center. If you carelessly fire Hextech Micro-Rockets into her plant barrier, you lose trade priority and mana, allowing Zyra to step forward with Grasping Roots to lock you down for a deadly Stranglethorns follow-up.
why: This matchup is a pure war of attrition between your mechanical creations. While your H-28G Evolution Turret setup establishes early lane dominance, Zyra can easily match your wave clear by spawning her own plants using Rampant Growth. Crucially, her sprouted spitters and lashers act as physical shields that absorb the trajectory of your Hextech Micro-Rockets, completely neutralizing your primary burst and poke potential.

summary: Ornn can use Bellows Breath to become unstoppable, completely ignoring the knockup from Jarvan's E-Q combo.
howToPlay: To survive, never lead with Demacian Standard and Dragon Strike. Instead, walk up to poke with Martial Cadence and Dragon Strike from a distance, using Golden Aegis to absorb the slow from Volcanic Rupture. Only commit your knockup combo immediately after he wastes Bellows Breath on the minion wave. If he initiates with Call of the Forge God, use Cataclysm defensively to trap him and disrupt his ram redirect angle.
laneImpact: This interaction strips away your offensive pressure. Initiating with your flag-and-drag combo becomes a massive liability, as Ornn will punish your landing with Searing Charge against his Volcanic Rupture pillar. You cannot reliably freeze the wave or force him out of lane, meaning he safely gains free stats via Living Forge and outscales you without ever needing to risk a bad recall.
why: Ornn outscales Jarvan IV, but the immediate lane issue is his ability to nullify your primary engagement. When you launch your Demacian Standard and Dragon Strike combo, Ornn can reactively cast Bellows Breath. Its unstoppable status completely ignores your knockup, leaving you in melee range without your main crowd control while Ornn applies Brittle for a devastating counter-trade.

summary: Lux must play around the cooldown of Syndra's Scatter the Weak, as both mages possess the burst to instantly delete the other upon landing their respective crowd control.
howToPlay: Never throw your Light Binding proactively unless Syndra has already wasted Scatter the Weak. When her stun is on cooldown, you have a brief window to step forward, pop Lucent Singularity, and threaten her with Final Spark. Position yourself diagonally from her active Dark Sphere ground locations to make her stun angles highly predictable. If she manages to land her combo, immediately self-cast Prismatic Barrier to mitigate the damage.
laneImpact: Laning is incredibly tense because neither of you can step up to clear minions comfortably while the opponent's crowd control is available. You will find yourself using Lucent Singularity from a safe distance to match her Dark Sphere waveclear. A single misstep that allows Syndra to line up her stun forces you to drop wave control entirely, lose massive health, or take a forced recall that exposes your tower.
why: This matchup is a pure standoff of glass cannons where landing a single crowd control spell guarantees a kill. Because both of you possess the burst to instantly erase the other, everything revolves around Syndra's Scatter the Weak and your Light Binding. If Syndra misses her stun, she is entirely vulnerable to your full combo. Conversely, if you get caught by her sphere projection, her Unleashed Power will delete you.

summary: Bard can reactively cast Tempered Fate on his allies to absorb Malphite's Unstoppable Force without taking damage.
howToPlay: Position yourself well behind your marksman, forcing Malphite to choose between ultimate targets rather than hitting both of you. Keep Tempered Fate strictly off cooldown to react to his Unstoppable Force; never use it to initiate unless you know his ultimate is down. If he tries to poke with Seismic Shard, place a Caretaker's Shrine behind your carry to neutralize the health trade. Before committing to a Cosmic Binding stun, always pop his Granite Shield with a simple Meep-empowered basic attack first.
laneImpact: Before the ultimate milestone, you easily dominate the wave state. Malphite's melee nature makes him highly vulnerable to your ranged Traveler's Call attacks and Cosmic Binding stuns when he steps up to share minions. Once ultimates are unlocked, his presence under your tower is completely neutralized. He cannot threaten a dive because any attempt to use his signature engage results in an immediate stasis that traps him under tower fire.
why: This matchup swings entirely in your favor once both supports reach level 5. Malphite's entire threat revolves around his explosive engage with Unstoppable Force. However, because Tempered Fate has a cast range that allows you to stand safely behind, you can reactively throw your golden stasis directly onto your targeted allies. This completely absorbs his ultimate's knockup and damage, leaving Malphite deep in your territory with no escape.

summary: Timing Cri primal to silence Garen prevents him from activating Judgment after he hits with Decisive Strike.
howToPlay: Never waste Feral Scream to poke; hold it exclusively for when Garen runs at you with Decisive Strike active. When he approaches, stand near your minions so your Vorpal Spikes can clip him while you silence him. If he successfully activates Courage to reduce your initial damage, disengage using Rupture to knock him up and wait out his shield. Once he drops low enough, secure the execution with Feast before Demacian Justice can execute you.
laneImpact: Your ability to land this silence dictates who controls the minion waves. If you successfully mute his Judgment, Garen cannot easily clear minions, allowing you to freeze the wave near your turret. Conversely, failing this timing lets him shred your armor, push you under tower, and easily regenerate his health. A controlled lane allows you to safely farm with Vorpal Spikes and out-sustain him.
why: This lane is a pure war of attrition where Cho'Gath's Carnivore directly competes with Garen's Perseverance. The critical pivot relies on denying Garen's primary damage combo. When Garen charges with Decisive Strike, you must react quickly. Firing Feral Scream just as he strikes silences him, completely blocking him from immediately spinning with Judgment. This interrupts his trade rhythm, leaving him exposed to your retaliation.

summary: Taliyah's Unraveled Earth stuns Akali if she attempts to dash through it with Shuriken Flip or Perfect Execution.
howToPlay: To survive, your primary goal is to bait out Unraveled Earth before committing to any forward movement. Never initiate with Shuriken Flip while her ground stones are active. Instead, utilize Twilight Shroud to safely gather minion gold without exposing your hitbox. If she wastes her stones, you have a brief window to strike. Otherwise, accept losing some farm, preserve your health bar, and wait for your jungler to force her to deploy her defensive tools first.
laneImpact: This interaction forces you into a highly defensive posture from the first waves. Taliyah will constantly shove the lane using Threaded Volley, keeping you pinned under your turret where last-hitting is painful. If you step up to contest, she can easily zone you out or fish for a Seismic Shove. You will find yourself constantly bleeding health and unable to match her map rotations via Rock Surfing.
why: Taliyah holds complete control over your mobility because of how Unraveled Earth interacts with your kit. Whenever you attempt to close the gap using the second cast of Shuriken Flip or either dash of Perfect Execution, crossing her minefield triggers an immediate stun. This mechanic completely neutralizes your assassination threat, turning your primary engage tools into self-inflicted crowd control while leaving you vulnerable to her follow-up.

summary: Amumu must save Curse of the Sad Mummy to lock down Viego the moment he attempts to possess a soul via Sovereign's Domination.
howToPlay: To win this mental game, you must hold Curse of the Sad Mummy specifically for the moment Viego channels Sovereign's Domination over a fallen ally. During fights, do not throw your ultimate at his frontline; instead, stay near your vulnerable teammates and track the souls on the ground. When Viego dashes in with Heartbreaker or attempts a possession, immediately trigger Curse of the Sad Mummy to lock him in place, allowing your team to burst him down before he gains invulnerability.
laneImpact: This matchup turns teamfights and skirmishes over objectives into high-stakes standoffs. Viego will use Harrowed Path to sneak around the pits and fish for stuns with Spectral Maw, hoping to secure a quick kill. Your presence forces him to play extremely cautiously, delaying his entry into fights because he knows that getting caught during Sovereign's Domination means instant death. If you waste your crowd control early, he will sweep your entire team.
why: The duel between these two junglers hinges entirely on how you disrupt Viego's reset chain. While Viego relies on Sovereign's Domination to heal and chain-cast his way through skirmishes, your kit is designed to halt him mid-animation. The match remains even because if he dodges your Bandage Toss, he can shred you with Blade of the Ruined King; however, your lock-down potential makes any teamfight extremely dangerous for him if he tries to transform.

summary: Darius can aggressively invade Evelynn's jungle early, as she cannot contest him before unlocking Demon Shade and her ultimate.
howToPlay: Start by taking your first buff quickly, then immediately march into her side of the jungle. Track her starting position and catch her at her second buff. If she marks you with Allure, do not retreat; instead, use Apprehend to pull her in before the charm triggers, then execute her with Crippling Strike and Decimate. If she manages to escape using Last Caress, immediately take her remaining camps to permanently starve her.
laneImpact: By invading her early camps, you disrupt her pathing and delay her access to Demon Shade. Since she cannot contest you without her ultimate, she is forced to give up her camps or die trying to defend them. This denies her the gold needed for her assassin spikes, rendering her map pressure non-existent and securing early neutral control for your laners.
why: Darius completely dominates the early jungle phase because Evelynn lacks any dueling power before she unlocks Demon Shade and Last Caress. If she tries to clear, you can walk straight into her camps. Her Hate Spike and Allure cannot burst you down, and you can easily stack Hemorrhage during these prolonged early skirmishes, leaving her with no escape or response.

summary: Camille must bait out Teemo's Blinding Dart before using Precision Protocol, relying on Hookshot to close the gap and lock him down.
howToPlay: To survive, you must hold Blinding Dart exclusively for her Hookshot engage; never use it to poke. When you see her grapple towards a wall, prepare to blind her the split second she lands on you, neutralizing Precision Protocol. Use Move Quick to dodge the outer edge of Tactical Sweep to deny her healing. Finally, place a Noxious Trap directly at your feet when she initiates The Hextech Ultimatum to slow her down inside her own zone.
laneImpact: This mobility dynamic forces you into a highly defensive posture. You cannot safely trade with Toxic Shot near the side walls, severely limiting your lane presence. Camille will constantly fish for Hookshot angles to force your Blinding Dart. If she succeeds, she gains complete wave control, threatening a deadly dive once she unlocks The Hextech Ultimatum, which leaves you with nowhere to run even with Move Quick active.
why: Camille dominates this matchup by turning your range advantage against you. Her Hookshot allows her to ignore the distance, bridging the gap instantly from any nearby wall. Once she is on top of you, her Adaptive Defenses shield mitigates your Toxic Shot poison, while she attempts to bait out your Blinding Dart. If she successfully forces your blind early, her Precision Protocol will shred your health pool without any counterplay.

summary: Silencing Renekton with Cri primal when he dashes in with Slice and Dice prevents him from using Ruthless Predator to stun.
howToPlay: To execute this, never throw Feral Scream defensively to poke; hold it exclusively for when Renekton starts the first cast of Slice and Dice. Once silenced, follow up immediately with Rupture under his feet and auto-attack him with Vorpal Spikes. If he activates Dominus to survive, walk back and wait out his ultimate's duration before executing him with Feast.
laneImpact: This interaction completely strips Renekton of his early lane dominance. Instead of zoning you, he is forced to use Cull the Meek just to secure last hits. Every time he tries to force a trade, you win the health exchange, allowing you to safely trigger Carnivore to stay completely healthy. This constant pressure pushes him under tower, where he cannot easily roam.
why: Renekton relies on dashing in with Slice and Dice to deliver a quick, empowered stun with Ruthless Predator. Cho'Gath completely shuts down this aggressive sequence. By timing Feral Scream right as the crocodile dashes forward, you lock him out of his abilities, leaving him stranded in your minion wave without his burst or his stun.

summary: Morgana's Black Shield can absorb your burst, while her Dark Binding easily punishes predictable Shunpo dagger placements.
howToPlay: Never throw Dark Binding randomly to poke. Instead, keep it ready and stand near your minion wave. When Katarina drops a dagger via Bouncing Blade, immediately place Tormented Shadow over it to deter her. If she takes the bait and uses Shunpo onto the dagger, fire your Dark Binding directly at her landing frame, then channel Soul Shackles to guarantee the kill before she can escape.
laneImpact: You completely control the mid lane tempo by constantly shoving waves with Tormented Shadow. Katarina is forced to farm under turret, neutralizing her Voracity roaming potential. She cannot safely trade with you, as any aggressive Shunpo forward puts her at risk of a lethal counter-engage, allowing you to secure early plates and lock her to her lane.
why: Katarina's damage relies entirely on her jumping to daggers dropped by Bouncing Blade or Preparation. Because her Shunpo landing spots are completely predictable, you can pre-aim Dark Binding directly onto her daggers. If she attempts to force an engage with Death Lotus, your Black Shield absorbs her magic burst, while Soul Shackles easily interrupts her ultimate channeling by locking her in place.

summary: Olaf's Ragnarok makes him completely immune to Amumu's Bandage Toss and Curse of the Sad Mummy, allowing him to run Amumu down freely.
howToPlay: To survive, you must track his movements constantly and path away from him. Never initiate a fight on Olaf with Bandage Toss unless you know his ultimate is down. Instead, save your charges of Bandage Toss to hook onto jungle monsters over walls to escape.
