howToPlay: To survive, you must absolutely hold Light Binding as a deterrent and never launch it offensively. Use Lucent Singularity to poke only when Kassadin steps up to last-hit with Nether Blade. When he inevitably initiates with Riftwalk, do not panic-cast your root. Wait until his blink animation ends to guarantee Light Binding hits him at point-blank range, then mitigate his burst with Prismatic Barrier as you retreat to safety.
laneImpact: This constant threat paralyzes your wave control. You cannot push aggressively beyond the river, as stepping up invites a sudden Riftwalk engage. Attempting to poke with Lucent Singularity becomes ineffective if he absorbs it with Void Stone, while throwing Light Binding risks instant death if you miss. Consequently, you are forced to play defensively near your turret, sacrificing lane priority and allowing Kassadin to scale safely.
why: Kassadin's passive Void Stone mitigates your early poke, but the lane truly shifts when he unlocks Riftwalk. This ultimate allows him to effortlessly bait your Light Binding and blink directly over the projectile. Once your primary crowd control is bypassed, Lux is completely defenseless against his gap-close, leaving you exposed to a devastating trade from Nether Blade and Force Pulse without any means of self-peel.

summary: Irelia can use Defiant Dance to absorb your burst, then easily catch you with Flawless Duet when you try to swing away.
howToPlay: Prioritize strict wave management: freeze the minions just outside your turret range to deny her space for Bladesurge. Never initiate trades with Heroic Swing; instead, hold it exclusively to escape after she misses Flawless Duet. If she channels Defiant Dance, stop attacking immediately to avoid wasting your passive shield. Only channel Comeuppance when her defensive channel is down, or she will easily absorb the entire volley of bullets.
laneImpact: You must completely abandon your usual early lane dominance. If the minion wave gets frozen near her tower, Irelia will use low-HP minions as stepping stones with Bladesurge to close the gap and dive you. This constant threat forces you to play defensively under your turret, depriving you of roaming opportunities with Going Rogue and leaving your jungler without mid lane priority.
why: Irelia is a nightmare because her Defiant Dance easily mitigates your initial burst from Dirty Fighting and Avengerang. If you try to escape using Heroic Swing, its predictable trajectory makes you a sitting duck for her Flawless Duet. Getting stunned mid-air resets her Bladesurge, allowing her to stick to you relentlessly and execute you under your own turret.

summary: Irelia can easily reset Bladesurge on low-health minions to close the gap and stun Corki with Flawless Duet before he can Valkyrie away.
howToPlay: To survive, you must actively keep the minion wave frozen just outside your turret range. Constantly monitor the health of your own minions; when one is low, step back immediately to bait her Bladesurge. Never use Valkyrie aggressively; hold it exclusively to react to her Vanguard's Edge or to escape after dodging Flawless Duet. If she freezes, use Missile Barrage to break the freeze from maximum safety without walking into her dash range.
laneImpact: This constant threat forces you into a highly defensive posture. You cannot stand near your own dying minions, as they act as literal launchpads for her Bladesurge. Consequently, you will have to concede early wave control, often farming from extreme range using Phosphorus Bomb. This deprives you of priority, allowing her to easily stack Ionian Fervor and crash waves to roam while you are stuck under tower.
why: Irelia completely neutralizes your ranged advantage because of how her Bladesurge interacts with low-health minions. She can rapidly chain dashes to close the entire distance of the mid lane instantly. If she catches you off-guard, she will set up Flawless Duet to stun you. Because Valkyrie has a slight cast delay, her stun will interrupt or catch you before you can fly to safety.

summary: Rumble's high base durability and shield make him impossible for Talon to burst, while his constant flame damage forces Talon off the wave.
howToPlay: Keep your Heat meter above 50 to ensure Flamespitter and Scrap Shield are always empowered in the Danger Zone. When Talon attempts to secure minions, tag him with Electro Harpoon to slow his retreat, then chase him down. If he disappears using Shadow Assault, do not panic-retreat; instead, immediately lay down The Equalizer on top of your own position to scorch his invisible pathing, forcing him to abort his burst or die in the fire.
laneImpact: This matchup dynamic forces Talon to play passively under his turret, bleeding minion gold. Because you constantly threaten him with Flamespitter, he cannot contest wave priority and is forced to use Rake solely to farm from a distance. While you comfortably crash waves and chip away at his tower, Talon is restricted from using Assassin's Path to roam, protecting your side lanes from his early signature map pressure.
why: Rumble naturally dominates Talon because Scrap Shield completely absorbs the return damage of Rake, preventing Talon from applying the third stack of Blade's End. Whenever Talon tries to step up to melee range to farm or trade with Noxian Diplomacy, he is forced to walk directly into the continuous melt of Flamespitter. Since Talon cannot reliably burst through your shield or match your persistent magic damage, he is entirely locked out of direct combat.

summary: Gragas can survive Teemo's early poke with Happy Hour and easily burst him down post-6 using Explosive Cask to knock him out of safety.
howToPlay: To survive, never use Move Quick aggressively; keep its active speed boost ready to dodge Body Slam or step out of Barrel Roll zones. Position your Noxious Trap behind your own minion line rather than in the river. This creates a safe retreat path if he tries to launch you backward. If he activates Drunken Rage, back off immediately and wait out the damage reduction before resuming your basic attacks.
laneImpact: The early lane is a battle of attrition where you must constantly pressure him while he uses Barrel Roll to farm from afar. However, you cannot easily force him out of lane or crash waves effectively. The moment both of you hit level six, the pressure spikes. If you push too deep, a single well-placed barrel will displace you, leaving you vulnerable to a fatal Body Slam follow-up.
why: Gragas can shrug off your early Toxic Shot harass thanks to the constant healing from Happy Hour. While your ranged pokes should theoretically dominate a melee match, his sustain keeps him in the lane. Once he unlocks Explosive Cask, the dynamic shifts dramatically. He can launch you out from under your turret or away from your safe zones directly into his full burst combo, turning your range advantage into a liability.

summary: Yuumi cannot block Alistar's Headbutt-Pulverize combo on her host, and Alistar can easily roam to map-wide objectives while Yuumi is locked to her lane partner.
howToPlay: Watch for Yuumi detaching to trigger Bop 'n' Block; if she does, instantly interrupt her with Headbutt to lock her out of You and Me!. If she remains safely attached, execute your Headbutt and Pulverize combo directly on her host whenever they step up to last-hit. When the enemy lane plays too passively, do not force dives under their turret. Instead, run straight to mid lane or secure neutral objectives, exploiting Yuumi's inability to rotate alone.
laneImpact: This matchup completely removes any threat of counter-engage, allowing you to dictate when trades happen. While Yuumi relies on Zoomies to sustain her marksman, your Triumphant Roar keeps your health high during short trades. Once you push the wave, you gain absolute freedom to roam. Yuumi is forced to stay attached to her partner under tower, leaving her team completely outnumbered during map-wide skirmishes.
why: Yuumi's attachment via You and Me! makes her entirely unable to block your Headbutt into Pulverize combo on her host. When you knock up her carry, you effectively disable both champions simultaneously without facing any bodyblocking. Additionally, if she attempts to counter-engage with Final Chapter, Alistar can instantly purge the root using Unbreakable Will, completely neutralizing their defensive tools during your all-in burst.

summary: Xin Zhao's Crescent Guard can block the damage and follow-up from Amumu's ranged allies after Amumu engages.
howToPlay: To survive, you must track his starting camp and mirror his pathing to avoid him entirely in the early game. Never initiate with Bandage Toss if your ranged allies are too far to step inside his eventual Crescent Guard circle. Instead, use Despair and Tantrum to clear your camps quickly, aiming to counter-gank on the opposite side of the map. Only commit Curse of the Sad Mummy after he has already used his ultimate or when your melee allies can dive inside his ring with you.
laneImpact: In the jungle, this interaction makes early skirmishes near scuttle crabs or neutral objectives incredibly risky. Xin Zhao will aggressively seek you out with Audacious Charge and Wind Becomes Lightning, knowing you cannot duel him. If you try to fight back, his Determination heals him through your Tantrum damage. This constant threat forces you to concede early river control, putting pressure on your laners who lack your backup.
why: Xin Zhao heavily disrupts your team-fighting identity. While your Bandage Toss into Curse of the Sad Mummy is a premier engage tool, his Crescent Guard acts as a hard counter. By sweeping away and blocking all damage from your ranged allies standing outside his arena, he isolates you. Even if you apply Cursed Touch and burn him with Despair, your team cannot follow up on your crowd control.

summary: Karma's Inner Flame pokes Alistar down early, and her Inspire shield speed boost allows her ADC to easily outrun his Headbutt range.
howToPlay: To survive, use the lane bushes to hide your model and avoid the splash damage from Inner Flame. Do not blindly initiate. Instead, bait out her Inspire by walking forward threateningly, then step back. Once her shield is on cooldown, or if she wastes her Mantra on a missed poke, you have a brief window to strike. If you do get locked down by Focused Resolve, activate Unbreakable Will instantly to break the root and escape.
laneImpact: You will constantly find yourself pushed under your turret, struggling for wave control. Because Karma can safely poke with Inner Flame, you cannot easily step up to trigger Triumphant Roar without losing half your health. If you get caught by Focused Resolve while trying to secure minions, you will face heavy damage. This constant pressure limits your map rotations and forces you to concede early dragon priority.
why: This matchup is dictated by Karma's oppressive ranged pressure. In the early game, her Inner Flame relentlessly chips away at your health, forcing you to play defensively. Whenever you attempt to close the distance for a Headbutt and Pulverize combo, she nullifies your threat by casting Inspire. This shield's movement speed burst allows her and her ally to effortlessly dance outside your initiation range while kiting you backward.

summary: Urgot can buffer his Disdain to ignore Pantheon's Shield Vault stun, flipping Pantheon behind him and bypassing the frontal protection of Aegis Assault.
howToPlay: Focus on spacing and chipping his health down with the tapped version of Comet Spear. Never initiate with Shield Vault unless you see him waste Disdain. If you get caught by Corrosive Charge, move laterally to dodge his incoming charge. If you do get flipped, delay using Aegis Assault until after the displacement to block his Purge during your retreat.
laneImpact: You cannot blindly force short trades, which severely limits your early pressure. A single successful counter-dash from Urgot chunks your health bar, forcing you under tower and conceding wave control. This health deficit puts you in immediate execute range of Fear Beyond Death, preventing proactive map plays with Grand Starfall.
why: The lane revolves around Urgot's ability to buffer Disdain to completely negate the stun from your Shield Vault. If he times his dash correctly, he flips you behind him. This displacement bypasses the frontal protection of Aegis Assault, leaving you exposed to his rapid Purge fire and passive Echoing Flames leg blasts.

summary: When Camille traps you with The Hextech Ultimatum (R), you can drop Twilight Shroud (W) to safely stealth and wait out the duration of her zone.
howToPlay: To win this, never engage with *Hookshot* while her *Twilight Shroud* is off cooldown. Instead, position yourself near walls to threaten instant wall-dives, forcing her to play defensively. When you cast *The Hextech Ultimatum*, expect her shroud immediately; do not swing blindly. Instead, back off slightly to outer range, use *Tactical Sweep* to sweep the smoke area to fish for her silhouette, and wait out her stealth before committing your *Precision Protocol*.
laneImpact: Trades are incredibly volatile. If Akali lands *Shuriken Flip*, she can bypass your *Tactical Sweep* outer-cone slow entirely. Your goal is to bait her energy pool down with short trades using *Precision Protocol*. Missing a *Hookshot* against her high mobility means she will instantly chase you down with *Perfect Execution*, forcing you to play defensively under tower and yielding all lane priority.
why: This duel hinges on how your ultimate interacts with her stealth. While *The Hextech Ultimatum* prevents Akali from escaping the perimeter, she can immediately counter your lock-down by casting *Twilight Shroud*. Inside her smoke screen, she becomes completely untargetable, neutralizing your offensive window. Your physical shield from *Adaptive Defenses* is also bypassed if she initiates with her heavy magic damage, making raw stats less reliable.

summary: Senna deals physical damage that bypasses the magic damage absorption of Black Shield, though the shield still blocks Last Embrace's root.
howToPlay: Shift your build priority entirely toward physical defense items to survive her heavy physical trades. Do not waste Dark Binding trying to fish for long-range catches through minion waves; hold it strictly as a defensive tool when she steps forward to harvest mist. If she misses Last Embrace, use that brief window to safely drop Tormented Shadow for wave control, staying positioned behind your minions to break her direct line of sight.
laneImpact: You are constantly shoved under tower because Senna's Piercing Darkness easily heals back any chip damage from Tormented Shadow while poking you down. Trading becomes impossible; she outranges you over time, forcing early recalls and letting her stack passive mist unchecked. This continuous pressure locks you in lane, preventing any roam opportunities to help your jungler, while your ADC is forced to farm under constant threat of tower dives.
why: Senna completely neutralizes your defensive utility because her heavy physical harass from basic attacks and Piercing Darkness entirely bypasses the magic damage absorption of Black Shield. While your Black Shield successfully prevents the root from Last Embrace, it absorbs zero damage from her trade patterns. This allows Senna to freely collect souls and scale her range while chipping your health bar down without any threat of a magic shield mitigation.

summary: Graves uses Quickdraw to slide out of Infernal Chains and dodge your Q sweetspots while stacking armor.
howToPlay: To survive this matchup, never initiate with Infernal Chains. Instead, force Graves to use Quickdraw defensively by aiming your first strike of The Darkin Blade directly at him. Only commit your Umbral Dash to adjust your sweetspots after he has spent his dash. If he blinds you with Smoke Screen, immediately back away using the bonus movement speed from World Ender rather than blindly swinging your sword and losing your passive sustain.
laneImpact: This mechanical advantage allows Graves to invade your jungle with impunity and contest camps early. You cannot comfortably contest Scuttle Crabs or defend your buffs in direct duels, as he will bait The Darkin Blade and force you out of your own jungle. If you fall behind in gold, his ranged pressure and End of the Line burst will completely lock you out of neutral objectives during the mid-game.
why: Graves systematically dismantles your skirmishing power because his Quickdraw is the perfect counter to your combo. Whenever you land Infernal Chains, he can simply dash out of the pull zone while simultaneously dodging the sweetspots of The Darkin Blade. This dodge also stacks armor on him, directly neutralizing the physical damage of your Deathbringer Stance and reducing the healing you receive from Umbral Dash.

summary: Ambessa can use Repudiation to block the third strike knock-up of Three Talon Strike, turning the tide of an early duel.
howToPlay: To win these duels, you must bait out her shield before committing your knock-up. Strike her twice with Three Talon Strike, then deliberately pause your basic attacks or use Wind Becomes Lightning to slow her down and force her to panic-cast Repudiation. If she holds it, use Audacious Charge to stay glued to her during Drakehound's Step dashes, saving your final knock-up punch until her glowing shield visual effect fades.
laneImpact: Because of this interaction, contesting Scuttle Crabs or invading her jungle becomes a high-stakes guessing game. If you engage blindly with Audacious Charge, she can easily kite with Drakehound's Step and wait for your third strike to deploy Repudiation. A failed duel means giving her Public Execution resets later, which completely destroys your team's skirmish pressure around the early neutral objectives.
why: Early jungle skirmishes between Xin Zhao and Ambessa are decided by a tight reaction-time window. Your primary crowd control and damage source, the third strike of Three Talon Strike, can be completely neutralized if Ambessa times Repudiation correctly. This block not only absorbs your knock-up but triggers her shield and counter-damage, swinging what should be a winning duel directly into her favor.

summary: Jayce can use Thundering Blow to knock Jarvan IV away mid-dash during his E-Q combo, preventing the knockup.
howToPlay: To win these burst trades, you must bait out Thundering Blow before committing. Walk up to threaten him with Martial Cadence enhanced attacks and use Golden Aegis to absorb his initial ranged poke. If he switches to his melee hammer to knock you away, that is your window. Once his knockback is on cooldown, instantly drop Demacian Standard and Dragon Strike to lock him down.
laneImpact: Because of this interaction, mindless aggression will get you poked down. If Jayce holds his hammer form, you cannot freely contest the wave with short burst trades. Forcing an early Cataclysm without securing a knockup first leads to disaster, as he can simply knock you out of your own arena or speed away with Hextech Capacitor. The lane becomes a tense stand-off where wave priority shifts based on who holds their key cooldowns.
why: This skill matchup revolves around the split-second interaction of your main engage. If you launch your Demacian Standard and follow up with Dragon Strike, a reactive Jayce can interrupt your flight mid-air with Thundering Blow. This completely nullifies your knockup, leaving you stranded in melee range without your primary escape or armor shred, while Jayce safely disengages or retaliates with his ranged forms.

summary: Lissandra's Glacial Path (E) engage is highly predictable, allowing Heimerdinger to easily land a stun with CH-2 Electron Storm Grenade (E).
howToPlay: Establish a triangle of H-28G Evolution Turret units slightly behind your minion wave, standing near them to benefit from Hextech Affinity. Always hold CH-2 Electron Storm Grenade; never throw it proactively to poke. When Lissandra projects Glacial Path toward you, walk slightly backward and aim your grenade directly at the end of her claw's path. If she hesitates to teleport, punish her with Hextech Micro-Rockets while keeping your distance to avoid Frozen Tomb.
laneImpact: This interaction completely neutralizes Lissandra's offensive pressure, forcing her to use Ice Shard solely for farming under her own turret. Since she cannot safely engage on you, you maintain permanent priority to crash waves and chip away at her tower plate health. Her inability to find quick lane kills severely limits her roam potential, keeping her locked in mid lane while you steadily build a massive gold advantage.
why: Lissandra relies heavily on Glacial Path to close the gap and initiate her burst. Because the claw's trajectory is completely visible and her teleport destination is highly predictable, you can easily time CH-2 Electron Storm Grenade directly onto her arrival point. Stunning her mid-engage completely shuts down her Ring of Frost threat, leaving her vulnerable to your pre-placed H-28G Evolution Turret barrage.

summary: Orianna constantly zones Annie with Command: Attack, making it nearly impossible for Annie to get into range without using Flash.
howToPlay: To survive this lane, never stand in a direct line between Orianna and her ball. Use the bonus movement speed from Molten Shield to bait and dodge Command: Attack, then immediately step up to farm. Accept losing some gold to preserve your health bar. Do not attempt a raw offensive engage; instead, save your Pyromania stun and only commit your Flash for a decisive Summon: Tibbers burst when your jungler arrives to punish her aggressive positioning.
laneImpact: This extreme range deficit forces you to play defensively under your turret, bleeding minion gold. You are forced to burn Molten Shield just to absorb Command: Attack poke while farming with Disintegrate. Because you are constantly chipped down and pushed in, you lose all mid-lane priority, preventing you from setting up Summon: Tibbers plays or assisting your jungler in the river without risking a deadly Command: Shockwave cascade.
why: Orianna's sphere creates an impassable barrier that completely neutralizes your offensive range. By constantly repositioning her ball with Command: Attack, she keeps you outside the radius of your Disintegrate and Incinerate. You cannot approach the wave to stack Pyromania safely because she will trigger Command: Dissonance the moment you step forward, exploiting your lack of mobility to poke you down without taking any retaliatory damage.

summary: Poppy's Steadfast Presence blocks all three casts of Riven's Q (Broken Wings) and her E (Valor), grounding and stunning her instantly.
howToPlay: Never waste your primary defensive tool proactively. Hold Steadfast Presence until Riven commits to her first Broken Wings or Valor animation. Once she is grounded and stunned by the barrier, immediately follow up with Heroic Charge to slam her into the nearest jungle wall, then smash her with Hammer Shock. If she tries to turn the fight with Blade of the Exile, use Keeper's Verdict to instantly disengage and deny her the duel.
laneImpact: This interaction shifts the entire jungle dynamic in your favor. Riven is forced to avoid direct river skirmishes and cannot safely contest Scuttle Crabs or epic monsters. If she attempts to invade or secure an objective, you can easily trap her near terrain. Her inability to freely skirmish limits her early gank pressure, forcing her into a defensive, slower farming route while your lanes scale safely.
why: Poppy completely shuts down Riven's high-mobility jungle playstyle thanks to a single, devastating interaction. Your Steadfast Presence acts as an impassable barrier, blocking all three casts of Broken Wings and her Valor dash. This instantly grounds and stuns her, stripping away her mobility and leaving her unable to stack Runic Blade effectively. Without her constant movement, she becomes a sitting duck in the river or her own jungle camps.

summary: Fiddlesticks can completely waste Tryndamere's Undying Rage by casting Terrify to force him to run away.
howToPlay: To survive this matchup, you must track his crowd control cooldowns meticulously. Never initiate an engage with Spinning Slash unless you have seen him waste Terrify on an ally first. If he initiates with Crowstorm from the fog of war, use Mocking Shout immediately to slow his advance, then spin over a wall to escape rather than triggering Undying Rage prematurely. Your primary goal is to split-push lanes where he is absent, forcing him to map-cover.
laneImpact: In the jungle, this interaction strips away your duel priority. You cannot safely invade him because any skirmish near his camps allows him to chain Terrify into Bountiful Harvest, turning the fight around. During objective contests, his Crowstorm ambush potential forces you to play defensively, preventing you from flanking or diving their backline because he will simply peel you off with his crowd control, leaving your team without frontline damage.
why: Fiddlesticks completely neutralizes your offensive threat by exploiting your reliance on close-range combat. The moment you activate Undying Rage to survive fatal damage, he can cast Terrify to force you into a helpless retreat, effectively ticking down your ultimate's precious seconds. Combined with the healing from Bountiful Harvest and the silence from Reap, you will struggle to stick to him long enough to land critical hits and refresh Spinning Slash.

summary: Rumble's magic damage completely bypasses Wukong's Stone Skin armor passive, making early magic resist itemization mandatory to survive the lane.
howToPlay: Abandon your standard offensive build path and rush magic resistance immediately on your first recall. During the early waves, let Rumble push and use Golden Staff to last-hit safely from a distance. If he tries to dive or trap you, use Warrior Trickster to absorb his damage and escape. Do not attempt a full-on engage with Cyclone unless your jungler is actively ganking, as you cannot win a 1v1 battle of attrition.
laneImpact: You will be shoved under tower constantly. Any attempt to contest the wave using Nimbus Strike results in taking heavy, unmitigated magic damage. This forces early, unfavorable recalls, costing you gold and experience. You cannot trade back effectively with Golden Staff because you are too squishy, allowing Rumble to secure free lane priority, roam to secure the river, or chip away at your tower.
why: Rumble's constant magic damage completely ignores the bonus armor you gain from Stone Skin. Because your passive is useless against his flames, you lack any natural defense to withstand his trade patterns. When you try to gap-close, his magic damage melts your health pool before you can even stack your armor, rendering your primary defensive tool completely obsolete in this lane.

summary: Cho'Gath can silence Ekko with Cri primal when he is low on health, preventing him from activating Chronobreak to escape and heal.
howToPlay: Do not waste Feral Scream early in trades; save this silence specifically for when Ekko's health drops near your Feast indicator threshold. When he initiates with Phase Dive, wait for the dash to end before placing Rupture directly under yourself to interrupt his retreat. If you miss your knock-up, disengage immediately and let Carnivore heal you back up rather than chasing him into his Parallel Convergence zone.
laneImpact: The lane quickly becomes an uneven war of attrition. While Ekko attempts quick trades with Phase Dive and Timewinder, your passive Carnivore heals back his burst damage effortlessly. This constant sustain forces Ekko to burn through his mana or stay in lane with low health. Once he is chipped down into execution range, he is forced to play extremely passively, giving you absolute control over the mid lane priority.
why: Ekko relies on Chronobreak to cheat death and reverse bad trades, but Cho'Gath completely neutralizes this safety net. By landing Feral Scream when Ekko's health drops, you lock him out of his ultimate entirely. This silence window prevents his escape and healing, leaving him completely vulnerable to a sudden, high-damage execution from Feast before he can react.

summary: Viktor can drop Gravity Field on top of himself to deter Kai'Sa from using Killer Instinct to dive him.
howToPlay: Keep a safe distance to easily dodge Void Seeker, as this projectile is her only way to mark you from afar. Never use Gravity Field aggressively to fish for stuns; instead, hold this ability specifically to react to her Killer Instinct. If she attempts to dive you, immediately cast it on yourself, follow up with Siphon Power for the shield, and use Hextech Ray to burst her down while she is stunned and unable to reposition.
laneImpact: This interaction dictates a lane where you hold complete control over the wave state. Kai'Sa cannot safely step up to clear minions with Icathian Rain without putting herself in range of your Hextech Ray poke. Since she lacks natural waveclear without isolating targets, you can easily shove her under turret, denying her roam timers and forcing her to use Supercharge defensively rather than to trade.
why: Kai'Sa relies on marking you with Void Seeker or plasma stacks to trigger Killer Instinct for a high-burst dive. However, Viktor completely shuts down this aggressive leap because his Gravity Field acts as an absolute zone of denial. Placing this stun field directly under your feet makes her ultimate target point a death trap, while your Siphon Power shield mitigates any initial burst from her Icathian Rain.

summary: Seraphine must position behind minions to block Death Sentence while using Beat Drop to punish Thresh when he walks up to Flay.
howToPlay: Always keep at least two minions between you and Thresh to nullify Death Sentence. When Thresh steps past his own wave to threaten Flay, immediately cast an Echoed Beat Drop to root him in place, rendering him unable to close the gap. Keep Surround Sound ready to shield his initial burst if you get caught, and only unleash Encore when Thresh is locked down by your minions or after he has already wasted his hook.
laneImpact: You cannot freely push the wave with Stage Presence boosted attacks, as standing still to poke invites a fatal hook. If Thresh lands Death Sentence, his follow-up with Flay and The Box will easily secure a kill or force your Flash. This pressure forces you to play defensively under your turret, sacrificing early priority and limiting your ability to assist your jungler, while Thresh uses Dark Passage to bring his allies for easy dives.
why: Thresh dictates the pace of this lane because his Death Sentence can instantly pull you out of your safe backline positioning. While your High Note allows you to poke him from a distance, your fragile health bar makes you highly vulnerable to his all-in potential. The matchup hinges on how you utilize minion waves to block his hook while using Beat Drop to counter his aggressive forward movements when he tries to set up Flay.

summary: Syndra's Scatter the Weak has a longer effective range than Brand's combo, allowing her to stun and burst him first.
howToPlay: To survive, you must anchor yourself behind your own caster minions and focus on farming with the outer edge of Pillar of Flame. Never walk in a straight line when her Dark Sphere is already on the ground. If she wastes Scatter the Weak and misses, you have a brief window to step up, use Conflagration to spread Blaze, and threaten a Sear stun. If she holds her stun, match her patience and farm safely.
laneImpact: You cannot step up to contest the wave safely. Every time you attempt to clear minions with Pillar of Flame, you risk walking into her sphere placement line. This forces you to concede early priority, letting her stack her Transcendent passive passively. If you get chunked by a projected sphere, you are forced into a premature recall, giving her free roam opportunities while you struggle.
why: This matchup is dictated by raw reach and burst speed. Syndra outranges you because her Scatter the Weak can launch a Dark Sphere from well outside your spellcasting perimeter. Because your Conflagration and Pillar of Flame require you to step forward, she can easily intercept your approach, stun you instantly, and follow up with Force of Will and Unleashed Power before you can even apply your Blaze passive.

summary: Ashe's Enchanted Crystal Arrow is a reliable tool to stun Akshan mid-air during his Heroic Swing, stopping his engage instantly.
howToPlay: To survive, you must position strictly behind your minion wave to block Volley and make it harder for her to land Enchanted Crystal Arrow directly. Never initiate with Heroic Swing while her ultimate is off cooldown; instead, hold this ability exclusively as an escape tool after she commits her crowd control. Wait for your support to bait out her ultimate before you commit your damage, or focus on farming safely with Avengerang until you get a clear gank from your jungler.
laneImpact: You cannot freely contest the wave because Ashe's Volley constantly chips away at your health from a distance, forcing you to play defensively under your turret. Initiating trades becomes highly risky. If you attempt to clear waves with Avengerang, she can retaliate with Ranger's Focus to punish your shorter range. This constant pressure delays your roam timings, keeping you locked in lane and unable to utilize Going Rogue to help your map.
why: Ashe heavily restricts your mobility because her Frost Shot slow makes it difficult to walk up and trigger Dirty Fighting. More critically, any attempt to aggressively flank or escape with Heroic Swing is completely shut down by Enchanted Crystal Arrow. If she fires her ultimate while you are swinging on your rope, the projectile is practically impossible to dodge mid-air, instantly stunning you and leaving you dead in your tracks.

summary: Rammus's Frenzying Taunt is completely negated by Mundo's passive, and Mundo's magic damage from Infected Bonesaw bypasses Rammus's high armor.
howToPlay: To survive, never engage Mundo alone. Instead, wait for an ally to trigger Goes Where He Pleases with another crowd control effect before you commit your Frenzying Taunt. During team skirmishes, use the leap from Soaring Slam to jump over Mundo and target his backline, rather than wasting your Defensive Ball Curl trying to tank his magic damage. If cornered, use Powerball to escape.
laneImpact: In the jungle, this interaction prevents you from contesting scuttle crabs or initiating direct duels. If you attempt a gank, Mundo can easily counter-gank; his Heart Zapper and Blunt Force Trauma allow him to clear camps faster, meaning he will consistently out-tempo your map pressure. Because Powerball is easily blocked by his body, you cannot lock down his carries.
why: Dr. Mundo completely neutralizes your primary ganking tool because Goes Where He Pleases absorbs the crowd control from Frenzying Taunt instantly. Furthermore, while Rammus thrives on stacking armor to boost Rolling Armordillo and Defensive Ball Curl, Mundo's Infected Bonesaw deals heavy magic damage based on your current health, entirely bypassing your physical defenses during direct duels.

summary: Viktor can drop Gravity Field directly on top of you while you are locked in place channeling Breath of Light.
howToPlay: Never initiate a channel of Breath of Light unless you see Viktor waste Gravity Field to zone or peel. When you need to gather Stardust, bait his Hextech Ray first by moving laterally, then use a quick Singularity to collect minions. If Viktor aggressively drops his zone on you, immediately cancel your channel and use Astral Flight to retreat safely before the stun triggers. Patience during his long cooldown windows is your only path to scaling.
laneImpact: This interaction severely restricts your wave management. You cannot freely use Singularity and Breath of Light to clear waves because Viktor will punish your immobility with Gravity Field and chunk you with Hextech Ray. Consequently, you are forced to farm defensively near your tower, conceding early lane priority and slowing down your passive scaling while Viktor safely stacks his Glorious Evolution and controls the mid lane.
why: Your main source of damage and Stardust, Breath of Light, forces you to stand completely still to channel. This self-root is a massive liability against Viktor, who can effortlessly drop Gravity Field directly on top of your static hitbox. If you try to trade back or clear waves with your channel, you instantly trigger his stun, leaving you vulnerable to a follow-up Hextech Ray and Arcane Storm.

summary: Yasuo can completely block Seraphine's ultimate Encore and basic abilities using Wind Wall, while using Sweeping Blade to easily dodge her slow skillshots.
howToPlay: To survive this matchup, you must pop his Way of the Wanderer shield with a basic attack before committing any mana. Never cast Encore or Beat Drop while his Wind Wall is available; instead, hold these spells to threaten him and force him to play defensively. If he dashes forward with Sweeping Blade, use Surround Sound immediately to absorb Steel Tempest's damage, then retreat toward your tower until his tornado charge expires.
laneImpact: You cannot safely contest the wave because stepping up to use High Note exposes you to a sudden Sweeping Blade engage. Yasuo will freeze the lane or shove you under tower, forcing you to burn Surround Sound to survive. His Way of the Wanderer shield constantly absorbs your poke, meaning you lose every health trade and are forced to recall early, sacrificing map pressure.
why: Yasuo's Wind Wall acts as a complete shutdown to your entire offensive kit, swallowing High Note, Beat Drop, and even your game-changing Encore. Because your spells have slow projectile speeds, he can easily react to them. Additionally, his Sweeping Blade gives him high mobility through your minion wave, allowing him to effortlessly slide out of your linear skillshots while charging Steel Tempest.

summary: Ashe's continuous slows from Frost Shot prevent Jhin from utilizing his passive movement speed to kite, and Enchanted Crystal Arrow easily cancels his Curtain Call.
howToPlay: Keep the minion wave frozen close to your turret by using Captive Audience in the lane bushes to slow down her fast pushes. Never activate Curtain Call within her vision unless you have confirmed that her Enchanted Crystal Arrow is on cooldown. When she turns on Ranger's Focus, immediately retreat to break the trade, then look to retaliate with Deadly Flourish only once her attack speed steroid has run its course.
laneImpact: Because her Volley easily outranges your basic attacks, you will constantly struggle to maintain priority. If you let her push you under turret, her superior reach allows her to poke you down relentlessly while you try to last-hit. This forces you to waste your Dancing Grenade defensively on the minion wave rather than looking for aggressive bounces, giving up all pressure on the bottom side of the map.
why: Ashe completely shuts down your kinetic playstyle. The burst of movement speed you rely on from Whisper is instantly negated by her constant slows from Frost Shot, leaving you incredibly easy to run down. Furthermore, activating your Curtain Call turns you into a sitting duck, making you the ultimate target for her Enchanted Crystal Arrow, which will stun you and cancel your ultimate instantly from afar.

summary: Viego can use Heartbreaker to dodge a crucial Q sweetspot while closing the distance to burst you down.
howToPlay: When fighting Aatrox, never waste Heartbreaker early. Bait out the first two strikes of The Darkin Blade, then cast your ultimate to blink through the final sweetspot and strike him. If he snares you with Infernal Chains, charge Spectral Maw to either stun him out of his combo or dash out of the pull zone. Always fight near walls where Harrowed Path provides the movement and attack speed necessary to out-DPS his World Ender healing.
laneImpact: Jungle skirmishes over Scuttle Crabs or objective entries become high-stakes duels where missing a single ability shifts the pressure. If Aatrox misses Infernal Chains, he cannot prevent you from closing in. Viego's stealth from Harrowed Path forces Aatrox to guess his Q angles blindly. The player who mismanages their cooldown windows loses total control over their jungle camps, granting the opponent free reign to invade.
why: This jungle duel revolves around the precise timing of Aatrox's The Darkin Blade. Aatrox relies on hitting those sweetspots to trigger knockups and sustain via Umbral Dash. However, Viego possesses the ultimate counter-tool: launching Heartbreaker allows you to leap over his third Q strike, completely dodging the critical sweetspot damage and crowd control while closing the gap to instantly burst him down before he can reset his Deathbringer Stance.

summary: Aurora can use Across the Veil to match Akali's stealth, making the lane a battle of who lands their skillshots first.
howToPlay: Never initiate a trade with Across the Veil; keep it strictly as a reaction to her Twilight Shroud or to dodge Perfect Execution. Use The Weirding to slow Akali and back away if she dashes forward with Shuriken Flip. If you miss Twofold Hex, immediately retreat to your caster minions to prevent her from exploiting your cooldown. When she activates her ultimate, trap her inside Between Worlds to restrict her massive dash range.
laneImpact: Trades are incredibly explosive but brief. Since both of you have tools to disengage, neither can easily force a full lane-ending dive without a major health lead. Minion waves act as shields; staying behind them prevents Akali from landing Shuriken Flip, allowing you to poke with Twofold Hex. The lane's control constantly swings back and forth based on who wastes their defensive mobility tool first.
why: This matchup is a pure duel of stealth and evasion. When Akali drops her Twilight Shroud to reposition and seek a trade, you can immediately respond with Across the Veil to enter your own brief invisibility and break her target lock. This nullifies her natural defensive advantage, turning their skirmishes into a tense mechanical race to see who can land Twofold Hex or Shuriken Flip first.

summary: Jarvan IV's Dragon Strike armor shred helps cut through Malphite's high armor, but Malphite's Unstoppable Force can easily dodge or counter-engage on Cataclysm.
howToPlay: To survive, position yourself near your own minion wave to make Malphite choose between hitting you or pushing the lane with Seismic Shard. Never initiate with Cataclysm while his Unstoppable Force is active; instead, bait his ultimate by walking up with Golden Aegis activated to absorb the initial burst. If he misses or uses his dash offensively, immediately retaliate with your Dragon Strike armor shred.
laneImpact: This matchup quickly devolves into a war of attrition. Malphite will constantly poke you down with Seismic Shard while regenerating his Granite Shield. If you step up too far to force trades with Demacian Standard and Dragon Strike, you risk getting slowed and crushed by Ground Slam. This constant harass limits your ability to freeze the wave, forcing you to play defensively under your own turret.
why: While your Dragon Strike provides crucial armor reduction to chip away at Malphite's high natural defense, the ultimate duel is heavily skewed. If you attempt to trap him with Cataclysm, Malphite can use the crowd-control immunity of Unstoppable Force to shrug off the impact or outright escape the arena, leaving you vulnerable to his high-impact counter-engage.

summary: Master Yi's Highlander makes him completely immune to the slow from Hecarim's items, and Alpha Strike can dodge the knockback of Devastating Charge.
howToPlay: To survive, you must play around his cooldown windows. Never initiate with Devastating Charge if his Alpha Strike is available; instead, run at him to force it out or wait for him to commit it first. If he activates Highlander, disengage immediately using Onslaught of Shadows to fear him away. If you must fight, wait until his Meditate is down so your Rampage and Spirit of Dread can actually cut through his health.
laneImpact: This scaling gap means you cannot contest him in isolated river duels once he gets his ultimate. If you meet him in the jungle, he will force fights knowing Meditate can stall out your Spirit of Dread duration. This pressure forces you to play defensively, giving up early scuttle crabs and jungle priority, which slows down your gold generation and puts your lanes under threat.
why: Master Yi naturally outscales you, and his kit directly counters your main tools. When he activates Highlander, he completely ignores any slows from your build. Worse, a skilled Yi will use Alpha Strike to dodge the crucial knockback from your Devastating Charge, leaving you with no way to disengage while his Wuju Style melts your health pool.

summary: Ezreal can use Arcane Shift to buffer and escape the stun of Enchanted Crystal Arrow if timed perfectly, neutralizing your primary engage.
howToPlay: Never use Arcane Shift offensively while Enchanted Crystal Arrow is available. Instead, bait her Volley behind minions, using Mystic Shot to thin the wave and keep your Rising Spell Force stacked. If she fires her ultimate from range, wait for the arrow to be right on top of you before hitting Arcane Shift to buffer the crowd control. If you mistime this buffer, immediately charge Trueshot Barrage to deal trade damage before her Ranger's Focus melts your health pool.
laneImpact: When Enchanted Crystal Arrow is offline, you gain a massive window to dictate the wave state. Landing Mystic Shot consistently reduces your cooldowns, allowing you to stack Rising Spell Force and out-push her. However, if she forces your Arcane Shift with Volley spam or raw pressure, her arrow becomes a lethal threat that forces you to forfeit priority or face a deadly freeze.
why: This even lane revolves around how you handle Ashe's ultimate. While Volley matches your Mystic Shot poke, the absolute turning point is Enchanted Crystal Arrow. If you time Arcane Shift perfectly, the cast animation buffers the stun, blinking you to safety even as the arrow connects. This completely negates her primary tool to lock you down for her Ranger's Focus barrage.

summary: Katarina must stand near her daggers to waveclear, making her a predictable target for your Avengerang and Heroic Swing.
howToPlay: Position yourself away from her dropped daggers to deny her Shunpo damage, but close enough to punish her with Dirty Fighting double attacks when she steps up. Hold Heroic Swing until she commits to a dagger or uses her Death Lotus; using it prematurely lets her escape or turn the fight. Once she is forced to base, immediately use Going Rogue to stealth-roam towards active skirmishes, securing easy hunts on her jungler or side lanes.
laneImpact: This constant threat of physical burst forces Katarina to play defensively, sacrificing health or gold under her turret. You easily secure early priority, letting you crash waves and dictate roam timings before she can even dream of moving. By keeping her pinned and chunked, you neutralize her skirmishing potential and protect your side lanes from her lethal Death Lotus rotations.
why: Katarina cannot safely farm without dropping daggers via Bouncing Blade and Preparation. Because she must step near these daggers to trigger her Voracity passive and clear the wave, her positioning is completely telegraphed. This predictability allows you to easily line up Avengerang through the minions to poke her, while prepping a devastating Heroic Swing trajectory directly onto her landing spot the moment she uses Shunpo.

summary: Teemo's Toxic Shot (P) poke is largely absorbed by Galio's Shield of Durand (W) passive shield, and Teemo lacks the mobility to escape Galio's E-W combo.
howToPlay: Walk up confidently and bait Teemo into activating his Move Quick speed boost. Once that temporary mobility expires, strike immediately by aiming your Justice Punch directly at him during his basic attack animation, following up with Winds of War and a quick Shield of Durand taunt. If you miss your knockup, do not chase him into potential Noxious Trap spots; instead, fall back until your passive magic shield regenerates before trying again.
laneImpact: This matchup completely flips the usual ranged-versus-melee dynamic. You can ignore Teemo's Blinding Dart because your main damage comes from Winds of War and the area-of-effect slam of Colossal Smash rather than basic attacks. You will constantly hold wave priority, forcing Teemo under his turret where he struggles to farm, while preventing him from safely littering the lane with his invisible Noxious Trap mushrooms.
why: Teemo thrives on suffocating melee champions with his Toxic Shot poison, but your Shield of Durand passive magic shield completely neutralizes this damage over time. Because Teemo has no real dashes to escape, any attempt he makes to poke you leaves him incredibly vulnerable. Once he steps forward, he cannot outrun your Justice Punch and Shield of Durand crowd control chain, making him an easy target to lock down.

summary: Ambessa can bait Master Yi's Alpha Strike, then immediately lock him down with Public Execution once he reappears.
howToPlay: When initiating a skirmish, start with Cunning Sweep and Lacerate to chip his health down. Do not commit your ultimate early. Instead, watch his character model closely; the instant he activates Alpha Strike to dodge your outer-edge strike, hover your cursor over his landing location. As soon as he reappears, immediately cast Public Execution to lock him down. If he tries to mitigate the damage using Meditate, your suppression will immediately interrupt his channel.
laneImpact: In the jungle, this pressure completely disrupts Master Yi's farming speed. You can aggressively invade his camps, as he cannot safely fight you near walls where your Drakehound's Step thrives. By denying him clean camps, you delay his Highlander power spike. He is forced to play defensively, surrendering early neutral objectives and river control because he risks getting caught and executed every time he tries to contest.
why: Ambessa dominates this duel because her high-tempo dashes from Drakehound's Step force Master Yi to make a choice. He wants to dodge your damage with Alpha Strike, but you can easily bait this out. The moment he becomes targetable again, he has no escape, allowing you to instantly suppress him with Public Execution before he can stack Double Strike or run you down with Highlander.

summary: Aatrox's physical vamp from Umbral Dash easily out-sustains Malphite's Seismic Shard poke during the laning phase.
howToPlay: To execute this perfectly, pop his Granite Shield with a simple auto-attack or the tip of The Darkin Blade before committing to a full trade. Always save your Umbral Dash to reposition your Q sweetspots or to slide out of his slow zone after he hits you with Seismic Shard. Once he is low on mana, freeze the wave near your turret and zone him out. If he attempts to escape with Unstoppable Force or turn on you, activate World Ender to chase him down.
laneImpact: This absolute sustain advantage translates into complete dominance over wave states. You can slow push massive waves into his turret because Malphite cannot step up to contest without taking devastating trades. While he struggles to last-hit under tower under pressure, you can freely bounce the wave or lock it near your side, forcing him to overextend or lose precious gold while his Granite Shield remains constantly broken.
why: Malphite relies on chipping away your health with Seismic Shard, but his limited mana pool cannot compete with your endless recovery. The passive physical vamp from Umbral Dash allows you to heal back all of his magical damage simply by landing your strikes. Because Seismic Shard has a high cost and low base damage early on, Aatrox easily wins this war of attrition without needing to rely on fruit or recalls.

summary: Ezreal can easily reposition with Arcane Shift to dodge Jhin's Deadly Flourish or escape the path of Curtain Call.
howToPlay: To survive, you must play around his cooldowns. Never initiate with Deadly Flourish; instead, conserve it until after he uses Arcane Shift aggressively or defensively. Rely on Dancing Grenade bouncing off dying minions to poke him safely behind your wave. If you decide to open Curtain Call, wait until your support forces his blink, or target his support instead to force a favorable numbers advantage while his mobility tool is unavailable.
laneImpact: This interaction neuters your aggressive trade potential, forcing a slower, more defensive laning phase. Because you cannot reliably land Deadly Flourish, you lose the threat of sudden all-ins. Ezreal will freely poke with Mystic Shot while keeping his distance, slowly chipping away at your health bar. This limits your priority, pushing you to farm under turret and reducing your capacity to assist in river skirmishes.
why: Ezreal holds a distinct advantage because Arcane Shift serves as a reliable emergency button to bypass your entire pick potential. Whenever you attempt to lock him down with Deadly Flourish, he can instantly blink out of the projectile's path. This mobility also makes him exceptionally slippery when you channel Curtain Call, allowing him to easily escape your firing sector before your fourth Whisper shot can find its mark.

summary: Lux's Light Binding can root Alistar mid-engage, but if she misses, she has no escape from his Headbutt-Pulverize combo.
howToPlay: Never use Light Binding aggressively unless Alistar is already locked down or too low to fight back. Keep this projectile specifically to interrupt his Headbutt or to zone him when he tries to walk up. Cast Lucent Singularity into lane bushes to reveal his position and slow his approach. If Alistar activates Unbreakable Will to break your root, immediately retreat, using Prismatic Barrier to absorb his carry's damage while you wait out his ultimate.
laneImpact: Because Alistar heals through Triumphant Roar, your poke must be relentless; sporadic damage won't stick. Successfully kiting him allows you to push waves and secure tower pressure. However, the moment your positioning falters and you get caught by Headbutt, his lane partner will easily follow up. Surviving his burst with Prismatic Barrier is rare, meaning one mistake instantly flips lane control and forces an early, costly recall.
why: This skill matchup hinges entirely on how you space against Alistar's threat range. You want to constantly harass the minotaur with Lucent Singularity to trigger Illumination, but doing so safely requires keeping Light Binding ready. If Alistar initiates with Headbutt, a well-timed Light Binding can stop him mid-dash. Missing this crucial skillshot leaves you completely exposed to his devastating Pulverize and subsequent Trample lockup.

summary: Akali can easily dodge Brand's Sear and Pillar of Flame using Shuriken Flip or Perfect Execution to close the gap and burst him down.
howToPlay: Bait his Pillar of Flame by walking forward, then immediately react with Shuriken Flip to dodge sideways and mark him. Do not immediately recast it if he is holding Sear; wait out his panic stun attempt inside your Twilight Shroud. Once his projectile misses, reactivate to fly in, trigger Assassin's Mark, and finish him with Perfect Execution. If he plays extremely safe, use your mobility to dive him directly when his mana is low.
laneImpact: Early on, Brand will try to poke you down with Pillar of Flame while you collect CS. However, because he must cast spells to clear, he naturally pushes the wave. This leaves him overextended. Once you reach level five, the threat of your Perfect Execution completely freezes his aggressive posture, giving you complete priority to crash waves and hunt him under his own tower.
why: Brand depends entirely on landing Pillar of Flame and following up with Sear to stun you. However, Akali has a massive kit advantage because Shuriken Flip and Perfect Execution allow her to effortlessly dodge these slow skillshots. Once you bypass his initial spell rotation, Brand has no escape tools, making him incredibly vulnerable to your burst damage.

summary: Lucian can use Relentless Pursuit to close the gap and bypass Volley's slow, quickly bursting you down with Lightslinger double-shots.
howToPlay: Maintain maximum distance and never cast Volley unless Relentless Pursuit is on cooldown. If he dashes forward aggressively, immediately fire Enchanted Crystal Arrow point-blank to halt his Lightslinger onslaught, then use the stun duration to disengage rather than fight back. Keep Ranger's Focus ready by tagging minions, but only commit to auto-attacking when Lucian's mobility spell is fully expended and your support can peel for you.
laneImpact: You cannot safely contest wave priority, as stepping up past your caster minions invites an immediate dash engage. Every time you throw out Volley to secure farm, you leave yourself vulnerable to his dive; if he capitalizes, you are forced to retreat to tower or burn spells. This pressure limits your gold income, delays your scaling, and forces you to play defensively under turret while Lucian controls the river.
why: Lucian severely punishes your lack of mobility by using Relentless Pursuit to instantly bypass the slow from Volley. Once he slides past your main self-peel, his Lightslinger double-shots trigger rapidly alongside Piercing Light, chunking your health bar before Frost Shot can create meaningful distance. Since your basic attacks rely on ramping up Ranger's Focus, his immediate, explosive burst heavily outvalues your sustained damage in short, aggressive trades.

summary: Braum's Unbreakable shield can intercept and completely destroy Brand's Sear and Pyroclasm projectiles, neutralizing his entire burst combo.
howToPlay: First force Unbreakable's facing with Pillar of Flame or Conflagration, then change angle before sending Sear. Do not launch Pyroclasm into the shield's front. If Winter's Bite hits, leave before Concussive Blows stacks; when it misses, reclaim an angle and apply Blaze to the carry rather than Braum.
laneImpact: Casting the whole sequence into the shield deals little and lets Braum walk forward while your abilities recover. If Winter's Bite lands, his duo's attacks then threaten the stun and push you away from the wave. Side angles matter more here than the number of spells you cast.
why: Unbreakable blocks the first projectile and reduces following damage from the same direction. It can remove Sear or Pyroclasm's first bounce, then protect Braum's carry. Winter's Bite also applies the first Concussive Blows stack, making an extended exchange dangerous for an immobile Brand.

summary: Morgana's Black Shield completely absorbs the crowd control of Alistar's Headbutt-Pulverize combo, leaving him stranded in the enemy minion wave.
howToPlay: Never cast Black Shield proactively; hold it specifically for the moment Alistar winds up his Headbutt. Stand slightly behind your ADC to bait his advance, then immediately react with your shield. Once Alistar’s combo fails and he is stranded, lock him down instantly with Dark Binding and drop Tormented Shadow underneath him. If he activates Unbreakable Will to survive, disengage immediately and wait out its duration before resuming your aggressive poke.
laneImpact: Because Alistar cannot reliably engage without risking a disastrous counter-attack, his lane partner is forced to play extremely defensively. You can safely position forward to poke with Tormented Shadow, slowly grinding down their health. Since Alistar’s Triumphant Roar only offers minor sustain, your constant pressure forces them under tower, allowing your duo to easily control the wave state and secure deep river vision with absolute safety.
why: This matchup is heavily in your favor because Black Shield completely neutralizes Alistar’s entire identity. When Alistar attempts his Headbutt into Pulverize initiator combo, a well-timed Black Shield on his target entirely absorbs the knock-up and knock-back. This leaves the massive minotaur sitting uselessly deep in your minion wave, having burned his primary crowd control tools while remaining completely exposed to your retaliation.

summary: Lillia's passive movement speed from Blooming Blows allows her to effortlessly dance around your The Darkin Blade sweetspots.
howToPlay: Never initiate with The Darkin Blade when she has full stacks. Instead, wait in brush to ambush her, or hold your Umbral Dash exclusively to reposition your sweetspots after she commits her Watch Out! Eep! dash. If she catches you in the open river with high momentum, do not chase. Use Infernal Chains defensively to force her to path sideways, and activate World Ender only to escape her sleep wake-up damage or to match her rotation to a collapsing teammate.
laneImpact: Because you cannot lock her down, Lillia easily secures Scuttle Crabs and rotates faster to skirmishes. In neutral objective fights, her ability to lob Swirlseed from safety can slow you down, setting up a multi-man Lilting Lullaby. You will constantly find yourself outpaced in your own camps, unable to challenge her deep invades because you cannot land Infernal Chains on a target moving that fast.
why: In the jungle, you will struggle immensely because of Lillia's hyper-mobility. Every time she hits a camp or you with her abilities, she stacks Blooming Blows, gaining massive movement speed. This extra velocity makes it incredibly easy for her to effortlessly dance in and out of your The Darkin Blade sweetspots, rendering your main damage source and knockups completely useless.

summary: Aurora can use Across the Veil to drop aggro and dodge your Heroic Swing shots, turning the trade in her favor if you commit too early.
howToPlay: Never initiate with Across the Veil. Keep it specifically to counter Akshan's Heroic Swing. Position yourself near your own minions to block Avengerang's extension path, and use The Weirding to slow his approach if he tries to flank with Going Rogue. If he commits to a swing, press Across the Veil to break his target lock, then instantly drop Between Worlds to trap him mid-flight and burst him down.
laneImpact: The threat of Heroic Swing prevents Aurora from blindly pushing the wave with Twofold Hex, as Akshan can punish her if Across the Veil is on cooldown. Trades are explosive and frequent; a single successful Avengerang hit followed by a swing can force an early recall. Conversely, if Aurora successfully baits the swing, she secures complete priority to shove the lane and roam.
why: Aurora and Akshan engage in a high-stakes spacing duel where any misstep is punished. The core matchup revolves around Akshan's Heroic Swing. If Akshan swings in, Aurora can immediately cast Across the Veil to enter brief invisibility, forcing him to drop targeting and lose his crucial Heroic Swing shots. This completely neutralizes his main burst, allowing Aurora to retaliate with Twofold Hex and Spirit Abjuration.

summary: Miss Fortune is highly vulnerable to Heroic Swing all-ins when she channels Bullet Time, as she cannot move to dodge his damage.
howToPlay: To survive, never channel Bullet Time unless Akshan has already committed his Heroic Swing or is completely CC'd by your support. Keep your distance from walls to limit his grapple angles, and use Make It Rain to slow his movement, making it harder for him to find a clean swing path. If he tries to lock you down with Comeuppance, position yourself behind a minion wave or your support so the bullets hit them instead of you.
laneImpact: During the laning phase, Akshan uses Avengerang to push waves while poking you, which threatens to trigger Dirty Fighting's shield if you try to retaliate. Because of his constant threat of a Heroic Swing all-in, you cannot freely step up to use Double Up on low-health minions. If you lose your passive Strut movement speed to his poke, you are forced to play defensively under tower, sacrificing priority and letting him roam.
why: Akshan dominates this lane because your ultimate, Bullet Time, forces you to stand completely still, making you an easy target for his Heroic Swing. While you channel your cone of bullets, Akshan can easily anchor his grapple to a nearby wall, swinging completely out of your firing angle while unloading massive physical damage. This mobility mismatch turns your strongest teamfight tool into a self-inflicted trap.

summary: Poppy's Steadfast Presence completely shuts down Ambessa's Drakehound's Step dashes, grounding her and dealing heavy damage.
howToPlay: To dominate, never initiate with Steadfast Presence; instead, walk up using the extra range of Iron Ambassador to bait her into casting Cunning Sweep. Once she commits to a direction, activate your zone to catch her passive dash, then position yourself to slam her into a wall with Heroic Charge. If you misstep and she bypasses your zone with Public Execution, immediately use a quick cast of Keeper's Verdict to knock her airborne and reset the fight.
laneImpact: In the jungle, this matchup changes how skirmishes around objectives and scuttle crabs play out. Ambessa cannot safely contest territory because her skirmishing power is gated by your defensive aura. If she attempts to clear camps near you, you can force highly asymmetric health trades where her Repudiation shield is wasted while she is grounded. This constant threat forces her to concede river priority, allowing you to secure early map control.
why: Ambessa relies entirely on constant dashes from Drakehound's Step after every ability to reposition and burst her targets. Poppy completely neutralizes this offensive flow because her Steadfast Presence stops these passive leaps dead in their tracks. By grounding Ambessa and dealing magic damage when she tries to trigger her mobility, Poppy strips away her combat agility, leaving her vulnerable to a quick Hammer Shock smash.

summary: Ornn can use Bellows Breath to become Unstoppable and ignore Aatrox's Q knockups, but he remains vulnerable to Aatrox's sustained physical vamp.
howToPlay: To secure this advantage, do not commit all three strikes of *The Darkin Blade* immediately if his *Bellows Breath* is available. Instead, bait his fire breath with your first strike, then reposition laterally with *Umbral Dash* to avoid the Brittle application. Once his fire stops, pull him back with *Infernal Chains* and unleash your full combo. If he attempts to escape using *Searing Charge*, interrupt his dash trajectory with your remaining sweetspots to seal the kill.
laneImpact: You dictate the wave's positioning because Ornn cannot safely contest your sustain without burning major mana. Whenever he misses *Volcanic Rupture* or wastes *Searing Charge* into a wall, a massive window opens. You can drag him into long trades using *Infernal Chains*, forcing him under his turret with low health. This denies him the safety needed to utilize *Living Forge*, rendering his passive crafting advantage useless in lane.
why: While Ornn can timed *Bellows Breath* to shrug off the knockups from *The Darkin Blade*, he cannot stop your relentless healing. Since *Bellows Breath* makes him unstoppable but doesn't reduce your incoming sustain, your passive *Deathbringer Stance* and the physical vamp from *Umbral Dash* will consistently repair any damage he inflicts. He simply lacks the DPS to outpace your constant health regeneration in a drawn-out duel.

summary: Ezreal can freely poke Vayne with Mystic Shot whenever she steps up to last-hit, using Arcane Shift to stay out of range of her Tumble and Condemn.
howToPlay: Constantly position yourself behind your own minions to block her direct line of sight while spamming Mystic Shot as she approaches the wave. Never use Arcane Shift aggressively unless her Tumble is down and you have a clear health advantage; save this blink to escape if she attempts to pin you against the wall with Condemn. If you miss several skillshots and she manages to freeze, use Trueshot Barrage to break the freeze from a safe distance.
laneImpact: This range discrepancy forces Vayne to constantly bleed health just to secure minions, giving you complete control over the wave state. You can easily slow-push waves while keeping her low, meaning she cannot contest your dragon lane priority. This relentless health pressure forces her into terrible, early recall timings, allowing you to secure plates and build a massive gold lead before she can scale.
why: Ezreal completely dictates this matchup because Vayne's short-range kit has no answer to your long-range poke. Every time she moves forward to last-hit, you can easily clip her with Mystic Shot. If she tries to close the gap with Tumble to trade back or set up a stun with Condemn, you can instantly disengage using Arcane Shift, leaving her completely exposed and unable to retaliate.

summary: Annie can easily sidestep Brand's Pillar of Flame using the movement speed from Molten Shield, then retaliate with a guaranteed stun combo.
howToPlay: Position yourself slightly behind your own minions so Brand cannot land a direct Sear if he tries to aggressive flash. Always hold Molten Shield specifically to react to the ground animation of Pillar of Flame. The moment he misses, immediately run forward with your increased speed, trigger Pyromania with a targeted Disintegrate to lock him down, and follow up with Incinerate and Summon: Tibbers to secure an easy kill.
laneImpact: Because you can neutralise his main poke, Brand is forced to play extremely far back. He cannot use Pillar of Flame on the minion wave without leaving himself open to an immediate stun. This allows you to control the wave pace with Disintegrate. You can safely freeze or crash waves at will, denying him gold while keeping him constantly threatened by a sudden Summon: Tibbers burst.
why: This matchup leans heavily in Annie's favor because Brand's entire damage threat relies on landing Pillar of Flame to trigger Blaze. By activating Molten Shield, you gain the instant movement speed required to easily sidestep his circular ground target. Once Pillar of Flame is wasted, Brand has no reliable way to stun you with Sear, leaving him completely vulnerable to your Pyromania-infused counter-attack.

summary: Caitlyn must avoid standing directly behind low-health minions to prevent Miss Fortune from landing critical Double Up bounces.
howToPlay: To win this trade war, adopt a diagonal positioning rule relative to the minion wave. Never stand in a straight line behind your dying minions; instead, stand off to the side where you can safely land Headshot procs. Hold your 90 Caliber Net strictly to escape her Bullet Time or to reposition if she tries to run you down with Strut. If she misses a Double Up, immediately punish her with a Piltover Peacemaker while her bounce is on cooldown.
laneImpact: Because of this threat, wave control becomes highly volatile. If Miss Fortune uses Make It Rain to shove and slow you, you must respond with Piltover Peacemaker to prevent her from locking you under turret. Trading health is extremely punitive here; whoever drops low first loses the ability to contest the wave, as a well-placed Yordle Snap Trap or a sudden Bullet Time can easily seal a dive or force an early recall.
why: This lane is a pure horizontal shootout where your superior auto-attack range and Piltover Peacemaker are constantly threatened by Miss Fortune's Double Up. While you want to abuse your Headshot passive to poke her down from maximum range, she can punish your standard laning posture instantly if you align yourself behind low-health minions. Her Double Up bounce deals devastating critical damage, offsetting your natural range advantage.

summary: Kindred can drop Lamb's Respite inside Cataclysm to save themselves and their team from Jarvan's burst combo.
howToPlay: To survive, prioritize protecting your jungle entrances with Golden Aegis for slow and vision. Do not initiate with your full Dragon Strike and Demacian Standard combo; instead, walk up to use Martial Cadence and Golden Aegis first, forcing Kindred to use Dance of Arrows defensively. Save Cataclysm until after Lamb's Respite has been forced out by your teammates' damage, or use your arena purely to isolate other priority targets away from Kindred's protective circle.
laneImpact: In the jungle, Kindred will aggressively invade your camps to stack Mark of the Kindred, knowing you cannot easily duel them. If you attempt to contest them, their Wolf's Frenzy and Dance of Arrows allow them to kite your melee range effortlessly. Failing an early fight means giving up control of your neutral camps, which a snowballing Kindred will exploit to pressure your lanes.
why: This matchup is defined by how Kindred completely neutralizes your engage. When you lock them down with Cataclysm and commit your Dragon Strike and Demacian Standard burst, Kindred simply drops Lamb's Respite inside your arena. This denies your Martial Cadence execute and protects their entire team from your initial burst, leaving you trapped in your own wall while they retaliate with Dance of Arrows.

summary: Syndra can easily interrupt your Breath of Light channel from a safe distance using Scatter the Weak.
howToPlay: To survive, prioritize farming from maximum distance solely using Singularity to gather Cosmic Creator stacks. Never channel Breath of Light unless Syndra has recently wasted Scatter the Weak; this cooldown is your only safe window to actively clear. If she holds her stun, remain patient under turret and accept losing some farm. Should she catch you with Unleashed Power, immediately use Astral Flight defensively toward your tower rather than trying to fight back.
laneImpact: You cannot safely contest the wave state or secure priority. Every time you attempt to clear minions using Singularity and Breath of Light, Syndra will punish your stationary posture with Force of Will and Dark Sphere. This forced passivity pushes you under your turret, bleeding tower plates and preventing you from assisting your jungler, while allowing Syndra to freely scale and upgrade her abilities through Transcendent.
why: This matchup is entirely dictated by how easily Syndra can disrupt your trading patterns. Your primary damage tool, Breath of Light, requires you to remain stationary or fly in a predictable line during Astral Flight. Syndra can effortlessly interrupt this channel from a safe distance by launching a Dark Sphere with Scatter the Weak. This immediate knockback and stun completely cancels your DPS while leaving you immobilized and exposed to her follow-up burst.

summary: Janna's Howling Gale can easily interrupt Alistar's Headbutt mid-dash, and her Monsoon completely resets any successful engage he manages to land.
howToPlay: Never throw Howling Gale randomly for poke; keep it ready solely to react to his Headbutt animation. Position yourself slightly behind your ADC so you can reactively peel for them. If Alistar activates Unbreakable Will to cleanse your knock-up, do not panic or waste damage; simply use Tailwind's extra movement speed and the slow from Zephyr to kite backwards until his massive damage reduction wears off.
laneImpact: Because you can consistently deny his initiation, Alistar cannot easily contest the wave or secure bush control. This allows you to safely harass him with Zephyr and shield your AD carry with Eye of the Storm whenever he tries to step up. The lane becomes a slow poke-out where Alistar's Triumphant Roar cannot keep up with your constant ranged pressure, forcing him to play defensively under tower.
why: Janna completely shuts down Alistar's primary engage pattern. His reliance on using Headbutt to close the distance is utterly neutralized by a well-timed Howling Gale, which stops his dash mid-air. Even if he manages to flash-combo with Pulverize, casting Monsoon immediately blows him away, rendering his follow-up Trample useless and wasting his dive attempt entirely.

summary: Use your multiple Drakehound's Step dashes to easily close the gap on Mini Gnar and burst him down before he can build enough Rage for Mega Gnar.
howToPlay: Trigger your engage when Gnar's rage bar is low, ensuring he cannot transform mid-fight. Start with Cunning Sweep, using the Drakehound's Step dash to close the gap and trigger the Slam follow-up. Save Repudiation specifically to block his Boomerang Throw slow or to absorb the stun from Boulder Toss if he manages to transform. If he attempts to escape with Hop, immediately match it with Public Execution to lock him down and finish him off.
laneImpact: This dynamic strips Gnar of his usual ranged harassment advantage. He is forced to respect your dash range, meaning you can easily control the wave state. If he steps up to stack Hyper on minions, you can instantly initiate a trade. You will secure early health leads that force him into terrible recall timings, neutralizing his tower pressure and preventing him from ever safely farming in his vulnerable Mini state.
why: Ambessa dominates this matchup because Mini Gnar cannot maintain his spacing against her relentless mobility. Every time you cast Cunning Sweep or Lacerate, Drakehound's Step provides a swift dash that completely bypasses his Boomerang Throw slow and Hop retreat. This allows you to rapidly stick to him and deplete his fragile health pool before his Rage Gene can transition him into the tanky Mega Gnar form.

summary: Wukong can clone with Warrior Trickster to dodge Kayle's Radiant Blast and close the gap with Nimbus Strike.
howToPlay: Stand parallel to your minion wave to tempt her into casting Radiant Blast for waveclear. The moment you see the projectile animation, press Warrior Trickster forward to tank the hit, then immediately press Nimbus Strike onto her. Follow up with Golden Staff for armor reduction. If she responds with Divine Judgment, simply walk alongside her and delay your second Cyclone activation until her golden invulnerability shield expires.
laneImpact: This matchup dynamic forces Kayle to play incredibly defensively, relying solely on Starfire Spellblade to secure distant last hits. Because you threaten a lethal burst trade whenever her main spell is down, you easily control the wave's positioning. You can freely deny her gold, slow push massive waves to dive her, or force her to burn Celestial Blessing for raw survival instead of trading.
why: Wukong holds a massive advantage because Kayle relies heavily on Radiant Blast to keep melee lane opponents at bay. When she casts it, you can instantly deploy Warrior Trickster to absorb the slow and armor shred. This leaves Kayle completely defenseless against your immediate gap-closer, Nimbus Strike, allowing you to execute a massive burst combo before she can safely retreat to her tower.

summary: Viktor's Hextech Ray (E) is a ground-targeted laser trace, meaning it completely bypasses Yasuo's Wind Wall (W) to poke him down safely.
howToPlay: To survive, trigger his Way of the Wanderer shield with a basic attack before committing your mana. Only cast Gravity Field directly on top of yourself when he commits to a Sweeping Blade dash towards you, forcing him to abort his trade or get stunned.
