If he wastes his tornado from Steel Tempest, you have a six-second window to step forward and poke. If he freezes near his tower, fall back and wait for the wave to bounce.
laneImpact: This matchup forces a delicate balancing act under your tower. Yasuo will aggressively shove the wave with Steel Tempest to create dash targets, seeking to force you into bad recall timings. You must concede early priority, using Hextech Ray to thin the wave from afar. If you let him stack his tornado and dash in, a single knock-up leads to Last Breath, ending your laning phase immediately.
why: Yasuo holds the upper hand because Sweeping Blade allows him to constantly dodge your skillshots and close the gap for lethal trades. However, this lane remains manageable due to a unique interaction: your Hextech Ray is a ground-targeted laser that completely ignores his Wind Wall. While he can easily block your Siphon Power projectile, you can consistently bypass his main defense to chip away at his health bar.

summary: Teemo's Blinding Dart (Q) does not affect the damage of your Five Point Strike (Q) or Shuriken Flip (E), allowing you to easily burst him down.
howToPlay: Let Teemo push the early waves while preserving your health. Once you unlock Twilight Shroud, use its cover to bypass his Toxic Shot harass while farming. When you reach level five, fish for Shuriken Flip. If it connects, immediately reactivate it even if he uses Blinding Dart, then execute him using Five Point Strike and Perfect Execution. If you accidentally trigger a Noxious Trap, retreat into your shroud to drop aggro and reset.
laneImpact: While Teemo's Toxic Shot makes the first two levels tedious, the pressure shifts entirely to you once you unlock Twilight Shroud. He cannot safely poke you under your shroud, nor can his Move Quick save him from your gap-closers. You will control the lane pace completely, forcing Teemo to freeze near his tower or risk getting instantly deleted the moment he steps up to farm.
why: Teemo relies on Blinding Dart to shut down auto-attackers, but your primary damage comes entirely from spells. Both Five Point Strike and Shuriken Flip bypass his blind completely, meaning his main defensive utility is useless against your spell rotations. Once you land your shuriken, you can confidently commit to an all-in burst, knowing his poison cannot outdamage your rapid ability sequence.

summary: Corki can easily escape the area of Miss Fortune's Bullet Time using Valkyrie while immediately retaliating with his own Missile Barrage.
howToPlay: To win this matchup, never activate Bullet Time unless you have forced Corki to burn Valkyrie first, or he is hard CC'd by your support. Stand diagonally behind your minions to line up Double Up angles while avoiding his straight-line Gatling Gun. If he dashes forward aggressively with Valkyrie, drop Make It Rain directly on yourself to slow his pursuit and use the Strut active to safely disengage.
laneImpact: The lane revolves around constant attrition. You must use Double Up bounces to pressure Corki through minion waves while keeping Strut active to dodge his Phosphorus Bomb. If he gets his Special Delivery upgrade, you lose all lane priority; his enhanced dash can force you off the wave entirely or cancel your movement speed, turning the poke war heavily in his favor.
why: This lane is a relentless long-range shootout where your ultimate can easily backfire. While you aim to lock Corki down with Make It Rain to set up Bullet Time, his Valkyrie allows him to slide right out of your cone of fire. Worse, because you are rooted during your ultimate, he can immediately turn and shred you from safety with Missile Barrage rockets.

summary: If Maokai uses Twisted Advance on Galio's ADC, Galio can time Justice Punch to knock Maokai up as soon as he emerges.
howToPlay: Position yourself slightly behind your partner, maintaining a diagonal angle that lets you react instantly to Twisted Advance. Never waste Justice Punch for raw damage or wave clear; keep it solely to match his engage. If Maokai manages to bait your dash and locks down your ally, immediately charge Shield of Durand to taunt him and his partner, mitigating the burst while you wait for an opening.
laneImpact: Because of this mechanical standoff, the lane becomes a tense zone-control game. Maokai will try to use Sapling Toss to secure brush control and poke you down, preventing you from stepping up to use Winds of War on the wave. If you get chipped down, Maokai's Sap Magic sustain lets him win war-of-attrition trades. Neither side can easily force a tower dive without risking a massive counter-engage via Hero's Entrance or Nature's Grasp.
why: This skill matchup revolves around the clash of engages. When Maokai attempts to lock down your marksman with the untargetable root of Twisted Advance, he telegraphs his exact landing spot. By buffering Justice Punch directly into his destination, you can immediately interrupt his follow-up Bramble Smash. This neutralizes his engage check, turning his aggressive dive into a vulnerable position where your Colossal Smash can retaliate.

summary: Lissandra can interrupt Corki's Valkyrie mid-flight using Ring of Frost or lock him down instantly with Frozen Tomb.
howToPlay: Never cast Valkyrie aggressively unless Lissandra has just wasted both Ring of Frost and Glacial Path. When farming, stand offset from your own minions to prevent her from poking you with the splitting cone of Ice Shard. If she teleports toward you with her claw, walk backward immediately rather than panic-dashing; only use your flight once she has committed her root, or when you are completely out of her Frozen Tomb range.
laneImpact: Because of her lethal lockdown, you cannot safely step past the midpoint of the lane. Lissandra will constantly clear waves with Ice Shard to force you under turret or set up devastating ganks. If you get caught too far forward, her Glacial Path allows her to close the gap instantly, forcing you to choose between taking heavy damage or risking an interrupted Valkyrie that leads directly to your death.
why: Your safety in this matchup is entirely compromised by Lissandra's instant crowd control. The moment you attempt to escape or reposition with Valkyrie, she can interrupt your flight mid-air using Ring of Frost. Once she unlocks Frozen Tomb, she gains an unmissable point-and-click stun that locks you in place, preventing any defensive spellcasting and leaving you completely vulnerable to her follow-up.

summary: Galio can use Justice Punch (E) to dodge Brand's Pillar of Flame (W) and immediately close the gap to lock him down before he can trigger Blaze (P).
howToPlay: Position yourself slightly to the side of your minion wave to force Brand to choose between harassing you or pushing. Keep your finger ready on Justice Punch; the moment you see the ground glow for Pillar of Flame, dash forward. If you get caught or miss, immediately hold Shield of Durand to absorb the incoming Sear stun and mitigate the Blaze explosion damage, then back off until your mobility cooldowns recover.
laneImpact: Brand's constant urge to push with Pillar of Flame creates constant threat. Every time he misses this key ability, he is left completely vulnerable to your all-in. Because you easily shrug off his minor poke with Shield of Durand's passive magic shield, you can dictate trade health-bars. This pressure forces him to play defensively, preventing him from roaming with his high damage or safely clearing waves under his own turret.
why: Galio dominates this matchup because Brand relies heavily on landing his delayed Pillar of Flame to set up his explosive combos. By reacting quickly, you can use the backward dash of Justice Punch to slide out of the targeted circle while simultaneously surging forward to close the gap. This swift engage locks Brand down before he can chain Sear or Conflagration to trigger his explosive Blaze passive.

summary: Vladimir can use Sanguine Pool to dodge the burst from your Moonfall, leaving you vulnerable without cooldowns.
howToPlay: Never waste Sanguine Pool to dodge her basic Crescent Strike poke; save it strictly for the moment she dashes in with Lunar Rush and initiates Moonfall. If she successfully baits your pool, retreat immediately to the safety of your turret. Once you successfully dodge her ultimate burst, immediately drop Hemoplague on her and follow up with a empowered Transfusion and Tides of Blood to punish her empty cooldown bar.
laneImpact: Early on, Diana holds wave priority because her Pale Cascade and Moonsilver Blade clear faster than your weak early Tides of Blood. She will attempt to poke you down to force early recalls. Once you both unlock your ultimates, the lane becomes a psychological standoff. Diana cannot safely commit to an all-in because missing Moonfall leaves her completely vulnerable to your sustained Transfusion counter-attacks.
why: This mid lane matchup is defined by how Diana uses her aggressive diving tools against your defensive scaling. Diana wants to land Crescent Strike to reset Lunar Rush and pull you in with Moonfall. However, your Sanguine Pool is the ultimate counter-measure. By pooling her ultimate's impact, you deny her primary burst window, leaving her completely exposed in melee range without her major cooldowns.

summary: Jax's Counter Strike blocks all three hits of Xin Zhao's Three Talon Strike, preventing the knockup and winning the duel.
howToPlay: To execute this flawlessly, never initiate with Counter Strike. Instead, walk up or use Leap Strike to close the distance, then hit him with Empower. Wait for Xin Zhao to commit his Three Talon Strike before spinning your lantern. If he tries to disengage using Crescent Guard, use your Leap Strike to jump back onto him instantly. Keep your Relentless Assault stacks high on jungle monsters before starting the fight to maximize your damage output.
laneImpact: This interaction dictates the tempo of the early game, allowing you to invade his camps and contest Scuttle Crabs with absolute confidence. Because Xin Zhao relies on early skirmishes to snowball, your ability to deny his main crowd control and damage completely halts his momentum. He cannot safely contest objectives like the Rift Herald or Dragons if you are nearby, forcing him to play passively or risk dying in his own jungle.
why: Jax completely dominates the 1v1 skirmishes in the jungle due to how his defensive kit directly neutralizes Xin Zhao's main offensive tool. When Xin Zhao engages with Audacious Charge and activates Three Talon Strike, Jax can immediately activate Counter Strike. This entirely blocks all three empowered auto-attacks, negating his healing from Determination and preventing the crucial third-hit knockup, leaving Xin Zhao completely defenseless and unable to win the duel.

summary: Darius's heavy slow from Crippling Strike severely reduces Hecarim's damage output from his passive Warpath.
howToPlay: To survive these skirmishes, prioritize using Onslaught of Shadows or Devastating Charge to bypass Darius entirely during team fights, targeting his backline instead. Never initiate a direct charge directly into him. If he attempts to pull you with Apprehend, bait the pull first, then immediately use the knockback from Devastating Charge to push him away before he can apply Crippling Strike. Keep your distance and only use Rampage from the outer edge of his Decimate circle.
laneImpact: You cannot contest Darius in direct 1v1 river skirmishes or isolated jungle duels. If he catches you with Apprehend, he will force a deadly close-quarters clash. Since your Spirit of Dread healing cannot out-sustain his fully stacked Noxian Guillotine, losing a jungle duel gives him total map pressure, allowing him to easily shut down your ganking lanes and steal your camps.
why: Hecarim relies on high movement speed to convert into raw physical power via Warpath. Darius completely shuts down this offensive scaling the moment he lands Crippling Strike. This massive slow immediately tanks your attack damage mid-fight, leaving you with weakened Rampage sweeps. Additionally, trying to run away or reposition with Devastating Charge becomes impossible once slowed, allowing Darius to easily stack Hemorrhage.

summary: Placing Flame Chompers directly underneath yourself or your support when Samira uses Wild Rush can interrupt her combo and prevent her from stacking Daredevil Impulse.
howToPlay: To survive, never throw Flame Chompers! aggressively. Instead, hold them until Samira commits with Wild Rush, throwing them directly at your feet or your support's feet to snare her mid-dash and disrupt her Daredevil Impulse stacks. Only fire Zap! or Super Mega Death Rocket! after she wastes Blade Whirl. If she initiates with her ultimate, immediately run outside its radius while retaliating with Switcheroo! minigun attacks.
laneImpact: You are forced into a defensive posture, farming from afar using Switcheroo! in rocket form to avoid entering her dash range. If you step too far forward, a quick Wild Rush engage will force your Summoner Spells or send you back to base. This constant pressure limits your gold income, delays your scaling, and allows her to command the lane pace.
why: Samira dominates this matchup by capitalizing on your lack of mobility to stack Daredevil Impulse rapidly. Her Wild Rush lets her close the distance instantly, while Blade Whirl effortlessly deletes your Zap! projectile. Once she neutralizes your ranged poke, she can easily trigger Inferno Trigger, leaving your low-mobility kit completely overwhelmed by her explosive, close-range area-of-effect physical damage.

summary: Ambessa must use Drakehound's Step to dash inside Darius's Decimate ring to avoid the heal and outer-edge damage.
howToPlay: Never initiate with your dash. Instead, start skirmishes with Lacerate to slow him, forcing him to wind up Decimate. The moment his axe circles, trigger Drakehound's Step to dash close to his model. Use Repudiation to absorb the damage from Crippling Strike or block the displacement of Apprehend. If he successfully reaches five stacks, disengage immediately using Public Execution defensively if necessary to escape over a wall.
laneImpact: In the jungle, this power dynamic makes early scuttle contests and invades highly risky for you. If Darius catches you with Apprehend, he can easily stack Hemorrhage and force your flash. A failed trade means giving up objective priority or being forced into an early recall, which slows down your clear and leaves your laners vulnerable to his high-damage ganks.
why: Darius naturally dominates this jungle matchup because his Hemorrhage stacks punish extended duels, while Decimate provides massive sustain. Because Ambessa lacks innate healing, she cannot win a war of attrition. The duel hinges entirely on your reaction time: you must use Drakehound's Step to dash directly into his inner ring when he swings, denying him both the heal and his maximum damage threshold.

summary: Fiora can react to Camille's Hookshot with Riposte to stun her, turning Camille's primary engage tool into a liability.
howToPlay: To survive, use Tactical Sweep to safely farm and poke from a distance while keeping your distance from her Lunge range. When you do use Hookshot, cling to the wall and delay your second cast; this bait can trick Fiora into wasting Riposte prematurely. If she misses her parry, you have a brief window to trade with Precision Protocol. Finally, use the untargetability of The Hextech Ultimatum to dodge Riposte or reset vital angles from Grand Challenge.
laneImpact: You cannot use Hookshot aggressively to initiate trades, which strips away your offensive pressure and forces you into a defensive farming role. Fiora will constantly pressure you with Lunge to poke your vitals, while holding Riposte to deny your disengage. This makes wave control incredibly difficult, as jumping onto her near her tower invites a deadly counter-stun and a fatal chase down the long lane.
why: This matchup revolves entirely around the interaction between your Hookshot and Fiora's Riposte. Because your wall-dive has a highly predictable trajectory, Fiora can easily time her barrier to block the stun and turn it back on you. Failing this skill check means you get stunned, allowing her to easily strike the vitals from Duelist's Dance and win any trade instantly.

summary: Morgana can reactively cast Black Shield to block Ahri's Charm, neutralizing Ahri's pick potential in skirmishes.
howToPlay: Never cast Black Shield preemptively to absorb simple poke from Orb of Deception; keep it strictly ready for when you see the heart of Charm flying. When Ahri tries to use Spirit Rush to position aggressively, stand your ground. Reactively shield her crowd control, then immediately retaliate with Dark Binding and Soul Shackles to lock her down under your Tormented Shadow while she has no escape charges left.
laneImpact: During the laning phase, Ahri's ability to threaten solo kills is completely paralyzed. If she uses Orb of Deception to match your waveclear from Tormented Shadow, she lacks the damage to break your Black Shield. You can comfortably shove her under turret, preventing her from using Spirit Rush to roam and impact other lanes, which starves her of the gold needed to snowball.
why: This matchup swings heavily in your favor because Black Shield completely nullifies Ahri's main threat. Ahri's entire assassination sequence relies on landing Charm to guarantee the return damage of Orb of Deception. By holding your spell shield and casting it reactively, you shut down her pick potential and leave her with only raw, avoidable damage, rendering her aggressive dashes useless.

summary: Kennen can easily escape Jax's Leap Strike engage using Lightning Rush, while poking Jax down with ranged magic damage.
howToPlay: Survival requires a complete shift in your build path toward early defensive, magic-resistant options rather than rushing raw damage. Never initiate with Leap Strike; instead, walk up to farm and save it strictly to escape or to jump on him only if he wastes Lightning Rush. If he traps you under tower with Slicing Maelstrom, use Counter Strike to mitigate his basic attacks, absorb the stun, and immediately retreat to live another day.
laneImpact: You are permanently shoved under your turret, forced to bleed gold while digesting constant ranged magic damage. Because Kennen denies any form of trade, you cannot stack Relentless Assault on the wave without being heavily poked. This constant attrition forces early, unfavorable recalls, giving Kennen free reign to chip at your tower plates or rotate to help his team, while you are stuck desperately trying to catch up in farm.
why: Kennen neutralizes your main offensive tool with absolute ease. Whenever you attempt to close the distance using Leap Strike, he can instantly activate Lightning Rush to zoom away, rendering your Counter Strike useless. While you retreat with your cooldowns spent, he relentlessly punishes you from a safe distance using Thundering Shuriken and Electrical Surge, stacking Mark of the Storm to stun you before you can even touch him.

summary: Samira can use Blade Whirl to completely destroy Miss Fortune's Bullet Time ultimate channel.
howToPlay: To survive and win, you must bait out Blade Whirl before committing to any major fight. Force her to waste it by casting Make It Rain to slow her down, or rely on your support to trigger her defensive spin. Once her barrier is on cooldown, you have a brief window to safely channel Bullet Time. If she initiates with Wild Rush while her block is up, activate Strut to reposition immediately.
laneImpact: During the laning phase, this interaction strips away your zoning power. You cannot safely lock Samira under her tower with Make It Rain and Bullet Time because she will simply block the ultimate and engage with Wild Rush. Trades are highly volatile; if you try to poke with Double Up, she can react with Blade Whirl to absorb the projectile and deny Love Tap.
why: This matchup revolves entirely around the devastating interaction between your ultimate and Samira's defensive tool. While Miss Fortune relies on Bullet Time to dominate teamfights, Samira can instantly delete every single wave of your channel using her Blade Whirl. Because her projectile-blocking barrier completely nullifies your main damage source, you cannot freely press your ultimate whenever she has this ability ready.

summary: Draven's massive early damage with Spinning Axe completely shuts down Vayne's weak laning phase, preventing her from reaching her late-game power spikes.
howToPlay: Prioritize survival by letting the wave crash and farming exclusively with Tumble under tower. Watch the ground indicators for Spinning Axe; if Draven steps forward aggressively to catch one near a wall, immediately use Condemn to pin him and disengage. Never use Final Hour to initiate; keep it strictly to escape his Whirling Death or to dodge Stand Aside with the temporary invisibility. Accept losing some gold to keep your health high.
laneImpact: You will be constantly shoved under your turret as Draven uses Blood Rush to threaten you whenever you step up. If you try to contest the wave, he will chunk your health bar, forcing early recalls that bleed gold and experience. This permanent pressure allows him to stack League of Draven safely, while your inability to secure priority leaves your jungler without any bot-side support.
why: Draven's early-game dominance hinges entirely on Spinning Axe, which inflicts massive physical damage that dwarfs your basic attacks. Because your own Silver Bolts requires three consecutive hits to trigger and Tumble offers only a minor initial damage boost, you cannot win short trades. This damage disparity prevents you from safely farming, stalling your transition into the late-game hyper-carry enabled by Final Hour.

summary: Kai'Sa can use Killer Instinct to instantly close the gap and bypass Corki's long-range Missile Barrage poke for an isolated duel.
howToPlay: Always position yourself directly inside your minion wave to dilute the damage of her Icathian Rain. Never use Valkyrie offensively; you must hold it exclusively to escape after she commits with Killer Instinct. If she marks you with Void Seeker, immediately retreat behind your wave and activate Gatling Gun to shred her armor and magic resistance the moment she attempts to dash onto you.
laneImpact: You cannot afford to throw Phosphorus Bomb blindly, as missing it grants her a window to activate Supercharge and hunt you down. The lane dynamic shifts dramatically around wave states; staying near your minions prevents her Icathian Rain from isolating you. If you get chunked early, your ability to roam with Special Delivery is entirely neutralized, forcing you to play defensively under tower.
why: This lane is defined by the tension between your long-range poke and her sudden gap-close. While you attempt to whittle her down safely using Missile Barrage, Kai'Sa can completely bypass this distance. By landing Void Seeker to mark you with Second Skin, she can instantly trigger Killer Instinct to force an isolated duel, turning your artillery advantage into a deadly close-quarters burst trade.

summary: Hecarim can use the massive movement speed from Devastating Charge to chase down Talon even after he escapes over walls with Assassin's Path.
howToPlay: When patrolling, hold Devastating Charge until Talon commits his Assassin's Path over a wall. Once he vaults, trigger your speed boost to loop around the obstacle and collide with him, or use Onslaught of Shadows to fear him mid-jump. If he pops Shadow Assault to turn invisible, immediately activate Spirit of Dread to sustain through his initial burst while keeping him in range. If you lose track of him, immediately shadow your most vulnerable sidelane instead of blindly farming.
laneImpact: The early game turns into a relentless game of cat-and-mouse across the river. Talon will try to secure quick kills with Noxian Diplomacy and Rake on vulnerable lanes. Because you cannot easily block his wall jumps, you must focus on counter-ganking. Arriving slightly late but with maximum momentum allows you to turn his assassination attempts into extended brawls where your Rampage and Spirit of Dread easily out-DPS his long cooldowns.
why: This jungle duel revolves entirely around high-speed skirmishing and horizontal map movement. Talon relies heavily on Assassin's Path to slip over terrain and bypass traditional jungle vision. However, Hecarim's Warpath converts his extreme mobility into raw power. By activating Devastating Charge, you can match Talon's wall-hopping rotations, wrapping around the terrain to run him down or intercept his escape before his Blade's End passive can threaten your laners.

summary: Yunara can use Kanmei's Steps / Untouchable Shadow to quickly reposition out of Make It Rain and avoid Miss Fortune's follow-up poke.
howToPlay: To survive this lane, conserve your mana and stop fishing with Make It Rain. Instead, leverage the passive speed of Strut to bait her Arc of Judgment / Arc of Ruin and farm safely using Love Tap resets. Only unleash Make It Rain after she commits Kanmei's Steps / Untouchable Shadow to clear or trade. If she activates her ultimate, Transcend One's Self, play defensively and hold Bullet Time until her enhanced dash is fully spent.
laneImpact: Because your main zone tool is easily baited, you struggle to secure wave priority. Yunara uses Cultivation of Spirit to match your clear, while her Arc of Judgment / Arc of Ruin keeps you at a distance. Whittling down her health becomes highly inefficient. If you continuously expend mana on failed slows, she will force you under turret, compromising your recall timings and leaving you vulnerable to heavy hybrid damage.
why: This matchup is dictated by Yunara's mobility countering your zone control. Your primary trading tool, Make It Rain, is meant to trap opponents for heavy follow-up. However, Yunara easily nullifies this slow by activating Kanmei's Steps / Untouchable Shadow to surge or dash out of the rain. By escaping the zone instantly, she completely avoids your poke and prevents you from setting up clean Double Up bounces.

summary: Annie can hold her Pyromania stun to completely shut down Ahri's Spirit Rush engage, bursting her down instantly with Summon: Tibbers.
howToPlay: Keep your Pyromania counter at three or four charges constantly. If Ahri attempts to engage using Spirit Rush, do not panic-fire Disintegrate immediately, as she might dodge it. Instead, wait for her to commit her dash, then drop Summon: Tibbers directly on her head to trigger the stun, followed by Incinerate. Use Molten Shield's movement speed to sidestep her incoming Charm, ensuring she cannot return any damage before she perishes.
laneImpact: This matchup forces Ahri into a defensive posture. She must use Orb of Deception to waveclear from afar rather than poke you. Because of your zoning power, you dictate when trades happen. If she steps up to trigger Essence Theft's healing on you, you can easily shield with Molten Shield and punish her. You will comfortably secure lane priority, leaving her unable to roam.
why: Ahri relies entirely on the mobility of Spirit Rush to angle her Charm and position her Orb of Deception. However, Annie completely neutralizes this slippery playstyle. By holding a charge of Pyromania, you threaten an instant, unavoidable stun. The moment Ahri dashes forward, a quick Incinerate or Summon: Tibbers completely halts her momentum, leaving her incredibly vulnerable to an immediate, lethal burst.

howToPlay: Pathing/positioning: constantly thin the wave. The goal isn’t perma-push; it’s to remove low HP minions that grant easy resets. Keep a retreat lane toward your tower and avoid standing inside the wave when she’s ready to dash. Key timing: respect her level spikes (level 5) and especially reset windows on the wave. If the wave is perfect for her (multiple low HP minions), step back before she even moves — avoid the moment you’re forced into a panic jump. Decision-making: if you lack jungle vision or your jump is down, you don’t “test a trade.” You take the information, play controlled, and accept losing some prio. Your win condition becomes: survive, scale, and create objective value when she can’t force the duel.
laneImpact: In lane she can deny last-hit space when the wave sits mid and she has resets ready. You may feel in control because you’re autoing, but once she gets a favorable wave, the lane flips: you must back off, drop CS, and often give up prio. At level 5 and first items, she becomes even more oppressive: if she lands her setup, she forces an all-in where your kit has no time to breathe. Getting a counter-kill is great, but most of the time she dictates when fights start. Midgame, she also punishes you hard in side lane lanes without vision. Tristana top often wants to split; Irelia loves explosive side duels and long chase angles.
why: Irelia is hard because she doesn’t respect distance: she uses the minion wave as a staircase to reach you, while Tristana top relies on distance to keep trades clean. Other bruisers must run at you; Irelia arrives already on top of you with DPS and sustain. Your jump isn’t a perfect answer: jump too early and she can follow with another dash; jump too late and you’re already inside an all-in where she sticks and forces the fight. This matchup demands strict wave control, otherwise you face her kit at maximum efficiency. The bigger the wave, the more fuel you give her — and Tristana naturally pushes and crashes waves. That default plan helps Irelia, which is why the matchup is categorized as hard.

summary: Caitlyn's superior base attack range allows her to land Headshot procs when you step up to last-hit, forcing you to rely on Volley to farm safely.
howToPlay: To survive, stand strictly behind your caster minions and only step forward when Caitlyn's Headshot passive indicator is empty. Use Volley exclusively to last-hit multiple low-health minions at once, conserving your mana. Never walk in straight lines near the tower ruins to avoid Yordle Snap Trap. Once you hit level five, look to catch her off guard with Enchanted Crystal Arrow only if she mispositions while casting Piltover Peacemaker, as its wind-up locks her in place.
laneImpact: This range deficit constantly pushes you under your own turret. Because you must use Volley to secure cs from safety, you cannot match Caitlyn's wave clearance. She will fast-push you in, then set up Yordle Snap Trap under your tower to restrict your movement. This constant chip damage slowly prepares you for an easy finish via her Ace in the Hole if you drop too low.
why: Caitlyn's superior basic attack range completely shuts down your normal farming rhythm. Every time you step up to last-hit, she can easily trigger a Headshot without drawing minion aggro. Since you cannot match her auto-attack reach, you are forced to bleed mana using Volley from afar just to secure minions, leaving you unable to consistently stack Ranger's Focus or trade back effectively.

summary: Blinking over Lux's Light Binding with Shunpo leaves her completely defenseless against your full burst.
howToPlay: Never throw Light Binding proactively while Katarina has Shunpo available. Instead, bait her aggressive dash by standing near your tower, using Prismatic Barrier to mitigate her initial Bouncing Blade poke. Only release your snare when she locks herself into her Death Lotus channel, which forces her to stand still. If you miss, immediately retreat to the safety of your turret range.
laneImpact: You cannot safely step past your caster minions once Katarina sets up a dagger with Bouncing Blade or Preparation. Missing your snare means giving up mid priority entirely, forcing you to farm from extreme range with Lucent Singularity. This concedes early roam potential to Katarina, allowing her to easily pick up kills in the side lanes if she gets a single trigger.
why: Lux depends entirely on her Light Binding to keep Katarina at bay. However, Katarina can easily react to the slow projectile speed of Light Binding by using Shunpo to blink directly onto Lux or a nearby dagger. This instant displacement completely bypasses Lux's main self-peel tool, leaving her vulnerable to Katarina's devastating Voracity resets and full Death Lotus channel.

summary: Pantheon can easily time Aegis Assault to block the delayed damage from Zed's Death Mark, rendering Zed's ultimate useless.
howToPlay: To consistently win these skirmishes, you must hold Aegis Assault specifically for his ultimate. Never waste this cooldown during initial trades. When Zed targets you with Death Mark, wait for him to reappear behind you, then direct your shield toward him to absorb his entire burst. Once his ultimate fails, lock him down with a Mortal Will empowered Shield Vault to burst him before he can escape back to his Living Shadow.
laneImpact: This defensive advantage translates into total map control. Knowing Zed cannot safely duel you after level five, you can aggressively invade his camps and force skirmishes. Zed is forced to rely on Living Shadow to escape your counter-jungle attempts, which completely drains his offensive pressure and allows you to secure neutral objectives and ganks without facing any real threat of a counter-engage.
why: This jungle matchup is highly favorable because your kit directly invalidates Zed's assassination potential. Whenever Zed commits with Death Mark, you can simply channel Aegis Assault facing him to block both his incoming Razor Shuriken and the final delayed mark explosion. By neutralizing his ultimate's damage, you strip away his primary scaling threat and turn him into an easy target for your physical burst.

summary: Master Yi's Highlander makes him immune to the slow from Infected Bonesaw, while Wuju Style's true damage shreds Mundo's health pool.
howToPlay: Avoid any 1v1 encounters after Master Yi hits level five. If he invades and triggers Highlander, do not waste your Infected Bonesaw trying to slow him; instead, use Blunt Force Trauma to quickly clear a monster to escape, or trigger Heart Zapper to store damage before popping Maximum Dosage to run away. Only engage him when his Wuju Style is on cooldown, or when he commits Alpha Strike on an ally, leaving him vulnerable to your team's hard crowd control.
laneImpact: Because you cannot duel him, Master Yi dictates the jungle tempo. You cannot contest crabs or epic monsters directly if he is nearby. An early skirmish where he gets resets via Highlander will snowball the match. You will find yourself forced to concede your jungle camps or rely on your lanes to bail you out when he invades, as you cannot peel him off with Infected Bonesaw.
why: Your main defensive tool as a jungle tank, the health-scaling regeneration of Maximum Dosage, is completely invalidated by Master Yi. When he activates Wuju Style, his true damage bypasses your massive health bar and armor. Furthermore, your primary self-peel and spacing tool, the slow from Infected Bonesaw, is completely useless once he activates Highlander, allowing him to run you down without any counterplay.

summary: Sett can interrupt Shen's global teleport, Stand United, by pulling him with Facebreaker or suppressing him with The Show Stopper.
howToPlay: Always hold either Facebreaker or The Show Stopper when Shen reaches level five and looks to teleport. When he casts Stand United, immediately use one of these crowd control abilities to cancel his channel. During standard laning, wait out the duration of Spirit's Refuge before activating Knuckle Down, and counter his Shadow Dash taunt by absorbing the incoming damage with Haymaker to retaliate with true damage once his shield expires.
laneImpact: During short trades, Shen uses Shadow Dash to engage and Spirit's Refuge to deny Sett's damage. If Sett wastes Knuckle Down into Shen's defensive zone, he loses the trade. However, if Shen tries to save an ally across the map with Stand United, Sett can punish him. Successfully interrupting the channel keeps Shen stuck in lane, allowing Sett to dominate the wave and secure heavy turret damage.
why: This matchup is an even battle of cooldown management and utility denial. Sett wants to execute his basic attack loops with Pit Grit and Knuckle Down, but Shen's Spirit's Refuge completely blocks these auto-attacks. The lane pivots entirely around how Sett responds to Shen's ultimate, Stand United. Sett has the perfect tools to cancel this global map pressure instantly using Facebreaker or The Show Stopper.

summary: Orianna can safely dismantle H-28G Evolution Turrets (Q) from a distance using Command: Attack (Q) and Command: Dissonance (W).
howToPlay: To survive, stop placing your H-28G Evolution Turret in the minion wave where her area damage can clear both simultaneously. Instead, hold them in reserve and only deploy a turret deep behind your own caster minions to secure safe retreat paths. Use Hextech Micro-Rockets to match her push from afar. If she steps up too aggressively to harass you, reserve your CH-2 Electron Storm Grenade to deter her, rather than using it to fish for stuns.
laneImpact: Without your H-28G Evolution Turret cluster to secure the wave, Orianna dictates the lane state. She will constantly push you under tower, forcing you to use Hextech Micro-Rockets just to secure last hits rather than trading. You will lose your passive movement speed from Hextech Affinity, making you an incredibly vulnerable target for her Command: Shockwave once she decides to dive or set up a gank with her jungler.
why: Orianna completely neutralizes your defensive setup because her sphere easily outranges your placements. By combining Command: Attack and Command: Dissonance, she can comfortably destroy your H-28G Evolution Turret setups from complete safety without ever entering your threat range. This leaves you without your main source of zone control, as her low-cooldown sphere repositioning makes it impossible to keep your turrets alive for more than a few seconds.

summary: Morgana's Black Shield (E) completely negates the trapping effect and slow of Between Worlds (R).
howToPlay: To survive and find openings, you must bait out Black Shield before committing your ultimate. Use the movement speed from Across the Veil to bait her Dark Binding, or jump sideways to dodge it. If she panics and shields herself, you have a fifteen-second window where Between Worlds becomes lethal. If she holds her shield, focus on using The Weirding to disengage and clear waves safely from a distance rather than forcing fights.
laneImpact: During the laning phase, Morgana will constantly push the wave with Tormented Shadow, forcing you to use Twofold Hex to match her clear rather than poke. If you get hit by Dark Binding while trying to trade, her pool deals massive damage, forcing an early recall. Because your ultimate cannot reliably lock her down, you cannot easily secure solo kills, giving her free reign to safely farm.
why: This matchup is dictated by how Morgana uses Black Shield to completely neutralize your primary threat. When you cast Between Worlds, she can simply shield herself or her target, nullifying the cage's boundary knockback and slow. Since your ultimate relies on trapping her within the arena to bounce around safely, her ability to walk right through your walls ruins your kill pressure and leaves you vulnerable.

summary: Teemo must bait out Yasuo's Wind Wall before using Blinding Dart to neutralize his Steel Tempest and basic attacks.
howToPlay: Start trades by chipping away his passive shield with Toxic Shot. Fake an aggressive approach to bait his Wind Wall, then immediately use Move Quick to retreat and wait out its duration. The moment his wall disappears, strike with Blinding Dart to shut down his Steel Tempest and auto-attacks. If he manages to land a knock-up, quickly retreat into your own minion wave to ensure his Sweeping Blade pursuit forces him into taking heavy minion aggro.
laneImpact: This dynamic forces Yasuo to play defensively, allowing you to establish early wave priority. By popping his Way of the Wanderer shield with a simple basic attack, you set up high-damage trades. When he dashes forward with Sweeping Blade, you can easily control the lane's center. Your Noxious Trap placements around the lane entryways and minion wave prevent him from executing aggressive sweeps without taking massive damage and being slowed.
why: Teemo dominates this midlane matchup because Yasuo relies entirely on basic attacks and his Steel Tempest to deal damage. While Wind Wall can block your Blinding Dart, his defensive barrier has a massive cooldown compared to your blind. Once you force him to deploy his wall defensively, he is completely vulnerable. Following up with Blinding Dart neutralizes his offensive output entirely, leaving him unable to trade back effectively.

summary: Vladimir can use Sanguine Pool to dodge the second cast of Fear Beyond Death, completely avoiding the execute.
howToPlay: Keep Sanguine Pool strictly to counter Fear Beyond Death's second cast or to escape a desperate Disdain dash. When trading, use your ranged advantage to land Transfusion when it is empowered, while baiting out his Corrosive Charge. If he misses his slow, immediately charge Tides of Blood to punish him. Never pool early during his Purge if his ultimate is still up; always hold it as your ultimate life insurance policy.
laneImpact: Urgot wants to poke with Corrosive Charge and flip you with Disdain to trigger Echoing Flames. Because you can sustain through his harass with Transfusion and safely clear with Tides of Blood, Urgot is forced into a passive lane. Once you hit your mid-game spikes, your Hemoplague teamfight presence far outvalues his single-target lock-down, turning the top lane into a free scaling zone for you.
why: Urgot relies heavily on his ultimate, Fear Beyond Death, to secure kills against targets. However, Vladimir completely neutralizes this execution threat because Sanguine Pool makes him untargetable, allowing him to dodge the second cast (the chains pulling him in) even if he is below the health threshold. This completely breaks Urgot's kill pressure while Vladimir's Crimson Pact ensures he outscales the dreadnought.

summary: Tristana can jump directly onto Jhin with Rocket Jump and burst him down with Explosive Charge before he can cycle through his Whisper shots.
howToPlay: To survive, you must maintain a strict safety buffer, staying just outside of her Rocket Jump range. Keep your distance and focus on farming with Dancing Grenade. Never waste Deadly Flourish blindly; hold this ability specifically to root Tristana mid-air if she attempts to leap forward, or to peel her off after she initiates. If she does manage to jump on you, place a Captive Audience trap directly beneath yourself to slow her down while retreating toward your turret.
laneImpact: This matchup forces Jhin onto the defensive, as standing too close to dying minions exposes him to passive splash damage from Draw a Bead. Tristana easily pushes waves using Explosive Charge on towers or front minions, threatening to dive Jhin if he is chipped down. You will constantly find yourself pinned under turret, sacrificing early priority and leaving your jungler without bot-side support during early skirmishes.
why: Tristana completely disrupts Jhin's methodical rhythm by forcing high-speed engagements. Because Jhin is locked into the fixed attack speed of Whisper, he cannot match the raw burst of Tristana's Explosive Charge combined with Rapid Fire in a direct duel. If she uses Rocket Jump to close the gap, she can fully stack her bomb and detonate it before Jhin can even chamber his fourth critical shot.

summary: Vayne's short range forces her to step up for last hits, making her highly vulnerable to Double Up bounces and Make It Rain slow zones.
howToPlay: To survive, you must maintain a diagonal line relative to your low-health minions, ensuring you are never directly behind them to deny her Double Up angles. Never use Tumble aggressively; keep this roll strictly as a reactive tool to escape the slow of Make It Rain. If she attempts to force a fight by casting Bullet Time, immediately use Condemn to push her away or disrupt her positioning if she gets too close, prioritizing survival over trading.
laneImpact: This constant threat forces you to concede wave control, leaving you pinned under your own turret while bleeding health. You cannot safely contest her push, which allows Miss Fortune to freely stack waves and set up massive tower pressure. If you drop too low trying to farm, she can easily lock you down with Make It Rain and channel a lethal Bullet Time under your structure without taking turret aggro.
why: Miss Fortune completely locks you out of your CS range by turning your own minion wave against you. Because of your short basic attack range, you must step forward to trigger Silver Bolts or last-hit. This positions you perfectly for a catastrophic Double Up bounce from dying minions, while her Make It Rain slow zone ensures you cannot easily dodge the incoming bounce or her Love Tap follow-up.

summary: Teemo's Blinding Dart does not stop the damage from Pantheon's Comet Spear or the block from Aegis Assault, allowing Pantheon to easily burst him down.
howToPlay: To execute this cleanly, prepare Mortal Will before jumping in. Initiate with Shield Vault to lock him down. If Teemo panics and uses Blinding Dart, do not waste time basic-attacking; immediately cast Comet Spear followed by Aegis Assault to absorb his retaliatory poison. Save Grand Starfall to cut him off if he attempts to escape with Move Quick, and always sweep bushes to uncover him if he tries to trigger Guerrilla Warfare.
laneImpact: This interaction completely strips Teemo of his usual ranged lane dominance. He cannot safely step up to poke you with Toxic Shot without risking a lethal trade. You easily dictate wave positioning, letting you crash waves at will or freeze them near your tower. Once you hit your level spikes, the threat of your burst forces Teemo to cower near his turret, granting you free priority to impact the map.
why: Teemo relies heavily on Blinding Dart to neutralize physical duelists, but his blind does absolutely nothing to stop the high physical damage of your Comet Spear. Furthermore, when he tries to trade back with his poison-infused basic attacks, Aegis Assault completely blocks his frontal damage. This leaves the squishy yordle completely vulnerable to your high-burst physical spells, as his primary defensive tool is rendered entirely useless against your main damaging abilities.

summary: When Leona engages with Zenith Blade, Braum can use Stand Behind Me to protect his ADC and easily trigger Concussive Blows on her.
howToPlay: To survive, stand defensively behind your minions to block Winter's Bite. Never initiate with Zenith Blade unless Braum has already wasted Stand Behind Me. Instead, play reactively; hold Shield of Daybreak to stun him if he jumps forward, and activate Eclipse to absorb the retaliatory burst. If he initiates with Glacial Fissure, focus entirely on peeling for your carry rather than attempting to dive the enemy backline.
laneImpact: This dynamic completely paralyzes your lane pressure. Because your primary engage is neutralized, you must concede wave control, allowing Braum to push you under tower. Attempting to force fights results in terrible trades; Braum uses Unbreakable to block your partner's follow-up damage while Concussive Blows leaves you stunned and vulnerable, stripping away your dragon priority.
why: Initiating with Zenith Blade is highly risky because Braum can instantly counter your dive. When you dash in, Braum uses Stand Behind Me to shield his carry, placing himself directly in your path. He then easily stacks Concussive Blows on you with Winter's Bite and basic attacks, turning your aggressive play into a stun trap where you get focused down.

summary: Ekko uses Phase Dive to blink out of your Infernal Chains zone before the pull triggers.
howToPlay: Never lead your ganks or skirmishes with Infernal Chains. Instead, initiate with the first strikes of The Darkin Blade, using Umbral Dash to adjust your sweetspots and force Ekko to panic-cast Phase Dive defensively. Once his blink is on cooldown, immediately throw Infernal Chains to lock him down. If he successfully triggers Z-Drive Resonance and runs, back off; wait for your cooldowns to cycle before re-engaging his slippery kit.
laneImpact: Because Ekko can easily escape your primary displacement, direct 1v1 duels in the river often stall out. You cannot reliably burst him before he retreats or resets with Chronobreak. This stalemate means secure priority around neutral objectives is hard to force alone, as his safety allows him to poke with Timewinder and threaten steals with Phase Dive without fearing an immediate, fatal lockdown from your combo.
why: This jungle duel hinges entirely on how you sequence your crowd control against his high mobility. While your Infernal Chains should theoretically set up devastating sweetspots for The Darkin Blade, Ekko can consistently negate this by using Phase Dive to blink out of the impact zone before the pull triggers. This interaction forces a constant dance around his dash cooldown, turning every skirmish into a test of timing.

summary: Caitlyn can punish Ezreal with Headshot autos when he steps up to farm, but she must place Yordle Snap Trap behind him to catch his Arcane Shift trajectory.
howToPlay: Never use Arcane Shift offensively if Caitlyn has her Yordle Snap Trap ready, as she will try to predict your landing spot by placing a trap behind you. Instead, bait out her Piltover Peacemaker first, then use Essence Flux followed by Mystic Shot to chunk her health. If she manages to hit you with 90 Caliber Net, immediately disengage with your blink to avoid the guaranteed follow-up Headshot, resetting your position to poke from maximum range.
laneImpact: The lane revolves around a constant trading of range. Caitlyn will try to shove the wave to setup Yordle Snap Trap under your turret, aiming to restrict your movement. However, because you can safely thin the wave with Mystic Shot and Trueshot Barrage, her tower pressure is heavily neutralized. Once you poke her down during her long ability downtime, you easily secure priority, forcing her to play defensively and delaying her scaling.
why: While Caitlyn boasts superior base range to clip you with Headshot when you step up to farm, this matchup leans in your favor because of your superior low-cooldown poke. Mystic Shot allows you to farm safely from a distance or retaliate instantly. Her Piltover Peacemaker and 90 Caliber Net have long, punishing cooldowns. If she misses her skillshots, you can aggressively blink forward with Arcane Shift to force a trade she cannot win.

summary: Shyvana lacks any basic ability CC to interrupt Bountiful Harvest, allowing Fiddlesticks to out-sustain her in direct duels.
howToPlay: Prioritize a strict farming route to build up your Fury of the Dragonborn stacks away from his position. If you cross paths, do not initiate with Dragon's Descent unless his Bountiful Harvest is already on cooldown. Instead, use the movement speed from Burnout to disengage immediately. Only commit to fights when your teammates can provide the hard crowd control needed to interrupt his drain, allowing you to safely burst him down.
laneImpact: Because you cannot fight Fiddlesticks directly, you lose the ability to contest him at camps or scuttle crabs early. He can clear his jungle with immense sustain while you must focus on optimizing your own clear speed using Burnout and Flame Breath. If you fall behind in clearing speed, he will secure map priority and use Crowstorm to execute devastating ganks before you can stack your Fury of the Dragonborn.
why: In direct skirmishes, you cannot cancel Fiddlesticks' Bountiful Harvest because none of your basic abilities, including Twin Bite, Burnout, or Flame Breath, possess any form of crowd control. Since he can channel his entire drain uninterrupted, his health pool constantly recovers while yours depletes. He easily out-sustains your melee damage, making early duels in the river highly unfavorable unless he is already extremely low.

summary: Vladimir can use Sanguine Pool to dodge Aatrox's Infernal Chains pull, but its extremely long cooldown leaves him vulnerable to subsequent Q rotations.
howToPlay: Prioritize walking perpendicular to dodge Infernal Chains instead of reflexively pressing Sanguine Pool. Only pool if you are guaranteed to get pulled into a sweetspot of The Darkin Blade. When his abilities are on cooldown, aggressively step forward to land your empowered Transfusion to match his passive healing. If he activates World Ender, immediately disengage instead of fighting through his ultimate's increased healing.
laneImpact: Once Sanguine Pool is spent, you must concede the minion wave and retreat toward your turret. Aatrox will exploit this twenty-second vulnerability window to freeze the wave or crash a massive wave to setup a dive using World Ender. If you get dragged by Infernal Chains without your pool, the knockups from The Darkin Blade will chunk your health bar, forcing an early recall.
why: This matchup is a battle of attrition where cooldown mismatches override pure sustain. While Sanguine Pool perfectly counters the pull of Infernal Chains, its massive cooldown is your undoing. Aatrox can cycle through multiple rotations of The Darkin Blade and reposition with Umbral Dash long before you recover your safety net, allowing him to force deadly trades while healing back your poke with Deathbringer Stance.

summary: Cho'Gath's Festin deals true damage, completely bypassing the magic damage shield from Galio's Shield of Durand.
howToPlay: Walk forward aggressively when Galio misses his Justice Punch, as he loses his only escape. Silence him with Feral Scream to prevent him from channeling Shield of Durand, then chain it into Rupture for a guaranteed knock-up. Always hold Feast until his health bar falls below the threshold, ignoring his defensive stance. If he attempts to channel Hero's Entrance to save a teammate, immediately disrupt him with either Rupture or Feral Scream to cancel his flight.
laneImpact: Because Galio cannot shield your true damage, he is forced into defensive wave clear. When he uses Winds of War to push, he creates massive cooldown windows where you can force trades. You can easily out-sustain him, trapping him in lane with low health. This prevents him from using Hero's Entrance to impact other lanes, stripping away his primary map-wide utility while you stack Feast on minions under his tower.
why: You completely shut down Galio because your ultimate, Feast, deals raw true damage that ignores the magic shield from his Shield of Durand. While Galio wants to absorb magic poke and retaliate, his defensive tool is useless against your execution. Furthermore, your Carnivore passive constantly heals back any chip damage he inflicts with Winds of War, rendering his mana-heavy poke entirely obsolete over long trades.

summary: Lucian can easily dodge Deadly Flourish with Relentless Pursuit and punish Jhin during his Whisper reload animation.
howToPlay: Never cast Deadly Flourish unless Lucian has already wasted Relentless Pursuit to clear minions or trade. Keep your distance and focus on bouncing Dancing Grenade through low-health minions to poke him from safety. If he dashes forward aggressively to start a fight, immediately drop a Captive Audience behind you and retreat toward your tower. Save Curtain Call strictly for securing long-range kills after your support lands hard crowd control first.
laneImpact: This creates constant pressure where Lucian can step past your minions to force short, explosive trades. If you misposition, his Piercing Light will poke you through the wave, forcing you to farm passively under tower. You lose control over the minion wave's state, preventing you from setting up Captive Audience traps safely. This loss of priority forces your jungler to play around the opposite side of the map.
why: Lucian dominates this matchup by capitalizing on Jhin's fixed attack cadence. Whenever you try to lock him down with Deadly Flourish, he can instantly react and slide away using Relentless Pursuit. This defensive dash immediately positions him to retaliate with Lightslinger double shots, catching you completely defenseless while Whisper is forced into its slow four-second reload animation.

summary: Leona can interrupt Rell's jump engage by timing Shield of Daybreak to stun her mid-air.
howToPlay: To win this skill matchup, never initiate with Ferromancy: Crashdown if Leona has Shield of Daybreak ready. Instead, use Full Tilt to bait her Zenith Blade, then activate Shattering Strike to break her Eclipse shield when she commits. If you get caught out, immediately cast Magnet Storm to drag her away from your carry, preventing her from follow-up casting Solar Flare on your squishy target while you are immobilized.
laneImpact: Because of this mid-air denial, neither support can safely force a hard engage while the other's crowd control is available. If Leona misses Zenith Blade, you gain a massive window to punish her. However, if she interrupts your jump, your ADC will be left without peel against her Sunlight procs. This creates a highly defensive lane where wave control is dictated entirely by who holds their primary initiation.
why: This matchup is a tense standoff decided by the timing of your Ferromancy: Crashdown. While Rell wants to initiate, Leona can completely shut down your engage by casting Shield of Daybreak to stun you mid-flight, leaving you stranded in your slow dismounted form. If she wastes this stun, your Break the Mold will steal her Eclipse resistances, turning her own defensive steroid against her.

summary: Corki can easily escape the area of Miss Fortune's Bullet Time using Valkyrie while immediately retaliating with his own Missile Barrage.
howToPlay: Always stay diagonal to your low-health minions to deny her clean angles for Double Up. Crucially, never use Valkyrie offensively when she has her ultimate ready. Hold it specifically as your escape button. The moment she channels Bullet Time, cast Valkyrie sideways to clear the zone, then immediately unload Missile Barrage rockets at her static body. If you accidentally waste your dash early, retreat immediately behind terrain to break her line of sight.
laneImpact: Both of you can clear waves quickly, creating a constant tug-of-war. If you stand directly behind low-health minions, you will take massive damage from her Double Up bounces. Miss Fortune relies on Strut to dodge your skillshots, but landing a single Phosphorus Bomb or Missile Barrage halts her movement speed, allowing you to force even trades and prevent her from securing easy lane priority.
why: This lane is a pure skill matchup defined by long-range trades. Miss Fortune uses Make It Rain and Double Up to poke from behind minions, while you match her with Phosphorus Bomb and Gatling Gun. The ultimate showdown hinges on her channel: when she casts Bullet Time, you can immediately slide out of the cone with Valkyrie and fire back with Missile Barrage, turning her stationary state into an easy target.

summary: Diana must dive into melee range with Lunar Rush, putting her in perfect range for Cho'Gath's Cri primal and high-damage Épines vorpales.
howToPlay: Never waste Feral Scream to poke; keep it ready as your primary defensive tool. When Diana hits you with Crescent Strike, expect the incoming Lunar Rush. Stand your ground, silence her immediately upon her arrival, and activate Vorpal Spikes to win the physical brawl. If she manages to bait your silence without committing, retreat toward your tower and use Carnivore to recover your health before contesting the next wave.
laneImpact: This matchup dynamic completely neutralizes Diana's lane pressure, forcing her to play defensively. Because she risks a devastating counter-engage every time she dashes, she must rely solely on Crescent Strike to farm from afar. This allows you to comfortably control the minion waves, sustain endlessly with Carnivore, and keep her pinned under her turret, bleeding gold while you scale your maximum health safely.
why: Diana's entire game plan revolves around hitting Crescent Strike to dive you with Lunar Rush. By jumping directly into melee range, she plays right into your strengths. She cannot dodge Feral Scream once she has committed to her dash, which silences her and prevents her from activating Pale Cascade or Moonfall. This leaves her completely exposed to your heavy Vorpal Spikes trade.

summary: Mordekaiser can target Viego with Realm of Death to deny him from possessing fallen allies via Sovereign's Domination during teamfights.
howToPlay: Position yourself directly between Viego and your low-health allies during mid-game skirmishes. Do not waste Realm of Death early in the fight; hold it specifically for the moment Viego tries to channel Sovereign's Domination or dives with Heartbreaker. If he uses Spectral Maw to gap-close, pull him back with Death's Grasp, activate Darkness Rise, and drag him into your duel before he can touch a single soul on the ground.
laneImpact: In the jungle, this interaction shifts the power balance of skirmishes around objectives. Viego cannot freely skirmish or secure early kills because any death on Mordekaiser's team becomes a trap rather than a reset source. Viego is forced to play passively near walls with Harrowed Path, unable to aggressively dive Mordekaiser's backline with Heartbreaker, knowing he will be locked in a 1v1 he cannot win.
why: Mordekaiser dominates this matchup because he can completely shut down Viego's teamfight reset potential. When Viego attempts to trigger Sovereign's Domination on a fallen teammate's soul, Mordekaiser can cast Realm of Death to banish him to the Death Realm. This isolates Viego, cutting him off from the battlefield souls, negating his passive healing, and stripping away his offensive momentum.

summary: Corki can bully Katarina early with Gatling Gun and match her map-wide roams using the high mobility of Special Delivery.
howToPlay: Position yourself laterally away from the daggers dropped by Bouncing Blade to completely neutralise her Shunpo engage angles. Always hold Valkyrie to escape her Death Lotus radius if she attempts an all-in. When Hextech Munitions grants you the package, immediately look at the side lanes; timing your base recalls to pick up Special Delivery right as she attempts a desperate roam allows you to crash onto her skirmish and turn the fight.
laneImpact: You easily dictate the minion wave's position from level one. By keeping Katarina shoved under her turret with Phosphorus Bomb, you force her to choose between losing gold or taking poke. Since she cannot safely trade without exposing herself to Gatling Gun, she is pressured into desperate roams. However, her absence allows you to rapidly demolish her tower, while your Special Delivery package threatens to counter-gank her target.
why: As a ranged marksman, Corki naturally oppresses the melee Katarina. Whenever she steps up to fetch a dagger from Bouncing Blade, you can shred her resistances using Gatling Gun. Even if she tries to escape the trade with Shunpo, your continuous damage output wins. Later, when she seeks to roam to get Voracity resets, the extreme map-wide dash of Special Delivery ensures you arrive at side-lane skirmishes simultaneously to shut her down.

summary: Fiora can easily react to the highly telegraphed Rupture animation with Riposte to stun Cho'Gath and initiate a lethal trade.
howToPlay: You must play a mind game with your spell casting. Never lead with Rupture. Instead, walk up and use Feral Scream to silence her first, preventing her from using Riposte reactively. Alternatively, bait her Riposte by walking forward as if to cast, then immediately side-step. Once Riposte is on its long cooldown, you have a brief window to use Rupture safely, farm with Vorpal Spikes, or secure a minion with Feast to heal up via Carnivore.
laneImpact: Because casting your primary crowd control is a death sentence, you lose all initiative. Fiora can stand in front of your minions, using Lunge to poke your vitals from Duelist's Dance. If you try to fight back with Vorpal Spikes, she simply activates Bladework to out-trade you. You will be forced under your turret, struggling to secure Feast stacks and relying entirely on Carnivore to survive her constant poke.
why: Your laning phase is dictated by a massive mechanical disadvantage. The startup delay on Rupture is a massive tell for Fiora, allowing her to easily react with Riposte. By parrying your knock-up, she doesn't just negate your crowd control; she stuns you instead, putting you at the mercy of her Lunge and Duelist's Dance true damage without any escape tool.

summary: Poppy's Steadfast Presence blocks both Talon's Noxian Diplomacy dash and his Assassin's Path wall-hops, grounding and stunning him.
howToPlay: When skirmishing near jungle walls, never lead with Steadfast Presence. Keep this defensive aura ready and position yourself between Talon and the nearest wall. Wait for him to initiate Noxian Diplomacy or target a wall with Assassin's Path, then activate your barrier to ground him. Once he is stuck, use Heroic Charge to slam him into the very wall he tried to jump, and finish him off with Hammer Shock.
laneImpact: In the jungle, this interaction ruins Talon's pathing and flank attempts. He cannot safely contest scuttle crabs or invade your camps because you can easily trap him against the tight jungle corridors. If he tries to escape over a wall, you shut him down instantly, leaving him vulnerable to a follow-up Heroic Charge into the terrain. This completely halts his snowball potential and starves his lanes of gank pressure.
why: Poppy completely neutralizes Talon's identity as a highly mobile jungle assassin. His entire kit relies on jumping over walls with Assassin's Path or closing the gap using Noxian Diplomacy. Because your Steadfast Presence actively blocks both of these moves, grounding and stunning him instead of letting him escape or engage, Talon becomes an easy target whenever he tries to move.

summary: Malphite's Ground Slam completely shuts down Tryndamere's auto-attack DPS, and Seismic Shard allows Malphite to easily kite out Undying Rage.
howToPlay: Never engage with Spinning Slash while Ground Slam is available. Instead, bait this slam by walking up, then immediately spin backward. If he wastes Seismic Shard to poke you, that is your only cue to trade. If you get caught low and must use Undying Rage, immediately use Mocking Shout to slow his retreat, but only after he has already cast his shard, otherwise his stolen speed will still outpace your dash.
laneImpact: You cannot contest waves early when Malphite's Granite Shield is up. Every short trade you attempt will be met with Ground Slam, leaving you unable to retaliate while he chips away at your health. Under tower, he can poke you with Seismic Shard with impunity, forcing you to constantly consume your Battle Fury with Bloodlust just to stay alive, destroying any chance of establishing split-push pressure.
why: Malphite is your ultimate mechanical wall. His Ground Slam cripples your attack speed, completely neutralizing the critical strike threat from Battle Fury. Even if you manage to force an all-in, his Seismic Shard steals your movement speed, allowing him to simply walk away and comfortably waste the entire duration of your Undying Rage. You cannot bypass this dual defensive layer in a straight duel.

summary: Taliyah's Défilage tellurique (E) stuns Galio if he tries to dash with Justice Punch (E), making it difficult for him to engage directly.
howToPlay: To survive this lane, you must adopt a passive positioning strategy. Never lead with Justice Punch while her Défilage tellurique is off cooldown. Instead, focus on farming from a safe distance using Winds of War. If she wastes her stone field, you have a brief window to move forward. Otherwise, hold Shield of Durand to absorb her poke, and look to match her roams using Hero's Entrance once she activates Mur de la tisseuse.
laneImpact: During the laning phase, this interaction forces you into a defensive posture. Taliyah will comfortably clear waves with Rafale filée and zone you from CS. If you try to step up to use Colossal Smash on the minions, she can threaten a Poussée sismique to fling you back. You will find yourself pushed under turret, losing priority and arriving late to help your jungler.
why: The matchup is heavily dictated by how Taliyah's ground control shuts down your mobility. Whenever you attempt to engage or escape using Justice Punch, Taliyah can instantly react with Défilage tellurique. This field triggers a painful stun on your dash, completely halting your forward momentum and leaving you exposed. Because your primary engage tool is neutralized, you cannot easily force trades against her.

summary: Sett must run directly at you with Knuckle Down, making him an easy target for your CH-2 Electron Storm Grenade stun.
howToPlay: To survive, you must abandon standard aggressive trades and focus on defense. Never use Knuckle Down directly towards Heimerdinger unless his CH-2 Electron Storm Grenade has already been wasted. Instead, use the movement speed to dodge laterally. Let the wave crash, and use Haymaker solely to absorb the burst from UPGRADE!!! empowered rockets. Keep your health high enough to set up a gank with The Show Stopper.
laneImpact: You will find yourself permanently shoved under your turret as H-28G Evolution Turret continuously pushes the minion wave. Attempting to clear them exposes you to heavy poke from Hextech Micro-Rockets. Because you cannot trade back without being stunned, your health pool will constantly dwindle, forcing early recalls that cost crucial gold and experience while granting Heimerdinger complete lane control.
why: Sett relies on closing the gap, but Heimerdinger's setup completely shuts this down. When you activate Knuckle Down to rush him, your linear movement path becomes entirely predictable. This makes you a trivial target for his CH-2 Electron Storm Grenade, which stuns you mid-charge. Combined with his H-28G Evolution Turret nest, any attempt to engage results in taking massive automated damage while you are immobilized.

summary: Rammus's Defensive Ball Curl reflects Master Yi's rapid basic attacks back at him, while Frenzying Taunt forces Yi to kill himself on the armor.
howToPlay: Do not initiate with Frenzying Taunt immediately. Instead, roll in with Powerball and wait for him to panic-cast Alpha Strike to dodge. The moment he reappears, activate Defensive Ball Curl and immediately lock him down with Frenzying Taunt. If he attempts to channel Meditate to survive your reflection damage, interrupt him instantly with Soaring Slam. Prioritize heavy armor stacking over utility to maximize your passive damage.
laneImpact: This matchup completely shuts down Master Yi's ability to contest the jungle or secure objectives early. Whenever he attempts to contest scuttle crabs or secure neutral monsters, your presence alone forces him to retreat. He cannot duel you at any point; if he tries to engage with Alpha Strike, he places himself in immediate danger of a lethal counter-engage, crippling his gold generation and robbing his lanes of any jungle pressure.
why: Master Yi relies entirely on rapid basic attacks amplified by Double Strike and Highlander to shred targets. Rammus completely neutralizes this offensive engine. By activating Defensive Ball Curl, you turn his high attack speed into a self-destructive loop. Forcing him into this state with Frenzying Taunt ensures he cannot escape or use Meditate, effectively making him tear his own health bar apart against your massive armor.

summary: Vladimir can easily dodge Poppy's engage attempts with Sanguine Pool, allowing him to safely scale into a late-game threat.
howToPlay: Keep your distance from the lane walls to prevent Poppy from finding any angle to stun you. Never use Sanguine Pool offensively; hold it strictly as your escape button for when she attempts to charge. If she wastes her gap-closer, immediately retaliate by charging Tides of Blood and unleashing Hemoplague to punish her lack of mobility, securing an easy lane victory as you outscale her.
laneImpact: Since Poppy cannot reliably lock you down, you dictate the wave's tempo. You can safely harass her with Transfusion every time she steps up to secure minions. This continuous health drain forces her into defensive recall timings, giving you complete freedom to slow-push waves or pressure her under turret with Tides of Blood without fearing any sudden jungle dives.
why: Poppy relies on hard engage to lock down her lane opponents, but your Sanguine Pool completely neutralizes her aggressive charge attempts. By turning untargetable whenever she tries to pin you, you render her primary offensive tool useless. This safe disengage ensures you easily survive her early burst, allowing Crimson Pact to passively convert your growing health pool into unstoppable late-game magic power.

summary: Using Heroic Swing to circle around Brand lets you easily dodge his linear Sear stun while delivering high physical burst.
howToPlay: To survive, never cast Sear preemptively. You must hold this ability until Akshan actually commits to his Heroic Swing. Aim your stun directly at his anchor point or wait until he collides with you or a minion to guarantee the hit. Position yourself strictly behind your minion wave or near terrain corners to block his swing path. If he catches you in the open, immediately drop Conflagration and Pillar of Flame at your own feet to force a trade via Blaze as he closes the distance.
laneImpact: Akshan's constant threat of a physical burst trade forces you to play defensively under or near your turret. You cannot easily contest his push, as using Pillar of Flame on the minion wave leaves you completely vulnerable. He will easily clear waves with Avengerang, gain lane priority, and use Going Rogue to roam toward side lanes undetected, putting immense pressure on your entire map while you are stuck clearing.
why: This matchup is highly unfavorable for Brand because of how Akshan's mobility counters your self-defense. When you attempt to defend yourself, Akshan uses Heroic Swing to orbit around you. This rapid circular movement makes it incredibly easy for him to dodge your linear Sear skillshot, preventing you from triggering your stun, while his physical damage rapidly shreds your squishy health bar.

summary: Kalista's constant hops from Martial Poise make it incredibly difficult for Jhin to land Deadly Flourish or any Curtain Call shots.
howToPlay: To survive, you must hold Deadly Flourish strictly for when Kalista is locked in her Pierce animation or immediately after she has committed Rend, limiting her dodge potential. Position yourself deep behind your caster minions, relying on Dancing Grenade bounces to farm safely from a distance. If you must use Curtain Call, fire only from deep fog of war where she cannot visually predict the trajectory of your shots before they launch.
laneImpact: Because you cannot reliably root her, Kalista dominates short trades. She can aggressively stack spears with Pierce and rip them out with Rend before you can retaliate with Whisper's fourth shot. This mobility deficit forces you to play defensively under tower, ceding control of the minion waves. If her support uses Fate's Call to knock you up, you lack the direct escape tools to survive her rapid execution.
why: Kalista's constant hops from Martial Poise completely neutralize your telegraphed skillshots. Every auto-attack allows her to reposition effortlessly, making it nearly impossible to lock her down with Deadly Flourish even if she triggers Captive Audience. When you open Curtain Call, her high-frequency jumps allow her to easily dodge your critical final bullets, turning your ultimate into a stationary trap while she closes the distance.

summary: Rammus's Defensive Ball Curl heavily punishes Lee Sin's Flurry attack speed buff by reflecting massive magic damage.
howToPlay: When skirmishing, do not waste Frenzying Taunt immediately when Lee Sin lands Sonic Wave. Instead, wait for him to commit to the second activation of Sonic Wave to dash onto you. The moment he connects, activate Defensive Ball Curl to absorb the impact, and immediately follow up with Frenzying Taunt to lock him into attacking you while his Flurry is active. If he tries to kick you away with Dragon's Rage, use Soaring Slam to leap back into the fray or escape over walls if the fight turns.
laneImpact: In the jungle, this matchup shifts map pressure entirely in your favor. Lee Sin cannot comfortably contest neutral camps or invade you, knowing that a counter-engage will force him to take massive self-inflicted damage. While he tries to use Safeguard to escape or shield himself, your ability to quickly cross the river with Powerball allows you to match his ganks and counter-gank effectively, neutralizing his early-game snowball potential.
why: Lee Sin relies heavily on his passive Flurry to weave rapid basic attacks between his spell casts for jungle clearing and skirmishing. However, activating Defensive Ball Curl turns this attack speed buff against him. Because Rolling Armordillo converts your armor into bonus damage, the reflected magic damage from Defensive Ball Curl melts Lee Sin's health bar the faster he attempts to strike you during his passive window.

summary: Walk out of Shen's Spirit's Refuge zone to land your basic attacks and stack Hemorrhage elsewhere.
howToPlay: To secure your advantage, never waste your attacks when Shen deploys his protective zone. The moment he activates Spirit's Refuge, immediately walk out of the zone instead of mindlessly attacking. Position yourself to block his retreat, then resume applying Hemorrhage stacks with basic attacks and Crippling Strike once the field vanishes. If he tries to escape, pull him back with Apprehend to guarantee a fatal Noxian Guillotine.
laneImpact: In lane, you dictate the wave state because Shen cannot contest your push without risking a lethal pull from Apprehend. This pressure forces him to make a costly choice: stay to defend his tower or use Stand United to help his team, leaving you to demolish his turret. If he dashes forward with Shadow Dash, he exposes himself to a devastating counter-engage where Decimate easily heals back his initial burst.
why: Darius naturally dominates this matchup because Shen cannot match your sustained damage in extended duels as the game progresses. While Ki Barrier and Twilight Assault grant him short-term trades, he relies heavily on Spirit's Refuge to block your auto-attacks. Since your passive Hemorrhage requires consecutive hits to trigger Noxian Might, his defensive zone is his only real protection. Once that zone expires or you bypass it, his dueling power falls off drastically.

summary: Xin Zhao's strong early dueling and knockup from Three Talon Strike makes him a nightmare for Fiddlesticks to duel or drain against.
howToPlay: When invading, do not immediately blow Three Talon Strike.
