He will immediately follow up with Transfusion to leech his health back while you are retreating, turning any aggressive leap into a net loss for you.

summary: Soraka can place Equinox directly under Alistar when he engages, silencing him and preventing his follow-up Trample stun.
howToPlay: Walk up aggressively to threaten Headbutt without casting it, baiting her to waste Equinox preemptively. Once her silence is on cooldown, you have a fifteen-second window to execute your full crowd control rotation. If you get caught inside her zone, immediately trigger Unbreakable Will to cleanse the silence, allowing you to secure the Trample stun on Soraka herself before she can run away.
laneImpact: Because Astral Infusion and Wish constantly negate your burst damage, short skirmishes favor her if you cannot lock her down. Missing an engage or getting silenced mid-combo means you will be poked out by Starcall while your Triumphant Roar struggles to match her raw healing output. You must force fights only when her defensive zone is unavailable, otherwise her lane sustain slowly chokes you out.
why: This even matchup hinges entirely on how you play around Soraka's silence. When you initiate with Headbutt into Pulverize, she can instantly drop Equinox directly beneath you. This silence shuts down your ability to charge up and activate the Trample stun, leaving you stranded in the minion wave while she heals up her marksman using Astral Infusion.

summary: Aegis Assault can block the entire damage of your third The Darkin Blade cast if you do not position behind him.
howToPlay: To survive and win these duels, you must manipulate his shield direction. When casting your third The Darkin Blade, use the active part of Umbral Dash to slide directly behind Pantheon while he channels Aegis Assault. This bypasses his frontal damage reduction entirely. Always hold your Infernal Chains until after he commits his Shield Vault, forcing him to walk through the slow zone or burn his defense early. If he holds his shield, delay your final strike to waste his cooldown.
laneImpact: This dynamic makes early river skirmishes extremely dangerous for you. Contesting the Rift Scuttler directly often results in a quick death if Pantheon catches you with a fully charged Mortal Will. You cannot safely invade his camps, and his semi-global pressure with Grand Starfall means any aggressive gank you attempt can instantly turn into a deadly counter-gank where his burst outpaces your slow healing.
why: Pantheon dominates the early jungle skirmishes because his Aegis Assault perfectly counters your primary damage source. When you commit to your third cast of The Darkin Blade, he can simply raise his shield to absorb the entire impact. Combined with his point-and-click stun from Shield Vault and the raw burst of Comet Spear, he can easily win quick trades before your Deathbringer Stance or Umbral Dash can recover your health.

summary: Xayah can use the untargetability of Featherstorm to cleanly dodge Enchanted Crystal Arrow and turn the fight with her Bladecaller feathers.
howToPlay: Your goal is to bait out Featherstorm without committing your ultimate. Poke constantly with Volley to force her into a defensive posture. Never fire Enchanted Crystal Arrow from plain sight while her ultimate is off cooldown; instead, wait for her to use it during a chaotic skirmish or shoot from the fog of war. If she manages to dodge it anyway, immediately stop chasing and move laterally to avoid the straight line of her returning Bladecaller feathers.
laneImpact: You cannot easily secure kills with your ultimate once Xayah reaches level five, which severely limits your lane pressure. She will comfortably farm using Clean Cuts and zone you off with Double Daggers. If you step up to stack Ranger's Focus, she can activate Deadly Plumage to out-DPS you in raw trades, forcing you to play defensively and rely on Volley from a safe distance to prevent her from crashing waves.
why: Xayah directly counters your primary engagement tool because her Featherstorm grants her untargetability to completely bypass Enchanted Crystal Arrow. While you want to lock her down from range, she can reactively dodge your ultimate and immediately drop a lethal field of feathers. This allows her to pull them back with Bladecaller, rooting you in place and reversing any aggressive trade you try to initiate.

summary: Use Repudiation to block the knockup from Yone's Mortal Steel Q3, turning his engage into a favorable trade for you.
howToPlay: Never waste Repudiation during simple farming. Hold this shield specifically for the moment Yone dashes forward with his Mortal Steel knockup. When he activates Soul Unbound, track his movement direction and prepare your finger on the button; as the tornado flies, trigger your shield to absorb the impact, then instantly dash forward with Drakehound's Step to execute a full Cunning Sweep and Lacerate combo. If you miss-time the shield, retreat immediately and use Public Execution defensively.
laneImpact: Trade priority swings wildly depending on who bluffs successfully. When Yone has his tornado ready, you must concede minor wave pressure to ensure you can react. If you absorb his crowd control, you can force him back to his starting spirit body with low health, gaining immediate control over the minion wave and creating a massive health lead that prevents him from farming comfortably.
why: This matchup is a high-speed duel of mobility, dictated by how you manage your defensive response to his third cast of Mortal Steel. While Yone relies on Soul Unbound to initiate trades with his tornado, your ability to negate his setup determines the winner. Blocking his knockup with Repudiation completely denies his trade momentum, leaving him vulnerable to a swift Cunning Sweep counter-offensive before his cooldowns recover.

summary: Soul Shackles forces Yuumi's attached ally to retreat or face a stun, exposing Yuumi if her host dies.
howToPlay: Walk aggressively past the minion wave when Yuumi's host is isolated. Hold Dark Binding until they are forced to run in a straight line to escape your Soul Shackles. If Yuumi attempts to block your skillshots, cast Tormented Shadow directly under her to punish her low health pool. When Final Chapter is cast, immediately place Black Shield on your carry to allow them to keep chasing the host without getting rooted.
laneImpact: This interaction forces Yuumi's ADC into a defensive posture, fearing your forward positioning. You can easily control the wave with Tormented Shadow, pinning them under tower. Since Yuumi relies on Zoomies to sustain trades, forcing her host to constantly run from Dark Binding or Soul Shackles drains their mana rapidly. This pressure prevents Yuumi from safely detaching to trigger Bop 'n' Block, destroying their lane sustain.
why: Morgana scales incredibly well because Yuumi's attachment mechanic with You and Me! becomes a liability against Soul Shackles. When you trigger your ultimate, the host must drag Yuumi away or both get stunned, isolating them. Additionally, Black Shield completely negates Yuumi's slow from Prowling Projectile and the root from Final Chapter, shutting down her entire utility kit while Tormented Shadow constantly punishes their static positioning.

summary: Tryndamere's Undying Rage prevents you from getting World Ender takedown extensions during close skirmishes.
howToPlay: Never commit your World Ender early in skirmishes against him. Instead, use Infernal Chains to tether him when he dives with Spinning Slash, and execute your The Darkin Blade strikes to kite backward. If he activates Undying Rage, immediately use Umbral Dash defensively to buy time. Only re-engage with your passive Deathbringer Stance once his five-second invulnerability expires, ensuring you secure the kill and the healing reset.
laneImpact: Because you cannot easily burst him down, objective contests become highly risky. Tryndamere can spin over walls with Spinning Slash and initiate fights while ignoring your The Darkin Blade knockups using his ultimate. This forces you to play defensively in your own jungle, as a failed duel means he will out-sustain you with Bloodlust and steal your camps, putting your entire team behind on map pressure.
why: Tryndamere's kit directly neutralizes your crucial teamfight engine. During skirmishes, you rely on World Ender takedowns to extend your form and boost your healing. However, Undying Rage allows him to absorb your entire combo while staying at one health, completely blocking your reset. Meanwhile, his passive Battle Fury combined with Bloodlust healing lets him match your Deathbringer Stance sustain during prolonged jungle duels.

summary: If Lux misses her Light Binding, Jayce can immediately close the gap with To the Skies! and burst her before she can recover.
howToPlay: To survive, you must hold Light Binding exclusively as a defensive deterrent. Only use Lucent Singularity to farm from safety or chip his health pool. If Jayce attempts to engage with To the Skies!, cast Prismatic Barrier immediately to absorb the initial impact, then fire your root point-blank to lock him down under your turret. Never walk past the halfway point of the lane unless his transformation cooldown is active.
laneImpact: Because of this constant leap threat, you must forfeit early wave priority. You cannot use Light Binding to secure minions or trade, meaning Jayce can shove you under turret or poke you down from range. Every wave becomes a tense standoff where stepping up to trigger Illumination auto-attacks puts you in lethal range of his hammer.
why: This lane is dictated by the high-stakes threat of your crowd control. While you can poke Jayce from afar using Lucent Singularity, missing your Light Binding is a death sentence. Without that root, Jayce will immediately activate Transform Mercury Cannon to swap forms, lunge onto you with To the Skies!, and execute his full burst combo while you are completely defenseless.

summary: Lee Sin can use Dragon's Rage to kick Darius away and deny his Decimate heal or Noxian Guillotine execute.
howToPlay: Never initiate a fight with Decimate if Lee Sin has Dragon's Rage ready. Instead, stack Hemorrhage using Crippling Strike and basic attacks first. Force him to use his ultimate defensively to create space. If he kicks you away, use Apprehend immediately to pull him back in as soon as the displacement ends. Save your Noxian Guillotine until his safeguard options are exhausted or when he is locked in his Sonic Wave dash animation.
laneImpact: Jungle skirmishes around Epic Monsters and Scuttle Crabs are incredibly volatile. If Lee Sin has his ultimate available, you cannot mindlessly invade or force objectives, as he can disengage the fight instantly. His Safeguard and Sonic Wave give him superior terrain traversal, meaning any health trade you lose to a denied Decimate forces you to concede your camps or drop priority, directly impacting your gold income and map pressure.
why: This jungle duel is a high-stakes mechanical dance centered on your healing and execution thresholds. While your Hemorrhage stacks can overpower Lee Sin in extended skirmishes, his mobility allows him to dictate the pace. The matchup hinges entirely on Dragon's Rage; a well-timed kick can launch you away during your Decimate windup to deny crucial healing, or displace you mid-air to completely disrupt your Noxian Guillotine execution.

summary: Wukong can block Powerball with Warrior Trickster's clone, but Rammus easily outscales his physical damage in mid-game teamfights.
howToPlay: Never initiate a skirmish using *Nimbus Strike* when Rammus has his defensive tools ready. Instead, hold *Warrior Trickster* to block *Powerball* or to drop threat when he attempts to use *Frenzying Taunt*. In teamfights, completely ignore Rammus; bypass him to target his squishy backline with *Cyclone*. This activates *Stone Skin* against multiple enemies, allowing you to disrupt his teammates while Rammus wastes his crowd control on your clone or your frontline.
laneImpact: You cannot duel Rammus 1v1 in the river. If you engage while *Defensive Ball Curl* is active, his *Frenzying Taunt* forces you to shred yourself, especially after you gain attack speed from *Nimbus Strike*. This dynamic limits your early objective pressure and forces you to play defensively, as Rammus can initiate ganks much faster with *Powerball*, leaving your lanes vulnerable unless you track his position perfectly.
why: Rammus is a natural counter to Wukong's physical kit because *Defensive Ball Curl* and *Rolling Armordillo* punish your basic attacks. However, you possess a major safety net: you can drop the decoy from *Warrior Trickster* directly into his path to absorb *Powerball* before he reaches you. Despite this trick, as the game transitions to teamfights, Rammus's sheer armor scaling completely nullifies your *Golden Staff* and *Cyclone* damage.

summary: Varus can lock Ziggs down with Chain of Corruption to guarantee a full Blighted Quiver burst combo before Ziggs can escape with Satchel Charge.
howToPlay: Stand outside your own minion wave to force Ziggs to choose between hitting you or the minions with Bouncing Bomb. Hold Chain of Corruption until he throws out Hexplosive Minefield, as he is briefly locked in his casting animation. If he tries to disengage with Satchel Charge, reactively throw your ultimate to catch him right as he lands, then immediately follow up with Hail of Arrows.
laneImpact: Ziggs will constantly try to shove the wave with Hexplosive Minefield to secure easy recall windows or chip at your tower. By matching his push with your own auto-attacks empowered by Living Vengeance, you keep the wave in the center. This prevents him from getting easy damage on your turret while forcing him to step up into the threat range of your ultimate.
why: This long-range poke war heavily tilts in your favor because Ziggs relies on predictable positioning to land Bouncing Bomb. While he wants to keep his distance, your Chain of Corruption completely shuts down his safety net. By anchoring him in place, you deny him the ability to blast himself away with Satchel Charge, leaving him entirely exposed to a massive Blighted Quiver burst combo triggered by Piercing Arrow.

summary: Annie's instant burst with Summon: Tibbers easily overwhelms Mel's fragile health pool before she can establish zone control.
howToPlay: Keep your Pyromania passive sitting at three charges to bait Mel into thinking she is safe, then quickly activate Molten Shield for a sudden burst of movement speed to close the distance while instantly priming your stun. Launch Summon: Tibbers directly on top of her the millisecond she steps forward to cast. If she plays incredibly safe and hugs her tower, use your lane priority to dive her with the bear tanking the turret shots.
laneImpact: Before level five, use Disintegrate to match her wave clear while preserving mana. The moment you secure your ultimate, the threat of your instant stun forces Mel to retreat far behind her minions. She cannot safely step up to contest the wave, allowing you to crash minions at will, secure easy recall timings, and roam to the side lanes while she is trapped under her turret, terrified of your burst.
why: Mel relies heavily on setting up zone control to dictate the mid lane, but she lacks the defensive stats to survive sudden burst. Once you unlock Summon: Tibbers, your ability to instantly drop the bear with a Pyromania charge bypasses all of her zoning tools. By combining this stun with Incinerate and Disintegrate, you delete her fragile health pool before she can even react or establish her territory.

summary: Twilight Shroud (W) breaks the auto-targeting of Urgot's Purge (W), forcing him to manually aim or stop firing entirely.
howToPlay: To survive, you must position defensively near your own tower, keeping Disdain strictly as a defensive tool to buffer her Shuriken Flip engage rather than using it to initiate. Only activate Purge after she has wasted her Twilight Shroud, or use Corrosive Charge to scout her location inside the smoke. If she commits her ultimate, Perfect Execution, wait out the first dash before attempting to land Fear Beyond Death to turn the fight.
laneImpact: Because you cannot consistently trade damage when her shroud is up, Akali dictates the wave's tempo. She can easily poke you down with Five Point Strike whenever you step up to trigger Echoing Flames on minions. If you lose too much health before level five, her Perfect Execution becomes an unavoidable dive threat, forcing you into early, disadvantageous recalls that cost you plate gold.
why: The core of this matchup lies in how Akali's Twilight Shroud completely shuts down your primary damage. When she drops her smoke screen, the automatic targeting of Purge is broken, leaving you unable to lock onto her while she weaves in and out with Assassin's Mark. Your Disdain is also highly predictable, making it easy for her to dodge with Shuriken Flip and retaliate.

summary: Aurora can use Across the Veil to turn invisible and reposition, easily dodging your Singularity pull.
howToPlay: Keep a strict rule: never waste Across the Veil until you see the visual indicator of Singularity. Stand diagonally to the minion wave to force him to choose between farming or targeting you. Once he casts his vortex, activate your invisibility to hop outward, then retaliate instantly. Cast Between Worlds to lock him in place, following up with Twofold Hex and The Weirding to trigger Spirit Abjuration before his Astral Flight can carry him away.
laneImpact: This mobility advantage forces Aurelion Sol into a defensive posture, as he cannot safely deploy Singularity to stack his Cosmic Creator on waves. Every time he attempts to clear, you can aggressively step past his zone, trading with Twofold Hex and The Weirding. He will be shoved under his tower, bleeding pressure and allowing you to secure early priority for skirmishes.
why: Aurelion Sol relies heavily on pinning you down with Singularity to guarantee the damage of his channeled Breath of Light. Because Aurora can cast Across the Veil to leap, turn invisible, and swiftly reposition, she can effortlessly escape his gravitational pull. This mobility interaction completely negates his primary zoning tool, leaving him vulnerable to rapid, one-sided trades that he cannot easily retaliate against.

summary: Ekko can use Chronobreak to escape your Moonfall pull and heal back most of your burst damage.
howToPlay: To break this deadlock, you must bait out Chronobreak without committing your ultimate. Engage with Crescent Strike followed by Lunar Rush, using Pale Cascade to win the short trade, then walk away. Only cast Moonfall if his ultimate is on cooldown, or if you can use it to force him to panic-cast Chronobreak, keeping a second Lunar Rush reset ready to chase him down at his landing clone position once he reappears.
laneImpact: Before level five, trades are decided by how you use Pale Cascade to absorb Timewinder and block his Z-Drive Resonance third-hit burst. Once ultimates are unlocked, the threat of Chronobreak forces a stalemate where neither assassin can safely commit to an all-in. You must match his wave clear using Crescent Strike and Moonsilver Blade passive sweeps, as letting him push allows him to setup Parallel Convergence from out of vision.
why: This matchup revolves around the interaction between Moonfall and Chronobreak. While Diana possesses the raw damage to burst Ekko using Crescent Strike and Lunar Rush, her ultimate is easily countered. The moment you pull him in with Moonfall, Ekko can activate Chronobreak to instantly escape the impact zone, negate your crowd control, and undo your initial burst with his massive self-heal.

summary: Ornn can use Searing Charge and Call of the Forge God to chain-CC Tryndamere, running down the duration of Undying Rage.
howToPlay: To secure this advantage, pivot your early purchases toward heavy armor components immediately instead of magic resistance. During skirmishes, never initiate with Searing Charge; instead, save this mobility tool to disrupt Tryndamere the moment he activates Undying Rage. If he tries to escape with Spinning Slash, immediately deploy Call of the Forge God to pull him back into your crowd control chain, ensuring his ultimate runs out safely before he can reach his tower.
laneImpact: This interaction transforms the lane into a zone of absolute trade denial. Tryndamere cannot safely use Spinning Slash forward, as any aggressive dash leaves him vulnerable to a counter-engage. Since Ornn easily stacks armor, Tryndamere's critical strikes from Battle Fury lose their threat. Tryndamere is forced to waste Bloodlust on lane sustain rather than scaling, stripping away his early-game lane pressure and tower-taking threat.
why: Ornn naturally counters Tryndamere's ultimate-heavy diving playstyle. When Tryndamere pops Undying Rage, Ornn has the perfect toolkit to neutralize his invulnerability. By linking Searing Charge off terrain or a pillar and following up with Call of the Forge God, Ornn can chain knock-ups together, wasting the entire five-second duration of Tryndamere's death-defying state while completely halting his auto-attacks.

summary: Malphite's Seismic Shard (Q) poke cannot be dodged, and his Granite Shield (P) makes it incredibly difficult to chunk him down before he out-sustains you.
howToPlay: To survive, alter your build path early to prioritize magic resistance and health regeneration instead of rushing pure offensive power. During the laning phase, hold your Shuriken Flip specifically to disengage after he targets you with Seismic Shard, rather than using it to dive in. Only commit your Perfect Execution if you have successfully chipped away his Granite Shield with a max-range Five Point Strike beforehand, ensuring your execution damage isn't entirely absorbed by his passive.
laneImpact: This constant point-and-click poke war forces you into a defensive stance where you cannot easily contest the wave. You will find yourself forced to drop minions or use Twilight Shroud defensively just to farm under your turret. Your health pool will deplete much faster than Malphite's, forcing early recalls that cost you gold and XP, while his Unstoppable Force makes you incredibly vulnerable to dives once you are chipped down.
why: Malphite represents a highly tedious matchup because his point-and-click Seismic Shard cannot be dodged, slowly eroding your health bar from safety. Whenever you attempt to retaliate with Five Point Strike or Shuriken Flip, his Granite Shield absorbs your initial burst damage. This passive shield, combined with his constant movement speed steal, prevents you from efficiently executing your trade combos before he safely retreats.

summary: Syndra can use Scatter the Weak to push Swain away whenever he activates Demonic Ascension, wasting his ultimate's duration.
howToPlay: To secure your advantage, always keep Scatter the Weak off cooldown when Swain reaches his ultimate threshold. Never cast it aggressively unless his Nevermove has already missed. Position yourself slightly behind your own minions to easily sidestep his root, then instantly retaliate with a quick Dark Sphere and Force of Will combo. If he decides to activate Demonic Ascension, wait for him to step forward, blow him back, and then unleash your full burst.
laneImpact: This interaction forces Swain into a defensive posture. He cannot freely clear waves with Death's Hand without stepping into your range, allowing you to constantly poke him down with Dark Sphere. Since his primary engagement tool, Nevermove, is highly telegraphed, you can comfortably maintain lane priority. This positioning advantage translates into early tower pressure and secure recall windows while Swain is forced to farm under tower, bleeding health.
why: Syndra naturally dictates this lane because Swain relies on proximity to deal damage. When Swain attempts to close the distance with Demonic Ascension, Syndra's Scatter the Weak acts as a perfect counter-measure, forcefully pushing him away and denying his healing drain. Since Swain lacks mobility tools, being knocked back completely wastes his ultimate's duration, leaving him vulnerable to a follow-up burst from Unleashed Power.

summary: Malphite's Ground Slam drastically slows your attack speed, crippling your ability to quickly trigger Drakehound's Step empowered attacks.
howToPlay: To survive this war of attrition, abandon your pure lethality rush and pivot your build toward early magic resistance and health regeneration. In lane, look to absorb the tracking damage of Seismic Shard with a well-timed Repudiation shield. Never commit your Drakehound's Step attacks while his Ground Slam is available. If he wastes it on minions, immediately use Lacerate to slow him and execute your full combo.
laneImpact: You cannot play this as a standard burst lane. Malphite will constantly chip away at your health using Seismic Shard while absorbing your retaliation with Granite Shield. Because Ground Slam prevents you from winning quick trades, you lose the power to crash waves at will. This turns the lane into a grueling war of attrition where securing clean recalls becomes difficult, and his Unstoppable Force constantly threatens dives if you drop too low.
why: This matchup is dictated by how Malphite's Ground Slam directly counters your passive loop. Every time you cast Cunning Sweep or Lacerate, you rely on Drakehound's Step to quickly dash and unleash rapid, empowered basic attacks. However, Ground Slam's massive attack speed reduction completely freezes your animation speed. This prevents you from quickly reclaiming energy, leaving you sluggish and unable to execute your fast-paced assassin combos.

summary: When Alistar engages with Headbutt, Galio can immediately charge Shield of Durand to taunt the follow-up attackers.
howToPlay: Pivot your strategy entirely toward protecting your carry. Instead of engaging, save Headbutt to knock Galio away the instant he winds up Justice Punch. If he manages to land his taunt, immediately activate Unbreakable Will to cleanse the control, then use Pulverize to disrupt his channel or protect your partner from Winds of War. Let Triumphant Roar sustain you through his passive poke, and never headbutt into him unless his defensive shield is down.
laneImpact: You are forced to play defensively under your turret, as proactive trades usually result in losing half your carry's health bar. Galio easily secures wave priority by pairing Colossal Smash with Winds of War. If you get shoved in, he can freely step back to unleash Hero's Entrance toward mid lane, while your lack of wave clear keeps you stuck, unable to match his global map pressure.
why: Engaging with your Headbutt-Pulverize combo is highly risky because Galio thrives on counter-engaging. The moment you fly in with Headbutt, he can immediately channel Shield of Durand. This zone taunt completely neutralizes your ADC's follow-up damage while exposing them to Winds of War. Your Trample stun takes too long to ramp up compared to his instant defensive response, turning your aggressive plays into self-traps.

summary: Predict Renekton's Ruthless Predator stun and block it with Repudiation to negate his burst and turn the trade in your favor.
howToPlay: Never initiate with Cunning Sweep when Renekton has high fury and his Slice and Dice is available. Instead, bait his dash, and the millisecond his weapon glows for Ruthless Predator, activate Repudiation to block the stun. If your shield is on cooldown, play safely out of his double-dash range. If you get stunned without your shield, disengage immediately using Lacerate and a Drakehound's Step backward rather than trying to salvage the trade.
laneImpact: You cannot contest waves carelessly when his fury bar is red. If Renekton holds his stun, he forces you to farm under tower, chipping away your health with Cull the Meek whenever you step up. If you fail to block Ruthless Predator, you are forced into an early recall, losing valuable gold and letting him crash massive waves, which gives him total priority to dive or roam.
why: Renekton dominates early skirmishes because his fury-infused Ruthless Predator shreds your health bar and locks you down instantly. Since your trading power relies on chaining Cunning Sweep and Drakehound's Step, getting stunned mid-dash ruins your rhythm. The entire matchup hinges on whether you can time Repudiation to absorb and block his stun, as his raw burst otherwise easily overwhelms your basic defensive stats.

summary: The passive movement speed from Strut allows Miss Fortune to easily weave around Zeri's Burst Fire basic attacks in lane.
howToPlay: To secure this lead, prioritize keeping your Strut passive active by avoiding unnecessary minion aggro. If Zeri attempts to close the distance using Spark Surge or activates Lightning Crash, immediately drop Make It Rain directly on her path to decay her momentum. Once she is slowed and her dash is spent, lock her down and channel Bullet Time to shred her health bar. If she manages to jump on you, swap targets between her and a minion to maximize Love Tap damage.
laneImpact: In the lane, this mobility gap translates to total wave control. As Zeri struggles to land Burst Fire through the minion wave, you can position aggressively to clip her with Double Up bounces off dying minions. This constant poke quickly forces her to burn Spark Surge defensively rather than using it to slide over walls for creative angles, keeping her pinned under tower and bleeding gold.
why: This matchup is dictated by your ability to constantly outmaneuver Zeri's linear threat. The passive movement speed from Strut gives you a massive advantage, allowing you to easily sidestep Zeri's Burst Fire basic attacks. Because her primary DPS relies entirely on landing these skillshot-style bursts, your natural swiftness makes her struggle to establish any consistent trade pattern, leaving her vulnerable every time she misses.

summary: Teemo's Blinding Dart completely neutralizes Sett's Knuckle Down damage, forcing Sett to rely on passive health regeneration.
howToPlay: Accept giving up early farm and let the wave crash into your tower. Never initiate with Knuckle Down while his Blinding Dart is available; instead, walk up to farm and use Facebreaker defensively to stun him if he overextends. When Teemo tries to poke you under your turret, activate Haymaker to absorb the poison from Toxic Shot with the shield while securing distant minions. Your goal is survival; wait for a gank before attempting any all-in with The Show Stopper.
laneImpact: Because you cannot trade back effectively, you will constantly lose control of the minion waves. Teemo will easily freeze the wave near his tower or slow-push massive waves into yours, forcing you to farm under pressure. Every minion you contest costs you a chunk of health from his ranged attacks. This constant pressure ruins your recall timings and prevents you from helping your team with early map rotations.
why: Teemo completely dictates the pace of this lane through relentless range harassment. Whenever you attempt to close the distance using the movement speed from Knuckle Down, Teemo will shut down your trade immediately with Blinding Dart. This blind makes your empowered punches completely useless, nullifying your primary burst. Consequently, you are forced to absorb Toxic Shot poison while retreating, relying solely on your Pit Grit passive regeneration to survive.

summary: Skarner can use Impale to suppress Xin Zhao and drag him out of his Crescent Guard ultimate, leaving him vulnerable to ranged damage.
howToPlay: During teamfights, do not waste Impale early on other targets. Position yourself near your carries and wait for Xin Zhao to dive with Audacious Charge and activate Crescent Guard. The moment he sets up his arena, immediately use Impale to pull him out of it. If he plays passively, use Ixtal's Impact to flank and force him into a bad position, ensuring your team can burst him down.
laneImpact: In the early jungle, you must respect Xin Zhao's aggressive skirmishing with Three Talon Strike and Audacious Charge. However, because you scale so much better, his pressure has an expiration date. Once you secure your ultimate, you dictate the pace around objectives. He can no longer safely contest neutral monsters because his signature defensive zone is easily bypassed by your crowd control.
why: Skarner naturally outscales Xin Zhao as the game transitions into teamfights. While Xin Zhao relies on Crescent Guard to block ranged damage and survive collapses, your Impale completely nullifies this defense. By suppressing him and physically dragging him out of his protective zone, you expose him to your team's backline damage, rendering his ultimate useless and turning his engage into a trap.

summary: Ezreal must stand near his minion wave to reduce Kai'Sa's Icathian Rain damage, while using Arcane Shift to dodge her Void Seeker.
howToPlay: Position yourself directly inside your own minion wave during trades to split the missiles of Icathian Rain. Never use Arcane Shift offensively unless you see her Void Seeker miss, or actively use it to blink sideways out of its path. If she tries to close the gap with Supercharge, land a quick Essence Flux and Mystic Shot combo to punish her approach, then back off before her Second Skin stacks can detonate.
laneImpact: Because you must hug your minions to dilute Icathian Rain, you cannot easily freeze the wave without taking heavy poke. Health trades are incredibly volatile; if you step too far to the side to land Essence Flux, you risk isolation. The lane becomes a tense dance around the caster minions, where the player who mistimes their mobility spell loses control of the wave and is forced into an unfavorable recall.
why: This duel is dictated by how you manage Kai'Sa's isolation damage. Her Icathian Rain deals massive burst if you are caught alone, but sharing the missiles with your minion wave neutralizes her primary threat. Meanwhile, her long-range poke from Void Seeker can be completely negated by your Arcane Shift, turning what should be her opening burst into a wasted cooldown and a window for you to counter-attack with Mystic Shot.

summary: Corki can use Valkyrie to easily escape Swain's Demonic Ascension radius, denying him crucial healing.
howToPlay: To win this war of attrition, always keep Valkyrie off cooldown. Never use it offensively unless Swain has already wasted his ultimate. Position yourself constantly on the move to dodge Nevermove, as its return trajectory is highly predictable. When Swain triggers Demonic Ascension, immediately cast Valkyrie backward to break the tether and wait out his transformation. While his ultimate is down, abuse your range advantage by firing Missile Barrage and Phosphorus Bomb to force him out of lane.
laneImpact: The lane progresses as a constant push-and-pull. Swain uses Death's Hand to clear waves and tries to pull you in with Nevermove. Getting hit by this root triggers Ravenous Flock, giving Swain the health advantage. You must match his push using Gatling Gun and Phosphorus Bomb. Tower pressure is minimal for both, but the lane swings based on who manages their health pool better before major map skirmishes.
why: This matchup is a battle of attrition where Swain relies on Ravenous Flock and Demonic Ascension to outsustain you in close-quarters trades. While his Death's Hand punishes proximity, your ranged tools like Phosphorus Bomb and Missile Barrage allow you to chip away at his health bar safely. Crucially, whenever Swain attempts to drain your health during his ultimate, your Valkyrie provides an instant escape to deny his healing entirely.

summary: Senna's Piercing Darkness allows her to trade and sustain through Lux's poke, while her scaling eventually outclasses Lux's damage.
howToPlay: Focus entirely on maintaining a frozen or neutral wave state rather than forcing raw damage. Use Lucent Singularity sparingly to match her push, and never throw Light Binding unless she steps forward to collect a soul or mispositions her Last Embrace. If she uses Curse of the Black Mist to disengage, retreat immediately to your turret and shield your ally with Prismatic Barrier to mitigate any long-range retaliation from Dawning Shadow.
laneImpact: This sustain engine forces you into a passive stance where traditional health trades are heavily tilted in her favor. You cannot afford to let the wave crash under your turret, as Senna will freely farm souls and harass you with Piercing Darkness through the minions. Losing control of the wave tempo means your ADC gets shoved in, giving Senna total freedom to secure deep vision or rotate.
why: Senna completely neutralizes your Lucent Singularity poke because Piercing Darkness provides her and her ADC constant sustain. While you expend mana trying to whittle them down, her Basic Attack passive allows her to safely harvest Mist from a distance, permanently increasing her range and damage. Because her scaling is infinite, your flat magic damage from Final Spark and Illumination quickly loses its threat level as the match progresses.

summary: Poppy's Steadfast Presence cannot block Singed's Fling because it is a displacement cast on her, not a dash performed by Singed.
howToPlay: To win trades, play around your passive Iron Ambassador to poke him down and secure a shield before he gets into Fling range. If he charges forward, do not waste Steadfast Presence; instead, use Heroic Charge on a minion to escape or pin him to a wall if he mispositions. If he activates Insanity Potion to run you down, use a quick cast of Keeper's Verdict to knock him airborne and disengage.
laneImpact: Since you cannot interrupt his engage, lane control dictates the pace. If Singed attempts to proxy or fast-shove with Poison Trail, you must respond by matching his clear using Hammer Shock. Allowing him to crash waves freely gives him easy recall windows or map rotations, while overextending to stop him opens you up to being flipped into a dangerous position far from your own tower.
why: This even matchup centers on a common misunderstanding of Poppy's defensive tools. While Steadfast Presence is excellent at stopping mobile skirmishers, it is completely useless against Singed's Fling. Because Fling is a targeted displacement cast upon you rather than a dash performed by Singed, your protective barrier will not block it. This allows him to bypass your primary defensive utility and toss you directly into his Poison Trail.

summary: Mordekaiser's Realm of Death isolates Hecarim, preventing him from healing off multiple targets with Spirit of Dread and stripping his movement speed advantage.
howToPlay: When contesting objectives, hold onto Realm of Death specifically for the moment Hecarim activates Devastating Charge or launches Onslaught of Shadows. Pull him in with Death's Grasp if he tries to kite away, then lock him down. Once inside your arena, hit him with an isolated Obliterate and activate Darkness Rise to shred his health. If he manages to disengage early, use Indestructible defensively to absorb his remaining Rampage stacks while waiting for your cooldowns to return.
laneImpact: This dynamic dictates the pace of jungle contests and objective fights. Hecarim cannot freely dive your backline with Onslaught of Shadows because you can immediately shut down his assault by banishing him. He is forced to play passively, avoiding direct counter-jungling and delaying his skirmishes. If he attempts to contest scuttle crabs or neutral objectives, your threat of isolation forces him to cede priority or risk dying alone in your arena.
why: You hold a massive advantage in direct skirmishes because Realm of Death completely neutralizes Hecarim's teamfight-oriented kit. Once you trap him in your pocket dimension, you strip away the extra targets he needs to sustain himself through Spirit of Dread. Furthermore, the isolation removes his momentum-based damage from Warpath, leaving him with only Rampage to fight back against your superior AP juggernaut stats.

summary: Veigar's Event Horizon acts as an impassable wall that immediately stuns you if you attempt to use Heroic Swing through it.
howToPlay: Your primary goal is to abuse Veigar's weak early levels. Force aggressive trades using Avengerang and your Dirty Fighting double-shot to chunk him before he unlocks his cage. Never initiate with Heroic Swing; instead, keep it strictly as an escape tool or wait until Event Horizon is completely on cooldown. If you do get trapped inside his cage, walk micro-adjustments to dodge Dark Matter rather than panic-swinging into the stun barrier.
laneImpact: Because Event Horizon denies your mobility, you lose the freedom to blindly trade with Heroic Swing. Veigar will safely stack Phenomenal Evil Power using Baleful Strike from a distance. If you cannot secure an early health advantage with Avengerang and Dirty Fighting before he gets his cage, he will freeze the wave, nullify your roam potential, and eventually threaten you with Primordial Burst under your own turret.
why: This matchup hinges on how Veigar's Event Horizon completely nullifies your main mobility tool. The moment you cast Heroic Swing, any contact with his cage's boundary immediately interrupts your flight, stunning you on the spot. This leaves you completely exposed to an easy Dark Matter follow-up and massive burst, turning your primary aggressive tool into a self-inflicted trap.

summary: Yone can easily bypass Seraphine's range using Soul Unbound and Fate Sealed, leaving her with very little room to safely cast her slow abilities.
howToPlay: Keep the minions permanently closer to your turret by only using High Note to thin the wave, never to push it. Never cast Beat Drop unless Yone has already committed his Soul Unbound; holding it is your only deterrent against his forward dash. If he unleashes Fate Sealed, immediately use your Echoed Surround Sound for the shield and movement speed to escape his burst range, prioritizing survival over landing an offensive Encore.
laneImpact: You cannot safely contest the wave near his tower, as a frozen lane allows Yone to run you down with Mortal Steel's third strike. Trying to trade health results in him absorbing damage with Spirit Cleave while chunking you down. This forces you to constantly forfeit priority, lagging behind in gold while being stuck under your own turret trying to farm safely with Stage Presence double casts.
why: Yone completely invalidates your range advantage because his Soul Unbound and Fate Sealed allow him to cross the lane instantly, ignoring the slow travel time of your Beat Drop and High Note. Once Yone closes the distance, Seraphine's lack of mobility makes her an easy target for his rapid physical and magical strikes from Way of the Hunter, turning any attempt to poke him into a lethal threat.

summary: Irelia can use Defiant Dance to mitigate Annie's entire burst combo, then easily run her down with Bladesurge resets.
howToPlay: Keep the minion wave frozen just outside your turret range by only last-hitting with Disintegrate. Never throw your Pyromania stun unless Irelia has already wasted Defiant Dance. Instead, sit on your four stacks as a deterrent to freeze her in place. If she attempts to force an engage with Flawless Duet, immediately activate Molten Shield for the movement speed boost to dodge the blades, then retreat safely under your tower.
laneImpact: You cannot step past the midpoint of the lane without risking a lethal chase. If you blindly push the wave, you create a runway of low-health minions for Irelia's Bladesurge, allowing her to stack Ionian Fervor instantly and dive you. This constant threat forces you to surrender early priority, bleed gold under your turret, and restricts your ability to roam and assist your jungler.
why: Annie's threat relies on locking down her target with a Pyromania stun and unloading Summon: Tibbers. Irelia completely nullifies this burst pattern using Defiant Dance, which heavily reduces your magical damage during her channel. Once your burst is wasted, she easily closes the gap with Bladesurge resets, stacking Ionian Fervor on low-health minions to run you down without any fear of retaliation.

summary: Lee Sin's Dragon's Rage can kick Amumu away to prevent his engage, but Amumu outscales him heavily in late-game teamfights.
howToPlay: Never initiate with Bandage Toss if Lee Sin has Dragon's Rage available, as he will immediately kick you into his team or away from your targets. Instead, walk up with Despair active and force him to make the first move. Track his jungle camps to predict his ganks, countering them by securing cross-map objectives. Hold your Curse of the Sad Mummy until he commits his Safeguard dash, ensuring he cannot escape your ultimate’s radius.
laneImpact: Your early pathing is entirely dictated by tracking Lee Sin's starting buff. If he lands Sonic Wave in your jungle, his Flurry gives him the attack speed to secure a kill before you can stack Tantrum. You must concede early Scuttle Crabs if your laners lack priority, as a duel at level three favors him. However, forcing him to use Safeguard defensively instead of making plays across the map is a major victory for your lanes.
why: This jungle duel is a race against the clock. Lee Sin uses Flurry and Sonic Wave to dominate early skirmishes, trying to invade your camps. While his Dragon's Rage can deny your Curse of the Sad Mummy by kicking you away before your team can follow up on Bandage Toss, your late-game scaling is vastly superior. If you survive his early pressure, your Despair and Cursed Touch will melt everyone in teamfights.

summary: Ezreal can poke Jinx down with Mystic Shot while she tries to farm, and can use Arcane Shift to instantly escape her Flame Chompers! if caught.
howToPlay: Capitalize on your early strength by holding Arcane Shift specifically for her Flame Chompers! or a sudden Zap!. Never use your blink aggressively unless Jinx has already wasted her traps. Stand just behind your minion wave to block her Zap! while aligning your Mystic Shot to clip her whenever she steps up to utilize the extra range of Fishbones. Once you hit your first major item spike, aggressively force trades to completely push her out of the lane.
laneImpact: This matchup quickly turns into a heavy poke dynamic where Jinx is forced under her turret, constantly low on health. Because you can safely stack Rising Spell Force on the wave while harassing her, you secure an early tempo advantage. This pressure lets you force her to recall at awkward times, delaying her expensive rocket upgrades and allowing you to safely secure plates or rotate before she can ever reach her critical late-game power.
why: You completely dictate the pace of this lane because Jinx lacks early mobility to dodge your skillshots. While she locks herself in place to farm with Pow-Pow or Fishbones, you can constantly chip away at her health bar using Mystic Shot from safety. Even if she tries to set up a trap or self-peel using Flame Chompers!, your Arcane Shift allows you to instantly blink over the traps, rendering her main defensive tool entirely useless.

summary: Bard must use Caretaker's Shrine to survive Lux's Lucent Singularity poke, while avoiding her Light Binding.
howToPlay: Position yourself aggressively parallel to the minion wave, using the bushes to hide the animation of Light Binding. Watch where Bard places his Caretaker's Shrine; when he or his carry walks toward a charging shrine to heal, immediately throw Lucent Singularity on that exact spot to punish them, followed by Final Spark if they are low. If Bard tries to escape or flank through a wall using Magical Journey, queue up Light Binding at the exit of his portal for an instant, guaranteed root.
laneImpact: This dynamic forces Bard to play defensively behind his minion wave, stripping away his ability to roam through Magical Journey. Your constant zone control with Lucent Singularity keeps the enemy duo pinned under tower, bleeding gold. Since Bard is forced to prioritize defensive Caretaker's Shrine placements over offensive trades, you secure total brush control and can easily deny him the space needed to land a stun with Cosmic Binding.
why: Lux dominates this matchup because her long-range Lucent Singularity constantly chips away at Bard and his ADC, forcing Bard to waste his mana and time setting up Caretaker's Shrine just to stay healthy. Because Bard must walk predictably to collect Traveler's Call chimes or place his shrines, he becomes an easy target for Light Binding, which completely neutralizes his roaming potential and setups.

summary: Irelia can easily close the gap on Aurora using Bladesurge (Q) and mitigate her burst with Defiant Dance (W).
howToPlay: Keep the minions close to your turret at all times. Never cast Twofold Hex on the wave when Irelia has marks active. If she initiates with Bladesurge, immediately use The Weirding to slow her and push yourself backward, then cast Across the Veil to safely drop aggro and reposition. If she bypasses this and traps you with Vanguard's Edge, use Between Worlds to jump to the opposite boundary to delay her onslaught until your tower can target her.
laneImpact: You cannot contest the wave near the center of the lane. If you push, Irelia will freeze and use low-health minions as stepping stones to run you down. You are forced to surrender early priority, meaning you will be stuck under tower trying to clear with Twofold Hex while Irelia secures deep vision or rotates to assist her jungler before you can even react.
why: Irelia completely neutralizes your ranged advantage because she can constantly reset Bladesurge on minions to jump directly onto you. When you try to retaliate with your three-strike combo from Spirit Abjuration or Twofold Hex, she can simply channel Defiant Dance to absorb your main burst. This leaves you vulnerable with no trading power while her passive is fully stacked.

summary: Akshan can use Heroic Swing to chase down Ezreal even after he uses Arcane Shift, but missing the grapple leaves him highly vulnerable to Mystic Shot spam.
howToPlay: Never commit Arcane Shift offensively unless Akshan has already bungled or spent Heroic Swing. Position yourself away from walls to limit his grapple angles, making it harder for him to lock onto you. If he initiates with his swing, immediately track his landing spot to punish him with a Mystic Shot and Essence Flux combo. If you get caught off guard, channel Trueshot Barrage from a safe distance to clear the wave and reset.
laneImpact: The lane is a constant race for wave priority where cooldowns dictate pressure. Akshan wants to push early using Avengerang to create room for aggressive swings. If you let him shove you under turret, he will look to roam with Going Rogue. You must use Rising Spell Force stacks to match his clear, forcing him to choose between using Heroic Swing defensively to escape or offensively to trade health.
why: This skill matchup is defined by how Ezreal manages his safety net against Akshan's aggressive mobility. While Arcane Shift is your premier escape tool, Akshan can easily match the distance and hunt you down by anchoring Heroic Swing to terrain. However, this high-mobility trade is double-edged; if Akshan miscalculates his grapple or hits a minion, his escape is gone, leaving him completely exposed to a relentless barrage of Mystic Shot and Essence Flux.

summary: Twisted Fate's Destiny reveals Akali even inside her Twilight Shroud, allowing his team to target her during teamfights.
howToPlay: Watch his Pick a Card cycles closely. The second he locks in a blue or red card to clear minions, immediately engage with Shuriken Flip. In teamfights, never drop Twilight Shroud early. Wait until he commits Destiny to teleport or reveal your team; once his ultimate's vision fades, you are free to dive his backline using Perfect Execution. If he holds his ultimate just to counter your shroud, use your raw mobility to flank instead.
laneImpact: Before he gets his ultimate, you can easily control the lane. Use Five Point Strike to clear waves and force him to farm under tower, preventing him from getting extra gold from charged Dice. The lane transforms into a map-wide race once he gets access to Destiny; you cannot let him roam freely while you slowly collect waves. You must push and match his rotations instantly.
why: You hold a clear kill advantage in lane, but Twisted Fate has a massive macro tool that neutralizes your safety. While you can out-duet him easily, his ultimate Destiny completely counters your Twilight Shroud. When he activates it, your absolute stealth is stripped away, revealing your position to his entire team during chaotic fights. You must respect this true sight because your shroud won't protect you once he flies.

summary: Gwen's Hallowed Mist can ignore Ambessa's outer-ring Cunning Sweep, and her Snip Snip! out-damages Ambessa in extended duels.
howToPlay: To win, you must force early skirmishes during her first clear when she is vulnerable. Never initiate with Public Execution while her Hallowed Mist is active; instead, walk into her zone or bait it out first. Save Repudiation specifically to absorb the final, heavy snip of her Snip Snip! or the slowing needles of Needlework. If a skirmish goes wrong, use Drakehound's Step combined with Lacerate to quickly dash away over terrain.
laneImpact: This matchup dynamic forces you to secure early leads before Gwen out-clears and out-scales you. You cannot safely contest isolated Scuttle Crabs if she has her stacks ready, as her Skip 'n Slash allows her to easily dodge your Public Execution or reposition inside her mist. Losing early jungle pressure means she will secure neutral objectives faster, leaving your lanes vulnerable to her scaling threat.
why: Gwen naturally outscales you because her Hallowed Mist makes her immune to the outer-edge sweet spot of your Cunning Sweep if she positions it well. In direct, extended jungle duels, her continuous Snip Snip! combined with the percentage health healing from A Thousand Cuts simply melts your health bar faster than you can burst her down, especially once she gets access to Needlework.

summary: Jax's Counter Strike completely blocks all rapid-fire attacks from Urgot's Purge, leaving Urgot defenseless during the duration.
howToPlay: To survive, you must bait out Counter Strike without activating Purge. If Jax activates his defensive helicopter spin, immediately stop attacking and prepare to buffer his stun with Disdain. Timing Disdain right as his stun triggers throws him behind you, preventing him from following up with his Grandmaster-at-Arms passive prods. Only initiate trades with Corrosive Charge to slow him from a distance, keeping your distance until his main defensive tool is on cooldown.
laneImpact: Every wave becomes highly tense because Jax can use Leap Strike to jump onto you when your Disdain is on cooldown. If you fight back with Purge during his Counter Strike, you lose the trade immediately and get stunned, leaving you vulnerable to his Empower-enhanced attacks. This forces you under turret, sacrificing early wave control and letting Jax safely stack his Relentless Assault.
why: Jax's Counter Strike completely neutralizes Urgot's primary source of damage by blocking every single rapid-fire tick of Purge. Because Purge attacks at an extremely high frequency, you end up feeding Jax's dodge mechanic instantly, maximizing the damage of his stun recast. Without your Purge DPS, you cannot trigger your Echoing Flames passive effectively, turning what should be your strongest trade tool into your own undoing.

summary: Tristana can jump directly onto you with Rocket Jump and stack Explosive Charge, forcing you to play extremely defensively without support intervention.
howToPlay: To execute this perfectly, watch Ashe's positioning when she attempts to secure last hits. The moment she missteps or wastes Volley on the wave, immediately use Rocket Jump directly onto her. Apply Explosive Charge and activate Rapid Fire to instantly detonate the bomb, resetting your jump. If she tries to retaliate with Enchanted Crystal Arrow at close range, use Buster Shot to push her away or secure the final blow while denying her the stun duration.
laneImpact: This dynamic forces Ashe to play incredibly far back, conceding control of the minion waves. Since she cannot step up without risking a sudden Rocket Jump engage, you can freely slow-push waves or pressure her under tower. She is forced to use Volley defensively to clear minions rather than poke you. This pressure limits her ability to look for cross-map plays with Enchanted Crystal Arrow, keeping her pinned and vulnerable.
why: Tristana completely dominates Ashe because of her raw gap-close and explosive burst. Ashe relies on the constant slows from Frost Shot and poke from Volley to keep you at bay, but she lacks any natural mobility to escape a hard engage. By using Rocket Jump to leap straight onto her, you bypass her spacing tools entirely and can quickly stack Explosive Charge, threatening a lethal burst before she can even ramp up her Ranger's Focus.

summary: If Bard roams to collect chimes, Blitzcrank can easily dive or zone Bard's isolated ADC with Rocket Grab.
howToPlay: To survive, you must limit your Traveler's Call roaming exclusively to when the wave is fully crashed under the enemy tower or when Blitzcrank misses Rocket Grab. Always position yourself slightly ahead of your ADC, keeping minion block active, holding Cosmic Binding to stun Blitzcrank against a wall if he charges forward with Overdrive. If your ADC is hooked, use Tempered Fate on the enemy ADC to prevent them from following up on the crowd control, rather than using it on Blitzcrank himself.
laneImpact: This dynamic paralyzes your lane pressure. You cannot safely deploy Caretaker's Shrine to sustain if you are constantly forced to hug your ADC to block Rocket Grab angles. If Blitzcrank gains wave control, he can freeze near his tower, forcing your ADC into a dangerous zone where any step forward results in a deadly Power Fist knock-up, while your Magical Journey escapes are useless if you get hooked first.
why: Bard's core loop of roaming for Traveler's Call chimes directly enables Blitzcrank's lethal kill-lane threat. The moment Bard steps away, Blitzcrank uses Overdrive to close the gap and lock down the isolated marksman with Rocket Grab and Power Fist. This creates a structural conflict: Bard must either abandon his scaling mechanic or leave his partner exposed to a sudden, fatal hook under or near the turret.

summary: Kha'Zix must wait out Vi's Vault Breaker before committing, as her Cease and Desist can lock him down instantly if he leaps in too early.
howToPlay: Never initiate a fight with Vault Breaker if Kha'Zix has his Leap available. Instead, walk directly into melee range, triggering Denting Blows and Relentless Force to force his hand. Save Cease and Desist for the exact moment he attempts to leap away or engage, securing an absolute shutdown. If he activates Void Assault to drop aggro, patient players will hold their ground, using Blast Shield to absorb his Unseen Threat re-engages.
laneImpact: This matchup shifts jungle control heavily in your favor, preventing Kha'Zix from invading or contesting objectives freely. He is forced to play passively, holding Leap defensively rather than using it to secure river skirmishes. This dynamic allows you to pressure neutral camps and secure double crabs with minimal fear of counter-jungling, as he cannot afford to face you without a clear numbers advantage.
why: Vi completely dominates the direct duel because Kha'Zix cannot safely use Leap to engage. If he jumps in prematurely, Cease and Desist provides an instant, unstoppable lockdown that leaves him completely vulnerable. Furthermore, his isolated Taste Their Fear burst is heavily mitigated by Blast Shield, while Denting Blows ensures Vi wins any extended skirmish once she connects Vault Breaker.

summary: Zed can use Death Mark to dodge Brand's Sear stun and easily burst him down due to Brand's lack of mobility.
howToPlay: You must hold Sear as an absolute deterrent. Never cast it proactively to trade. When Zed initiates with Death Mark, wait for the exact moment he reappears behind you. Instantly tag him with Conflagration and aim Sear directly behind your own model to secure the stun. This is your only window to survive; if you land it, follow up with Pillar of Flame and Pyroclasm to force a trade-kill before his mark detonates.
laneImpact: Once Zed unlocks Death Mark, you lose all offensive agency in the mid lane. You are forced to farm from extreme range with Pillar of Flame, as stepping forward invites a Living Shadow and Shadow Slash slow, setting up an easy dive. If he pokes you below half health, his Contempt for the Weak ensures a swift execution under your own turret, forcing poor recalls and letting him roam freely.
why: Zed completely neutralizes your defensive tools because Death Mark makes him untargetable, allowing him to easily bypass your Sear stun. If you try to trigger Blaze and throw Sear to peel yourself, he simply ults to dodge it. Without any mobility, Brand cannot escape the subsequent burst from Razor Shuriken and Shadow Slash, leaving you completely defenseless once your crowd control is wasted.

summary: Gwen can deploy Hallowed Mist to negate the damage and knockback of Hecarim's Devastating Charge if he initiates from outside the zone.
howToPlay: To survive this matchup, you must alter your approach angles. Never initiate with Devastating Charge from a distance if her Hallowed Mist is available. Instead, walk directly into melee range using Rampage and Spirit of Dread to bait her defensive zone first. Once she deploys the mist, use your ultimate Onslaught of Shadows to fear her inside her own zone, or wait out its duration before unleashing your knockback.
laneImpact: In the jungle, this interaction severely restricts your ganking and skirmishing power. Invading Gwen or contesting neutral camps becomes extremely risky because she can drop her mist to absorb your initial burst, then retaliate. If she blocks your Devastating Charge, she easily dominates the duel with Skip 'n Slash and Needlework, forcing you to retreat with low health and forfeit map pressure.
why: Gwen completely neutralizes your primary initiation threat with her Hallowed Mist. If you trigger your Devastating Charge from outside her zone, she can deploy her mist to negate both your incoming damage and the crucial knockback. Deprived of your initial momentum, you are forced into a losing close-quarters brawl against her high-DPS Snip Snip! and her passive healing from A Thousand Cuts.

summary: Olaf's Ragnarok grants complete immunity to the fear from Onslaught of Shadows and the knockback of Devastating Charge, allowing him to easily run Hecarim down.
howToPlay: To survive, track Olaf's starting buff and path to the opposite side of the map to avoid early skirmishes. Keep Devastating Charge purely as an escape tool to leap over walls or gain distance rather than trying to initiate on him. If a teamfight erupts, never launch Onslaught of Shadows directly at him; instead, target his backline and wait for Ragnarok to expire before trying to fight him with Rampage and Spirit of Dread.
laneImpact: This structural disadvantage means you cannot contest scuttle crabs or neutral objectives in direct duels. If Olaf invades your jungle, his Berserker Rage turns any low-health bait into a trap, meaning you must surrender your camps rather than fighting back. His fast clear with Undertow forces you into a defensive, reactive posture where you lose all early map pressure.
why: Olaf is your absolute worst nightmare in the river because Ragnarok completely nullifies your crowd control. When he activates his ultimate, he becomes entirely immune to the fear from your Onslaught of Shadows and the displacement of Devastating Charge. Without these tools to disrupt his advance, Olaf can easily run you down using Undertow slows while shredding you with Reckless Swing and Vicious Strikes.

summary: Jarvan can abuse Shyvana's weak pre-6 by forcing early ganks, and can trap her with Cataclysm if her Dragon's Descent is on cooldown.
howToPlay: Path defensively by starting on the opposite side of the map to avoid early duels. Use Flame Breath to secure contested camps from safety rather than fighting over scuttles. Crucially, never use Dragon's Descent to engage unless Cataclysm has already been deployed. Always keep your ultimate ready as an unstoppable escape tool to leap directly out of his arena.
laneImpact: This dynamic forces your lanes to play defensively while Jarvan IV dictates the early map tempo. While you power-farm camps to generate Fury of the Dragonborn, his active ganking puts your teammates behind. If he invades, your Burnout movement speed is insufficient to escape over walls, meaning you must concede early river control or risk giving away kills.
why: Shyvana needs to stack Draconic Bloodline but Jarvan IV thrives on early skirmishes. His Demacian Standard into Dragon Strike combo gives him unmatched early pressure compared to your pre-level 5 kit. If caught without Dragon's Descent, he can easily trap you inside Cataclysm, leaving you helpless as your basic abilities cannot cross his arena wall.

summary: Yasuo can completely nullify your Avengerang and Heroic Swing damage by placing Wind Wall in your flight path.
howToPlay: Pop his Way of the Wanderer shield with a single Dirty Fighting physical strike before committing any skills. If Yasuo wastes Wind Wall to block a simple Avengerang, you have a massive twenty-second window where he is incredibly vulnerable. Only initiate your Heroic Swing once that wind barrier is gone, ensuring you swing perpendicular to his Sweeping Blade path so he cannot interrupt your flight or set up an easy Last Breath.
laneImpact: Because your swing can be intercepted, you cannot safely use Heroic Swing for aggressive trades or wave clearance. Yasuo will use Sweeping Blade through your minions to bypass your range advantage and trigger his Way of the Wanderer shield. If you try to retaliate, his Wind Wall blocks your Comeuppance or Avengerang, forcing you to play under your turret and lose mid-lane priority.
why: Yasuo holds a massive structural advantage because his Wind Wall completely nullifies your primary tools. An angled Avengerang is easily erased, but the real danger lies in how he can drop his wall directly in the trajectory of your Heroic Swing. This instantly stops your swing momentum, cancels your damage, and leaves you stranded in melee range right next to his Steel Tempest.

summary: Lee Sin can use Dragon's Rage to kick Diana away when she initiates with Lunar Rush, completely ruining her engage.
howToPlay: To beat the blind monk, you must play a patient bait-and-switch game. Never initiate fights directly onto Lee Sin if his Dragon's Rage is available. Instead, clear camps rapidly using Moonsilver Blade and look to counter-gank. Use Crescent Strike to poke and threaten, but hold your Lunar Rush. Force him to waste Safeguard or commit his ultimate on your teammates first, then plunge in with Moonfall to clean up the fight.
laneImpact: Because of this dynamic, the early jungle rotation becomes a high-stakes race for map pressure. Lee Sin uses Flurry and Sonic Wave to execute fast, aggressive ganks before you scale. If you fall behind in clearing or fail to match his early skirmishes, he will snowball the map. Every neutral objective fight becomes a tense standoff where the first to commit can easily be punished.
why: This jungle duel revolves around Diana's initiation versus Lee Sin's peel. Your primary engage relies on hitting Crescent Strike to reset Lunar Rush and group enemies with Moonfall. However, Lee Sin possesses the perfect counter-button with Dragon's Rage. If you dash in blindly, he can instantly kick you away mid-flight or right after landing, completely nullifying your burst and leaving you stranded far from your targets.

summary: Morgana easily neutralizes Ziggs's lane pressure by matching his waveclear with Tormented Shadow (W) and using Black Shield (E) to block Satchel Charge (W) displacements.
howToPlay: Position yourself away from your minions so Ziggs must choose between targeting you with Bouncing Bomb or clearing the wave. Cast Tormented Shadow directly on the caster minions to match his push. Never waste Black Shield early; hold it to reactively block his Satchel Charge knockback. If he steps forward to trigger his Short Fuse passive on you, punish his lack of mobility by pinning him with Dark Binding and initiating Soul Shackles.
laneImpact: This interaction forces Ziggs to expend his mana pool on minion waves rather than poking you down. Because he cannot establish priority, his ability to secure early plates or assist his jungler vanishes. You dictate the pace of the lane, keeping him pinned under his own tower where he is highly vulnerable to a sudden Dark Binding catching him off guard.
why: Ziggs thrives on shoving you under turret with Bouncing Bomb and threatening a tower execute, but your kit completely shuts down his-siege. Placing Tormented Shadow on the wave neutralizes his pushing power instantly. Furthermore, your Black Shield entirely negates the displacement from his Satchel Charge, meaning he cannot peel you off or disrupt your positioning when you decide to step forward.

summary: Draven can easily out-trade Ezreal in direct auto-attack exchanges, but Ezreal can use Arcane Shift to escape all-ins and farm safely with Mystic Shot.
howToPlay: Prioritize using Mystic Shot solely to thin oncoming minion waves, preventing Draven from freezing or diving. Never use Arcane Shift offensively; hold it strictly as your reactive escape when he throws Stand Aside or runs at you with Blood Rush. When Draven moves to catch his axes, punish him by aiming Essence Flux followed by a Mystic Shot at his landing indicator, allowing you to chip his health safely from afar.
laneImpact: Draven’s need to catch Spinning Axe forces him to constantly auto-attack, naturally pushing the wave toward your tower. This creates a high-pressure lane where you are trapped under turret, struggling to match his push. If you let him crash massive waves, he will secure easy tower plates. Missing your skillshots means losing control of the wave tempo, allowing Draven to safely back with massive gold from League of Draven.
why: Draven's Spinning Axe provides massive physical damage that completely dominates Ezreal in raw auto-attack trades. If you try to stand and fight, his raw DPS wins easily. However, Ezreal has the perfect tools to survive this lane: you can use Arcane Shift to instantly disengage when Draven activates Blood Rush, and safely collect minions from a distance using Mystic Shot without ever entering his deadly attack range.

summary: Wukong can use Warrior Trickster to absorb Graves's End of the Line, then re-engage with Nimbus Strike once Graves's ammo is low.
howToPlay: Never initiate with Warrior Trickster. Instead, bait his End of the Line by standing near terrain, then cast your clone to absorb the blast. The moment he begins his reload animation, dash in with Nimbus Strike, activate Golden Staff to shred the bonus armor from his Quickdraw, and unleash Cyclone. If he manages to escape with a defensive Smoke Screen, simply back off into the bushes to drop minion aggro and wait for your cooldowns to cycle back.
laneImpact: Because New Destiny constantly pushes the minion wave toward you, you can easily set up a freeze near your turret. Graves cannot safely step up to harass you with basic attacks under your tower without risking drawing aggro. This pressure forces him to waste Quickdraw defensively, leaving him completely vulnerable to a dive or a deep freeze that deprives him of gold and experience throughout the early levels.
why: You dominate Graves because your Warrior Trickster decoy completely nullifies his main burst tool, End of the Line. When he fires his powder shell towards a wall, you can drop your clone to absorb both the initial hit and the explosive return damage. With his primary damage wasted on a dummy and his New Destiny ammo depleted after two quick shots, Graves is left completely defenseless against your physical counter-assault.

summary: Lissandra can self-cast Frozen Tomb to completely negate Annie's Summon: Tibbers burst, turning the lane into a farm-heavy scaling match.
howToPlay: To navigate this gridlock, never commit your full combo while her ultimate is off cooldown. Instead, sit on your Pyromania stun charges to deter her from engaging. If she initiates with Glacial Path, immediately pop Molten Shield to mitigate the incoming magic damage and reposition. Only unleash Summon: Tibbers after she has been forced to burn her defensive cooldown, or when your jungler can chain crowd control before she can react.
laneImpact: This defensive interaction shuts down solo kill pressure once ultimates are unlocked. Because you cannot reliably burst her down, the lane transitions into a pure farming lane. Lissandra will constantly shove you in using Ice Shard, forcing you to rely on Disintegrate to safely secure last hits under your turret, reducing the lane to a quiet scaling match where neither midlaner can easily force the other out.
why: This matchup is a direct clash of lockdown tools where ultimate abilities cancel each other out. While you hold the threatening stun from Pyromania, Lissandra has the perfect answer to survive your burst. The moment you cast Summon: Tibbers, she can instantly self-cast Frozen Tomb to become untargetable, entirely absorbing your initial burst and leaving you with an empty summon in a neutralised trade.

summary: Poppy's Steadfast Presence blocks both Hecarim's Devastating Charge and Onslaught of Shadows, grounding him and leaving him highly vulnerable.
howToPlay: Never cast Steadfast Presence preemptively just for the movement speed. Keep it strictly as a reactive tool for when Hecarim charges with Devastating Charge or leaps with Onslaught of Shadows. Position yourself between Hecarim and your vulnerable carries. Once you successfully ground him, immediately follow up with Heroic Charge to pin him against the nearest jungle wall, then smash him with Hammer Shock to shred his health while he cannot escape.
laneImpact: In the jungle, this interaction makes Hecarim's gank routes highly predictable and easily countered. If you shadow his pathing, any counter-gank becomes a death sentence for him, as he cannot safely dive your laners without getting stopped. During fights around neutral objectives, your presence alone forces him to delay his ultimate, Onslaught of Shadows, rendering his team's initiation awkward and allowing you to control the river's choke points effortlessly.
why: Poppy completely shuts down Hecarim's high-speed identity because of a single ability: Steadfast Presence. When Hecarim attempts to engage or escape using the movement speed of Devastating Charge or the leap from Onslaught of Shadows, your active barrier stops him dead in his tracks. This blocks his momentum-based damage from Warpath, grounds him, and deprives him of his crowd control, turning his primary engage tools into easy setups for your team.

summary: Poppy's barrier blocks Urgot's Disdain dash, leaving him grounded and unable to trigger his Echoing Flames behind her.
howToPlay: Keep your finger hovering over Steadfast Presence and never use it reactively for the movement speed alone; save it strictly to react to the startup animation of his Disdain. If he hesitates to dash, use the ranged buckler from Iron Ambassador to chip away his shield, then aim your Heroic Charge to slam him into the alcove or turret walls. If you accidentally misstime your barrier, immediately disengage with Hammer Shock to slow his Purge pursuit.
laneImpact: This denial completely shifts the trading dynamics in your favor. Urgot cannot safely zone you with Purge or walk past your wave, as failing a Disdain flip leaves him extremely vulnerable to a counter-engage. You can force him to farm from a distance using Corrosive Charge, securing easy wave priority. This allows you to constantly threaten him with wall stuns near his own turret.
why: Poppy completely shuts down Urgot's primary engage tool. Whenever Urgot winds up Disdain to flip you, activating Steadfast Presence cancels his dash mid-air. This leaves him grounded and completely unable to reposition behind you to trigger the devastating shotgun blasts from his passive Echoing Flames. Because his primary trade starter is neutralized, he loses his main source of burst damage.

summary: Caitlyn must avoid standing directly behind low-health minions to prevent Miss Fortune from landing critical Double Up bounces.
howToPlay: To win this positioning battle, constantly maintain your Strut passive to dodge her Piltover Peacemaker skillshots. Watch your own minion health bars like a hawk; the moment a caster minion is one hit from dying, align yourself to fire Double Up. If she plays defensively and avoids the bounce angle, use Make It Rain to slow her down and reposition. Never channel Bullet Time while her 90 Caliber Net is available to easily escape.
laneImpact: The wave dynamic shifts constantly based on who lands their primary poke. If Caitlyn successfully avoids your minion line, she can push you under tower and deploy Yordle Snap Trap to restrict your movement. However, landing a single critical Double Up heavily chunks her health pool, instantly stopping her aggression and forcing her to play safely, which neutralizes her siege potential and secures you priority.
why: This lane is a pure test of spacing and micro-positioning. Caitlyn aims to abuse her superior basic attack range and clear waves with Piltover Peacemaker, but she is highly vulnerable to Double Up. If she stands directly behind a low-health minion to secure a last hit, Miss Fortune can instantly punish her with a critical bounce. This threat keeps Caitlyn from freely zoning you despite her range advantage.

summary: Galio can counter Twisted Fate's Destiny (R) roams by using Hero's Entrance (R) to join the same skirmish and turn the tide.
howToPlay: To execute this lane perfectly, keep your eyes on the minimap as soon as Twisted Fate reaches level five. Never waste Hero's Entrance for raw skirmishing in your own lane; reserve it exclusively to counter his Destiny activations. When he locks a gold card with Pick a Card to set up a gank on you, reactively charge Shield of Durand to absorb the burst and reduce the stun's impact, then disengage with Justice Punch if his jungler is nearby.
laneImpact: Since Twisted Fate cannot easily kill you due to your magic shield, he will try to shove waves using Wild Cards and red cards from Pick a Card to secure recall windows. You must match this push with Winds of War and Colossal Smash to keep him pinned. If he attempts to step up to harass you with Stacked Deck active, you can punish him instantly by closing the gap.
why: Twisted Fate relies on unlocking global pressure with Destiny to snowball his sidelanes, but Galio is his perfect natural predator. Because your Hero's Entrance matches his semi-global range, you can immediately follow his teleportation.
