Furthermore, your innate magic damage mitigation from Shield of Durand makes you highly resilient against his Pick a Card and Wild Cards poke, allowing you to survive his lane harass and mirror his map movements effortlessly.

summary: Vayne can use Condemn to knock Jax away when he uses Leap Strike, preventing him from landing his Counter Strike stun.
howToPlay: Your entire lane survival relies on exploiting the long cooldown of Condemn. Never engage with Leap Strike while her knockback is available. Instead, bait her into mispositioning by using the brush to drop minion aggro. If she ever wastes her defensive tool, you have a massive window to aggressively jump in, combining Empower and Counter Strike to force a trade.
laneImpact: You will spend most of the early game trapped under your own turret, forced to forfeit minions to preserve your health bar. Attempting to trade is incredibly punishing; if she holds her knockback, you will take massive damage before you can ever retreat. This pressure limits your map presence, locking you in top lane.
why: This matchup is dictated by Vayne's ability to counter your primary gap-closer. Whenever you initiate with Leap Strike, Vayne can immediately react with Condemn to knock you back mid-air. This completely denies your Counter Strike stun setup. Without landing your stun, you are left stranded, exposed to her relentless Silver Bolts procs and Tumble spacing.

summary: Ahri must hold her Charm to interrupt Aurora's dash or catch her immediately as she exits Across the Veil.
howToPlay: Never throw Charm proactively when Aurora has Across the Veil available. Instead, clear waves with Orb of Deception and Fox-Fire, keeping your distance to avoid Twofold Hex. When Aurora jumps forward using her stealth, track her trajectory and launch Charm exactly where she exits Across the Veil. If she traps you with Between Worlds, use Spirit Rush to dash safely within the zone's boundaries, dodging her return damage until the arena fades.
laneImpact: Trades are short and incredibly fast-paced, meaning both midlaners constantly struggle to secure clean wave priority. Aurora uses The Weirding to shove and back away, while Ahri uses Orb of Deception to match the clear. If Aurora triggers her passive healing, Ahri must rely on Essence Theft to sustain. Health pools fluctuate rapidly, meaning a single mistimed trade forces an early recall, leaving the remaining midlaner free to pressure the tower.
why: This matchup is a high-speed duel where Ahri's Spirit Rush directly matches Aurora's slippery evasiveness. Neither can easily pin the other down because both rely on quick repositioning to land skillshots. While Aurora tries to trigger Spirit Abjuration using Twofold Hex and her stealth from Across the Veil, Ahri relies on Orb of Deception to trade back. The lane remains perfectly even, decided entirely by who misuses their movement tools first.

summary: You can reveal Talon during his Shadow Assault invisibility if you manage to hit him with Crescent Strike beforehand.
howToPlay: Do not blindly throw Crescent Strike to poke; instead, save it for when Talon steps up to Rake the wave. If he initiates with Shadow Assault, instantly tag him with Crescent Strike to keep him visible, then follow up with Lunar Rush and Moonfall to lock him down. If he attempts to escape over a wall using Assassin's Path, use your wave priority to immediately track his movement through the river, matching his rotations before he can ambush your side lanes.
laneImpact: This matchup turns into a high-speed roaming contest. You must exploit your superior wave clear to lock Talon under his turret, neutralizing his ability to search for flanks with Assassin's Path. By keeping the lane pushed, you force him to choose between losing crucial farm or letting you move first to secure map priority, ultimately starving him of the early skirmish kills he desperately needs to snowball.
why: Diana dictates this matchup because Crescent Strike completely neutralizes Talon's primary escape and burst tool, Shadow Assault. By marking him with Moonlight, you reveal his position even during his ultimate's invisibility, stripping away his element of surprise. Furthermore, Pale Cascade acts as a perfect shield buffer against his initial Noxian Diplomacy and Rake burst, allowing Moonsilver Blade's sustained magic damage to easily win any extended melee trade.

summary: Corki's Valkyrie allows him to match Ezreal's Arcane Shift safety, turning the lane into a pure skillshot battle between Missile Barrage and Mystic Shot.
howToPlay: To win this war of attrition, always position yourself diagonally behind your minion wave. This shield blocks his Mystic Shot while letting you lob Phosphorus Bomb over the frontline. Never initiate with Valkyrie unless his Arcane Shift is on cooldown and you have Special Delivery ready to block his path. If you drop low on health, play passively with Missile Barrage to secure farm from maximum range rather than risking a close-quarters duel.
laneImpact: With both marksmen boasting reliable escape tools, the wave remains highly dynamic but rarely crashes hard. You cannot easily dive Ezreal, and he cannot lock you down. Trades are decided incrementally by how many Mystic Shot bolts you block with minions while squeezing in your own Phosphorus Bomb and Gatling Gun shred. This constant micro-trading keeps both of you in lane, delaying decisive map rotations.
why: This matchup is a mirror of hyper-mobile poke champions where neither can easily pin the other down. Because Valkyrie instantly matches the defensive utility of Ezreal's Arcane Shift, raw engage is off the table. Instead, the lane devolves into a constant barrage of skillshots, pitting Corki's long-range Missile Barrage directly against Ezreal's Mystic Shot in a battle of pure aim and reaction speed.

summary: Using Spell Shield to block the initial application of Tristana's Explosive Charge completely shuts down her trading and all-in potential.
howToPlay: To win this mental war, you must bait out Spell Shield before committing your primary cooldowns. Walk forward with Rapid Fire active to threaten auto-attacks, but hold your Explosive Charge. Often, Sivir will panic-shield anticipating the bomb. If she does, disengage immediately, wait out the brief shield duration, and then use Rocket Jump to engage during her long cooldown window. Never initiate with Rocket Jump while her defensive shield is ready.
laneImpact: Sivir will relentlessly push the wave using Ricochet and Boomerang Blade, forcing you to farm under turret. Because you cannot safely threaten an all-in with Rocket Jump while her Spell Shield is active, you lose all lane priority. Any attempt to force a trade results in Sivir absorbing your damage, healing herself, and using Fleet of Foot to safely disengage while your support is left unable to follow up.
why: This lane is heavily dictated by how Sivir uses her Spell Shield. If she reacts quickly enough to absorb the initial cast of your Explosive Charge, your entire trading pattern collapses. Not only do you lose your primary source of burst damage, but you also forfeit the ability to reset Rocket Jump. Without that explosive threat, Sivir can easily out-damage you over longer trades with Ricochet and Boomerang Blade.

summary: Brand can easily poke Ryze with Pillar of Flame whenever Ryze steps up to spread Spell Flux on the minion wave.
howToPlay: Stand just out of range of his Rune Prison and watch your own low-health minions. The moment Ryze steps forward to cast Spell Flux, immediately place Pillar of Flame where he stands. If he gets aggressive and tries to close the gap, hit him with Sear to trigger the stun on your pre-existing Blaze stacks, then follow up with Conflagration and Pyroclasm if he tries to fight back inside his own minion wave.
laneImpact: This dynamic gives you total control over the wave state. Ryze cannot safely match your wave clear without eating constant poke, forcing him to farm under tower where his Overload resets are harder to use for trades. By keeping him pressured and low on health, you delay his scaling from Arcane Mastery and prevent him from using Realm Warp to impact other lanes, keeping him trapped in mid.
why: Ryze must get relatively close to the minion wave to mark it with Spell Flux before spreading his damage. Since his range is limited, this predictable movement gives you a massive window to drop Pillar of Flame directly on him. Because Ryze lacks mobility spells to dodge, he has to choose between taking heavy damage or giving up his wave clear, allowing your passive Blaze to easily chip away his health.

summary: Rumble's Flamespitter deals continuous area-of-effect magic damage that completely bypasses Yasuo's Wind Wall, forcing Yasuo to play defensively.
howToPlay: To maximize your advantage, maintain your Heat above 50 to empower your abilities through Junkyard Titan before trading. When Yasuo approaches the wave, activate Flamespitter and walk directly at him. If he tries to fight back, use Scrap Shield to absorb his Steel Tempest damage. Keep Electro Harpoon ready for when he tries to escape with Sweeping Blade, and drop The Equalizer directly along his retreat path to punish his defensive positioning.
laneImpact: Because Yasuo cannot block your main damage, he is forced to play defensively near his turret. You can easily maintain constant wave pressure by pushing him under tower with Flamespitter. This neutralizes his Sweeping Blade mobility, as he has fewer minions to dash through. It also prevents him from safely stacking Steel Tempest to threaten you with knockups, giving you absolute priority over the lane and early vision control.
why: This lane is entirely dictated by how Flamespitter interacts with Yasuo's defensive options. Since Flamespitter is a continuous, non-projectile cone of magic damage, Yasuo's Wind Wall is completely useless against it. This allows you to constantly melt his Way of the Wanderer shield and shred his health bar without him being able to block your primary damage source, turning every extended trade into an easy victory for you.

summary: Volibear's Thundering Smash is easily countered by placing a turret in his path and hitting him with CH-2 Electron Storm Grenade to stop his run.
howToPlay: Never throw your CH-2 Electron Storm Grenade proactively. Always hold it until Volibear commits to his Thundering Smash sprint. Position your H-28G Evolution Turret units in a triangular defensive grid slightly behind your caster minions, forcing him to run through their fire. If he attempts to dive you using Stormbringer, immediately cast UPGRADE!!! combined with H-28G Evolution Turret to drop an apex turret, then kite within your Hextech Affinity zone to out-damage his ultimate form.
laneImpact: This dynamic allows you to dictate the wave's position effortlessly. Since Volibear cannot approach without eating a CH-2 Electron Storm Grenade, you can slow-push massive waves using H-28G Evolution Turret. He is forced to farm under tower, exposing himself to poke from Hextech Micro-Rockets. Even if he tries to use Sky Splitter to shield himself or Stormbringer to disable your turrets, your range advantage and zoning power keep him trapped and bleeding health.
why: Volibear relies entirely on running you down with Thundering Smash to initiate trades. However, his linear approach play is completely neutralized by your H-28G Evolution Turret setup. When he charges, his predictable movement makes him an incredibly easy target for your CH-2 Electron Storm Grenade. Stunning him mid-sprint not only wastes his main mobility tool but triggers your turret lasers, turning his aggressive engage into massive self-inflicted damage.

howToPlay: Positioning: keep your range, but don’t give free dash angles by standing too close to the wave. The more you force awkward lunges, the more you can punish; the more you allow clean lunges, the more you expose yourself. Key timing: track parry and item spikes — that’s where the matchup flips. When parry is up, avoid obvious commits; when it’s down, take more aggressive pressure windows. Decision-making: if she wants to side, prepare an exchange plan. Instead of chasing every wave, coordinate cross-map value: objective, rotation, deep vision. The goal is to make her split not free, even if you don’t kill her.
laneImpact: In lane you can get prio, but any spacing mistake gives her a clean entry into an extended trade — and extended trades favor her. Once she hits an item, she becomes stable: sustain, lane hold, tower threat. That pressures you: either accelerate fast with plates, or accept the game will shift toward side control. Mid/late, her side presence becomes a magnet: someone must answer or structures fall. Answering as Tristana top often forces you into more defensive play than you want.
why: Fiora is unfavorable because she’s the side-duel archetype: even if you harass her, she can hold and later force you to answer. Tristana top, despite range, doesn’t like being assigned into a scaling duelist 1v1. She also has tools to disrupt your simple plan. Her dash grants access, parry can flip situations if you commit poorly, and true damage makes defensive stats less meaningful if you try to tank through. You can slow her down, but the reality is: if the game becomes pure side-lane chess, Fiora usually plays that game better than you.

summary: Xin Zhao's Crescent Guard blocks Ekko's Timewinder damage from outside the arena, making it hard for Ekko to proc Z-Drive Resonance.
howToPlay: To execute this flawlessly, do not initiate with Crescent Guard. Instead, wait for Ekko to commit with Phase Dive and launch Timewinder. The moment he does, activate Crescent Guard and use Audacious Charge to stick to him inside your arena, forcing him to fight in close quarters where Three Talon Strike will knock him up. If he tries to escape or turn the fight with Chronobreak, track his echo to avoid his ultimate's massive burst.
laneImpact: This interaction strips Ekko of his early skirmishing power, forcing him to concede crab priority and avoid direct jungle duels. Since he cannot safely proc Z-Drive Resonance while your ultimate is ready, Ekko must rely on Phase Dive defensively rather than using it to invade. This allows you to invade his camps aggressively, secure double scuttle crabs, and apply immense pressure on his lanes while he falls behind.
why: Xin Zhao dominates this jungle matchup because Crescent Guard completely neutralizes Ekko's primary burst tool. When Ekko attempts to set up his three-hit passive, Z-Drive Resonance, he relies heavily on the return stroke of Timewinder. By activating Crescent Guard, you block all damage from the returning projectile if Ekko is outside your arena, preventing him from securing his crucial third stack and the massive movement speed burst that follows.

howToPlay: Don’t give clean duels: keep trades short, use the wave to reduce vital angles, and reset instead of extending. Key timing: if you don’t have a kill window before she scales, shift to macro—push, reset, and show up for Herald/dragon rather than bleeding in side lane. Concrete decision: if Fiora splits and your team can force 5v4, prioritize objective acceleration over endless mirroring.
laneImpact: In lane, you can sometimes survive early levels, but once Fiora has an item and some XP, every neutral trade becomes bad. She can pin you in side lane lane and deny you from converting your scaling into objective presence. Even without dying, you can lose wave control and play permanently in reaction.
why: Fiora is a hard counter because she turns your main strength—long melee fights—into a weakness. Shyvana wins by stacking stats and grinding opponents down with sustained DPS. Fiora loves that pace: the longer the duel, the more vitals + true damage make your HP/armor less meaningful, and she has the mobility to choose when and where the exchange happens.

summary: While Nautilus can easily lock Brand down with Depth Charge, Brand's % max health burn from Blaze melts Nautilus if the engage is turned around.
howToPlay: Play behind the wave without lining up beside your carry, so Dredge Line cannot create two easy targets. Keep Sear until Blaze is applied and Nautilus walks forward; the stun should interrupt his pursuit, not provide casual poke. After a missed anchor, use Pillar of Flame and leave before Depth Charge can start another sequence.
laneImpact: The anchor threat reduces your poke angles and forces you to keep minions between Nautilus and yourself. One catch can cost enough health to surrender the wave and then brush control. Titan's Wrath also lets him absorb part of your first damage sequence.
why: Dredge Line brings Nautilus and Brand together, then Staggering Blow and Depth Charge extend the lockdown. Brand needs to ignite a target before Sear can stun it; when crowd control starts the exchange, he lacks the time required to sequence Blaze, Sear, and Pillar of Flame.

summary: While Rumble's magic damage is mitigated by Galio's Shield of Durand (W), Galio must avoid extended trades when Rumble overheats.
howToPlay: Always hold Shield of Durand until Rumble commits to his flames. When his heat bar approaches maximum, back away immediately to deny him overheated melee attacks, using Justice Punch backwards if necessary to escape his range. If you get chunked, focus on farming safely from a distance using Winds of War and prepare your Hero's Entrance to impact the side lanes rather than trying to force a solo kill against his high sustained damage.
laneImpact: The lane devolves into a war of attrition. You cannot easily shove Rumble under tower because his flame waves match your Winds of War and Colossal Smash clear. Short, sharp trades using Justice Punch to initiate and Shield of Durand to disengage keep your health bars even. If you misstime your engage and get caught by his overheated basic attacks, you lose priority and are forced into an early recall.
why: This matchup is a balancing act between magical mitigation and raw sustained damage. Your Shield of Durand passively absorbs Rumble's continuous flame spouts, neutralizing his primary magic poke. However, if you linger after your initial burst, Rumble's overheat state grants him empowered physical attacks that easily bypass your magic shield. It is a battle of cooldowns where you must trade only when your defensive shield is ready.

summary: Caitlyn must use her range to poke Yunara before she can activate Transcend One's Self, using 90 Caliber Net to disengage if Yunara dashes forward with Kanmei's Steps.
howToPlay: To survive this unfavorable matchup, always hold your 90 Caliber Net for her engage. The moment Yunara activates Kanmei's Steps to close the distance, fire your net to slide backward and trigger a guaranteed Headshot. Never commit to extended trades; instead, drop Yordle Snap Trap in her path to restrict her movement, and use Ace in the Hole from maximum distance only when she is low enough to be forced back.
laneImpact: This matchup revolves around a brutal spacing battle. You cannot afford to let Yunara push you under tower, as her bouncing attacks from Cultivation of Spirit will make farming painful. If she manages to keep her health high until she unlocks her ultimate, she will force you out of lane with aggressive forward dashes, ruin your recall timings, and rob you of your early plate-taking pressure.
why: Yunara's scaling hybrid damage from Vow of the First Lands makes her a dual-threat, but her real power lies in her ultimate Transcend One's Self, which amplifies her mobility and damage. Caitlyn's superior base range is her only shield here. You must abuse your auto-attacks and Piltover Peacemaker to chip away her health before she enters her trance, otherwise her combat stats will quickly overwhelm your traditional marksman kit.

summary: Yunara's high mixed damage from Cultivation of Spirit and safety from Kanmei's Steps makes it difficult for Akshan to find clean all-in angles without support setup.
howToPlay: To survive, prioritize holding the minion wave just outside your tower range. Never initiate with Heroic Swing unless your support lands hard crowd control to lock her down before she can use Kanmei's Steps. If she activates Transcend One's Self, immediately retreat and use Avengerang from maximum distance to clear the wave. If you get shoved in, cancel her backs with Comeuppance rather than forcing a dangerous roam.
laneImpact: Because Yunara's Cultivation of Spirit bounces attacks through the wave, she naturally pushes you under tower while poking you down. You cannot easily match her clear with Avengerang without exposing yourself to her Arc of Judgment / Arc of Ruin slow. This permanent pressure forces you into defensive wave management, limiting your opportunities to roam with Going Rogue.
why: Yunara outscales you heavily due to Vow of the First Lands converting critical strikes into magic damage, but the immediate threat is her trading power. When she activates Cultivation of Spirit, her mixed damage shreds your Dirty Fighting shield instantly. Attempting to punish her with Heroic Swing is highly risky because she can easily disengage or reposition using Kanmei's Steps, leaving you without a clean angle to commit.

summary: Aurora's slippery Across the Veil is completely neutralized by Annie's point-and-click Disintegrate stun.
howToPlay: Always hold your Pyromania stun at three charges, ready to instantly activate Molten Shield to bait Aurora into approaching. If she attempts to escape or engage with Across the Veil, lock her down with Disintegrate followed by an immediate Incinerate. If she retreats into Between Worlds, do not blindly chase her; instead, summon Summon: Tibbers directly on her predictable teleportation path to crush her health bar while she is trapped inside her own zone.
laneImpact: This interaction strips Aurora of her safety, forcing her to play passively behind her minions. She cannot safely step up to use Twofold Hex or trigger Spirit Abjuration without risking a lethal stun. You command complete control over the wave pace. When she wastes her cooldowns, you can shove her under turret or freeze the lane, starving her of gold and preventing her from roaming to side lanes.
why: Aurora relies heavily on the brief invisibility and dash of Across the Veil to safely trade and escape. However, Annie completely shuts down this slippery defensive option. Because Disintegrate is a point-and-click projectile, priming your Pyromania stun guarantees a lock-on hit that intercepts her mid-dash. Aurora cannot phase out or dodge your burst once Disintegrate is in flight, turning her main defensive tool into a useless spell.

summary: Poppy can block Kennen's E (Lightning Rush) dash with her barrier, making positioning near walls extremely dangerous if she attempts to tackle him.
howToPlay: Stand constantly between the minion wave and the river wall, baiting him to use Lightning Rush offensively or defensively. Never initiate with Heroic Charge unless his movement speed buff is already down, or you have activated Steadfast Presence to catch his dash mid-air. If he manages to poke you low with Electrical Surge passive stacks, use Iron Ambassador to grab a shield, absorb his burst, and safely disengage.
laneImpact: Because of this threat, Kennen cannot freely use his range to freeze you out. If he steps close to the side alcoves or walls to land Thundering Shuriken, he risks getting pinned. You will give up some early minion gold under tower, but the moment the wave bounces, the threat of your block-into-stun combo forces him to retreat, preventing him from building a massive, uncontested farm lead.
why: This matchup revolves entirely around how you handle Kennen's lightning-fast escape. While he tries to harass you with ranged attacks, his only safety net when overextending is Lightning Rush. By activating Steadfast Presence, you completely nullify his sprint, grounding him. This shutdown leaves him incredibly vulnerable to a swift Heroic Charge into the nearest wall, turning his main defensive tool into a death trap.

summary: Poppy's Steadfast Presence blocks Pantheon's Shield Vault dash, grounding him and preventing his primary engage and stun.
howToPlay: Never waste Steadfast Presence to clear jungle camps; always hold it until Pantheon commits to his Shield Vault. Position yourself directly between Pantheon and your vulnerable laners during skirmishes. If he channels Grand Starfall to join a fight, position yourself near his landing indicator to immediately interrupt his follow-up engage, or charge him into nearby walls with Heroic Charge to lock him down before he can block damage with Aegis Assault.
laneImpact: Because Pantheon cannot reliably execute his point-and-click stun near you, his early gank pressure and river skirmishing are neutered. You dominate fights around crabs and objectives. If he attempts to escape or turn a fight with Aegis Assault, your superior positioning allows you to walk behind him, rendering his shield useless while denying his team any priority in the river.
why: This jungle matchup is heavily in your favor because your Steadfast Presence completely neutralizes Pantheon's primary initiation tool. When Pantheon attempts to jump on you or your allies with Shield Vault, activating your defensive field stops him mid-air, grounding him and preventing the stun. This leaves him vulnerable without his main burst setup, while you can easily retaliate with Hammer Shock to shred his health.

summary: Gragas can use Body Slam to completely stop Hecarim's Devastating Charge momentum and cancel his engage.
howToPlay: To bypass this, never lead your ganks with Devastating Charge if Gragas is holding Body Slam. Instead, initiate with Onslaught of Shadows, which grants you unstoppable frames to bypass his collision entirely and fear him. Once he panics and wastes Body Slam, immediately activate Devastating Charge to run him down or reposition. Always activate Spirit of Dread during his Drunken Rage window to heal back his initial burst while stacking Rampage.
laneImpact: This interaction severely limits your early jungle skirmishing and objective contesting. Whenever you attempt to secure Scuttle Crabs or counter-gank, Gragas can effortlessly peel you off his allies or himself. It forces you into slow, passive clears, as forcing a fight often results in you eating a Barrel Roll slow and Drunken Rage slam after your initial charge is interrupted, turning potential double-kills into retreats.
why: Gragas completely stifles your primary initiation tool because Body Slam directly interrupts Devastating Charge mid-dash. When you gallop in, a well-timed Body Slam halts your momentum entirely, leaving you stranded in melee range without the displacement or the maximum Warpath attack damage bonus. This direct collision priority means Gragas can consistently deny your gank setups and skirmish entry.

summary: Yasuo's Wind Wall can completely block Annie's Disintegrate projectile, wasting her Pyromania stun if she doesn't bait it out first.
howToPlay: To survive, you must bait his Wind Wall using basic attacks before committing your stun. Keep Pyromania at three charges, then activate Molten Shield mid-fight to instantly prime the stun, catching him off guard. If he blocks your initial burst, immediately disengage with Molten Shield's movement speed to escape his Sweeping Blade and Last Breath combo. Rely on the instant cone of Incinerate or the massive AoE of Summon: Tibbers to bypass his wall entirely.
laneImpact: This dynamic ruins your ability to contest waves safely. Yasuo can use Sweeping Blade to dash through your minions, trigger Way of the Wanderer's shield to absorb minor damage, and threaten you with Steel Tempest. Since you cannot reliably stun him through his barrier, you must yield priority, farming under tower using Disintegrate's mana refund while he secures roam timings or pressures your mid-lane tower.
why: Yasuo holds a massive lane advantage because his Wind Wall can dissolve Annie's Disintegrate mid-air. When you have Pyromania fully charged, throwing your single-target projectile into his barrier not only nullifies your damage but completely consumes your passive stun without triggering its effects. This projectile-blocking threat forces you into a passive stance, allowing him to play aggressively knowing your primary self-defense tool can be erased on reaction.

summary: Poppy can block Lillia's Watch Out! Eep! dash with Steadfast Presence, but cannot stop Lillia's raw movement speed from Blooming Blows.
howToPlay: Never initiate with Heroic Charge unless Lillia is already positioned directly next to a wall. Instead, hold Steadfast Presence exclusively for the moment she winds up Watch Out! Eep! to deny her burst damage. When she has maximum stacks of Blooming Blows, back off and use Iron Ambassador to safely poke or farm. If she hits you with Swirlseed, immediately look to disengage using Keeper's Verdict to prevent her from capitalizing on Lilting Lullaby.
laneImpact: In early skirmishes, this creates a tense dance around neutral camps. If Lillia stacks Blooming Blows on monsters, she can weave in and out, baiting your abilities. Missing your Heroic Charge against a fast-moving Lillia leaves you vulnerable to a counter-engage with Lilting Lullaby. Neither jungler can easily invade the other without risking a prolonged, costly chase that pulls laners away from their lanes.
why: This jungle matchup hinges entirely on movement mechanics. While Poppy's Steadfast Presence is the perfect counter to interrupt the leap from Lillia's Watch Out! Eep!, grounding her mid-air, it does absolutely nothing to slow her down once she builds momentum. Lillia's passive speed from Blooming Blows allows her to easily kite around Poppy's melee range, completely bypassing your defensive aura without needing to dash.

summary: Poppy's Steadfast Presence (W) grounds and interrupts Yone's Mortal Steel (Q3) dash, completely neutralizing his primary engage and trading tool.
howToPlay: Stand constantly near the lane walls to threaten a Heroic Charge stun whenever Yone uses Soul Unbound. Never waste Steadfast Presence preemptively; hold it specifically for when his Mortal Steel wind charge is active and he moves forward. If he attempts to escape or engage with Fate Sealed, use a quick-cast tap of your own Keeper's Verdict to instantly knock him airborne and cancel his channel before he can slide away.
laneImpact: Because you can consistently shut down his Mortal Steel dashes, Yone cannot freely use Soul Unbound to harass you under your tower. You command the wave's position, forcing him to farm with his shorter range or bleed health. If he mispositions near the alcove or walls while trying to land Spirit Cleave, you can easily punish him, taking complete control of the lane's physical space.
why: This favorable matchup revolves entirely around denying Yone's mobility. Yone relies heavily on his third cast of Mortal Steel to initiate trades or escape. By activating Steadfast Presence the moment he launches his Q3 tornado dash, you ground him mid-air, blocking his knock-up and leaving him vulnerable to a swift Hammer Shock retaliation. His primary tool for aggressive trading becomes his biggest liability.

summary: Aurora can easily dodge Brand's Pillar of Flame (W) using Across the Veil (W) and counter-engage.
howToPlay: Walk aggressively to bait his Pillar of Flame. The moment you see his casting animation, activate Across the Veil to dodge sideways, then instantly close the gap with Twofold Hex. Follow up with The Weirding to slow him, triggering Spirit Abjuration for a quick burst and heal. If you accidentally get hit by his fire, immediately weave behind your minions to block his Sear and prevent any follow-up stun.
laneImpact: Your mobility advantage completely paralyzes Brand's wave clear. Every time he approaches the minion wave to cast Pillar of Flame, he risks getting countered. This constant pressure forces him to choose between losing farm under his turret or taking heavy trades. Once you unlock Between Worlds, his lack of mobility makes him an incredibly easy target for a dive or a clean solo kill.
why: This lane is highly favorable because Brand's entire threat relies on hitting Pillar of Flame to set up his passive damage. By using Across the Veil, you can reactively leap out of his ground-targeted circle, rendering his main damage tool useless. Without this setup, Brand cannot easily land Sear to stun you, leaving him completely exposed to a rapid counter-burst from Twofold Hex.

summary: Kassadin's magic damage shield from Null Sphere is useless against the true damage of Festin, and his early waveclear cannot match Cho'Gath's.
howToPlay: Shove the first three waves aggressively using Vorpal Spikes to force Kassadin under his tower. If he attempts to trade, silence him with Feral Scream to block his Riftwalk escape, then land Rupture right under his feet. When his health drops below the threshold, ignore his Null Sphere magic shield entirely and execute him directly with Feast. If the enemy jungler camps you, freeze the wave near your turret to deny him farm safely.
laneImpact: You establish absolute wave control early. Kassadin's slow clear forces him under turret, where he must use Nether Blade to last-hit. This constant pressure prevents him from roaming or stacking Force Pulse effectively. You can easily crash large waves to secure deep vision or take free recalls, while his lack of early damage means he cannot threaten your high health pool, which is constantly replenished by Carnivore.
why: This lane heavily favors you because Kassadin's defensive tools fail against your ultimate. While his Void Stone and Null Sphere generate magic shields to absorb ability damage, they are completely bypassed by the true damage of Feast. Furthermore, his weak early game and lack of AoE mean he cannot compete with your wave pressure using Rupture and Vorpal Spikes, allowing you to dictate the lane's pace from level one.

summary: Orianna's Command: Attack allows her to match Corki's poke, making the lane a pure test of dodging and wave management.
howToPlay: Always position yourself diagonally relative to Orianna's sphere to force her into wider, more predictable Command: Attack angles. Save Valkyrie strictly to escape her ultimate, Command: Shockwave, rather than using it offensively. Once you unlock Missile Barrage, use the Big One to secure ranged minions and poke her simultaneously. If she shields herself with Command: Protect, immediately back off and wait out the defensive buff before throwing another Phosphorus Bomb.
laneImpact: The lane constantly fluctuates based on who secures wave priority. If you get pushed under turret by Command: Attack and Command: Dissonance, you will struggle to retaliate with Phosphorus Bomb while farming. Conversely, overextending to trade invites Orianna to punish you with Command: Protect's shield. Health bars will deplete fast, meaning recall timings are dictated by who runs out of mana first or gets poked out of lane.
why: This matchup is a pure battle of attrition fought at maximum range. Orianna utilizes Command: Attack to constantly reposition her sphere and match the threat of your Phosphorus Bomb. Because both of you possess efficient, low-cooldown ranged tools to chip away at each other's health bars, neither champion can easily force a decisive all-in without first gaining a significant health advantage through superior spacing and skillshot accuracy.

summary: Sivir can reactively block Enchanted Crystal Arrow with Spell Shield, gaining mana and completely neutralizing your primary playmaking tool.
howToPlay: To break this deadlock, you must bait out her Spell Shield before launching your ultimate. Fire Volley at medium range to force her defensive reaction, as she might panic-shield the slow. Keep a close eye on her cooldowns; once her shield is down, you have a brief window to strike. Additionally, stack Ranger's Focus on the wave first, so you can quickly win the extended physical trade with basic attacks if she steps up too aggressively without her defensive spell.
laneImpact: Sivir easily dictates the tempo of the lane by pushing continuously with Boomerang Blade and Ricochet. Normally, you would punish such aggressive pushing by locking her down with Enchanted Crystal Arrow under your turret, but her Spell Shield makes this extremely risky. This safety allows her to keep you pinned under tower, chipping away at your health and forcing you into defensive farm cycles without any real threat of a counter-engage.
why: The matchup revolves entirely around how Sivir manages her Spell Shield. Your primary tool for initiating fights and securing kills is Enchanted Crystal Arrow, but she can easily react to its flight path, block the projectile, and heal herself. Because this interaction is heavily skewed in her favor, your ultimate ceases to be a reliable threat, and she can freely ignore your pick potential while poking you with Boomerang Blade.

summary: Kindred uses Dance of Arrows to easily dash out of Infernal Chains while kiting you from range.
howToPlay: To survive this matchup, never initiate with Infernal Chains. Instead, force Kindred to use Dance of Arrows first by positioning yourself near terrain where you can threaten them with a short The Darkin Blade coupled with Umbral Dash. Only cast your chains once their dash is on cooldown. If they deploy Lamb's Respite, stop trying to burst them; instead, time your third strike of The Darkin Blade to knock them up and push them out of the healing zone right as the effect expires.
laneImpact: This mobility gap makes jungle skirmishes incredibly dangerous for you. Kindred will aggressively invade your camps to hunt for Mark of the Kindred, knowing you cannot chase them down. If you contest these marks, they will activate Wolf's Frenzy to reduce their dash cooldown and apply Mounting Dread, forcing you to retreat with low health or burn World Ender defensively just to survive their relentless ranged assault.
why: Kindred completely neutralizes your engage tools by using the mobility of Dance of Arrows. Whenever you attempt to lock them down with Infernal Chains, they can instantly dash out of the pull zone while maintaining their distance. This allows them to easily avoid the sweetspots of The Darkin Blade. Because you cannot reliably land your knockups, Kindred can freely kite you with physical damage from a safe range.

summary: Galio can interrupt Rakan's Grand Entrance mid-air with a well-timed Justice Punch, turning the engage around.
howToPlay: Never initiate with Justice Punch unless Rakan's Grand Entrance is on cooldown. Stand slightly behind your ADC to bait Rakan's jump, then reactively dash forward. If he baits your E and dashes back with Battle Dance, immediately activate Shield of Durand to absorb incoming damage from Gleaming Quill. Save Hero's Entrance specifically to match his roam power when he uses The Quickness in river skirmishes.
laneImpact: When Rakan has Grand Entrance available, your duo must play spread out to avoid a double knock-up. A successful interruption allows you to lock him down with Shield of Durand, forcing his ADC to back off. If you waste Justice Punch early, Rakan will immediately initiate with The Quickness and Grand Entrance, securing free health trades and forcing you under tower.
why: This matchup is a pure test of reflexes centered around Rakan's Grand Entrance. Because his dash has a brief travel time, you can cast Justice Punch directly into his path. If your timing is precise, your knock-up overrides his, completely canceling his engage. However, missing this window leaves you vulnerable to a quick Battle Dance escape, making the lane a tense game of chicken.

summary: Nocturne's Shroud of Darkness can block the knockback of Devastating Charge or the fear from Onslaught of Shadows, turning the duel in his favor.
howToPlay: To survive this matchup, never initiate with Devastating Charge directly into him. Instead, run close to him using Spirit of Dread to sustain, and bait out his Shroud of Darkness with a basic attack or Rampage before committing your crowd control. If he initiates with Paranoia on an ally, wait in the wings and use your Onslaught of Shadows to fear him right as he lands, disrupting his Unspeakable Horror link before it triggers.
laneImpact: When Nocturne triggers Paranoia, your standard ganking routes are blinded, preventing you from saving teammates across the map. Because he clears camps quickly with Umbra Blades and wins isolated 1v1s, you cannot easily contest objectives or invade. This map-wide blackout forces your lanes to play defensively, while you must track his movement to turn his aggressive dives into counter-gank opportunities.
why: Nocturne holds a massive advantage in direct duels because his Shroud of Darkness can absorb either the high-impact knockback from your Devastating Charge or the crucial teamfight fear of your Onslaught of Shadows. Losing either crowd control tool strips away your burst damage and positioning control, leaving you highly vulnerable to his Duskbringer trail and the ensuing fear from Unspeakable Horror.

summary: Yuumi's lack of lane presence allows Bard to collect chimes with Traveler's Call without leaving his ADC vulnerable to hard engages.
howToPlay: Watch the wave state and wait until it bounces back toward your side before you utilize Magical Journey to rotate. Before you leave, charge three Caretaker's Shrine nodes behind your shooter. If Yuumi detaches to trigger Bop 'n' Block, immediately look to interrupt her with Cosmic Binding to lock her out of her host. If a fight breaks out while you are returning, use Tempered Fate to freeze the enemy carry, separating them from Yuumi's healing.
laneImpact: This dynamic completely removes the typical risk of leaving your partner alone. You can drop a couple of Caretaker's Shrine packs under your tower, then disappear into the jungle. Your ally won't get dived because the enemy lane cannot tank tower shots or lock them down without Final Chapter. This allows you to secure deep vision while Yuumi remains glued to her partner, wasting her scaling potential.
why: Yuumi relies entirely on You and Me! to attach to her marksman, meaning her lane presence is extremely passive. Since she cannot threaten a hard engage, you can comfortably leave the lane to gather chimes with Traveler's Call. While you collect these, your carry is perfectly safe because Yuumi's only poking tool is Prowling Projectile, which lacks the burst or crowd control to punish a solo target.

summary: Mordekaiser can use Realm of Death to peel Skarner away from teammates, preventing Skarner from dragging an ally with Impale.
howToPlay: To counter this, never initiate with Impale while Mordekaiser has his ultimate available, unless you target Mordekaiser himself. Stand behind your frontline, using Shattered Earth / Upheaval to poke and Seismic Bastion to absorb Obliterate damage. Wait for him to cast Realm of Death on a teammate. Once he enters his realm, quickly use Ixtal's Impact to pin his remaining allies against a wall and secure a free capture.
laneImpact: During objective skirmishes around Epic Monsters, your threat level is severely neutralized. Mordekaiser will hover near his carries, using Death's Grasp to disrupt your approach. If you try to charge in, the constant threat of his Realm of Death forces you to play defensively, as getting isolated means losing your Smite utility and letting his Darkness Rise shred your health bar without any backup.
why: This match-up turns on how Mordekaiser negates your team-fight initiation. When you attempt to execute an aggressive flank with Ixtal's Impact to set up Impale, Mordekaiser can immediately cast Realm of Death on you. This banishes you to his pocket dimension, instantly breaking your tether and pulling you completely away from your allies, leaving your team vulnerable while you are trapped in a deadly duel.

summary: Interrupting her Vault Breaker with a well-timed The Darkin Blade sweetspot prevents her from applying Denting Blows quickly.
howToPlay: When you spot Vi charging Vault Breaker, hold your first cast of The Darkin Blade. Wait for her to release the dash, then react with Umbral Dash to adjust your angle and land the sweetspot directly in her path. If she bypasses your knockup with Cease and Desist, immediately trigger World Ender to match her mobility, use Deathbringer Stance to heal through her initial burst, and drag her back using Infernal Chains.
laneImpact: In the jungle, this interaction dictates who controls river skirmishes and objective pressure. When Vi has Vault Breaker ready, you cannot contest her directly without backup, as her Cease and Desist offers an unstoppable follow-up. If she misses or you cancel her dash, the power dynamic shifts instantly, allowing you to lock her down with Infernal Chains and safely secure camp priority.
why: Vi's jungle dueling relies heavily on landing Vault Breaker to immediately shred your armor and gain attack speed via Denting Blows. As Aatrox, your primary defense is interrupting her mid-dash charge using the knockup from a precise The Darkin Blade sweetspot. If you fail this micro-interaction, she easily triggers Blast Shield and melts you, but stopping her dash completely ruins her burst rotation.

summary: Poppy's Steadfast Presence completely blocks Rengar's Unseen Predator leaps, grounding him and preventing him from accessing targets.
howToPlay: Your main rule is to hover closely around your vulnerable teammates rather than chasing Rengar. Never waste Steadfast Presence to clear camps or start a fight; hold it exclusively for his Unseen Predator leap indicator or when his Thrill of the Hunt mark appears over an ally's head. If he manages to cleanse your crowd control using an empowered Battle Roar, immediately charge up Keeper's Verdict to launch him away and completely reset the fight.
laneImpact: In the jungle, this interaction strips Rengar of his early skirmishing pressure. He cannot safely contest Rift Scuttlers or invade your camps, as any bush-dependent duel turns into an easy stun for you. Your presence during counter-ganks completely invalidates his Thrill of the Hunt engages. By restricting his ability to snowball off isolated targets, you force him into a passive farming style that delays his lethal item power spikes.
why: Rengar's entire assassination pattern relies on jumping from bushes or stealth via Unseen Predator. Poppy completely shuts down this primary tool with Steadfast Presence. Activating this field whenever the Pridestalker attempts a leap immediately knocks him out of the air, grounding him and preventing him from reaching your fragile allies. Without his jump, his burst potential from Savagery is instantly neutralized, leaving him highly vulnerable to your counter-engage.

summary: While Annie can easily burst Twisted Fate in a direct duel, she struggles to match his global map pressure from Destiny.
howToPlay: To win this execution battle, you must play aggressively whenever your Pyromania stun is charged. Use Molten Shield to quickly close the gap and threaten a lethal Summon: Tibbers combo if he locks a blue card. If Twisted Fate activates Destiny behind his tower where you cannot reach him to interrupt the channel, do not follow him through the river; instead, immediately shove the wave to damage his turret and punish his map rotation.
laneImpact: The lane revolves around wave priority. Twisted Fate will continuously clear minions from a safe distance using Wild Cards and Pick a Card to search for roam opportunities. This forces Annie into a tough spot: she must expend her mana and Pyromania stacks using Disintegrate to match his push, or preserve her stun to threaten a solo kill, which ultimately grants him free roam timers.
why: This matchup is a race between raw combat power and map-wide presence. If Twisted Fate steps too close, Annie can instantly delete him using a Pyromania-infused stun combined with Summon: Tibbers and Incinerate. However, Twisted Fate's ultimate, Destiny, allows him to bypass direct confrontation entirely, letting him influence side lanes with global teleports that Annie simply cannot match in raw speed.

summary: Alistar can interrupt Pyke's Phantom Undertow dash with a well-timed Pulverize, preventing Pyke from landing his stun.
howToPlay: Position yourself slightly offset from your carry to bait Pyke's aggression. Never waste Pulverize to poke; keep it ready solely to intercept Phantom Undertow. If Pyke does manage to hook your ally with Bone Skewer, do not panic. Headbutt him away instantly to break his follow-up chain. If you are targeted by Death from Below while low, activate Unbreakable Will to cleanse any lingering slow and mitigate incoming damage, surviving his execute window.
laneImpact: Pyke's threat is neutralized in even-numbered skirmishes. Since you can deny his stun, he cannot safely fish for pulls with Bone Skewer without risking a deadly counter-engage. Every time Pyke misses his hook or fails a dash, his massive cooldown windows allow you to walk up, trigger Trample, and force him to burn Ghostwater Dive defensively. This keeps him low on health and unable to secure execution thresholds for Death from Below.
why: This matchup swings heavily in your favor because you hold the ultimate tool to shut down Pyke's main engage. Whenever Pyke attempts to dash forward with Phantom Undertow to stun your marksman, a well-timed Pulverize completely halts his movement mid-air. This denies his crowd control entirely, leaving him extremely vulnerable and exposed in the middle of your minion wave with no easy way to escape.

summary: Nocturne can block Mordekaiser's Realm of Death or Death's Grasp with a well-timed Shroud of Darkness.
howToPlay: To win this, you must bait out Shroud of Darkness before committing. Start skirmishes by walking up with Darkness Rise active or using Obliterate to force his shield. Never cast Realm of Death while his spell shield is available; instead, hold it until you see the purple barrier fade. If he channels Unspeakable Horror on you, use Indestructible immediately to absorb his burst before the fear lands, then use Death's Grasp to disengage if he still has his shield.
laneImpact: This interaction severely limits your jungle skirmishing. You cannot contest scuttle crabs or neutral objectives safely because Nocturne can counter-gank using Paranoia to bypass your vision. In 1v1 river duels, you are forced to play incredibly passively, unable to initiate with Death's Grasp. If he blocks your ultimate, you lose all pressure, forcing your laners to play defensively under their towers to avoid his global threat.
why: Nocturne holds a massive advantage in the jungle because his Shroud of Darkness completely nullifies your primary tools. A reactive Nocturne will wait for the animation of your Realm of Death or Death's Grasp, absorbing the spell to gain massive attack speed. This leaves you trapped in a duel without your stat-stealing arena, or unable to pull him away while he shreds you with Duskbringer and Unspeakable Horror.

summary: Olaf's Ragnarok grants him complete immunity to Rupture and Cri primal, leaving Cho'Gath with no way to peel Olaf off himself.
howToPlay: Your survival depends on maintaining a defensive posture, never crossing the lane's midpoint once Olaf has his ultimate ready. Save Rupture strictly for securing minions from a safe distance rather than trying to poke him. If he attempts a desperate tower dive, wait out the duration of Ragnarok before immediately chaining Feral Scream to silence his abilities, then look for a decisive execute with Feast.
laneImpact: Reaching level six severely restricts your freedom on the lane. Should Olaf freeze the wave, stepping up to trade with Vorpal Spikes becomes suicidal, as he can simply run you down with Ragnarok. You are forced to farm from maximum distance using Rupture, which rapidly depletes your mana pool and starves you of the vital healing from Carnivore.
why: The entire matchup hinges on Olaf's ultimate, Ragnarok. Once active, it completely negates your crowd control, rendering both the knock-up from Rupture and the silence of Feral Scream entirely useless. Without these essential tools to peel him off, you have no way to halt his advance, leaving you defenseless against his relentless close-quarters assault.

summary: Yone can use Soul Unbound (E) to safely trade from distance and bypass the boundaries of Between Worlds (R).
howToPlay: To survive this lane, never cast *Between Worlds* while Yone has *Soul Unbound* available; wait until he returns to his body before trapping him. Keep your distance and use *The Weirding* to slow his forward dashes, combined with *Across the Veil* to safely reposition and drop his target lock. Focus on farming, using *Twofold Hex* to clear waves from afar, and only trade when his spirit projection is on its lengthy cooldown.
laneImpact: This interaction strips away your post-level five kill pressure, turning your ultimate into a zoning tool rather than a lethal trap. Whenever Yone prepares *Mortal Steel* for his knock-up dash, you are forced to play defensively. He can aggressively initiate trades with *Soul Unbound*, chip away at your health using *Spirit Cleave* for shields, and force you to burn *Across the Veil* prematurely just to survive his burst.
why: Yone holds a distinct advantage because *Soul Unbound* completely bypasses the confinement of *Between Worlds*. When you attempt to trap him, he can simply snap back to his physical body, ignoring your ultimate's boundaries entirely. Furthermore, his *Soul Unbound* grants him explosive forward mobility to ignore your ranged advantage, making it difficult to safely trigger *Spirit Abjuration* without exposing yourself to his rapid, dual-damage strikes.

summary: Lissandra must get into close range to use Ring of Frost, allowing Brand to easily land his Sear stun combo.
howToPlay: Always hold your Sear until Lissandra commits. When she projects Glacial Path, position yourself slightly behind her path's end point. The moment she teleports, immediately use Conflagration followed by Sear to stun her before she can react with Ring of Frost. If she saves herself using Frozen Tomb, do not panic; simply pre-cast Pillar of Flame and unleash Pyroclasm right as her stasis ends to instantly burst her down.
laneImpact: This dynamic forces Lissandra to play defensively, using Ice Shard to secure minions from a distance, which naturally pushes the wave toward your side. You dictate the pace of the lane. Every time her Glacial Path is on cooldown, she loses all safety, allowing you to aggressively zone her out or trap her under turret with Pillar of Flame, creating a massive CS lead without risking your life.
why: Lissandra's threat relies entirely on closing the gap to trigger Ring of Frost. However, her predictable approach, whether walking up or using Glacial Path, plays directly into your hands. Because she must enter your effective range to deal meaningful damage, she exposes herself to an easy Blaze setup. You can easily tag her with Conflagration and stop her mid-advance with a guaranteed Sear stun, completely neutralizing her aggression.

howToPlay: Positioning: stay out of her small trade patterns and apply consistent harass. The goal isn’t a risky all-in; it’s continuous pressure. Key timing: wave crash + recall. Take a clean reset after crashing, return with an item, repeat. Cleaner recalls mean less oxygen for her. Decision-making: if her jungler can punish you, adapt with wards and safer wave states, but keep the plan. Take plates when safe; otherwise use prio to help objectives rather than forcing a risky dive.
laneImpact: In lane you can often take control from the first levels. Kayle must choose between last-hitting and eating autos. With good wave management you can freeze and force her to step up. Level 5 matters: her ult can save situations, but it doesn’t turn her into a true duelist. You must respect the ult, yet you can keep pressure and prio. Midgame, if you took plates/tower, you already accelerated the game before she becomes a real carry threat.
why: Kayle is favorable because she needs time and levels, and Tristana top can turn early game into constant oppression. You can deny waves, secure prio, and convert plates before she reaches comfort. She has limited tools to force you early. If you stay disciplined, you can harass cleanly without getting flipped. This is one of the matchups where your default plan (push + hit tower) can work very well. The key is not letting her breathe. If you give her a free lane, she will scale and the matchup becomes much less comfortable.

summary: Lee Sin can use Dragon's Rage to kick you away during your World Ender, wasting your ultimate's duration.
howToPlay: To survive this matchup, you must meticulously track the cooldown of Dragon's Rage. Never trigger World Ender proactively while his kick is up. Instead, wait for him to target a teammate, or position your back against thick terrain to minimize the knockback distance. When engaging, land Infernal Chains first to force him to burn Safeguard defensively before you commit your precious The Darkin Blade charges.
laneImpact: This interaction forces you to play defensively during early river skirmishes and objective contests. If you try to secure a neutral monster, the looming threat of his Dragon's Rage prevents you from fully committing. A single kick displaces you from the fight, rendering your physical vamp useless and giving him free rein to pressure your laners while you struggle to catch up.
why: This jungle duel heavily favors Lee Sin due to his superior mobility. Using Safeguard and Sonic Wave, he easily dances around your The Darkin Blade sweetspots. The ultimate dealbreaker is his Dragon's Rage; the moment you activate World Ender to turn a fight, he will kick you away, forcing you to watch your ultimate's duration bleed out while you are helplessly displaced.

summary: Viktor can drop Gravity Field directly on top of himself when Ekko dashes in, forcing Ekko to retreat or get stunned.
howToPlay: Always hold Gravity Field exclusively for Ekko's aggressive leaps; never cast it preemptively to catch him. Position yourself slightly behind your caster minions, forcing him to walk through your wave if he wants to land Timewinder. If he manages to catch you off guard with an unexpected Parallel Convergence stun, immediately disengage using the movement speed boost from Siphon Power and reset your positioning behind your minion line.
laneImpact: This defensive safety net allows you to dictate the wave's positioning with total confidence. You can easily keep the minions near your turret or slowly build massive waves to crash into his tower. Use Hextech Ray to continuously chip away at his health while he tries to clear waves under pressure, preventing him from roaming to find kills since he is trapped defending his own structure.
why: Viktor dominates this matchup because Ekko is forced to commit to close-range combat to be effective. Whenever Ekko attempts to close the gap using Phase Dive, you can place Gravity Field directly under your own feet. This immediate zone denial leaves Ekko with a terrible choice: abort his trade and retreat instantly, or get stunned inside your zone while taking a heavily empowered Siphon Power to his face.

summary: Akali can use Twilight Shroud to deny Talon the basic attack needed to trigger his Blade's End passive bleed.
howToPlay: Never waste Twilight Shroud aggressively if Talon has his cooldowns up; hold it as a defensive counter-measure to block his passive. When he walks up to farm, poke him with Five Point Strike and step back to prime Assassin's Mark. If he abandons the lane using Assassin's Path, do not mindlessly follow through the jungle; instead, shove the wave immediately to punish his tower, or use Perfect Execution to cut off his escape route.
laneImpact: Since Talon cannot safely trade into your shroud, he is forced to use Rake to shove waves and look for roams using Assassin's Path. This turns the lane into a pure race of map presence. You hold the leverage to punish his wave clear with Five Point Strike, preventing him from securing easy recall timings or roaming without losing mid tower plates.
why: This matchup swings heavily in your favor because of how Twilight Shroud interacts with Blade's End. Talon relies on stacking his passive with Rake and Noxian Diplomacy, but he must land a final basic attack to trigger the bleed. By dropping your shroud the moment he engages, you deny him target selection, completely neutralizing his burst potential while you retaliate with Five Point Strike.

summary: Camille must save Hextech Ultimatum or Hookshot to dodge the true damage center of Sett's Haymaker during all-ins.
howToPlay: To survive the all-in, you must never use your mobility tools to engage. Keep your finger on The Hextech Ultimatum or stand near terrain to instantly activate Hookshot the moment Sett winds up Haymaker. By jumping over him or dashing laterally, you completely escape the true damage center line. If he attempts to slam you with The Show Stopper, use your untargetability frames to nullify his ultimate's impact entirely.
laneImpact: You are forced onto the defensive, relying on the outer edge of Tactical Sweep to safely farm and chip away at his health. Committing to an aggressive Hookshot is highly risky because Sett can interrupt your dash with Facebreaker or grab you right out of the air. This limits your wave priority, forcing you to slow-push or hold the wave near your turret to avoid being run down by Knuckle Down.
why: Sett thrives when you try to burst him down because your Precision Protocol trade pattern rapidly fills his grit meter. When he unleashes Haymaker, the shield absorbs your damage while the center line deals lethal true damage. While Adaptive Defenses can absorb his basic attacks from Pit Grit and Knuckle Down, it won't save you from his max-grit true damage strike, turning an apparent win into a sudden defeat.

summary: Leona can use Eclipse to absorb Nautilus's initial burst from Staggering Blow and Dredge Line, then counter-engage on his ADC.
howToPlay: Position yourself slightly ahead of your carry to bait Nautilus into targeting you. The moment his Dredge Line connects, immediately trigger Eclipse to mitigate his incoming Riptide and Staggering Blow damage. Once the root expires, ignore Nautilus entirely; use Zenith Blade and Shield of Daybreak to dive onto his ADC. If Nautilus targets your carry instead, immediately drop Solar Flare on the enemy marksman to disrupt their follow-up.
laneImpact: The threat of Dredge Line forces you to stand parallel to your marksman, preventing Nautilus from isolating either of you. Whenever he hooks you, the trade swings in your favor because you easily survive the initiation, allowing you to bypass Nautilus entirely. The lane becomes a tense standoff where neither support can blindly dive forward without risking a devastating counter-engage.
why: This matchup is a pure test of reaction and execution. Nautilus seeks to lock you down using Dredge Line followed by a Staggering Blow root. However, because Leona can activate Eclipse during his hook's travel time, you can completely absorb his initial burst. This leaves Nautilus vulnerable with his defensive Titan's Wrath shield wasted, while your team retains the tools to strike back.

summary: Pantheon's Aegis Assault can block Amumu's initial burst, but Amumu's Tantrum passive reduces the physical damage from Pantheon's rapid-fire attacks.
howToPlay: Start on the same side of the map as Amumu to actively cross paths in the river or on his own camps. Do not launch your empowered Shield Vault immediately if he is full health, as his Tantrum will absorb too much damage. Instead, use your Comet Spear from a distance to chip away his health pool, then trigger Aegis Assault as soon as he tries to retaliate with his bandages. If Amumu avoids you, use Grand Starfall to counter-gank.
laneImpact: This dominance allows you to constantly invade his jungle to track his movements. By stealing his camps and forcing him to retreat, you delay his power spike and the acquisition of his Curse of the Sad Mummy. Amumu finds himself unable to gank safely, which releases immense pressure on all your lanes and secures you control of the river.
why: Pantheon dominates early jungle duels because your Aegis Assault perfectly blocks Amumu's initial burst initiated by his Bandage Toss. However, keep in mind that the passive of his Tantrum significantly reduces the physical damage of your rapid attacks, especially the triple strike from your Shield Vault empowered by Mortal Will. You must use patience instead of aiming for an instant burst.

summary: Fiora can react to Aatrox's highly telegraphed Q3 with Riposte to stun him and turn the trade completely in her favor.
howToPlay: To survive, you must bait out Riposte without committing to the final strike of The Darkin Blade. Cast your first two Qs, then use Umbral Dash laterally to reposition and delay your third strike, or simply let it expire. Keep Fiora at bay with Infernal Chains only when her Lunge is on cooldown. If she exposes a vital facing her, hug the terrain to deny her Duelist's Dance procs and prevent her from triggering the healing zone of Grand Challenge.
laneImpact: This interaction forces you into a highly defensive posture right from level one. You cannot safely contest the wave or crash it without risking a massive counter-engage. Every time Fiora freezes the wave or threatens you under tower, you are forced to give up gold. If you waste your knockups, she will run you down with Bladework and Grand Challenge, leaving you zero room to help your jungler.
why: Fiora's kit directly neutralizes your main damage source. The biggest threat is her Riposte, which she can easily reactively cast during your highly telegraphed third strike of The Darkin Blade. Because of this, she doesn't just block your knockup; she stuns you in return. Coupled with her Lunge to easily dodge your sweetspots and pop Duelist's Dance vitals, she dictates the pace of every trade.

summary: While Vladimir can use Sanguine Pool to dodge Light Binding or Final Spark, Lux can heavily punish his weak early game with constant Lucent Singularity poke.
howToPlay: To lock in your advantage, constantly harass him with Lucent Singularity and trigger Illumination with basic attacks whenever his crimson resource bar isn't fully charged. Never lead with Light Binding or Final Spark while his Sanguine Pool is active; instead, hold these spells to threaten him. If he panics and sinks into his pool to avoid raw poke, immediately deploy your full burst combo the second he resurfaces.
laneImpact: This range advantage forces Vladimir under his turret, where he must choose between losing minions or charging Tides of Blood at the expense of his own health pool. You will easily secure mid priority, enabling secure river rotations while Vladimir is trapped. Because his wave clear is sluggish early, you can delay his scaling spikes by forcing frequent, unfavorable recall timings that starve him of gold.
why: Lux dictates the pace because Vladimir's weak early game leaves him highly vulnerable to Lucent Singularity. Although he can nullify Light Binding or Final Spark using Sanguine Pool, doing so costs him a significant portion of his current health. Since his Transfusion healing is minimal in the early levels, you can constantly deny him access to the wave from a safe distance before he can acquire his core stat spikes.

howToPlay: Approach diagonally, plan your lines, and don’t step up without wave control: pushing without vision makes you vulnerable and she kites even easier. Key timing: your best windows are level 5 + a favorable wave where you can force her to fight inside your minions. Concrete decision: if she has flash/cleanse and you have no help, don’t invest your whole kit into her—play tower pressure and clean resets to show up for the objective.
laneImpact: Every failed entry costs HP and wave. If you get zoned, your recall timings get delayed and you lose first-move to Herald. As she gains confidence, she can play more aggressive and deny your scaling conversion.
why: Vayne is hard because she combines two things that punish you: true damage versus bruiser stats and a reset tool (Condemn) that breaks your chase. Shyvana lacks reliable hard CC to stop her spacing, so she can turn the lane into an attrition exercise.

summary: Swain's Demonic Ascension allows him to out-sustain Annie's burst, meaning she must rely on short Pyromania trades rather than committing to all-ins.
howToPlay: To survive, always keep your Pyromania passive charged to at least three stacks, allowing you to instantly threaten a stun if he steps up. When Swain casts Nevermove, use the movement speed from Molten Shield to sidestep the returning claw. If he activates Demonic Ascension, immediately disengage rather than fighting back; walk away and wait for his ultimate to expire. Use this downtime to push with Incinerate and roam to side lanes where your Summon: Tibbers burst actually secures kills.
laneImpact: Because Swain sustains through your poke, trying to force him out of lane is a losing battle that wastes your mana. He will use Death's Hand to push you under tower, while fishing for Nevermove roots to pull you. This constant pressure limits your ability to recall safely. You cannot match his lane presence once he gets his ultimate, meaning your mid lane priority drops significantly and you must look for roam opportunities elsewhere.
why: Swain's passive Ravenous Flock and his ultimate Demonic Ascension completely nullify Annie's signature burst damage. While you want to summon Summon: Tibbers for a decisive kill, Swain's constant health drain during his ultimate means he will easily heal back your burst. This forces you to abandon one-shot attempts and instead play around quick, stun-infused Pyromania trades using Disintegrate or Incinerate to slowly chip him down.

summary: Howling Gale can interrupt Thresh's Death Sentence dash or Flay follow-up, while Monsoon completely resets the fight if he lands a hook.
howToPlay: Position yourself parallel to your ADC, ensuring you always have a clear line of sight to react. Crucially, never cast Howling Gale offensively; hold this storm specifically to disrupt his Death Sentence dash or block a Flay setup. If he throws Dark Passage to bring his jungler, prepare your tornado on the lantern's path. Should an unexpected hook land on you, immediately use Monsoon to push everyone away and reset the lane dynamic.
laneImpact: This interaction forces Thresh to play defensively, robbing him of his usual lane dominance. Since his primary engage is so easily countered, you can safely harass him with Zephyr whenever he steps up to collect souls for Damnation. Your ADC enjoys free wave control and constant safety, meaning you can slowly chip away at their health bar and secure a gold advantage under their own turret.
why: Janna completely dictates the pace of this matchup because her entire kit serves as a hard stop to Thresh's forward momentum. While Death Sentence is his main tool to start fights, casting Howling Gale directly into his incoming flight path completely cancels his momentum. Even if he connects a hook and pulls your ADC, you can instantly drop Monsoon to blow him back and heal up, entirely neutralizing his pick potential.

summary: Ezreal can buffer Arcane Shift to escape Tristana's Rocket Jump engage, leaving her stranded with an uncharged Explosive Charge.
howToPlay: Never waste Arcane Shift offensively unless Tristana’s Rocket Jump is on its long cooldown. Hold your blink specifically to react to her jump animation. Once she is stranded near your minions with her jump wasted, immediately retaliate by landing Essence Flux followed by Mystic Shot. If she tries to disengage using Buster Shot, quickly react with Trueshot Barrage to punish her retreat path and secure an easy kill.
laneImpact: Because Tristana cannot safely engage with her leap, she loses all lane pressure. You can constantly poke her down with Mystic Shot and Essence Flux while she struggles to farm under threat. She cannot safely use Explosive Charge on your turret without risking a counter-all-in, forcing her to play defensively and giving you free rein to control the wave state and secure easy plating.
why: This matchup is heavily in your favor because you can completely neutralize Tristana's aggressive all-ins. Whenever she attempts to leap forward with Rocket Jump to apply and stack Explosive Charge, you can buffer Arcane Shift. By timing your blink to her jump animation, you escape the slow and damage, leaving her stranded in a vulnerable forward position with an unstackable bomb and no easy escape.

summary: Hecarim's high-speed engage via Devastating Charge can be stopped mid-air by a well-timed Terrify.
howToPlay: To win this tempo battle, never initiate a duel head-on with Devastating Charge if Fiddlesticks has Terrify available. Instead, run close to him to bait the fear, or flank with Onslaught of Shadows to apply your own fear first, interrupting his Bountiful Harvest. If he starts channeling Crowstorm from a bush, immediately use Devastating Charge to push him away from your team, or use Rampage and Spirit of Dread to out-sustain his drain.
laneImpact: Because both junglers clear camps exceptionally fast, your pathing determines who dominates the map pressure. If Fiddlesticks uses Terrify on a lane gank, you have a brief window to contest the scuttle or invade. However, if he saves it, entering his jungle is suicide. Failing an engage due to his fear means losing precious seconds, giving him the space to channel Crowstorm and wipe your teammates.
why: This matchup is a pure race of clear speed and skirmish timings, balanced on a knife-edge. While Hecarim relies on building momentum with Devastating Charge to crash into Fiddlesticks, the scarecrow can instantly neutralize this forward velocity. A reactive Terrify will stop your galloping charge dead in its tracks, canceling your displacement and leaving you vulnerable to Bountiful Harvest's drain.

summary: Poppy's Steadfast Presence blocks Renekton's Slice and Dice, grounding him and leaving him vulnerable to her wall-slam.
howToPlay: Never waste Steadfast Presence proactively. Hold it specifically as a reaction to his Slice and Dice animation. Position yourself permanently between the wave and the river wall, baiting him to dash in. If he activates Dominus, do not panic-fight; use Keeper's Verdict with a quick cast to knock him airborne, or charge it up to launch him away, completely wasting his ultimate's duration while you pick up your Iron Ambassador shield.
laneImpact: Because you shut down his double-dash, Renekton cannot freely chunk you with Cull the Meek and dash back out. This lets you dictate the wave state, forcing him to use Ruthless Predator on minions to build Fury rather than saving it for you. You can freeze the wave near your tower, turning any attempt he makes to step up into a lethal wall-stun threat under your own terms.
why: Renekton relies entirely on Slice and Dice to initiate trades or escape. By activating Steadfast Presence the moment he dashes, you completely cancel his mobility, grounding him on the spot. This denial leaves him helpless right next to the terrain, setting up an easy angle for your Heroic Charge stun and a subsequent Hammer Shock slam while his main defensive tool is on a long cooldown.

summary: Mordekaiser's passive magic penetration from Death's Grasp and AP damage profile completely bypass Rammus's high-armor Defensive Ball Curl.
howToPlay: Prioritize early magic damage and magic penetration items rather than defensive armor, maximizing your damage output against his health pool. During skirmishes, save Death's Grasp to cancel his Powerball escape or pull him back if he tries to roll away. When he forces you to attack him with Frenzying Taunt, immediately activate Indestructible to absorb the reflected damage, ensuring you win the trade and maintain full control over the neutral objectives.
laneImpact: In the jungle, this matchup strips Rammus of his early dueling pressure. He cannot safely contest Scuttle Crabs or defend his camps against your invades, as he lacks the damage to threaten you. When he attempts to gank lanes using Powerball, you can easily counter-gank or force him into Realm of Death, isolating him away from his allies and stealing his tank stats to secure easy neutral objectives.
why: Rammus relies heavily on his Defensive Ball Curl to boost his armor and reflect physical attacks, making him an anti-AD powerhouse. However, your entire damage profile is magic-based, rendering his primary defensive tool highly ineffective. Furthermore, the magic penetration granted by Death's Grasp naturally shreds through any magic resistance he attempts to build, ensuring your Obliterate and Darkness Rise melt his health pool during skirmishes.

summary: Morgana can reactively block Zenith Blade or Shield of Daybreak with Black Shield, forcing Leona to bait the shield before engaging.
howToPlay: Hold your Black Shield strictly for Leona's Zenith Blade animation or an obvious Solar Flare. Never waste it preemptively, as its long cooldown is her only window of opportunity. Position yourself parallel to your carry to instantly shield whoever Leona targets. If she misses Zenith Blade, immediately punish her with Dark Binding followed by Tormented Shadow to trigger Soul Siphon healing, keeping your health pool too high for her to ever burst you down.
laneImpact: Because Leona cannot engage reliably, you can safely walk up to harass her with Tormented Shadow and fish for Dark Binding. This pressure forces Leona and her carry under their turret, granting your lane priority for early drakes or scuttle crabs. Leona's health bar will constantly dwindle from your poke, making her too weak to find a proper engage window, which secures you easy recall timings and tower plate gold.
why: Morgana holds a massive advantage because Black Shield completely negates Leona's primary engage tools. Reacting to Zenith Blade or Shield of Daybreak with Black Shield leaves Leona stranded in the middle of your minion wave with no follow-up crowd control. This interaction shifts the pressure entirely onto Leona, who cannot safely commit without first baiting out your defensive shield, allowing you to dictate the pace of every skirmish.

summary: Teemo's Blinding Dart makes Graves's New Destiny pellets miss entirely, rendering him unable to trade or stack True Grit.
howToPlay: Never waste Blinding Dart on minion last-hits; hold it strictly for when Graves uses Quickdraw to initiate a trade. Stand away from terrain to deny him the instant wall-bounce damage from End of the Line. If he drops Smoke Screen to disorient you, immediately activate Move Quick to back out of the cloud, then turn around to punish him with poisoned attacks while his defensive dash is on cooldown.
laneImpact: Graves is forced into a defensive posture, unable to contest the wave with basic attacks. He must waste End of the Line just to secure minions, pushing the wave into you and leaving him open to deep freezes.
