You can easily harass him under his turret with Toxic Shot and use Noxious Trap to block his escape routes, keeping him constantly low and preventing any aggressive lane priority.
why: This matchup is heavily in your favor because Graves's entire damage output relies on his basic attacks. Whenever he dashes forward, a well-timed Blinding Dart completely neutralizes his New Destiny passive. All of his shotgun pellets will miss, preventing him from dealing damage or generating defensive stacks of True Grit via Quickdraw. This leaves him entirely vulnerable while your Toxic Shot continuously chips away at his health bar.

summary: Vayne's Condemn can instantly interrupt Samira's Inferno Trigger, forcing Samira to either block it with Blade Whirl or wait for Vayne to waste it.
howToPlay: Your main priority is to never cast Condemn preemptively. Wait for Samira to dash in with Wild Rush and activate her Inferno Trigger. If she activates Blade Whirl early, she is vulnerable; if she holds it, use Tumble to reposition away from her slash radius. Once her projectile-blocking barrier fades, immediately fire your Condemn to cancel her ultimate. If you misplay and waste your knockback early, immediately retreat with Final Hour stealth to deny her the reset.
laneImpact: This interaction dictates the rhythm of every trade under tower or in the lane. Samira cannot blindly dive or force all-ins because the threat of being pinned or interrupted is constant. Vayne can safely farm and poke with Tumble and Silver Bolts, knowing she holds the ultimate defensive tool. As long as Vayne holds her knockback, Samira is forced to play passively, bleeding gold and losing priority during crucial dragon skirmishes.
why: Vayne holds a massive advantage in this duel because her Condemn acts as a hard stop to Samira's ultimate. Since Samira needs to stack Daredevil Impulse to activate Inferno Trigger, she has to commit forward with Wild Rush. When she does, Vayne can immediately cancel the massive channel of Inferno Trigger with a well-timed Condemn, rendering Samira's primary damage source useless unless she successfully blocks it beforehand using Blade Whirl.

summary: Teemo's Move Quick allows him to easily dodge Mordekaiser's Obliterate and Death's Grasp, letting him safely poke from a distance.
howToPlay: Concede early minions and let the wave crash. Only throw Death's Grasp if Teemo steps up too far to auto-attack and has his Move Quick on cooldown. If you manage to pull him in, immediately activate Darkness Rise and force Realm of Death to trap him before he can escape. If you hit a Noxious Trap, immediately activate Indestructible to mitigate the slow and damage, then retreat to the safety of your tower.
laneImpact: You will find yourself pinned under your own turret, bleeding health every time you step up to last-hit. Teemo's relentless harassment forces you to deplete Indestructible early just to survive the poison. If you drop too low, you are forced into bad recalls, losing waves and letting him place Noxious Trap clusters around the river, completely blocking your jungler from assisting you.
why: Teemo's constant mobility from Move Quick makes this lane exceptionally difficult for Mordekaiser. Whenever you attempt to close the distance or fish for a catch, the swift scout easily steps out of your Death's Grasp and sidesteps Obliterate. This allows him to constantly apply pressure with Toxic Shot from safety, rendering your melee-range threat null while he chips away at your health bar.

summary: Zyra can spawn plants with Rampant Growth to block Leona's pathing and use Grasping Roots to stop her mid-engage.
howToPlay: To survive, you must play a game of baiting. Position yourself slightly parallel to your minion wave to draw out her Grasping Roots without getting hit. Once her root is on cooldown, you have a brief window to move forward. If she tries to block you with Rampant Growth plants, immediately activate Eclipse to mitigate their spit damage, and only use Zenith Blade when you have a clear angle that bypasses her spawned seedlings. If you miss, immediately retreat to prevent Stranglethorns from locking you down permanently.
laneImpact: This constant threat of blockage forces you into a passive posture behind your minion wave, conceding early bush control. If you get caught by Grasping Roots while trying to step up, Zyra's plants will chunk your health pool, forcing an early recall and leaving your marksman vulnerable under tower. Because you cannot easily threaten an engage, Zyra freely pushes the waves, locking you down while her Stranglethorns scales to dominate dragon skirmishes.
why: Zyra completely disrupts your engage tools by cluttering your path with her plants. Whenever you try to step up, she can spawn a seed with Rampant Growth directly in front of her, meaning your Zenith Blade or straight-line movement gets body-blocked by spitting thorns. Worse, if you do manage to launch yourself, a well-timed Grasping Roots will root you mid-air, leaving you stranded far from her while Garden of Thorns plants shred your health.

summary: Morgana's Black Shield completely negates the knockup from Rupture and the silence from Cri primal, leaving Cho'Gath with no crowd control.
howToPlay: To survive this matchup, you must bait out Black Shield before committing to any trade. Maximize your Vorpal Spikes to secure last hits without using mana, saving Rupture as a defensive tool to disengage when she walks up. If she wastes her shield, you have a brief fifteen-second window to strike. Otherwise, focus solely on healing via Carnivore and execute minions with Feast to stack your health safely.
laneImpact: Without the threat of your crowd control, Morgana can safely clear waves from a distance using Tormented Shadow and fish for Dark Binding roots. You are forced to rely on Carnivore to sustain through her persistent magic damage, but you cannot pressure her under turret. If she lands her root, she can easily setup Soul Shackles to force you out of lane.
why: Morgana represents a massive wall for Cho'Gath because her Black Shield entirely absorbs and negates both the knockup from Rupture and the silence from Feral Scream. Since your entire kit relies on landing these crowd control abilities to set up Feast, her spell shield completely shuts down your offensive threat, leaving you unable to interrupt her or secure trades.

summary: Kindred can kite Tryndamere's Spinning Slash using Dance of Arrows, and timing Lamb's Respite to overlap with Undying Rage neutralizes his dive threat.
howToPlay: To survive this matchup, never initiate with Spinning Slash unless Kindred has already wasted Dance of Arrows inside Wolf's Frenzy. Instead, walk up or flank, using Mocking Shout when their back is turned to cripple their mobility and AD. If they deploy Lamb's Respite, stop attacking them inside the circle; instead, build up your Battle Fury on nearby targets and prepare to use Bloodlust for a crucial heal right as their zone ends to survive their execution.
laneImpact: This interaction severely limits your jungle dueling and skirmishing presence. Contesting Mark of the Kindred camps becomes a massive risk, as Kindred can bait your dive under towers or in the river. Since you cannot reliably burst them down before they activate Lamb's Respite, you lose pressure around neutral spawns. You are forced to power-farm your camps with Battle Fury rather than seeking proactive jungle duels.
why: Kindred counters your direct engage by easily kiting Spinning Slash with the short-cooldown hops of Dance of Arrows. The matchup becomes incredibly frustrating because your ultimate threshold is completely neutralized; when you trigger Undying Rage to survive, Kindred simply drops Lamb's Respite. This overlap protects them during your peak damage window, leaving you vulnerable to a fatal Mounting Dread execution the moment the healing circle expires.

summary: Vladimir cannot match Galio's map pressure with Hero's Entrance (R), allowing Galio to impact side lanes while Vladimir slowly scales.
howToPlay: Accept that you cannot follow Hero's Entrance directly. Instead, ping your allies immediately when Galio moves, and use his absence to safely charge Tides of Blood and fast-shove the wave to deny him gold. Keep Sanguine Pool ready in case he attempts an aggressive Justice Punch and Shield of Durand dive under your turret. Focus entirely on securing your own resources to reach the teamfight phase where your Hemoplague can outvalue his utility.
laneImpact: The lane turns into a frustrating waiting game. Galio will ignore your Transfusion harass, using his natural magic damage shield to absorb trades before crashing minions under your turret. While you struggle to clear under tower, he disappears into the fog of war. If you try to follow his Justice Punch roams, you risk getting ambushed in the river without the safety of Sanguine Pool, forcing your sidelanes to play defensively.
why: Galio dominates this matchup because he can effortlessly shove the lane with Winds of War and Colossal Smash, then instantly impact the map using Hero's Entrance. As Vladimir, your early waveclear with Tides of Blood is too weak and costly to match his push. You are locked in mid-lane, slowly stacking Crimson Pact and waiting for Hemoplague power spikes, while Galio creates massive advantages for his team across the map.

summary: Janna can interrupt Pyke's Phantom Undertow dash with Howling Gale, but must be careful as Eye of the Storm's shield does not prevent execution by Death from Below.
howToPlay: Never throw Howling Gale proactively to poke; you must hold it exclusively to react to Phantom Undertow. Position yourself slightly behind your ADC, using Tailwind's passive speed to help them dodge Bone Skewer. If your ally's health drops into the execution threshold, do not rely on Eye of the Storm; instead, cast Monsoon instantly to blow Pyke away and heal your partner out of the danger zone before he can cast his ultimate.
laneImpact: Pyke will constantly use Ghostwater Dive to vanish into brush, threatening a Bone Skewer pull from the fog. This forces you into defensive posturing, rendering your Zephyr poke highly risky to execute. If Pyke bypasses you to pressure your ADC, the lane's outcome hinges on whether you can interrupt his dash. Missing your tornado means giving Pyke an easy double kill and roaming priority to terrorize your midlaner.
why: This matchup is a pure test of reflexes centered on Pyke's engage. The lane remains strictly even because while you have the perfect tool to disengage—using Howling Gale to knock Pyke out of his Phantom Undertow dash before the stun lands—any misstep is lethal. Crucially, your Eye of the Storm shield cannot block the true damage execution of Death from Below, meaning a low-health ally is never safe just because you shielded them.

summary: Aurora can use Between Worlds (R) to restrict Ekko's movement, making it easier to predict his Chronobreak (R) clone.
howToPlay: Never cast Between Worlds raw; wait for Ekko to use Phase Dive offensively. Once he is committed, trap him. Keep a close eye on his holographic shadow trailing behind him. If he tries to escape or turn the fight with Chronobreak, cast Twofold Hex directly onto his clone's path inside your arena. If you misplay the trap and he stuns you with Parallel Convergence, immediately use Across the Veil to slip into stealth and reposition.
laneImpact: Before level five, the lane is a constant baiting game. Ekko will try to clear waves with Timewinder while looking for cheeky stuns with Parallel Convergence. You must use Twofold Hex to poke him down whenever he steps up to hit the melee minions. If he commits with Phase Dive, a quick The Weirding disengages the trade instantly. The lane is decided by who manages their health bar better before the ultimate spike.
why: This matchup is a highly volatile dance of displacement and repositioning. While Ekko relies on Phase Dive to close the distance and trigger Z-Drive Resonance, your mobility matches his. The ultimate turning point hinges on Between Worlds. By trapping Ekko inside your dimensional boundary, you severely limit where his Chronobreak clone can trail, removing the guesswork from his ultimate escape and letting you lock down his temporal escape route.

summary: Vayne can easily react to Shen's Shadow Dash with Condemn, keeping him at a distance while shredding him with Silver Bolts.
howToPlay: Prioritize your health bar over individual minion gold. Position yourself far back, using the brush to break her vision and prevent Night Hunter from giving her free movement speed. Only use Twilight Assault defensively to trigger Ki Barrier's shield when soaking inevitable poke. Never use Shadow Dash forward unless her Condemn is on cooldown. If she activates Final Hour, immediately retreat toward your turret and prepare to use Spirit's Refuge to survive her invisible assault.
laneImpact: You are entirely denied from controlling the minion wave, forced to bleed gold under your turret. Any attempt to step up to secure minions results in heavy poke. While Spirit's Refuge can temporarily block her basic attacks, Vayne simply waits out the zone. Furthermore, you cannot safely cast Stand United in her line of sight, as she will immediately interrupt your channel with Condemn, neutralizing your global presence.
why: Vayne completely shuts down your primary tool for closing the gap. Whenever you attempt to initiate with Shadow Dash, she can instantly react with Condemn to knock you back before you connect. Once your gap-closer is on cooldown, you are stranded at her mercy. She will easily kite you using Night Hunter and Tumble, shredding your health with successive Silver Bolts procs while you cannot retaliate.

summary: Using Twilight Shroud (W) or Shuriken Flip (E) when Jax activates Counter Strike (E) completely neutralizes his stun and trading potential.
howToPlay: To survive, never initiate with Leap Strike while her defensive tools are ready. Instead, walk up to farm, and use Counter Strike defensively to block Assassin's Mark empowered attacks. If she wastes Twilight Shroud, you have a twenty-second opening where you can aggressively trade using Leap Strike and Empower. Should she hit you with Shuriken Flip, activate Counter Strike immediately to block her follow-up dash damage and force her to back off.
laneImpact: This interaction forces you into a defensive posture where you cannot safely contest the wave. Attempting to force trades when her Twilight Shroud is active leads to disastrous health losses, ruining your recall timings and giving her total wave control. You must concede early priority, farming under tower while conserving your health pool, which prevents you from helping your jungler or pressure her tower before scaling.
why: Akali commands this lane because her defensive mobility perfectly counters your primary threat. Whenever you activate Counter Strike to initiate a trade, she can immediately nullify your stun and damage by slipping into Twilight Shroud or flipping away with Shuriken Flip. Without the threat of your evasion and stun landing, your Leap Strike and Empower combos lose all their pressure, leaving you exposed to her swift magic damage retaliation.

summary: Varus's physical damage poke from Piercing Arrow (Q) bypasses Galio's magic shield, forcing Galio to play defensively under tower.
howToPlay: Maintain your distance just outside of his Justice Punch range, keeping the lane pushed to deny his roams. Always hold onto Chain of Corruption to counter his aggressive forward dashes; if he attempts to charge Shield of Durand, immediately root him to stop his engage. If his jungler coordinates a gank to break your siege, use Hail of Arrows to slow the pursuers and retreat safely.
laneImpact: This physical pressure forces Galio to retreat under his turret, bleeding health whenever he steps up to use Winds of War on the minions. You hold absolute control over the wave's tempo, allowing you to slow push large waves and chip away at his tower. Because he is trapped clearing waves under turret, his signature roaming tool, Hero's Entrance, becomes virtually useless as he cannot leave lane.
why: In this mid lane matchup, your physical damage profile completely neutralizes Galio's passive magic damage shield. Since his natural defenses are designed to soak magic threats, your charged Piercing Arrow strikes him for full damage. He cannot easily contest the wave when your basic attacks stack Blighted Quiver and your Hail of Arrows slows his attempts to engage with Justice Punch, forcing him into a defensive stance.

summary: Poppy's anti-dash zone completely blocks Wukong's Nimbus Strike, preventing him from engaging or easily positioning for his Cyclone.
howToPlay: Never activate Steadfast Presence preemptively. Instead, hover near your vulnerable carries during teamfights and reactively press it the moment Wukong targets them with Nimbus Strike. Once he is grounded and his dash is canceled, immediately follow up with Heroic Charge to slam him into the nearest wall or river terrain. If he manages to activate Cyclone, use a quick-cast Keeper's Verdict to instantly knock him airborne and disrupt his spin, protecting your backline.
laneImpact: Because you completely shut down his primary engage tool, Wukong cannot safely contest Rift Herald or Dragon skirmishes. If he attempts to jump into the pit with Nimbus Strike, you trap him in place, forcing him to waste Warrior Trickster defensively rather than using it to trick your allies. This restriction stifles his early ganking pressure, giving your laners a much safer map state while you secure neutral objectives.
why: Your entire advantage in this jungle matchup hinges on how Steadfast Presence utterly neutralizes Wukong's main gap-closer. When the monkey attempts to initiate or escape using Nimbus Strike, activating your defensive ring instantly grounds and knocks him down. By denying him this initial dash, you prevent him from easily sliding into your team to set up a devastating multi-man knock-up with Cyclone.

summary: Varus must use the maximum range of Piercing Arrow to poke Mel down before she can set up her zone control spells.
howToPlay: Stand well behind your caster minions, forcing Mel to choose between targeting you or the wave. Hold Chain of Corruption to disengage if she tries to advance and drop her zoning spells directly on you. Activate Blighted Quiver before releasing a fully charged Piercing Arrow from maximum range to maximize your snipe damage. If she successfully blocks you out, concede the priority, farm under turret using Hail of Arrows, and wait for her to overextend.
laneImpact: If Mel establishes her zones early, she will easily shove waves and pin you under tower, chipping your health while you struggle to farm. Every time you miss a Piercing Arrow, you cede mid-lane priority, allowing her to rotate or secure vision. You cannot match her wave clear safely without using Hail of Arrows to thin minions, which unfortunately leaves you vulnerable to her aggressive forward positioning.
why: Mel excels at controlling the mid lane with her zoning spells, making it highly dangerous for you to step into medium range. Because Varus lacks mobility, getting caught in her setup means taking massive magic damage. Your only saving grace is the extreme reach of Piercing Arrow. You must charge and release this ability from absolute safety to chip her health down before she can choke out your movement options.

summary: Syndra can knock Ahri out of her Spirit Rush dash using Scatter the Weak, preventing her from landing a close-range Charm.
howToPlay: To survive, never dash directly at Syndra. Position diagonally relative to her Dark Sphere placements to avoid quick stuns. Always hold your Spirit Rush until she wastes Scatter the Weak to push a wave or harass. If she discipline-holds her knockback, do not force the fight; instead, use Orb of Deception to clear waves from maximum range, then use your mobility to assist your jungler rather than trying to force a solo kill in mid.
laneImpact: This interaction forces you onto the defensive, limiting your ability to contest waves. Since you cannot reliably threaten an all-in, Syndra can freely poke you with Dark Sphere while shoving the lane with Force of Will. If you get chipped down, you will be forced into awkward recall timings under your own tower, giving her free reign to stack Transcendent shards and secure early mid priority.
why: Syndra dictates the pace of this matchup because her defensive tools completely shut down your aggressive options. Whenever you attempt to close the gap with Spirit Rush, she can reactively use Scatter the Weak to knock you out of your dash. This interruption completely ruins your momentum, preventing you from getting into the optimal angle to land Charm, leaving you vulnerable to a massive burst of Dark Sphere and Unleashed Power.

summary: Hecarim's Devastating Charge can push you out of your own Q sweetspot ranges during a duel.
howToPlay: To survive these duels, never initiate with your full combo. Hold Infernal Chains until Hecarim commits his Devastating Charge. Use Umbral Dash defensively to reposition immediately after he pushes you, allowing you to realign the sweetspots of The Darkin Blade. Activate World Ender only when you can guarantee a static fight, and rely on Deathbringer Stance to heal up if he tries to run you down with his superior speed.
laneImpact: In the jungle, this mobility imbalance means you struggle to contest the Scuttle Crabs or secure early river priority. If Hecarim finds you in the river, his low cooldown Rampage combined with Spirit of Dread will out-sustain you if he successfully disrupts your knockups. A failed duel because of a displaced sweetspot forces you to concede your camps or arrive late to counter-gank, putting your lanes behind.
why: Hecarim's superior movement speed from Warpath allows him to dictate the pace of jungle skirmishes. The core danger lies in Devastating Charge; its knockback is the perfect counter to your combo. When you attempt to chain your strikes, a well-timed charge from Hecarim pushes you completely out of range, ruining the sweetspot alignments of The Darkin Blade and leaving you unable to heal or deal damage.

summary: Diana needs to land Crescent Strike to gap-close with Lunar Rush, otherwise Lillia's high movement speed from Blooming Blows allows her to easily kite.
howToPlay: Do not initiate with Lunar Rush dry. Instead, track Lillia's movement pattern and wait for her to lock herself into the animation of Watch Out! Eep! before casting Crescent Strike. This guarantees your Moonlight reset. If she manages to dodge your initial crescent arc, immediately back off and use Pale Cascade to absorb any incoming Swirlseed damage. Do not chase her while her movement speed stacks are fully charged; instead, wait for her stacks to decay before re-engaging.
laneImpact: Clear speeds are neck-and-neck, making the jungle pathing highly competitive. When contesting Scuttle Crabs or epic monsters, missing your initial skillshot gives Lillia the freedom to poke you down with Swirlseed and kite you across the river. If she secures enough space to cast Lilting Lullaby, you will be put to sleep before you can even get close enough to pull her in with Moonfall, costing your team early objective control.
why: This matchup is a high-speed pursuit in the jungle where Diana's target acquisition faces Lillia's hit-and-run capabilities. Everything hinges on Crescent Strike. If you land this arc, you get a reset on Lunar Rush to close the gap instantly. If you miss, Lillia accumulates passive stacks from Blooming Blows, boosting her movement speed to a point where she can easily dance outside your melee range while applying Dream-Laden Bough.

summary: Wukong can block Ryze's targeted Rune Prison with Warrior Trickster's clone before engaging with Nimbus Strike.
howToPlay: Position yourself constantly near the side brushes to drop minion aggro and obscure your engage angle. Never open a trade blindly with Nimbus Strike; instead, walk up or use bushes to force Ryze into panic-casting Rune Prison. The moment you see his casting animation, press Warrior Trickster to intercept it, then instantly close the gap with Nimbus Strike and shred him using Golden Staff. If he holds his root, simply farm and scale with Stone Skin armor.
laneImpact: This interaction dictates the wave dynamic, forcing Ryze to play defensively instead of abusing his ranged advantage. He cannot safely clear waves with Spell Flux and Overload bounces if he constantly fears your burst. By holding your clone threat, you restrict his movement behind his minions, preventing him from zoning you. This safety allows you to secure easy gold, control the crash timings, and health-threaten him under his own turret.
why: Ryze relies entirely on his targeted Rune Prison to halt your gap-closers and safely kite you with Spell Flux and Overload. However, Wukong completely disrupts this defensive loop. By deploying Warrior Trickster reactively, you can bait and absorb his Rune Prison with your clone. Without this single point-and-click crowd control to keep you at bay, Ryze cannot escape your immediate Nimbus Strike follow-up.

summary: Pantheon's point-and-click Shield Vault (W) stun setup is too fast to react to, and his Aegis Assault (E) blocks all of your frontal burst damage.
howToPlay: Always hold your Shield Vault when walking up to prevent her from safely escaping with Shuriken Flip. Do not waste Aegis Assault early; save it specifically to block the incoming damage when she commits with Perfect Execution. If she manages to slip into Twilight Shroud, immediately back off toward your minion wave and prep a charged Comet Spear to strike her the moment she reveals herself to last-hit.
laneImpact: This advantage grants you absolute control over the wave state from the very first levels. Akali is forced to yield lane priority, allowing you to slow-push and deny her gold. You can easily set up dives under her turret since Aegis Assault can absorb turret shots at the end of an exchange, forcing her into terrible recall timings and securing you early plates.
why: You completely dictate this high-burst matchup through two decisive tools. Your point-and-click Shield Vault provides an instant stun that Akali cannot react to or hide from with Twilight Shroud. Furthermore, when she attempts to unload her quick burst using Five Point Strike or her Perfect Execution dashes, your Aegis Assault completely negates her frontal damage, leaving her vulnerable and resource-depleted.

summary: Karma's Mantra-boosted Inner Flame exerts heavy lane pressure that Janna's Eye of the Storm can only partially mitigate due to its longer cooldown.
howToPlay: To survive, you must play behind your minion wave to force her Inner Flame to clip minions, which naturally pushes the lane and limits direct hits. Save Howling Gale strictly to interrupt her if she tries to advance and root with Focused Resolve. If she misses her empowered blast, immediately step up to poke with Zephyr. If you get shoved too low, use Monsoon defensively to reset the dive threat rather than saving it for a teamfight.
laneImpact: This cooldown disparity forces you and your carry under tower, as Karma easily secures wave priority with her splash damage. Trying to trade back with Zephyr is risky; if she shields herself with Inspire, you lose the trade entirely. Expect your health pool to slowly dwindle, making early recalls inevitable and leaving your turret vulnerable to plates being taken while you are forced to play defensively.
why: Karma dominates the early neutral space because her Mantra-infused Inner Flame deals immense area-of-effect damage on a significantly shorter rotation than your Eye of the Storm. While you can absorb some of her poke with your shield, the math is heavily against you. You will constantly find your Eye of the Storm on cooldown while her next empowered projectile is already flying toward your marksman.

summary: Varus must stay outside the range of Veigar's Event Horizon while using Piercing Arrow to chip away at his health.
howToPlay: Never charge Piercing Arrow while walking directly towards Veigar, as the self-slow makes you an easy target for Event Horizon. Instead, bait his cage by hovering just outside its maximum range. If he misses it, immediately punish him with Hail of Arrows to slow him, apply Blighted Quiver stacks with basic attacks, and pop them from afar. If you get caught inside the cage, stand still to dodge Dark Matter rather than panicking into the stun.
laneImpact: Your positioning directly dictates who controls the wave tempo. Consistently dodging the cage allows you to safely push with Hail of Arrows and force Veigar to use Baleful Strike for farming under turret rather than stacking on you. Conversely, getting caught once forces you to burn your summoners or face a lethal Primordial Burst execution, completely giving up your lane pressure and mid priority.
why: This matchup is a pure test of range control. Varus outranges Veigar's threat zone using long-range Piercing Arrow snipes, but stepping even slightly too close invites an immediate Event Horizon. If Veigar traps you in his cage, his Dark Matter and Baleful Strike will easily chunk your health pool while stacking his Phenomenal Evil Power. Your entire survival hinges on maintaining that precise outer limit.

summary: Diana can abuse Shyvana's weak pre-6 clear and lack of crowd control to secure early crab control and invades.
howToPlay: Path aggressively to cross paths with Shyvana at level three. When invading her camps, save Crescent Strike to scout bushes or mark her before she can run with Burnout. If she attempts to flee using that movement speed, use Lunar Rush to close the gap instantly. Hold Moonfall to interrupt her positioning or pull her back after she attempts to leap away with Dragon's Descent, ensuring she cannot escape your burst.
laneImpact: This matchup dynamic turns the river and Shyvana's own jungle into a playground for Diana. Because Shyvana cannot lock you down, you easily secure both Scuttle Crabs. Striking her with Crescent Strike followed by Lunar Rush forces her out of her own camps. By invading her early, you delay her acquisition of Draconic Bloodline stacks, severely weakening her mid-game transition and leaving her lanes completely unprotected from your ganks.
why: Diana dominates the early jungle because Shyvana lacks any crowd control to disrupt her. While Shyvana tries to stack Fury of the Dragonborn using Burnout and Flame Breath, she remains highly vulnerable. Diana utilizes Moonsilver Blade for rapid, sustained early clearing, and Pale Cascade provides a protective shield that completely negates Shyvana's early damage from Twin Bite, allowing Diana to force early skirmishes without fear of being locked down.

summary: Teemo's Move Quick allows him to easily stay out of Fling range while applying constant Toxic Shot poison to punish Singed's farm attempts.
howToPlay: Never chase Singed directly when he retreats, as running into his Poison Trail is his only way to deal damage to you. Instead, hold your Move Quick specifically for when he drops Mega Adhesive or tries to rush you with his passive speed. To secure your lead, pivot your build toward raw magic penetration and consistent slows to completely shut down his defensive scaling. If he flips you with Fling, immediately blind him with Blinding Dart to mitigate his basic attacks during his escape.
laneImpact: Singed is entirely starved of gold and forced to suffer under his own turret, unable to proxy-farm behind your tower. Because you constantly chip away his health with Toxic Shot, he must burn through his potions early or recall repeatedly. You will establish a permanent slow-push, securing total lane control and forcing him to waste his ultimate, Insanity Potion, purely for survival rather than roaming.
why: Teemo dominates this matchup by capitalizing on a massive range advantage. By utilizing Move Quick, you can effortlessly stay outside the initiation range of Singed's Fling. Whenever Singed attempts to approach the wave, his lack of gap-closers leaves him completely exposed to relentless basic attacks amplified by Toxic Shot, rendering his Poison Trail useless as he is forced to retreat.

summary: Tempered Fate is an excellent tool to interrupt Seraphine's Encore or freeze her before she can cast her high-impact spells.
howToPlay: To win this matchup, hold Tempered Fate specifically for when Seraphine begins her Encore animation or when she groups with her allies to cast Surround Sound. Position yourself near the side walls to threaten a Cosmic Binding stun whenever she steps up to poke. If she plays too safely, use Magical Journey to flank her from the jungle, catching her from behind before she can react with Beat Drop.
laneImpact: During the laning phase, Seraphine will try to shove the wave using High Note and poke you down. However, her aggressive pushing makes her incredibly susceptible to ganks. If she mispositions to land a Stage Presence passive attack, you can easily punish her with Cosmic Binding against the minion wave or walls. Once she wastes Surround Sound to absorb trades, you gain a massive window of vulnerability where her lack of mobility can be exploited.
why: Seraphine relies on long casting animations and setup to impact teamfights, particularly with her ultimate. Bard's Tempered Fate completely neutralizes this by putting her in stasis mid-cast, canceling the extension of Encore or freezing her before she can chain her Stage Presence-empowered Beat Drop. Since her defensive utility from Surround Sound has a massive cooldown, interrupting her rhythm leaves her incredibly vulnerable to your team's follow-up.

summary: Garen should save Courage to mitigate Mordekaiser's isolated Obliterate damage during Realm of Death.
howToPlay: To survive, pivot your early gold toward magic defense instead of raw damage. During skirmishes, your primary goal is to bait his abilities. When Mordekaiser pulls you into Realm of Death, never panic. You must absolutely save Courage to block his isolated Obliterate strike inside his ultimate. Use Decisive Strike to cleanse his slows, then spin with Judgment to shred him, but keep your defensive shield held strictly for his highest burst moment.
laneImpact: You will constantly find yourself pushed under turret, as Mordekaiser easily clears waves while poking you with Obliterate. Trading directly is perilous because any extended fight triggers his passive aura. This constant pressure limits your ability to roam, forcing you to utilize Perseverance frequently under your tower to sustain through his relentless magic damage harass and avoid being forced into early, disadvantageous recalls.
why: Mordekaiser dominates this matchup by turning the lane into a raw test of stats where Garen struggles to match his magic damage. Once Darkness Rise activates, his persistent aura melts your health, while Death's Grasp keeps you from easily disengaging. If you try to execute him with Demacian Justice, his Indestructible shield can completely deny your ultimate, making standard short trades highly ineffective.

summary: Use Apprehend to disrupt Urgot's Disdain dash mid-animation to prevent him from flipping and shielding.
howToPlay: Never use Disdain proactively while Darius has Apprehend available. Instead, bait his pull by moving just within its edge, then immediately buffer your dash or use Corrosive Charge to slow him down. If he wastes Apprehend, you have a brief window to turn on Purge and rotate your Echoing Flames shotgun knees. If he catches you, save Fear Beyond Death for a maximum range execution only after his Decimate has missed.
laneImpact: This interaction forces you to play defensively near your turret. Initiating any trade with Disdain is extremely risky; if Darius interrupts your dash, you lose your primary defensive tool and cannot out-damage his Decimate healing. You must concede early wave control, farming safely from a distance with Corrosive Charge while preventing him from getting easy execution resets with Noxian Guillotine.
why: Darius dominates this matchup because his Apprehend can cancel Urgot's Disdain mid-dash. If you try to escape or engage with your shield, a reactive pull from Darius stops you completely, leaving you without your shield or displacement. This allows him to easily stack his Hemorrhage passive using Crippling Strike, turning what should be a safe retreat into a lethal chase.

summary: Bard can use Magical Journey to escape Nami's Tidal Wave or use Tempered Fate to freeze her team during her engage.
howToPlay: To win this positioning battle, stand parallel to your ADC to split Nami's Ebb and Flow targets, preventing her from getting double bounces. Never use Magical Journey aggressively if Nami has Tidal Wave available; instead, hug walls so you can immediately open a portal to escape her wave. If she initiates from afar, hold Tempered Fate to freeze her incoming follow-up attackers rather than trying to hit Nami herself, effectively wasting her engage window.
laneImpact: Both of you constantly fight for bush control to land your respective skillshots. While Nami uses Tidecaller's Blessing to help her ADC push waves and poke, you must counteract this sustained damage by preparing Caretaker’s Shrine relics behind your tower. Missing a Cosmic Binding or stepping into an Aqua Prison instantly swings the lane pressure, forcing early recalls and letting Nami's lane partner crash waves to secure plate gold.
why: This matchup is a constant trade war where positioning dictates survival. Nami relies on the bouncing heals of Ebb and Flow to dominate short trades, while Bard matches this pressure with Cosmic Binding stuns. The lane remains perfectly even because Bard can completely neutralize Nami’s massive Tidal Wave engages, either by escaping through Magical Journey or using Tempered Fate to freeze Nami's allies mid-initiation.

summary: Janna can use the movement speed from Tailwind to help her ADC dodge Aqua Prison, but must watch out for Nami's Ebb and Flow bounce trades.
howToPlay: To win this, maintain a strict diagonal spacing: stay near enough to your marksman so Tailwind helps them dodge Aqua Prison, but never stand close enough to let Ebb and Flow bounce between you. Hold Eye of the Storm specifically to mitigate the extra damage from Tidecaller's Blessing. If Nami initiates with Tidal Wave, immediately react with Monsoon to push her carries away and reset the fight.
laneImpact: The laning phase revolves around baiting key cooldowns. When Nami misses Aqua Prison, she loses all lane pressure, allowing you to walk up and secure wave priority. But if her Ebb and Flow bounces successfully during skirmishes, your ADC will slowly get poked out of lane. This constant trading dance dictates who controls the brush, directly impacting your ADC's safety during farming.
why: This lane is a pure duel of enchanter utility. Your passive Tailwind provides your marksman with the essential movement speed required to reactively sidestep Nami's slow-moving Aqua Prison. However, you cannot simply trade passively; Nami will exploit any close-range posturing by casting Ebb and Flow, which bounces to heal her ally while chipping away at your health bar, punishing static positioning.

summary: Amumu can interrupt Vi's Vault Breaker or lock her down with Curse of the Sad Mummy immediately after she lands Cease and Desist.
howToPlay: When contesting camps or objectives, never throw Bandage Toss blindly. Instead, walk up with Despair active and wait for her to wind up Vault Breaker, then interrupt her mid-dash. If she targets your carry with Cease and Desist, position yourself right next to her target. The millisecond she finishes her unstoppable animation, unleash Curse of the Sad Mummy to disable her before she can proc Denting Blows.
laneImpact: In skirmishes around the river or during counter-ganks, this matchup prevents Vi from playing aggressively. She cannot safely execute her gank combos because you can reactively shut down her dive. If she tries to match your clear speed, Despair and Tantrum allow you to sweep through camps faster, giving you the priority to setup objectives while forcing her to hold her dash.
why: You hold the upper hand because Vi relies heavily on charging Vault Breaker to initiate or escape, which you can easily disrupt with Bandage Toss. Furthermore, her ultimate Cease and Desist makes her unstoppable during the dash, but the exact moment she lands, she is highly vulnerable. You can instantly buffer Curse of the Sad Mummy to lock her down, rendering her initial burst useless.

summary: Olaf's Ragnarok makes him completely immune to the pull and slow of Moonfall, allowing him to easily run Diana down.
howToPlay: To survive this matchup, you must track his ultimate cooldown meticulously. Never initiate with Moonfall if you suspect Ragnarok is available; instead, poke from a distance using Crescent Strike. If he charges at you, use Pale Cascade to absorb the initial burst from Reckless Swing and retreat. Only engage in skirmishes when you can target his vulnerable allies, or wait out the duration of his crowd-control immunity before committing your full burst.
laneImpact: In the jungle, this interaction makes direct duels near the Rift Scuttler or inside your own camps extremely dangerous. You cannot contest neutral objectives alone because Olaf will force an all-in the moment you step up. If he hits you with Undertow, you are forced to retreat using Lunar Rush on a distant monster, costing you tempo and leaving your camps open to aggressive counter-jungling.
why: Your ultimate combo relies heavily on pulling enemies in to burst them down, but Olaf completely shuts this down. When he activates Ragnarok, he gains absolute immunity to the displacement and slowing effects of Moonfall. Without this crowd control, Diana cannot stop his advance, and he can easily shrug off your initial damage while tearing you apart in close quarters with his high physical damage.

summary: Block the stun from Camille's Hookshot with a well-timed Repudiation, neutralizing her main engage tool.
howToPlay: To win this duel, you must manipulate Ambessa's reaction times. Never use Hookshot directly onto her from max range. Instead, latch onto a wall and delay your second cast, or dive slightly to the side to bait her Repudiation shield. Once her shield expires, immediately engage with Precision Protocol to trade while her defenses are down and your Adaptive Defenses shield is ready to absorb her counter-attack.
laneImpact: Every trade in the lane hinges on this single cooldown window. If Ambessa holds Repudiation, Camille is forced to play defensively, using Tactical Sweep from a distance to secure minions and match wave clear. If Camille misses or has her Hookshot countered, Ambessa will relentlessly chase her down with Lacerate and Cunning Sweep, forcing Camille to concede priority or risk getting executed by Public Execution.
why: This skill matchup revolves entirely around the interaction between Camille's Hookshot and Ambessa's Repudiation. When Camille launches off the wall, Ambessa can reactively cast Repudiation to completely absorb the impact, nullifying the stun while generating a shield that absorbs Camille's follow-up Precision Protocol strike. Without the crowd control from her main mobility tool, Camille is left vulnerable to Ambessa's rapid Drakehound's Step dashes.

summary: Sett can pull Jarvan IV out of his E-Q dash with Facebreaker if timed perfectly, or absorb the Cataclysm burst with Haymaker.
howToPlay: To survive, you must bait out Sett's key defensive tools. Never initiate with your Demacian Standard and Dragon Strike combo unless his Facebreaker is on cooldown. Instead, poke him with single Martial Cadence attacks and walk back. If he misses his pull, that is your cue to trade. When using Cataclysm, immediately walk or flash out of the center line of his Haymaker to avoid the true damage zone while his shield decays.
laneImpact: This dynamic turns the lane into a battle of attrition where Sett slowly squeezes you out. If you blindly use your flag-and-drag, he will pull you in, activate Knuckle Down, and trade back with superior sustain. You cannot easily crash waves or force early recalls, meaning you are often stuck under tower, relying on Golden Aegis to survive chip damage while he maintains priority.
why: Sett heavily punishes your signature combo because Facebreaker can interrupt your Dragon Strike mid-air if he reacts to your Demacian Standard placement. Even if you connect, his Pit Grit passive gives him continuous health regeneration that outvalues your Martial Cadence poke. Furthermore, trying to execute him with Cataclysm is highly risky, as he can simply absorb your entire burst with the massive shield from Haymaker and retaliate with true damage.

summary: Syndra's Scatter the Weak can knock Annie back mid-walk, preventing her from closing the distance to cast Summon: Tibbers.
howToPlay: To survive, never walk directly at Syndra when her Scatter the Weak is available. Instead, activate Molten Shield for the burst of movement speed and feign an aggressive step forward, then quickly dodge sideways to bait her knockback. Once she wastes her defensive sphere push, you have a brief window to flash-forward and unleash Summon: Tibbers combined with Incinerate. If she holds her spell, reset your position and farm safely.
laneImpact: You are forced onto the defensive, spending most of the early game farming under turret with Disintegrate. Because you cannot safely close the gap, Syndra freely harasses you using Dark Sphere and Force of Will while you try to last-hit. This constant harassment depletes your Molten Shield quickly, forcing early recalls and letting Syndra secure mid priority to stack her Transcendent passive safely.
why: Syndra completely controls this lane by exploiting your shorter reach. While you want to charge Pyromania and run forward to drop Summon: Tibbers, Syndra denies this easily. The moment you step up, she casts Scatter the Weak to shove you backward mid-walk. This knockback, especially when combined with a Dark Sphere, halts your advance and leaves you stunned out of range, unable to retaliate.

summary: Vladimir can use Sanguine Pool to dodge Garen's Demacian Justice, making it crucial to silence him first with Decisive Strike.
howToPlay: Back away immediately when his blood bar fills, indicating an empowered Transfusion. To engage, bait his Sanguine Pool by running at him with Decisive Strike activated, but do not strike immediately; instead, spin with Judgment to shred his armor. Save your Demacian Justice until he is silenced by your Decisive Strike, or after his pool has ended. If you get chunked down, let Perseverance heal you safely behind your minions.
laneImpact: Since Vladimir has no resource costs and heals off waves, trading health is usually a losing battle unless you fight during his specific ability downtimes. You will often find yourself pushed under turret, absorbing pressure while your Courage shields his fully charged Tides of Blood hits. If you fail to respect his third Transfusion spike, you will be forced into a bad recall, forfeiting lane priority.
why: Vladimir slowly wears you down with ranged Transfusion pokes while matching your Perseverance passive regeneration. The lane becomes a battle of attrition where you can't easily execute him. He holds a massive defensive tool: Sanguine Pool completely nullifies your ultimate, Demacian Justice. To secure any kill threat, you are forced to shut down his escape route by landing Decisive Strike first, preventing him from slipping away.

summary: When Ekko commits with Phase Dive, Annie can instantly stun him with Pyromania, preventing him from escaping with Chronobreak.
howToPlay: To execute this flawlessly, always maintain at least three stacks of Pyromania. When Ekko steps up, bait him by walking near his Parallel Convergence zone but use the movement speed from Molten Shield to escape it. Hold your stun specifically for his Phase Dive; never waste your passive on a random Disintegrate poke if he has his dash up. If he manages to activate Chronobreak, wait out his return location to drop Summon: Tibbers right where his hologram lands.
laneImpact: This interaction forces Ekko into a defensive posture, fearing to step up for CS. You can freely harass him with Disintegrate whenever he tries to clear waves with Timewinder. Because his engage is so heavily punished, Ekko cannot easily contest lane priority or secure clean recalls. If he attempts a desperate dive under your turret, Pyromania combined with Summon: Tibbers guarantees an easy kill while Molten Shield mitigates his initial burst.
why: Annie dictates this lane because Ekko must cross into her range to threaten a kill. Whenever Ekko dashes forward using Phase Dive, he locks himself into a predictable trajectory. Annie can immediately shut down this aggression by triggering Pyromania with Disintegrate or Incinerate. Stunning him mid-dash prevents him from triggering Z-Drive Resonance, leaving him completely vulnerable and unable to safely reset his health bar with Chronobreak.

summary: Smoke Screen can slow Hecarim and reduce his vision, neutralizing the bonus damage from Devastating Charge before he reaches Graves.
howToPlay: To secure your advantage, never engage in a straight line where Smoke Screen easily intercepts your run. Instead, initiate with Onslaught of Shadows from over a wall to fear Graves instantly, bypassing his blind entirely. If he attempts to escape with Quickdraw, immediately activate Devastating Charge to run him down. Alternatively, hold your speed boost until you see his smoke canister fly, dodging laterally to maintain your Warpath momentum and crush him.
laneImpact: This dynamic forces Graves to play defensively, fearing your flanking potential. Since he cannot easily stack True Grit against your magic damage from Spirit of Dread, his armor-stacking advantage is minimized. If you control the jungle corridors, Graves is forced to use End of the Line purely to clear camps rather than harass, yielding crab priority and allowing you to invade his camps with impunity.
why: Hecarim naturally dominates this jungle duel because Rampage easily out-sustains Graves' limited reload-based DPS. However, the matchup pivots around Graves using Smoke Screen to block your approach. The near-sightedness and slow from this utility grenade completely halt Devastating Charge, stripping away your Warpath bonus Attack Damage and preventing you from landing your crucial displacement tool before he can Quickdraw away.

summary: Kayle's lack of early mobility makes her an easy target for your Shuriken Flip (E) and Perfect Execution (R) all-ins before she can protect herself with Divine Judgment (R).
howToPlay: Harass her constantly with Five Point Strike whenever she tries to last hit. Once she uses Celestial Blessing for movement speed, immediately launch Shuriken Flip. If she has reached level five, use the first dash of Perfect Execution to force out Divine Judgment, hide inside Twilight Shroud to wait out her invulnerability, then execute her with the second dash.
laneImpact: This matchup is a ticking clock where you hold all the cards early. Kayle is forced to play passively, relying on Starfire Spellblade and Radiant Blast to secure minions from safety. You can easily freeze or slow-push to deny her gold, delaying her Divine Ascent power spikes and rendering her useless for early map skirmishes.
why: Kayle's complete lack of early defensive mobility makes her incredibly vulnerable to your burst. Before she unlocks Divine Judgment, she has no reliable way to survive your all-in. You can easily tag her with Shuriken Flip when she steps up to farm, following up with Perfect Execution to secure a kill before she can react with Celestial Blessing.

summary: Aatrox must space his Q sweetspots to prevent Volibear from reaching him with Thundering Smash and applying Frenzied Maul.
howToPlay: Never initiate with Umbral Dash forward; instead, save this dash to disengage or reposition laterally when Volibear charges with Thundering Smash. Use Infernal Chains defensively to pull him back if he tries to run you down. If he successfully shields himself with Sky Splitter, back off immediately and wait for the shield to decay before resuming your The Darkin Blade chain. If you get chunked, play safely around your Deathbringer Stance cooldown to recover.
laneImpact: Because both of you possess immense sustain, short trades rarely stick unless someone gets zoned off the minions. Pushing Volibear under his turret can be dangerous because Stormbringer disables your tower during dives, but keeping the wave frozen near your side forces him to overextend. A single mistake in wave placement allows Volibear to drop Sky Splitter to shield himself while crashing the waves.
why: This matchup is a constant battle of recovery where your Deathbringer Stance and Umbral Dash passive compete directly against Volibear's Frenzied Maul healing. The entire lane hinges on distance. If you fail to space the sweetspots of The Darkin Blade, the bear will activate Thundering Smash to close the gap, stun you, and easily mark you for a devastating second bite.

summary: Cho'Gath must use Cri primal to silence Volibear and prevent him from getting a second bite with Frenzied Maul.
howToPlay: When Volibear runs at you with Thundering Smash, do not panic-cast Rupture immediately, as he can dodge it or close the gap during the cast time. Instead, wait for him to land the stun and apply the first mark of Frenzied Maul. Immediately upon recovery, blast him with Feral Scream to silence him, preventing the second bite, then use Vorpal Spikes and Rupture to disengage safely while Carnivore recovers your health.
laneImpact: Since Volibear can crash waves easily with The Relentless Storm and dive you post-level 5 using Stormbringer, you cannot afford to drop low. If he marks you with Frenzied Maul and you fail to disengage, his healing forces you out of lane, costing you plates. However, executing short trades keeps your health bar high enough to neutralise his dive threat and scale safely.
why: Volibear thrives in extended duels due to Frenzied Maul, which heals him and deals massive damage on the second bite, supported by the attack speed of The Relentless Storm. Cho'Gath can win the sustain war using Carnivore on minions, but only if he denies Volibear's healing. This matchup hinges on using Feral Scream to block the second cast of Frenzied Maul, cutting the demigod's trading power in half.

summary: The constant slows from your Frost Shot passive directly reduce Kalista's Martial Poise jump speed, severely limiting her mobility and attack speed.
howToPlay: Maintain a strict spacing rule by staying at your maximum attack range to abuse her slowed movement. Never let her get close enough to stack multiple spears for a deadly Rend. Keep your Enchanted Crystal Arrow ready to lock her down completely if she mispositions away from her partner. If she manages to jump forward using Pierce, immediately use Volley to break her momentum, then walk backward to reset your spacing.
laneImpact: In the lane, this interaction allows you to dictate every trade. When Kalista tries to step up to secure last hits with Rend, you can punish her with Volley from a safe distance. Since she cannot easily jump away while slowed, you can easily stack Ranger's Focus on her. This constant pressure forces her to concede wave control, preventing her from setting up aggressive Fate's Call engagements.
why: This matchup is heavily in your favor because of how Frost Shot interacts with Martial Poise. Every single one of your basic attacks or a well-placed Volley applies a slow that directly cripples the speed of Kalista's dash animations. By slowing down her jumps, you actively reduce her effective attack speed and mobility, turning her signature kiting tool into a sluggish liability.

summary: Both champions have high early burst, but Lucian can use Relentless Pursuit to dodge Avengerang and return fire with Lightslinger.
howToPlay: Never initiate with Avengerang while Lucian's Relentless Pursuit is off cooldown. Instead, walk up to trigger your Dirty Fighting double-shot and shield. This forces him to either back off or use his dash defensively. Once Relentless Pursuit is spent, immediately throw your boomerang to secure the hit. If he tries to escape or turn with The Culling, use Heroic Swing to rotate behind him or escape his linear firing path.
laneImpact: One mistimed trade dictates the entire laning phase. If Lucian successfully dodges your boomerang, his double-tap burst forces you to retreat under turret, forfeiting Dragon priority and risking a dive. Conversely, if you clip him with Avengerang first and ignite your Dirty Fighting shield, his health bar melts, giving you complete control over the wave and forcing him to waste his recall.
why: This matchup is a volatile duel of instant bursts in the Dragon lane. Your early trades hinge entirely on the trajectory of Avengerang. If you throw it blindly, Lucian will instantly react with Relentless Pursuit to slip past the projectile, positioning himself to unload a devastating Lightslinger double-tap. Because both of you possess lethal frontloaded damage, whoever baits the other's movement tool wins the immediate engagement.

summary: Caitlyn can place Yordle Snap Trap along walls to block Akshan's Heroic Swing pathing, forcing him to play defensively.
howToPlay: Establish a strict positioning rule: always stay near the center of the lane while keeping your Yordle Snap Trap charges reserved specifically for the terrain nearest to his current position. Never waste 90 Caliber Net offensively; hold it to disengage if he finds an angle around your traps. If he attempts to channel Comeuppance, immediately step behind your minion wave or use your traps to disrupt his pathing and walk out of his vision.
laneImpact: This restriction forces Akshan to play incredibly defensively, stripping away his ability to trade with Dirty Fighting shields. With his main escape route blocked by your wall traps, you can safely shove waves using Piltover Peacemaker. He is forced to farm under turret, bleeding health whenever he steps up, which quickly translates into early plate gold and total dragon-side priority.
why: Caitlyn dominates this matchup by completely neutralizing Akshan's main mobility tool. Because Akshan relies on hugging terrain to launch his Heroic Swing, strategically placing your Yordle Snap Trap along the lane walls creates an impassable barrier for his grapple. Attempting to swing through these zones instantly roots him, leaving him vulnerable to a guaranteed Headshot follow-up while denying him any aggressive gap-close.

howToPlay: Positioning: keep moving to avoid telegraphed charges and use the wave so he can’t hit you for free. Priority: break his shield as soon as it appears. Key timing: when he starts a long animation (charge), punish or back off, but don’t hover in-between. Clear decisions keep you safe. Decision-making: convert prio into real value. Take a plate when safe. If you sense gank/ult risk, reset and show up to objective. You win by converting pressure, not by forcing flashy kills.
laneImpact: In lane you can often secure prio and control resets. Sion can tank, but he must still choose between taking the wave and preserving HP. Breaking his shield consistently heavily reduces his trade power. At level 5, his ult adds roam/catch risk, but in pure lane he remains predictable. If you respect charge angles and don’t overextend without jump, you can keep punishing. Midgame, if Sion forces front-to-back fights, your DPS value is strong. The main rule is not getting surprised by an engage from fog.
why: Sion is often favorable because you can exploit his slowness. He wants trades where he lands CC; you can chip, break shield, and punish long animations. Tristana is great at turning a slow tank into plate gold. The key: you don’t “duel” Sion, you wear him down. Use range and push to deny his preferred tempo. As long as you don’t give a free all-in, you control the lane. Your win condition is clear: prio, plates, tower, then objective rotations while he’s slow to respond.

summary: Warwick's Primal Howl damage reduction and fear can completely negate Viego's burst from Blade of the Ruined King and Spectral Maw in early 1v1s.
howToPlay: Never initiate with Spectral Maw when Warwick is healthy. Instead, bait out Primal Howl by kiting backward using the camouflage and movement speed from Harrowed Path. Once his damage reduction expires and his fear is wasted, you have a brief window to strike with Blade of the Ruined King. If he catches you with Infinite Duress, immediately use Heartbreaker defensively to reposition over a wall to survive his relentless pursuit.
laneImpact: This matchup forces you off active scuttle crab contests and early invades. If Warwick tracks you with Blood Hunt, he can force duels you cannot win, leaving you low on health and forcing premature recalls. This lack of early pressure means your laners must play defensively, as Warwick can freely dive them with Infinite Duress while you are stuck clearing camps to safely reach your item spikes.
why: Warwick absolutely dominates the early jungle duels because his Primal Howl grants immense damage reduction right when you try to burst him down with Blade of the Ruined King and Spectral Maw. Once the damage reduction ends, the subsequent fear interrupts your basic attack flow, letting his Eternal Hunger and Jaws of the Beast easily out-sustain your damage before you can ever trigger Sovereign's Domination.

summary: The knockup from any of your The Darkin Blade casts immediately cancels Fiddlesticks' Bountiful Harvest channel.
howToPlay: Do not throw away The Darkin Blade blindly. When you engage, lead with Infernal Chains to slow him and pull him back, then wait for him to panic and activate Bountiful Harvest. The second his draining channel animation starts, unleash your first or second The Darkin Blade sweetspot, using Umbral Dash if needed to adjust your range. If he attempts to escape using Terrify, immediately pop World Ender to close the distance and run him down with your increased movement speed.
laneImpact: In the jungle, this interaction turns Fiddlesticks' camps into a dangerous zone for him. You can aggressively invade his territory, knowing that if you catch him clearing with Bountiful Harvest, a quick knockup secures an easy kill. He cannot contest scuttle crabs or neutral objectives directly because your threat of interrupting his drain forces him to play defensively, ruining his early clearing tempo and map pressure.
why: This matchup swings heavily in your favor because you hold a hard stop to Fiddlesticks' primary tool. Whenever the scarecrow begins to drain you with Bountiful Harvest, any of your sweetspot strikes from The Darkin Blade will immediately interrupt his channel. This completely denies his healing and massive damage, leaving him incredibly vulnerable as his key combat ability goes on a long cooldown.

summary: Ambessa can block Viego's Spectral Maw stun with Repudiation, turning the duel in her favor before he can stack Blade of the Ruined King.
howToPlay: To survive, never initiate with Spectral Maw. Instead, activate Harrowed Path near walls to gain attack speed and force her to guess your position. Bait out her Repudiation by charging your stun without releasing it immediately. Once her shield expires, launch Spectral Maw to lock her down, then quickly stack Blade of the Ruined King. If she activates Public Execution, use Heartbreaker to dodge the trajectory and reposition to safety.
laneImpact: This interaction forces you to cede early river priority and scuttle crab contests. If Ambessa catches you in the river, she can force a fight where Public Execution will execute you if you drop low. You cannot contest her invades directly, meaning your clear speed and neutral objective fights are constantly delayed, forcing you to play defensively around your turrets.
why: Ambessa holds a massive advantage in direct skirmishes because her Repudiation completely absorbs the stun of your Spectral Maw while granting her a shield. This denial prevents you from safely applying and detonating the marks from Blade of the Ruined King. Without this burst healing and damage, Ambessa easily out-duels you using Drakehound's Step and Lacerate to dance around your Harrowed Path mist.

summary: Vayne must use Tumble to dodge Yunara's Arc of Judgment poke while using Condemn to disengage if Yunara activates Transcend One's Self.
howToPlay: To survive, you must play reactively and respect her cooldowns. Save Tumble exclusively to dodge sideways when she casts Arc of Judgment, neutralizing her main poke tool. If she decides to commit by activating Transcend One's Self to chase you down, immediately use Condemn to shove her away and disengage. Never initiate trades without Final Hour active, and prioritize safety over aggressive positioning until you have your ultimate.
laneImpact: Expect to spend most of the early game farming under your turret. Yunara's Cultivation of Spirit allows her attacks to bounce through your minion wave, pushing you back and chipping at your health. Attempting to proc Silver Bolts will often result in taking heavy counter-poke. You must accept losing some gold to keep your health bar high enough to prevent dive setups and maintain presence for future map skirmishes.
why: This matchup is highly unfavorable due to Yunara's superior range and the hybrid damage scaling from Vow of the First Lands. Her primary zoning tool, Arc of Judgment, slows you down and sets up her aggressive bursts. Once she activates her ultimate, Transcend One's Self, she gains access to enhanced mobility and a devastating linear beam that completely outranges your basic attacks, making raw trades extremely dangerous.

summary: Once Lux misses her Light Binding, Ahri can freely dash forward with Spirit Rush to secure an easy kill.
howToPlay: Never cast Light Binding aggressively unless Ahri has already exhausted her Spirit Rush charges. Instead, rely on Lucent Singularity to slowly chip away at her health and trigger Illumination with safe basic attacks. If she dashes aggressively towards you, immediately cast Prismatic Barrier to mitigate the incoming Fox-Fire and Orb of Deception damage while falling back. Keep your distance and only throw your binding defensively when her dash trajectory is predictable.
laneImpact: Before level five, you can match her Orb of Deception waveclear using Lucent Singularity. However, once Spirit Rush is unlocked, the lane dynamic shifts dramatically. Missing a single Light Binding forces you to retreat entirely behind your turret, giving Ahri total control of the wave. This allows her to clear with Fox-Fire and roam to side lanes while you are stuck safely clearing under tower.
why: This matchup is dictated by the threat of your Light Binding against Ahri's ultimate mobility. While you can poke safely with Lucent Singularity, Ahri's Spirit Rush allows her to easily dodge your skillshots. If you throw out Light Binding and miss, she can immediately dash forward with Spirit Rush, bypassing your minions to land an easy Charm and burst you down before your main self-peel returns.

summary: Lillia's Blooming Blows and high movement speed allow her to easily kite Jax, as Counter Strike cannot block her spell-based damage.
howToPlay: Never initiate a fight with Leap Strike. Instead, walk up to camps or objectives, and save Leap Strike either as an escape tool over walls or to gap-close only after Lillia has missed her Swirlseed or committed Watch Out! Eep!. When she activates Lilting Lullaby, immediately use Leap Strike to jump to a blast cone, ward, or monster to put distance between you before the sleep kicks in.
laneImpact: You cannot contest scuttle crabs or direct skirmishes early on. If you jump in, Lillia will hit you with Swirlseed, slow you down, and run circles around you. This forces you to concede early river priority and play a reactive game. If she catches you in the river, she can easily poke you down and set up Lilting Lullaby to secure a kill or force your escape tools.
why: Lillia is a nightmare encounter for you because your defensive signature, Counter Strike, only dodges basic attacks. Since Lillia's damage comes entirely from spells like Blooming Blows and Watch Out! Eep!, your evasion is useless. Worse, every time she hits you, she gains massive movement speed from Blooming Blows, allowing her to dance just out of reach of your club.

summary: Vayne can easily dodge Rupture with Tumble, then proceed to shred Cho'Gath's massive health pool with Silver Bolts.
howToPlay: To survive, completely concede early lane priority and let the wave crash. Never initiate with Rupture; hold it until she commits Tumble forward or use it strictly to farm from safety. When she pushes you under tower, lead with Feral Scream to silence her roll and knockback, preventing her from using Condemn against the tower walls, then use Vorpal Spikes to quickly clear the wave and trigger Carnivore.
laneImpact: You will spend the entire laning phase trapped under your own turret. Vayne's Night Hunter allows her to aggressively posture and deny you access to the minion wave. Attempting to walk up to trigger Carnivore results in heavy punishment, as she will easily proc Silver Bolts. This constant pressure forces terrible recall timings, leaving your tower vulnerable while she scales out of control.
why: This matchup is a nightmare because Vayne completely neutralizes your main threat. Whenever you cast Rupture to catch her, she easily sidesteps it using Tumble. Once your primary crowd control is on cooldown, she can freely abuse her ranged advantage to trigger Silver Bolts, melting your health pool with maximum health true damage that renders your hard-earned Feast stacks counterproductive.

summary: Lux can easily land Light Binding on you while you are stationary during your Breath of Light channel.
howToPlay: To survive, never tap Breath of Light unless Lux has just wasted Light Binding, or you are safely positioned behind at least two minions to block its trajectory. If she holds her root, focus on dropping Singularity to farm from afar and conserve your Astral Flight. Should she throw her cage and miss, immediately activate Astral Flight diagonally to reposition while blasting her, forcing her to rely on Prismatic Barrier to absorb your retaliation.
laneImpact: Because of this threat, you cannot freely clear waves with Breath of Light without risking a lethal trade. If you get rooted under her turret or in the middle of the lane, she will strip your health, forcing early recalls that delay your Cosmic Creator stacking. Consequently, you must often concede mid priority, allowing Lux to shove waves with Lucent Singularity and threaten your side lanes while you struggle to collect Stardust safely.
why: This matchup revolves around a dangerous vulnerability during your main damage tool. Whenever you channel Breath of Light, you become a completely static target, making you incredibly easy prey for Lux's Light Binding. If she catches you with this root, she can immediately follow up with Lucent Singularity and Final Spark to delete your health bar. Your immobile state turns her skillshots from speculative pokes into guaranteed hits.

summary: Pantheon can block Mega Gnar's ultimate damage and stun follow-up by facing him with Aegis Assault.
howToPlay: To win, space carefully when Gnar's Rage Gene is nearly full. Do not panic-use Aegis Assault on his Hop; instead, hold it specifically for the moment he winds up Boulder Toss. If he misses or you block his ultimate, immediately retaliate with an empowered Shield Vault followed by Comet Spear. If you misstime your shield and get stunned, disengage immediately using Grand Starfall to reset your map presence rather than fighting his high-health Mega form.
laneImpact: During Mini Gnar phases, he will try to poke you down with Boomerang Throw and trigger Hyper. However, your threat of a Mortal Will-empowered Shield Vault keeps him from playing too aggressively. Once Gnar's Rage Gene peaks, he is forced to seek a wall-slam. Because you can deny this with Aegis Assault, you control the wave state, forcing Gnar to waste his Mega form farming under tower or taking bad trades.
why: Pantheon dominates this matchup because he can completely neutralize Mega Gnar's most threatening burst. When Gnar builds up his Rage Gene and transforms, his ultimate playmaking tool, Boulder Toss, becomes highly predictable. By using Aegis Assault directly facing Mega Gnar, you block the massive impact damage and the subsequent wall-stun, leaving Gnar vulnerable and motionless while his tanky form's cooldowns are spent.

summary: Vayne can easily push Garen away with Condemn whenever he uses Decisive Strike to try and close the distance.
howToPlay: To survive, sacrifice gold and focus on securing experience. Keep the wave just outside your turret's range to minimize her chase space. Never use Decisive Strike offensively unless she wastes Condemn. Instead, hold Courage to absorb the third strike of Silver Bolts when she pokes you under tower. If she freezes the lane near her turret, do not walk up; hide in the brush and let her push back.
laneImpact: You are forced into a purely defensive posture, trapped under your turret while Vayne dictates the minion waves. Attempting to contest farm results in her triggering Silver Bolts repeatedly, forcing early recalls that cost massive gold and experience. Because you cannot trade back, Vayne freely chips away at your tower plates, securing a massive gold advantage while scaling safely into a late-game threat without any map pressure from your side.
why: This matchup is highly unfavorable for Garen because Vayne completely neutralizes your engage. Every time you activate Decisive Strike to cleanse slows and rush toward her, she can instantly cast Condemn to knock you back before you can strike. This denial, paired with her Tumble to dodge and Silver Bolts to shred your health with true damage, makes closing the distance nearly impossible without a mistake on her part.

summary: Skarner can use Impale to suppress Lillia and drag her into his team, but she can easily kite his Shattered Earth outside of his ultimate range.
howToPlay: To win this, you must hold Ixtal's Impact until Lillia commits her dash from Watch Out! Eep! or is slowed by Seismic Bastion. Never chase her in open areas where Blooming Blows stacks are high. Instead, position yourself inside tight jungle corridors where she has less room to dodge. If she hits you with Swirlseed and prepares Lilting Lullaby, retreat toward a wall so you can escape or counter-engage immediately once the sleep wears off.
laneImpact: In the jungle, this translates to highly volatile skirmishes around camps and objectives. Lillia will attempt to poke with Swirlseed and clear camps quickly, using her speed to avoid Ixtal's Impact. If Skarner fails to pin her near walls, she dictates the pace of the map. However, if Skarner secures a flank, his threat of Impale forces Lillia to play extremely passively, giving Skarner's team priority over neutral monsters.
why: Skarner's ability to lock down Lillia rests entirely on landing Impale to drag her back, neutralizing her high mobility. However, Lillia's passive from Blooming Blows grants her massive movement speed, allowing her to dance outside his range. She can easily dodge Shattered Earth throws and out-kite his slow-moving melee threat, making the matchup a tense game of spacing where one misstep from either jungler determines the fight.

summary: Darius easily wins extended duels against Viego by stacking Hemorrhage, as long as he dodges or pulls Viego out of Spectral Maw.
howToPlay: Never fight Darius alone without a massive health advantage. Track his pathing and invade the opposite side of the map to secure camps safely. When skirmishing with allies, do not initiate with Spectral Maw; hold it until Darius locks himself in his Decimate animation so he cannot dodge or pull you with Apprehend. If he stacks Hemorrhage to four, immediately disengage using Harrowed Path towards a wall to escape his execution range.
laneImpact: Darius will actively seek to invade your camps, knowing he wins 1v1 clashes. If he invades you while you are clearing with Harrowed Path, you are forced to retreat and cede camp priority, which slows down your gold generation. This pressure forces your laners to play defensively, as any skirmish near the river risks giving Darius an easy reset chain with Noxian Guillotine.
why: Direct duels in the river are lethal because Darius thrives on the extended skirmishes Viego usually wants. Your DPS relies on continuous Blade of the Ruined King procs, but this gives Darius the exact time he needs to stack Hemorrhage. If Darius uses Apprehend to cancel your Spectral Maw dash or simply sidesteps it, his Noxian Guillotine will execute you before your passive can trigger.

summary: Nami can bubble Alistar's ADC with Aqua Prison when Alistar engages, turning his dive into a split-focus trade.
howToPlay: To win this matchup, stand slightly parallel to your ADC to bait Nami's skillshots without letting her hit both of you. Never use *Headbutt* unless *Aqua Prison* has just missed, or you can immediately follow up with *Trample* to chain-cc her. If she holds her bubble, use *Headbutt* defensively to knock her away when she steps up to poke with *Ebb and Flow*.
laneImpact: Because *Triumphant Roar* offers slower passive healing compared to the immediate bounce of *Ebb and Flow*, you cannot afford bad trades. A split-focus fight caused by a mistimed dive forces your partner to retreat, granting Nami's lane massive wave control. Missed engages translate directly to being shoved under turret, where Nami can freely poke with *Tidecaller's Blessing* empowered attacks.
why: This lane is a constant balance between your engage potential and Nami's defensive disruption. The core danger lies in how she responds to your forward dive. If you commit with *Headbutt* and *Pulverize*, Nami will bypass you entirely to launch *Aqua Prison* directly at your follow-up shooter. This splits the focus, leaving you deep in enemy territory while your partner is bubbled.

summary: Mundo's passive Goes Where He Pleases completely blocks Vi's Vault Breaker or Cease and Desist, denying her primary engage tool.
howToPlay: Monitor your passive status constantly; never contest neutral objectives if Goes Where He Pleases is on cooldown. When Vi charges Vault Breaker, stand in front of your squishy allies to intercept it safely. If she triggers your passive, rush to collect the canister immediately to restore health and lower the cooldown. Activate Heart Zapper during her Relentless Force flurry to recoup the burst damage, then pop Maximum Dosage to run her down once her mobility is exhausted.
laneImpact: In the river and during skirmishes, your immunity dictates who holds pressure. When Vi cannot rely on a sudden Vault Breaker from the fog of war, her gank potential drops drastically. She is forced to wait for your passive to be down before contesting Scuttle Crabs.
