Bait his jump with your first two strikes, using Umbral Dash defensively to create distance. Once he materializes from Alpha Strike, immediately drop Infernal Chains on him. If he triggers Highlander, use the mobility of World Ender to retreat rather than fighting.
laneImpact: In the jungle, this structural disadvantage severely limits your skirmishing power. You cannot contest objectives or duel him directly. If Master Yi invades your camps, you are forced to concede territory because a direct fight during his Highlander means he will run you down, ignoring the slow from Infernal Chains and easily dodging your critical strikes to secure free kills.
why: Master Yi naturally outscales you and hard-counters your mechanical pattern. The moment you cast the third strike of The Darkin Blade or try to pull him with Infernal Chains, his Alpha Strike grants him untargetability, completely neutralizing your crowd control. Since your healing from Umbral Dash and Deathbringer Stance relies on landing sweetspots, his evasion halts your sustain while he shreds you with Wuju Style.

summary: Rammus's Defensive Ball Curl reflects Kindred's rapid auto-attacks, and Frenzying Taunt forces her to kill herself on his armor.
howToPlay: When engaging, do not waste Frenzying Taunt immediately if Kindred has Lamb's Respite active. Instead, roll in with Powerball, activate Defensive Ball Curl to absorb her initial panic damage, and wait out the golden circle. The moment her ultimate healing zone expires, taunt her to guarantee she dies right after the effect ends. Shift your build priority heavily towards pure armor scaling early on to make your passive reflection damage lethal before she can scale.
laneImpact: This hard counter completely disrupts Kindred's hunting patterns. She cannot safely contest her Mark of the Kindred in your jungle because any 1v1 encounter ends in her demise. You can aggressively invade her camps, knowing that even if she tries to kite with Dance of Arrows, a simple Powerball collision shuts down her escape. Your presence forces her to play passively, destroying her mark-stacking tempo and neutralizing her early-game map pressure.
why: Kindred relies entirely on rapid auto-attacks to trigger Mounting Dread and maximize her damage inside Wolf's Frenzy. This plays directly into your hands. When you activate Defensive Ball Curl, her high attack speed becomes her biggest weakness. Forcing her into a duel with Frenzying Taunt obliges her to strike your spiked shell repeatedly, causing her to quickly obliterate her own health bar through your massive armor scaling.

summary: Gwen's Snip Snip! deals percentage health true damage that completely bypasses Garen's Courage shield and resistances.
howToPlay: To survive, shift your build path heavily toward magic resistance rather than general health to mitigate her A Thousand Cuts and Needlework. In lane, never initiate with Decisive Strike; save its silence and movement speed boost to cleanse the slow from Needlework and escape her zone. If she misses her fully stacked Snip Snip!, use Perseverance passively behind your turret to recover your health before attempting to contest the next wave.
laneImpact: You are forced into a defensive posture where contesting waves becomes incredibly risky. Whenever you try to clear with Judgment, Gwen can easily reposition with Skip 'n Slash to align her Snip Snip! stacks on you. This constant threat of true damage pushes you under your turret, forcing frequent recalls and sacrificing early priority, which prevents you from assisting your jungler or rotating.
why: Gwen completely neutralizes your defensive scaling because her Snip Snip! center cuts deal percentage health true damage, augmented by A Thousand Cuts. When you activate Courage to absorb her burst, its damage reduction and shield are entirely ignored by this true damage. Since your natural tankiness is bypassed, you cannot win extended trades against her continuous healing, making her scaling advantage insurmountable in straight duels.

summary: Nocturne's Shroud of Darkness can block Amumu's Bandage Toss, allowing Nocturne to fear him with Unspeakable Horror.
howToPlay: You must never lead with Bandage Toss. Walk up with Despair activated and use Tantrum to force him to panic-cast Shroud of Darkness. Only throw your bandage once his spell shield is down. If he catches you off guard with Paranoia, immediately drop Curse of the Sad Mummy to break his tempo before Unspeakable Horror triggers, then use your Bandage Toss defensively to grapple to a nearby jungle monster.
laneImpact: In the jungle, this interaction makes early scuttle duels and direct counter-jungling incredibly risky for you. If Nocturne invades, you cannot fight back without losing your primary escape tool. Once he reaches level five, his Paranoia allows him to bypass your vision and counter-gank you instantly, turning your proactive gank attempts with Curse of the Sad Mummy into deadly traps.
why: The jungle matchup hinges on a reactive game of chicken. If you initiate with Bandage Toss, Nocturne easily blocks it with Shroud of Darkness, instantly nullifying your crowd control. While you are stunned by your own failed engage, he will tether you with Unspeakable Horror, forcing a fear that shuts down your Despair and Tantrum damage, leaving you completely vulnerable.

summary: Rengar can instantly cleanse Skarner's Impale suppression using an empowered Battle Roar, neutralizing Skarner's primary pick tool.
howToPlay: To win this, you must bait out his ferocity before committing. Start skirmishes by charging with Ixtal's Impact to force him to use his abilities and build Ferocity early. Once he uses his empowered Battle Roar to heal or escape other crowd control, a wide window opens where he cannot cleanse. Only then should you unleash Impale. If he holds his stacks, focus on applying Threads of Vibration with Shattered Earth / Upheaval to grind him down instead.
laneImpact: In the jungle, this standoff delays your proactive skirmishing. You cannot easily lock him down when he jumps out of bushes with Thrill of the Hunt. If you waste your crowd control early, his high burst from Savagery will shred through your Seismic Bastion shield. This stalemate forces both of you to play reactively around neutral objectives, as neither can easily force a decisive duel without backup.
why: This matchup revolves entirely around the interaction between your suppress and his cleanse. Rengar can completely neutralize Impale by casting an empowered Battle Roar, which breaks your suppression instantly. Because of this, you cannot blindly dive him. Unless you track his Ferocity stacks from Unseen Predator, your ultimate risks being completely wasted, turning what should be a secure lockdown into a free escape for the hunter.

summary: Galio can charge Shield of Durand to taunt Rell and her ADC when she attempts to engage, neutralizing her follow-up.
howToPlay: Position yourself slightly behind or directly on top of your ADC, acting as an impassable roadblock. Never waste Shield of Durand to poke; keep it ready as an exclusive reaction to her forward leap. If she misses her engage, immediately chain Justice Punch and Colossal Smash onto her ADC to punish their bad positioning. If she tries to abandon the lane to roam, match her map pressure instantly using the semi-global range of Hero's Entrance.
laneImpact: Because Rell cannot safely engage without getting countered, she is forced to play passively, yielding bush control to you. This dominance allows you to safely poke with Winds of War and secure wave control with Colossal Smash without fear of a sudden lockdown. If Rell grows impatient and attempts a desperate dive, a swift counter-engage guarantees a favorable health trade, often forcing early recalls or securing easy tower-dive setups.
why: Galio naturally shuts down Rell's aggressive engage tools because her predictable dive puts her right into your optimal range. The moment she jumps forward to bind or stun your carry, you can immediately channel Shield of Durand. This wide-area taunt catches both Rell and her approaching ADC, completely neutralizing their burst window. By absorbing her initial crowd control, your protective taunt turns her proactive dive into a disastrous trap for her lane partner.

summary: Xin Zhao's Audacious Charge allows him to close the gap instantly, and Three Talon Strike can knock Lillia up before she can kite away.
howToPlay: When hunting Lillia, position yourself in brush near her jungle camps to ambush her before she stacks her passive. Avoid engaging when she already has maximum movement speed. Hold Wind Becomes Lightning to slow her down if she tries to roll away with Swirlseed. If she attempts to cast Watch Out! Eep!, use Audacious Charge to dash behind her or reposition out of the high-damage epicenter, ensuring you win the trade cleanly.
laneImpact: This matchup dynamic grants you massive early-game agency in the jungle. Lillia cannot safely contest scuttle crabs or defend her own camps if you decide to invade. Your threat of an all-in forces her to concede territory, meaning you can easily secure early neutral objectives. If she tries to fight for priority, a quick Audacious Charge combo will force her out of the river or secure a first blood.
why: Lillia relies entirely on stacking movement speed from Blooming Blows to kite her opponents. However, Xin Zhao completely shuts down this skirmishing style. By using Audacious Charge, you can instantly close the distance, ignoring her speed. Once on top of her, the rapid knock-up from Three Talon Strike disrupts her movement pattern and cancels her escape attempts before she can build momentum or land Watch Out! Eep!.

summary: Vladimir can use Sanguine Pool to dodge the high-damage second cast of Akali's Perfect Execution.
howToPlay: To survive, you must bait out Sanguine Pool before launching your ultimate. Initiate trades using Shuriken Flip to close the distance, then shroud yourself with Twilight Shroud to force him to panic-pool. Once he emerges from his bloody pool, you have a brief window to strike. Delay the second strike of Perfect Execution to its absolute limit to ensure he cannot dodge the executing blow. If he holds his pool, simply disengage and repeat the cycle.
laneImpact: This sustain dynamic forces you into passive wave clear, as trading with Five Point Strike and Assassin's Mark only yields temporary damage that Vladimir erases with Transfusion. You cannot easily force him out of lane, meaning his Hemoplague and Tides of Blood eventually push you under turret. If you try to dive or all-in, his Sanguine Pool safety net ensures you waste your energy while losing valuable turret plating.
why: Why this lane behaves this way: Vladimir's Crimson Pact and Transfusion give him endless health regeneration that outlasts Akali's energy-gated Five Point Strike poke. The true bottleneck is Vladimir's Sanguine Pool, which effortlessly nullifies the execution damage of Akali's second dash of Perfect Execution. This ability to dodge your primary burst window forces a war of attrition where his sustain naturally overcomes your assassin threat.

howToPlay: Play diagonally from Sett and avoid leaving a minion on the opposite side of Facebreaker. Apply Explosive Charge for a short trade, then retreat before his Grit fills Haymaker. Keep Rocket Jump to leave his approach and return only after the cone is spent. While The Show Stopper is available, preserve even more distance.
laneImpact: A pushed wave reduces your kiting space and lets Sett use minions with Facebreaker. Even without a kill, Haymaker's center can erase your health lead and force a poor recall. Rocket Jump remains valuable, but spending it offensively leaves Sett free to advance with Knuckle Down.
why: Tristana wants to wear Sett down from range, but Facebreaker pulls targets positioned on both sides and can stun them. Damage received then feeds Haymaker, which grants a shield before striking in a cone. The longer you chase after Explosive Charge, the more Sett can convert your own poke into a powerful return.

summary: Tristana must use Rocket Jump to dodge Varus's Chain of Corruption, as getting rooted during her Explosive Charge setup guarantees her defeat.
howToPlay: To survive, adopt a highly defensive stance and focus on scaling via Draw a Bead. Never use Rocket Jump aggressively unless Varus has already missed Chain of Corruption. Instead, hold your jump strictly to reactively buffer or escape his ultimate's projectile. If he does snare you, immediately use Buster Shot to push him away, preventing him from detonating his Blighted Quiver stacks, and abort the trade until your cooldowns return.
laneImpact: Because of Hail of Arrows and Living Vengeance, Varus easily secures wave priority, forcing you to farm under turret. Every attempt to walk up for a last hit exposes you to high-damage Piercing Arrow snipes. Your health pool will constantly bleed, making safe recalls difficult and putting massive pressure on your tower. You cannot safely contest his push unless his main crowd control is down.
why: Varus dominates the neutral game by wearing you down from afar with Piercing Arrow and Hail of Arrows. While your all-in with Explosive Charge and Rapid Fire has higher burst potential, it is entirely gatekept by Chain of Corruption. If you initiate and get rooted mid-combo, your DPS halts instantly, preventing you from detonating your bomb or securing the Rocket Jump reset, which leads to your swift demise.

summary: Janna can interrupt Nautilus's Dredge Line dash mid-air with a well-timed Howling Gale, preventing him from applying Staggering Blow.
howToPlay: Position yourself parallel to your carry, just outside the minion wave, to tempt him into throwing his hook. You must hold Howling Gale exclusively to react to Dredge Line; never use it to poke. If he targets your ally with Depth Charge, wait out the initial knockup, then immediately channel Monsoon to push him away before he can follow up with Riptide, keeping your carry perfectly safe.
laneImpact: Because Nautilus cannot reliably engage, his lane presence is severely diminished. You can establish lane priority easily, pushing the wave and poking him down with Zephyr whenever he steps up. If he tries to trade with Titan's Wrath shield, you simply mitigate any residual damage using Eye of the Storm, forcing him under his tower with low health and preventing him from roaming to impact the map.
why: Janna completely controls this matchup because Nautilus relies on a single linear motion to start fights. When he fires Dredge Line, you can reactively launch Howling Gale to knock him up mid-dash. This instantly cancels his forward momentum, keeping him at a distance and preventing him from ever reaching your carry to apply his passive Staggering Blow root, rendering his primary engage tool useless.

summary: Kai'Sa can use Killer Instinct to dash out of the area-of-effect of Bullet Time and reposition behind Miss Fortune for an easy kill.
howToPlay: To survive, alter how you trigger your ultimate. Never initiate with Bullet Time while Kai'Sa has her plasma marks active on you, as this enables her Killer Instinct. Instead, focus on short, quick trades using Love Tap and Double Up. Only channel your ultimate if Kai'Sa has already used her dash, or when she is heavily crowd-controlled by your team. If she activates Supercharge to close the distance, immediately retreat using the passive movement speed from Strut.
laneImpact: During the early levels, you can bully Kai'Sa with Double Up bounces off dying minions, using Strut to dodge her Void Seeker. However, once both of you reach level five, the dynamic shifts drastically. You can no longer freely cast Bullet Time to clear waves or force her back under tower. If you try, she will bypass your Make It Rain slow and dive you, forcing you to play defensively.
why: This matchup hinges on the threat of your ultimate. While Miss Fortune excels at zoning, Kai'Sa possesses a direct hard-counter to your main damage tool. The moment you channel Bullet Time, Kai'Sa can instantly activate Killer Instinct to dash completely out of the cone of fire, gaining a shield and placing herself directly behind you. This turns your strongest offensive window into an immediate death sentence.

summary: Garen can instantly cleanse Nasus's Wither by activating Decisive Strike.
howToPlay: Never initiate a trade by leading with Decisive Strike. Instead, simply walk up to Nasus and begin spinning with Judgment. Force him to panic-cast Wither to escape your damage. The moment the slow hits you, press Decisive Strike to instantly break the control, silence him, and secure the trade. If he activates Fury of the Sands, mitigate his retaliatory burst with Courage and walk away, returning to execute him with Demacian Justice once his ultimate expires.
laneImpact: You dictate the minion waves from the very first level. By holding the wave near your tower, you force Nasus to choose between stepping up to stack Siphoning Strike and taking heavy damage, or using Spirit Fire to farm. Your passive Perseverance ensures you out-sustain him, allowing you to build a massive minion crash and dive him when his Fury of the Sands is down.
why: This matchup heavily favors Garen due to a direct ability counter. Nasus relies entirely on Wither to isolate you, escape ganks, or force extended trades. However, Garen's Decisive Strike immediately cleanses this massive slow on activation. Because you can nullify his primary defensive and offensive tool at will, Nasus cannot safely trade or prevent you from shredding him with Judgment.

summary: Maokai's Twisted Advance makes him untargetable, meaning Janna must time Howling Gale to release right as he emerges to prevent his Bramble Smash follow-up.
howToPlay: Never cast Howling Gale aggressively; you must hold it exclusively to counter Maokai's Twisted Advance. Position yourself slightly behind your carry, allowing you to easily aim the tornado's path along his incoming dash trajectory. If he catches you off guard with Nature's Grasp, immediately prepare Monsoon to push him away after the roots expire. Apply Eye of the Storm only after his initial crowd control lands to absorb the inevitable Bramble Smash damage.
laneImpact: The constant threat of this interaction dictates wave control and positioning. When Maokai controls the brush using Sapling Toss, your carry is forced into a defensive posture, sacrificing gold. A missed Howling Gale completely strips away your safety, resulting in a devastating all-in. However, successfully interrupting his engage lets you safely punish his long cooldowns with Zephyr and auto-attacks, swinging the health lead back in your favor.
why: This matchup is a pure test of reflexes centered on Maokai's primary engage. When Maokai casts Twisted Advance, he becomes untargetable, bypassing your initial defenses. However, the split second he materializes to root his target, you have a precise window to release Howling Gale. Triggering it too early misses his untargetable state, while reacting too slowly allows him to chain Bramble Smash to shove your ally backward.

summary: Time Repudiation to block Irelia's Flawless Duet stun, preventing her from getting a free Bladesurge reset on you.
howToPlay: Never initiate with Public Execution or jump forward with Drakehound's Step when her Flawless Duet is active. Keep your distance and monitor her passive stacks. When she deploys her first blade, hover your finger over Repudiation. Cast it the moment the second blade flies to negate the stun. If you misstime this and get marked, immediately use Lacerate to slow her and dash away to safety, giving up the wave rather than giving her a kill.
laneImpact: When Irelia has minions to reset Bladesurge on, you cannot contest the wave. She will constantly fish for Flawless Duet. Missing your Repudiation shield timing means taking massive physical damage under tower or being forced into an early recall. If you successfully block her stun, her aggressive posture collapses, allowing you to safely clear with Cunning Sweep and Lacerate without risking a lethal dive.
why: Irelia thrives on dancing through your wave with Bladesurge, generating Ionian Fervor stacks to out-dps you. This lane revolves entirely around her Flawless Duet. If she stuns you, she gets a free Bladesurge reset and easily wins the extended duel. However, Ambessa can turn this mobility clash around by using Repudiation to absorb the stun, leaving Irelia vulnerable without her reset once her abilities are on cooldown.

summary: Tristana can jump directly onto you with Rocket Jump and stack Explosive Charge, forcing you to play extremely defensively without support intervention.
howToPlay: Keep Volley available to poke from max range, but never step inside her Rocket Jump radius. If she commits forward with her jump, immediately fire Enchanted Crystal Arrow mid-air to stun her upon landing, then activate Ranger's Focus to kite backward. Never duel her without your support's crowd control to interrupt her Rapid Fire. Use Hawkshot to scout her jungler so you know when you can safely hover near your tower.
laneImpact: You are forced to cede lane priority and play near your turret. Tristana's passive, Draw a Bead, eventually outranges you, while her passive explosive damage pushes the wave into you anyway. You cannot safely contest her CS or freeze. Missing even one step forward invites a jump-in that either forces your summoners or sends you back to base, starving your early gold income.
why: Tristana's Rocket Jump completely bypasses your Frost Shot slow, allowing her to land directly on you. Once close, she triggers Rapid Fire to instantly stack Explosive Charge. Your lack of mobility means you cannot escape the blast radius before it detonates, turning every trade into a lethal all-in where her burst heavily outvalues your sustained DPS.

summary: If Seraphine is hit by Sleepy Trouble Bubble, she is an easy target for a maximum-range Paddle Star! due to her lack of mobility.
howToPlay: Position yourself strictly in the center of the lane, keeping a wave of minions between you and Zoe to block Sleepy Trouble Bubble. If you are about to fall asleep, immediately cast Surround Sound to shield the incoming Paddle Star! damage. When she aggressive-teleports, aim Encore at her return marker from Portal Jump; this guarantees a charm on her predictable return point, turning her own dive into a deadly counter-engage.
laneImpact: Zoe's ability to throw Sleepy Trouble Bubble through the mid lane walls forces you into highly restrictive positioning. You cannot safely use Stage Presence to double-cast High Note for wave clear near the side ledges. Every missed dodge means losing over half your health bar to Paddle Star!, giving Zoe free lane priority, forcing premature recalls, and preventing you from using Surround Sound to sustain yourself.
why: This matchup is defined by Zoe's ability to punish your low mobility. If you get clipped by her Sleepy Trouble Bubble, you cannot escape, turning you into a sitting duck for a devastating, maximum-range Paddle Star!. Because Seraphine lacks any quick dash or escape tool, surviving Zoe's pick potential relies entirely on avoiding that initial bubble. Your Beat Drop is too slow to interrupt her rapid Portal Jump trading patterns.

summary: Syndra can knock Ahri out of her Spirit Rush dash using Scatter the Weak, preventing her from landing a close-range Charm.
howToPlay: Never waste Scatter the Weak to fish for random stuns while Ahri has Spirit Rush available. Keep your distance and align yourself behind your minion wave to block any direct Orb of Deception or Charm. The moment she charges forward with her ultimate, cast Scatter the Weak directly into her path to stop her dash. If she misses her charm, immediately retaliate with Dark Sphere and Unleashed Power to secure the kill.
laneImpact: Ahri is forced to play defensively, unable to use Spirit Rush aggressively to force you out of lane or set up easy ganks. Since you can consistently cancel her dashes, you maintain control over the minion waves. You can safely poke her with Dark Sphere and Force of Will while her Essence Theft healing fails to match your scaling power, restricting her ability to roam and pressure other lanes.
why: Syndra dominates this burst-heavy matchup because her defensive tool directly negates Ahri's primary offensive gap-closer. When Ahri attempts to activate Spirit Rush to aggressively close the distance, you can interrupt the dash mid-air using Scatter the Weak. This knockback completely denies Ahri the proximity she needs to guarantee an easy Charm, turning her forward momentum into a fatal mistake.

summary: Aurelion Sol must stand still to channel Breath of Light, making him an easy target for a full Heroic Swing rotation.
howToPlay: To survive this onslaught, you must play defensively near your turret and completely abandon the idea of using Breath of Light on Akshan unless his Heroic Swing is on cooldown. Place Singularity directly on your caster minions to secure farm from a safe distance. If he attempts to dive you under turret, prepare Falling Star to interrupt his swing mid-air. Prioritise safety over gold early; your scaling with Cosmic Creator will eventually outvalue his single-target assassination potential once you reach teamfights.
laneImpact: Akshan will aggressively push the first waves with Avengerang to secure an early level advantage. If you attempt to thin the wave with Singularity, he will immediately capitalise on your positioning, using Heroic Swing to dive past your tower range or force a premature Astral Flight. This constant pressure denies you Cosmic Creator stacks, forces you into bad recall timings, and allows Akshan to roam freely with Going Rogue while you are trapped under turret.
why: The lane is heavily tilted in Akshan's favor due to how Breath of Light locks you in place. While you stand still to channel your starfire, Akshan can easily anchor Heroic Swing on a nearby wall to circle around you, unleashing a devastating burst of physical damage while bypassing your minions. Your lack of early mobility means you cannot escape his Dirty Fighting shield trades, making your primary trading tool a self-inflicted trap.

summary: Senna's Piercing Darkness and basic attacks heavily poke Alistar down, while Last Embrace roots him if he tries to walk up to engage.
howToPlay: To survive, abandon any lane presence and hug the alcove or bush to break her line of sight, denying her free souls. Never walk straight at her; instead, wait for her to waste Last Embrace before attempting an engage with Headbutt and Pulverize. If you do get caught by her root while trying to peel, activate Unbreakable Will immediately to cleanse the crowd control and absorb the incoming burst instead of dying.
laneImpact: This constant harassment forces you to play defensively under your own turret, bleeding health and priority. Your passive Triumphant Roar cannot sustain through her non-stop poke, leading to early, forced recalls that ruin your ADC's wave control. Because you are pinned down and vulnerable, your jungler loses all support in the bot-side river, giving up scuttle crabs and early neutral objectives without any contest.
why: Senna completely shuts down your engage potential by exploiting your melee nature. Her long-range basic attacks combined with Piercing Darkness constantly chip away at your health bar from safety. Whenever you attempt to close the distance to setup a Headbutt or Pulverize, she can easily react with Last Embrace, rooting you mid-stride and leaving you completely exposed to her relentless poke and soul harvesting.

summary: Twilight Shroud (W) allows you to remain completely invisible and safely stall out the entire 5-second duration of Tryndamere's Undying Rage (R).
howToPlay: Never commit your Undying Rage while Akali still has Twilight Shroud available. Instead, bait her smoke screen by initiating short trades using Mocking Shout to slow her when her back is turned, then immediately retreat with Spinning Slash. Only commit to an all-in if you see her waste her energy or shroud. If she dives you with Perfect Execution, hug your turret, use Bloodlust for emergency healing, and focus solely on surviving.
laneImpact: You can never safely freeze or pressure Akali under her turret. If you attempt a heavy trade, she uses Five Point Strike to slow your approach and retrieves Assassin's Mark to chunk you. When you try to escape with Spinning Slash, her Shuriken Flip allows her to follow you anywhere. This constant threat forces you to play defensively, sacrificing early wave control and giving her free roam priority.
why: Your entire lethal potential relies on auto-attacking during Undying Rage, but Akali's Twilight Shroud completely denies this. When you trigger your ultimate, she simply drops her smoke screen to go invisible, stalling out the entire 5-second duration of your survival window. Without targets to hit, you cannot utilize Battle Fury crits or reset Spinning Slash, leaving you completely vulnerable the moment your ultimate expires.

summary: Poppy's barrier blocks Urgot's Disdain dash, leaving him grounded and unable to trigger his Echoing Flames behind her.
howToPlay: Your survival hinges on baiting out her barrier before using your dash. Stay near the center of the lane to avoid her wall-slam, and use Corrosive Charge to poke. Never activate Purge or Disdain while her golden aura is active. If she misplays and uses it, you have a twenty-second window to fight. If she catches you, fire Fear Beyond Death to slow her and walk away.
laneImpact: Because you cannot reliably land Disdain, you lose all kill pressure and must concede wave priority. Poppy can easily zone you away from the minions, forcing you to farm from a safe distance using Corrosive Charge. Trying to force trades through her barrier will cost you massive health, leading to early recalls and lost turret plates.
why: This matchup is dictated by how Poppy's protective barrier interacts with your primary engage. Whenever you attempt to close the distance, her barrier completely blocks Disdain, grounding you on the spot. Without the flip, you cannot maneuver around her to trigger the Echoing Flames shotgun knees on her backside, leaving your damage output heavily crippled.

summary: Braum can block Sona's Crescendo with Unbreakable, but her passive scaling and healing will outvalue him if he cannot find early engages.
howToPlay: Never blindly cast Crescendo while Braum has Unbreakable ready; instead, wait for him to waste it on your Hymn of Valor before unleashing your ultimate. Use Song of Celerity to bait out and sidestep Winter's Bite. If he tries to jump forward with Stand Behind Me, immediately hit his carry with a Power Chord enhanced by Aria of Perseverance to reduce their damage, then safely retreat.
laneImpact: You dictate the lane's pace by keeping Braum at a distance. Since he relies on Winter's Bite to initiate, dodging it with Song of Celerity leaves him helpless. This allows you to safely poke with Hymn of Valor, slowly forcing Braum and his carry under their tower. Without early kills, Braum cannot match your scaling, turning the lane into a war of attrition that you easily win.
why: Sona naturally dominates this matchup through her superior scaling. While Braum can completely block Crescendo using Unbreakable, his kit lacks the sustain to survive your constant poke. Every Hymn of Valor and Aria of Perseverance trade slowly drains his health pool. Unless he triggers Concussive Blows early, Sona's healing and Power Chord utility will inevitably outvalue his defensive shield as the game progresses.

summary: Varus can abuse Vayne's lack of waveclear by shoving waves with Hail of Arrows and harassing her under turret with Piercing Arrow where she cannot easily Tumble away.
howToPlay: To survive, you must abandon any hope of matching his push and focus on minimizing damage. When Varus winds up Piercing Arrow, do not Tumble immediately; wait for him to release the arrow and use your roll perpendicular to its trajectory, keeping yourself away from the turret wall to preserve your dodge angle. Save Condemn exclusively to push him back if he tries to walk up and trigger his Blighted Quiver stacks with basic attacks.
laneImpact: This matchup turns into a grueling war of attrition where you are permanently pinned. Because you are constantly clearing minions under turret, you cannot contest early drakes, and your jungler loses all bottom-side priority. Varus will stack Blighted Quiver on the minions or you, using the threat of Chain of Corruption to lock you down for an easy dive once your health is chipped away.
why: Varus completely suffocates you from level one because Vayne has zero tools to match his waveclear. He will constantly drop Hail of Arrows onto the minion wave, forcing you to farm under your turret. Once you are trapped against your own tower, your Tumble becomes incredibly predictable, allowing him to easily charge and aim Piercing Arrow to chunk your health bar without any risk of retaliation.

summary: Vladimir can use Sanguine Pool to dodge Death from Below, denying Pyke his gold reset and healing back up.
howToPlay: Always hold onto Sanguine Pool specifically for Death from Below during skirmishes; do not waste it to dodge Bone Skewer or Phantom Undertow unless absolutely necessary. When Pyke charges Bone Skewer, stand behind your minions or prepare to dodge laterally. If he roams with Ghostwater Dive, immediately shove the wave with Tides of Blood to punish his tower. Keep your health high with empowered Transfusion casts to bait him into a bad ultimate attempt.
laneImpact: Pyke is forced into a passive lane where he cannot easily execute Vladimir. Vladimir can safely push waves with Tides of Blood, forcing Pyke under tower where his waveclear is weak. Pyke is forced to roam using Ghostwater Dive, but if he fails to find kills, he falls behind permanently. Vladimir secures free scaling, maintaining high health to prevent Pyke from ever setting up a dive with Bone Skewer.
why: Vladimir completely neutralizes Pyke's primary execution threat because Sanguine Pool allows him to slip away right as Pyke casts Death from Below. By turning untargetable during the ultimate's animation, Vladimir cancels the execute, denies Pyke his gold reset, and uses Transfusion to recover any lost health. Pyke's reliance on burst damage is countered by Vladimir's pool and natural healing from Transfusion, making Pyke's kill windows incredibly narrow.

summary: Wukong can use Warrior Trickster to absorb Xin Zhao's third Three Talon Strike knock-up, turning the early skirmish in his favor.
howToPlay: To win, never open a skirmish with Warrior Trickster. Instead, jump in using Nimbus Strike and immediately strike with Golden Staff to shred his armor. Watch his spear glows carefully during Three Talon Strike; only trigger your decoy right as his third auto-attack animation begins. If you misstime this and get knocked up, immediately disengage using the movement speed from Cyclone or retreat towards walls where his Wind Becomes Lightning cannot easily track your escape route.
laneImpact: Because this matchup is so volatile, early scuttle crab duels and jungle invasions are decided entirely by whoever initiates first. If Xin Zhao forces an engagement with Audacious Charge, you cannot afford to panic. Successfully baiting his combo near the river bushes determines who secures early map pressure, as the victor gains the freedom to invade or execute healthier ganks while the loser is forced to yield camp control.
why: This duel is a pure battle of reaction times centered on your clone. While Xin Zhao relies on his passive healing from Determination and the sequential threat of Three Talon Strike to dominate early skirmishes, your Warrior Trickster is the ultimate spoiler. By timing your invisibility to absorb his third strike knock-up with your clone, you completely negate his crowd control and main damage source, turning a deadly duel into a winning trade.

summary: Galio can instantly interrupt Katarina's Death Lotus (R) using either Shield of Durand (W) taunt or Justice Punch (E) knock-up.
howToPlay: Never waste both Shield of Durand and Justice Punch simultaneously during skirmishes. Always hold at least one of these crowd control tools specifically for when Katarina activates Death Lotus. Use Winds of War to harass her whenever she approaches a dagger dropped by Bouncing Blade or Preparation. If she attempts to roam, immediately walk toward the side lane and use Hero's Entrance to protect your teammates the moment she commits to a dive.
laneImpact: This interaction completely strips Katarina of lane priority. She cannot step up to clear minions without risking a heavy trade, allowing you to shove waves effortlessly with Winds of War and Colossal Smash. Because she cannot kill you, she is forced to seek roams, but your Hero's Entrance allows you to follow her map rotations instantly, neutralizing her global impact while she loses mid-lane gold.
why: You completely shut down Katarina's kill threat because her primary damage source, Death Lotus, is a channeled ability that you can instantly interrupt. Both Shield of Durand and Justice Punch provide immediate hard crowd control to cancel her ultimate. Additionally, the passive magic shield from Shield of Durand naturally mitigates her Bouncing Blade poke, leaving her with no viable trading patterns against you.

summary: Garen can use the tenacity from Courage to shrug off the brittle knockup from Ornn's Searing Charge.
howToPlay: To win these trades, you must bait out Courage before committing. Start by poking with Volcanic Rupture to threaten an engage. If he panics and shields, wait out the brief duration of his defense before using Bellows Breath and Searing Charge. If he silences you first with Decisive Strike, use the displacement of Call of the Forge God to disengage and reset your positioning rather than fighting back immediately.
laneImpact: Because of Garen's Perseverance, short trades are useless unless you can consistently break his passive. When you fail your Searing Charge knockup due to his mitigation, Garen will freeze the wave or force you back with Demacian Justice if you remain low. Missing your crowd control window gives him free reign to shred your armor and push you under tower, starving you of forge opportunities.
why: This matchup is a pure test of execution centered around Garen's ability to negate your crowd control. The defining moment of every trade relies on Courage. If Garen activates this shield to absorb the impact of your Searing Charge, the massive tenacity bonus allows him to shrug off the brittle knockup almost instantly. This prevents you from executing your full combo while leaving you exposed to a devastating Judgment spin.

summary: Jhin can easily shove Vayne under turret using Dancing Grenade and poke her down while she struggles to last-hit.
howToPlay: To survive, use Tumble purely to secure minion last-hits under turret or dodge Jhin's Deadly Flourish. Never use it forward into Whisper's fourth shot. Hold Condemn to push Jhin away if he tries to walk up and abuse his fourth shot under your tower. Once Jhin commits Curtain Call, activate Final Hour to gain the movement speed from Night Hunter and stealth from Tumble, letting you reposition and avoid the deadly final shots.
laneImpact: You will spend the entire early game trapped under your turret, losing priority and health. Jhin's fast push deprives you of opportunities to stack Silver Bolts. Every CS under tower exposes you to Captive Audience traps and long-range Curtain Call snipes, forcing early recalls that bleed gold and XP while your jungler loses control over the bottom river.
why: Jhin's range and wave-clear advantage dominate this matchup. He uses Dancing Grenade to rapidly clear the wave, forcing it under your tower. While you struggle to last-hit with Vayne's short-range single-target attacks, Jhin can easily poke you with Whisper's fourth shot or setup Deadly Flourish to lock you down from safety without ever entering your Tumble range.

summary: Ambessa can use Drakehound's Step and Lacerate's slow to kite Tryndamere during Undying Rage, but cannot match his raw DPS in a face-to-face brawl.
howToPlay: When Tryndamere initiates with Spinning Slash, do not immediately use Public Execution. Instead, trigger Lacerate to slow him, followed by a dash from Drakehound's Step to create distance. Save Repudiation to absorb his initial high-crit burst or block the slow from Mocking Shout if your back is turned. Once he activates Undying Rage, continually dash away using your passive-empowered strikes on jungle monsters or minions to stall out his five seconds of immortality.
laneImpact: Because you cannot match his raw DPS, you lose the freedom to contest scuttle crabs or invade his camps early on. If he catches you with high fury, his Spinning Slash allows him to stick to you, forcing a defensive Repudiation. This passive stance means you will often have to concede early jungle pressure, forcing your lanes to play safer while you focus on safe clearing.
why: Tryndamere dominates direct, sustained duels in the jungle due to the raw critical strike damage from Battle Fury. If you attempt a head-on brawl, his constant auto-attacks will quickly force out your defensive options. Even if you chunk him down, Undying Rage completely nullifies your execution damage from Public Execution. Your only saving grace is using Lacerate and Drakehound's Step to outmaneuver him during his ultimate.

summary: Camille must use Hookshot to disengage when Volibear activates Thundering Smash to prevent him from chaining Frenzied Maul.
howToPlay: To survive, you must hold Hookshot defensively. The moment Volibear activates Thundering Smash and runs at you, fire Hookshot at the wall to pull yourself away, denying his stun and preventing him from landing Frenzied Maul. Use Tactical Sweep from maximum range to safely secure minions and thin the crashing wave without getting within his engage radius. If he wastes Sky Splitter to zone you, only then can you briefly trade with Precision Protocol.
laneImpact: Volibear’s passive The Relentless Storm constantly pushes the wave, forcing Camille under her turret. This makes it difficult to maintain wave control, as any attempt to thin the minions invites a devastating Sky Splitter slow. Trading health becomes extremely punishing because Volibear heals up instantly on the wave, eventually diving you with Stormbringer if you drop too low from failed trades.
why: Volibear dominates this lane through relentless healing from successive Frenzied Maul bites and the shield from Sky Splitter. Camille relies on short trades, but if Volibear lands Thundering Smash, he guarantees his marked bite, winning any extended duel. Because Adaptive Defenses cannot mitigate both his hybrid physical and magical lightning damage from The Relentless Storm, Camille cannot out-sustain his constant pressure.

summary: Evelynn can abuse Shyvana's lack of early CC to gank lanes, and later shred her with Allure's magic resist reduction.
howToPlay: To counter her early tempo, you must prioritize tracking Evelynn's starting camp. Use Flame Breath and Burnout for rapid clears, then place deep wards on her camps before Demon Shade activates. If she marks you with Allure, do not try to fight her head-on; instead, immediately use the unstoppable leap of Dragon's Descent to disengage and break her line of sight, or use its displacement to disrupt her Whiplash follow-up before she can trigger the charm.
laneImpact: This imbalance heavily skews the early game map pressure. While you are busy farming camps with Twin Bite and Flame Breath to secure Fury of the Dragonborn stacks, Evelynn easily secures early kills across the map. Your lanes will suffer because you cannot match her gank tempo without CC. Once she reaches level five, her stealth forces your teammates under tower, starving you of active backup when contesting major neutral objectives.
why: Evelynn exploits Shyvana's complete lack of crowd control before unlocking Dragon's Descent, allowing her to pressure lanes unimpeded. While Shyvana relies on Burnout to clear, Evelynn utilizes Demon Shade to slip past standard wards. Once Evelynn scales, Allure becomes a lethal threat; its massive magic resistance reduction melts Shyvana's bruiser defenses, allowing her to easily execute you with Last Caress even if you have collected numerous stacks of Fury of the Dragonborn.

summary: Jax's Counter Strike blocks all of Irelia's basic attacks, completely shutting down her Ionian Fervor damage.
howToPlay: Never initiate trades by wasting Counter Strike preemptively. Instead, walk up and use Leap Strike and Empower to force a response. Hold Counter Strike until she commits to a fight with Bladesurge or reaches maximum stacks. If she tries to block your stun with Defiant Dance, simply walk behind her or delay your recast to maximize your basic attacks. If she misses Flawless Duet, immediately jump on her to force a flash or a kill.
laneImpact: This interaction shifts wave control entirely into your hands. Irelia cannot safely use Bladesurge to clear low-health minions without exposing herself to a devastating trade. Whenever she attempts to stack her passive on the wave, you can threaten an engage. This forces her to concede priority, allowing you to slow-push waves, dive her under tower with Grandmaster-at-Arms, or lock her out of gold entirely.
why: Jax dominates this matchup because Counter Strike completely neutralizes Irelia's primary win condition. Irelia relies heavily on stacking Ionian Fervor through her Bladesurge resets to shred opponents with rapid auto-attacks. By activating Counter Strike, you block her entire offensive output while her passive is fully stacked, turning her strongest skirmishing windows into useless, wasted energy while you ramp up your own Relentless Assault.

summary: Rammus's Defensive Ball Curl and Frenzying Taunt force Jax to damage himself through basic attacks, rendering Jax's high attack speed a liability.
howToPlay: To survive, you must alter your entire build path. Shift your itemization away from pure attack speed and physical damage, opting instead for magic resistance and armor penetration to mitigate his Defensive Ball Curl. In fights, never use Leap Strike to initiate on him. Instead, save your Leap Strike to escape over walls when he approaches with Powerball. If you get caught, immediately trigger Counter Strike before his Frenzying Taunt lands to delay his teammates' follow-up damage.
laneImpact: In the jungle, this matchup completely alters your skirmishing potential. You cannot contest Rammus directly in the river or during counter-ganks. If he rolls in with Powerball and catches you, his Frenzying Taunt ensures you commit suicide on his spiked shell. This forces you to yield early scuttle crabs and neutral objectives, as any 2v2 encounter where he locks you down results in a swift death for you.
why: Rammus is your ultimate counter because of how his kit punishes your natural auto-attack speed from Relentless Assault. When he activates Defensive Ball Curl and forces you to attack him with Frenzying Taunt, your own high-speed strikes are turned against you. Every hit triggers his defensive damage reflection, amplified by his armor, meaning you will literally shred your own health bar before Counter Strike can even protect you.

summary: Riven must save her Valor (E) or third Broken Wings (Q) to dash out of the center line of Sett's Haymaker (W) when he casts it at full Grit.
howToPlay: Initiate trades with Knuckle Down and basic attacks to force Riven into using Ki Burst and Valor. Never rush your Haymaker; hold it until your grit bar is completely full. To guarantee the true damage hit, pull her back with Facebreaker right as she tries to execute her third Broken Wings strike, or use The Show Stopper to lock her in place before unleashing your shield blast so she cannot dash away.
laneImpact: Because Riven must constantly respect your Haymaker, she is forced to play defensively, giving you complete control over the wave. You can slow push to crash massive waves, forcing her under tower where Facebreaker threats prevent her from safely farming. Every trade she attempts drains her resources faster than yours, allowing you to establish a massive health lead and dive her with The Show Stopper.
why: Sett dominates this duel because his Haymaker completely eclipses Riven's burst pattern. While Riven relies on cycling Broken Wings and Ki Burst to chip your health, she cannot match your raw grit generation. The matchup hinges on her Valor or final Broken Wings dash; if she burns them offensively, she has no escape from the true damage centerline of your shield blast.

summary: Rammus uses Frenzying Taunt to force you to auto-attack him while Defensive Ball Curl is active, dealing massive damage back to you.
howToPlay: You must shift your build path toward armor-penetrating options early rather than raw attack damage. During skirmishes, never initiate with Umbral Dash; instead, hold it to escape his incoming Powerball. If he successfully lands Frenzying Taunt, do not panic. Once the taunt ends and Defensive Ball Curl expires, use Infernal Chains to drag him back and safely land The Darkin Blade sweetspots to recover your health.
laneImpact: Rammus neutralizes your early skirmishing power in the river. While you clear camps faster, his high mobility from Powerball allows him to counter-gank your lanes effectively. In any 2v2 fight, his ability to force you into attacking his Defensive Ball Curl means you cannot easily secure crucial early takedowns to trigger your World Ender resets, granting his laners free pressure across the map.
why: This jungle matchup is dictated by how Rammus punishes your physical damage output. The moment he activates Defensive Ball Curl, attacking him becomes suicidal. By locking you down with Frenzying Taunt, he forces you to auto-attack his spiked shell, triggering Deathbringer Stance against yourself. This crowd control completely interrupts the flow of your The Darkin Blade combos, leaving you unable to heal through physical damage.

summary: Milio's Breath of Life can cleanse the stun from Cosmic Binding, but it cannot cleanse the stasis from Tempered Fate.
howToPlay: To win this, bait out Warm Hugs with basic attacks empowered by Traveler’s Call before committing your mana. Never initiate a hard engage with Cosmic Binding when Milio's Breath of Life is available. Instead, launch Tempered Fate directly onto Milio to lock him out of the fight first. Once he is frozen in stasis, line up your Cosmic Binding on his landing spot, ensuring an inescapable stun the moment he emerges.
laneImpact: Laning dissolves into a battle of attrition where your Caretaker’s Shrine competes with Milio's Cozy Campfire and Warm Hugs to keep marksmen healthy. If you blindly throw Cosmic Binding, Milio will shield the damage and out-sustain you. You cannot force quick kills under tower; instead, you must chip away at their resources, forcing Milio to exhaust his mana on heals before you look for a deep portal play.
why: This skill matchup revolves around Milio's ability to negate your crowd control. While a well-placed Cosmic Binding can stun Milio or his carry, Milio can instantly wipe this stun away using Breath of Life. However, his ultimate is completely useless against the golden stasis of Tempered Fate. Because Tempered Fate bypasses his cleanse entirely, you possess the ultimate tool to freeze him or his allies, leaving them vulnerable right as the stasis ends.

summary: Xayah can completely negate Tristana's Explosive Charge burst by using Featherstorm to become untargetable, then rooting her with Bladecaller when she lands.
howToPlay: To survive, you must trick Xayah into wasting her ultimate. Bait her defensive reaction by poking with simple auto-attacks enhanced by Draw a Bead and Rapid Fire without committing your jump. Only apply Explosive Charge after she panics and triggers Featherstorm. If she holds it, use Buster Shot defensively to push her away when she activates Deadly Plumage, disengaging safely rather than trying to force a fight you cannot win.
laneImpact: This interaction forces you into a passive stance during laning. You cannot safely initiate with Rocket Jump because Xayah's Clean Cuts and Double Daggers constantly litter the lane with feathers, threatening a quick root if you push too far. Trading with Rapid Fire feels unrewarding when she can match your DPS with her own Deadly Plumage while keeping her defensive ultimate ready to negate your all-in.
why: Xayah completely shuts down your offensive pressure because she can instantly nullify your main source of burst. The moment you commit with Explosive Charge, she can activate Featherstorm to become untargetable, causing your bomb to tick down uselessly. Worse, as she lands, she repositions her feathers to trigger Bladecaller, locking you down mid-air if you try to escape with Rocket Jump or simply rooting you for a deadly trade.

summary: Aatrox can interrupt Garen's Decisive Strike charge by spacing his The Darkin Blade sweetspots to knock him back.
howToPlay: Always hold your Umbral Dash to reposition the first two strikes of The Darkin Blade precisely when Garen runs forward with Decisive Strike. Do not fully commit with your third strike if his Courage shield is active; wait out those brief seconds before unleashing your full combo. If you miss your sweetspots and get silenced, immediately walk back, then turn the fight around with World Ender once the silence expires to heal back up with Deathbringer Stance.
laneImpact: You dictate the wave's tempo from level one. Garen is forced to use Judgment on the minion wave to keep up, which pushes the line toward you and leaves him defenseless. If he wastes Courage trying to mitigate your poke, you can immediately lock him down with Infernal Chains and force a heavy trade. You will consistently hold a health advantage, forcing him under tower or to take bad recalls.
why: This matchup favors you because you can completely shut down Garen's trade pattern. Whenever he activates Decisive Strike to charge at you, you can space the sweetspots of your The Darkin Blade to knock him back and cancel his advance. Because Garen lacks a dash, he must run directly at you, making him an easy target for your Infernal Chains. This constant harassment prevents his Perseverance from ever activating.

summary: Dashing with Bladesurge to dodge Mordekaiser's Obliterate is crucial to winning duels inside his Realm of Death.
howToPlay: Never cast Obliterate proactively when Irelia has active marks or low-health minions nearby to dash to. Instead, hold your slam and use basic attacks to trigger Darkness Rise. When you pull her with Death's Grasp, anticipate her immediate Bladesurge response behind you; aim your slam backward or wait for her to lock herself into the Defiant Dance channel. If she misses Flawless Duet, that is your window to cast Realm of Death and fight her without her maximum burst.
laneImpact: Wave position dictates who holds the threat. When Irelia has low-health minions to reset Bladesurge, she can easily bait Death's Grasp and reposition. If you miss your pull, she will instantly stack Ionian Fervor and force heavy trades. This constant threat prevents you from blindly pushing, as a frozen wave near her turret allows her to chase you down the long lane with Vanguard's Edge.
why: This lane is a pure skill check determined by mobility versus raw power. Irelia relies on stacking Ionian Fervor and baiting your abilities. The duel hinges on whether she can use Bladesurge to dash through minions or yourself to dodge Obliterate. If she successfully evades this heavy slam, especially once isolated inside Realm of Death, her sustained physical damage will overwhelm your shield from Indestructible.

summary: Jhin can punish Jinx's lack of mobility by trapping her with Captive Audience and securing a root with Deadly Flourish.
howToPlay: Keep a Captive Audience trap active in the lane bushes to zone Jinx out. Hold onto your Deadly Flourish until she locks herself in place to cast Zap! or throw Flame Chompers!, making her a sitting duck. If you miss your root and she tries to retaliate with Super Mega Death Rocket!, immediately break her line of sight and fallback to prepare your Curtain Call from a safe distance to finish her off.
laneImpact: You command the wave's tempo from the very first wave. By bouncing Dancing Grenade through dying minions, you constantly shove Jinx under her turret while chipping away at her health. This constant pressure denies her the freedom to stack her minigun's attack speed. She is forced to bleed mana using Switcheroo! rockets to clear, leading to early recalls and massive local tower plate leads for you.
why: Jinx relies entirely on her Switcheroo! rocket range to farm safely since she has no natural dashes. Jhin easily exploits this immobility. By placing Captive Audience in her narrow pathing lanes, you force her to step into the slow zone. This sets up an effortless Deadly Flourish to root her in place, allowing you to follow up with Whisper's heavy fourth shot before she can trigger Get Excited! to run away.

summary: Varus can use Chain of Corruption to root Twisted Fate in place when he steps forward to throw a Gold Card, setting up an easy Piercing Arrow.
howToPlay: To execute this, always maintain a safe distance when Pick a Card is cycling. The moment you see him lock the yellow card and walk toward you, immediately cast Chain of Corruption to stop him mid-stride. Follow up with Hail of Arrows to slow his retreat and apply Blighted Quiver stacks, then detonate them with a quick Piercing Arrow. If you miss your ultimate, retreat immediately to avoid his gold card stun and subsequent Wild Cards burst.
laneImpact: This range advantage prevents Twisted Fate from freely farming or using charged Dice to build a gold lead. He is forced to use Wild Cards from afar to secure minions, draining his mana pool rapidly. Because he cannot safely step up to trade, you dictate the wave state, keeping him pinned under his turret and preventing him from finding clean windows to channel Destiny for side-lane roams.
why: Varus dominates Twisted Fate by completely neutralizing his short-range card selection. Whenever Twisted Fate locks a Gold Card using Pick a Card and steps forward to throw it, he is forced into a predictable path. You can easily interrupt this advance with Chain of Corruption, rooting him in place before he reaches his auto-attack range, which perfectly lines up a fully charged Piercing Arrow to shred his health.

summary: Braum can block Sona's Crescendo with Unbreakable, but her passive scaling and healing will outvalue him if he cannot find early engages.
howToPlay: You must act aggressively during levels one to three. Look for a clean Winter's Bite to slow her, then use Stand Behind Me to close the gap and trigger Concussive Blows. Save Unbreakable specifically to intercept Crescendo when teamfights break out, as neutralizing her ultimate is your primary win condition. If she plays extremely safe, do not waste your health trying to poke; instead, wait for her to step forward to trigger a Power Chord before launching Glacial Fissure.
laneImpact: Sona will steadily chip away at your health using Hymn of Valor while negating your trade attempts with Aria of Perseverance. If you play defensively, she will freely stack her passive and scale safely. This constant pressure limits your ability to step up, forcing your ADC under tower. If you do not secure a kill before she reaches her ultimate, her sustain ensures you lose the lane purely through health deficits.
why: Sona's late-game scaling with Aria of Perseverance and Power Chord outclasses Braum's defensive kit over time. While Braum can completely negate Crescendo using Unbreakable, Sona's constant shielding and poke from Hymn of Valor create a war of attrition that Braum cannot win passively. He must exploit his early-game level spikes to force fights before Sona's utility becomes overwhelming.

summary: Kayn can completely waste Tryndamere's Undying Rage duration by infesting him with Umbral Trespass.
howToPlay: To survive this, never initiate a duel unless you have maximum Battle Fury. If Kayn engages, save Mocking Shout for when he attempts to flee into terrain with Shadow Step, forcing him to fight. If you must use Undying Rage, immediately prepare to cast Spinning Slash over a wall the split-second Kayn exits you with Umbral Trespass, allowing you to escape and heal with Bloodlust rather than dying instantly.
laneImpact: Because of this ultimate interaction, you lose the freedom to invade Kayn or force early river skirmishes. He can safely farm camps and easily escape through walls with Shadow Step if you try to corner him. In skirmishes around neutral objectives, Kayn will actively bait your Undying Rage knowing his team can collapse on you the second Umbral Trespass ends, severely crippling your frontline pressure.
why: This jungle duel hinges on the interaction between your ultimates. While you rely on Undying Rage to win close skirmishes, Kayn possesses the ultimate stall tool. The moment you activate your ultimate to survive, Kayn can cast Umbral Trespass to infest you, hiding inside your champion model. This completely wastes the active duration of your invulnerability, leaving you a sitting duck with zero health when he finally emerges.

summary: Rell's highly telegraphed engage tools are easily reacted to and neutralized by a well-timed Black Shield.
howToPlay: To survive, you must bait out Black Shield without committing your main dive. Walk up aggressively to threaten Full Tilt, but hold your Ferromancy: Crashdown. If she panics and uses her shield, back off immediately; you now have a twenty-second window to look for a real engage. Alternatively, if she binds your ally, use Shattering Strike to break her shield if she places it, but never jump in blindly while her defensive cooldown is available.
laneImpact: This interaction paralyzes your lane presence, forcing you to play passively near your tower. You cannot step up to secure bush control, as walking forward invites a Dark Binding that halts you instantly. Your ADC will constantly be pushed under turret under pressure from Tormented Shadow. Attempting to force fights results in massive health deficits, as a blocked knock-up leaves you isolated and unable to escape.
why: Morgana completely shuts down your initiation. Whenever you attempt to engage with Ferromancy: Crashdown or Full Tilt, she has ample time to react with Black Shield, rendering your crowd control useless. Because Ferromancy: Crashdown has a highly telegraphed jump animation, she can easily shield her ADC, leaving you dismounted, extremely slow, and a prime target for a retaliatory Dark Binding and Tormented Shadow pool.

summary: Casting Realm of Death on Shyvana right after she uses Dragon's Descent steals her massive bonus stats, turning her ultimate against her.
howToPlay: Never initiate a fight with Realm of Death. Instead, clear camps and wait for Shyvana to engage first. When she flies in with Dragon's Descent, immediately cast your ultimate to capture her. If she tries to run away inside the realm, use Death's Grasp to pull her back into your Darkness Rise aura. If her Twin Bite or Flame Breath burst gets dangerous, activate Indestructible to absorb the damage and secure the kill.
laneImpact: In the jungle, Shyvana's early clear is fast, but she cannot contest you at neutral camps once you both unlock your ultimates. Because you dominate the duel, she is forced to play passively and cannot freely stack her Fury of the Dragonborn. Any attempt by her to secure objectives with Dragon's Descent becomes a massive liability, as you can trap her, steal her stats, and secure the area.
why: This matchup heavily favors you because Shyvana relies entirely on the massive stat steroid from Dragon's Descent to win duels. By holding your Realm of Death until she commits her ultimate, you can immediately steal those enhanced dragon attributes. This instantly strips away her tankiness and damage scaling, leaving her vulnerable in the death realm while your own Darkness Rise and Obliterate burn through her reduced health pool.

summary: Akali can use the micro-stun on the first cast of Perfect Execution to immediately cancel Katarina's Death Lotus.
howToPlay: To translate this advantage into kills, you must hold the first cast of Perfect Execution specifically for her ultimate. When she initiates with Shunpo and triggers Death Lotus, immediately dash through her to cancel the channel. If she hesitates to ult, use Twilight Shroud to deny her target selection while poking her down with Five Point Strike. Only launch Shuriken Flip when her teleport options are on cooldown to guarantee your execution.
laneImpact: This interaction completely paralyzes Katarina’s solo kill pressure once you both reach level five. In early trades, she cannot safely use Shunpo onto her daggers from Bouncing Blade or Preparation without risking a heavy trade from your Five Point Strike and Assassin's Mark. She is forced to play defensively, meaning you dictate the wave pace and secure mid-lane priority easily.
why: Akali holds all the cards in this high-octane duel because her kit directly neutralizes Katarina's ultimate win condition. While both of you rely on high-mobility burst, the crucial interaction lies in Perfect Execution. The first cast of your ultimate provides a micro-stun that instantly interrupts Katarina's Death Lotus, stripping away her primary teamfight damage and leaving her completely vulnerable to your counter-burst.

summary: Amumu's Curse of the Sad Mummy can lock you down and prevent you from healing via Umbral Dash passive.
howToPlay: Position yourself slightly outside the sweep of his first two The Darkin Blade strikes to bait his forward movement. Hold your Curse of the Sad Mummy specifically for when Aatrox activates World Ender and attempts to dash in with Umbral Dash. Once he commits, lock him down instantly. If you miss your initial Bandage Toss, disengage immediately into your jungle camps to let his ultimate expire before re-engaging with Despair.
laneImpact: In early skirmishes, whoever initiates first often loses the upper hand. If Aatrox catches you with Infernal Chains, you will be forced to burn Bandage Toss defensively or face critical damage. However, when contesting early Scuttle Crabs or Epic Monsters, your ability to deny his sustain with a perfectly timed crowd control chain determines who controls the river, dictating which team secures early priority and map-wide pressure.
why: This jungle duel revolves around neutralizing Aatrox's massive skirmish healing. While Aatrox relies on landing The Darkin Blade sweetspots and utilizing Umbral Dash for continuous physical vamp, your ultimate, Curse of the Sad Mummy, is the ultimate countermeasure. Locking him down completely prevents him from attacking or repositioning, effectively shutting off his Umbral Dash passive healing and leaving his health pool vulnerable to your Despair and Cursed Touch magic damage amp.

summary: Olaf's Ragnarok makes him completely immune to the knockups of The Darkin Blade and the pull of Infernal Chains.
howToPlay: When pathing, track his ultimate closely. If Olaf activates Ragnarok, immediately use Umbral Dash over a wall or backward to disengage, saving Infernal Chains until his immunity fades. Do not attempt to stand and fight with World Ender while his ultimate is active; instead, wait out those six seconds of crowd control immunity. If he traps you in a choke point, prioritize landing basic attacks to cycle your Deathbringer Stance for survival rather than trying to hit impossible sweetspots.
laneImpact: In the jungle, this interaction makes early skirmishes incredibly dangerous. Olaf can aggressively invade your camps or contest Scuttle Crabs, knowing he can shrug off your crowd control. If he catches you with Undertow slows, you cannot peel him off with Infernal Chains. This pressure forces you to forfeit early neutral objectives and play defensively, delaying your World Ender spikes and forcing your lanes to play without active jungle priority.
why: Olaf directly counters your entire kit because activating Ragnarok makes him immune to the knockups of The Darkin Blade and the pull of Infernal Chains. Without these crowd controls, you cannot land your sweetspots reliably, which drastically reduces the damage of your The Darkin Blade and the healing from Umbral Dash or Deathbringer Stance. His Berserker Rage and Vicious Strikes then easily out-sustain your raw damage in close-quarters combat.

summary: Mordekaiser can use Indestructible to shield against Renekton's Ruthless Predator burst, then run him down with Darkness Rise during the cooldown window.
howToPlay: Never preemptively waste your *Indestructible* shield for minor poke; save its massive barrier specifically for when Renekton's blades glow with *Ruthless Predator*. When he dashes forward with *Slice and Dice*, stand your ground. As he tries to retreat after his combo, pull him back with *Death's Grasp* to trigger *Darkness Rise* and run him down. If he activates *Dominus* to survive, immediately counter with *Realm of Death* to steal his amplified health.
laneImpact: Because you can consistently negate his burst, Renekton is forced to play defensively. He cannot easily stack *Reign of Anger* on the minion wave without risking a deadly pull from your *Death's Grasp*. This gives you total control over the wave state. You can easily set up slow pushes, crash huge waves under his turret, and harass him with isolated *Obliterate* strikes while he struggles under pressure.
why: This matchup hinges on neutralizing Renekton's burst rotation. The crocodile wants to dash in with *Slice and Dice*, execute an empowered *Ruthless Predator* stun, and retreat. By saving *Indestructible* to absorb the exact moment he unleashes his stun, you negate his entire trading pressure. Once his main burst is spent on your shield, his long cooldowns leave him completely defenseless against your *Darkness Rise* aura in an extended chase.

summary: Teemo's Blinding Dart completely negates Jax's basic attacks and Empower, forcing Jax to wait out the blind before trading.
howToPlay: To survive, never initiate with Leap Strike while his blind is available. Instead, walk up to threaten farm and bait out Blinding Dart. Once he wastes it, you have a brief window to engage using Leap Strike and Empower. If he holds his blind, activate Counter Strike to block his basic attacks while you retreat to the safety of the brush. If your health drops too low, abandon CS entirely and simply soak experience.
laneImpact: This dynamic forces you to concede early wave control, as securing minions exposes you to relentless Toxic Shot poke. If you initiate a trade recklessly, a well-timed Blinding Dart leaves you defenseless, resulting in disastrous health trades that force premature recalls. Consequently, you will spend the early game defending your tower, struggling to maintain equal gold while waiting for safe windows to farm.
why: Teemo completely neutralizes your offensive threat by utilizing his ranged advantage alongside a specific defensive tool. When you attempt to close the distance, his Blinding Dart nullifies your basic attacks and cancels the bonus magic damage from Empower. This interaction prevents you from stacking Relentless Assault during trades, meaning you cannot out-damage his toxic passive unless his primary defensive utility is entirely depleted.

howToPlay: Hold Sear until Rakan starts Grand Entrance and apply Blaze with Conflagration or Pillar of Flame on his landing area. Aim the stun after he arrives, then stand between him and your carry without chasing Battle Dance. While The Quickness is active, separate your duo so only one player can be charmed.
laneImpact: If you spend Sear on poke, Rakan can use Grand Entrance during its cooldown and leave with Battle Dance. If you hold it, he must respect the area around your carry and the lane stays steadier. A successful knock-up restores his brush control; a stopped entry gives you wave priority.
why: Grand Entrance requires Rakan to land inside your duo to knock targets up, then Battle Dance returns him to an ally. That entry gives Brand a nearby target for Blaze and Pillar of Flame, but the initial control can interrupt your setup. The matchup therefore depends on keeping Sear for the landing.

summary: Kassadin's Null Sphere shields him against Brand's magic damage, and his Riftwalk allows him to easily dodge Brand's skillshots post-6.
howToPlay: To survive, you must focus entirely on controlling the minion wave near your turret. Never blindly push with Pillar of Flame. Instead, use Conflagration to safely thin the wave while keeping the minions on your side of the lane. Keep your Sear ready to deter his aggressive jumps; never throw it proactively while his Riftwalk is off cooldown. If he does engage with Riftwalk, immediately drop Pyroclasm and Conflagration on him to punish his dive.
laneImpact: This matchup severely limits your early pressure. You cannot safely trade health because Kassadin sustains through your poke, meaning you cannot easily force him out of lane. After level five, the threat of Riftwalk into Force Pulse means you cannot overextend past the river. You are forced to play back, which concedes mid priority and lets him freely scale into an unstoppable late-game monster.
why: Kassadin is your worst nightmare because he is built to absorb magic damage and dodge skillshots. Every time you try to poke him, his Null Sphere generates a magic shield that nullifies your Pillar of Flame damage, while his Void Stone grants him additional shielding just for you casting spells. Once he unlocks Riftwalk, he can effortlessly blink over your Sear and Pillar of Flame, rendering your entire burst combo useless.

summary: Sona's Aria of Perseverance can nullify Seraphine's poke, forcing Seraphine to look for a decisive Encore to burst Sona down before she out-scales.
howToPlay: Stop wasting mana on raw poke. Instead, save your Echo cast from Stage Presence for a double Beat Drop to root Sona when she steps up to trigger Hymn of Valor. The moment she wastes Aria of Perseverance, you have a twelve-second window where her sustain is offline. Use this exact gap to call your jungler or commit with Encore to burst her down instantly. If she plays safely out of range, use Surround Sound to match her rotations and protect your carry from her Crescendo.
laneImpact: Sona's lane pressure is deceptive; while she rarely threatens to kill you early, her Hymn of Valor coupled with Power Chord slowly chips away at your carry. If you spam High Note to respond, her Aria of Perseverance will erase the damage, leaving you mana-starved. This neutralizes your wave control and forces a slow, defensive lane where Sona comfortably farms her passive, slowly choking out your map presence.
why: Sona's Aria of Perseverance systematically neutralizes your poke from High Note and Beat Drop, leaving you unable to whittle down her health pool. Because Sona's late-game teamfighting scaling far outpaces yours, trading passively only plays into her hands. You cannot win a battle of attrition against her constant healing and shielding, making you reliant on finding a high-impact Encore to burst her before she takes over.

summary: Syndra can knock you out of your Heroic Swing mid-flight using Scatter the Weak, completely halting your engage.
howToPlay: Never initiate trades with Heroic Swing unless you have physically seen Syndra cast Scatter the Weak. Instead, use Going Rogue to approach from stealth and bait her stun using simple movement. If she holds her spell, poke her with Avengerang and your double-shot passive, Dirty Fighting. Should she miss or waste the knockback, immediately swing in for a full-burst trade. If she catches you mid-swing because you miscalculated, use Comeuppance from behind minions to salvage the trade.
laneImpact: When Scatter the Weak is active, you cannot use Heroic Swing aggressively, forcing you to farm passively with Avengerang. This shifts the wave priority in Syndra's favor, allowing her to stack Dark Sphere charges and poke you down. However, the moment she wastes her knockback to clear waves or harass, the power dynamic flips instantly, opening a massive window for you to dive in.
why: The matchup hinges entirely on how you use Heroic Swing. Because Syndra's Scatter the Weak can knock you directly out of your swing mid-air, a reckless engage will always leave you stunned and vulnerable. You have the mobility advantage, but only if you respect her basic defensive tool, turning this midlane duel into a tense baiting game around her crucial self-peel cooldown.

summary: Orianna can disrupt your stationary Breath of Light channel from safety using Command: Shockwave.
howToPlay: To survive, you must anchor your positioning behind your caster minions, using Singularity solely to freeze or slow down incoming waves rather than to fight. Never activate Breath of Light while her Command: Shockwave is available unless she has already misplaced her ball. If she moves forward to zone you, use Astral Flight backward immediately to escape the radius of her Command: Dissonance, accepting that you must give up some farm to secure your scaling.
laneImpact: During the early levels, Orianna dictates the wave state by placing her ball aggressively. If you attempt to secure minions using Singularity, she will punish you with Command: Attack and Command: Dissonance. You are forced to farm under tower, bleeding health whenever you try to match her push. This constant harass delays your Stardust scaling and forces early recalls, giving her free opportunities to pressure your mid turret.
why: Orianna dominates this matchup because her sphere allows her to zone you from a distance where you cannot safely channel. When you try to stack Stardust using Breath of Light, you must stand still, making you an easy target. She can easily reposition her ball with Command: Attack and immediately interrupt your channel from afar using Command: Shockwave, completely neutralizing your primary damage source while keeping herself entirely out of your reach.

summary: Varus must avoid standing near walls where Zoe can extend the range of her Sleepy Trouble Bubble to set up a lethal Paddle Star!.
howToPlay: Maintain a strict midline positioning, staying dead center in the lane to maximize your distance from both side walls. Never hug the terrain. If Zoe uses Portal Jump forward to fish for a bubble, immediately fire Hail of Arrows to slow her return path, then charge Piercing Arrow to punish her predictable snapback location. Keep Chain of Corruption ready to lock her down instantly if she attempts an aggressive forward teleport within your tower's range.
laneImpact: You are forced into a defensive posture, constantly tethering away from the river ledges. This restriction limits your ability to safely secure minions with basic attacks, forcing you to deplete your mana using Piercing Arrow or Hail of Arrows from deep under your turret.
