If Zoe secures lane priority, she can use Spell Thief on dropped active items to roam, while you remain trapped, unable to follow.
why: Zoe dominates this poke war because her Sleepy Trouble Bubble can travel through mid lane's thick walls, catching you off guard. If she lands it, she easily setup a maximum-distance Paddle Star! combined with Portal Jump and More Sparkles! to instantly burst your health bar. While your Piercing Arrow offers great retaliatory range, Zoe's mobility and threat from fog of war make trading highly asymmetric.

summary: Swain lacks the mobility to escape your Singularity, allowing you to freely stack Stardust whenever he attempts to engage with Demonic Ascension.
howToPlay: During the early levels, focus on safe farming while keeping a watchful eye on his Nevermove trajectory. Always hold Astral Flight to instantly disengage if he manages to land a root. Once he unlocks Demonic Ascension and tries to force a fight, place Singularity behind him to cut off his advance, then channel Breath of Light. If he ever flashes forward to force an engage, immediately fly backward to reset your spacing.
laneImpact: This interaction shifts the minion dynamic entirely in your favor. Because Swain cannot aggressively step up without risking a massive health loss inside your zone, you dictate the wave flow. You can easily freeze the minion line near your tower or shove him under his turret using Singularity. This neutralizes his Vision of Empire roams and completely starves him of his Ravenous Flock passive stacks.
why: Swain relies on marching forward during Demonic Ascension to drain your health, but his complete lack of mobility tools makes him the ultimate target for your zoning. The moment he activates his ultimate, dropping Singularity directly on his path traps him. He cannot escape the pull easily, allowing you to safely channel Breath of Light and harvest massive Stardust stacks off his slow-moving frame.

summary: Viktor can zone Galio with Gravity Field (W) when Galio tries to engage, but Galio can match Viktor's waveclear using Winds of War (Q).
howToPlay: Never cast Gravity Field offensively. Hold it exclusively to drop on top of yourself the moment Galio winds up Justice Punch. Use Hextech Ray to thin the wave from a safe distance, aiming to hit both the caster minions and Galio when he steps up to trigger Colossal Smash. If he manages to shove you in and starts moving toward the side lanes, immediately use Arcane Storm to clear the remaining wave and threaten his tower rather than blindly following.
laneImpact: Because Winds of War counters your natural push, you cannot easily trap Galio under his turret. If you misuse your skills, he will crash the wave and look for a Hero's Entrance play elsewhere. Constant trade skirmishes occur when he steps up for Colossal Smash; shielding his burst with Siphon Power is essential to keep your health high enough to prevent him from taking free recalls.
why: This matchup is a pure battle of lane priority. Galio wants to shove and roam, matching your poke easily because Winds of War clears minions from a safe distance. However, his forward engage with Justice Punch is highly predictable. You can completely shut down his aggressive trades by placing Gravity Field directly in his path, forcing him to choose between retreating or getting stunned.

summary: Galio can use the wide area of Shield of Durand (W) to taunt Akali even while she is hidden inside her Twilight Shroud (W).
howToPlay: Never initiate with Justice Punch if Akali has Shuriken Flip available, as she can easily dodge and tag you. Instead, walk up and hold your Shield of Durand. Wait for her to drop Twilight Shroud, then immediately charge and release your taunt inside the smoke. Once she is forced to reveal herself, hit her with a guaranteed Winds of War and Colossal Smash combo, then use Justice Punch to knock her up as she tries to retreat.
laneImpact: Because Akali cannot safely use her shroud to reset trades, she is forced to play passively behind her minions. You can easily shove the wave using Winds of War and Colossal Smash without fear of her retaliating with Five Point Strike. This constant priority allows you to look for Hero's Entrance plays on the side lanes while she is stuck clearing under her tower, bleeding gold.
why: Galio naturally shuts down Akali's assassination attempts because her main defensive tool, Twilight Shroud, is completely countered by your Shield of Durand. When she hides in her smoke to stall or prepare Assassin's Mark procs, the massive area-of-effect taunt forces her to reveal herself and attack you, stripping away her safety. This completely disrupts her rhythm and turns her stealth zone into a trap.

summary: Jax's Counter Strike completely blocks Camille's Precision Protocol, forcing her to bait the ability out before committing with Hookshot.
howToPlay: To survive, use Tactical Sweep from maximum range to secure minion last hits and slowly chip his health. Never initiate with Hookshot; instead, walk up to trigger your Adaptive Defenses shield, baiting Jax into activating Counter Strike. The instant his lantern spins, use Hookshot to grapple onto a nearby wall, perching safely out of his reach until his defensive stance expires, then dive back in to retaliate.
laneImpact: You cannot contest waves early, as Jax can zone you off the minions by holding his Evasion. If you step up to last hit, Leap Strike followed by Empower allows him to trade with zero risk. You will constantly find yourself pushed under turret, bleeding gold, while Jax maintains high Relentless Assault stacks, making any direct duel impossible and giving him free reign to crash waves and threaten plate damage.
why: Jax completely neutralizes your offensive pressure because Counter Strike blocks both activations of Precision Protocol. Since Camille relies on the true damage from her second sweep, Jax can simply activate his evasion whenever you try to trade, completely absorbing your main burst. This forces you into a passive state, as jumping in with Hookshot while his defensive tool is up results in a disastrous stun and swift retaliation.

summary: Aatrox must use Umbral Dash backwards to escape Darius's Decimate inner circle and prevent Hemorrhage stacks.
howToPlay: Never initiate trades with Umbral Dash; keep it strictly to react when Darius winds up Decimate. If he misses his pull, Apprehend, you have a solid window to pressure him with The Darkin Blade and Infernal Chains. Should Darius get too close, immediately activate Deathbringer Stance for the extra range and healing, then drop Infernal Chains to pull him back while retreating.
laneImpact: Missed dashes mean Darius pulls you with Apprehend, leading to a lethal Noxian Guillotine. When Aatrox successfully spaces the Decimate, he maintains wave control, allowing him to slow-push and harass with The Darkin Blade. However, failing a single trade forces an early recall, giving Darius free reign to freeze the lane, crash massive waves, and threaten tower dives.
why: This lane is a knife-edge spacing duel. Darius relies on landing the outer edge of Decimate to heal and stack Hemorrhage alongside Crippling Strike. Aatrox keeps him at bay with The Darkin Blade. The entire matchup hinges on a single movement: Aatrox using Umbral Dash backwards to escape Darius's Decimate inner circle and prevent Hemorrhage stacks, turning a deadly trade into a favorable disengage.

summary: Tempered Fate is an excellent tool to interrupt Seraphine's Encore or freeze her before she can cast her high-impact spells.
howToPlay: To survive, never cast Encore while Bard still holds Tempered Fate, unless you are completely out of his range. Track his cooldowns meticulously; when his ultimate is down, you have a brief window to play aggressively and use Beat Drop to lock down targets. Position yourself strictly in open space, far from terrain, to deny him easy Cosmic Binding angles. If he portals in with Magical Journey, immediately prepare Surround Sound to absorb the incoming burst and disengage.
laneImpact: In lane, Bard's threat forces a very passive posture. You cannot safely fish for poke with High Note without risking a sudden Cosmic Binding stun. Because Traveler’s Call gives him roaming power, he will often leave lane, but his Caretaker’s Shrine keeps his ADC healthy while he is gone. If you try to punish this absence by pushing, his Magical Journey can quickly bring him back to catch you overextended.
why: Bard holds the upper hand because his Tempered Fate acts as the ultimate counter-engage tool against your teamfight setup. The moment you wind up Encore or prepare an Echo-amplified Beat Drop, he can freeze you in stasis, completely wasting your cast or isolating you from your ADC. Additionally, your need to line up linear spells makes you a prime target for Cosmic Binding near walls or minions.

summary: Poppy's Steadfast Presence active completely blocks Camille's Hookshot dash, leaving Camille stranded and highly vulnerable.
howToPlay: Never waste Steadfast Presence just for its movement speed; keep it strictly to react to her Hookshot. Position yourself close to the lane walls to bait her into grappling, then reactively activate your shield to knock her down. The moment she is grounded, immediately align your Heroic Charge to slam her into that same wall, following up with Hammer Shock. If she tries to trap you with The Hextech Ultimatum, simply use Keeper's Verdict to blow her out of her own zone.
laneImpact: This interaction completely strips Camille of her offensive initiative. She cannot safely use Tactical Sweep to poke or thin the wave without exposing herself to a sudden Heroic Charge. Since she cannot rely on Hookshot to escape, she is forced to concede wave control. You can safely freeze the wave near your turret, forcing her to step up into narrow corridors where any mistake results in a fatal wall-stun.
why: Poppy hard-counters Camille because Steadfast Presence acts as an absolute wall against Camille's primary engagement tool, Hookshot. When Camille attempts to grapple off a wall to dive you, activating Steadfast Presence instantly interrupts her mid-air, grounding her and preventing her from triggering her attack speed buff. This leaves her stranded without an escape, turning her primary offensive tool into a self-inflicted stun trap right next to terrain.

summary: K'Sante's All Out converts his defensive stats into offensive power, allowing him to shred Mundo with true damage while ignoring Mundo's passive CC block.
howToPlay: To survive, you must anchor yourself strictly to the lane's center or your own tower. Never hug the alcove or walls when his ultimate is up. Keep Infected Bonesaw active to poke and slow his advances, and always save Maximum Dosage for the immediate aftermath of his All Out activation, using the sudden health surge and movement speed to disengage rather than fight his amplified true damage.
laneImpact: This interaction forces you into a defensive tempo game. Early on, you can contest waves using Infected Bonesaw to farm from afar, but K'Santé's Footwork and Path Maker make trading directly dangerous. Once he reaches level five, stepping past the river midpoint is lethal; a single bad trade allows him to kidnap you under his tower, destroying your recall timings and starving you of gold.
why: K'Sante turns your high-HP pool into a liability once he unlocks All Out. This ultimate converts his resistances into raw offensive power and amplifies Dauntless Instinct to shred you with true damage. Crucially, All Out's displacement ignores the crowd-control immunity of your Goes Where He Pleases passive by forcibly repositioning you over walls regardless, turning your main defensive tool into a wasted cooldown while you are dismantled.

summary: Jax's Counter Strike completely blocks Shyvana's Twin Bite, neutralizing her primary source of burst damage during duels.
howToPlay: Track her camp rotations and invade her when her Burnout is on cooldown from clearing. Use Leap Strike to close the distance immediately after she uses Flame Breath on a monster. Once in melee range, do not activate Counter Strike immediately; wait for the distinctive animation of Twin Bite to trigger your dodge, neutralizing her burst. If she attempts to escape using Dragon's Descent, follow her immediately with an empowered Leap Strike combined with Empower to finish her off.
laneImpact: This matchup shifts the jungle pressure entirely in your favor, allowing you to delay her scaling. Since Shyvana needs to clear camps to stack Fury of the Dragonborn, your ability to bully her out of her own camps severely delays her Dragon's Descent and overall power. You can aggressively contest her camps, forcing her to forfeit monsters or risk dying in her own jungle while her Flame Breath mark goes to waste.
why: Jax completely dominates the 1v1 duels in the jungle because Counter Strike entirely negates Shyvana's Twin Bite. Since Twin Bite is her primary source of burst damage and resets her auto-attack timer, dodging both strikes removes her lethal threat. Without her double-strike landing, Shyvana cannot match Jax's ramping attack speed from Relentless Assault, leaving her with only the damage over time from Burnout to fight back.

summary: Rakan can use Battle Dance to escape Rell's engage attempts, then immediately turn the fight with Grand Entrance on her vulnerable ADC.
howToPlay: To succeed, never start a fight with Ferromancy: Crashdown. Instead, run at them with Full Tilt to threaten the flip, forcing Rakan to burn Battle Dance prematurely. Once he has jumped away, you can safely use Shattering Strike to break his Fey Feathers shield or drop Magnet Storm to disrupt his Grand Entrance. Always position yourself slightly ahead of your ADC to intercept his jump path.
laneImpact: This interaction forces a very tense, reactive laning phase where neither support can blindly shove. If you miss your entry, your ADC is forced to retreat under tower, giving up wave control and priority. However, if you can zone Rakan away from his ally, his Fey Feathers shield won't save him from Shattering Strike, meaning lane dominance hinges entirely on who controls the spacing.
why: The lane revolves around baiting movement spells. If you commit with Ferromancy: Crashdown, Rakan can easily dodge the impact by casting Battle Dance to jump to his partner. This leaves you slowed and dismounted, giving Rakan the perfect opportunity to immediately counter-engage with Grand Entrance on your now-defenseless ADC, turning your own aggression into a lethal trap.

summary: Vayne can easily dodge Mordekaiser's skillshots with Tumble and use Condemn to push him away if he attempts to trap her in the Realm of Death.
howToPlay: Survival requires absolute discipline under your own turret. Never initiate with Death's Grasp; instead, hold it to threaten a pull only if she overextends into turret range. When she activates Final Hour, immediately retreat and use Indestructible to block the third stack of Silver Bolts rather than trying to chase her. If you must use Realm of Death, wait until she has already wasted Condemn, otherwise you will spend your entire ultimate running back to her.
laneImpact: Because you cannot threaten her, you are forced to concede early wave control. Vayne will comfortably freeze or slow-push while using Silver Bolts to punish you every time you walk up to secure minion gold. Your Indestructible shield will constantly be depleted just to absorb her ranged poke, forcing you into early, disadvantageous recalls that bleed tower plates and leave you starved of gold.
why: Landing your skillshots is almost impossible because Vayne can reactively dodge both Obliterate and Death's Grasp using the short-cooldown dash of Tumble. Even if you manage to close the distance or trap her inside your Realm of Death, she holds a supreme counter-measure; her Condemn will instantly knock you away to the edge of your own arena, leaving you helpless while she melts you with Silver Bolts.

summary: Neither champion has hard crowd control to trigger Goes Where He Pleases, turning the lane into a pure sustain battle between Transfusion and Infected Bonesaw.
howToPlay: To break this endless loop, you must alter your build path early to rush anti-healing and magic resistance rather than your usual health-stacking items, as his Crimson Pact scales off his own health anyway. Back off immediately when his resource bar turns red, indicating his empowered Transfusion is ready. Once it decays, step up to throw Infected Bonesaw or clear the wave with Blunt Force Trauma. If he dives you under tower, activate Maximum Dosage early to bait his Hemoplague explosion.
laneImpact: Trades are constant but rarely lethal early. Vladimir tries to poke you down with his third, empowered Transfusion while using Sanguine Pool to dodge your counter-attacks. Because you both have immense staying power, neither of you can easily force a recall. The lane stays locked in a stalemate where minion waves are cleared slowly using Blunt Force Trauma and Tides of Blood until one player mismanages their health pool.
why: Since Vladimir lacks any hard crowd control, your passive Goes Where He Pleases is completely useless here, never giving you those healing canisters. Instead, this matchup becomes a direct, uninterrupted battle of attrition between your Infected Bonesaw and his Transfusion. Because both of you can constantly regenerate health without needing to base, the lane is decided entirely by who manages their health costs and healing cycles better.

summary: Garen must use Decisive Strike to silence Sett before he can cast Haymaker at maximum grit.
howToPlay: Initiate short trades with Judgment instead of leading with your silence. As Sett’s grit bar fills up, hit him with Decisive Strike to silence him, preventing his Haymaker, then immediately retreat while activating Courage to block his physical attacks. If you fail to silence him in time, quickly step sideways to dodge the center line of Haymaker while your shield is up. Lastly, never cast Demacian Justice while his golden shield is active; wait for it to decay.
laneImpact: Sett's constant threat of Facebreaker forces you to respect his zone, making blind wave-clearing with Judgment highly dangerous. If he pulls you in, a simple trade escalates into a disaster. You cannot comfortably crash waves when his The Show Stopper is online, as he can slam you into his tower. Every bad trade where he lands a high-grit Haymaker forces you out of lane, granting him free plates and total wave control.
why: Sett dominates extended trades because Pit Grit and Knuckle Down out-damage you in melee range, while his Haymaker converts your own damage into a massive shield and true damage nuke. Because both champions possess high passive health regeneration, this becomes a war of attrition. The entire matchup hinges on Decisive Strike; you must silence Sett right as his grit bar peaks, preventing him from casting Haymaker before you disengage.

summary: Kindred must use Dance of Arrows to dodge Vault Breaker, as getting hit allows Vi to chain her crowd control before Lamb's Respite can be cast.
howToPlay: Never initiate with a fully charged Vault Breaker from plain sight, as Kindred will easily dodge it. Instead, run at them to trigger Blast Shield and force Dance of Arrows first. Once they dash, release your punch or lock them down directly with Cease and Desist, which guarantees your follow-up CC. If they hold their dash, use Relentless Force to trade while saving your gap-closers.
laneImpact: This dynamic heavily restricts Kindred's freedom to collect passive marks in the river. Since they cannot risk facechecking you, you can aggressively invade their camps. Every skirmish is decided by whether Kindred's dash is available. If they burn Dance of Arrows to clear a camp or kite, you gain immediate jungle priority and can force them off objectives.
why: You hold the upper hand because your explosive crowd control can completely deny Kindred's ultimate. The entire matchup hinges on Vault Breaker. If you land this punch, you can immediately chain your crowd control into Cease and Desist, bursting them down before they can react with Lamb's Respite. To survive, Kindred is forced to anticipate your charge and use Dance of Arrows defensively to dodge.

summary: Amumu's Tantrum flat physical damage reduction is highly effective against Jax's rapid basic attacks from Relentless Assault.
howToPlay: To survive this matchup, you must track Amumu's cooldowns and avoid initiating with Leap Strike. Save your jump to escape over walls when he commits with Bandage Toss. Only engage if his Tantrum has just been wasted on jungle monsters and his team cannot follow up. If he triggers Curse of the Sad Mummy, use Counter Strike immediately to dodge the basic attacks of his allies while waiting out his crowd control before trying to retaliate with Empower.
laneImpact: In the jungle, this interaction prevents you from contesting Amumu in direct duels or early skirmishes. If you try to fight him near camps, his Despair and constant Tantrum resets will melt your health bar while yours barely scratches his armor. You will lose priority for early Scuttle Crabs, forcing you to concede objectives or risk getting locked down by Bandage Toss for an easy enemy collapse.
why: This matchup is highly unfavorable because Jax relies on stacking Relentless Assault for rapid basic attacks, which directly plays into Amumu's strengths. The passive component of Tantrum grants Amumu flat physical damage reduction that severely cripples your attack-speed-based DPS. Furthermore, every strike you land reduces the cooldown of Tantrum, allowing Amumu to spam his area-of-effect damage while shrugging off your physical pressure.

summary: Mordekaiser can use Death's Grasp or Realm of Death to interrupt Shen's Stand United channel, preventing him from assisting his team across the map.
howToPlay: To salvage this matchup, never channel Stand United in his line of sight. Wait for him to waste Death's Grasp on a pull attempt before walking back to cast. If he holds it, use Shadow Dash defensively to escape his Realm of Death range or to slide under your turret. When you must ult to save a carry, accept that you will lose at least two plates; do not hesitate to sacrifice your tower if it guarantees a major cross-map shutdown.
laneImpact: Because you must retreat deep under tower or into your jungle to cast Stand United, Mordekaiser gains free reign over the wave. He will shove you in with Obliterate and Darkness Rise, chipping your tower or taking plates. If you try to match his push, he wins short trades using Indestructible to negate your Twilight Assault damage, slowly grinding you down and locking you to your tier-one turret.
why: Mordekaiser completely neutralizes your primary map influence. Your goal with Stand United is to turn fights elsewhere, but Mordekaiser can easily cancel the channel using the displacement of Death's Grasp or by banishing you directly with Realm of Death. This means you cannot safely cast your ultimate while visible in lane, forcing you to forfeit minion waves just to find a safe fog-of-war position to channel.

summary: Teemo's Blinding Dart outranges Vayne's basic attacks, preventing her from proc'ing Silver Bolts during short trades.
howToPlay: Never initiate trades with Blinding Dart raw. Instead, bait her forward by threatening her with Toxic Shot enhanced auto-attacks. The moment she uses Tumble forward to retaliate, immediately fire Blinding Dart to negate her enhanced attack and prevent Silver Bolts progress. If she tries to pin you with Condemn, use Move Quick to reposition away from walls and deploy Noxious Trap in her retreat path to punish her retreat.
laneImpact: Vayne is forced into a defensive posture, unable to freely contest the minion wave. Whenever she steps up to farm, you can deny her gold and force her to use Condemn defensively. This keeps her pinned under her turret, bleeding gold, while you maintain complete bush control using Guerrilla Warfare and secure easy recall timings without losing turret plates.
why: Teemo's Blinding Dart has a longer range than Vayne's basic attack range. When Vayne tries to use Tumble to initiate a trade, Teemo can immediately shut her down. By blinding her instantly, she cannot land the three consecutive hits needed to trigger Silver Bolts, rendering her primary damage source useless while Toxic Shot ticks away at her health.

summary: Lucian needs to abuse his Lightslinger passive and Piercing Light early to build a lead before Vayne scales with Silver Bolts and Final Hour.
howToPlay: To survive, you must hold Tumble strictly as a defensive tool to dodge the linear trajectory of Piercing Light. Do not attempt trade-backs; focus purely on securing minions under tower. Once you reach level five and have Final Hour, wait for him to waste Relentless Pursuit forward before popping your ultimate. Utilize Condemn to push him away if he attempts to channel The Culling, neutralizing his ultimate's massive burst.
laneImpact: You will constantly be pushed under tower as Lucian uses Piercing Light to clear waves and poke you simultaneously. This lane-wide pressure forces you to sacrifice early gold to preserve your health bar, delaying your core items. If you get chunked too low, Lucian will zone you off experience or setup a dive with Relentless Pursuit, bleeding your turret's plates and letting him rotate first.
why: Lucian dominates the early game by combining Piercing Light with his Lightslinger double-attacks, chunking your health before you can retaliate. Vayne struggles here because her early DPS is gated by getting three hits for Silver Bolts. However, if you survive this early pressure, the scaling gap closes dramatically once you unlock Final Hour and max out Silver Bolts, allowing you to out-DPS him in extended duels.

summary: Wukong can close the distance instantly with Nimbus Strike and disrupt Twitch's Spray and Pray ultimate using Cyclone knockups.
howToPlay: Avoid initiating on the enemy frontline during teamfights. Instead, hover in the fog of war and wait for Twitch to break his Ambush stealth and trigger Spray and Pray. The moment he reveals himself, instantly jump him with Nimbus Strike, shred his armor with Golden Staff, and disrupt his output with Cyclone. If he attempts to reposition or escape, use Warrior Trickster to close any remaining distance and apply your second knock-up.
laneImpact: Throughout the early skirmishes and objective contests, this dynamic grants you immense map pressure. Twitch cannot safely stack Deadly Venom or cast Contaminate when threatened by an immediate engage. This vulnerability forces him to yield crab control and delay his jungle clears, as entering unwarded river corridors risks a fatal encounter with you before he can ever ramp up his DPS.
why: This matchup is highly advantageous because you possess the perfect tools to shut down Twitch's primary damage window. When Twitch exits Ambush and activates Spray and Pray to pierce your team, your Nimbus Strike allows you to instantly gap-close. Follow up immediately with Cyclone to knock him airborne, completely neutralizing his ultimate's duration and leaving him defenseless against your burst.

summary: Thresh can interrupt Zenith Blade mid-dash with Flay, so Leona should look to engage when Flay is on cooldown or use Solar Flare to stun from range first.
howToPlay: To bypass this disruption, you must change your engage pattern. Never lead with Zenith Blade unless you have seen Thresh waste Flay on minions or to push. Instead, wait for level five and initiate from distance with Solar Flare. If the center stun lands, you can follow up with your full crowd control chain before he can react. Alternatively, stand parallel to your carry to block incoming Death Sentence hooks with your active Eclipse armor.
laneImpact: Since you cannot freely press Zenith Blade, you lose early lane priority and wave control. If you attempt a raw engage and get interrupted, Thresh immediately retaliates with Death Sentence to lock down your carry, or uses Dark Passage to easily rescue his own AD carry from any bad trade. This pressure forces you to play defensively under your own tower, sacrificing early gold and map presence.
why: This matchup is heavily dictated by how your Zenith Blade interacts with Thresh's Flay. Because Zenith Blade has a predictable, linear dash, a skilled Thresh can easily react and sweep you out of the air mid-flight. This completely cancels your primary engage tool, leaving you stranded in the minion wave without triggering your Shield of Daybreak stun, while his Damnation armor scaling makes him progressively harder to burst down.

summary: Vladimir can use Sanguine Pool to dodge Aatrox's Infernal Chains pull, but its extremely long cooldown leaves him vulnerable to subsequent Q rotations.
howToPlay: Start trades by angling the first strike of The Darkin Blade to force him sideways, then throw Infernal Chains directly at him. The moment he sinks into Sanguine Pool, immediately stop attacking and hold your remaining Q strikes. Once he resurfaces, use Umbral Dash forward to land the final sweetspots. If he plays too safely after pooling, freeze the minions near your turret to starve him of Transfusion targets.
laneImpact: This dynamic turns the lane into a constant zone of threat. You can easily control the wave minion flow because Vladimir cannot contest your push without risking an engage. Every time you force him to pool, he must retreat to his tower, giving up gold and experience. This pressure forces him into defensive Hemoplague usage just to survive, stripping away his mid-game teamfight threat before he can scale.
why: Aatrox dominates this matchup because his relentless healing from Deathbringer Stance and Umbral Dash outpaces Vladimir's Transfusion over prolonged trades. While Vladimir can dissolve into Sanguine Pool to escape the pull of your Infernal Chains, doing so burns his only defensive tool. Because Sanguine Pool's cooldown is nearly double that of your own abilities, he is left completely defenseless against your next two rotations of The Darkin Blade.

summary: Annie can hold her Pyromania passive to instantly stun Akali with Disintegrate or Summon: Tibbers the moment she tries to engage.
howToPlay: Your only real openings occur when Annie mismanages her passive. Monitor her stun counter constantly; if she uses Disintegrate to last-hit and drops her Pyromania charges, immediately look to trade with Shuriken Flip. If she refuses to discharge her stun, stay out of her range and use Five Point Strike exclusively for safe farming. When she inevitably summons Tibbers, immediately drop Twilight Shroud to buy time and retreat rather than attempting to fight through the bear's burn.
laneImpact: This threat forces you into a highly defensive posture where you must forfeit early wave control. Annie can easily zone you away from the minion wave with her ranged advantage, forcing you to bleed health or burn energy using Five Point Strike just to secure last hits. If you try to force a trade, a quick Pyromania-infused Incinerate leaves you stunned and vulnerable to massive retaliation from Summon: Tibbers.
why: Annie's Pyromania is a constant roadblock for your aggressive options. Because she can simply hold onto her four-charge stun indefinitely, any attempt to close the distance with Shuriken Flip or Perfect Execution is met with an instant point-and-click Disintegrate or an area-of-effect Summon: Tibbers. This immediate lockdown prevents you from weaving Assassin's Mark passive attacks and completely neutralizes your safety inside Twilight Shroud.

summary: Using Shuriken Flip (E) to dodge his Decimate (Q) outer ring completely neutralizes his healing and passive stack generation.
howToPlay: To survive, never initiate trades with Decimate. Instead, walk up to last-hit and wait for Akali to waste Shuriken Flip offensively or to clear minions. The moment that tool is down, hook her in with Apprehend, immediately slow her with Crippling Strike to prevent her from escaping, and only then swing your axe. If she hides in Twilight Shroud, immediately retreat toward your minions to deny her the space to proc Assassin's Mark.
laneImpact: Because you cannot reliably land the outer ring of Decimate, trading health becomes highly disadvantageous. Akali will constantly poke you with Five Point Strike and slip into Twilight Shroud to drop minion aggro and block your Apprehend. You are forced to concede wave control, sitting under your tower to avoid being whittled down into the execution threshold of her Perfect Execution.
why: This matchup hinges entirely on how Akali uses Shuriken Flip to deny your main healing source. Whenever you wind up Decimate to stack Hemorrhage, she can easily flip backward, completely escaping the outer blade's damage and heal. Denied this crucial sustain and your passive progression, you are left vulnerable while she retains the option to recast her shuriken and dash back onto you with an empowered Assassin's Mark.

summary: Shyvana lacks crowd control to stop Ekko, allowing him to safely disengage with Z-Drive Resonance or setup Parallel Convergence on her predictable Dragon's Descent landing.
howToPlay: To beat his scaling, focus purely on a speed-clearing tempo. Do not initiate fights with Dragon's Descent ; instead, farm your camps rapidly to secure Fury of the Dragonborn stacks. Wait for Ekko to waste Parallel Convergence or Phase Dive before joining a fight. If he jumps on you, use the movement speed from Burnout to dodge Timewinder's return path, then retaliate with Flame Breath only after he has used Chronobreak to escape.
laneImpact: Because you cannot lock him down, Ekko dictates the pace of skirmishes and can invade with Phase Dive to steal camps. If you get caught in a counter-gank, his burst from Timewinder combined with his passive will easily out-damage your sustained Burnout DPS. This forces you into a passive farming route, delaying your Fury of the Dragonborn stacks and giving him map priority.
why: Shyvana's lack of hard crowd control makes locking Ekko down almost impossible. When you launch yourself forward with Dragon's Descent, your landing trajectory is highly predictable. This gives Ekko the perfect window to place Parallel Convergence directly onto your landing spot for an easy stun, or simply proc Z-Drive Resonance to gain massive movement speed and disengage safely before you can apply Twin Bite or Flame Breath marks.

summary: Jarvan's Demacian Standard provides attack speed to allies, encouraging grouping which denies Kha'Zix his isolation damage from Taste Their Fear.
howToPlay: Never facecheck bushes in your jungle; toss Demacian Standard first to gain vision. During teamfights, resist the urge to dive their backline immediately. Instead, hold your Dragon Strike and Demacian Standard combo to drop it directly on your vulnerable carries. This provides them defense through grouping and armor shred on Kha'Zix when he breaks Void Assault stealth. If jumped while alone, activate Golden Aegis to slow him and retreat toward your closest camp.
laneImpact: Invading or contesting Scuttle Crabs alone is highly dangerous, as Kha'Zix can easily catch you isolated in the river and shred your health bar. However, during early skirmishes around lanes or objectives, your flag alters the map dynamic. If you fight near your laners, his threat level plummets, forcing him to use Leap defensively rather than to execute, stalling his snowball potential.
why: This jungle duel hinges on how well you manage spatial distance around your teammates. Kha'Zix relies entirely on Taste Their Fear dealing amplified damage to isolated targets. By dropping your Demacian Standard, you provide an active incentive for your allies to group up within its attack speed aura. This natural gathering of your team directly denies his isolation passive, neutralizing his burst potential during skirmishes.

summary: Aim Decimate carefully when Irelia has low-health minions nearby, as she will try to use Bladesurge to dodge the outer blade.
howToPlay: Never cast Decimate proactively when your own minions are low; instead, wait for her to commit Bladesurge to a target, then swing. Use Apprehend to disrupt her dash mid-air, which cancels her reset and leaves her stranded without mobility. If she parries your burst with Defiant Dance, hold Noxian Guillotine until the physical damage reduction channel ends, then execute her before she can stack Ionian Fervor to full power.
laneImpact: The wave state dictates the pressure. When your minions are dying, Irelia gains massive threat because she can reset Bladesurge to dance around you and dodge your skillshots. If you push mindlessly, you hand her the perfect runway to stack her passive and out-trade you. A single missed Decimate on a crashing wave completely ruins your health bar and forces a terrible recall, giving her free tower pressure.
why: This matchup is a pure execution race where your passives collide. Irelia wants to stack Ionian Fervor on the wave before jumping on you, while you need to stack Hemorrhage to trigger Noxian Might. The entire lane hinges on whether she can use Bladesurge to dodge into your inner handle during Decimate, denying your healing and outer blade damage while putting herself in prime position to shred you.

summary: Sett can interrupt Shen's global teleport, Stand United, by pulling him with Facebreaker or suppressing him with The Show Stopper.
howToPlay: Walk up to bait his Facebreaker before attempting any cross-map teleports. If he holds it, use Shadow Dash backwards to create distance, then channel Stand United out of his visual range. When trading in lane, always hold Spirit's Refuge until Sett activates Knuckle Down to block his heavy-hitting punches, and immediately sidestep to avoid the true damage center of his Haymaker while your Ki Barrier absorbs the remaining physical damage.
laneImpact: Because Sett can cancel your teleport, you cannot simply retreat under tower and channel to save your team. You are forced to contest the wave directly. Missing your Shadow Dash allows Sett to pull you in with Facebreaker and charge up a massive Haymaker. This pressure restricts your map-wide impact, anchoring you to the top lane unless you find a clean window where his crowd control is down.
why: This lane is a pure contest of cooldown tracking and denial. Sett holds the ultimate tool to shut down your global presence, as either his Facebreaker pull or The Show Stopper suppression can instantly cancel your Stand United channel. Meanwhile, your Spirit's Refuge completely nullifies his Knuckle Down and Pit Grit punches, turning his aggressive trades into wasted animations if timed correctly.

summary: Riven can use Valor and Broken Wings to dance around Aatrox's Q sweetspots, but she is highly vulnerable if caught by Infernal Chains without dashes.
howToPlay: To win this duel, never cast Infernal Chains until you see Riven commit Valor or at least two hops of Broken Wings. Hold your Umbral Dash defensively to reposition your second and third The Darkin Blade strikes reactively rather than trying to predict her dashes. If she activates Blade of the Exile to all-in you, immediately trigger World Ender, use your enhanced movement speed to kite backward, and wait out her ultimate's duration before turning the fight.
laneImpact: Every trade in this lane is explosive and swings momentum immediately. If Riven successfully baits your first two The Darkin Blade strikes, she will initiate short, punishing trades with Ki Burst and retreat before you can retaliate. Conversely, pulling her back with Infernal Chains locks her in place, allowing you to crash the wave, force her under turret, and establish a massive health lead that secures early lane priority.
why: This matchup is a pure test of spacing and reaction times. Riven relies on the rapid dashes of Broken Wings and the shield from Valor to weave inside and outside of your The Darkin Blade sweetspots, neutralizing your main damage source. However, her high-mobility dance relies entirely on these short cooldowns; if she expends them and gets caught by Infernal Chains, she cannot escape the pull, leaving her completely exposed to a massive counter-offensive.

summary: Pantheon can instantly cancel Sion's Decimating Smash charge by using Shield Vault, completely neutralizing Sion's primary waveclear and damage tool.
howToPlay: To execute this perfectly, never use Shield Vault proactively to initiate trades. Walk up and threaten Sion with Comet Spear pokes instead. Force him to activate Soul Furnace or start charging Decimating Smash out of desperation. The moment you see his axe raise, unleash Shield Vault to cancel it, then follow up with an empowered Comet Spear using Mortal Will. If he tries to escape or engage with Unstoppable Onslaught, block his retreat path or use Aegis Assault to absorb his burst.
laneImpact: This interaction dictates the entire laning phase, stripping Sion of his waveclear and lane priority. He cannot charge Decimating Smash to thin out incoming minions without risking a heavy trade. You can freeze the wave at will, deny him passive health from Glory in Death by keeping him away from minions, and dive him easily. This constant pressure prevents Sion from scaling safely or executing comfortable recalls.
why: This lane is heavily skewed in your favor because Sion relies entirely on charging Decimating Smash to threaten both you and the wave. As Pantheon, your Shield Vault acts as an instant, unmissable interrupt. By jumping on Sion the moment he starts swinging his axe, you completely shut down his primary damage and crowd control, leaving him vulnerable with his main tool on cooldown.

summary: Cho'Gath can easily interrupt Aurelion Sol's channeled Breath of Light using either Rupture or Cri primal.
howToPlay: Position aggressively near the minion wave and hold your Rupture. Wait for him to start channeling Breath of Light before casting your spells; interrupting him mid-cast maximizes his cooldown penalty. Use Feral Scream for an instant silence if he steps too close, then follow up with Vorpal Spikes to trade. If he flies away with Astral Flight, aim Rupture slightly ahead of his flight path to knock him out of the sky and execute him with Feast.
laneImpact: This interaction shifts complete control of the minion waves into your hands. Without an uninterrupted Breath of Light, the dragon cannot match your push or clear waves quickly. You can easily freeze the lane near your turret, forcing him to overextend to farm. If he attempts to escape using Astral Flight, a well-timed Rupture knocks him down, securing free kills or forcing early recalls.
why: Cho'Gath completely shuts down Aurelion Sol's trading loop because the dragon must stand still to channel Breath of Light. Both Rupture and Feral Scream instantly interrupt this channel. By cancelling his primary damage source and wave clear tool, you deny him the ability to safely collect Cosmic Creator stacks, leaving him unable to trade back effectively while you sustain through any minor poke with Carnivore.

summary: Lulu can easily interrupt Rell's telegraphed engage by using Whimsy to polymorph her mid-dash, leaving her stranded and vulnerable.
howToPlay: To survive, you must play a patient baiting game. Never initiate with Ferromancy: Crashdown while Lulu holds her polymorph. Instead, feign aggression with Full Tilt to force her to waste Whimsy defensively or on her ally for speed. The moment that ability is on cooldown, you have a brief window to strike. Use Shattering Strike to instantly destroy her Help, Pix! shields, and save Magnet Storm to disrupt her team before she can cast Wild Growth.
laneImpact: This reaction-based counter-matchup strips away your offensive pressure from the very first wave. You cannot safely threaten the bushes because any interrupted jump results in massive health loss from Glitterlance and Help, Pix!. Consequently, your ADC is forced to yield lane priority, allowing Lulu to poke you down under turret while her team safely scales.
why: Lulu possesses the ultimate tool to dismantle your primary engage. Whenever you attempt to close the distance with Ferromancy: Crashdown, the slow, highly visible jump gives her ample time to react. By casting Whimsy mid-dash, she polymorphs you before you can impact the ground. This instantly cancels your knock-up, leaving you dismounted, incredibly slow, and completely exposed to immediate retaliation.

summary: Amumu can buy Control Wards to spot Evelynn's Demon Shade and intercept her with Bandage Toss before she can charm a teammate with Allure.
howToPlay: Prioritize purchasing Control Wards on every single recall and place them in high-traffic river brushes to constantly expose her Demon Shade. When you see her Allure heart forming over an ally, immediately position yourself between them and her projected path. Hold your Bandage Toss until she reveals herself to strike. Once she is bound, activate Despair and spam Tantrum to shred her health pool, forcing her to burn Last Caress defensively rather than for a kill.
laneImpact: This dynamic strips Evelynn of her map-wide terror, forcing her into a passive farming style. Her ganking lanes become predictable because she cannot bypass your defensive setups without being caught. During skirmishes, she is forced to play extremely far back, meaning your laners can push aggressively knowing that any attempt she makes to engage with Whiplash will result in an immediate Curse of the Sad Mummy counter-engage.
why: Amumu dominates this matchup because his heavy crowd control completely neutralizes Evelynn's assassination threat. While she attempts to stalk your allies using Demon Shade, your ability to lockdown targets with Bandage Toss makes her incredibly vulnerable. If she marks someone with Allure, you can reactively intercept her mid-approach, triggering Cursed Touch to amplify your team's damage before she can ever escape with Last Caress.

summary: Vladimir can use Sanguine Pool to dodge Ahri's Charm, neutralizing her burst while healing back any poke with Transfusion.
howToPlay: Never use Sanguine Pool to clear waves; keep it strictly as a counter to Charm. Position yourself behind your minion wave to force Ahri to use Orb of Deception to clear instead of poking you. Once she wastes her crowd control, aggressively walk up with your empowered Transfusion and Tides of Blood to force her to retreat or burn Spirit Rush defensively.
laneImpact: You dictate the tempo of the minion waves. Since Ahri cannot easily burst you, you can safely hold the wave just outside your tower, forcing her to overextend. Her Essence Theft cannot keep up with your resource-free sustain. This constant pressure prevents her from finding roaming opportunities with Spirit Rush, locking her in mid while you slowly build a massive gold advantage.
why: This matchup heavily favors you because Ahri relies entirely on landing her Charm to set up her burst. By saving Sanguine Pool specifically to dodge this projectile, you completely nullify her offensive threat. Even if she tries to wear you down with Orb of Deception, your Transfusion allows you to easily out-sustain her health pool, turning her attempts at poke into wasted mana.

summary: Zyra can easily halt Rumble's forward momentum during his Flamespitter runs by landing Grasping Roots to keep him at bay.
howToPlay: You must bait out Grasping Roots before committing to any forward trade. Use Scrap Shield to absorb poke from her plants while dodging her root sideways. Once Grasping Roots is on cooldown, you have a brief window to retaliate. Charge your heat, land an Electro Harpoon to slow her down, and only then activate Flamespitter to pressure her. If she drops Stranglethorns, immediately disengage with Scrap Shield's movement speed.
laneImpact: This interaction forces you to play defensively under your turret. Zyra will constantly generate seeds with Garden of Thorns and Rampant Growth, using them to push the wave and poke you. If you try to clear her plants with Flamespitter, you put yourself in range of Grasping Roots. This keeps you locked in lane, preventing roaming and letting her secure mid priority.
why: Rumble relies on moving forward with Flamespitter to deal his primary damage, but Zyra's kit excels at stopping this approach. Every time you heat up to chase her down, she can easily deploy Grasping Roots to root you in place, leaving you burning fuel helplessly while her Garden of Thorns plants and Deadly Spines chip away at your health bar from safe range.

summary: Senna's physical damage poke ignores Galio's magic shield, and Curse of the Black Mist makes her untargetable for Justice Punch.
howToPlay: To survive, you must play strictly around bushes to break her vision and force her to walk up. Never initiate with Justice Punch while her Curse of the Black Mist is available; instead, bait her Last Embrace first. Once she steps up to poke, use Winds of War to chunk her from safety, then execute a flash-taunt combo with Shield of Durand to lock her down before she can camouflage. If this all-in fails, immediately fall back under tower.
laneImpact: This structural mismatch forces you into a highly defensive posture from the very first wave. Senna will constantly harvest souls and poke you down under your own turret, rendering Winds of War useless for wave control as you must save your health. Your inability to contest her range means your ADC is starved of farm, and you cannot easily roam with Hero's Entrance without losing your tower extremely early.
why: Senna completely neutralizes your defensive tools while shutting down your initiation. Because her Piercing Darkness and basic attacks deal physical damage, they entirely bypass the passive magic shield from Shield of Durand. Even worse, if you try to engage with Justice Punch, she can activate Curse of the Black Mist, turning into an untargetable wraith that breaks your lock-on and leaves you stranded and exposed.

summary: Diana can reset Lunar Rush on Brand after hitting Crescent Strike, forcing an all-in that Brand struggles to survive without a precise stun.
howToPlay: Position yourself on the opposite side of Crescent Strike’s curved trajectory to make it easier to sidestep. You must hold Sear religiously; never throw it out to poke. When she commits with Lunar Rush, immediately use Conflagration followed by Sear for an instant, point-blank stun. If she activates Pale Cascade to absorb your retaliatory damage, hold Pyroclasm for a brief second until her shield dissipates before unleashing your full explosive sequence.
laneImpact: This matchup forces you into a highly defensive posture where pushing waves is dangerous. Attempting to poke her with Pillar of Flame often puts you within her dash range, making every trade a massive risk. If she successfully chunks your health, she will freeze the wave or dive you, driving you off the farm and preventing you from assisting with river skirmishes while she roams freely.
why: Diana's threat lies entirely in landing Crescent Strike to apply her passive mark. Once you are marked, she can execute a double Lunar Rush to gap-close instantly, pulling you into Moonfall's heavy burst. As an immobile mage, Brand cannot escape this engagement raw. Your survival hinges on reacting instantly with Sear to stun her mid-dive, which requires her to already be ablaze from another spell.

summary: Yuumi's lack of body-blocking presence allows Galio to freely land Justice Punch on her ADC, while her Final Chapter can be mitigated by Shield of Durand.
howToPlay: Position yourself aggressively in front of your minions to deny the enemy ADC any safe farming zone. When Yuumi detaches to trigger Bop 'n' Block, ignore her and immediately aim Justice Punch at her vulnerable carry. If they attempt to turn the fight with Final Chapter, immediately hold and channel Shield of Durand to absorb the magical waves, ensuring you stay healthy enough to finish the fight with Winds of War once the root expires.
laneImpact: This dynamic forces the enemy duo into a highly defensive posture. Every time the ADC steps up to farm, they risk a sudden Justice Punch leading into Colossal Smash and Winds of War. Yuumi is forced to burn massive mana on Zoomies to keep her partner alive, destroying their lane sustain and leaving them vulnerable to diving plays once you unlock Hero's Entrance.
why: Yuumi's attachment via You and Me! removes any frontline defense for her carry, giving you a clear lane to strike. Because she cannot block skillshots for her partner, your Justice Punch becomes an unblockable tool to initiate on the isolated ADC. Even when she unleashes Final Chapter to peel, your Shield of Durand provides the perfect defensive channel to absorb the waves, mitigating the threat before executing your burst.

summary: Jarvan IV's Cataclysm traps Darius in melee range, which actually benefits Darius by letting him easily stack Hemorrhage.
howToPlay: When he initiates with Cataclysm, do not panic and waste your Flash. Instead, use Crippling Strike immediately to slow him, keeping him in range. Position yourself near the edge of his arena to ensure the outer blade of Decimate strikes him for maximum damage and healing. Always hold Apprehend to pull him back if he tries to escape over his wall using Demacian Standard and Dragon Strike.
laneImpact: This interaction completely dictates river skirmishes and objective contests. Jarvan IV cannot safely contest Scuttle Crabs or initiate fights in the jungle, as his primary engagement tool becomes his own death trap. You hold immense pressure during counter-ganks; if he dives your laners, your arrival guarantees a turning point, forcing him to abandon his own jungle.
why: Jarvan IV relies on locking down targets with Cataclysm, but trapping you in his arena plays directly into your hands. Instead of securing a kill, he forces a close-quarters brawl where he cannot escape your basic attacks. This allows you to rapidly stack Hemorrhage. Once you reach maximum stacks inside his own wall, Noxian Might ensures you easily execute him with Noxian Guillotine.

summary: When Alistar engages with Headbutt, Galio can immediately charge Shield of Durand to taunt the follow-up attackers.
howToPlay: Maintain a diagonal positioning near your ADC, ensuring you are close enough to react but spread out enough to prevent Alistar from hitting you both with Pulverize. Never waste Shield of Durand proactively; keep it ready to interrupt the enemy follow-up the split second you see Alistar start his Headbutt. If he activates Unbreakable Will to cleanse your crowd control, immediately pivot your focus away from him. Use Justice Punch to knock up his carry instead, or prepare Hero's Entrance to counter his dive.
laneImpact: This interaction forces Alistar to play passively, stripping away his playmaking potential. Since he cannot safely initiate without risking his partner being locked down, you dictate the lane's pace. You can safely poke with Winds of War and help secure wave priority with Colossal Smash. Alistar is forced to trigger Triumphant Roar defensively, bleeding lane control and allowing your carry to farm with absolute safety under your protective wing.
why: Galio dominates this matchup because Alistar's linear engage pattern plays directly into your defensive zone. When Alistar uses Headbutt to close the gap, he separates himself from his follow-up. By immediately charging Shield of Durand, you can taunt the incoming enemy marksman before they can capitalize on Alistar's Pulverize. This completely neutralizes their offensive burst while leaving Alistar isolated and vulnerable to your Winds of War retaliation.

summary: Lux's Lucent Singularity provides long-range poke that outranges Janna's Zephyr, forcing Janna to play defensively and rely on Eye of the Storm.
howToPlay: Position yourself parallel to your minion wave, keeping Janna at the maximum edge of your Lucent Singularity. Never throw Light Binding blindly; instead, hold it for the exact moment she steps up to apply Eye of the Storm. If she attempts to escape your poke with Tailwind, use the slow from Lucent Singularity to lock her down, then unleash Final Spark to delete her before she can react with Monsoon.
laneImpact: By neutralizing Janna’s offensive presence, you easily control the wave’s momentum. She cannot match your push because charging Howling Gale is too slow and predictable. You can constantly shove her under tower, forcing her to choose between using Eye of the Storm to protect her AD carry from your poke or mitigation on the turret itself, generating an enormous gold lead through early tower plates.
why: You hold a distinct range advantage in this matchup. Your Lucent Singularity outranges Janna's Zephyr by a wide margin, completely preventing her from walking up to poke or apply her passive slow. Whenever she steps forward to trade, she is forced to eat your AoE damage, which quickly drains her resources as she must constantly shield herself or her carry with Eye of the Storm just to survive.

summary: Orianna can safely poke Brand from outside his range using Command: Attack and shield his return damage with Command: Protect.
howToPlay: To survive, never stand inside your own minion wave; make her choose between poking you with Command: Attack or pushing the wave. If she steps too far forward to place her ball, wait for her to waste Command: Protect before attempting to land your Pillar of Flame and Sear combo. If she misses her skillshots, look to spread Blaze through the minions to force her to retreat, saving your Pyroclasm for when she commits her Command: Shockwave.
laneImpact: This constant outranging forces you to yield wave priority. You will find yourself constantly farming under tower, struggling to land Conflagration to spread your passive through the wave without getting caught by Command: Dissonance. Your health bar will slowly dwindle, forcing early recalls and leaving you unable to assist your jungler, while Orianna remains safe and healthy behind her protective ball.
why: Orianna completely dictates this lane by keeping her Ball positioned ahead of your range. She repeatedly harasses you with Command: Attack from a distance where your Pillar of Flame cannot reach her. Even if you step forward to trade, she immediately negates your retaliation with Command: Protect, using the shield to absorb your Blaze passive burn while you take free damage from her zone.

summary: While Ziggs can poke from afar with Bouncing Bomb (Q), Galio can easily clear waves with Winds of War (Q) and use Hero's Entrance (R) to impact the map.
howToPlay: Position yourself away from your minion wave to force Ziggs to choose between hitting you or clearing with Bouncing Bomb. If he misses, immediately use Winds of War on the wave. When your side lanes clash, step back into the fog of war. The moment an ally is engaged, trigger Hero's Entrance to dive into the fight. If Ziggs tries to stop your recall with Mega Inferno Bomb, use Shield of Durand to shrug off the damage.
laneImpact: This matchup quickly turns into a battle of wave clearance. While Ziggs hopes to push you in to execute your tower with Satchel Charge, your fast clear prevents him from ever getting that chip damage. You dictate the recall and roam timings. By shoving the wave instantly, you create huge windows to disappear into the fog of war, forcing Ziggs to play defensively under his own tower.
why: Ziggs relies on keeping you at bay by bouncing his Bouncing Bomb and using Short Fuse to chip your health. However, his poke cannot pin you down. With Winds of War, you can safely obliterate minions from a distance, neutralizing his wave clear. Once you unlock Hero's Entrance, you bypass his long-range defense entirely, converting your lane priority into instant map pressure that his immobile kit cannot match.

summary: Caitlyn must abuse her 150-range advantage to constantly poke Vayne with basic attacks and Headshots whenever Vayne steps up to last-hit.
howToPlay: Prioritize survival over gold by holding Tumble strictly to dodge Piltover Peacemaker rather than using it aggressively to farm. Do not try to force three-hit trades with Silver Bolts. Instead, focus on preserving your health. If she wastes 90 Caliber Net, that is your cue to activate Final Hour and use the bonus speed from Night Hunter to close the gap. Look for a quick Condemn against the lane walls to lock her down.
laneImpact: You will find yourself pushed under your turret constantly, losing control of the wave. Caitlyn will place Yordle Snap Trap around your tower to restrict your movement and zone you from CS. This continuous pressure slowly chips away at your health bar, leaving you vulnerable to a lethal Ace in the Hole dive. Consequently, you must accept a gold deficit early on.
why: Caitlyn's massive 150-range advantage allows her to abuse Headshot and basic attacks every time you step forward to trigger Silver Bolts or secure a minion. If you attempt to close the distance with Tumble, she can easily disengage using 90 Caliber Net while landing a guaranteed critical headshot, ensuring you can never trade back effectively. Her Piltover Peacemaker also punishes you behind the wave.

summary: Yasuo's Wind Wall can completely delete Ornn's Call of the Forge God ram, requiring Ornn to bait out the wall before casting his ultimate.
howToPlay: To win this lane, you must never launch Call of the Forge God when Yasuo has Wind Wall available. Instead, poke his Way of the Wanderer shield down with Volcanic Rupture from a safe distance. Force him to use his wind barrier by threatening a Searing Charge engage near a pillar. If he panics and deploys it, you have a massive twenty-second window to safely unleash your ultimate. Hold Bellows Breath specifically to block the knock-up from his third Steel Tempest, preventing his Last Breath follow-up.
laneImpact: During the laning phase, Yasuo will constantly push the wave using Steel Tempest while looking for short trades. Ornn can neutralise Yasuo's aggressive Sweeping Blade dashes by casting Bellows Breath to apply Brittle and gain unstoppable status against the tornado from Steel Tempest. However, if Ornn wastes Call of the Forge God into an active Wind Wall, he loses all kill pressure, allowing Yasuo to safely scale, farm, and threaten Last Breath setups.
why: This even matchup hinges entirely on how Yasuo's Wind Wall interacts with Ornn's Call of the Forge God. While Ornn wants to initiate teamfights or trades with his massive ram, a reactive Yasuo can completely dissolve the projectile with a single defensive cast. Yasuo relies on Sweeping Blade to dance around Volcanic Rupture pillars, meaning Ornn cannot easily land Searing Charge knock-ups without first stripping away Yasuo's high mobility and his Way of the Wanderer shield.

summary: When Leona lands Zenith Blade, Alistar can immediately Headbutt her away from his ADC before she can apply Shield of Daybreak.
howToPlay: To survive, you must play defensively and bait Alistar into wasting his abilities. Never use Zenith Blade unless you see him use Headbutt on your ADC or to secure a minion. If he mispositions and wastes this cooldown, you have a brief window to engage. Alternatively, wait for your ultimate, Solar Flare, to initiate from a distance, or focus your crowd control on Alistar himself if he attempts to dive your carry under your tower.
laneImpact: Because your standard engage is neutralized, you lose all lane pressure. You cannot safely contest the minion waves, and trying to force trades results in Alistar using Pulverize to counter-engage on your ADC. This forces you to play passively near your turret. You will bleed gold, lose priority for river vision, and cannot easily assist in early skirmishes because Alistar dictates the pace.
why: Alistar completely shuts down your main initiation tool. Every time you cast Zenith Blade to dive onto the enemy marksman, Alistar can react instantly with Headbutt. He will knock you far away before you can follow up with Shield of Daybreak, isolating you from your target. This makes your Sunlight passive useless, as your ally cannot follow up, leaving you exposed and wasting your Eclipse defensive stats.

summary: Vladimir can use Sanguine Pool (W) to dodge Dark Binding (Q) or escape Soul Shackles (R), turning the lane into a passive farm matchup.
howToPlay: To win this war of attrition, stop throwing Dark Binding blindly. Instead, drop Tormented Shadow directly on the caster minions to force Vladimir to use his abilities on the wave rather than trading. Save Black Shield exclusively to absorb his empowered Transfusion or the burst from Hemoplague. If he panics and wastes Sanguine Pool defensively, only then should you look to lock him down with Soul Shackles before his pool cooldown recovers.
laneImpact: Because active trading is mostly ineffective, the lane shifts entirely to relentless wave pressure. You can easily shove Vladimir under his turret using Tormented Shadow, forcing him to spend his health pool on Tides of Blood to clear. However, you cannot easily punish his recalls or dive him. This neutralizes the mid lane, preventing both of you from roaming effectively, as leaving the wave unattended means losing valuable gold to passive farming.
why: This matchup revolves around an unbreakable stalemate. Whenever you attempt to lock Vladimir down with Dark Binding or set up a stun with Soul Shackles, he can simply sink into Sanguine Pool to evade the crowd control entirely. Because his Transfusion heals back any minor poke you land, and your Soul Siphon keeps you healthy, neither of you can easily force a kill, resulting in a pure battle of attrition.

summary: Garen's Perseverance easily out-regenerates Malphite's Seismic Shard poke, while Decisive Strike cleanses the slow.
howToPlay: Never activate Decisive Strike before his projectile hits you; wait for Seismic Shard to impact, then cleanse the slow to run him down. Spin immediately with Judgment to shred his Granite Shield and armor. If he fights back, trigger Courage to block the burst from Ground Slam. Keep pushing waves to deny him roam opportunities with Unstoppable Force, and execute him with Demacian Justice once his health bars dwindle under tower.
laneImpact: This resource disparity gives you complete authority over the minion waves. Since Malphite cannot realistically poke you down, you can comfortably slow-push waves into his turret. This forces him to burn his mana on Ground Slam and Thunderclap to secure last hits under tower. He will constantly face bad recall timings, giving you free opportunities to chip his plates or invade the jungle.
why: Garen commands this matchup because Malphite's signature lane-harass is entirely neutralized. When Malphite hurls Seismic Shard to chip away at your health and run, activating Decisive Strike instantly removes the movement speed steal. Furthermore, any minor damage Malphite manages to stick on you is quickly erased by Perseverance, allowing you to stay healthy while he drains his limited mana pool.

summary: Galio must lock down Sona with Shield of Durand before she can scale, but her Crescendo can stop his engage in its tracks.
howToPlay: You must force the issue before level five. Hide in the bushes to channel Shield of Durand out of her vision, then use Flash to unleash an instant taunt before she can react with Song of Celerity. If she already has Crescendo, never lead with Justice Punch, as she will easily interrupt the dash. Instead, wait for her to waste her ultimate or coordinate with your jungler to burst her down.
laneImpact: Passive laning plays directly into Sona's hands. If you fail to secure early kills, her Aria of Perseverance nullifies all poke from Winds of War and Colossal Smash. Once she gets Crescendo, she gains complete lane control, forcing you under tower. This pressure prevents you from finding roams, rendering Hero's Entrance useless as you are pinned down defending your ADC from her constant poke.
why: Sona naturally outscales you through the relentless healing of Aria of Perseverance and poke from Hymn of Valor. Your only window to prevent this scaling gap is locking her down early with Shield of Durand. However, once she unlocks Crescendo, she can instantly interrupt your Justice Punch mid-dash or stun you while you channel your taunt, completely neutralizing your engage and leaving you vulnerable to her Power Chord poke.

summary: Placing Flame Chompers in Tristana's flight path or directly on yourself can interrupt her Rocket Jump and deny her the reset.
howToPlay: To convert this favorable matchup, never initiate with Rocket Jump if Jinx still holds her traps. Instead, walk up to trade with Rapid Fire and Explosive Charge to force a reaction. If she drops Flame Chompers! defensively, step aside to avoid the root, wait for them to expire, and then jump forward. If you get caught mid-flight, immediately use Buster Shot to push Jinx away, preventing her from triggering Get Excited! off your mistake.
laneImpact: During the laning phase, this interaction dictates when you can safely play for the kill. Jinx will try to poke you down with the rocket form of Switcheroo! and slow you with Zap!. However, because her defensive traps have a massive cooldown, the moment Jinx wastes Flame Chompers! to zone you or miss-positions them, she is completely defenseless against your all-in, forcing her to play passively under her tower.
why: Tristana dominates Jinx through pure explosive power, but the entire matchup hinges on Jinx's ability to disrupt your engage. While your Explosive Charge paired with Rapid Fire easily out-bursts her minigun or rockets, Jinx can completely shut down your aggression by throwing Flame Chompers! directly in your flight path. This interrupts Rocket Jump mid-air, trapping you in place and leaving you unable to secure the crucial jump reset.

summary: Wukong can bait Kayn's Reaping Slash with Warrior Trickster, but Rhaast's knockup can disrupt Wukong's Cyclone.
howToPlay: To win this duel, never initiate with Cyclone if Kayn has Rhaast form active and Blade's Reach is off cooldown. Instead, engage with Nimbus Strike, then immediately deploy Warrior Trickster to absorb his initial Reaping Slash. Wait for his knockup animation to miss your clone before unleashing your ultimate. If he holds his crowd control, delay your rotation and rely on the armor from Stone Skin to win the basic attack trade.
laneImpact: Because both of you clear the jungle at a similar pace, early skirmishes around the Rift Scuttler or deep invades dictate the tempo. If you successfully trick Kayn with your clone, you force his Shadow Step defensively, stripping away his map pressure. Conversely, if he lands his knockup on you during a crucial river fight, he secures objective control and accelerates his transformation passive.
why: This jungle matchup is a pure battle of wits centered around deception and timing. Your primary weapon is Warrior Trickster, which perfectly baits Kayn's Reaping Slash, leaving him empty-handed in close quarters. However, once Kayn transforms into Rhaast, the dynamic shifts; his knockup from Blade's Reach can cancel your Cyclone mid-spin, completely neutralizing your primary teamfight tool if you commit too early.

summary: Syndra can use Scatter the Weak (E) to push Aurora away when she attempts to engage with Across the Veil (W).
howToPlay: To master this lane, you must never cast Scatter the Weak proactively unless Aurora's Across the Veil is on cooldown. Stand slightly behind your caster minions, using Dark Sphere and Force of Will to secure last hits and chip her health down. If she leaps forward, instantly react with Scatter the Weak to push her back, then follow up with a quick Dark Sphere. If she traps you inside Between Worlds, walk toward the center to avoid the borders and prepare your Unleashed Power to burst her first.
laneImpact: During the laning phase, wave control becomes a tense chess match. Aurora will try to use Twofold Hex to push and poke simultaneously, forcing Syndra to choose between farming with Dark Sphere or matching the push. If Syndra wastes Scatter the Weak, Aurora immediately gains the freedom to zone her or search for a kill with Between Worlds. Conversely, if Syndra holds her knockback, Aurora is forced to play passively, neutralizing the lane's kill pressure.
why: This matchup revolves around a high-stakes duel of bursts where whoever mismanages their defensive tool gets obliterated. Aurora relies on Across the Veil to close the distance and trigger Spirit Abjuration, but Syndra can completely shut down this aggression by launching a well-timed Scatter the Weak. Because both champions possess lethal ultimate abilities in Unleashed Power and Between Worlds, the lane remains perfectly balanced on who respects the other's threat range.

summary: Poppy's Steadfast Presence blocks Nidalee's W: Pounce, grounding her and preventing both her escape and her cougar form burst.
howToPlay: Never initiate a fight with Steadfast Presence; hold this ability specifically to react to her Pounce animation. Sidestep her Javelin Toss first to deny her the hunted mark, then walk directly into her melee range. Once she panics and attempts to leap away, trigger your shield to ground her, then immediately use Heroic Charge to smash her into the nearest wall, finishing her off with a maximum-health Hammer Shock.
laneImpact: This interaction dictates the flow of early skirmishes and river contests. Nidalee cannot safely invade your camps or contest the Scuttle Crab, as any aggressive Pounce leaves her locked down and vulnerable to a quick Hammer Shock. You dictate the pace of objective fights because she cannot dive your backline or secure smite range without risking a shutdown that costs her team map-wide pressure.
why: Poppy completely shuts down Nidalee's jungle pressure because Steadfast Presence acts as an impenetrable barrier against Pounce. When Nidalee tries to leap in cougar form to execute you or escape after a Javelin Toss, activating your Steadfast Presence stops her mid-air, grounds her, and strips away her entire burst combo. Without her hyper-mobility, she becomes an incredibly fragile target trapped in melee range of your hammer.

howToPlay: Positioning: don’t chase into poison. Play range, punish when he steps up, and reset the moment he looks for flip. Key timing: his proxy/roam windows. When he disappears behind tower, choose quickly: take plates fast or push and reset — don’t hesitate. Singed abuses unclear timings. Decision-making: ward deeper and play map reads. With vision, punish tower. Without vision, secure your reset instead of greeding — keep the structural advantage without giving a free kill.
laneImpact: In lane you can hold the wave and punish his approaches. If he wants to take the wave, he must expose himself to autos. At level 5 he gains real catch potential, but you can respond with discipline. The mistake is chasing him through poison or being caught without jump. Midgame, when Singed proxies/roams, you must decide fast: punish tower or follow. Tristana top is great at punishing tower, so you can often take winning trades.
why: Singed is favorable because your kit punishes his weird approaches. He wants to flip you into poison and force messy fights. Tristana can auto from range and has jump to reset the engage if you react in time. You can also convert tower value when Singed proxies: while he runs behind, you take real value (plates) as long as you don’t get trapped by roams/ganks. It’s still macro-demanding, but structurally you have natural tools to avoid being dragged into his plan.

summary: Avoid using Apprehend until Jayce commits to hammer form, as he can easily knock you away with Thundering Blow.
howToPlay: To survive, you must discipline yourself to never cast Apprehend first. Instead, position defensively and invite Jayce to initiate. When he gets greedy and leaps onto you with the hammer version of To the Skies!, wait out his Thundering Blow knockback. The moment you are pushed away, instantly use Apprehend to pull him back. Follow up with Crippling Strike to slow him, guarantee the outer edge of Decimate, and stack Hemorrhage for an unexpected Noxian Guillotine execute.
laneImpact: This constant threat of being disengaged forces you to play defensively near your turret. Jayce will control the minion waves, using Lightning Field to push while poking you with accelerated projectiles. If you waste Apprehend and get knocked back, you cannot stack Hemorrhage, costing you massive health. You will find yourself trapped under tower, losing gold and unable to help your jungler.
why: Jayce dominates this lane by abusing his range advantage with Transform Mercury Cannon to poke you down. Your only tool to force a trade is Apprehend, but if you throw it out blindly, Jayce will simply swap to hammer form and use Thundering Blow to swat you away. This interaction completely neutralizes your engage, leaving you slow and vulnerable to his ranged harass.

summary: Time Repudiation to block Garen's Decisive Strike silence, absorbing the damage and allowing you to retaliate with Cunning Sweep.
howToPlay: To win this, never initiate trades with a direct Decisive Strike. Instead, run towards her to trigger her defensive instinct, then immediately spin with Judgment first. Once she panics and activates Repudiation, wait out the brief shield duration before striking her with your empowered silence. If she holds her shield, use Courage to mitigate her Cunning Sweep damage, and execute her with Demacian Justice only after her Repudiation is down.
laneImpact: The lane's wave control fluctuates entirely around these short skirmishes. When Repudiation is on cooldown, Ambessa must play defensively, allowing you to push the minion wave safely with Judgment. However, if she successfully parries your Decisive Strike, she gains complete lane priority, forcing you to use Courage defensively and giving her the perfect window to crash the wave and secure a clean recall.
why: This matchup is a pure duel of reaction times centered on your silence. Ambessa relies on her Repudiation shield to absorb the impact of your Decisive Strike and negate its silence. If she succeeds, she can easily counter-attack with Cunning Sweep and her highly mobile passive. However, if you force her to waste her shield, your Judgment will shred her while she is silenced and unable to dash away.

summary: Viktor can zone Galio with Gravity Field (W) when Galio tries to engage, but Galio can match Viktor's waveclear using Winds of War (Q).
howToPlay: To succeed, never initiate with Justice Punch unless Viktor has already wasted Gravity Field. Instead, stand parallel to the wave, using Winds of War and Colossal Smash to quickly clear the caster minions. If Viktor overextends to land Siphon Power, step back to let his shield decay, then look for a short trade. When local pressure stalls, rely on Hero's Entrance to impact side lanes rather than forcing a dry solo kill.
laneImpact: Because direct engages are highly risky, the mid lane becomes a pure tug-of-war of wave management. Viktor will constantly seek to poke you down with Hextech Ray and trade safely using Siphon Power's shield.
