When your engage fails, immediately activate Eclipse and retreat toward your tower to absorb the counter-attack.
laneImpact: This matchup forces you into a passive defensive posture. Because Milio can deny your dash, attempting to force trades often leaves you stranded in the minion wave with your Eclipse wasted. His lane partner will easily poke you down using the extra range from Cozy Campfire and burn damage from Fired Up!, slowly chipping away your health and forcing early recalls that cost your team dragon priority.
why: Milio holds all the tools to shut down your aggression. Whenever you launch forward with Zenith Blade, a reactive Milio can knock you back mid-flight using Ultra Mega Fire Kick, preventing you from applying Shield of Daybreak. Even if you land a perfect Solar Flare from afar, his Breath of Life instantly cleanses the stun and heals his marksman, completely neutralizing your primary initiation tools.

summary: Akali can use Shuriken Flip to mark Veigar before he casts Event Horizon, allowing her to dash to him once the cage expires.
howToPlay: To execute this flawlessly, bait his cage by walking aggressively forward, then instantly throw Shuriken Flip when he casts Event Horizon. Do not panic if you are trapped inside; drop Twilight Shroud to remain untargetable, avoiding Dark Matter. The absolute rule is to hold your second Shuriken Flip cast until the boundary disappears. If you misstime the mark, back off, wait for your energy to regenerate, and strike only when his defensive cooldown is down.
laneImpact: This interaction forces Veigar into a highly defensive posture, rendering him unable to safely stack Phenomenal Evil Power with Baleful Strike. He must choose between using Event Horizon to secure minions or saving it to deter your dives. Consequently, you easily dictate the wave's position. This pressure allows you to crash massive waves and freely search for flank angles using Perfect Execution to snowball the match.
why: Your superior mobility completely neutralizes Veigar's self-peel. While Event Horizon is his only reliable tool to keep you at bay, your Shuriken Flip provides the perfect counter. If you land the shuriken on him before he raises his defensive cage, you mark him safely. You can then wait out the stun barrier's duration inside your Twilight Shroud and reactivate the dash to strike him the instant his cage dissolves.

summary: Mordekaiser's Realm of Death steals a percentage of Cho'Gath's massive health pool, making Mordekaiser incredibly tanky inside the death realm.
howToPlay: Shift your early purchases heavily toward magic resistance rather than rushed health items to minimize the value Mordekaiser steals. During trades, save Feral Scream to silence him when he attempts to chain Death's Grasp into Obliterate. If you get dragged into Realm of Death, do not try to fight his inflated stats; instead, use Rupture to delay his advance and walk away until his ultimate expires, reserving Feast only for guaranteed execution thresholds.
laneImpact: You lose the ability to contest the wave actively once Mordekaiser reaches level five. If you walk up to trade, his Death's Grasp pulls you into Darkness Rise territory, forcing long, losing skirmishes. You are relegated to farming safely from a distance with Rupture, as pushing the lane makes you an easy target for Realm of Death, trapping you far from the safety of your turret.
why: This matchup is defined by how Mordekaiser exploits your scaling. The massive health pool you accumulate through Feast becomes your biggest liability when he triggers Realm of Death. By stealing a percentage of your maximum stats, Mordekaiser gains an immense amount of tankiness inside his arena, turning your own defensive growth into his ultimate weapon and rendering your raw health advantage completely counterproductive.

summary: Ryze can instantly interrupt your Heroic Swing with a point-and-click Rune Prison, leaving you stranded in close range.
howToPlay: To survive and win trades, you must absolutely hold Heroic Swing until Ryze wastes Rune Prison. Focus on short trades using Avengerang to pierce through minions, followed by your Dirty Fighting double-tap to trigger your movement speed boost and shield. If Ryze uses his root to secure a cannon minion or to escape, that is your immediate green light to swing in. Otherwise, play safely near your tower, using Going Rogue to roam if he leaves lane.
laneImpact: Because your main escape and engagement tool is neutralized, you lose the freedom to play aggressively. Trying to clear waves or trade using Heroic Swing often results in getting locked down under Ryze's tower or caught in the river. This forces you to rely solely on Avengerang for wave clear. Consequently, Ryze dictates the lane's tempo, shoving you in and using Realm Warp to impact other lanes while you are stuck farming.
why: This matchup is dictated by how Ryze's point-and-click Rune Prison completely shuts down your Heroic Swing. The moment you attempt to swing around a mid lane wall, Ryze can instantly root you mid-air without needing to aim. This cancels your primary mobility tool, leaving you stranded in close range where his Spell Flux and Overload combo can easily tear through your health bar before you can trigger your Dirty Fighting shield.

summary: Morgana's Black Shield completely negates Braum's Concussive Blows stun, making it difficult for him to peel or lock down targets.
howToPlay: To survive, never use Winter's Bite proactively unless Morgana's Black Shield is on its long cooldown. Instead, save Stand Behind Me to quickly leap to your ADC when they are targeted by Dark Binding, immediately raising Unbreakable to intercept the projectile. If she commits with Soul Shackles, use Glacial Fissure to knock her up and delay the tether pop, giving your partner enough time to break the range and escape the stun.
laneImpact: During the laning phase, Morgana will constantly zone your ADC with Tormented Shadow, chipping away at your health while you try to block her Dark Binding with Unbreakable. Because your stun threat is neutralized by Black Shield, your ADC must play defensively. You cannot easily contest the wave, forcing you under tower where her Soul Shackles can set up devastating dives or easy lane resets.
why: This matchup is heavily dictated by how Morgana uses her Black Shield to completely shut down your passive, Concussive Blows. Whenever you try to stack your stun via Winter's Bite or basic attacks, she can instantly shield her ADC, nullifying your crowd control. This leaves you unable to peel effectively, while her Dark Binding can easily catch you out if you misposition to apply pressure.

summary: Using Indestructible to absorb the true damage from Sett's Haymaker allows Mordekaiser to win extended trades after his passive activates.
howToPlay: To secure victory, never initiate trades with Death's Grasp unless Sett's Facebreaker is down. Bait his Knuckle Down, land isolated Obliterate strikes, and stack your passive. When Sett prepares his Haymaker, do not panic-dodge sideways if you cannot escape the central true damage zone; instead, activate Indestructible at that exact micro-second to neutralize the blast. If you misstime this and take full damage, immediately cast Realm of Death to steal his stats and survive the remaining duel.
laneImpact: Because both of you possess immense sustain through Pit Grit and Indestructible, neither can easily force the other out of lane early. Wave states remain highly contested; Sett will try to pull you into his minions with Facebreaker to stun you. Missing Obliterate or wasting Death's Grasp leaves you vulnerable to a swift Knuckle Down engage, turning the lane into a tense dance where trading health bars only ends when one player mismanages their defensive cooldowns.
why: This matchup is a brutal battle of attrition dictated by how you manage your shield timings against his burst. Sett relies on Knuckle Down and Facebreaker to force short, explosive trades that build up his grit. If he unleashes Haymaker, the true damage in the center can turn the tide. However, if you trigger Darkness Rise and hold Indestructible to perfectly absorb that true damage blast, your superior sustained magic damage wins out.

summary: Varus can use Hail of Arrows to slow Zyra and clear her Rampant Growth plants simultaneously from a safe distance.
howToPlay: Position yourself just outside the range of her Grasping Roots and watch her seed placements. Never waste Hail of Arrows on empty space; hold it specifically for the moment she activates Rampant Growth. Once her plants are cleared and she is slowed by the rain, immediately prime Blighted Quiver and release a fully charged Piercing Arrow to chunk her. If she attempts to retaliate with Stranglethorns, counter immediately with Chain of Corruption to lock her down and finish her.
laneImpact: This interaction completely shifts wave control in your favor. Zyra cannot establish her garden to push the wave or zone you off minions. Every time she tries to summon plants with Rampant Growth, your Hail of Arrows erases them while chipping her health. This constant safety allows you to maintain high pressure, secure easy recalls, and lock her under turret where she cannot safely dodge Piercing Arrow.
why: Varus dominates this lane by completely neutralizing Zyra's zone control. Because your attack range and spell reach exceed her threat zone, you can stay out of range of Grasping Roots. The crucial mechanical advantage lies in Hail of Arrows: this single ability instantly clears her Rampant Growth plants from afar while slowing Zyra herself, stripping away her primary source of poke and leaving her highly vulnerable to your follow-up.

summary: Bard can use Cosmic Binding to stun Thresh and his ally when they attempt to click Dark Passage to escape or engage.
howToPlay: Position yourself constantly behind minions to block Death Sentence, and always keep one Caretaker’s Shrine fully charged behind your ADC. Never waste Cosmic Binding proactively; hold it specifically for the moment Thresh throws Dark Passage or tries to engage. If he manages to trap you with The Box, cast Tempered Fate directly on his ADC to stall their damage, then use Magical Journey through the nearest wall to slip away safely.
laneImpact: Because Thresh can fish for hooks, you cannot blindly wander to collect chimes from Traveler’s Call without sacrificing lane pressure. If you are pulled, Flay will disrupt your escape, leaving you vulnerable under your own turret. This threat forces you to play defensively near your Caretaker’s Shrine, meaning you will often lose priority and have to concede early brush control to avoid deadly blind hooks.
why: Thresh holds the lane's threat because one hit from Death Sentence forces you or your carry into The Box. However, Thresh's reliance on Dark Passage to taxi his jungler or save his ADC is his biggest vulnerability. When an ally clicks the lantern, they path directly to Thresh. Lining up Cosmic Binding right as they collide creates an instant, inescapable double stun, turning his primary escape into a death trap.

summary: Vayne's short range forces her to step up for last hits, making her highly vulnerable to Double Up bounces and Make It Rain slow zones.
howToPlay: Position yourself constantly behind your low-health minions to bait her forward. Always hold Double Up until she commits to her last-hit animation, ensuring she cannot reactively dodge with Tumble. If she activates Final Hour to engage, immediately drop Make It Rain on your own feet to slow her advance and disrupt Night Hunter, then retreat using your Strut passive speed. Only channel Bullet Time once she has wasted Condemn, preventing her from interrupting your ultimate.
laneImpact: By constantly threatening these bounces, you dictate the minion waves. Vayne is forced to use Tumble defensively just to dodge your poke, stripping away her early threat. You will easily build a massive minion lead, pushing her under her tower where she struggles to farm. This constant health attrition prevents her from seeking trades, giving you free recalls and uncontested tower plating while she is trapped under turret.
why: Vayne's notoriously short basic attack range forces her to walk directly into your threat zone to secure minion gold. This predictable movement path allows you to easily line up Double Up bounces off dying minions directly onto her. Since she lacks any long-range tools to retaliate, dropping Make It Rain whenever she steps up guarantees she either absorbs heavy magic damage and slow, or misses crucial gold.

summary: Poppy's Steadfast Presence blocks both Viego's Spectral Maw dash and his Heartbreaker ultimate, grounding him and leaving him vulnerable.
howToPlay: To survive, you must play with extreme patience and track her defensive cooldowns meticulously. Never lead an engagement with Spectral Maw. Instead, use Harrowed Path's camouflage to hover near skirmishes, baiting Poppy into activating Steadfast Presence prematurely. Once her defensive aura fades, you have a brief window to strike. If she holds her skill, focus your Blade of the Ruined King on her front-line allies to melt them safely without committing your dashes.
laneImpact: In the jungle, this dynamic severely limits your skirmishing freedom. You cannot contest Scuttle Crabs or secure early neutral objectives safely if Poppy is nearby, as she can interrupt your escape routes through walls. Ganking lanes becomes highly risky because she can counter-gank and lock you down mid-dash, preventing you from triggering Sovereign's Domination and snowballing the map.
why: Poppy completely disables your offensive threat because her Steadfast Presence acts as an impassable barrier for your primary gap-closers. If you attempt to initiate with the dash from Spectral Maw or try to execute a target using Heartbreaker, her active aura will instantly ground and stun you. This reaction shuts down your assassination potential and leaves you completely exposed to her team's follow-up.

summary: Zed can use Death Mark to dodge Varus's Chain of Corruption, landing behind him for an easy burst kill.
howToPlay: To survive, you must absolutely hold your Chain of Corruption. Never throw it proactively. When Zed initiates with Death Mark, wait for him to reappear behind you, then immediately fire Chain of Corruption directly behind your character model to lock him down under your turret or interrupt his burst. If his Living Shadow is on cooldown, use that brief window to safely punish him with Piercing Arrow and apply Blighted Quiver stacks, but retreat the moment his shadow clone is available again.
laneImpact: While you can bully Zed early using Piercing Arrow and Blighted Quiver, the dynamic flips entirely once he unlocks Death Mark. You are forced to freeze the wave near your turret, as stepping past the midpoint makes you an easy target. Because you must respect his Living Shadow threat range, you will lose mid priority, allowing Zed to freely roam to side lanes while you are stuck safely clearing waves.
why: This matchup is dictated by how Zed's Death Mark interacts with your Chain of Corruption. As an immobile marksman, your only reliable self-peel is your ultimate. However, Zed can easily activate Death Mark to become untargetable, completely dodging your Chain of Corruption while gap-closing to land behind you. Without this crowd control to keep him at bay, his subsequent Razor Shuriken and Shadow Slash combo will instantly delete your health bar.

summary: If Fizz uses Playful to dodge Syndra's Scatter the Weak, she is left with no self-peel against his burst.
howToPlay: To survive, you must absolutely hoard Scatter the Weak like a lifeline, never using it proactively unless Fizz has already burnt Playful. Position yourself strictly near your own tower, using long-range Dark Sphere casts to harvest Transcendent shards safely. If he catches you with Chum the Waters while your stun is down, immediately retreat under your turret and prepare to use Unleashed Power.
laneImpact: You are forced into a defensive posture, unable to aggressively use Dark Sphere or Force of Will to harass him near his tower. If the wave pushes too far toward him, Fizz can easily chase you down the long lane using Chum the Waters to slow and knock you up. Missing your stun means giving up all mid priority.
why: The core of this matchup revolves around Fizz using Playful to bypass your primary defensive tool. If you launch Scatter the Weak to push him away or stun him, and he hops on his trident to dodge it, you lose your only reliable self-peel. Without that knockback, Fizz can easily close the distance with Urchin Strike and deploy his full burst.

summary: Rammus's Defensive Ball Curl and Frenzying Taunt punish Kha'Zix heavily for attempting to duel him, forcing Kha'Zix to focus on squishier targets instead.
howToPlay: To maximize this advantage, prioritize target selection over mindless chasing. Never waste your Frenzying Taunt on beefy targets; instead, shadow your vulnerable allies. When Kha'Zix uses Leap or emerges from Void Assault to strike them, immediately activate Defensive Ball Curl and taunt him. By positioning yourself as a direct counter-engage tool, you shut down his only win condition and force him into a suicidal engage.
laneImpact: This matchup dynamic completely strips Kha'Zix of his early jungle agency. Unable to contest you in the river or safely counter-jungle, he must abandon direct skirmishes and hunt your squishier lanes instead. This predictable behavior allows you to secure neutral objectives with ease while tracking his desperate movements, knowing he cannot afford to face you when contesting the river crabs.
why: Kha'Zix relies entirely on physical burst, making him exceptionally weak against Rammus's heavy armor stacking. When he attempts to fight, activating Defensive Ball Curl and locking him in place with Frenzying Taunt completely reverses the duel. Instead of securing a quick assassination, he is forced to shred his own health pool against your spikes, making any direct confrontation in the jungle a guaranteed disaster for him.

summary: Aria of Perseverance easily nullifies Tormented Shadow poke, allowing Sona to safely scale into her dominant late game.
howToPlay: To survive, stop using your pool for random damage and instead freeze the minions near your turret. Force Sona to overextend if she wants to poke. You must hold Dark Binding as a deterrent; never throw it unless her Song of Celerity is down and she is mispositioned. If she tries to initiate with Crescendo, react instantly with Black Shield on your carry to block the stun, then counter-engage using Soul Shackles to turn her scaling advantage against her.
laneImpact: You cannot win an attrition war, meaning mindless pushing only helps Sona farm safely under tower. If you waste mana on Tormented Shadow to clear waves, Sona will use Hymn of Valor and her Power Chord to punish you while you lack pressure. This lack of threat forces you into awkward recall timings and concedes priority, letting her team secure early drakes while you are stuck protecting your turret from her slow, relentless push.
why: Sona's lane sustain completely shuts down your main trading pattern. Every time you drop Tormented Shadow to wear down her or her marksman, she immediately counters the damage with Aria of Perseverance. Because Soul Siphon only heals you when you inflict damage, her constant shielding denies your passive healing. This effortless negation allows Sona to safely accumulate gold and experience, reaching her powerhouse late-game scaling without ever facing real pressure.

summary: Miss Fortune is highly vulnerable to Heroic Swing all-ins when she channels Bullet Time, as she cannot move to dodge his damage.
howToPlay: Always stand diagonally to your dying minions to completely deny Miss Fortune's Double Up bounce damage. Keep Heroic Swing off cooldown specifically for her ultimate; the moment she channels Bullet Time, immediately grapple behind her or to her side to break her channel with raw burst. If she attempts to escape using Strut, use Going Rogue to gain the movement speed needed to catch up and clean up the kill with Comeuppance.
laneImpact: Miss Fortune will try to pressure you under tower using waveclear from Double Up. However, because she lacks escape tools, she must play with extreme caution once she reaches level five. She cannot freely channel Bullet Time in the open without risking an immediate Heroic Swing counter-engage. This fear grants you total control over the lane's physical space, allowing you to zone her off farm.
why: Akshan naturally dictates this matchup because Miss Fortune’s ultimate, Bullet Time, forces her to stand completely still. This immobility turns her into the perfect target for Heroic Swing, allowing you to swing around her cone of fire and unleash high-velocity damage. Furthermore, the shield from Dirty Fighting absorbs her Love Tap poke, ensuring you win short trades before committing to a full, vertical flank.

summary: Braum can intercept Thresh's Death Sentence with Stand Behind Me and Unbreakable, protecting his ADC at the cost of taking the hook himself.
howToPlay: Always stand slightly behind or parallel to your ally to maintain the correct angle for Stand Behind Me. Never waste Unbreakable to block simple auto-attacks; hold it exclusively for when Thresh winds up Death Sentence. If you get hooked, immediately look to hit him with Winter's Bite and stack Concussive Blows to turn his engage into a stun. Use Glacial Fissure to disrupt the path of any enemy trying to click his Dark Passage lantern.
laneImpact: Because you can shield your marksman, Thresh cannot easily force aggressive trades under your tower. However, if he lands Death Sentence directly on you while Unbreakable is down, his Flay and The Box can quickly lock you down for an easy kill. Wave pressure remains neutral as both of you threaten strong counter-engage, meaning neither support can blindly step up to contest brush control without risking a deadly trade.
why: This matchup is a pure test of reflexes and positioning around Thresh's hook. The entire lane dynamic revolves around whether you can reactively block Death Sentence. By combining Stand Behind Me to leap to your carry and immediately raising Unbreakable, you can absorb the hook and negate its follow-up. However, this means you intentionally take the crowd control, turning the lane into a constant battle of spacing and baiting.

summary: Kassadin's Null Sphere silences you, which instantly cancels your Breath of Light channel and leaves you defenseless.
howToPlay: Your goal is to survive and farm Stardust safely. Drop Singularity from a safe distance to clear minions without stepping into Null Sphere range. Never use Astral Flight aggressively; save it solely as an escape tool when he initiates with Riftwalk. If he freezes the wave near his tower, do not walk up to break it; instead, wait for the wave to crash or coordinate with your jungler to reset it.
laneImpact: You cannot trade back effectively, forcing you to play a purely defensive laning phase. Attempting to freeze or contest the wave with Breath of Light results in getting silenced and heavily chunked by his Nether Blade and Force Pulse combo. This loss of priority means you will be stuck under tower, bleeding gold, while Kassadin gains free roam timers to impact the map with his high mobility.
why: Kassadin completely shuts down your main damage source. Whenever you try to channel Breath of Light, he can immediately throw Null Sphere. The silence instantly interrupts your breath, leaving you completely vulnerable with no back-up damage. Furthermore, his Void Stone magic shield absorbs your poke, and once he gets Riftwalk, he can easily close the distance to burst you down while you are silenced.

summary: Vladimir can use Sanguine Pool to dodge Jax's Counter Strike stun, allowing him to safely sustain with Transfusion.
howToPlay: To secure this advantage, never use Sanguine Pool defensively for anything other than Jax's Counter Strike. When you see him charge his helicopter strike and jump with Leap Strike, pool immediately. As you emerge, immediately charge Tides of Blood and follow up with a empowered Transfusion to drain his health pool. If Jax plays too safely, zone him off the wave by holding your third Transfusion charge, forcing him to lose crucial experience.
laneImpact: Because Jax cannot reliably lock Vladimir down, the laning phase becomes an oppressive war of attrition that Vladimir naturally dominates. Jax is forced to play passively, bleeding gold and pressure, as any attempt to contest the wave leaves him open to constant ranged harassment. Vladimir can safely freeze the minion wave or slowly build massive slow pushes, forcing Jax to farm under tower while constantly being chipped away.
why: This matchup hinges on Vladimir's ability to completely nullify Jax's primary offensive tool, Counter Strike. When Jax initiates with Leap Strike, Vladimir can simply activate Sanguine Pool to avoid the incoming stun and damage. Once Jax's defensive spin ends without connecting, Vladimir is free to retaliate and replenish any lost health with Transfusion, turning what should be a dangerous engage into a heavily one-sided trade.

summary: Jarvan can throw Demacian Standard into brushes to gain vision, preventing Rengar from utilizing Unseen Predator leaps.
howToPlay: Never initiate a jungle camp clear with Demacian Standard if you suspect Rengar is lurking nearby, as you will lack the vision tool to scout adjacent bushes. Hold this ability specifically to reveal high-traffic brush zones before entering them. If he jumps you first, immediately activate Golden Aegis to mitigate his Savagery burst, then drop your flag-and-drag combo to knock him up or trap him inside Cataclysm once his Battle Roar cleanse is wasted.
laneImpact: During river skirmishes and objective contests, this interaction dictates who controls the pace. If you blindly facecheck bushes near the Scuttle Crab, Rengar will shred you. Conversely, scouting ahead with your flag forces Rengar to retreat or waste Thrill of the Hunt defensively. The jungle territory becomes highly volatile, where secure pathing relies heavily on your ability to deny Rengar his leap zones.
why: This jungle duel revolves entirely around bush dominance and reaction times. Rengar relies on Unseen Predator to leap from cover and burst you down with Savagery. However, Jarvan IV possesses the perfect tool to neutralize this threat: Demacian Standard grants immediate vision when tossed into unwarded bushes, stripping the hunter of his leap mechanics and leaving him exposed to a counter-engage.

summary: Lillia's Blooming Blows deals true damage on the outer edge, bypassing Rammus's Defensive Ball Curl armor buffs.
howToPlay: Avoid isolated skirmishes entirely and focus your pressure on lanes away from her pathing. When forced to engage, actively position inside the inner ring of Blooming Blows to dodge the true damage. Charge in with Powerball to close the distance instantly, then lock her down with Frenzying Taunt so she cannot build movement stacks. If she triggers Lilting Lullaby, save Soaring Slam to jump over a wall to safety before sleep kicks in.
laneImpact: Lillia dictates the jungle's pace by clearing camps significantly faster than you can. Contesting her in the river is suicidal, as she easily kites you. If she tags you with Swirlseed, she will initiate Lilting Lullaby to put you to sleep from afar, halting your Powerball charges before you can ever get close, forcing you to forfeit early Scuttle Crabs.
why: This matchup is an uphill battle because Lillia completely bypasses your defensive toolkit. Whenever you activate Defensive Ball Curl to boost your armor, she relies on the outer edge of Blooming Blows to shred you with true damage, rendering your primary defense useless. To make matters worse, her passive Dream-Laden Bough melts your high-HP pool with maximum health magic damage, neutralizing your tankiness.

summary: Xin Zhao's Three Talon Strike can knock Darius up, but Darius wins if he survives the initial burst and stacks Hemorrhage.
howToPlay: To win these skirmishes, you must play around his healing. When Darius winds up Decimate, use Audacious Charge immediately to dash inside the inner handle of his axe, minimizing his damage and denying his heal. If he manages to stack Hemorrhage to four, activate Crescent Guard to knock him back and disengage. Never commit to a duel if your Three Talon Strike is on cooldown, as you lack the crowd control to interrupt his stacking.
laneImpact: In the river and jungle corridors, every encounter is highly volatile. If you meet Darius near the Scuttle Crab, the skirmish is decided instantly by who initiates. Initiating with Wind Becomes Lightning to slow him allows you to control the engagement distance, but if Darius pulls you in with Apprehend first, you are forced into an extended fight where his Noxian Guillotine will execute you easily, giving up early map priority.
why: This jungle duel is a strict race against time governed by execution. Your upfront burst from Audacious Charge paired with the rapid knock-up of Three Talon Strike can shred Darius before he reacts. However, if he survives this initial onslaught, his passive Hemorrhage begins to stack up, turning the tide as his damage escalates. You must burst him down or disable him before he reaches five stacks and gains massive power.

summary: Garen must silence Kayle with Decisive Strike to execute her with Demacian Justice before she can cast Divine Judgment.
howToPlay: When initiating trades, wait for Kayle to launch Radiant Blast before activating Decisive Strike to instantly cleanse the slow. Once you close the gap, silence her first, then shred her armor with Judgment while mitigating any retaliation with Courage. If she plays defensively near her tower, freeze the minion wave on your side to force her to overextend, making her an easy target for your silence-into-execute burst combination.
laneImpact: Early on, Kayle relies on Starfire Spellblade to last hit and Radiant Blast to slow your approaches. However, Perseverance easily negates this poke. By constantly threatening to engage, you force Kayle to waste mana on Celestial Blessing to run away. This constant pressure pushes her under turret, letting you control the wave tempo and dive her the moment she falls into execution range.
why: Garen dictates this matchup because Kayle is weak before Divine Ascent fully matures. The entire dynamic centers on a race to level 5. Once both of you unlock your ultimates, your win condition is straightforward: you must catch her with Decisive Strike to apply the silence. This brief window prevents her from casting Divine Judgment, allowing you to instantly execute her with Demacian Justice before she can react.

summary: Lux can trade evenly with Viktor by using Prismatic Barrier to shield against his Siphon Power while landing Lucent Singularity from a safer distance than his Hextech Ray.
howToPlay: Stand behind your caster minions and monitor Viktor's positioning. When he approaches to last-hit or trigger Siphon Power, immediately throw Prismatic Barrier to negate his burst, then retaliate with Lucent Singularity. Never step forward to trigger Illumination with an auto-attack if his Gravity Field is available, as he will trap you and follow up with Arcane Storm. If you miss Light Binding, immediately retreat to avoid his full laser and ultimate combo.
laneImpact: The lane quickly becomes a war of attrition where neither mage can easily force the other out without a massive misplay. If you fail to shield his Siphon Power, Viktor's shield allows him to win the trade and push you under tower with Hextech Ray. Conversely, if you consistently hit Lucent Singularity from maximum range, you force him to play defensively, delaying his Glorious Evolution upgrades.
why: This matchup is a pure battle of ranges and shield timing. Viktor wants to trade with Siphon Power and poke with Hextech Ray, but you can completely neutralize his short-range trading pattern. By casting Prismatic Barrier as he steps up, you absorb the damage from his empowered attack, while simultaneously using Lucent Singularity to chip his health from a distance that his laser cannot easily punish.

summary: Graves's Quickdraw grants armor but no magic resistance, leaving him highly vulnerable to Diana's AP burst once she dashes in with Lunar Rush.
howToPlay: To execute this, track Graves's position in the river and always initiate from the brush to catch him off guard. Do not throw Crescent Strike blindly; wait until he uses Quickdraw to reposition, then hit him with your projectile. Once marked, execute your Lunar Rush and activate Pale Cascade to absorb his End of the Line damage. If he blinds you with Smoke Screen, retreat slightly using the attack speed and movement from Moonsilver Blade until your vision returns.
laneImpact: In the jungle, this dynamic shifts early pressure entirely to your side. Graves cannot safely invade your camps or contest scuttle crabs because he dreads a direct confrontation. Since your AP burst wins the duel, you command river priority. If he attempts to secure objectives, your threat of a sudden engage forces him to concede space, leaving his lanes vulnerable to your ganks while he falls behind in farm.
why: This jungle matchup leans heavily in Diana's favor due to how their defensive tools interact. While Graves relies on Quickdraw to stack physical armor, this defense does absolutely nothing against your magic damage. Once you tag him with Crescent Strike, you can bypass his range advantage. Your Lunar Rush gap-close exposes his lack of magic resistance, allowing your full AP burst to shred his health pool before his New Destiny reload cycle ramps up.

summary: Yasuo's Wind Wall cannot block any of Sett's abilities, allowing Sett to easily pull him with Facebreaker when he dashes.
howToPlay: Position yourself constantly in the middle of your own minion wave. This ensures you always have targets on both sides to trigger the stun on Facebreaker when Yasuo dashes in. Hold your Haymaker specifically for when he attempts to cast Last Breath or after he commits his Steel Tempest tornado, ensuring the true damage center-line hits him while he is locked in animation. If he plays extremely safe, use Knuckle Down to zone him completely off the gold.
laneImpact: You dictate the pace of every trade near the minion wave. Yasuo cannot safely farm with Steel Tempest without exposing himself to your pull. When he tries to stack his tornado, you can stand directly inside your wave, forcing him to take bad trades where your Pit Grit out-sustains his poke. This constant threat of being grabbed under your tower or slammed by The Show Stopper forces him into defensive, low-income lane play.
why: Yasuo is completely defenseless against your kit because Wind Wall cannot block any of Sett's attacks or abilities. Whenever he attempts to dance through your minions with Sweeping Blade, his movement path is highly predictable. This allows you to easily disrupt his mobility with Facebreaker, pulling him out of his dash before unleashing a heavy Knuckle Down sequence to shred his Way of the Wanderer shield.

summary: Darius's passive armor penetration from Apprehend and true damage from Noxian Guillotine bypass Rammus's Defensive Ball Curl.
howToPlay: When fighting Rammus, save Apprehend to cancel his Powerball escape or interrupt his charge before he reaches your allies. When he activates Defensive Ball Curl, do not panic; use Crippling Strike and Decimate to quickly apply Hemorrhage stacks. Once you reach maximum stacks, immediately unleash Noxian Guillotine to execute him through his temporary defenses. If he targets you with Frenzying Taunt, let your passive damage tick up while waiting to strike back.
laneImpact: This matchup allows you to invade Rammus aggressively. He cannot contest you at camps because his slow clear makes him vulnerable to your early power. If he attempts to escape with Powerball, you can pull him back. Your ability to shred him means he must concede river priority and Scuttle Crabs, drastically limiting his map pressure and forcing him to take suboptimal, desperate ganks.
why: Rammus relies entirely on stacking armor to reflect physical damage back at you. However, Darius naturally counters this defense. The passive armor penetration granted by your Apprehend completely undermines his Defensive Ball Curl bonuses. Furthermore, once you stack Hemorrhage, your Noxian Guillotine deals massive true damage that ignores his bolstered defensive stats, turning his tankiness into a liability during direct jungle duels.

summary: Ahri can bypass Veigar's Event Horizon cage by positioning outside of it before using Spirit Rush to chase him down.
howToPlay: When trading, never dash directly into Event Horizon. Instead, bait Veigar into casting his cage by walking forward, then walk backward to stay outside its boundary. Once the walls appear, use Spirit Rush laterally to flank the cage and instantly follow up with Charm and Fox-Fire. If he plays too safely, use Orb of Deception to shove the wave hard and immediately roam to assist your jungler, leaving Veigar to choose between following you or stacking his passive.
laneImpact: In lane, this dynamic forces Veigar to play incredibly defensively, conceding wave control. You can safely clear minions with Orb of Deception and harass him under tower. Since Veigar cannot safely step up without risking a Charm, you secure early priority. This allows you to secure quick recall timings and roam to side lanes, snowballing the map while Veigar is stuck farming Baleful Strike under his turret.
why: Ahri dominates Veigar because his primary defensive tool, Event Horizon, is easily bypassed. While Veigar relies on landing this stun to setup Dark Matter or escape, Ahri's high mobility completely neutralizes it. By staying mobile and positioning correctly, she can wait out the cage or use Spirit Rush to dash around the perimeter, closing the gap instantly to burst him down before he can scale his Phenomenal Evil Power.

summary: Poppy's Steadfast Presence stops Kindred's Dance of Arrows dash, and Keeper's Verdict can blast Kindred away from her Lamb's Respite.
howToPlay: To execute this perfectly, always hold Steadfast Presence until you see Kindred start the animation for Dance of Arrows, rather than pressing it preemptively. When they drop Lamb's Respite, do not panic or burst them down immediately. Instead, position yourself inside the circle and begin charging Keeper's Verdict. Time the release just before the zone ends to fling Kindred far away, allowing your team to collect the kill while you benefit from the final heal.
laneImpact: This interaction completely shifts the power dynamic during early skirmishes and objective fights. Kindred cannot safely contest their Mark of the Kindred camps in your jungle or the river, as stepping near any wall invites a devastating Heroic Charge stun. You dictate the pace of neutral objectives because Kindred's ultimate is no longer a safe zone, forcing them to concede early scuttle crabs and play with constant fear of being counter-jungled.
why: Poppy naturally dominates this matchup because her kit completely neutralizes Kindred's core defensive tools. When Kindred attempts to kite or escape using the short dash of Dance of Arrows, activating Steadfast Presence instantly blocks their movement, grounding them for an easy follow-up. Moreover, when Kindred deploys Lamb's Respite to survive fatal damage, a charged Keeper's Verdict lets you eject them from their own sanctuary, leaving them vulnerable to death.

summary: Olaf's Ragnarok (R) makes him immune to CC, but it does not reveal you in Twilight Shroud (W), allowing you to easily waste his ultimate's duration.
howToPlay: To dominate this lane, never use Twilight Shroud offensively when Olaf's Ragnarok is available. Instead, bait his ultimate by poking with Five Point Strike or engaging with Shuriken Flip, then immediately drop your shroud when he screams and charges. Walk in circles within the smoke to evade Undertow axes. Once his ultimate fades and his resistances are lowered, unleash Perfect Execution to secure the kill before his Vicious Strikes can heal him back up.
laneImpact: This interaction shifts the lane pressure entirely in your favor once ultimates are unlocked. Olaf cannot brainlessly dive or force long trades because your Twilight Shroud acts as a safety zone that stops his aggressive momentum. You can safely poke him with Five Point Strike to chip away his health pool. Once his Ragnarok expires, he becomes an easy target for an all-in burst, preventing him from utilizing Berserker Rage safely.
why: Olaf relies entirely on sticking to you with Undertow and shredding you during Ragnarok. However, your Twilight Shroud completely shuts down his offensive pressure. Even though his ultimate makes him immune to any crowd control, it does not grant him true sight. By hiding inside your smoke, you force him to mindlessly pace around while his ultimate's duration ticks away uselessly, neutralizing his main combat steroid.

summary: Lucian can use Relentless Pursuit to easily dodge Phosphorus Bomb and retaliate instantly with his Lightslinger passive.
howToPlay: To survive, prioritize wave management over direct confrontation. Keep the minions just outside your tower range and use Gatling Gun to thin the wave safely. Never initiate with Phosphorus Bomb; instead, hold this ability until Lucian uses Relentless Pursuit offensively, then retaliate on his landing spot. If he locks you down with The Culling, immediately use Valkyrie diagonally to escape his linear line of fire, preserving your health until your Package arrives.
laneImpact: This threat forces you to play defensively under your turret. Because you cannot reliably land Phosphorus Bomb without getting punished, Lucian easily dictates the wave pace, pushing you in to chip away at your tower. If you waste Valkyrie to escape his aggressive dashes, you lose all safety, allowing Lucian to zone you completely from gold or even execute you with The Culling if your health gets too low.
why: Lucian dominates the early trades because his high mobility neutralizes your primary poke. Every time you throw a Phosphorus Bomb to harass or farm, Lucian can reactively dash with Relentless Pursuit to completely avoid the damage. He then instantly triggers his Lightslinger double-tap, forcing a highly uneven trade that chunks your health bar before you can shred his resistances with Gatling Gun.

summary: Yone can use the movement speed from Soul Unbound to easily dodge Aatrox's Infernal Chains and Q sweetspots.
howToPlay: To survive, you must play around the cooldown of Soul Unbound. Never initiate trades with your full combo while he has this tool ready. Instead, bait his spirit form out and use Umbral Dash backwards to minimize damage, or time your Infernal Chains to hit his physical body right as he is forced to snap back. Once he returns to his anchor, you have a twenty-second window to unleash World Ender and aggressively punish his lack of escape.
laneImpact: Because Yone can dodge your sweetspots so easily, you lose the ability to pressure the minion wave safely. He can freely stack Mortal Steel to threaten his third-cast tornado, forcing you to retreat. If you attempt to fight back, his Spirit Cleave shield absorbs your un-empowered swings. This forces you into a defensive posture under your turret, bleed gold, and lose priority during crucial early skirmishes.
why: This matchup hinges on Yone's ability to completely neutralize your primary damage tool. When he activates Soul Unbound, the massive movement speed bonus allows him to effortlessly sidestep the sweetspots of your The Darkin Blade. Furthermore, this extra mobility lets him walk straight out of your Infernal Chains before the pull triggers, leaving you vulnerable to his Mortal Steel strikes without any way to retaliate effectively.

summary: Neither jungler has hard CC to interrupt the other, turning the matchup into a pure farming race where Shyvana prioritizes dragons while Mundo scales for teamfights.
howToPlay: Maximize your clear speed by resetting your auto-attacks with Twin Bite inside your Burnout aura. Do not waste time chasing him; his passive Goes Where He Pleases makes early skirmishes fruitless. Instead, track his pathing and rush the first dragon the moment Dragon's Descent is active. If Dr. Mundo contests, use Flame Breath to shred his high health pool, but prioritize the objective's health bar to secure your vital Fury of the Dragonborn stacks.
laneImpact: Because ganks are hard to force without reliable CC, lanes on both sides receive very little early pressure. The jungle remains quiet until Epic Monsters spawn. You will find yourself constantly tracking his position to steal away camps with Flame Breath while he attempts to out-sustain you. If you fail to secure the first drake, you fall behind in stacks, shifting the pressure entirely onto your laners to survive his mid-game teamfight scaling.
why: This matchup is a pure speed-clearing contest because neither of you possesses the hard crowd control required to lock down or interrupt the other. Dr. Mundo relies on Infected Bonesaw for slow and Heart Zapper for sustain, while you use Burnout and Twin Bite to tear through camps. Without CC to force errors, you both powerfarm, but your passive Fury of the Dragonborn demands you secure elemental dragons to scale.

summary: Vayne can use Condemn to push Twitch away and cancel his Ambush opener, preventing him from stacking Deadly Venom.
howToPlay: You must absolutely hold Condemn as your primary defensive tool; never waste it for simple poke. Position yourself near the lane bushes to drop minion aggro and limit Twitch's stealth angles. When you hear his Ambush exit sound, immediately push him away to deny his burst. If he triggers Spray and Pray, use Final Hour combined with Tumble to reposition invisibly, forcing him to waste his ultimate's duration searching for you.
laneImpact: Because Twitch can approach invisibly, lane pressure is highly psychological. If he wastes Venom Cask to clear minions, you can use Tumble forward to force a short trade with Silver Bolts. However, overextending makes you vulnerable to his stealth engages. The lane remains even because neither can safely push the tower without tracking the other, turning the lane into a tense stand-off.
why: This skill matchup pits Vayne's superior single-target dueling against Twitch's teamfight potential. The lane hinges on Twitch trying to surprise you out of Ambush to quickly stack Deadly Venom. If you react quickly with Condemn, you can knock him back immediately, neutralizing his attack speed burst and stopping him from setting up a massive Contaminate execute. It's a pure test of reaction speed.

summary: Parrying the true damage center of Sett's Haymaker or his Facebreaker pull is crucial to winning extended duels.
howToPlay: To outplay her, you must delay your crowd control. Never start a trade by pulling her with Facebreaker immediately; instead, run at her with Knuckle Down to force an early Riposte. If she holds her parry, angle your Haymaker slightly to the side to avoid her shield while still gaining your grit barrier, or use The Show Stopper to reposition behind her, disrupting her Duelist's Dance vital alignments.
laneImpact: Because of this delicate balance, trades are explosive and leave little room for error. A successful parry allows Fiora to trigger Grand Challenge and dive you, while a baited Riposte lets Sett zone her away from the wave with Knuckle Down. Minion waves often freeze near the middle as both players fear committing without a clear advantage, making health bars fluctuate wildly based on who lands their key ability first.
why: The matchup centers entirely on a high-stakes psychological game between Sett's crowd control and Fiora's defensive reaction. Since Fiora relies on Riposte to parry either the stun from Facebreaker or the true damage center of Haymaker, the duel is an active mind game. If she blocks Facebreaker, she stuns Sett and wins easily; if she parries Haymaker, she mitigates Sett's biggest burst potential, turning the fight in her favor.

summary: Galio can interrupt Aurelion Sol's Breath of Light (Q) channel using Justice Punch (E) or Shield of Durand (W), disrupting his waveclear.
howToPlay: Position yourself aggressively parallel to the minion wave. Do not waste Justice Punch to clear minions; instead, hold it until Aurelion Sol starts channeling Breath of Light. If he drops Singularity to zone you, walk around it and use Justice Punch to close the gap, or flash-taunt with Shield of Durand. Once he is forced to retreat, immediately push the wave and look at your minimap to launch Hero's Entrance toward active side lane fights.
laneImpact: By constantly interrupting his Breath of Light, you deny Aurelion Sol the ability to shove waves effectively. This allows you to clear the lane quickly using Winds of War and your passive Colossal Smash. Having permanent priority means you can easily disappear from the mid lane to look for side lane ganks, using Hero's Entrance to join skirmishes before he can slowly fly over with Astral Flight.
why: Aurelion Sol relies heavily on channeling Breath of Light to secure his Cosmic Creator stacks and melt minion waves. Since he must remain stationary during this channel, he is extremely vulnerable to your crowd control. You can easily disrupt his main source of damage and waveclear by knocking him up with Justice Punch or taunting him with Shield of Durand, completely shutting down his early game scaling engine.

summary: Black Shield (E) can block the knockup from Fate Sealed (R), but Yone's high physical damage and mobility make it difficult to land Dark Binding (Q).
howToPlay: Never throw Dark Binding proactively while Yone has Soul Unbound available; save it exclusively to punish his return to his starting spirit clone or when he commits to a straight-line dash during Mortal Steel. Keep your distance when his wind queue is charged. If he initiates with Fate Sealed, instantly cast Black Shield on yourself to absorb the crowd control, then immediately drop Tormented Shadow under you and activate Soul Shackles to force him to retreat rather than completing his burst combo.
laneImpact: Yone will constantly threaten you with his third Mortal Steel cast, forcing you to play defensively under tower. When he initiates with Soul Unbound, you are forced to retreat, conceding mid-lane priority. This limits your ability to safely drop Tormented Shadow on the wave, resulting in early tower pressure and allowing Yone to roam freely into your jungle while you struggle to clear minions safely.
why: Yone's dual damage from Way of the Hunter and physical burst bypasses the magic-only damage absorption of Black Shield, leaving you vulnerable to his raw damage even if you block the knockup from Fate Sealed. Furthermore, his swift dashes via Mortal Steel and Soul Unbound make predicting his movement to land Dark Binding incredibly difficult, letting him close the distance and shred you before you can lock him down.

summary: Olaf's Ragnarok completely negates Ornn's CC-heavy kit, allowing Olaf to run Ornn down without fear of Searing Charge or Call of the Forge God.
howToPlay: To survive, you must anchor yourself to your turret and use Volcanic Rupture exclusively to farm from maximum range. Never initiate with Searing Charge; save this dash to escape toward your tower the instant he triggers Ragnarok. If he dives you, use Bellows Breath to shield yourself from Reckless Swing's true damage. Never waste Call of the Forge God on an active Ragnarok.
laneImpact: From level six onwards, you lose the ability to safely contest the wave. If Olaf lands a single Undertow while you are extended past the midpoint, he can simply activate Ragnarok to ignore Searing Charge and run you down with Vicious Strikes. This constant threat forces you to surrender wave control, turtle under your tower, and absorb immense pressure.
why: Olaf represents a mathematical nightmare for you because Ragnarok completely dismantles your crowd control-heavy identity. When he activates his ultimate, your primary defensive and offensive tools, namely Call of the Forge God and Searing Charge, fail to knock him up or slow him down. This immunity allows him to bypass your Bellows Breath brittle procs entirely while easily chasing you down.

summary: Jinx must avoid standing directly behind low-health friendly minions to prevent Miss Fortune from landing a critical Double Up bounce.
howToPlay: To survive, you must constantly visualize the linear angle between Miss Fortune, your low-health minions, and yourself. Stand diagonally or off to the side of the wave, using the extended range of Switcheroo! in rocket form to safely secure last hits from afar. Save your Zap! to retaliate only when she steps forward aggressively, and hold Flame Chompers! to self-peel immediately if she tries to run you down with Strut or channel Bullet Time.
laneImpact: This continuous attrition forces you into a defensive stance, making it highly risky to contest wave priority. If you take even one bad bounce, you are forced to farm under tower where Make It Rain can easily trap you for further damage. This low health pressure ruins your recall timings, allows her to chip plates with her attack speed from Strut, and ultimately prevents you from matching her lane presence.
why: Miss Fortune excels at squeezing you out of the lane by exploiting your need to step up for last hits. Her primary tool, Double Up, deals devastating critical damage if it bounces off a dying minion directly into you. Coupled with the passive damage from Love Tap and the slowing zone of Make It Rain, she can constantly chip away at your health bar before you can even retaliate with your own basic attacks.

summary: Kennen can kite out Tryndamere's R (Undying Rage) by using E (Lightning Rush) and landing stuns via his Passive (Mark of the Storm) to prevent Tryndamere from landing auto-attacks.
howToPlay: To survive, you must play defensively and bait his escape tool before committing. Never engage with Spinning Slash unless his Lightning Rush is on cooldown. If he wastes it to poke or clear, that is your window to trade. Use Mocking Shout when his back is turned to slow him down and offset his speed boost. If he activates Slicing Maelstrom, do not hesitate to retreat immediately rather than trying to fight through the stuns.
laneImpact: This dynamic leaves you constantly poked down under your turret. Kennen will harass you with Thundering Shuriken and empowered autos from Electrical Surge to deny you from building Battle Fury. You cannot easily crash waves or threaten dives because he can disengage instantly. If you overextend trying to force a trade, you will be forced to use Bloodlust just to survive, losing all your pressure and priority.
why: Kennen counters your ultimate pressure because he possesses the perfect tools to neutralize your melee threat. Whenever you activate Undying Rage to secure a kill, Kennen can simply activate Lightning Rush to gain massive movement speed and escape. If you try to close the gap, his passive Mark of the Storm allows him to stun you repeatedly, leaving you running in place while your ultimate ticks away uselessly.

summary: Warwick's massive healing from Eternal Hunger and damage reduction from Primal Howl prevent Diana from ever winning a sustained 1v1 fight.
howToPlay: To survive, you must rush anti-heal itemization immediately to cut down his self-healing. Never initiate fights; instead, path to the opposite side of the map to secure cross-map ganks. If he jumps on you with Jaws of the Beast, use Pale Cascade to absorb his immediate damage while you retreat. If a teamfight erupts, save your Moonfall to disrupt his Infinite Duress channel when he targets your carries, rather than using it to engage.
laneImpact: This matchup severely limits your early map pressure. You cannot contest Scuttle Crabs or fight him for neutral objectives, as his Blood Hunt reveals your position if you get low clearing camps. If he invades your jungle, you must abandon your camps; trying to defend them results in him using Infinite Duress to suppress you, leading to an easy death and giving up complete control of your side of the map.
why: Warwick completely shuts down your assassination potential. If you engage with Crescent Strike and Lunar Rush, he can easily activate Primal Howl to absorb your initial burst. Once your main damage is on cooldown, his passive Eternal Hunger provides him with massive healing that scales as his health drops, meaning you can never win a prolonged duel in the river or jungle camps.

summary: Aurora can use the movement speed from Across the Veil (W) to dodge Command: Attack (Q) and trade effectively.
howToPlay: Walk aggressively into her range to bait her Command: Attack, then immediately react with Across the Veil to sidestep it. Once her ball is out of position, quick-cast Twofold Hex and pop Spirit Abjuration for a quick burst trade before she can recall the ball with Command: Protect. If you get caught by Command: Shockwave, immediately use The Weirding to slow her and disengage, preserving your health rather than forcedly committing.
laneImpact: Successfully dodging her ball dictates who controls the wave. If Orianna misses her Command: Attack, she loses her primary tool for clearing minions or poking you, allowing you to shove with Twofold Hex and secure priority. However, if she lands her combos, she will freeze the wave, poke you down with Clockwork Windup enhanced auto-attacks, and force a bad recall that hurts your team's river presence.
why: This matchup is a pure contest of spacing, where Orianna seeks to zone you with her ball's positioning. The lane's equilibrium hinges on how you respond to Command: Attack. Because Orianna's threat relies entirely on where her ball lands, using the sudden movement speed and invisibility from Across the Veil to bait and dodge her initial cast allows you to bypass her zone and retaliate.

summary: Interrupting her Vault Breaker with a well-timed The Darkin Blade sweetspot prevents her from applying Denting Blows quickly.
howToPlay: Never initiate with a fully charged Vault Breaker from a distance if Aatrox has his sword glowing. Instead, run at him to bait The Darkin Blade strikes, using your Blast Shield to absorb the damage. Alternatively, cast Cease and Desist directly to become unstoppable, bypassing his knockups entirely. Once his three strikes are on cooldown, immediately unleash Vault Breaker and Relentless Force to shred his armor before he can activate World Ender.
laneImpact: This volatile interaction dictates who controls the river skirmishes and neutral camps. Missing your initial punch or getting interrupted allows Aatrox to tether you with Infernal Chains and heal back up. Conversely, forcing him to waste his first strikes on monsters gives you free rein to invade his camps, secure Scuttle Crabs, and force him out of his own jungle before he can scale.
why: You hold the upper hand in this jungle duel because your sustained armor shred can easily melt Aatrox. However, the entire matchup hinges on a single micro-interaction: Aatrox will try to interrupt your Vault Breaker mid-flight using The Darkin Blade sweetspots. If he successfully knocks you back, you cannot trigger Denting Blows quickly, allowing him to outsustain your damage with Deathbringer Stance and World Ender.

summary: Akali can use Twilight Shroud to prevent Ekko from targeting her with Phase Dive, disrupting his three-hit passive proc.
howToPlay: To execute this plan, hold your Twilight Shroud and activate it only when you see the forward dash of his Phase Dive. If Ekko casts Parallel Convergence to gain a shield, immediately disengage using Five Point Strike to slow him, or use Shuriken Flip to leap away from the stun zone. Once his defensive options are exhausted, unleash Perfect Execution to burst him down before he can react with Chronobreak.
laneImpact: This interaction allows you to dictate the wave state during early levels. Ekko is forced to use Timewinder defensively to secure minions rather than poke you, knowing that stepping forward invites a devastating trade. This keeps him on the back foot, delaying his item spikes and neutralizing his mid-game roam potential, while forcing him to play passively until he unlocks Chronobreak.
why: This melee assassin matchup tilts heavily in your favor because Twilight Shroud completely shuts down Ekko's offensive pattern. When he attempts to dash in with Phase Dive to trigger his third Z-Drive Resonance stack, activating your shroud instantly makes you untargetable. Deprived of his empowered auto-attack, Ekko cannot proc his passive burst or gain his escape velocity, leaving him extremely vulnerable to your retaliation.

summary: Ezreal can buffer Arcane Shift to escape Tristana's Rocket Jump engage, leaving her stranded with an uncharged Explosive Charge.
howToPlay: Never initiate with Rocket Jump unless you have seen Ezreal waste Arcane Shift. Instead, focus on farming with Draw a Bead and only trade with basic attacks and Rapid Fire when he steps up to shoot Mystic Shot. If he aggressively blinks forward, immediately cast Buster Shot to knock him back, neutralizing his Rising Spell Force stacks. Hold your jump as a defensive tool to reposition safely rather than an offensive trigger.
laneImpact: You cannot reliably force all-ins, which heavily stifles your early kill pressure. Ezreal safely farms and pokes you down from a distance using Mystic Shot and Essence Flux. Attempting to match his push with Explosive Charge on minions often leaves you overextended. If you fall behind in health, you will find yourself trapped under tower, constantly dodging Trueshot Barrage while unable to contest the wave.
why: This matchup hinges entirely on how Ezreal's mobility neutralizes your aggressive burst. Whenever you try to initiate with Rocket Jump and attach Explosive Charge, Ezreal can buffer Arcane Shift to instantly blink away. Because his escape cast-time cannot be interrupted by your jump's landing impact, he leaves you stranded deep in the lane with an uncharged bomb, preventing you from getting the Rapid Fire attacks needed to trigger your reset.

summary: Since Black Shield (E) only absorbs magic damage, it offers no protection against Zed's physical burst from Death Mark (R), requiring precise timing on Dark Binding (Q) when he reappears.
howToPlay: Never throw Dark Binding proactively when Zed has his Living Shadow or Death Mark available, as missing it leaves you completely defenseless. When he targets you with Death Mark, stand still and prepare to cast Dark Binding directly behind your character model the instant he materializes. Follow up immediately with Tormented Shadow and Soul Shackles to lock him down, using Soul Siphon's passive healing to survive any lingering physical damage he managed to apply before your crowd control kicked in.
laneImpact: Zed’s Living Shadow allows him to poke you from safety with Razor Shuriken and Shadow Slash, forcing you to play defensively. You cannot contest deep waves easily; instead, you must rely on Tormented Shadow to clear minions safely from a distance. If you step up too far without Dark Binding ready, he will instantly trigger his Death Mark, threatening a solo kill that ruins your tower pressure and mid-priority.
why: This matchup is highly volatile because your primary defensive tool, Black Shield, only absorbs magic damage. Zed’s entire burst kit is purely physical, meaning his Death Mark and physical combos completely bypass your shield's protection. Because you cannot block his raw damage, you are entirely reliant on landing Dark Binding the exact moment he reappears behind you from his ultimate to prevent his lethal follow-up.

summary: Viktor can easily poke Karma down with Hextech Ray (E) from safety, forcing her to play defensively and preventing her from using Focused Resolve (W).
howToPlay: Position yourself constantly behind your own minion wave to block her Inner Flame splash damage. Use Hextech Ray to simultaneously thin the wave and clip her when she steps up to shield herself with Inspire. If she tries to run at you with her movement speed buff to land Focused Resolve, immediately drop Gravity Field directly on your own feet and retreat with Siphon Power for the shield. If you miss your laser, back off until its cooldown returns to avoid her retaliatory trade.
laneImpact: By keeping Karma low with constant lasers, you dictate the wave's tempo entirely. She is forced to burn Inner Flame on clearing minions rather than poking you, ruining her wave control. This denies her any lane priority, trapping her under turret and preventing her from roaming to support her jungler. You safely secure perfect recall timings and a massive gold lead as her tower health gradually decays under your constant pressure.
why: This lane swings heavily in your favor because Hextech Ray allows you to damage Karma from outside her effective range. Karma wants to approach to tether you with Focused Resolve or trade shields with Inspire, but your superior poke forces her to use her resources defensively. She cannot safely trigger her Mantra cooldown reductions on you, allowing you to comfortably stack Glorious Evolution while she is stuck playing behind her wave.

summary: Mordekaiser can use Realm of Death to isolate Vi after she commits with Cease and Desist, stripping her of stats and neutralizing her dive.
howToPlay: Never cast Realm of Death prematurely while Vi has her charge ready. Instead, position yourself near your priority targets and wait for the visual indicator of her Cease and Desist. The moment she flies in, prepare to pull her with Death's Grasp if she tries to disengage, or immediately trap her in your duel. If you miss your timing and she triggers Blast Shield, activate Indestructible to survive her initial burst, then retaliate with isolated Obliterate strikes.
laneImpact: In the jungle, this even dynamic turns every neutral objective skirmish into a high-stakes standoff. If Vi uses Vault Breaker to rush objectives, she leaves herself vulnerable to Death's Grasp. However, if you waste Indestructible early, her Denting Blows armor shred will quickly melt your health bar. Skirmishes are decided purely by who baits the other's defensive cooldowns first during river contests.
why: This jungle matchup revolves around Vi's initiation and Mordekaiser's ultimate counter. When Vi charges with Vault Breaker or commits her unstoppable Cease and Desist to dive your backline, she is locked into a predictable trajectory. By timing Realm of Death right as she lands, you strip her of crucial defensive stats from Blast Shield and isolate her, completely neutralizing her dive and turning her engage into a deadly trap.

summary: Pantheon's Shield Vault provides a point-and-click stun that halts Hecarim's high-speed Devastating Charge instantly, leaving him vulnerable to early burst.
howToPlay: To survive, plan your jungle pathing to avoid direct contact with him in the early levels. When ganking, never lead with Devastating Charge if Pantheon is nearby; instead, wait for him to commit Shield Vault on an ally first. If he jumps on someone else, you can safely flank, activate Spirit of Dread to survive his Aegis Assault, and use Onslaught of Shadows to fear him from behind his directional shield to turn the fight.
laneImpact: Because of this threat, contesting early river objectives or scuttle crabs directly is incredibly risky. Pantheon's superior early pressure forces you to play defensively in your own jungle, as getting caught means dying before Spirit of Dread can sustain you. Furthermore, his ability to match your map presence with Grand Starfall means any poorly timed roam or gank you attempt can turn into a deadly counter-gank.
why: Pantheon dominates the early jungle duels because his Shield Vault is a direct counter to your main engagement tool. The moment you activate Devastating Charge to build up speed and attack damage via Warpath, he can point-and-click stun you mid-stride. This completely kills your momentum, cancels your knockback, and leaves you stationary and defenseless against a quick, empowered Comet Spear burst.

summary: Block Urgot's Disdain flip with Repudiation to deny him his shield and positioning advantage, then shred him with Cunning Sweep.
howToPlay: Position yourself constantly near Urgot’s front arc to bait his dash, but never commit your own dashes mindlessly. Keep Repudiation ready specifically for when you see his charge animation begin. If he tries to slow you with Corrosive Charge first, use Lacerate to reposition and maintain your angle without wasting your defensive shield. Should you mistime your block and get flipped, immediately activate Public Execution to turn the battle around and execute him before his Purge wears you down.
laneImpact: Urgot's lane dominance collapses once he cannot threaten you with his flip. Because you consistently win trades by blocking Disdain, you dictate wave placement, forcing him to farm from a distance with Purge. This creates massive health differentials, allowing you to crash large minion waves and secure free recall timings. Urgot is forced to play defensively under tower, bleeding gold and losing the ability to assist his jungler.
why: This matchup revolves around Urgot's attempt to execute his trade using Disdain. When he dashes forward to flip you, your Repudiation acts as the ultimate counter-measure. By timing it to absorb the impact, you block the displacement and stun, negate his shield creation, and immediately retaliate. Without his flip, Urgot cannot easily trigger multiple Echoing Flames passives, allowing your Cunning Sweep to shred his health bar while he is stuck in place.

summary: Sidestep or use Apprehend to reposition during Sett's Haymaker to avoid the true damage center line before executing him with Noxian Guillotine.
howToPlay: During extended trades, never use Apprehend just for damage. Keep it ready for when Sett charges his Haymaker. The moment you see him wind up, quickly sidestep the center line or use Apprehend to pull and displace him, forcing his true damage to miss. Once his shield quickly decays, immediately dunk him with Noxian Guillotine. If you get stunned by Facebreaker first, delay your ultimate until you can safely reposition.
laneImpact: Every trade in this lane carries lethal risk, forcing both of you to fight for wave control with extreme caution. Whichever juggernaut missteps and gets pulled by Facebreaker or Apprehend is forced into a deadly all-in. Neither of you can safely roam or assist your jungler if you lose the health lead, meaning a single execution error permanently surrenders top lane priority.
why: This lane is a high-stakes duel where Hemorrhage directly fuels Sett's Grit meter. As you stack your passive, Sett prepares to unleash Haymaker for a massive shield and burst. The fight is decided by a split-second interaction: if you can bypass his central true damage zone, your Noxian Guillotine will easily tear through his remaining health once his temporary shield decays.

summary: Shen's Spirit's Refuge blocks Jax's basic attacks, mirroring how Jax's Counter Strike blocks Shen's Twilight Assault empowered attacks.
howToPlay: Walk up to the wave to stack Relentless Assault instead of initiating with Leap Strike. If Shen taunts you with Shadow Dash, immediately trigger Counter Strike to negate his Twilight Assault damage. Hold your Empower until his Spirit's Refuge zone dissipates so your damage isn't wasted. Finally, keep Leap Strike ready when he has his ultimate, allowing you to quickly close the gap and stun him out of Stand United.
laneImpact: Short, explosive trades dictate the lane, keeping wave states neutral as both of you hesitate to commit. If you waste Counter Strike, Shen will immediately force a trade with Shadow Dash. However, his global threat with Stand United is heavily checked by your presence; you can either cancel his channel with the stun from Counter Strike or immediately punish his departure by taking plates.
why: This matchup is a pure battle of attack-blocking zones. Shen relies on Twilight Assault to deal his main damage, which is completely negated by your Counter Strike. Conversely, when you try to retaliate with Empower and Relentless Assault stacks, Shen drops Spirit's Refuge to nullify your basic attacks. Neither champion can brute-force the other without baiting out these mirroring defensive tools first.

summary: Use Apprehend to disrupt Urgot's Disdain dash mid-animation to prevent him from flipping and shielding.
howToPlay: Position yourself slightly to the side of your minion wave, baiting Urgot into aiming his *Disdain* forward. Always hold onto *Apprehend* specifically for this animation; never use it to initiate a trade unless he has already wasted his dash. If you successfully disrupt his dash, immediately reset your auto-attack with *Crippling Strike*, stack your *Hemorrhage*, and finish him with *Noxian Guillotine* before his *Fear Beyond Death* can execute you.
laneImpact: Because you hold this disengage check, Urgot is forced to play defensively, fearing a lethal pull under your tower. You can easily slow-push waves to force him to farm with *Corrosive Charge*. This pressure allows you to walk up, land a healing *Decimate* on his outer edge, and control the lane rhythm. Urgot cannot trade back with *Purge* effectively if he cannot lock you down first.
why: Darius dominates this matchup because he can completely nullify Urgot's primary defensive and offensive tool. When Urgot winds up his *Disdain* to dash, flip, and shield himself, Darius can reactively pull him out of the air using *Apprehend*. Canceling this dash leaves Urgot incredibly vulnerable, preventing his shield from absorbing damage and stopping his passive *Echoing Flames* from firing off easily from behind you.

summary: Ahri can hold her Charm specifically to interrupt Katarina's Death Lotus, completely neutralizing her teamfight threat.
howToPlay: Your golden rule is to never throw Charm proactively unless Katarina has already used Shunpo to jump onto a dagger. Always hold onto this ability during skirmishes specifically to interrupt Death Lotus. If you miss your projectile, immediately activate Spirit Rush to dash out of her ultimate's radius, healing back up with Essence Theft stacks before re-engaging once her daggers disappear.
laneImpact: This matchup dynamic forces Katarina to play incredibly passively, fearing your crowd control. You can safely shove waves using Orb of Deception to poke her down under tower while she struggles to farm with Bouncing Blade. Her roam potential is severely crippled because she cannot risk leaving her turret while you have the mobility of Spirit Rush to match her map rotations or dive her directly.
why: Ahri completely dictates this lane because her Charm hard-counters Katarina's entire win condition. Katarina relies on jumping in with Shunpo and channeling Death Lotus to wipe out teams, but a single well-aimed heart instantly stops her ultimate mid-cast. Without the massive damage from her channel, Katarina is left highly vulnerable, unable to trigger Voracity resets while your Orb of Deception and Fox-Fire clean up her remaining health.

summary: Mordekaiser's Indestructible shield easily absorbs Twitch's opening burst from Ambush and Spray and Pray, allowing Morde to turn and counter-engage.
howToPlay: When navigating the river or entering unwarded areas, never waste Indestructible on camps; hold it specifically for when Twitch breaks stealth. Once he activates Spray and Pray, activate your shield to soak the pierce damage, then pull him back with Death's Grasp. If he tries to kite away, drag him into the Realm of Death where his stealth is useless, and crush him with Obliterate. Focus your gold on armor-heavy magic items early.
laneImpact: This matchup dynamic completely strips Twitch of his early skirmishing pressure. He cannot safely contest scuttle crabs or invade your camps, as any ambush he attempts backfires. You can aggressively secure objectives, knowing that even if he opens with Venom Cask and Contaminate, you will always win the ensuing trade, forcing him to play passively and fall behind.
why: Twitch relies entirely on catching you off-guard in the jungle with Ambush and maximizing his pierce damage via Spray and Pray. However, his initial burst is completely countered by your Indestructible. By turning the rat's opening volley into a massive shield, you negate his main win condition, easily keeping him in range to trigger your Darkness Rise and beat him in a prolonged duel.

summary: Ornn's Bellows Breath applies Brittle for maximum percent-health magic damage, which bypasses Malphite's armor-stacking defense.
howToPlay: Initiate trades with Volcanic Rupture to summon a pillar, then slide in with Searing Charge to knock him up if he mispositions. Immediately follow up with Bellows Breath to apply Brittle and clap him with an auto-attack. If he reacts with Unstoppable Force to escape or counter-engage, use the unstoppable frame of your own Bellows Breath to completely negate his knock-up. Should you miss your pillar setup, simply back off and wait for your cooldowns rather than letting him retaliate with Thunderclap.
laneImpact: Because Malphite cannot match your wave clear or trade effectively, you dictate the lane's flow. His Seismic Shard poke will quickly drain his mana pool without breaking your sustain, allowing you to crash waves at will. Since he cannot match your short-trade burst, you can constantly threaten him under tower or comfortably use Living Forge to build items in lane, extending your item advantage without giving him a free recall window.
why: Malphite naturally stacks armor to boost Ground Slam and withstand physical damage, but this defense is entirely useless against your kit. When you use Bellows Breath, you inflict percent-health magic damage and apply Brittle. Consuming this mark with a basic attack bypasses his Granite Shield and high armor, melting his health bar in short, bursty trades while his own magic damage scales poorly.

summary: Sona must use Song of Celerity to dodge Death Sentence, as getting hooked usually results in a fatal all-in before she can scale.
howToPlay: Never activate Song of Celerity mindlessly for simple movement; save its mana and cooldown exclusively for when Thresh winds up his Death Sentence. Always position diagonally to him behind your minion wave. If he misses his hook, you have a brief window to step forward, poke with Hymn of Valor, and charge your Power Chord. If caught, immediately use Crescendo to interrupt his follow-up Flay and buy time.
laneImpact: This threat forces Sona to play defensively behind her minions, limiting her ability to safely poke with Hymn of Valor. Thresh can easily zone you away from gold, using Dark Passage to set up deadly ganks or rescue his partner. If you step up too far, he will trap you inside The Box, leaving you with no room to maneuver or protect your carry.
