why: Thresh dominates the early lane pressure because a single successful Death Sentence bypasses all of Sona's sustain from Aria of Perseverance. Sona's fragile health pool makes her an easy target for his follow-up Flay. To survive and scale, Sona must constantly anticipate the hook, using the sudden movement speed from Song of Celerity to sidestep his crowd control before he can pull himself in.

summary: Sett must hold Haymaker until Wukong uses Warrior Trickster, ensuring the true damage blast isn't wasted on a clone.
howToPlay: To survive this lane, never use Warrior Trickster offensively. Instead, trade with basic attacks and Nimbus Strike to chip him down. Only activate Warrior Trickster right as Sett's grit bar fills up, predicting the exact moment he releases Haymaker to redirect his true damage center onto your clone. If he holds it, immediately disengage sideways. If he catches you with The Show Stopper, quickly buffer Cyclone to disrupt his follow-up.
laneImpact: This standoff forces you into a highly defensive stance. You cannot freely initiate with Nimbus Strike followed by Golden Staff because Sett will drag you back with Facebreaker and stack his Grit. Because you must respect his high damage and the threat of The Show Stopper, you will constantly yield wave control, resulting in slow bleeds of health and delayed recalls under tower while Sett maintains priority.
why: Sett's passive Pit Grit and Knuckle Down dominate short trades, but the matchup revolves around Haymaker. A smart Sett will actively hold Haymaker until you commit Warrior Trickster, preventing you from easily dodging his massive true damage shield blast. If you use your clone early, he simply aligns his true damage center on your real body, completely bypassing Wukong's Stone Skin armor stacks.

summary: Garen must bait out Jayce's Thundering Blow knockback before committing Decisive Strike to stick to him.
howToPlay: To win trades, you must bait out Thundering Blow before committing. Walk towards him menacingly to trigger his defensive instinct. If he jumps on you with To the Skies!, activate Courage to mitigate the burst. Once he uses his knockback, immediately activate Decisive Strike to break any lingering slows, close the remaining distance, and spin with Judgment. This setup ensures your Demacian Justice can actually reach him for the execute.
laneImpact: You will spend most of the early levels pushed under your turret, absorbing shockwaves. Jayce will attempt to whittle your health down, trying to disable your Perseverance passive with constant ranged basic attacks. Failing to dodge his poke means losing turret plating or being forced into a bad recall, which hands Jayce complete control over the top side of the map.
why: Jayce dictates the pace of this matchup by shifting between ranged poke and melee defense. While you want to close the distance, his Transform Mercury Cannon gives him the tools to kite you indefinitely. The core issue is his Thundering Blow knockback; if you charge in blindly, he will simply swat you away, wasting your mobility and leaving you exposed to heavy ranged retaliation.

summary: Amumu can use Bandage Toss to stop Hecarim's Devastating Charge mid-run, neutralizing his engage momentum.
howToPlay: To win this matchup, you must bait out Bandage Toss before committing your main movement speed burst. Run in unpredictable angles or use the threat of Onslaught of Shadows to make Amumu waste his skillshot. If he misses or uses his charges, immediately activate Devastating Charge to run down his squishy allies. If Amumu holds his crowd control, focus on peeling for your team with Spirit of Dread and short Rampage trades.
laneImpact: In the jungle, this interaction dictates how skirmishes and river fights play out. When contesting objectives, Hecarim cannot blindly flank because Amumu can lock him down before he reaches the backline. If Hecarim forces an engage with Onslaught of Shadows, Amumu can immediately counter with Curse of the Sad Mummy, matching the crowd control and leaving Hecarim vulnerable to sustained magical damage from Despair and Tantrum.
why: Hecarim relies heavily on the momentum of Devastating Charge to initiate and deal burst damage, but Amumu possesses the perfect tool to halt this. A well-timed Bandage Toss intercepts Hecarim mid-dash, completely canceling his knockback and leaving him stranded. If Hecarim cannot secure his initial burst, Amumu can easily retaliate with Cursed Touch and Despair, turning Hecarim's aggressive sprint into a self-destructive dive.

summary: Yone can use Soul Unbound to bypass Brand's skillshots and close the distance, executing him with Fate Sealed.
howToPlay: Never throw your Sear reactively when Yone charges in his spirit form. Instead, stand near your turret and aim your Pillar of Flame at his physical body's return anchor. Watch his projection closely; the moment Soul Unbound ends and he snaps back, cast Conflagration and Pyroclasm to punish his retreat. If he manages to land Fate Sealed on you under your tower, immediately flash away rather than trying to trade back.
laneImpact: This threat forces you into a highly defensive posture, conceding early wave control. You cannot safely step up to use Conflagration on the minions without risking a sudden engagement. Every time Yone has his Mortal Steel tornado ready, you must retreat to your tower. This constant pressure limits your recall windows, chips away at your health, and prevents you from helping your jungler secure nearby objectives.
why: Yone holds a massive advantage because his Soul Unbound allows him to effortlessly dodge your Pillar of Flame and Sear skillshots while surging forward. By bypassing your zoning tools, he completely negates your defensive stun setup. Once he closes the gap with this spirit form, he can easily chain Mortal Steel knockups directly into Fate Sealed, bursting you down before your passive Blaze can even ramp up.

summary: Blocking Pantheon's Shield Vault with Repudiation denies his full Mortal Will combo and leaves him vulnerable.
howToPlay: Never waste Repudiation to block his Comet Spear poke; keep your finger on this shield exclusively for his Shield Vault jump animation. If he panics and deploys Aegis Assault to block your frontal damage, immediately trigger Drakehound's Step after casting Lacerate or Cunning Sweep to dash directly behind his shield. This allows you to bypass his directional defense and shred his health pool while he is locked in his channel.
laneImpact: Because you hold the tools to negate his main crowd control, you can aggressively contest the Scuttle Crabs and invade his jungle camps without fear. Pantheon cannot safely secure objectives or win isolated skirmishes if you hover near. Even when he attempts to impact other lanes using Grand Starfall, your superior dueling power allows you to counter-gank effectively, converting his cross-map rotations into direct losses.
why: This jungle matchup hinges on your ability to react to Pantheon's initial burst setup. When he attempts to initiate with Shield Vault, a well-timed Repudiation completely absorbs the stun and shields his follow-up damage. By negating this initiation, you prevent him from easily stacking or executing his empowered Mortal Will combo, turning his aggressive dive into a highly vulnerable window where his damage dramatically plummets.

summary: Jayce can use the movement speed from Hextech Capacitor to dodge Mordekaiser's Death's Grasp and avoid being pulled into melee range.
howToPlay: To counter this, never initiate with Death's Grasp while Jayce has his transformation ready. Instead, use Obliterate to farm from a safe distance and walk up to threaten him. Force him to use To the Skies! to engage on you in hammer form. Once he commits to melee range and has expended his transformation movement speed, cast Death's Grasp behind him to pull him back in, activating Darkness Rise to win the extended duel.
laneImpact: When Jayce easily evades your pull, he gains complete control over the wave. He will use his ranged forms to thin the minions while poking you under tower, forcing you to rely heavily on Indestructible to absorb the harassment. This constant pressure delays your recalls and prevents you from assisting your jungler, as you are stuck clearing waves while he holds priority and threatens to chip down your turret plates.
why: This matchup revolves entirely around how you fish for pulls. Every time Jayce swaps stances, Hextech Capacitor grants him a sudden burst of movement speed. This extra mobility allows him to easily sidestep Death's Grasp, leaving you vulnerable to his ranged poke. If he successfully bait-and-dodges your pull, you lose all threat, as he can safely chip away at your health from afar without fear of being forced into a melee brawl.

summary: Camille can easily catch Mini Gnar with Hookshot when his Hop is on cooldown, but must respect Mega Gnar's crowd control.
howToPlay: Watch Gnar's rage meter closely; never commit Hookshot when he is about to transform. When he is in Mini form, bait out his Hop by walking forward with the movement speed from Precision Protocol. The moment he lands from his jump, launch your Hookshot to catch him, using Adaptive Defenses to absorb his Boomerang Throw retaliation. If he manages to transform into Mega Gnar, immediately back off and use Tactical Sweep from maximum range.
laneImpact: The lane's pace swings violently based on Gnar's rage bar. During Mini Gnar phases, you can freeze the wave near your turret, forcing him to overextend for farm where Hookshot can reach him. Once Gnar transforms, you must yield wave priority and fall back, as his enhanced durability and stun threat prevent safe health trades.
why: This matchup revolves around punishing Mini Gnar's vulnerability. While Gnar is small, his only escape is Hop. If he wastes this jump, Camille can immediately initiate with Hookshot to close the distance, bypassing his range advantage. However, when his Rage Gene triggers and he transforms into Mega Gnar, his massive crowd control from Boulder Toss and Hyper turns the tables, making direct aggression highly dangerous for Camille.

summary: Poppy's Steadfast Presence (W) blocks both your Shuriken Flip (E) and Perfect Execution (R) dashes, leaving you grounded and highly vulnerable.
howToPlay: To survive, you must strictly hold your Shuriken Flip and Perfect Execution whenever her defense is ready. Use the maximum range of Five Point Strike to chip away at her health and bait her into activating Steadfast Presence preemptively. Once she wastes this crucial cooldown, you have a brief opportunity to strike. If she catches you off guard, immediately drop Twilight Shroud to break vision and safely wait out her defensive buff.
laneImpact: This mechanical block strips away your lane pressure, forcing you to surrender minion control. You are relegated to farming under tower with Five Point Strike, unable to contest her push. Any aggressive trade risks a massive health deficit, ruining your recall timings and preventing you from roaming. Your main goal shifts from finding solo kills to minimizing losses and preserving your turret.
why: Poppy completely dictates the pace of this lane through Steadfast Presence. This protective zone immediately interrupts the dashes of your Shuriken Flip and Perfect Execution, leaving you grounded and pacified. Without your signature mobility, you cannot safely trigger Assassin's Mark or escape her retaliation, turning your primary offensive tools into dangerous liabilities that leave you completely exposed.

summary: Using Shuriken Flip (E) to dodge Ornn's Searing Charge (E) knockup allows you to safely re-engage and poke him down with passive-enhanced attacks.
howToPlay: To neutralise her mobility, never initiate with Searing Charge. Instead, use Volcanic Rupture to poke her from a distance and force her to move. Keep your distance and focus on farming with Living Forge to build resistance. If she burns Shuriken Flip offensively or misses it, that is your cue to look for a quick Bellows Breath trade. Should she shroud, step back immediately and wait out the cloud before stepping up again.
laneImpact: Because of this threat, you cannot freely crash waves. If you use your abilities to push, Akali will drop Twilight Shroud to zone you from the farm or freeze near her turret. Missing a trade means she dictates the wave pace, forcing you to take heavy damage from Five Point Strike every time you step up to collect minions, eventually forcing a bad recall that costs you turret plates.
why: This matchup revolves around a high-stakes movement duel. Your primary threat is Akali using Shuriken Flip to reactively hop away when you launch Searing Charge. If she successfully avoids your knockup this way, she can instantly reactivate the shuriken to fly back onto you, triggering Assassin's Mark to chunk your health bar while your main escape and crowd control tool is on cooldown.

howToPlay: Shorten commits: don’t all-in without reading his grit. Key timing: trade after he use E or when grit is low, and commit with a large wave to cushion the return. Decision: in teamfights, if Sett has an ult angle onto your backline, your best role may be zoning/threatening him instead of sprinting past to a distant target.
laneImpact: In lane, you can get surprised: you trade well, then a good W deletes a chunk and you lose priority. Once low, you can’t play the wave. In fights, he can also knock you out of an angle or threaten your carry while you’re ‘busy chasing’.
why: Sett is unfavorable because he can absorb your DPS and then flip the trade right when you think you’ve won. Grit + W directly punishes champions who want to hit for a long time. His ult can also reposition you and break chase lines.

summary: You must abuse your ranged advantage to pop Yone's Spirit Cleave shield before committing to a Heroic Swing trade.
howToPlay: Trigger Yone's *Spirit Cleave* shield using your ranged auto-attacks or a well-placed *Avengerang* from a safe distance, then wait out the brief shield duration before doing anything else. Never initiate with *Heroic Swing* while he has his third *Mortal Steel* charge ready or while *Soul Unbound* is active. If he misses his knockup, use that brief opening to execute a flanking grapple, utilizing *Dirty Fighting* to secure the kill.
laneImpact: Controlling the wave is vital to preventing Yone from freely building charges of *Mortal Steel*. If you let him push, he will constantly zone you with his third strike tornado and *Soul Unbound* combos. By matching his push with *Avengerang*, you force Yone to choose between using his sweeps on the minions or trying to shield himself from your double-taps, dictating who controls the mid lane priority.
why: This skill matchup hinges on how you manage the distance between Akshan's ranged autos and Yone's threat zone. While *Way of the Hunter* gives Yone devastating close-quarters damage, your *Dirty Fighting* double-tap allows you to chip him down from afar. However, Yone can negate this harassment using the shield from *Spirit Cleave*. If you swing in while his shield is active, you lose the trade.

summary: Viktor's Hextech Ray outranges Teemo's entire kit, allowing him to poke and clear waves without ever entering Blinding Dart range.
howToPlay: Maximize your range advantage by aiming Hextech Ray to clip Teemo while securing last hits. Never walk into his auto-attack range; if he activates Move Quick to close the gap, immediately drop Gravity Field directly on his path to stun him, then follow up with Siphon Power and Arcane Storm. If you accidentally step on a Noxious Trap, immediately back off and shield yourself with Siphon Power to absorb the poison damage.
laneImpact: Teemo is forced into a defensive posture, unable to use Guerrilla Warfare for stealth-based ambushes in the mid lane brushes. You can easily keep him shoved under his turret using the superior wave clear of Hextech Ray. This constant pressure denies him the freedom to roam and deploy Noxious Trap minefields in the river, keeping the map safe for your jungler while you secure a massive gold lead.
why: Viktor completely dictates this matchup because Hextech Ray easily outranges Teemo's entire offensive kit. Teemo relies on landing Blinding Dart and applying Toxic Shot through basic attacks to trade, but he cannot get close enough to execute this. Since Blinding Dart only neutralizes basic attacks, its crowd control is useless against Viktor's spell-casting loop, allowing you to safely burn his health bar from afar.

summary: Morgana can reactively block Zenith Blade or Shield of Daybreak with Black Shield, forcing Leona to bait the shield before engaging.
howToPlay: To survive, you must bait out Black Shield before committing. Walk up aggressively to threaten with Shield of Daybreak without casting Zenith Blade, forcing her to waste her shield. Once Black Shield is on its long cooldown, you have a brief window to strike. If she holds it, wait for your level five; casting Solar Flare from maximum range can force a panic shield on one target, allowing you to instantly redirect your Zenith Blade onto the other unprotected enemy.
laneImpact: This interaction forces you into a passive state where you cannot safely step forward. If you attempt a raw engage, a quick Dark Binding will stop you mid-dash or pin you down, followed by Tormented Shadow to burn your health. You lose all bush control, allowing Morgana to freely poke you down and push the wave under your tower, which slowly chips away at your tower's health while starving your ADC.
why: Morgana completely neutralizes your engage potential. Whenever you try to lock down her or her ADC with Zenith Blade or Shield of Daybreak, she can reactively cast Black Shield to absorb the magic damage and completely negate your crowd control. Since your kit relies heavily on these consecutive stuns to trigger Sunlight, her spell shield leaves you stranded in the middle of their minion wave without any follow-up.

summary: Poppy's Steadfast Presence blocks and stuns Irelia whenever she attempts to use Bladesurge, removing her mobility.
howToPlay: Position yourself deliberately near your own low-health caster minions. Hold Steadfast Presence specifically for when Irelia’s blades glow or when she steps up to execute a minion with Bladesurge. Never waste this ability offensively. If she misses her Flawless Duet, immediately walk up to trigger Iron Ambassador for a free shield, then use Hammer Shock to punish her retreat. If she catches you with Vanguard's Edge, cast Keeper's Verdict quickly to disengage her ultimate's zone.
laneImpact: This shutdown dynamic lets you dictate the wave's position. By holding your defensive aura, you force Irelia to crash waves slowly, preventing her from easily setup-killing low-health minions. If she steps up to thin the wave with Bladesurge, you can crash her against the lane walls with Heroic Charge. She is forced to play under her turret, bleeding gold while you pressure her or deny her farm safely.
why: You completely shut down Irelia's entire kit because Steadfast Presence directly counters her Bladesurge. Whenever she attempts to dash to a minion for a reset or onto you to stack Ionian Fervor, activating your aura interrupts her movement, grounds her, and prevents further mobility. Without her mobility, she cannot dodge Hammer Shock or escape a wall-stun from Heroic Charge, turning her main threat into a free trade for you.

summary: Since Corki deals primarily magic damage, Galio's Shield of Durand (W) passive shield is highly effective, and Galio can easily out-roam him early.
howToPlay: Use Winds of War on the wave to force Corki to use his abilities on minions rather than on you. When you spot an opportunity, walk forward to threaten with Shield of Durand; he will likely dash away with Valkyrie, draining his mana. Keep a close eye on the map and prepare to trigger Hero's Entrance the moment Corki picks up his Package, as you can easily beat his Special Delivery rotation to any skirmish.
laneImpact: Since you comfortably absorb his magic harass, you can aggressively push waves with Winds of War and Colossal Smash. Corki is forced to farm under turret, burning through mana, or risk using Valkyrie defensively if you threaten a Justice Punch engage. This permanent lane priority grants you uncontested roam windows to impact side lanes before he ever receives his first Package.
why: Corki relies on Hextech Munitions to convert his basic attacks into magic damage, which directly feeds into the passive magic shield of your Shield of Durand. Because his primary poke from Phosphorus Bomb and Gatling Gun is heavily magic-based, your innate damage reduction neutralizes his ranged advantage. He cannot chip away at your health bar effectively, leaving him unable to match your wave clear or threaten you.

summary: Braum can block Malphite's Seismic Shard poke with Unbreakable, but must use Stand Behind Me to dodge the Unstoppable Force knockup.
howToPlay: To execute this, always position yourself slightly behind your marksman but close to your caster minions. Save Stand Behind Me exclusively as an escape tool to dodge Unstoppable Force rather than using it to trade. When Malphite steps forward to use Ground Slam on the wave, hit him with Winter's Bite to trigger Concussive Blows, forcing him to retreat while his passive Granite Shield is down.
laneImpact: This defensive superiority completely neutralizes Malphite's ability to poke you out of lane or force early recalls. Because Seismic Shard consistently hits Unbreakable instead of your marksman, you maintain a health lead that prevents Malphite from securing lane priority. Once both supports unlock their ultimates, Malphite is forced into a passive state, unable to safely launch his signature engage without risking a massive counter-attack.
why: Braum holds a significant advantage because his defensive tools perfectly counter Malphite's predictable aggression. Malphite's primary lane pressure relies on chipping away health with Seismic Shard, which is easily negated by Unbreakable. When Malphite reaches his ultimate power spike and targets your carry with Unstoppable Force, your quick reflex with Stand Behind Me allows you to leap clear of the impact zone, rendering his primary engage useless.

summary: Zilean can easily punish Rell's telegraphed crash-down engage by placing a double Time Bomb stun on her landing location while speeding up his ally with Temporal Mirage.
howToPlay: To survive, you must bait Zilean's Temporal Mirage before ever committing to a hard engage. Stand parallel to your ADC to split Zilean's focus, forcing him to throw single Time Bomb zoning tools. If he wastes his Twisted Timeflow to reset his bombs, that is your cue. Use the movement speed from Full Tilt to bait his slow, then immediately disengage. Only cast Magnet Storm if Zilean has already used Chronoshift, or target Zilean himself to prevent its cast.
laneImpact: Because jumping in blindly results in an immediate double bomb counter-stun, Rell cannot initiate trades freely. Zilean's duo will constantly push the wave using Time Bomb, forcing Rell under her tower where she takes poke. If Rell tries to use Full Tilt to run them down, Zilean simply uses Temporal Mirage to slow her down or speed his ADC away, neutralizing any aggressive pressure and bleeding Rell's health.
why: Rell's main engage tool, Ferromancy: Crashdown, is slow and highly predictable. Zilean can easily react to this telegraphed jump. By placing a double Time Bomb on her exact landing zone, he triggers an instant area-of-effect stun. Simultaneously, Zilean uses Temporal Mirage to speed up his carry, allowing them to effortlessly dodge Rell's knockup while locking Rell down in her slow, dismounted state.

summary: Master Yi can easily dodge Mordekaiser's Obliterate with Alpha Strike and melt him inside Realm of Death using the true damage from Wuju Style.
howToPlay: Never cast Obliterate or Death's Grasp proactively while Master Yi has his Alpha Strike available. Instead, clear camps with basic attacks and wait for him to commit his untargetability. Once he reappears, immediately pull him with Death's Grasp to disrupt his flow, then activate Indestructible to absorb his Wuju Style true damage burst. If forced to use Realm of Death, wait until he is locked in his Meditate channel to guarantee your full combo.
laneImpact: You cannot contest isolated river skirmishes or neutral camps directly against him, as he will scale much faster if he secures early gold. If you meet him in the river, his Highlander makes him immune to the slow from Darkness Rise, letting him run you down. This forces you to concede direct jungle pressure, slowing down your clear speed as you must path defensively to avoid deadly encounters.
why: In direct jungle skirmishes, Master Yi holds a massive mechanical advantage because his Alpha Strike allows him to effortlessly dodge the narrow slam of your Obliterate. Even if you trap him inside your Realm of Death, his Wuju Style bypasses your stolen defensive stats by dealing raw true damage, allowing him to quickly shred through your Indestructible shield.

summary: Milio can use Ultra Mega Fire Kick to knock Galio back during Justice Punch, and his Breath of Life completely cleanses Galio's Shield of Durand taunt.
howToPlay: To survive, you must play a patient waiting game. Never lead with Justice Punch unless you see Milio waste his Ultra Mega Fire Kick on minion clear or poke. Instead, use Winds of War to help your carry clear waves from safety. If Milio triggers his Breath of Life during a skirmish, immediately back off and delay your next engage; that ultimate has a massive cooldown window. Save your Hero's Entrance to counter-engage when the enemy overextends under your turret.
laneImpact: Consequently, aggressive lane presence is highly punishable. Standard trade attempts leave your ADC exposed, as Milio uses Cozy Campfire and Warm Hugs to trade back safely from distance while you retreat empty-handed. You cannot easily lock down the lane or secure early kills. This forces your bot lane under tower, slowly bleeding health to their ranged poke while you struggle to find a clean angle to crash the wave or roam.
why: This matchup is heavily dictated by Milio's ability to deny your primary engage tools. Whenever you attempt to close the distance using Justice Punch, Milio can easily interrupt your dash mid-air with Ultra Mega Fire Kick. Furthermore, even if you manage to bypass this knockback or flash in to channel a massive Shield of Durand, his Breath of Life instantly purges the taunt from his entire team, neutralizing your crowd control.

summary: Janna can use Eye of the Storm to absorb Glitterlance poke, while saving Howling Gale to disrupt Lulu's ADC if they try to follow up on Whimsy.
howToPlay: Position slightly behind your ADC to bait Lulu into aiming Glitterlance at them, allowing you to instantly shield them with Eye of the Storm. Never throw Howling Gale preemptively just to poke; save this whirlwind exclusively for when Lulu casts Whimsy on her ally to engage. If your ADC gets polymorphed by Whimsy, immediately cast Zephyr on the enemy carry to match their movement speed and disengage safely.
laneImpact: Because both of you possess heavy defensive tools, direct kills are rare. Instead, trading is defined by shield efficiency. If you mistime Eye of the Storm against Glitterlance, Lulu will slowly force you under turret, compromising your ADC's recall timings. However, if you successfully block her poke while keeping Howling Gale ready, you can prevent her from pushing the wave, keeping the lane perfectly centered.
why: This matchup is a pure enchanter standoff where neither side holds a natural advantage. Lulu relies on Help, Pix! and Glitterlance to chip away at your health, but you can neutralize this poke with a well-timed Eye of the Storm. The lane turns on how you react to Whimsy; holding onto Howling Gale is essential to shut down her carry's offensive push the moment they receive Lulu's buff.

summary: Akshan can easily poke Akali down with his Dirty Fighting passive and Avengerang, forcing her to give up early minion waves.
howToPlay: Maintain a slow-pushing wave and position yourself aggressively past her minion line to zone her out. Never use Heroic Swing forward unless she has already wasted her Shuriken Flip, as she can easily interrupt your flight. If she hides inside her Twilight Shroud, immediately step back and wait out the smoke rather than blindly chasing. Should she attempt to engage with Perfect Execution, use your Heroic Swing defensively to escape toward your tower.
laneImpact: This absolute range dominance allows you to dictate the wave's tempo from the first minute. By slow-pushing the initial waves, you force Akali to choose between losing precious health or sacrificing gold under her turret. This massive early pressure keeps her pinned down, starving her of resources and preventing her from securing the early roam priority she needs to get snowballing.
why: As a ranged marksman, you hold a massive early advantage over the melee assassin. Your double-shot passive, Dirty Fighting, combined with Avengerang, lets you constantly poke Akali whenever she steps up to last-hit. If she tries to retaliate with Five Point Strike, your Dirty Fighting shield absorbs her poke, ensuring you always win these short trades before she can even unlock Twilight Shroud.

summary: Morgana's Black Shield completely blocks Annie's Pyromania stun, rendering her primary engage and self-peel useless.
howToPlay: Your only play is to exploit the massive cooldown window of Black Shield. Never commit your Summon: Tibbers while her shield is active. Instead, use the extra movement speed from Molten Shield to bait out and dodge her Dark Binding. If she wastes her spell shield defensively, you have a brief opportunity to strike. Otherwise, focus entirely on farming safely with Disintegrate and wait for your jungler to burn her shield first before you attempt any stun setup.
laneImpact: You cannot contest Morgana's wave clear. She will constantly drop Tormented Shadow to shove you under turret, forcing you to use Disintegrate just to secure last hits. If you step up to retaliate, you risk getting caught by Dark Binding while your Molten Shield is down. This permanent pressure keeps you locked in mid lane, preventing you from roaming to assist your jungler.
why: Morgana completely shuts down your offensive threat because her Black Shield negates the stun from your Pyromania passive. Since your entire trading pattern and kill pressure rely on landing a stunned Summon: Tibbers or Incinerate, her spell shield renders your primary burst combo obsolete. Any attempt to engage is easily absorbed, leaving you vulnerable to her immediate counter-attack.

summary: Morgana's Black Shield completely blocks Annie's Pyromania stun, rendering her primary engage and self-peel useless.
howToPlay: Never cast Black Shield proactively; hold it until Annie actually casts her Pyromania-empowered spell. Watch her passive bar; when she has four stacks and moves forward, bait her throw, shield the impact, and immediately counter with Dark Binding and Tormented Shadow. If you miss your root or mistime the shield, quickly fall back using Soul Shackles to zone her and Tibbers away until your shield's cooldown recovers.
laneImpact: Because Annie cannot threaten you with a stun while your Black Shield is available, you can safely drop Tormented Shadow to shove her under tower. She is forced to waste Disintegrate to farm under turret instead of poking you. This pressure prevents her from roaming with Summon: Tibbers to help her jungler, locking her in mid lane while you safely scale and heal back any minor poke with Soul Siphon.
why: Your entire advantage stems from how Black Shield completely invalidates Annie's passive. When Annie builds up four charges of Pyromania, she relies on landing a stunned Disintegrate, Incinerate, or Summon: Tibbers to burst you down. By shielding yourself reactively to block that stun, you strip away her defensive self-peel and all her offensive threat, leaving her completely exposed to your counter-attack.

summary: Draven can easily run Jinx down with Blood Rush and Spinning Axe before she can scale or trigger Get Excited!.
howToPlay: To survive, you must manage your wave defensively to keep it just outside your turret range. Never use Flame Chompers! aggressively; hold them specifically to zone Draven or interrupt his pathing when he activates Blood Rush to chase you down. Use the long-range rocket form of Switcheroo! or the slow from Zap! to pick up distant minions safely. If he missteps or drops a Spinning Axe, only then can you briefly step forward to stabilize the wave.
laneImpact: This power disparity forces you into a defensive posture from the very first wave. Draven will use his high damage to freeze the wave near his tower or crash it to dive you. If you step up to last-hit, he will use Stand Aside to disrupt your retreat and chunk your health bar. This bleeding of gold and pressure prevents you from helping your jungler and invites heavy dive threat under your own turret.
why: Draven dominates this matchup because his early-game raw power dwarfs yours. By activating Blood Rush, he gains the mobility to close the gap instantly, hitting you with devastating Spinning Axe attacks. You cannot match this DPS in the early levels with Switcheroo!, and without an early takedown to trigger Get Excited!, you simply cannot outrun or out-trade his aggressive forward positioning.

summary: Rakan can bait out Light Binding and easily dodge it using Battle Dance, then immediately counter-engage with Grand Entrance.
howToPlay: To survive, you must discipline yourself to hold Light Binding. Use Lucent Singularity strictly to chip away at Fey Feathers, but never step up for basic attacks unless Rakan has already depleted his Battle Dance dashes. If he initiates with Grand Entrance without baiting your cage first, cast Light Binding directly onto his landing indicator to lock him down mid-dash, and cast Prismatic Barrier to protect your carry from any follow-up burst.
laneImpact: This constant threat of a counter-engage severely limits your lane pressure. Missing your root means giving up control of the brush, as Rakan can easily force trades using Grand Entrance or even The Quickness. You cannot safely step up to trigger Illumination with basic attacks, and Rakan's Fey Feathers combined with Gleaming Quill allows his duo to easily heal back any minor poke from Lucent Singularity.
why: Rakan excels at neutralizing your crowd control because of his extreme mobility. When you throw Light Binding, he can reactively activate Battle Dance to dash to his ally, effortlessly dodging your root while shielding his partner. With your primary defensive tool on cooldown, he is free to instantly turn the fight around by launching himself forward with Grand Entrance, catching you completely unprotected.

summary: Kassadin can negate Ahri's poke with the magic shield from Null Sphere, safely scaling until his Riftwalk out-values her mobility.
howToPlay: Never throw Charm when Kassadin has Riftwalk ready, as he will easily blink over it to burst you. Instead, slow-push the early waves and hold Orb of Deception to punish him only when his Null Sphere is on cooldown. If he freezes the wave near his tower, stop trying to trade; use Fox-Fire to quickly crash the minions and look to roam with your jungler before he reaches his scaling spikes.
laneImpact: Because Null Sphere shrugs off your trades, you cannot easily force Kassadin out of lane. You must focus on shoving him under tower with Orb of Deception to exploit his weak early waveclear before he gets Force Pulse charges. If you fail to lock the wave, he scales for free. Eventually, his Riftwalk roam pressure forces you to stay glued to your mid turret, losing all priority for river skirmishes.
why: Your magic poke with Orb of Deception and Fox-Fire is constantly absorbed by the magic shield Kassadin gains from casting Null Sphere. While Essence Theft offers you some lane sustain, it cannot match his passive scaling. Once he unlocks Riftwalk, his zero-cooldown blinks completely outclass the mobility of your Spirit Rush, turning what was once a safe distance into a lethal zone where he easily dodges Charm.

summary: Jhin can easily shove Vayne under turret using Dancing Grenade and poke her down while she struggles to last-hit.
howToPlay: Push the wave aggressively using Dancing Grenade on dying minions to maximize the bounce damage onto Vayne. Stand near the center of the lane to avoid giving her an easy angle to stun you against the walls with Condemn. If she attempts to farm under her turret, prep a Deadly Flourish to root her when she pauses to strike. Once she is low and trapped, retreat slightly to safely unleash Curtain Call.
laneImpact: This matchup translates into total wave control for you. By constantly shoving waves into her turret with Dancing Grenade, you force Vayne to focus on difficult last-hitting under tower. This pressure denies her the freedom to trigger Silver Bolts on you. You will easily secure early tower plates and keep her trapped, preventing her from using Night Hunter to chase you down.
why: Your massive range advantage dictates this matchup. Vayne is a short-ranged hunter who must step forward to last-hit, making her extremely vulnerable to the bouncing bounces of your Dancing Grenade. As she tries to farm under pressure, your Whisper fourth shot deals chunking damage she cannot trade back. Her Tumble is simply too short to close the distance without taking massive damage.

summary: Braum's Unbreakable can block Nami's Tidal Wave entirely, but he remains vulnerable to her ground-targeted Aqua Prison bubble.
howToPlay: Never activate Unbreakable preemptively just to block Nami's basic attacks. Instead, save your shield specifically for Tidal Wave when her ultimate is up. When she throws Aqua Prison, use Stand Behind Me to leap to a minion or your ADC to dodge the circular impact zone. Once her bubble is on cooldown, immediately look to engage with Glacial Fissure to lock her down before she can heal her ally.
laneImpact: During the laning phase, Nami will constantly attempt to poke your ADC using Ebb and Flow and Tidecaller's Blessing. To match her tempo, you must threaten with Winter's Bite without exposing yourself to her bubble. If she misses Aqua Prison, her pressure vanishes, allowing you to walk up, trigger Concussive Blows, and force her to retreat or burn her ultimate defensively.
why: This skill matchup hinges on how you position your shield. While Unbreakable completely absorbs Nami's Tidal Wave, neutralizing her primary engage or disengage tool, it offers absolutely no protection against Aqua Prison. Because her bubble is a ground-targeted area-of-effect spell rather than a standard projectile, Nami can easily bypass your shield to stun you directly if you stand still while blocking her wave.

summary: Jax can use Leap Strike to close the gap on Kayle and Counter Strike to block her ranged basic attacks before she can scale.
howToPlay: Start trading heavily at level one or two. Walk up to the wave to force her back, saving Leap Strike for when she tries to disengage with Celestial Blessing. Activate Counter Strike mid-air or right after landing to absorb her Starfire Spellblade retaliations. If she plays extremely safe under turret, do not force a dive if she has Divine Judgment ready; instead, freeze the wave near your tower and zone her completely from XP range.
laneImpact: This matchup creates immense early pressure. You can zone Kayle off the first waves since her Radiant Blast cannot stop your aggressive leaps. Because she cannot contest your wave control, you can stack slow pushes, crash them, and dive her before she gains range. Kayle is forced to use Celestial Blessing defensively, draining her mana and locking her in a miserable, low-resource lane.
why: Jax completely dictates this matchup because Kayle relies entirely on her basic attacks from Starfire Spellblade to farm and poke. Before she reaches her high-level passive evolutions, Jax can easily bypass her kiting. By pairing Leap Strike to instantly close the distance with Counter Strike to negate all her physical DPS, Jax nullifies her early trading power and forces her under tower.

summary: Use Decimate while Jax is spinning Counter Strike to heal and deal damage without relying on basic attacks.
howToPlay: When Jax activates Counter Strike to stun you, do not run away immediately in a straight line. Instead, swing Decimate while he is spinning his lantern. This guarantees the outer-edge blade damage and heals you, bypassing his physical dodge. Save Apprehend for after his Leap Strike is spent; if he tries to disengage after a trade, pull him back to force a longer fight once his defensive cooldown is gone, allowing you to finally stack Hemorrhage and execute with Noxian Guillotine.
laneImpact: Jax will constantly threaten to jump on you with Leap Strike when his Counter Strike is ready, forcing you to play defensively near your turret. You cannot easily freeze the wave because if he activates his Evasion, you must retreat, giving up priority. Trades are short and sharp; if he blocks your Crippling Strike, you lose the trade immediately and risk being chased down by his Grandmaster-at-Arms passive.
why: Jax has the upper hand because his Counter Strike completely denies your basic attacks and Crippling Strike, halting your Hemorrhage stacks. Since his passive Relentless Assault ramps up his attack speed rapidly, a straight auto-attack duel is suicidal. Your saving grace is that Counter Strike cannot block Decimate, allowing you to bypass his evasion if you space correctly.

summary: Poppy's ability to block dashes completely shuts down Xin Zhao's Audacious Charge, preventing him from engaging or reaching his marked targets.
howToPlay: To survive this matchup, you must alter your skirmish approach. Never lead with Audacious Charge. Instead, walk directly into melee range to strike with Three Talon Strike, forcing Poppy to decide whether to activate her barrier prematurely. Use Wind Becomes Lightning purely for its slow to help you close the gap on foot. If forced into a teamfight, use Crescent Guard to knock her away before attempting to charge her allies.
laneImpact: This interaction severely cripples your early skirmishing and ganking pressure. If Poppy counter-ganks, she renders your engage useless, leaving your targets completely safe. You lose the ability to contest Scuttle Crabs or secure early objectives because she can zone you away from the pit. This forces you into a passive farming style, giving her team free reign over the map lanes while you fall behind in pressure.
why: The jungle matchup hinges entirely on how Poppy's dash-blocking barrier neutralizes your primary gap-closer. When you attempt to close the distance on an enemy marked by Wind Becomes Lightning, Poppy can activate her zone to instantly interrupt Audacious Charge. This interruption knocks you down, leaving you stranded, unable to reach your target to unleash Three Talon Strike or benefit from Determination healing.

summary: Gnar can use Hop to dodge Sett's Facebreaker or jump out of the true damage zone of Haymaker.
howToPlay: Never initiate with Facebreaker while Gnar has his jump available. Instead, bait out Boomerang Throw, walk forward to threaten him, and wait for him to panic-cast Hop. Once his jump is on its long cooldown, you have a brief window to force a trade using Knuckle Down to catch him, followed by Facebreaker. If he transforms, use The Show Stopper to redirect his Boulder Toss engage away from your tower.
laneImpact: This dynamic forces you into a defensive stance where Gnar commands wave priority. You will constantly absorb poke while trying to last-hit under your turret, slowly building up your Pit Grit passive but unable to convert it into aggressive trades. If Gnar mismanages his Rage Gene and transforms into Mega Gnar, the lane shifts to melee, but your window to punish him is strictly limited to when his Hop is on cooldown.
why: Mini Gnar maintains a constant spacing advantage using Boomerang Throw to slow you, while Hyper provides him bursts of speed. Whenever you attempt to close the distance with Knuckle Down, Gnar can reactively use Hop to bounce away. This single mobility tool allows him to effortlessly dodge your Facebreaker pull or escape the high-damage center of your Haymaker, leaving you exposed without any retaliation.

summary: Leona must abuse Senna's weak early game by engaging with Zenith Blade whenever Senna steps up to collect souls.
howToPlay: Position aggressively in the lane bushes to hide your Zenith Blade animation and deny Senna’s vision. Watch the souls dropping from dying minions; as soon as Senna moves toward one, launch your Zenith Blade. If she misses Last Embrace or wastes Piercing Darkness on the wave, immediately force the all-in. Should you miss your engage, activate Eclipse and back off defensively to absorb any retaliatory poke while your cooldowns recover.
laneImpact: This threat completely stifles Senna’s early game scaling. She cannot safely step up to harvest souls or poke with Piercing Darkness without risking a lethal engage. Consequently, her lane partner is left without reliable support pressure, allowing your duo to control the wave, crash it for easy recall timings, and safely rush level five to unlock Solar Flare, sealing your lane dominance before Senna can acquire significant range.
why: Senna's passive soul-harvesting mechanic forces her into predictable, static animations when she tries to collect Mist. This vulnerability is Leona's primary window. By firing Zenith Blade the moment Senna pauses to strike a soul or cast Piercing Darkness, you bypass her ranged advantage. Following up with Shield of Daybreak and Eclipse detonates Sunlight marks, instantly melting her fragile health pool before she can activate Curse of the Black Mist to escape.

summary: Caitlyn can punish Ezreal with Headshot autos when he steps up to farm, but she must place Yordle Snap Trap behind him to catch his Arcane Shift trajectory.
howToPlay: When Ezreal steps up for a minion, immediately punish him with a Headshot auto-attack. Crucially, do not throw Yordle Snap Trap directly under him; instead, place it slightly behind his position to intercept his natural Arcane Shift retreat path. If he blinks into your trap, follow up instantly with Piltover Peacemaker. Always stand behind your own minion wave to block his Mystic Shot, and hold 90 Caliber Net exclusively to disengage if he attempts an aggressive forward blink.
laneImpact: This matchup becomes a tedious poke war where Ezreal tries to thin the wave with Mystic Shot and Trueshot Barrage to prevent Caitlyn from shoving. If Caitlyn fails to pressure him, Ezreal safely scales, reducing her tower-taking power. Missing a Piltover Peacemaker allows Ezreal to aggressively blink forward with Arcane Shift and land an Essence Flux combo, forcing Caitlyn to retreat with 90 Caliber Net and lose lane priority.
why: Ezreal's constant Mystic Shot spam from range outpaces Caitlyn's poke if she plays passively. While Caitlyn's Headshot gives her a massive auto-attack trading tool when Ezreal walks up to farm, his Arcane Shift allows him to easily escape or reposition away from her skillshots. To win trades, Caitlyn must exploit the window when his Arcane Shift is on cooldown, as his Rising Spell Force makes extended duels dangerous.

summary: Rammus's Defensive Ball Curl deals massive damage back to Graves because each individual pellet from New Destiny triggers the thorn damage.
howToPlay: Pivot your build entirely towards heavy armor to maximize the lethal feedback of Defensive Ball Curl and Rolling Armordillo. When hunting Graves in his jungle, roll in with Powerball but do not instantly use your crowd control. Wait for him to panic and use Quickdraw to dash away, then immediately lock him down with Frenzying Taunt. If he drops Smoke Screen to blind you, activate Soaring Slam to slow his escape and keep him within your thorns.
laneImpact: Graves cannot safely contest any scuttle crabs or invade your camps. His usual aggressive dueling is neutralized because his Quickdraw armor stacks do nothing against your magic damage return. He is forced to waste Smoke Screen defensively to escape your rollouts. This absolute dominance allows you to steal his raptors, secure early drakes without contest, and dive his laners under their own towers with impunity.
why: Rammus completely neutralizes Graves due to a devastating interaction between their core kits. Graves's basic attacks from New Destiny fire multiple pellets per shot. When you activate Defensive Ball Curl, every single one of those individual pellets triggers your thorn damage return. This means Graves melts his own health bar instantly whenever he attempts to kite or duel you, especially as Rolling Armordillo scales your damage with armor.

summary: Jinx's Flame Chompers! can be placed in Akshan's swing path to immediately stop his Heroic Swing and set up an easy kill.
howToPlay: Never throw Flame Chompers! aggressively; always hold them as a defensive tool specifically to counter Heroic Swing. Position yourself near the center of the lane, away from walls where Akshan can easily anchor his grapple. If he commits to a swing, place your traps directly in his path of rotation to snare him mid-air. Once he is rooted, swap to Switcheroo! minigun to burst him down, and use Zap! to prevent his escape.
laneImpact: This matchup becomes a race for wave control. Akshan uses Avengerang to quickly clear minions, looking to crash the wave and roam using Going Rogue. If you let him shove you under turret, he will dive you or poke you safely. You must use Switcheroo! rocket form to actively match his clear, preventing him from gaining the tempo needed to execute his aggressive rotations.
why: Akshan dominates the early game because his Dirty Fighting shield and double-shot passive make short trades highly unfavorable for you. He easily pushes with Avengerang to create priority. Yet, his primary mobility, Heroic Swing, is entirely linear and predictable. If he attempts to dive or escape using his grapple, throwing Flame Chompers! directly into his flight path instantly interrupts his movement, grounding him for a deadly retaliation.

summary: Jinx has no defensive mobility, making her an incredibly easy target for Enchanted Crystal Arrow to set up guaranteed kills for your support or jungler.
howToPlay: Keep the wave shoved using Ranger's Focus to match her rocket clear, forcing Jinx to burn mana. Always hold Enchanted Crystal Arrow for when Jinx steps up to last-hit with Switcheroo! or tries to throw Zap!, which briefly roots her in place. If she drops Flame Chompers! defensively, simply walk around them while applying Frost Shot slows. Coordinate with your support to chain CC the moment your arrow connects.
laneImpact: You dictate the tempo by keeping the minion wave crashing. Jinx wants to use Switcheroo! rocket form to clear waves, but doing so drains her mana and exposes her to your Volley poke. Constantly pushing her under tower forces her to farm awkwardly. This pressure prevents her from activating Get Excited! off early skirmishes, keeping her trapped while your jungler gets free ganks.
why: Ashe's ability to consistently slow Jinx with Frost Shot and poke with Volley strips away her spacing control. Because Jinx lacks any defensive mobility or dashes, she relies entirely on perfect positioning. Once you reach level five, Jinx has no built-in tools to dodge Enchanted Crystal Arrow. A single hit from this global ultimate guarantees a kill, as Jinx cannot escape the follow-up crowd control.

summary: Braum's Unbreakable can block the roots from Maokai's Nature's Grasp ultimate, protecting his entire team behind him.
howToPlay: Always position yourself slightly ahead of your carry, but keep Stand Behind Me ready to adjust your angle instantly. When Maokai throws Nature's Grasp, do not panic-cast; wait for the roots to get close, then activate Unbreakable facing the incoming wave to absorb it. If he jumps in with Twisted Advance, immediately hit him with Winter's Bite to apply Concussive Blows, turning his aggressive engage into an easy stun and a free kill for your team.
laneImpact: Maokai's bush pressure with Sapling Toss is heavily mitigated because you can step up safely. He cannot easily force fights on your carry because any attempt to use Twisted Advance puts him in melee range, where you retaliate with Winter's Bite and quick auto-attacks. This keeps the wave dynamic in your favor, allowing your duo to maintain lane priority and secure clean recalls without fear of sudden all-ins.
why: Maokai relies on massive crowd control to lock down your team, but your kit completely neutralizes his primary engage. When Maokai casts Nature's Grasp, your Unbreakable shield acts as a mobile wall that intercepts the entire wave of roots. This prevents the crowd control from reaching your carry, rendering his ultimate useless while allowing you to easily trigger Concussive Blows on him when he tries to follow up with Twisted Advance.

summary: Kalista's constant hopping via Martial Poise makes it exceptionally difficult for Corki to land his Phosphorus Bomb and Missile Barrage rockets.
howToPlay: To survive, adopt a strict safety-first positioning rule. Do not throw Phosphorus Bomb randomly; instead, wait for her to lock herself into her basic attack animation to secure the hit. Keep Gatling Gun active during her short-range hops to shred her armor without needing precise aim. Most importantly, never use Valkyrie offensively unless her Fate's Call is completely down, and save your Package to disengage from her support's knock-up rather than initiating.
laneImpact: You will find yourself constantly pushed under turret because missing Phosphorus Bomb on Kalista means you forfeit control of the minion wave. She can easily trade while you miss, stacking spears with Rend to force you out of lane or secure early drakes. If you try to match her push, she can engage with Fate's Call, leaving you with no choice but to burn Valkyrie defensively, sacrificing your Package pressure.
why: Kalista's passive, Martial Poise, completely disrupts your offensive rhythm. Every time she executes a basic attack, she hops, making her an incredibly slippery target. This constant, unpredictable movement makes landing your main poke tools, Phosphorus Bomb and Missile Barrage, highly unreliable. Because your damage profile heavily relies on hitting these skillshots to chunk her down before fights, her innate mobility nullifies your primary laning pressure.

summary: Fizz can use Playful to dodge Akali's Shuriken Flip or the execution damage of Perfect Execution.
howToPlay: To win this, never initiate with Shuriken Flip. Instead, harass him with Five Point Strike and trigger Assassin's Mark when he steps up to farm. If Fizz throws Chum the Waters, immediately drop Twilight Shroud to prevent him from targeting you with Urchin Strike. Only activate the execution of Perfect Execution once you see him land from Playful. If he holds his jump, rely on your passive basic attacks to force it out first.
laneImpact: In lane, this creates a tense standoff where neither can easily clear waves without exposing themselves. If you use Five Point Strike to push, Fizz will punish you with Urchin Strike and Rending Wave. Trades are short and explosive. Post-level 5, the threat of Chum the Waters means you must hold Twilight Shroud to survive his all-in, making wave control a secondary concern to health preservation.
why: This matchup is a pure skill-based assassin duel defined by how Fizz uses Playful against your burst. Because both of you are melee AP threats, the lane remains perfectly even until one commits. If Fizz manages to dodge Shuriken Flip or the second dash of Perfect Execution using his untargetability, he wins the trade. Conversely, if you bait his jump, your high base damage will overwhelm him.

summary: Lee Sin can easily waste Tryndamere's Undying Rage duration by knocking him away with Dragon's Rage and dashing away with Safeguard.
howToPlay: To survive this match, never initiate fights with Spinning Slash; save it to close the gap after he uses Safeguard or to escape over a wall if he kicks you away. Only commit to a deep duel if you can catch him with Mocking Shout when his back is turned, slowing his escape. If he still has Dragon's Rage available, focus on farming your jungle and counter-ganking rather than seeking isolated fights.
laneImpact: In the jungle, this interaction ruins your ability to contest neutral camps or force duels in the river. You cannot safely invade his camps because any attempt to run him down with Spinning Slash will be met with Sonic Wave to escape or Dragon's Rage to peel you off. This forces you into a defensive farming pattern, giving him free rein to pressure your lanes while you struggle to find proactive plays.
why: Lee Sin completely neutralizes your ultimate pressure through his supreme disengage tools. The moment you activate Undying Rage to survive a close duel, he can immediately cast Dragon's Rage to launch you far away, then follow up with Safeguard to hop to a position out of reach. This combination burns through your precious five seconds of invincibility without letting you land a single auto-attack, leaving you helpless and dying.

summary: Rammus's Defensive Ball Curl heavily punishes Pantheon's empowered Shield Vault triple-strike, turning Pantheon's own burst against him.
howToPlay: Shift your build away from pure lethality toward heavy armor penetration and health. During skirmishes, never initiate with Shield Vault unless Rammus has already wasted Defensive Ball Curl. Instead, poke from distance with Comet Spear to chip his health. If he charges at you with Powerball, intercept him with Aegis Assault facing his direction to absorb the impact and block the immediate follow-up damage, then use Grand Starfall to counter-gank his map plays rather than fighting him head-on.
laneImpact: You lose all early 1v1 agency in the river and cannot contest objectives or Scuttle Crabs directly. If Rammus intercepts you with Powerball, his Frenzying Taunt forces you to auto-attack his spiked shell, guaranteeing you lose the duel. This map-wide pressure forces you to play reactively, conceding early neutral camps and leaving your lanes vulnerable to his high-speed ganks while you struggle to safely clear your camps.
why: Your main engage tool backfires horribly here. When you use your empowered Shield Vault via Mortal Will, the rapid triple-strike hits Rammus while his Defensive Ball Curl is active. Instead of shredding him, this interaction triggers his armor-scaled damage reflection three times instantly, melting your own health bar. His passive Rolling Armordillo further amplifies this self-destructive burst, turning your core assassination tool into a suicide button.

summary: Yone can use Soul Unbound to cleanse or dodge Varus's Chain of Corruption by snapping back to his original body.
howToPlay: To survive, you must play strictly around his Mortal Steel charges. When his wind is active, step back and use Piercing Arrow to farm from maximum distance. Never cast Chain of Corruption proactively while his Soul Unbound is available. Instead, hold your ultimate until his spirit return animation is forced, or use Hail of Arrows to slow him down as he runs at you. If he dives with Fate Sealed, flash immediately rather than trying to outplay his burst.
laneImpact: You are forced into a defensive posture from the very first waves. Yone's threat of a Soul Unbound trade means you cannot safely step up to auto-attack minions to trigger Living Vengeance. He easily gains priority by zoning you with Mortal Steel tornados. Under your turret, he will constantly chip your health down using Spirit Cleave, forcing bad recall timings and rendering you unable to assist your jungler.
why: This lane is exceptionally difficult because your ultimate defense, Chain of Corruption, is completely neutralized by Yone's kit. When Yone engages using Soul Unbound, he can simply snap back to his starting point to cleanse or completely dodge the spreading root of your ultimate. Without this crowd control to keep him at bay, you are left defenseless against his raw gap-closing burst via Mortal Steel and Fate Sealed.

summary: Ambessa can use Repudiation to block the displacement of Lee Sin's Dragon's Rage if she anticipates the kick.
howToPlay: When dueling Lee Sin, never waste Repudiation early to block his Sonic Wave or Tempest damage. Instead, use Drakehound's Step and Lacerate to dance around his skillshots, saving your shield specifically for the animation of Dragon's Rage. If he tries to dash away using Safeguard, immediately lock him down with Public Execution to shut down his escape routes. If you miss your timing, retreat instantly and wait for your cooldowns to recover before contesting.
laneImpact: In the jungle, this mechanical deadlock prevents either of you from forcing reckless invades. Skirmishes around river crab or early skirmishes are incredibly tense; whoever misses their key spell first loses pressure. If you mistime Repudiation against his Dragon's Rage, Lee Sin will launch you away, secure the objective, and escape. Conversely, blocking his kick halts his momentum, turning the tide of 2v2 skirmishes and securing neutral monster control.
why: This jungle matchup is a high-speed mobility duel entirely dictated by split-second reactions. Lee Sin relies on landing Sonic Wave to initiate or execute, but the ultimate swing factor is how you time Repudiation. If you anticipate his Dragon's Rage, you can completely absorb the displacement of his kick, leaving him vulnerable at close range where your Drakehound's Step dashes can easily outmaneuver his attempts to escape with Safeguard.

summary: Irelia can easily stun you with Flawless Duet while you are channeling Breath of Light, then execute you with Bladesurge resets.
howToPlay: To survive, you must establish a strict positioning rule: never use Breath of Light unless Irelia has already wasted Flawless Duet. Keep the minion wave permanently frozen just outside your turret range to prevent her Bladesurge dash chains. If she dives you with Vanguard's Edge, immediately use Astral Flight to fly backward toward your second turret, rather than trying to fight back with Falling Star, which she can easily reduce with Defiant Dance.
laneImpact: This threat forces you to play completely passive, conceding lane priority from the first wave. You cannot safely collect Cosmic Creator stacks using Breath of Light on minions because Irelia will jump on marked targets with Bladesurge. Every attempt to clear with Singularity will push the wave, exposing you to her Vanguard's Edge engage far from your turret.
why: Irelia represents an absolute nightmare for Aurelion Sol due to how your primary damage tool works. When you stand still to channel Breath of Light, you become a stationary target. This makes it trivial for Irelia to land Flawless Duet to stun you. Once stunned, your channel is broken, and she can instantly close the gap and execute you with relentless Bladesurge resets.

summary: Jax can use Counter Strike to block Sett's Knuckle Down empowered attacks, then use Leap Strike to dodge the true damage center of Haymaker.
howToPlay: To survive, you must bait out Counter Strike without committing your own spells. Walk up to simulate an engage, then immediately walk away. Only activate Knuckle Down after his spin ends. If he jumps on you with Leap Strike, use Facebreaker immediately to pull him in and interrupt his flow, forcing a raw trade where your basic attacks can actually connect. Never throw Haymaker until he has spent his leap.
laneImpact: Because of this defensive advantage, Jax can walk up to slow-push waves or freeze them near his tower. You cannot contest short trades safely; every time you walk up to secure a minion, he threatens to initiate with Counter Strike. This forces you to drop CS or take heavy damage, leading to an early HP deficit that ruins your first recall timing and forces you under turret.
why: Jax controls this matchup because Counter Strike completely nullifies your primary trade tool, Knuckle Down, denying your Pit Grit progression. If you try to retaliate with Haymaker once the stun wears off, he can easily use Leap Strike to jump onto a minion or behind you, completely avoiding the true damage center. This leaves you with wasted cooldowns and zero trade power.

summary: Talon can match your Astral Flight map rotations by jumping over walls with Assassin's Path to ambush you.
howToPlay: Never initiate an Astral Flight rotation unless Talon is visible elsewhere. Instead, drop Singularity on the wave from a safe distance and harvest Cosmic Creator stacks under tower. If Talon jumps you with Noxian Diplomacy, drop Falling Star directly on yourself to disrupt his Blade's End proc, then use your flight toward the safety of your tier-two turret rather than over side-walls where Assassin's Path allows him to hunt you down.
laneImpact: Because Talon clears quickly with Rake, he will constantly disappear into the river. You cannot safely contest his movements with Astral Flight without risking a deadly face-check. This forces you to play defensively under your turret, using Singularity to hold the wave, while your side lanes suffer from his constant, unreactable pressure since you cannot safely match his rotations.
why: Your map influence relies entirely on using Astral Flight to bypass terrain, but Talon's Assassin's Path makes him the ultimate counter-roamer. He can easily match your flight trajectory by vaulting over the jungle walls. This turns your rotation into a death trap, as he can intercept you mid-way or ambush you at your destination with Shadow Assault before you can even land.

summary: Akshan can easily dodge Jhin's Curtain Call or Deadly Flourish using Heroic Swing, then close the distance to burst him down.
howToPlay: To survive, you must hold Deadly Flourish as a pure self-defense tool rather than an offensive opener. Only cast it if Akshan has already committed his Heroic Swing and its trajectory is locked. Position yourself strictly in the center of the lane, far from the walls to limit his grapple angles. If he tries to dive you, force him to swing into a pre-placed Captive Audience trap to slow his momentum and disrupt his burst.
laneImpact: This interaction forces you into a highly defensive posture under your own turret. Because Akshan can use Going Rogue to approach stealthily and Heroic Swing to engage from unpredictable angles, you cannot safely push the wave with Dancing Grenade. If you step past the river, one bad trade means he can dive you or execute you with Comeuppance if you try to retreat with low health.
why: Akshan's high mobility completely neutralizes Jhin's long-range setup. Whenever you try to lock him down with Deadly Flourish or open up with Curtain Call, he can immediately activate Heroic Swing to swing off a wall, dodging the projectile entirely. Once he evades your crowd control, he uses that momentum to close the gap and unleash his high burst damage, leaving Jhin with no escape tools.

summary: Gragas can interrupt Ornn's Bellows Breath brittle application or Searing Charge dash using Body Slam.
howToPlay: To win this stalemate, bait out his Body Slam before committing to a hard trade. Position yourself near your Volcanic Rupture pillar but do not immediately cast Searing Charge; wait to see if he panics and charges first. If he uses Body Slam offensively, you have a clear fifteen-second window to retaliate with Bellows Breath and Call of the Forge God to chunk him down. If he holds his displacement, simply focus on farming and out-scaling.
laneImpact: Gragas will constantly throw Barrel Roll to slow your push and chip away at your health bar. If you recklessly use Volcanic Rupture and attempt to engage, a quick Body Slam into Drunken Rage leaves you taking heavy magic damage without being able to trade back. The lane becomes a slow, methodical chess match where whoever wastes their primary movement tool first loses control of the minion wave.
why: This matchup is a war of attrition where Gragas relies on Happy Hour to heal back your poke, while you use Living Forge to stay in lane without recalling. The critical pivot is Gragas using Body Slam to cancel your Searing Charge mid-dash or disrupt you right as Bellows Breath applies Brittle. Because Body Slam has priority over your charge, he can completely deny your knock-up setup and winning trades.

summary: Olaf's Ragnarok completely ignores the knockback of Keeper's Verdict and the stun of Heroic Charge, allowing him to easily run Poppy down.
howToPlay: To survive, your primary positioning rule is to hug your turret and use Iron Ambassador from maximum range to secure minions. Keep Steadfast Presence ready solely for the passive armor boost when low on health, rather than trying to block non-existent dashes. If Olaf freezes the wave or dives you with Ragnarok active, do not fight back; instead, use the movement speed from Steadfast Presence to run behind your tower and wait out his ultimate's duration.
laneImpact: This immunity transforms the lane into a constant zone of danger where you cannot safely contest waves. If you step up to farm, Olaf can fish for an Undertow slow and run you down with Reckless Swing. Since you cannot peel him off with Keeper's Verdict after level six, any extended trade results in your death, forcing you to bleed gold under tower while he freely pressures your plate armor.
why: Poppy relies heavily on locking down targets against walls or peeling with her ultimate, but Olaf completely shuts this down. Once Olaf activates Ragnarok, he becomes entirely immune to crowd control, meaning your Heroic Charge cannot stun him and Keeper's Verdict fails to knock him back. Combined with his Undertow slowing you repeatedly, your defensive tools are nullified, leaving you defenseless against his raw true damage.

summary: Maokai can use Bramble Smash (Q) to knock Rell back mid-air during her jump engage, completely canceling her crowd control.
howToPlay: To survive this matchup, you must bait out his primary peel tool before leaping. Instead of leading with your jump, use the movement speed from Full Tilt to threaten a close-range stun, forcing him to make a decision. Only cast Ferromancy: Crashdown once you see Bramble Smash go on cooldown. If Maokai initiates first with Twisted Advance, immediately counter-engage with Magnet Storm to pull him away from your carry, turning his own forward dive against him.
laneImpact: This reaction-based shutdown strips away your lane pressure, forcing you to play defensively. You cannot contest bush control because Maokai safely zones you out with Sapling Toss, and any aggressive forward movement risks getting locked down by Twisted Advance. Consequently, you are pushed under your turret, losing priority for river skirmishes and leaving your carry exposed to heavy poke while you wait for the wave to crash.
why: Maokai completely neutralizes your primary initiation tools through reactive disruption. The moment you commit to the sky with Ferromancy: Crashdown, he can instantly deploy Bramble Smash to knock you back mid-flight. This cancels your knock-up entirely, stranding you in your slow, dismounted form. Because your main crowd control is so easily interrupted, you cannot easily trigger Break the Mold, leaving you extremely vulnerable while his Sap Magic keeps him sustained.

summary: Wukong can use Warrior Trickster to absorb Viego's Spectral Maw stun, leaving Viego vulnerable to a Cyclone follow-up.
howToPlay: To survive, never lead with Spectral Maw when invading or defending. Instead, mask your presence inside Harrowed Path and use the bonus attack speed to strike with Blade of the Ruined King first. Force Wukong to panic-use Warrior Trickster under pressure. Once his decoy fades, you have a brief window to unleash your fully charged stun. If he initiates with his ultimate, use Heartbreaker defensively to hop over a wall and reset.
laneImpact: This interaction strips away your early skirmishing power around the Scuttle Crabs and jungle camps. Knowing he can block your stun, Wukong will confidently invade your territory with Nimbus Strike. You cannot easily contest neutral objectives or secure double-scuttle because missing your stun means giving him a free path to ultimate setups. This forces you to play defensively, ceding early map pressure and delaying your gold spikes.
why: Wukong's ability to completely negate your primary crowd control dictates this duel. When you charge Spectral Maw to initiate or peel, Wukong can deploy Warrior Trickster to leave a clone in his place, absorbing the projectile stun entirely. With your only crowd control wasted on a decoy, he can immediately counter-engage with Cyclone to knock you up, using his passive Stone Skin to easily win the extended physical trade.

summary: Varus's Hail of Arrows applies Grievous Wounds, severely cutting Vladimir's Transfusion healing during trades.
howToPlay: Watch Vladimir's resource bar closely; when it turns red, signaling an empowered Transfusion, instantly cast Hail of Arrows on his target to nullify his massive heal. Never throw Chain of Corruption raw while his Sanguine Pool is available, as he will easily dodge the root. Instead, force his pool with basic attacks empowered by Blighted Quiver, then lock him down with your ultimate once he resurfaces.
laneImpact: This healing deficit completely alters the trading dynamic in mid. Vladimir cannot safely pool his health with Tides of Blood because he cannot recover the cost. You can comfortably freeze the wave or shove him under turret, using Blighted Quiver stacks popped by Piercing Arrow to chip away at his HP pool. He is forced into defensive, early recalls, giving you ultimate priority to assist your jungler.
why: Vladimir's entire laning phase revolves around sustaining through poke using Transfusion. As Varus, you completely shut down this game plan because Hail of Arrows inflicts Grievous Wounds on demand. Whenever he steps up to drain a minion or trade with you, dropping the rain of arrows cuts his healing in half, allowing your physical attacks and Piercing Arrow snipes to permanently stick and force him out of lane.

summary: Block Urgot's Disdain flip with Repudiation to deny him his shield and positioning advantage, then shred him with Cunning Sweep.
howToPlay: To survive, you must play defensively and strictly hold Disdain as a disengage tool rather than an offensive opener. Use Corrosive Charge from a safe distance to slow her down and farm safely, forcing her to burn her energy. If she wastes Repudiation aggressively, you have a brief window to fight back using Purge. Finally, never fire Fear Beyond Death unless her spell-blocking shield is completely on cooldown, ensuring your execution connects.
laneImpact: Because your primary defensive tool is so easily neutralized, you cannot safely contest early waves. Your passive Echoing Flames naturally pushes the minion wave, leaving you overextended. If Ambessa freezes the wave near her turret, any attempt to break it with Purge exposes you to a deadly chase where her Drakehound's Step lets her dance around your shotgun legs, forcing early recalls or dive setups.
why: This matchup hinges entirely on how Ambessa responds to your main engage. Whenever you attempt to dash forward with Disdain, she can easily activate Repudiation to absorb the impact, nullify your flip's crowd control, and deny your shield. Left exposed in melee range without your displacement, you become an easy target for her Cunning Sweep slash and slam, allowing her to easily out-trade you.

summary: Annie can easily sidestep Brand's Pillar of Flame using the movement speed from Molten Shield, then retaliate with a guaranteed stun combo.
howToPlay: To survive, you must play with extreme patience. Never lead a trade with Pillar of Flame; instead, wait for Annie to waste Molten Shield before throwing it, or cast it exactly when she locks herself in her Disintegrate animation. Keep a constant eye on her Pyromania tracker. If she activates her stun and rushes you, prepare a defensive Conflagration into Sear combination to stun her mid-stride and disengage immediately.
laneImpact: This reaction speed difference forces you into a defensive posture, surrendering mid-lane priority. Annie can safely farm and manage the wave using Disintegrate while holding her stun threat. If you step up too far to clear minions with Conflagration, she can instantly drop Summon: Tibbers to delete your health bar, forcing you to recall prematurely or lose massive chunks of tower plating.
why: Annie counters your poke pattern because the instant movement speed from her Molten Shield allows her to easily sidestep your Pillar of Flame. The moment you miss this crucial spell, she can aggressively close the gap. With her Pyromania passive fully charged, she will immediately lock you down with Disintegrate or Incinerate, leaving you completely vulnerable to her full burst combo without any way to fight back.

summary: Land the outer edge of Decimate to out-heal Mordekaiser's passive damage inside his Realm of Death.
howToPlay: To secure your lead, never cast Decimate defensively or too early in his Realm of Death. Walk alongside Mordekaiser to match his movement, holding your Q until he locks himself into the cast animation of Obliterate or Death's Grasp. This lock-in guarantees your outer blade lands perfectly. If you miss-space and hit with the handle, immediately reset the fight using Crippling Strike's slow to disengage, then wait for your cooldowns before re-engaging.
laneImpact: This advantage allows you to aggressively freeze the wave near your turret, forcing Mordekaiser to step up and risk an all-in. If he attempts to farm with Obliterate, his isolated damage is wasted on minions, leaving him vulnerable. You can constantly threaten Apprehend to pull him into long, punishing trades. This pressure forces him into bad recall timings, granting you plating gold and preventing him from assisting his jungler.
why: Darius dominates this matchup because his raw physical pressure outpaces Mordekaiser's sustained magic damage. Even when isolated within Realm of Death, you hold the definitive trump card. By perfectly spacing Decimate so the outer blade strikes Mordekaiser, you trigger a massive heal that completely negates the ticking aura of Darkness Rise. Since Hemorrhage stacks continuously during these extended duels, your Noxian Guillotine will easily execute him before his shield can save him.

summary: Kayn can ignore the terrain of Cataclysm completely by using Shadow Step to walk through the arena walls.
howToPlay: To win this matchup, never initiate with Cataclysm unless you have seen Kayn use Shadow Step to enter the fight. Instead, lead with your Demacian Standard and Dragon Strike combo to knock him up, forcing him to react. If he attempts to escape through a wall, use Golden Aegis to slow him, which can interrupt his wall-walking state if he takes damage.
