When he uses Umbral Trespass to dodge your burst, prepare your combo at his exit point.
laneImpact: Because Shadow Step trivializes your terrain, you cannot rely on Cataclysm to secure isolated skirmishes in the river. This creates a high-stakes tracking race where you must predict Kayn's pathing through walls. If you fail to mirror his movements, Kayn will use his superior wall-crossing mobility to execute unexpected ganks, securing his form transformation early and shifting the map pressure heavily in his team's favor.
why: The duel revolves around how Kayn neutralizes Jarvan IV's signature arena. While Cataclysm is designed to trap mobile targets, Kayn can simply activate Shadow Step to walk right through the rock walls, completely nullifying your ultimate's containment. This interaction turns a normally lethal lockup into a wasted cooldown, allowing Kayn to escape or reposition for a counter-engage with Reaping Slash or Blade's Reach depending on his chosen form from The Darkin Scythe.

howToPlay: Simple plan: you don’t need to kill him. Push, reset, vision, and arrive on time. Key timing: at level 5, use transform to secure objective fights, not a random turret dive. Decision: if your team is engage-vulnerable, position to disrupt Ornn’s setup while still threatening carries behind him.
laneImpact: You can take priority with good trades, and Ornn often must choose between managing wave and staying healthy. In fights, be mindful: his AOE control is dangerous for your team even if you can enter hard in dragon form.
why: Ornn is favorable mainly because he doesn’t pressure kills in lane, while you can convert scaling into objective tempo. He wants to survive and play teamfights; Shyvana wants to accelerate timings where she arrives first and forces fights around objectives.

summary: Morgana's Black Shield completely absorbs Lissandra's Ring of Frost root and Frozen Tomb stun, neutralizing her primary crowd control tools in teamfights.
howToPlay: Never cast Black Shield proactively; hold it until you see her teleport via Glacial Path or cast Frozen Tomb. If she baits your shield, immediately retreat toward your tower until it returns from cooldown. When she steps up to clear waves, align your Dark Binding with the path of her Ice Shard to catch her locked in her cast animation, then follow up with Tormented Shadow.
laneImpact: Because she cannot safely lock you down, you dictate the wave's pace. Use Tormented Shadow to constantly shove Lissandra under her tower, forcing her to burn mana using Ice Shard on minions rather than poking you. When she tries to engage with Glacial Path, you can walk forward aggressively, knowing her follow-up is completely neutralized, securing easy health advantages.
why: This matchup heavily favors you because Black Shield completely shuts down Lissandra's entire offensive identity. Her primary engage relies on heavy lockdown, but your Black Shield absorbs both the root from Ring of Frost and the crucial stun from Frozen Tomb. Without her crowd control, Lissandra cannot lock you down for her burst, turning her aggressive dives into wasted cooldowns while you safely retaliate.

summary: Amumu's Despair deals percentage max HP magic damage, which bypasses Rammus's high armor from Defensive Ball Curl.
howToPlay: When skirmishing, do not panic if he uses Frenzying Taunt on you; simply keep Despair active to melt his health pool while you are forced to attack him. Save your Bandage Toss to cancel his Powerball charge when he tries to escape or engage on your allies. During major teamfights, wait for him to commit with Soaring Slam, then immediately follow up with Curse of the Sad Mummy to lock down his backline before they can follow his lead.
laneImpact: This matchup shifts jungle control entirely in your favor. Rammus cannot safely duel you near camps, meaning you can aggressively secure objectives and contest his neutral monsters. When he tries to speed through the river with Powerball to gank your lanes, your superior clear speed allows you to either counter-gank immediately or strip away his camps, leaving him under-leveled and unable to match your teamfight threat.
why: Amumu naturally dismantles Rammus in direct jungle skirmishes because Rammus relies heavily on building armor to boost his damage through Rolling Armordillo and reflect attacks with Defensive Ball Curl. However, your Despair deals continuous percent-health magic damage that completely bypasses his armor-stacking defenses. Combined with Cursed Touch which amplifies all magic damage Rammus takes, you turn his defensive stat-checking into a liability.

summary: Senna outranges Bard and can easily farm souls off him, while using Piercing Darkness to sustain through his poke.
howToPlay: Do not walk up to trade unless Senna misses Last Embrace. Place your Caretaker’s Shrine far behind your turret so your carry can safely heal without being poked. Only use Cosmic Binding reactively when she tries to step forward to harvest a soul. If she attempts to escape a gank using Curse of the Black Mist, aim Tempered Fate to lock her down before she gains camouflage, allowing your team to close the gap.
laneImpact: This matchup completely ruins your lane control. Because Senna constantly chips away at your health, you are forced to spend mana on Caretaker’s Shrine rather than playing aggressively. This endless pressure pushes your wave under turret, making it extremely dangerous for you to roam and collect chimes for Traveler’s Call, which in turn stalls your own scaling and map presence.
why: Senna's massive Basic Attack range allows her to easily harvest souls from you whenever you step up. If you try to trade back using Cosmic Binding, she simply negates your poke by casting Piercing Darkness through the minion wave to heal herself and her ally. This constant sustain and range advantage means she scales rapidly while punishing your shorter-range presence.

summary: Jax can use Counter Strike to block Ornn's basic attacks and prevent him from popping Brittle marks applied by Bellows Breath.
howToPlay: Never initiate with Bellows Breath while his defensive options are up. Instead, poke from safety using Volcanic Rupture. If Jax initiates with Leap Strike and immediately triggers Counter Strike, use Searing Charge to dash away toward safety before the stun lands. Only commit to popping brittle marks after you have successfully baited out his dodge, or use the knock-up from Call of the Forge God to disengage if he catches you off guard.
laneImpact: Because you cannot easily trade into him, wave positioning becomes your lifeline. Allowing Jax to stack Relentless Assault on minion waves gives him the leverage to crash large waves and poke you under tower with Leap Strike and Empower. If you mismanage the lane state, he will quickly chip away at your turret plates, outscaling you and threatening to split-push your entire side of the map.
why: This matchup revolves around a tense mind game regarding your brittle application. While Bellows Breath is your primary tool for winning short trades, Jax possesses a hard counter in Counter Strike. By activating his defensive stance, he completely dodges the basic attack required to trigger the brittle explosion, neutralizing your burst potential and leaving you vulnerable to a heavy counter-attack.

summary: Ornn's Searing Charge knockup is highly telegraphed, offering Fiora an easy opportunity to trigger Riposte's stun.
howToPlay: Never initiate with Searing Charge unless you have seen Fiora waste Riposte first. Instead, summon your Volcanic Rupture pillar as a psychological threat, delaying your dash to bait her parry. If she misuses her defensive tool, you have a brief fifteen-second cooldown window to safely clear the wave or use Bellows Breath to disengage. When she activates Grand Challenge, immediately hug a terrain wall to physically block her from hitting the final vital.
laneImpact: You are forced into a defensive, low-resource lane under your own turret. Fiora will constantly use Lunge to poke your vitals and deny you minions. If you walk up to clear waves with Bellows Breath, she can initiate with Grand Challenge and chase you down. This constant pressure prevents you from helping your team, locking you in the side lane while she threatens to destroy your tower.
why: Fiora completely dominates this matchup because her Riposte directly counters your entire crowd control kit, especially the heavily telegraphed Searing Charge. If you attempt to dash into a pillar from Volcanic Rupture or natural terrain, she can easily react, parrying the knockup to stun you instead. This interaction, combined with her passive Duelist's Dance shredding your built-in tankiness with true damage, makes trading directly almost impossible as the game goes on.

summary: Zilean can use the massive slow from Temporal Mirage to keep Rumble at a distance, preventing him from closing the gap to apply his melee damage.
howToPlay: To survive, use Electro Harpoon to secure minions from a safe distance and match Zilean's slow if he steps up. Never activate Flamespitter forward unless Temporal Mirage is on cooldown. If he uses his speed boost offensively, immediately absorb the incoming Time Bomb blast with Scrap Shield. Once you unlock The Equalizer, wait for him to waste Chronoshift on himself or an ally before committing your ultimate to a full-on team fight engagement.
laneImpact: Zilean’s ability to shut down your gap-close forces you into a passive stance under your own turret. You cannot contest the wave with Flamespitter without taking a double Time Bomb stun. This means Zilean dictates the wave state, keeping you pinned while he roams safely. Your health pool will constantly bleed through Scrap Shield if you try to step up, delaying your mid-game power spikes and leaving your jungler without mid-lane priority.
why: This lane is highly taxing because Zilean easily neutralizes your melee threat using Temporal Mirage. Whenever you attempt to advance to burn him with Flamespitter, his massive slow halts your approach instantly, leaving you stranded. He can easily outspace you, resetting his cooldowns with Twisted Timeflow to double up on Time Bomb if you try to commit, turning your aggressive posture into a self-inflicted health deficit.

summary: Syndra's Scatter the Weak completely denies Kai'Sa's attempts to close the gap, leaving her vulnerable to Unleashed Power.
howToPlay: Never cast Scatter the Weak preemptively just for poke. Always hold this spell as a reactive tool for when she activates Supercharge to run at you or marks you for Killer Instinct. Stand behind your own minions to dilute any stray missiles from Icathian Rain if she does get close. Once you successfully knock her back with a sphere, immediately follow up with Force of Will and then pull the trigger on Unleashed Power to delete her fragile health bar.
laneImpact: Because you hold the ultimate disengage tool, Kai'Sa cannot safely walk up to secure last hits without risking a heavy trade. You easily control the lane's pace by zoning her with Dark Sphere. She is forced to rely on Void Seeker from afar to farm, bleeding mana and health. This constant pressure pushes her under turret, denying her roam opportunities and allowing you to chip away at her plates or secure early priority.
why: Kai'Sa relies heavily on using her mobility from Supercharge or Killer Instinct to close the distance and isolate you for Icathian Rain. However, your Scatter the Weak acts as an absolute barrier. Any time she tries to dash or run forward, you can knock her back, completely neutralizing her short-range threat. Once she is displaced and slowed, she becomes a sitting duck, perfectly set up for a lethal Unleashed Power burst.

summary: Janna can easily react to Galio's Justice Punch with a quick Howling Gale, completely canceling his primary engage tool.
howToPlay: Always hold *Howling Gale* when Galio postures forward; never use it to poke. Position yourself slightly behind your ADC to bait his *Justice Punch*, then instantly double-tap the tornado to stop him. Once his dash is neutralized and he wastes *Shield of Durand* in thin air, immediately punish him with *Zephyr* and boost your ally with *Eye of the Storm*. If he manages to jump away with *Hero's Entrance*, use your *Tailwind* passive to quickly roam and counter-gank.
laneImpact: This interaction strips Galio of his lane pressure, forcing him to play passively. Since he cannot safely engage with *Justice Punch*, your ADC can safely control the minion waves without fearing a flash-taunt setup. Furthermore, when Galio looks to impact other lanes with *Hero's Entrance*, your safety allows you to mirror his movements or roam proactively while he is locked in his ultimate channel or stuck under his own turret.
why: Galio relies entirely on his forward dash to initiate skirmishes. Because his *Justice Punch* has a distinct wind-up animation, you can easily react by launching a quick *Howling Gale* to knock him out of the air. Denying this entry point completely neutralizes his follow-up *Shield of Durand* taunt and *Colossal Smash*, leaving him stranded and vulnerable to your ranged harass while his primary gap-closer is on cooldown.

summary: Howling Gale can interrupt Leona's Zenith Blade mid-flight, completely denying her ability to follow up with Shield of Daybreak.
howToPlay: To secure this advantage, never cast Howling Gale aggressively; hold it exclusively to react to her Zenith Blade. Stand slightly behind your marksman so you can easily aim the tornado through them. If Leona misses her engage or wastes Eclipse, immediately use Zephyr and auto-attacks to punish her cooldown window while applying Eye of the Storm to absorb any residual damage. If she catches you off-guard with Solar Flare, use Monsoon immediately to reset the fight.
laneImpact: This dynamic completely paralyzes Leona's aggressive laning phase, forcing her to play passively. Knowing her gap-closer can be cancelled, she cannot safely contest the minion waves or pressure your marksman under tower. You can easily maintain health advantages through safe trades, pushing her out of the lane or forcing early, unfavorable recalls that cost her team deep vision and dragon priority.
why: Janna completely dictates the pace of this lane because Howling Gale is a hard counter to Leona's main engage tool. Whenever Leona attempts to initiate with Zenith Blade, a well-timed tornado interrupts her dash mid-flight. This denies her the positioning required to trigger Shield of Daybreak, leaving her stranded and vulnerable to counter-harass while her defensive Eclipse is wasted.

summary: Poppy's Steadfast Presence blocks Yasuo's Sweeping Blade dashes, grounding him and leaving him highly vulnerable to her Hammer Shock.
howToPlay: Position yourself constantly near your own low-health minions, as these are the exact targets Yasuo wants to target with Sweeping Blade. Never initiate with Steadfast Presence; instead, hold it until he starts his dash animation to guarantee the knockup. If he manages to bait it out, back off immediately. Once you lock him down, quickly position yourself to angle a Heroic Charge into the nearest wall, then follow up with Hammer Shock to secure the trade.
laneImpact: This dynamic completely shifts the wave control in your favor. Yasuo cannot safely dash through minions to stack Steel Tempest or poke you without risking an immediate, punishing lockup. You can easily zone him away from his wave or freeze it. Any attempt he makes to force a trade near walls turns deadly, as a quick Heroic Charge into a stun guarantees a massive health lead and easy tower pressure.
why: Yasuo relies entirely on the constant mobility of Sweeping Blade to trade and dodge. By activating Steadfast Presence, you instantly shut down his primary movement tool. This grounds him on the spot, cancelling his dash and leaving him unable to dodge both parts of your Hammer Shock. Because his Wind Wall cannot block your hammer strikes, his defense is completely bypassed when he is locked down near you.

summary: Ezreal can poke Jinx down with Mystic Shot while she tries to farm, and can use Arcane Shift to instantly escape her Flame Chompers! if caught.
howToPlay: Position yourself strictly behind your minion wave to block Mystic Shot, using the Pow-Pow minigun form of Switcheroo! to farm safely. Never throw Flame Chompers! offensively unless you have seen him waste Arcane Shift first. Save them defensively to zone him if he blinks forward, and only use Zap! to poke when his escape tool is on cooldown.
laneImpact: You will regularly find yourself pushed under your turret, forced to burn mana using Switcheroo! rockets to grab minions from a safe distance. Ezreal easily maintains wave control by stacking Rising Spell Force. Absorbing too many Mystic Shot hits will force you into early, unfavorable recalls, losing precious gold and letting him pressure your tower.
why: Ezreal dominates this matchup by abusing the long range of Mystic Shot to chip away your health whenever you step up to farm. Your main defensive tool, Flame Chompers!, is heavily countered because he can reactively bypass the root entirely using Arcane Shift. This interaction makes it incredibly difficult to lock him down, leaving you vulnerable to his relentless physical poke.

summary: While Kassadin outscales Galio, Galio can abuse his early waveclear with Winds of War (Q) to roam with Hero's Entrance (R) before Kassadin reaches level 5.
howToPlay: Constantly pressure the first three waves using Winds of War to keep Kassadin pinned. Once you reach level five, immediately pan your camera to side lanes to find a Hero's Entrance opportunity. If he attempts to interrupt your roam or follow, use Justice Punch to knock him back, followed by Shield of Durand to lock him down. If no roam is available, focus on denying him Null Sphere shields by baiting his casts.
laneImpact: The early laning phase is entirely in your hands. Kassadin's weak early push forces him to use Nether Blade and Force Pulse defensively to secure minions. This minimizes his poke on you, keeping your health pool high. However, if you fail to convert this early pressure into side-lane advantages before he gets his ultimate, his scaling will quickly turn the mid-lane into an uphill battle.
why: This matchup is a race against the clock. While Kassadin's late-game scaling is superior, his early waveclear is atrocious. Before he unlocks Riftwalk at level five, you hold a massive priority window. By using Winds of War and Colossal Smash, you can shove him under tower effortlessly, using this tempo to impact side lanes with Hero's Entrance while he is trapped farming with Nether Blade.

summary: Jinx can outrange Xayah using Fishbones but must avoid standing directly between Xayah and her feathers to prevent being rooted by Bladecaller.
howToPlay: To win this, maintain a strict diagonal angle relative to Xayah and her deployed feathers, preventing a sudden root. Abuse your rocket launcher range from Switcheroo! to poke whenever her Bladecaller is on cooldown. If she activates her steroid to rush you, place Flame Chompers! directly in her path to halt her advance. Finally, never fire Super Mega Death Rocket! until she has already burnt her Featherstorm untargetability.
laneImpact: The laning phase becomes a high-stakes geometric puzzle. While you attempt to shove and poke with rockets, Xayah uses Deadly Plumage to match your clear speed and establish a zone of control. If you step into her feather path, you risk getting chunked out, forcing you to play defensively under turret, which delays your scaling and prevents you from helping secure early objectives.
why: This matchup is a pure test of spacing and awareness. By toggling Switcheroo!, you hold a significant range advantage over Xayah during trades. However, her Clean Cuts passive and Double Daggers constantly litter the lane with feathers. The danger arises when you neglect where these feathers land; if you stand between Xayah and her feathers, her Bladecaller will root you and swing the trade in her favor.

summary: Jayce can use Thundering Blow to knock Sett away when he activates Knuckle Down to run at him, denying the face-to-face trade.
howToPlay: To survive, you must bait out Thundering Blow before committing. Walk forward threateningly without using Knuckle Down, forcing him to waste his knockback early. Once his defensive tool is on cooldown, you have a brief window to activate Knuckle Down and pull him in with Facebreaker. If he holds his displacement, focus on farming under turret, using Haymaker to absorb his poke, and wait for your jungler to lock him down.
laneImpact: This interaction forces you to play on the defensive, conceding early wave control. Jayce will constantly poke you from range, making it risky to walk up for minions. If you waste your health trying to force trades, you will be forced into a bad recall or dove under tower. The lane is decided by how much health you can preserve before reaching the safety of your turret, limiting your map pressure.
why: Jayce dictates the distance in this lane by neutralizing your primary gap-closer. Whenever you activate Knuckle Down to sprint forward for a trade, Jayce can immediately deny your approach by using Thundering Blow in his melee form to knock you away. Because this disengage prevents you from landing Facebreaker or your basic attacks, you are left running backwards while taking heavy ranged poke without any way to retaliate.

summary: Tryndamere's Spinning Slash engage can be shut down instantly by a well-timed CH-2 Electron Storm Grenade stun, forcing him to waste Undying Rage defensively.
howToPlay: Always position your H-28G Evolution Turret trio in a defensive triangle to maximize Hextech Affinity movement speed when kiting. Never throw CH-2 Electron Storm Grenade proactively; hold it strictly as a counter-engage tool for when he commits Spinning Slash. If he tries to slow you with Mocking Shout, face him briefly to negate the slow, then immediately deploy UPGRADE!!! paired with H-28G Evolution Turret to melt his health pool if he persists.
laneImpact: This matchup dynamic completely locks Tryndamere out of the minion wave. He cannot easily build Battle Fury or sustain with Bloodlust without taking heavy poke from your H-28G Evolution Turret setup. You will constantly push him under tower, chipping away at its plates. If he tries to break the freeze or retaliate, a quick CH-2 Electron Storm Grenade seals his fate, forcing him to base early or lose his turret extremely fast.
why: Heimerdinger dominates because Tryndamere must close the gap with Spinning Slash to do damage. If he tries, Heimerdinger can intercept him mid-dash with CH-2 Electron Storm Grenade. This stun leaves Tryndamere vulnerable to a barrage of H-28G Evolution Turret lasers and Hextech Micro-Rockets. Unable to stack Battle Fury or stick to you, he is forced to activate Undying Rage early just to survive the turret onslaught rather than to dive you.

summary: Talon can easily dodge Seraphine's skillshots using Assassin's Path over walls, allowing him to flank and burst her down with Shadow Assault.
howToPlay: To survive, you must hold Beat Drop exclusively as a defensive reaction when he commits, never for farming. Stay strictly in the center of the lane, as far from the side walls as possible, to deny him easy Assassin's Path angles. If he goes missing, do not follow him blindly through the river; instead, spam ping your allies and use Surround Sound to safely push the wave and force him to lose gold under his tower.
laneImpact: This constant threat forces you to play extremely passively under your turret. You cannot safely contest waves with High Note without risking a deadly flank. If you push, Talon will use Assassin's Path to disappear into the jungle, leaving you blind to his roam timing. The pressure forces you to choose between giving up farm or risking an all-in burst every time his Shadow Assault is off cooldown.
why: Seraphine struggles immensely because Talon can completely bypass her zone control. Whenever you try to poke or self-peel with High Note or Beat Drop, Talon can use Assassin's Path to vault over the mid-lane walls, effortlessly dodging your slow-moving projectiles. This mobility allows him to close the distance instantly, flank from unexpected angles, and deploy his lethal Shadow Assault burst before you can react or trigger Stage Presence notes.

summary: Milio's Cozy Campfire gives his ADC extra range to bypass Janna's Zephyr poke, but Janna can negate his Ultra Mega Fire Kick engages with Howling Gale.
howToPlay: To win this skill matchup, never throw Howling Gale randomly for poke. Keep this tornado ready to reactively intercept his Ultra Mega Fire Kick projectile and protect your partner. When Cozy Campfire is active, rely on Tailwind to quickly move backwards and wait out the duration. Once their range boost expires, immediately retaliate with Zephyr and apply Eye of the Storm to your ally to win the short trade.
laneImpact: Laning phase shifts constantly around the activation of Cozy Campfire. When it is active, you must concede ground, as your shield from Eye of the Storm will be quickly depleted by their ranged advantage. Conversely, whenever Milio wastes his Ultra Mega Fire Kick, his lane loses its primary self-peel, allowing you to walk up, apply Zephyr, and force favorable health trades without fear of a sudden counter-engage.
why: This matchup is a pure duel of utility where spacing dictates the victor. Milio uses Cozy Campfire to grant his marksman artificial attack range, allowing them to harass you safely from outside your Zephyr poke radius. However, you hold the definitive response to his offensive attempts: a well-timed Howling Gale completely neutralizes the forward momentum of his Ultra Mega Fire Kick, shutting down his attempts to secure active lane control.

summary: Sett can cancel Sion's Decimating Smash charge instantly by pulling him with Facebreaker.
howToPlay: Position yourself constantly inside or just behind Sion's minion wave to stay within striking distance. Never use Facebreaker proactively to initiate; hold it strictly to react when Sion begins the red indicator of Decimating Smash. If he plays extremely safe, use Knuckle Down to close the gap and force him to react. Finally, when you deplete his health bar, immediately back off or save Haymaker to block the rapid basic attacks of his Glory in Death zombie form.
laneImpact: Sion is forced into a defensive posture, unable to use Decimating Smash to secure wave control or poke without getting punished. Whenever he attempts to clear minions, you can walk up with Knuckle Down to threaten a pull. His attempts to absorb trades using the Soul Furnace shield are easily bypassed by the true damage of Haymaker, allowing you to freeze the wave at will or dive him under tower with absolute impunity.
why: Sett completely shuts down Sion's primary threat because Facebreaker instantly cancels the charge of Decimating Smash, stripping Sion of his main damage and knock-up. Since Sion naturally accumulates massive permanent health through Glory in Death and Soul Furnace, he unwittingly scales Sett's ultimate. The Show Stopper transforms Sion's massive HP pool into a devastating weapon, allowing Sett to slam him directly into the enemy team for colossal area-of-effect damage.

summary: Renekton uses Slice and Dice to dash inside Aatrox's Q sweetspots, but Aatrox can punish him with Infernal Chains once his dashes are on cooldown.
howToPlay: To win, never start a trade by casting Infernal Chains. Instead, hold it until Renekton commits his first Slice and Dice forward. Use Umbral Dash to reposition your first two strikes of The Darkin Blade backward, keeping him at bay. If he uses his second dash to engage, immediately drop Infernal Chains on him; without mobility, he cannot escape the pull, guaranteeing your third sweetspot and a massive heal from Deathbringer Stance.
laneImpact: Laning phase is a tense dance where wave state dictates trade opportunities. When Renekton has high Fury from Reign of Anger, he will look to crash waves and force short trades. You cannot contest the wave blindly when his dashes are up. Missed sweetspots mean he controls the lane priority, but pulling him back with Infernal Chains completely flips the pressure.
why: This matchup is a pure duel of mobility and spacing. Renekton wants to use the double dash of Slice and Dice to slip inside the sweetspots of your The Darkin Blade, avoiding your knockups while delivering his burst. However, if you can bait out his dashes, he becomes highly vulnerable. The moment Slice and Dice is on cooldown, your Infernal Chains becomes inescapable, allowing you to land your full combo.

summary: Vi can lock down Evelynn with Cease and Desist before she can escape with Last Caress.
howToPlay: When hunting her, never initiate with Cease and Desist if she is unaware of you. Instead, use Vault Breaker to gap-close and trigger Denting Blows with your basic attacks and Relentless Force. Save Cease and Desist specifically for the moment she tries to channel Allure on a teammate or when her health drops near the threshold where she desperately wants to cast Last Caress. If she manages to slip into Demon Shade beforehand, activate Blast Shield to absorb her initial Whiplash burst.
laneImpact: This interaction changes how the jungle match plays out post-level-five. Evelynn cannot safely contest camps or secure crabs if you are nearby, as stepping out of Demon Shade to clear means risking a fatal encounter. If she attempts to charm you with Allure, you can charge Vault Breaker to close the distance or immediately override her burst attempt. This forces her into a defensive, passive farming style, giving you free rein over neutral objectives.
why: Evelynn relies on the threat of Demon Shade and her escape tool Last Caress to survive skirmishes. However, Vi completely shuts down this escape route. Once Evelynn reveals herself to strike or apply Allure, your Cease and Desist acts as an unstoppable lockdown. Since Cease and Desist cannot be interrupted or dodged once cast, you suppress her before she can activate the untargetable backward dash of Last Caress.

summary: While you can poke Kai'Sa down early with Volley, she can use Killer Instinct to dive past your front line and burst you down if you are isolated.
howToPlay: Never wander into the river or side bushes alone where Icathian Rain isolates its damage. Always position directly inside your minion wave. Keep Enchanted Crystal Arrow ready as a defensive tool; if she activates Killer Instinct to dive you, fire your ultimate point-blank to stun her mid-dash, then immediately activate Ranger's Focus to turn the fight. Use Hawkshot to track enemy positions in the lane bushes to prevent unexpected plasma marks.
laneImpact: Wave management dictates your safety. You must maintain a constant minion buffer to dilute her Icathian Rain missiles. Pushing her under tower prevents her from trading, but leaving yourself overextended in an empty lane invites a Void Seeker engage. Trades are won by chipping her health down before she can find an isolated angle to activate Supercharge and chase you.
why: This matchup is defined by the tension between your long-range poke and her sudden gap-close. Early on, you easily abuse her short range with Volley and Frost Shot slows. However, once she unlocks Killer Instinct, she can bypass your front line instantly if you are marked, utilizing Icathian Rain to burst you down rapidly whenever you isolate yourself from your minions.

summary: Her Whimsy can polymorph Alistar mid-Headbutt or immediately after his Pulverize, neutralizing his follow-up Trample stun.
howToPlay: To survive, you must bait out Whimsy before committing. Stand near your caster minions to threaten a flash-Pulverize rather than a predictable Headbutt approach. If Lulu wastes her polymorph on her ally for attack speed, that is your three-second green light to engage. If you get caught mid-dash, immediately activate Unbreakable Will to cleanse the polymorph, allowing you to quickly stack Trample and salvage the fight.
laneImpact: Because your primary engage is so easily neutralized, Lulu and her carry will constantly poke you down with Glitterlance and Pix, Faerie Companion. Every failed engage results in massive health loss, forcing you to rely on passive healing from Triumphant Roar. You will be pushed under your turret, struggling to protect your partner while Lulu uses Help, Pix! to safely win every short trade.
why: Lulu completely shuts down your engage potential by holding her crucial crowd control. When you attempt to initiate with Headbutt, she can reactively cast Whimsy to turn you into a harmless critter mid-dash, or immediately after you land Pulverize. This prevents you from charging up and landing the crucial stun from Trample, leaving you exposed in the middle of their minion wave without any follow-up.

summary: Use Drakehound's Step to dash inside the inner ring of Darius's Decimate to deny him healing and Hemorrhage stacks.
howToPlay: To secure your advantage, never initiate trades with Decimate. Instead, walk up to strike her with Crippling Strike first, slowing her down so she cannot easily react with Drakehound's Step. Save Apprehend specifically to pull her back if she tries to dash away or to cancel her Cunning Sweep animation. If she activates Repudiation to block your slow, delay your Noxian Guillotine until the brief shield decays to guarantee the execution.
laneImpact: During the laning phase, this dynamic prevents Ambessa from securing easy short trades. If she attempts to clear waves with Cunning Sweep, she risks being pulled. You can freeze the wave near your turret, forcing her to choose between losing gold or stepping up. When she tries to poke with Lacerate, any misstep allows you to lock her down, rapidly building stacks toward Noxian Guillotine while her low base durability makes mistakes lethal.
why: This matchup revolves around a high-stakes spacing war. Ambessa relies on Drakehound's Step to dash inside the inner handle of your Decimate, aiming to deny your healing and prevent Hemorrhage stacks. However, because you possess Apprehend to interrupt her movement and Crippling Strike to cripple her mobility, you hold the tools to control the distance and force extended trades where your passive easily overpowers her.

summary: Maokai must find an all-in with Twisted Advance (W) before Sona pokes him down with Hymn of Valor (Q) and out-sustains with Aria of Perseverance (W).
howToPlay: Maintain a safe distance just outside the reach of Twisted Advance, forcing Maokai to walk forward predictably if he wants to engage. Only step up to poke with Hymn of Valor when he hesitates, and immediately fall back. If he throws Sapling Toss into the lane brushes, reposition to the opposite side of the lane. Should he commit with Nature's Grasp, immediately counter with Crescendo to lock him down and protect your carry.
laneImpact: This matchup translates into total lane dominance where you dictate the wave state. Because Maokai cannot safely step up to use Bramble Smash without taking heavy damage, his ADC is forced under turret. Your relentless health trades force early recalls, giving your duo free plates. Once you unlock Crescendo, Maokai's engage threats are completely neutralized, securing your transition into an unstoppable teamfight powerhouse.
why: Sona naturally outscales Maokai as the match progresses, creating a massive utility gap. Maokai's primary win condition is locking you down early with Twisted Advance. However, because you fight from range, you can constantly chip his health with Hymn of Valor before he can engage. Any minor poke he attempts with Sapling Toss is immediately erased by your Aria of Perseverance, rendering his lane presence obsolete.

summary: Jinx must avoid trading with Lucian when his Relentless Pursuit is up, relying on Fishbones to farm from safety until she outscales him.
howToPlay: Survival hinges on your discipline with Switcheroo!. Activate Fishbones to secure minions from maximum range, accepting that you must sacrifice some mana to stay out of Lucian's dash range. Never initiate a trade while his Relentless Pursuit is available. If he aggressively dashes forward to force an exchange, immediately drop Flame Chompers! directly in his path to interrupt his advance, then retreat. Your goal is simply to collect gold safely until your superior late-game scaling takes over.
laneImpact: You will constantly find yourself pushed towards your turret, struggling to maintain wave control. Lucian can easily freeze the lane or crash massive waves to secure early tower plates. If you lose too much health trying to contest the farm, you will be forced into unfavorable recall timings or become highly vulnerable to The Culling under your own tower, starving you of gold and delaying your crucial item spikes.
why: Lucian dominates this matchup because his high early burst through Lightslinger and quick gap-close with Relentless Pursuit completely overwhelm Jinx's low baseline mobility. Whenever you step up to use Pow-Pow, he can instantly dash forward, dodge your skillshots, and trigger rapid double-attacks. This makes short, aggressive trades highly lethal for you, especially if he aligns Piercing Light through the minion wave to poke you from afar.

summary: Placing Gravity Field (W) directly behind Viktor when Zed casts Death Mark (R) guarantees a stun on Zed the moment he reappears.
howToPlay: To survive and turn the tides, you must hold Gravity Field exclusively for his ultimate. The very instant Zed targets you with Death Mark, cast Gravity Field directly behind yourself. Because he always materializes on your opposite side, he will reappear directly inside the device, guaranteeing an immediate stun. Follow up instantly by dropping Arcane Storm on his head, kiting back with the shield from Siphon Power, and aiming Hextech Ray to burst him down before he can reactivate his shadow.
laneImpact: You are forced into a defensive posture, where mismanaging the wave invites deadly dives. Whenever Zed uses Living Shadow to trade with Razor Shuriken and Shadow Slash, his main escape and poke tool is down for a long duration. This window allows you to aggressively push back with Hextech Ray or secure short trades using Siphon Power. If you waste Gravity Field prematurely, you forfeit all lane safety, allowing Zed to freeze and zone you completely.
why: Zed's mobility through Living Shadow heavily threatens your safety, bypassing your zoning tools to deliver explosive physical burst. Because your Glorious Evolution requires early passive stacks, Zed's ability to safely farm and poke with Razor Shuriken from range makes matching his pressure difficult. The matchup revolves around Death Mark; while its lethal damage can easily execute you, it also forces Zed into a predictable landing spot directly behind you, creating a narrow window for a counter-offensive.

summary: Alistar can interrupt Rakan's Grand Entrance with Pulverize, or Headbutt Rakan away from his target during Battle Dance.
howToPlay: Position yourself slightly behind your carry, acting as a human shield ready to react. Never waste Pulverize proactively; always hold it specifically to interrupt Grand Entrance when Rakan dashes in. If he triggers his ultimate, The Quickness, wait for the charm to hit you, immediately cleanse it using Unbreakable Will, and then Headbutt him away from your team. If you miss your timing, retreat until your cooldowns recover.
laneImpact: This interaction forces Rakan into a passive, reactive role where he cannot safely fish for aggressive knock-ups. His inability to reliably land Grand Entrance prevents his duo from dictating trade patterns, giving your carry free rein over wave positioning. Any chip damage Rakan attempts with Gleaming Quill is easily neutralized by Triumphant Roar, allowing you to slow-push waves and safely threaten dives under the enemy turret.
why: Alistar completely dictates the pace of this lane because his defensive kit perfectly neutralizes Rakan's mobility. When Rakan attempts to initiate with Grand Entrance, a well-timed Pulverize knocks him up mid-dash, canceling the crowd control entirely. Furthermore, if Rakan tries to retreat or reposition using Battle Dance, you can instantly Headbutt him away from his intended partner, leaving him stranded and highly vulnerable.

summary: Janna can freely roam with Tailwind and Zephyr's passive movement speed while Yuumi is attached with You and Me!, creating map-wide advantages.
howToPlay: To secure this advantage, push the wave early to gain priority. Once the wave crashes under the enemy turret, immediately activate Zephyr's passive speed to roam toward mid or deep ward the jungle. If Yuumi attempts to detach to trigger Bop 'n' Block, punish her immediately by releasing a quick Howling Gale to interrupt her re-attachment, leaving her highly vulnerable. Should your roam fail, quickly return to lane using your superior speed to protect your carry.
laneImpact: In lane, Yuumi's lack of physical presence reduces her pressure, allowing you to control the lane's pace. While she attempts to poke with Prowling Projectile, your Eye of the Storm easily negates her damage. Since she cannot easily clear waves or block your movements, you can shove the lane and walk away. This forces her carry to farm under tower, giving you free windows to invade or gank.
why: This matchup is dictated by map presence. While Yuumi remains tethered to her partner using You and Me!, she sacrifices solo agency. Janna exploits this passive state perfectly. Thanks to the combined passive movement speed from Tailwind and Zephyr, you can outpace Yuumi across the river. You can influence other lanes instantly, while she is locked to her host, unable to match your rotations without leaving her carry vulnerable.

summary: Ambessa's Drakehound's Step allows her to dash out of Aatrox's Q sweetspots every time she casts an ability.
howToPlay: To survive, adopt a bait-and-punish playstyle. Never initiate trades with your first Q-cast; instead, use Deathbringer Stance to secure minions and sustain. Hold Infernal Chains until she has exhausted her Drakehound's Step dashes. If she initiates with Cunning Sweep, use Umbral Dash laterally to escape her path. Only activate World Ender when her Repudiation shield is on cooldown, allowing you to chain your full combo without your control effects being blocked.
laneImpact: Consequently, you cannot easily contest the wave. Missing a single sweetspot allows Ambessa to aggressively dash forward, using Repudiation to absorb your retaliation and block the pull from Infernal Chains. This constant threat of counter-engagement forces you to farm defensively near your turret, as dropping into her kill range makes you an easy target for her Public Execution dive.
why: This matchup is dictated by how easily Ambessa negates your main damage source. Her Drakehound's Step gives her a short dash after every cast, allowing her to effortlessly slip out of your The Darkin Blade sweetspots. Whenever you attempt to set up a trade with your first two Q-casts, she can reactively trigger Cunning Sweep or Lacerate to reposition, dodging your knockups while simultaneously priming her own empowered strikes.

summary: Vayne can use Condemn to knock Akshan into a wall and stun him if he swings too close to terrain with Heroic Swing.
howToPlay: Position yourself constantly near the lane's walls to bait his aggression, but keep your finger hovered over Condemn. Never use this ability defensively for simple disengages; save it exclusively to cancel Heroic Swing mid-flight. If he plays passively and avoids swinging, farm safely under turret and wait for your level six spike. Once Final Hour is active, you can use the stealth from Tumble to break his Comeuppance lock-on and turn the fight.
laneImpact: Akshan will use Avengerang to shove the wave and poke you simultaneously, forcing you under tower. You cannot match his early push, meaning you must focus on securing last hits using Tumble while preserving your health bar. If you survive his initial lane pressure without dying, your Silver Bolts and Final Hour spike will naturally tilt the duel in your favor as the laning phase transitions into mid-game skirmishes.
why: This matchup pits Akshan's overwhelming early skirmishing against your superior late-game scaling. While Dirty Fighting and Avengerang give him early lane dominance, the matchup hinges on how you respond to his mobility. The ultimate deciding factor is your reaction speed: whenever Akshan commits to a trajectory with Heroic Swing near a wall, a well-timed Condemn will interrupt his flight, slamming him into the terrain for an easy stun.

summary: Twisted Fate can lock Corki down with a gold Pick a Card, but Corki can match TF's Destiny roams using Special Delivery.
howToPlay: Do not waste Valkyrie defensively unless you see him lock in a blue or red card from Pick a Card; if he pulls the gold card, you must stay out of his auto-attack range entirely. Time your backing sequences to synchronize with your package spawns. If he triggers Destiny while you lack Special Delivery, do not chase blindly. Instead, activate Gatling Gun and use Missile Barrage to rapidly demolish his mid turret, punishing his roam with massive local gold.
laneImpact: Expect a non-stop pushing battle. Twisted Fate will constantly throw Wild Cards to shove you under turret and secure safe recalls. If you let him clear freely, he will disappear into the fog of war. You must match this push using Phosphorus Bomb and Gatling Gun to keep him tethered to his tower, forcing him to choose between losing his own plates or abandoning his sidelane target.
why: This matchup is a pure map-pressure race. Twisted Fate relies on the point-and-click stun of a gold Pick a Card to lock you down, preventing you from contesting his lane priority before he channels Destiny. However, Corki has the perfect counter-global tool: grabbing the package from Hextech Munitions gives you the raw speed and the explosive zone of Special Delivery to immediately mirror his sidelane rotations.

summary: Yone's Soul Unbound (E) allows him to trade safely and dodge Galio's CC, while his physical and true damage bypasses Galio's magic shield.
howToPlay: To survive, let the minions push to you and use Winds of War strictly to secure farm from a safe distance. Never initiate with Justice Punch unless Yone has already wasted his Soul Unbound. If he dashes forward with his spirit, immediately charge Shield of Durand defensively to mitigate his physical burst, then use Justice Punch backwards toward your tower to escape his Fate Sealed follow-up.
laneImpact: You cannot contest the wave directly. Whenever you step up to use Colossal Smash or Winds of War, Yone can initiate with Soul Unbound and a stacked Mortal Steel tornado to shred your health. This constant threat forces you to play under your turret, losing priority and preventing you from finding windows to cast Hero's Entrance to impact the side lanes without losing your mid tower.
why: Galio struggles heavily here because Yone relies on physical attacks from Way of the Hunter and physical strikes from Mortal Steel, rendering the magic shield from Shield of Durand completely useless. Furthermore, during trades, Yone can activate Soul Unbound to gain massive movement speed, allowing him to easily bait out and dodge Justice Punch before snapping back safely to his original body.

summary: Warwick's Jaws of the Beast makes him immune to displacement, and his Infinite Duress can suppress Amumu before Amumu can cast Curse of the Sad Mummy.
howToPlay: Never seek 1v1 duels in the river; track his starting buff and path to the opposite side to clear safely. During skirmishes, hold Curse of the Sad Mummy until Warwick commits Infinite Duress on a teammate, allowing you to interrupt his suppression instantly. If he jumps on you, use Bandage Toss on a jungle monster to escape instead of fighting through Primal Howl.
laneImpact: You cannot contest neutral camps or Scuttle Crabs directly. If you drop low during your clear, Blood Hunt alerts him, leading to lethal counter-jungling where you cannot fight back. If he catches you, Primal Howl reduces your Tantrum and Despair damage while forcing a retreat, sacrificing your early map pressure.
why: Warwick dominates the jungle duel because Jaws of the Beast allows him to ignore the displacement of Bandage Toss while healing through Eternal Hunger. Furthermore, his Infinite Duress can suppress you instantly, locking you down before you can even react with Curse of the Sad Mummy, completely neutralizing your primary teamfight tool.

summary: Caitlyn must use 90 Caliber Net to disengage immediately when Tristana uses Rocket Jump to initiate an Explosive Charge trade.
howToPlay: Never use 90 Caliber Net offensively. Keep this tool available exclusively for when Tristana mid-air casts Rocket Jump. Position yourself near your Yordle Snap Trap line so that if she attempts to jump directly on you, she lands on a trap or gets slowed by your net, guaranteeing a Headshot counter-attack. If you misplay the net timing, immediately retreat to avoid letting her auto-attack to max out her bomb charges.
laneImpact: The lane oscillates between slow-pushing harassment and explosive all-ins. If you fail to interrupt her leap, the burst from Explosive Charge forces you out of lane, granting her massive tower pressure. However, when you successfully disengage, Tristana is left stranded deep in your wave without her main mobility, allowing you to retaliate with Piltover Peacemaker and push her under her own turret.
why: This even lane revolves entirely around how you respond to Tristana's aggressive leaps. Her trading power relies heavily on stacking Explosive Charge quickly while utilizing Rapid Fire. Because your natural range from Draw a Bead is superior early, she must use Rocket Jump to close the distance. If she lands and starts stacking her bomb, she wins the trade; if you immediately negate her jump, you win.

summary: Ezreal can use Arcane Shift to reposition away from Xayah's feathers, preventing her from rooting him with Bladecaller.
howToPlay: To secure this lead, you must strictly hold Arcane Shift until Xayah commits to pulling her feathers back with Bladecaller. Never use it offensively to engage unless her recall ability is on cooldown. Stand diagonally to her feather layout, forcing her to choose between farming or aiming Double Daggers at you. If she manages to bait your blink first, immediately back off and use Mystic Shot to farm from maximum range until your cooldown is back.
laneImpact: This interaction forces Xayah into a defensive posture. Since she cannot reliably root you with Bladecaller, her trades with Deadly Plumage become incredibly risky. You can constantly harass her with Mystic Shot and Essence Flux from outside her auto-attack range. She is forced to waste Featherstorm defensively or lose crucial minion waves under her turret, giving you permanent priority and allowing you to chip away at her tower.
why: Ezreal dominates this matchup because Xayah relies heavily on setting up zones with her feathers from Clean Cuts and Double Daggers to lock targets down. Since she has short range, she must lure you into her feather line to setup a Bladecaller root. However, Arcane Shift completely neutralizes this setup, allowing you to instantly blink out of the feathers' return trajectory and deny her crowd control entirely while maintaining your DPS.

summary: When Nautilus lands Dredge Line, Braum can jump to his ally with Stand Behind Me and apply Concussive Blows to stun Nautilus during his engage.
howToPlay: Always stand slightly behind or parallel to your carry, holding Stand Behind Me specifically for when Dredge Line connects. Once Nautilus pulls himself in, jump to your ally, immediately hit Nautilus with Winter's Bite, and follow up with basic attacks to trigger Concussive Blows. If he targets you instead, raise Unbreakable to absorb his Riptide damage, then use Glacial Fissure to knock him up and halt his retreat.
laneImpact: This interaction forces Nautilus to play incredibly passively, neutralizing his lane pressure. He cannot safely fish for hooks near your tower because a failed or even a successful Dredge Line results in him taking a massive, stunned counter-trade. Consequently, your duo secures superior wave control, allowing you to slow-push waves or safely protect your carry from sudden all-ins without fear of being zoned off.
why: Nautilus relies entirely on finding a pick with Dredge Line to start a fight, but this playstyle directly feeds into your defensive strength. The moment he pulls himself toward your carry, you can instantly close the gap using Stand Behind Me. This positions you perfectly to stack Concussive Blows on him. Because Nautilus locks himself into a forward position during his hook, your quick retaliation easily stuns him mid-engage.

summary: Timing Unspeakable Horror to fear Tryndamere right as he activates Undying Rage allows Nocturne to safely waste the duration of his ultimate.
howToPlay: To win this mental game, you must manipulate the timing of your engage. Never use Spinning Slash to gap-close unless Unspeakable Horror is already on cooldown, or you have enough Fury to melt him quickly. When he attaches the tether, immediately use Spinning Slash to break the leash distance before the fear triggers. If you are forced to activate Undying Rage while tethered, use Mocking Shout to slow him down as he tries to kite you, preserving your window to land crucial critical strikes.
laneImpact: In the jungle, this interaction dictates every skirmish and counter-gank. You cannot mindlessly invade his camps because Duskbringer gives him the speed to kite you out, while Shroud of Darkness can block your Mocking Shout if you use it too predictably. If Nocturne successfully neutralizes your Undying Rage with his fear during a duel, he secures total river priority, leaving you unable to contest objectives or protect your lanes from his Paranoia.
why: This duel hinges on how you manage your five seconds of invulnerability against his crowd control. When you trigger Undying Rage to survive, Nocturne wants to tether you with Unspeakable Horror. If the fear lands right as your ultimate starts, you will spend almost the entire duration running away helplessly, wasting your DPS while his Umbra Blades passive keeps him healthy enough to finish you off once your rage fades.

summary: Teemo's Blinding Dart does not affect the damage of Infected Bonesaw, allowing Mundo to easily poke Teemo down from a safe distance.
howToPlay: To exploit this edge, shift your early purchases toward magic resistance to neutralize Noxious Trap and Toxic Shot. Use the brushes to break line of sight, throwing Infected Bonesaw whenever he tries to farm. Hold Blunt Force Trauma to execute minions and launch them at him if he runs with Move Quick. If you miss too many cleavers, activate Heart Zapper to safely clear under your turret.
laneImpact: This interaction turns a pairing that is usually oppressive for melee champions into a slow bleed for the swift scout. By constantly landing Infected Bonesaw, you push Teemo behind his minion wave, preventing him from utilizing Guerrilla Warfare to harass you. You dictate the wave tempo, protect your turret plates from his ranged pressure, and force him into awkward recall timings before you dive him with Maximum Dosage.
why: Teemo relies heavily on Blinding Dart to shut down physical attackers, but this projectile has absolutely no effect on your Infected Bonesaw. Because your cleaver deals magic damage from a safe distance, you can completely bypass his blind mechanic. Additionally, the poison from Toxic Shot is easily neutralized by the passive health regeneration of Goes Where He Pleases, making this ranged matchup surprisingly easy for you to control.

summary: Twilight Shroud (W) prevents Volibear from targeting you with Frenzied Maul (W) to get his crucial second-cast heal.
howToPlay: Never initiate trades with Twilight Shroud; instead, hold it strictly as a defensive reaction when Volibear charges with Thundering Smash. Bait out his Sky Splitter by baiting his forward movement, then poke safely with Five Point Strike. If he manages to land his first Frenzied Maul, immediately drop Twilight Shroud to deny the follow-up bite. If you mess up this timing and get marked while shroud is on cooldown, disengage immediately using Shuriken Flip to retreat.
laneImpact: Because Volibear gains passive attack speed from The Relentless Storm, he will naturally push the wave toward your tower. You cannot contest his early push directly without taking heavy damage from his Sky Splitter shield trades. If you mismanage your Twilight Shroud, Volibear will dive you effortlessly using Stormbringer to disable your turret, ending your laning phase early and giving him free reign to roam.
why: Volibear relies on Frenzied Maul to outsustain you in extended fights. Since his second bite requires a targeted mark, entering Twilight Shroud right after his first bite completely breaks his combat loop. Without this target lock, he cannot trigger his massive heal, leaving him vulnerable. However, if he lands Thundering Smash or Sky Splitter beforehand, he can survive your burst while waiting for your shroud to dissipate.

summary: Kalista's Martial Poise allows her to easily dodge Ezreal's Mystic Shot, making it hard for him to trade back when she stacks Rend.
howToPlay: To survive, use Mystic Shot almost exclusively to secure distant minions rather than trying to poke her down. Never use Arcane Shift aggressively; you must hold it to react instantly when she launches her support with Fate's Call. When trading is unavoidable, wait until she commits to a basic attack animation to throw Essence Flux, and only unleash Trueshot Barrage from out of her vision so she cannot use Martial Poise to hop out of the blast zone.
laneImpact: This mobility imbalance prevents you from contesting the wave directly. Kalista can freely slow-push or shove, knowing she can dodge your retaliation. Walking up to last-hit exposes you to her forward hops; if she connects a few spears and pulls Rend, you are forced into an early Arcane Shift. This defensive retreat drains your mana rapidly, leaving you trapped under your turret while she chips away at your gold lead.
why: Kalista's Martial Poise represents a massive hurdle for you. Every basic attack or Pierce allows her to hop in any direction, making it effortless for her to dodge your linear Mystic Shot. Because your primary damage tool misses so frequently against her constant dashes, she can safely step forward to stack spears inside you, detonating Rend for a massive health advantage while you struggle to return any meaningful poke.

summary: Sona's lack of mobility makes her an easy target for Dredge Line, allowing Nautilus to burst her down before she can scale.
howToPlay: To survive, you must treat your minion wave as an absolute shield and never step into open space when Dredge Line is off cooldown. If Nautilus steps forward aggressively, immediately activate Song of Celerity to boost your movement speed and bait his hook. Should he bypass your frontline with Depth Charge, save Crescendo to counter-engage his ADC, and quickly apply the damage-reducing Power Chord from Aria of Perseverance.
laneImpact: This constant threat of engage completely paralyzes your lane presence, forcing you to play far behind your minion wave. You cannot step up to charge Power Chord safely, which cedes bush control entirely to Nautilus. Consequently, the enemy duo can easily slow-push waves to dive you with Depth Charge or freely roam to secure map pressure while you are stuck under turret.
why: Sona struggles in this matchup because her lack of innate mobility makes her incredibly vulnerable to Nautilus's Dredge Line. Every attempt to poke with Hymn of Valor exposes you to his hook. If he lands it, the follow-up crowd control from Staggering Blow and Riptide guarantees a quick death before Aria of Perseverance can mitigate the incoming burst damage.

summary: Jax can block Siphoning Strike with Counter Strike, but Nasus's Wither severely cripples Jax's attack speed during all-ins.
howToPlay: When trading, never initiate with Leap Strike. Instead, walk up and use Empower to poke him. Save Counter Strike for when he attempts to retaliate with Siphoning Strike. If he targets you with Wither, immediately use Leap Strike to jump back to a friendly minion, disengaging until the crippling slow wears off. Do not try to fight through his attack speed reduction; wait it out before resuming your assault.
laneImpact: The lane's outcome hinges entirely on your wave management. If you blindly push, Nasus will freeze near his turret, safely farm Siphoning Strike, and sustain via Soul Eater. You must freeze the minions on your side of the lane to force him to overextend for stacks. Letting him farm uncontested means he will eventually run you down under his Fury of the Sands.
why: This matchup is defined by how you trade your defensive cooldowns. You have the ultimate tool to block his main damage source, using Counter Strike to completely negate Siphoning Strike. However, Nasus counteracts your Relentless Assault attack speed scaling with Wither, which cripples your offensive momentum. If you use your defensive stance too early, he simply slows you to a crawl and stacks his damage freely.

summary: Irelia can use Bladesurge to dodge Ahri's Charm in the minion wave, then lock her down with Flawless Duet.
howToPlay: You must absolutely hold onto Charm as a deterrent, never casting it aggressively while Irelia has low-health minions to dash to. Keep the wave frozen just outside your turret range using Orb of Deception solely to thin the incoming wave. If she lands Flawless Duet or initiates with Vanguard's Edge, immediately use Spirit Rush to dash diagonally away from her blade wall, prioritizing survival over trying to trade back.
laneImpact: This matchup forces you into defensive farming under your own turret. Because you cannot reliably land Orb of Deception or Fox-Fire without risking a sudden counter-engage, you cannot contest the lane. Any attempt to push the wave gives Irelia a longer lane to chase you down. If she freezes, you are entirely locked out of gold, leaving your jungler completely isolated.
why: Irelia's unmatched mobility within the minion wave completely neutralizes your skillshot-reliant kit. By constantly resetting Bladesurge on dying minions, she can easily bait out or dodge your Charm. Once your crowd control is wasted, she can immediately follow up with Flawless Duet to stun you, building max stacks of Ionian Fervor to shred your health pool before you can disengage.

summary: Braum's Unbreakable shield cannot block Alistar's Pulverize knockup, but Braum's Concussive Blows make extended trades dangerous for Alistar.
howToPlay: To win this, stand parallel to your ADC to prevent Alistar from hitting both of you with a single Pulverize. Hold your Stand Behind Me specifically to leap back to safety if he attempts a Headbutt displacement. When he activates Unbreakable Will to cleanse your stun, do not waste your Glacial Fissure; wait out his defensive ultimate before recommitting your crowd control, or redirect your focus to his vulnerable marksman instead.
laneImpact: This dynamic forces a tense stand-off where neither support can blindly shove the wave. Since Alistar heals through Triumphant Roar, short poke with Winter's Bite is rarely enough to force him out. Instead, lane pressure hinges on positioning; if Alistar missteps to trigger Trample, you can lock him down under your tower, turning a simple engage attempt into a disastrous recall timing that costs his team botlane priority.
why: In this heavy tank clash, the lane is dictated by how you respond to Alistar's initiation. While your Unbreakable is completely useless against the vertical knockup of his Pulverize, Alistar cannot easily disengage once he commits. If he dives in, your ability to quickly stack Concussive Blows on him turns any extended skirmish into a deadly trap, punishing his aggressive dives heavily.

summary: Sidestep or use Apprehend to reposition during Sett's Haymaker to avoid the true damage center line before executing him with Noxian Guillotine.
howToPlay: To secure your Haymaker true damage, never cast it raw. Use Facebreaker to stun Darius first, locking him in place so he cannot sidestep or disrupt you with Apprehend. If he pulls you early with Apprehend, immediately activate Knuckle Down to reset your Pit Grit punches, build your shield quickly, and aim the center of Haymaker directly where he stands. If his Noxian Guillotine is ready, use The Show Stopper to buy time or reposition him away from your wave.
laneImpact: Every trade is highly volatile, preventing passive farming. If you miss your true damage, Darius easily secures wave control and freezes near his tower, forcing you into overextended positions. A single botched duel leads to an immediate snowball, giving Darius the lane pressure to dive you or threaten your jungler during river skirmishes.
why: This matchup is a pure battle of micro-positioning during all-ins. Darius aims to stack Hemorrhage to prime Noxian Guillotine, while you rely on Grit to absorb that damage. The critical swing point is Haymaker: Darius will attempt to sidestep the central true damage line or use Apprehend to displace you during its cast, rendering your shield useless and leaving you vulnerable to his ultimate execution.

summary: Heimerdinger's relentless push with H-28G Evolution Turrets (Q) forces Twisted Fate to choose between defending his tower or using Destiny (R) to roam.
howToPlay: Spread your H-28G Evolution Turret units to avoid his Wild Cards clearing them simultaneously. Always hold CH-2 Electron Storm Grenade to interrupt him if he locks a Gold Card with Pick a Card to trade. The moment you see him back away to channel Destiny, do not follow him; instead, activate UPGRADE!!! to deploy a massive turret and maximize tower damage, punishing his absence by securing an early first turret.
laneImpact: This constant shove strips Twisted Fate of his primary weapon: his roaming potential. Every time he looks to activate Destiny, your H-28G Evolution Turret setup threatens his mid lane plates. If he leaves, you can immediately drop UPGRADE!!! to demolish his tower. This forces him into a defensive posture, neutralizing his global threat and granting your team total mid-map priority during early skirmishes.
why: Your lane dominance hinges on how H-28G Evolution Turret neutralizes Twisted Fate's map-wide pressure. While he relies on Wild Cards and Pick a Card to manage waves, your continuous automated turrets force him under tower. He cannot match this push speed early on, turning his lane into a prison where he must choose between clearing minions or abandoning his tower to find a roam.

summary: Pantheon's point-and-click Shield Vault makes it impossible for Kayn to escape early skirmishes without taking massive damage.
howToPlay: Invade Kayn's jungle during his first clear and hold Shield Vault specifically for when he attempts to cast Shadow Step near terrain. Once he is stunned, unleash a rapid Mortal Will combo followed by Comet Spear to force his Flash or secure the kill. If he manages to reach safety, immediately pivot to gank the nearest lane with Grand Starfall while his weak early-game presence prevents him from counter-ganking effectively.
laneImpact: This matchup dynamic forces Kayn to play defensively, drastically slowing down his orb collection for The Darkin Scythe. You command early priority in the river, allowing you to secure Scuttle Crabs and contest his camps with zero fear. Because Kayn cannot easily escape your invades, he must concede his jungle camps or risk dying, which heavily delays his transformation and cripples his mid-game scaling.
why: Pantheon dominates the early jungle because Kayn is extremely weak before choosing a form with The Darkin Scythe. Whenever Kayn tries to slip away through walls using Shadow Step, your point-and-click Shield Vault immediately shuts him down. This instant stun prevents him from escaping, leaving him completely exposed to a heavy Mortal Will empowered physical burst from Comet Spear before he can react.

summary: Sona's Aria of Perseverance out-sustains Janna's shield poke over time, forcing Janna to find aggressive picks with Howling Gale before Sona scales.
howToPlay: Stop playing defensively and actively hunt for Sona when she steps forward to trigger her Hymn of Valor. Coalesce your pressure by holding Howling Gale to interrupt her movement rather than throwing it randomly to clear waves. Start trades by slowing her with Zephyr first, making it impossible for her to dodge a fast knock-up. Once she unlocks Crescendo, respect the threat of her ultimate by spacing away from your ADC to avoid being stunned together, and use Monsoon immediately if she attempts to flash-engage.
laneImpact: During the early levels, Sona will use Hymn of Valor to gradually chip away at your ADC's health bar while relying on Aria of Perseverance to erase any damage you return. If you play passively, she will slowly pressure you under your turret, ruining your recall timings and locking you in lane. This prevents you from utilizing Tailwind to roam and assist your jungler, effectively giving Sona free reign to scale safely.
why: Sona's continuous healing and shielding from Aria of Perseverance easily nullifies the poke you attempt with Zephyr and the AD-boosted trades from Eye of the Storm. Because Sona scales into an unstoppable team-fight engine, your passive defensive shielding cannot match her raw area-of-effect sustain over time. To win, you must disrupt her scaling early by landing proactive Howling Gale knock-ups before she reaches her late-game power spikes.

summary: Tristana can jump directly onto Jhin with Rocket Jump and burst him down with Explosive Charge before he can cycle through his Whisper shots.
howToPlay: Monitor Jhin's Whisper ammo bar constantly. The moment he fires his fourth shot or starts reloading, immediately launch forward with Rocket Jump. Place your Explosive Charge and trigger Rapid Fire to burst him down. If he tries to retreat under his tower or if a fight goes sideways, use Buster Shot to safely disengage or push him back into your landing zone. Avoid jumping when he has his fourth shot ready to prevent receiving a massive critical blow mid-air.
laneImpact: Jhin is forced into a defensive posture, unable to step up to use Dancing Grenade to clear waves without putting himself in your jump range. Your passive Draw a Bead automatically pushes the lane, giving you constant priority and allowing you to chip away at his tower. Since Jhin must conserve his Deadly Flourish to self-peel, he cannot safely trade health, leading to early recalls and massive gold leads for you.
why: Your massive burst threat dictates this matchup. By using Rocket Jump to leap directly onto Jhin, you bypass his range advantage and force a close-quarters duel. Once on top of him, activating Rapid Fire lets you fully stack and detonate Explosive Charge in seconds. Jhin's Whisper lock prevents him from matching this raw attack speed, ensuring you delete his health bar before he can even chamber his fourth critical shot.

summary: Garen's Judgment continues to deal damage and shred armor even while Jax is spinning Counter Strike.
howToPlay: Never initiate trades with Leap Strike unless Garen's Judgment is on cooldown. Instead, walk up to farm, and if he charges with Decisive Strike, activate Counter Strike right before his strike lands to block the silence. If he starts spinning, immediately use Leap Strike to a friendly minion or ward to escape the radius. Only re-engage with Empower and Grandmaster-at-Arms once his sword stops spinning, exploiting his long cooldown window to force a heavy trade.
laneImpact: This interaction forces a highly volatile trading pattern. If you waste Counter Strike early, Garen can immediately silence you with Decisive Strike and spin you down with Judgment, forcing you out of lane or executing you with Demacian Justice. Conversely, if you bait out his spin first, you can lock him down, stack Relentless Assault, and dictate the wave's push with total impunity.
why: The duel hinges on how you use Counter Strike against Garen's spin. While Counter Strike completely blocks Garen's Decisive Strike silence, it is useless against his Judgment. Garen's spin continues to shred your armor and deal damage even while you are dodging, meaning you cannot blindly use your defensive stance to win trades if he has his main damage ability ready.

summary: Jax can use Leap Strike to jump behind Sion to dodge Decimating Smash, or stun him with Counter Strike to interrupt the channel.
howToPlay: Stand inside your own minion wave to bait his Decimating Smash. Do not initiate with Leap Strike; instead, walk up to strike him with Empower and auto-attacks. The moment he begins channeling his axe, immediately Leap Strike to a minion behind him or activate Counter Strike to cancel his charge. If he activates Soul Furnace, focus on breaking the shield quickly with Empower before he can trigger the burst damage.
laneImpact: Sion must use Decimating Smash and Soul Furnace to clear waves, which naturally pushes the minions toward you. This allows you to freeze the wave near your turret, forcing Sion to walk up into your threat range. Once frozen, you can zone him completely or threaten a dive, rendering his high health pool useless while you freely stack Relentless Assault on the minions.
why: This matchup heavily favors Jax because you possess two direct answers to Sion's primary tool, Decimating Smash. When Sion starts charging his axe, you can instantly neutralize the threat by using Leap Strike to jump behind him, or by activating Counter Strike to stun him out of the channel. Because your passive Relentless Assault and Grandmaster-at-Arms outscale his tankiness, Sion can never match your raw DPS.

summary: Kassadin's Null Sphere magic shield absorbs Corki's magic-heavy basic attacks, allowing Kassadin to scale safely into a late-game threat.
howToPlay: To survive, never use Valkyrie aggressively; always keep it to escape his Riftwalk engagements. When trading, wait for him to waste Null Sphere on a minion before shredding him with Gatling Gun. If you obtain the Package, do not waste Special Delivery trying to dive him. Instead, use the massive movement speed boost to roam to side lanes, forcing him to choose between matching your map pressure or farming under his turret.
laneImpact: During the early levels, you cannot establish a health lead because his magic shields negate your trade attempts, while your spell-casting constantly charges his Force Pulse. Once Kassadin unlocks Riftwalk, the lane dynamic shifts heavily. He can easily blink over your Phosphorus Bomb or Missile Barrage, close the distance, and chunk your health bar with Nether Blade while silencing you, forcing you to play defensively under tower.
why: Your passive, Hextech Munitions, turns your basic attacks into magic damage, which completely plays into Kassadin's hands. Whenever you try to poke him with Phosphorus Bomb or auto-attacks, he responds with Null Sphere. The magic shield from both Null Sphere and his Void Stone passive absorbs almost all your damage, allowing him to neutralize your early lane pressure and scale comfortably into a late-game monster.

summary: Malphite's Unstoppable Force is completely negated by Goes Where He Pleases, leaving him with no way to lock down or burst Mundo.
howToPlay: Constantly throw Infected Bonesaw to crack his Granite Shield and prevent it from regenerating. When pushing the wave, align low-health minions to launch them with Blunt Force Trauma directly into his face. If he steps up to trade with Thunderclap, activate Heart Zapper to absorb his burst and immediately walk over your canister from Goes Where He Pleases to stay topped off. Save Maximum Dosage for his desperate, bait-style gank attempts, walking away freely.
laneImpact: You have total freedom to dictate wave states. Since Ground Slam cannot slow your skill-based farming, you can constantly shove Malphite under his tower using Blunt Force Trauma. He cannot punish your aggression or freeze the wave because any attempt to engage with Unstoppable Force fails, allowing you to chip away at his Granite Shield and secure easy plates while he struggles to last-hit under tower.
why: Malphite relies on Unstoppable Force to set up kills or ganks, but Goes Where He Pleases entirely negates this ultimate, leaving him unable to lock you down. Meanwhile, Malphite's magic damage from Seismic Shard is easily healed back through Infected Bonesaw and Maximum Dosage, turning this lane into a war of attrition where Malphite runs out of mana long before you run out of health.

summary: Kennen can easily poke Sett with basic attacks and Q (Thundering Shuriken), using E (Lightning Rush) to escape if Sett tries to pull him with E (Facebreaker).
howToPlay: Give up early minion gold to protect your health bar. Let him push, and use the shield from Haymaker to absorb Thundering Shuriken poke. Never initiate with Facebreaker; instead, walk up threateningly with Knuckle Down to bait out his Lightning Rush. Once his escape tool is on cooldown, you have a brief window to grab him with Facebreaker. If he overcommits with Slicing Maelstrom, use The Show Stopper to carry him away from your wave and disengage.
laneImpact: You will spend the early levels pushed under your turret, struggling to secure minions. Every time you step up to trigger Pit Grit on a minion, you risk eating an Electrical Surge active. If your health drops too low from constant poke, Kennen will freeze the wave or dive you with Slicing Maelstrom. This pressure forces premature recalls, setting you behind in gold and keeping you stuck in lane while Kennen roams.
why: Kennen's ranged advantage makes this matchup highly oppressive for Sett. He will constantly harass you with basic attacks and Thundering Shuriken to stack Mark of the Storm. Whenever you try to close the gap and pull him in with Facebreaker, Kennen can instantly activate Lightning Rush to zoom away safely. This interaction denies you any proactive trade, leaving you taking free damage while your primary engage tool is wasted.

summary: Hecarim's Onslaught of Shadows can fear Ekko, preventing him from casting Chronobreak during the crucial opening seconds of a fight.
howToPlay: Track Ekko's shadow closely. When a skirmish breaks out, do not initiate immediately with your ultimate. Instead, use Devastating Charge to force him to burn Phase Dive, then wait until his health drops to about half before unleashing Onslaught of Shadows. This precise timing guarantees the fear locks him out of Chronobreak, allowing your team to execute him. If he sets up Parallel Convergence, use your knockback to push him away from his own stun zone.
laneImpact: Ekko relies on swift rotations, using Parallel Convergence to set up aggressive lane dives. However, Hecarim's superior map mobility means you can easily track his pathing and turn his ganks into disastrous counter-ganks.
