Instead, walk up to bait his slam, cast *Warrior Trickster* right as he begins his *Boulder Toss* animation, and then immediately activate *Cyclone* to spin through his defenses and secure the kill.
laneImpact: During the laning phase, Gnar is forced to play defensively even when his rage bar rises. While Mini Gnar attempts to poke with *Boomerang Throw*, your ability to gap-close means he cannot safely harass you. When he transforms into Mega Gnar, you do not have to cede wave control; instead, you can actively bait his crowd control near the minion wave, secure a health lead, and easily dive him with *Cyclone*.
why: Wukong dominates this matchup because his mobility and cloning capability directly neutralize Gnar's predictable Mega form threat. When Gnar transforms and looks for a fight-ending *Boulder Toss* or *Hyper* stun, Wukong can cast *Warrior Trickster* to leave a clone behind, absorbing the crowd control or tricking Gnar into throwing his ultimate into empty space. Without those high-impact Mega cooldowns, Gnar is easily shredded by *Golden Staff* and *Nimbus Strike*.

summary: Camille can use Hextech Ultimatum to dodge K'Sante's third Ntofo Strikes knockup, preventing him from pulling her under tower.
howToPlay: Watch K'Santé's indicators closely to know when his third Ntofo Strikes is primed. Never engage with Hookshot when his knockup is ready; instead, space him out using the outer edge of Tactical Sweep. The moment he unleashes the shockwave, cast The Hextech Ultimatum to phase through it, then immediately reset your auto-attacks with Precision Protocol to shred his health bar while he is locked in his vulnerable state.
laneImpact: The constant threat of this interaction dictates where the minion wave sits. If K'Santé controls the space, he can threaten to drag you into tower range with Path Maker. However, when you hold The Hextech Ultimatum, K'Santé is forced to play defensively, unable to commit to All Out without risking a lethal counter-engage. One mistimed dodge determines who gets frozen out of the wave.
why: This matchup is a high-stakes spacing duel revolving around K'Santé's crowd control. He relies on stacking Ntofo Strikes to setup his displacement combos. Camille's safety hinges entirely on The Hextech Ultimatum. By timing this ultimate to leap over K'Santé's third Ntofo Strikes knockup, you completely negate his ability to pull you under his tower, turning his primary offensive tool into a wasted cooldown.

summary: Poppy's Steadfast Presence blocks both Lee Sin's Sonic Wave dash and Safeguard, grounding and knocking him up.
howToPlay: Never initiate with Steadfast Presence. Instead, bait his engage by walking near walls, tempting him to use Sonic Wave. The moment he reactivates it to fly towards you, activate your shield to knock him down, then immediately position yourself to slam him into the terrain with Heroic Charge. If he attempts to escape with Safeguard after a failed gank, stand between him and his retreat path to block the jump.
laneImpact: In the jungle, this interaction neutralizes Lee Sin’s early-game skirmishing power. He cannot safely contest Scuttle Crabs or invade your camps, as any attempt to dash in results in him getting locked down. Your counter-ganks are devastating; by denying his entry or exit, you turn his high-risk dives into easy double kills for your team, keeping him starved of the early snowball he desperately needs.
why: You completely shut down Lee Sin's high-mobility playstyle because your Steadfast Presence is the ultimate counter to his entire kit. Whenever he tries to execute a target with the second activation of Sonic Wave or escape using Safeguard, activating your barrier instantly cancels his movement, grounding him and leaving him completely vulnerable to your counter-engage.

summary: Vi can use Vault Breaker to interrupt Hecarim's Devastating Charge mid-dash, neutralizing his initiation damage and knockback.
howToPlay: To win this duel, never lead with Devastating Charge if Vi is holding her dash. Instead, run at her with Spirit of Dread active to absorb her initial burst, using Rampage to stack up your damage. Once she burns Vault Breaker offensively or to escape, activate your charge to run her down. If you need to force the engage, use the unstoppable frames of Onslaught of Shadows to bypass her crowd control entirely.
laneImpact: In early skirmishes, this interaction dictates map pressure and neutral camp contests. If you blindly charge into the river, a reactive Vi will shut down your ganking threat and counter-jungle you with ease. However, forcing her to miss Vault Breaker or baiting it out flips the dynamic, allowing your sustained AoE from Rampage and healing from Spirit of Dread to quickly overwhelm her before she can stack Blast Shield.
why: This jungle matchup hinges entirely on who initiates. While Hecarim relies on the momentum of Devastating Charge to deliver his initial burst and reposition his target, Vi holds a direct answer. A well-timed Vault Breaker can collision-check Hecarim mid-dash, completely canceling his knockback and leaving him vulnerable to her Denting Blows armor shred without his initial burst advantage.

summary: Camille must bait out Teemo's Blinding Dart before using Precision Protocol, relying on Hookshot to close the gap and lock him down.
howToPlay: Never initiate a trade by immediately casting both charges of Precision Protocol. Instead, hook onto the wall with Hookshot and stun Teemo to force a panic reaction. Once he fires Blinding Dart, use the movement speed from your first Precision Protocol activation or the slow from Tactical Sweep to kite backward. As soon as the blind duration expires, re-engage immediately with the second, true damage strike of Precision Protocol to chunk his health bar.
laneImpact: This matchup shifts from early safety to absolute lane dominance the moment Camille hits level three. Teemo is forced to play defensively, unable to freely poke with Toxic Shot because stepping too far forward invites a lethal wall-dive. He must constantly hold Blinding Dart, which limits his aggressive options. Camille can easily freeze the wave near her turret, creating a long lane where Teemo cannot escape Hookshot engages.
why: Camille naturally commands this matchup despite Teemo's ranged advantage because her Hookshot completely negates his distance. While Teemo relies on Blinding Dart to nullify auto-attacks, Camille's Adaptive Defenses provides a magic shield to absorb his toxic harass. Once Blinding Dart is baited out, Camille can unleash the true damage of Precision Protocol without fear of being blinded, making his squishy health pool vanish rapidly.

summary: Mordekaiser's Realm of Death transports you to an alternate dimension, leaving all your pre-placed H-28G Evolution Turrets behind.
howToPlay: During the early levels, focus on preserving your health bar. Stand behind your own minions to minimize damage from rockets, and save Indestructible to absorb any unavoidable poke. Dodge the slow-moving CH-2 Electron Storm Grenade first, then walk forward. Once in range, pull him with Death's Grasp and immediately cast Realm of Death. Inside, activate Darkness Rise and crush him, ensuring you never cast your ultimate while stunned.
laneImpact: Before you unlock your ultimate, Heimerdinger will aggressively push the wave and try to poke you under tower. Once you have access to Realm of Death, the dynamic shifts dramatically. He can no longer safely siege your tower or contest the wave. If he attempts to deploy a massive turret using UPGRADE!!!, you can simply isolate him away from it, neutralizing his massive ultimate investment entirely.
why: Heimerdinger's entire lane presence relies on the defensive zone created by his H-28G Evolution Turret setups. However, Mordekaiser possesses the ultimate counter-measure: Realm of Death. When cast, this ultimate pulls Heimerdinger into a pocket dimension, leaving all his pre-placed H-28G Evolution Turret structures behind on the normal Rift. Deprived of his mechanical artillery, the fragile inventor is left completely defenseless against your raw physical power.

summary: Aurora can use the leap from Across the Veil (W) to reposition, but must avoid touching Veigar's Event Horizon (E).
howToPlay: To execute this flawlessly, never cast Across the Veil aggressively before Veigar uses his cage. When he drops Event Horizon, remain calm and stand near the center of the ring to avoid the stun. Use the leap from Across the Veil to adjust your footing inside the safe zone, then retaliate with Twofold Hex and The Weirding. If he misses his cage entirely, immediately trap him with Between Worlds for an easy kill.
laneImpact: In lane, this dynamic forces Veigar into a defensive posture. Every time he uses Baleful Strike to stack his passive on minions, you can aggressively step forward. Since you can easily dodge Dark Matter with basic movement, Veigar is forced to waste Event Horizon defensively. This drains his mana rapidly, gives you permanent wave priority, and allows you to chip away at his health with Twofold Hex procs.
why: Aurora holds a distinct advantage because her mobility completely disrupts Veigar's static zoning. While Veigar relies heavily on trapping you inside Event Horizon to guarantee hits with Dark Matter and Baleful Strike, your kit offers superior evasion. The leap from Across the Veil gives you the perfect tool to reposition safely within his boundaries, letting you completely bypass his stun threat while maintaining offensive pressure.

summary: Ambessa can react to Ekko's Parallel Convergence stun with Repudiation, and use Public Execution to lock him down before he can cast Chronobreak.
howToPlay: When fighting Ekko, never waste Repudiation early; hold it specifically for the moment his Parallel Convergence bubble activates on you to absorb the shield-break and stun. Constantly track the position of his hologram. Once his health drops below half, immediately unleash Public Execution to suppress him. This prevents him from using Chronobreak entirely, ensuring a clean execution before he can reset the fight.
laneImpact: In the jungle, this advantage translates to total river dominance. Ekko cannot safely contest neutral objectives or battle for Scuttle Crabs, as he cannot win isolated duels against your kit. You can aggressively invade his camps, knowing that any defensive Parallel Convergence he drops will be turned against him. This pressure forces him to concede farm, keeping him permanently behind and unable to pressure your lanes.
why: Ambessa dominates this jungle matchup by hard-countering Ekko's primary setup. When Ekko attempts to trigger his Parallel Convergence stun, your Repudiation absorbs the burst and negates the crowd control completely. Furthermore, her Public Execution provides a reliable suppression that locks him down, preventing him from activating Chronobreak to escape or heal, turning his predictable assassination attempts into lethal traps.

summary: Camille's Adaptive Defenses physical shield completely absorbs Garen's Decisive Strike damage, allowing her to win short trades.
howToPlay: To survive, let Camille push the minions toward your side. If she triggers Adaptive Defenses, immediately back away and wait out the two-second shield before trying to fight back with Judgment. When she engages with Hookshot, activate Courage to mitigate the incoming stun and the true damage from her second Precision Protocol strike. Once her shield is on cooldown, you can look for short trades before executing her with Demacian Justice.
laneImpact: You cannot afford to play aggressively or trade blows randomly. Camille will use Tactical Sweep to poke you down and prevent your Perseverance from regenerating your health. If you constantly push the wave, she can easily freeze it near her tower and run you down with Hookshot or trap you with The Hextech Ultimatum, forcing an early recall or costing your team jungle pressure.
why: This lane is dictated by how Camille's Adaptive Defenses neutralizes your main trade opener. Whenever you charge in with Decisive Strike, her auto-attack triggers a massive physical shield that completely absorbs your silence's damage. Because Garen relies on this initial burst to chunk her down before spinning with Judgment, her passive shield consistently wins her these short skirmishes, leaving you with negative trades if you force the issue.

summary: Sona can neutralize the pick potential of Zilean's Temporal Mirage speed boost by counter-engaging with Crescendo or escaping with Song of Celerity.
howToPlay: Always hold Song of Celerity to reactively mirror Zilean's Temporal Mirage; do not waste your movement speed aura for casual poke. When he speeds up to engage, activate your aura to pull your carry back safely. If he overcommits, use Crescendo to lock him down before he can cast Chronoshift on his target. If his ultimate does land, immediately swap targets or stall the fight with Aria of Perseverance to waste his revival window.
laneImpact: Zilean constantly seeks to zone you with Time Bomb, forcing you to sustain through the poke using Aria of Perseverance. When Zilean uses Temporal Mirage to aggressively position for a double-bomb stun, your immediate speed boost or stun response prevents a complete collapse. Neither side can easily force a recall or dive, turning the lane into a neutral stalemate where lane priority depends entirely on ultimate cooldowns.
why: This matchup is a pure race of execution and timing, centered on Zilean using Temporal Mirage to force fights with double Time Bomb stuns. Sona can shut down his aggressive speed boosts directly. She neutralizes his pick potential by using Song of Celerity to outrun his chase or casting Crescendo to freeze his acceleration in its tracks, balancing the lane's pressure.

summary: Annie's instant Pyromania stun immediately cancels Katarina's Death Lotus, leaving her completely defenseless.
howToPlay: Always maintain three or four stacks of Pyromania whenever Katarina has her ultimate available. Never waste your stun on raw poke if she is looking to engage. Hold onto your stun-charged Disintegrate or Incinerate until she commits with Shunpo and begins her channel. If you accidentally discharge your stun prematurely, immediately activate Molten Shield to absorb her initial burst and retreat safely under your tower until your passive is fully recharged.
laneImpact: This matchup dynamic forces Katarina to play incredibly passively, preventing her from aggressively trading with Shunpo. You can easily control the wave with Incinerate and poke her whenever she tries to collect daggers from Bouncing Blade. Since she cannot safely channel her ultimate, she is forced to concede lane priority, allowing you to chip her tower and deny her crucial gold.
why: Katarina relies entirely on her ultimate to wipe out her lane opponent, but your passive Pyromania completely shuts down her offensive threat. The moment she jumps in to channel Death Lotus, any offensive spell you throw with four stacks instantly interrupts her spin. This leaves her extremely vulnerable in melee range with no escape tools, turning her primary kill window into a death trap.

summary: Taliyah's Unraveled Earth will stun you instantly if you attempt to use Astral Flight over her minefield.
howToPlay: To survive, treat Astral Flight purely as a late-reaction retreat tool, and never use it offensively or parallel to her position. Always keep yourself positioned away from terrain to limit her Rock Surfing approach angles. Place your Singularity defensively to slow her push from maximum range. If she misses Seismic Shove, you have a brief window to channel Breath of Light, but you must cancel it immediately if she lays down Unraveled Earth.
laneImpact: Because you cannot fly safely, you are forced to clear waves defensively from a distance. If you step up to drop Singularity on the wave, Taliyah can zone you with Threaded Volley or setup a deadly Seismic Shove into her mines. This denies you early Cosmic Creator stacks, giving her free rein to use Rock Surfing and Weaver's Wall to roam while you remain pinned under your tower.
why: The core of this matchup lies in how Taliyah completely shuts down your mobility. The moment you activate Astral Flight to reposition or escape, any overlap with her Unraveled Earth minefield triggers an instant stun. This interaction strips away your main defensive tool and safety net, leaving your channeled Breath of Light extremely vulnerable to being interrupted by her Seismic Shove combo.

summary: Lillia's high movement speed from Blooming Blows makes it hard to land Cunning Sweep, though Ambessa can block Lilting Lullaby with Repudiation.
howToPlay: To survive and win, never initiate with Public Execution while she has max stacks of Blooming Blows. Instead, wait in brush to ambush her, using Lacerate to apply a heavy slow. Save Repudiation strictly for the exact moment the drowsy indicator from Lilting Lullaby is about to turn into sleep. If she manages to kite your initial Cunning Sweep, immediately use Drakehound's Step to dash backward and disengage rather than chasing her down.
laneImpact: This dynamic forces you into a defensive farming pattern, as Lillia can easily kite you out in open river skirmishes. If she lands Swirlseed from afar, she can safely trigger Lilting Lullaby to force your Repudiation or secure a kill. You will constantly struggle to contest neutral objectives directly, losing early crab priority unless your lanes collapse to lock her down.
why: Lillia dominates this jungle duel because the bonus movement speed she gains from stacking Blooming Blows allows her to effortlessly dance around the outer edge of your Cunning Sweep, rendering your main damage and knock-up highly unreliable. While you have the tools to mitigate her sleep setup by timing Repudiation perfectly against Lilting Lullaby, her constant mobility makes landing your full offensive rotation an uphill battle.

summary: Ahri can interrupt Talon's Noxian Diplomacy leap with a well-timed Charm, stopping his burst before it starts.
howToPlay: Always hold onto Charm when Talon steps forward; never cast it aggressively unless his Noxian Diplomacy is on cooldown. Stand near the center of the lane to easily clear with Orb of Deception, then immediately look at the side lanes. If Talon manages to slip away using Assassin's Path over a wall, do not blindly follow his path. Instead, use Spirit Rush to quickly cross the river safely and counter-gank him before his Shadow Assault can surprise your allies.
laneImpact: This interaction forces Talon to play defensively, allowing you to use Orb of Deception to constantly push the waves under his tower. Because he cannot safely dash onto you, he loses the priority needed to utilize Assassin's Path for early map rotations. You dictate the pace of the lane, forcing him to choose between losing gold to his turret or taking heavy damage from your Fox-Fire while attempting to clear.
why: Ahri dominates this matchup because her Charm completely shuts down Talon's primary engagement tool. Whenever Talon attempts to close the gap using Noxian Diplomacy, a well-timed heart stops his leap mid-air, leaving him vulnerable and unable to apply his Blade's End stacks. By neutralizing his main gap-closer, you prevent him from executing his burst combo and safely disengage or turn the trade in your favor.

summary: Wukong can use Warrior Trickster to block Evelynn's Allure mark or absorb her Hate Spike spikes with his clone.
howToPlay: When hunting Evelynn, never initiate with Warrior Trickster. Instead, gap-close directly using Nimbus Strike and begin shredding her armor with Golden Staff. Hold your clone until the heart icon of her Allure is fully charged. Once she tries to trigger the charm, activate your clone to absorb her Hate Spike. If she attempts to escape using her Last Caress ultimate, immediately follow her retreat with the movement speed boost from Cyclone to secure the kill.
laneImpact: This interaction strips away Evelynn's early pressure in the river and her own camps. She cannot contest objectives or scuttle crabs because she risks a lethal counter-engage if she tries to mark you. Even after she unlocks Demon Shade, your threatening presence in her jungle limits her ganking paths, as you can easily shadow her lanes and neutralize her pick potential with a well-timed clone.
why: Wukong completely dismantles Evelynn's assassination sequence. When she targets you with her Allure mark, casting Warrior Trickster creates a decoy that easily intercepts her incoming Hate Spike or absorbs the charm trigger itself. Because her burst depends on triggering that mark, wasting her primary crowd control on your clone leaves her incredibly vulnerable. Your Stone Skin armor bonus then ensures you survive any residual damage while beating her down.

summary: Rumble's primary damage comes from Flamespitter, which is completely unaffected by Teemo's Blinding Dart.
howToPlay: To win this, activate Scrap Shield the moment Teemo steps up to apply Toxic Shot, absorbing his poke while you close the distance. Never activate Junkyard Titan's overheat silence unless his Blinding Dart is on cooldown. Save your Electro Harpoon to punish his Move Quick activation; once he is slowed, unleash an empowered Flamespitter. If you run into a Noxious Trap, immediately back off and use The Equalizer to clear the wave safely from afar.
laneImpact: Since Blinding Dart cannot stop Flamespitter, Teemo must constantly use Move Quick to stay out of your reach. If he missteps, your Electro Harpoon slows him, allowing you to force heavy trades. However, if you blindly chase him into his Noxious Trap, you will lose control of the wave, forcing a bad recall that gives him free tower pressure and delays your rotations to skirmishes.
why: This matchup revolves around Teemo trying to neutralize your damage with Blinding Dart, but failing because your primary threat is Flamespitter, a spell completely immune to blind. While his Toxic Shot inflicts continuous ranged harass, your Scrap Shield absorbs his initial poke. The lane remains even because Teemo's ranged advantage allows him to poke you down if you fail to manage the distance between his auto-attacks and your cone of fire.

summary: Sona can nullify Lux's Lucent Singularity poke with Aria of Perseverance, meaning Lux must land Light Binding to set up an all-in burst before Sona outscales.
howToPlay: Never throw your Light Binding randomly; hold it as a threat. Wait for Sona to step forward to trigger her Power Chord or poke with Hymn of Valor, as her movement becomes predictable during her attack animation. Punish this exact window with a quick bind-and-burst combo. If you miss your projectile, immediately step back and respect her Song of Celerity counter-engage, playing defensively until your cooldowns return to avoid being chunked down.
laneImpact: Standard trading patterns will bleed your mana pool dry while Sona comfortably keeps her carry healthy. If you passively throw out Lucent Singularity, you lose pressure, allowing Sona to safely scale towards her ultimate Crescendo. This passive state forces your jungler to play without bot-lane priority, as Sona's team-wide buffs from Hymn of Valor and Song of Celerity will gradually secure lane control and drake priority.
why: Sona's Aria of Perseverance completely neutralizes your standard Lucent Singularity poke, turning this lane into a ticking clock. Because her healing and shield scale immensely into the late game, simple war of attrition favors her. To break this passive sustain loop, you must fish for a decisive Light Binding to lock her down and execute a full burst rotation before her defensive utility makes her team unkillable.

summary: Aria of Perseverance easily nullifies Tormented Shadow poke, allowing Sona to safely scale into her dominant late game.
howToPlay: Always stand behind your minion wave to block her Dark Binding trajectory while maintaining maximum range. Keep Song of Celerity ready to dodge her unexpected skillshots or to quickly escape if she attempts to flash-engage with Soul Shackles. If your ADC gets caught by her root, do not panic; immediately cast Aria of Perseverance to absorb the burst from Tormented Shadow and use your Power Chord to weaken her follow-up.
laneImpact: This matchup turns the lane into a slow, controlled push where you dictate the wave's position. Since Tormented Shadow inevitably damages the minions when Morgana tries to poke, she will constantly push the wave toward your tower. You can easily hold the minions just outside your turret range using Aria of Perseverance to sustain through the incoming damage, denying her any real tower pressure while securing safe farm.
why: Morgana relies on slowly chipping away at your health using Tormented Shadow. However, your Aria of Perseverance completely neutralizes this damage with its combined heal and shield, turning her primary zoning tool into wasted mana. Because Morgana cannot easily break through your defensive aura without landing a risky Dark Binding, you safely bypass her early-game pressure and effortlessly scale toward your overwhelming late-game teamfighting power.

howToPlay: Drop some last-hits if it avoids free burst. Key timing: your windows return after he spends resources (rage/cooldowns) or when you come back with an item spike. Decision: if you can’t realistically catch him in lane, stabilize and convert your level-5 spike into Herald/dragon presence, not forced duels.
laneImpact: If you eat two rotations, you lose the HP needed to threaten all-ins. He can hold you under turret and deny priority, which hurts your objective fights. Midgame, he can also dip in/out and bait your ult timing without giving you the right fight.
why: Renekton is unfavorable because he dictates short explosive trades then exits. Shyvana wants continuous fights where stats and sustained DPS win. Renekton breaks that rhythm: chunk, stun, disengage—no clean conversion for you.

summary: Annie can easily predict Yone's return point during Soul Unbound to land a guaranteed Pyromania-charged Incinerate.
howToPlay: Never throw Disintegrate for farm unless you have at least three Pyromania charges ready to instantly react. When Yone gathers wind for his Mortal Steel dash, activate Molten Shield to gain the movement speed needed to sidestep his knockup. If he commits with Soul Unbound, do not panic run; instead, walk toward his starting mark. Cast Incinerate right onto his return portal to lock him down, then drop Summon: Tibbers to turn his aggressive dive into a lethal counter-burst.
laneImpact: Yone's constant threat of a third-cast Mortal Steel tornado forces you to concede early wave control, pushing you under tower. If you waste your stun, he will immediately punish you with Soul Unbound to trade heavily and force a premature recall. This constant pressure limits your ability to roam, locking you in lane while he dictates the early lane priority and pressures your health bar.
why: While Yone dominates long skirmishes with the mobility of Mortal Steel and mixed damage from Way of the Hunter, his aggression is highly predictable. When he projects forward using Soul Unbound, his original body remains tethered. By watching his spirit's duration, you can position yourself near his physical anchor and prepare a Pyromania stun with Incinerate the exact microsecond he is forced to snap back.

summary: Camille can use Hookshot to bait out Gwen's Hallowed Mist, then re-engage once the zone expires to land Precision Protocol.
howToPlay: To win, position yourself constantly near the top-lane walls to make your Hookshot casts unpredictable. Hook onto a wall to bait Gwen into panic-casting Hallowed Mist, then immediately abort the re-engage by dropping backward. Wait out her four-second zone of safety, then immediately activate Precision Protocol and use its bonus movement speed to outmaneuver her Snip Snip! cones. If she activates Needlework, use the untargetability of The Hextech Ultimatum to dodge her final, most damaging needle volley.
laneImpact: Every trade hinges on wave positioning and cooldown tracking. When Gwen has Snip Snip! fully stacked, you must space backward, using Tactical Sweep to farm safely and slow her advance. Wasting Hookshot aggressively without popping her Hallowed Mist first invites Gwen to run you down with Needlework and Skip 'n Slash. A single misstep on either side completely shifts the wave control and lane priority, leading to massive health differentials.
why: This matchup is a pure spacing duel dictated by how you interact with Gwen's untargetability. Camille relies on Hookshot to threaten engagements, but Gwen can completely neutralize this pressure with Hallowed Mist. Because Gwen gains bonus resistances inside her mist, forcing a fight there is suicide. The lane revolves around baiting this defensive zone with fake Hookshot threats, allowing you to strike with Precision Protocol once she is vulnerable.

summary: Hold your Apprehend and Noxian Guillotine to bait out Fiora's Riposte, as parrying either will lose you the fight.
howToPlay: To win, you must bait out her parry. Walk up and use Crippling Strike to slow her, then walk with her instead of immediately casting Apprehend. Force her to guess when your hook or Noxian Guillotine is coming. If she wastes Riposte, you have a clear window to strike with the outer ring of Decimate and stack Hemorrhage to maximum. If she triggers Grand Challenge, hug a wall immediately to deny her the final vital.
laneImpact: Every trade becomes a high-stakes waiting game where you cannot commit to an all-in unless Riposte is down. If you blindly throw out Apprehend, Fiora will stun you, reset her vitals with Grand Challenge, and easily shred you. This forces you to play defensively near your turret, ceding early wave control and making it difficult to stack Hemorrhage to reach your Noxian Might power spike.
why: Fiora holds the upper hand because her Riposte completely neutralizes your two most impactful tools: the displacement of Apprehend and the execution damage of Noxian Guillotine. While you want to stack Hemorrhage through prolonged trades, her Duelist's Dance and Lunge allow her to strike vitals and chip away your health before you can safely land the outer edge of Decimate.

summary: Vladimir can use Sanguine Pool to dodge the initial impact and stun of Summon: Tibbers, wasting Annie's primary burst tool.
howToPlay: To win this mental game, sit on three stacks of Pyromania instead of four. This hides your threat. Walk forward with Molten Shield to bait his Sanguine Pool, or use Incinerate to force a panic reaction without wasting your stun. Only drop Summon: Tibbers once he emerges from his pool or if he wastes Transfusion on a minion while his pool is on its long cooldown. If he refuses to bite, use your stun threat to zone him off the wave.
laneImpact: Vladimir relies on Transfusion to shrug off your poke, turning the lane into a battle of attrition. You cannot simply whittle him down. If you throw your stun carelessly, you lose all lane pressure, allowing him to clear waves with Tides of Blood and scale freely. The lane becomes a tense standoff where your level five spike is neutralized unless you can bait his untargetability before committing your ultimate.
why: This matchup revolves around a high-stakes reaction game. Your explosive burst depends entirely on landing Summon: Tibbers with Pyromania active. However, Vladimir can completely negate this dive potential using Sanguine Pool to melt into the ground, dodging both the initial damage and the stun. Because Disintegrate and Incinerate cannot force his pool reliably on their own, this interaction dictates the tempo of every single engagement.

summary: Poppy's Steadfast Presence blocks both Hecarim's Devastating Charge and Onslaught of Shadows, grounding him and leaving him highly vulnerable.
howToPlay: You must track her Steadfast Presence cooldown obsessively. Never start your Devastating Charge or cast Onslaught of Shadows while that golden circle is active or available. Instead, bait her into wasting it by running at her using only the movement speed from Warpath, then farming with Rampage and Spirit of Dread. If she triggers her barrier preemptively, you have a brief window to strike; if she holds it, focus entirely on clearing camps and counter-ganking where she is absent.
laneImpact: In the jungle, this matchup neutralizes your early gank pressure and skirmishing power. You cannot contest crabs or invade her territory because any duel near walls becomes a nightmare. If she catches you with her barrier up, she stops your Devastating Charge, leaving you stranded in her range. This forced passivity allows her to secure scuttles easily and rotate to lanes faster, draining your map pressure.
why: Poppy's Steadfast Presence is a direct, active counter to your entire mobile toolkit. The moment you activate Devastating Charge to engage or attempt to initiate a teamfight using Onslaught of Shadows, her protective barrier instantly interrupts your movement. It grounds you, inflicts magic damage, and leaves you completely immobile, turning your main sources of engagement and escape into self-inflicted crowd control.

summary: Brand can easily land his Sear stun on you if you stand still to channel Breath of Light.
howToPlay: Never throw your Sear blindly while he is actively moving. Instead, patiently wait for the exact moment he activates Breath of Light to lock himself in place, or when he flies in a predictable straight line with Astral Flight. Instantly tag him with Conflagration to apply Blaze, then throw your stun. If you miss this combo, immediately retreat behind your minions to avoid his Singularity pull, waiting out your cooldowns before stepping up again.
laneImpact: During the laning phase, Aurelion Sol will constantly try to drop Singularity to collect Cosmic Creator stacks from minions. If he steps up to execute them with Breath of Light, your threat of a sudden Sear stun forces him to cancel his channel or take massive damage. This prevents him from shoving you under tower easily, keeping the lane neutral and forcing both of you to trade health heavily whenever cooldowns are up.
why: This matchup is defined by how you exploit Aurelion Sol's self-lock. To channel Breath of Light, he must stand completely still, which completely neutralizes his ability to dodge. This stationary window makes him an incredibly easy target for your Sear projectile. By priming him first with Conflagration or a quick Pillar of Flame, you can instantly trigger your Blaze stun, interrupting his main damage source and winning the burst trade.

summary: Xin Zhao's Crescent Guard can knock Viego away and block his follow-up after Viego attempts to engage with Spectral Maw.
howToPlay: When contesting camps, track Viego's charge animation on Spectral Maw. Do not panic-cast your ultimate; wait for him to commit his dash, then instantly deploy Crescent Guard to push him away. Once his stun is wasted, immediately counter-engage using Audacious Charge followed by Wind Becomes Lightning to slow him, then execute your Three Talon Strike knock-up to finish him off before he can escape back into Harrowed Path.
laneImpact: This interaction turns the jungle matchup into a strict race for level five. Once you unlock Crescent Guard, Viego cannot safely contest epic monsters or invade your camps. You can aggressively secure scuttle crabs and start objectives knowing his Harrowed Path flanks are easily countered, forcing Viego into a passive farming style while you dictate the map's overall speed.
why: Xin Zhao naturally dominates Viego because his defensive ultimate completely shuts down Viego's primary engage tool. When Viego attempts to slide forward with Spectral Maw to lock you down, activating Crescent Guard immediately knocks him back. This isolates Viego outside his preferred range and invalidates his follow-up burst from Blade of the Ruined King, leaving him highly vulnerable in the jungle.

summary: Jinx lacks the built-in mobility to escape Corki's Special Delivery burn zone, making her highly vulnerable to package-delivery dives.
howToPlay: Capitalize on your package spawn times to dictate the skirmishes. When diving, wait for her to lock herself in place casting Zap! or farming with Switcheroo! rockets, then execute Special Delivery directly behind her to block her retreat. If she counters with Flame Chompers!, use Valkyrie to reposition safely or clean up with Missile Barrage and Phosphorus Bomb from safety. Do not sit on your package; use its threat immediately to zone her off the farm.
laneImpact: This vulnerability dictates the tempo of the entire dragon lane. Before you collect Hextech Munitions, Jinx can try to push with Switcheroo! and poke with Zap!. However, the moment your package is ready, she is forced to play extremely defensively, conceding wave control and priority. You can easily crash waves, force her under tower, and threaten a dive she cannot easily escape without her Flame Chompers! saving her.
why: Jinx relies entirely on Get Excited! for mobility, which requires a takedown first. This leaves her completely defenseless against your Special Delivery. Because she lacks any built-in dashes to escape the blazing trail, a well-aimed package-delivery dive forces her to burn Flash or melt inside the burn zone. Her Switcheroo! rockets cannot match the sudden, overwhelming burst and displacement of your package engage.

summary: Vladimir can use Sanguine Pool (W) to dodge the initial damage and trapping effect of Between Worlds (R).
howToPlay: Force his defense early by poking continuously with Twofold Hex and triggering Spirit Abjuration. Never initiate with Between Worlds. Instead, harass him until he is forced to panic-cast Sanguine Pool to survive your basic abilities. Once he emerges from his pool, he is extremely vulnerable; that is your cue to immediately drop Between Worlds to trap him and use Across the Veil to maneuver around him safely while finishing him off.
laneImpact: Because Vladimir relies on Transfusion to sustain, keeping the minions crashed under his turret forces him to choose between securing last hits with his single-target drain or using Tides of Blood, which costs him health. Pushing him in constantly limits his opportunities to trade with you. This pressure prevents him from generating a lead, letting you chip away at his tower while he struggles to match your speed.
why: Aurora dictates this matchup because Spirit Abjuration matches Vladimir's passive healing while Twofold Hex provides superior wave clear. However, you cannot simply burst him down with your ultimate; a skilled Vladimir will always use Sanguine Pool to slip through the boundary of Between Worlds, completely avoiding the lockdown and initial damage. This turns the lane into a battle of attrition where raw wave pressure beats his scaling.

summary: Galio can absorb Ahri's Charm (E) combo with Shield of Durand (W) damage reduction, and lock her down with Justice Punch (E) when she dashes with Spirit Rush (R).
howToPlay: To survive this lane, you must play a war of attrition. Use your Orb of Deception at maximum range to thin the wave and poke him simultaneously, utilizing Essence Theft to sustain through his retaliatory Winds of War. Never initiate with Charm; instead, hold it defensively to interrupt his Justice Punch if he charges at you. Only commit your Spirit Rush to chase once he has completely wasted his Shield of Durand, leaving him vulnerable to magic damage.
laneImpact: Because you cannot easily threaten him with solo kills, Galio can freely clear waves using Winds of War and Colossal Smash to shove you under turret. This constant pressure limits your roam timers, while his Hero's Entrance allows him to impact side lanes much faster than you can follow. Any trade you force usually ends with you losing more health to his passive-infused melee swings.
why: Galio naturally blunts your assassination potential because Shield of Durand grants him massive magic damage reduction, allowing him to easily absorb your entire Charm and Orb of Deception burst. Furthermore, his Justice Punch acts as an excellent zoning tool that can knock you out of the air right as you attempt to reposition or chase with Spirit Rush. This makes direct, aggressive skirmishing highly unfavorable for you.

summary: Mundo's passive blocks the knockback from Devastating Charge, but Hecarim's sustained healing from Spirit of Dread keeps him competitive in teamfights.
howToPlay: To win the skirmishes, actively body-block Hecarim's Devastating Charge for your allies when Goes Where He Pleases is active, wasting his main tool. Keep your distance with Infected Bonesaw to decay his movement speed and weaken his passive damage. If he commits with Onslaught of Shadows and activates Spirit of Dread, disengage temporarily to let his healing zone expire before triggering Maximum Dosage and Blunt Force Trauma to crush him.
laneImpact: Because both champions clear camps incredibly fast, this matchup quickly escalates into a map-wide skirmishing race. Hecarim relies on Devastating Charge to secure early ganks, but your ability to ignore this displacement makes you a formidable counter-ganker. If you clash in the river, your Infected Bonesaw slows him down, neutralizing his passive damage scaling, though his Spirit of Dread keeps him healthy enough to contest objectives.
why: This jungle matchup centers on a direct clash of sustain and displacement immunity. When Hecarim charges, Goes Where He Pleases completely absorbs the knockback of Devastating Charge, stripping away his primary initiation power. However, you cannot easily burst him down; Hecarim counteracts your tankiness with Spirit of Dread, draining massive health in close-quarters skirmishes to match your own natural recovery.

summary: Bard can predict Rakan's Grand Entrance and use Cosmic Binding to stun him as he lands near a wall or his ally.
howToPlay: Never throw Cosmic Binding blindly; hold it specifically to react to Rakan's forward dash. Stand near terrain to tempt his jump, then aim your projectile directly at your ally's feet the moment Rakan begins his Grand Entrance animation. If he coordinates The Quickness to charm you before you can react, immediately cast Tempered Fate on his backline to isolate him, or escape through a wall using Magical Journey to reset the engagement.
laneImpact: Missed spells dictate the lane's pressure. If Rakan wastes Grand Entrance, his threat vanishes, allowing you to pressure him with Meep-infused attacks from Traveler's Call. Conversely, if your Cosmic Binding misses, Rakan will instantly force trades, shielding his partner with Battle Dance to negate your poke. Health pools swing wildly based on these quick skirmishes, making passive farming impossible as both supports constantly fish for baiting opportunities.
why: This matchup is a high-speed duel of reflexes centered on Rakan's dash and your crowd control. The entire lane hinges on Grand Entrance. Because Rakan must commit to his landing spot, his predictable trajectory allows you to cast Cosmic Binding preemptively. By targeting his landing location, you can easily stun him against the very ally he tries to knock up or a nearby wall, turning his aggressive jump into a self-inflicted trap.

summary: Volibear's Frenzied Maul allows him to win sustained duels against Amumu, meaning Amumu must avoid early 1v1s in the river.
howToPlay: To survive, path to the opposite side of the map from Volibear at level one to guarantee a safe farm. If he invades your jungle, do not try to defend your camps; instead, use Bandage Toss on a distant jungle monster to escape through walls. Hold your Curse of the Sad Mummy exclusively for coordinated teamfights near objectives, where your superior crowd control can neutralize him before he can activate Stormbringer.
laneImpact: This matchup dynamic forces you to yield control of the early Scuttle Crabs. If Volibear catches you in the river, his Thundering Smash and Sky Splitter combo will lock you down and shield him, leading to your death or a forced Flash. You cannot contest neutral camps directly, which slows your jungle clearing tempo and delays your access to crucial teamfighting power spikes.
why: Volibear dominates early skirmishes because his Frenzied Maul provides immense healing and biting damage during sustained fights. While Amumu relies on consistent magic damage from Despair and Tantrum to clear and fight, he lacks the immediate burst to execute the bear. Once Volibear marks you with his first bite, his subsequent heals completely outpace your early damage output, making direct river duels mathematical suicide.

summary: Janna can easily react to Rell's engage dash with a quick Howling Gale, canceling her jump mid-air and leaving her vulnerable.
howToPlay: To execute this perfectly, stand parallel to your marksman and never use Howling Gale offensively. You must hold this storm specifically to react to her leap. If she attempts to walk up, slow her with Zephyr to waste her time. In the rare event that she catches you off-guard with a Flash engage, immediately channel Monsoon to blow her away and heal up before she can chain her crowd control.
laneImpact: Since Rell cannot safely jump in without being knocked down, she is forced to play passively behind her minions. This loss of threat allows you to walk up and harass her with Zephyr constantly. You can pressure their duo under tower, secure a significant gold lead for your marksman, and safely protect any counter-poke with Eye of the Storm without fearing a sudden hard engage.
why: This matchup is highly advantageous for you because Rell relies entirely on her jump to initiate fights, which is incredibly easy to disrupt. Whenever she leaps forward, you can instantly release a quick Howling Gale to knock her out of the air. This completely cancels her crowd control, leaves her dismounted and extremely slow, and wastes her primary tool while your ADC remains completely safe from her engage.

summary: Kha'Zix deals massive isolation damage with Taste Their Fear, making jungle duels highly dangerous for Darius unless he can fight near camps.
howToPlay: Never fight Kha'Zix in the open river. When clearing, pull camps like Raptors or Krugs slightly outward so you can fight him while standing next to them, neutralizing his isolated Taste Their Fear damage. If he initiates with Leap, immediately pull him with Apprehend to disrupt his momentum, then apply Crippling Strike to slow him down. If he uses Void Assault to reposition, focus on staying near any active target to avoid isolation until you can execute him with Noxian Guillotine.
laneImpact: You lose the freedom to contest Scuttle Crabs or invade blindly. Walking alone through the river becomes a massive liability, as Kha'Zix can use Leap to ambush you. This forces you to concede early river priority and play defensively around your camps. If you get caught isolated, you will be forced to burn flash or die, giving him total control over the early neutral objectives.
why: This matchup is defined by how Kha'Zix exploits your isolation. In the open river, his Taste Their Fear deals devastating isolated damage, bursting you down before you can stack Hemorrhage. While you excel in extended fights, his initial burst from Unseen Threat coupled with stealth from Void Assault prevents you from landing the outer edge of Decimate to heal, leaving you dead before you can retaliate.

summary: Tristana's Rocket Jump all-in can be neutralized if Yunara uses Kanmei's Steps to reposition or Untouchable Shadow to dodge the Explosive Charge stack accumulation.
howToPlay: To survive, you must play defensively and focus on lane discipline. Never initiate with Rocket Jump unless you see Yunara waste Kanmei's Steps or her ultimate Transcend One's Self is on cooldown. Instead, poke safely using Rapid Fire when she steps up to farm. If she activates her trance and chases with Untouchable Shadow, immediately disengage using Buster Shot to push her away and reset the distance before she stacks her damage.
laneImpact: Because your main offensive tool is so easily neutralized, you cannot safely push or force trades. If you waste Rocket Jump aggressively, you are left completely vulnerable to her Arc of Judgment slow and high sustained damage. You will often be forced to farm under tower, using Draw a Bead to safely secure last hits while Yunara controls the wave tempo and chips away at your tower plates.
why: Yunara naturally out-dpses you in extended trades because of her passive Vow of the First Lands and the attack speed from Cultivation of Spirit. Your primary win condition is a burst all-in using Explosive Charge. However, Yunara can easily neutralize your Rocket Jump engage. She can activate Kanmei's Steps to quickly run out of your range, or use Untouchable Shadow to dash away, preventing you from stacking your bomb.

summary: Shen's Spirit's Refuge blocks Camille's Precision Protocol attacks, but Camille can interrupt his Stand United with Hookshot.
howToPlay: Never commit your second *Precision Protocol* strike if Shen is standing inside his protective zone; instead, use the movement speed to disengage and wait out *Spirit's Refuge*. Bait his *Shadow Dash* by angling your *Tactical Sweep* from maximum range. Most importantly, always hold onto *Hookshot* when Shen has his ultimate ready, staying close enough to the brush or walls to instantly latch on and stun him the moment his channel begins.
laneImpact: Short trades are incredibly tense because of your overlapping shields. If you trigger *Adaptive Defenses* while he has *Ki Barrier* up, you will both absorb each other's initial burst. The lane remains even as long as you match his push, but the dynamic shifts dramatically once Shen reaches level five. Any failed attempt to cancel his ultimate means he turns the map in his team's favor while you slowly push his tower.
why: This skill matchup revolves around a direct clash of defensive utility. Shen can completely nullify your primary burst by deploying *Spirit's Refuge* to block both strikes of your *Precision Protocol*. However, you hold the ultimate tool to negate his global map pressure, as your *Hookshot* can immediately interrupt the channel of his *Stand United*, keeping him trapped in lane with you.

summary: Pantheon's point-and-click Shield Vault (W) stun setup is too fast to react to, and his Aegis Assault (E) blocks all of your frontal burst damage.
howToPlay: Absorb the pressure and prioritize surviving. Never use Shuriken Flip offensively unless his Shield Vault is on cooldown. If he jumps on you, immediately drop Twilight Shroud to buy time. Wait out his Aegis Assault before attempting to trigger your Assassin's Mark. If he raises his shield, use your mobility from Perfect Execution to dash behind him, bypassing his frontal protection to land your damage.
laneImpact: You cannot contest the early waves because walking up to use Five Point Strike invites an immediate Shield Vault trade that you will always lose. Pantheon will zone you off gold, crashing waves to dive you or roaming with Grand Starfall. Every trade leaves you chunked, forcing early recalls and letting him build a massive turret plating lead while your own map pressure is neutralized.
why: Pantheon completely shuts down your offensive options in this matchup. His point-and-click Shield Vault instantly stuns you before you can react with Twilight Shroud, leaving you exposed to his full combo. Even if you manage to strike back, his Aegis Assault effortlessly absorbs your frontal burst, rendering Five Point Strike and the execution damage of Perfect Execution entirely useless when he faces you.

summary: Ornn can use Bellows Breath to become unstoppable, completely ignoring the knockup from Jarvan's E-Q combo.
howToPlay: Never initiate with Bellows Breath; always hold it as a counter-reaction to the moment he drops his Demacian Standard. If he attempts to trap you with Cataclysm, do not panic. Use the arena walls he creates to trigger your Searing Charge knockup, then follow up immediately with Call of the Forge God to turn his own terrain into a lethal trap. If you misstime your unstoppable window, disengage immediately with Volcanic Rupture to slow his pursuit.
laneImpact: Once Jarvan IV misses or has his flag-and-drag combo neutralized, his massive cooldowns leave him entirely defenseless. You can freely control the wave, forcing him to farm under tower where his Golden Aegis cannot save him from under-tower poke. This massive pressure gap ensures you forge items lane-side via Living Forge while he is forced into terrible recall timings, creating a gold and scaling advantage.
why: This matchup leans heavily in your favor because Jarvan IV relies entirely on his Demacian Standard and Dragon Strike combo to initiate favorable trades. By timing Bellows Breath to gain unstoppable status, you completely negate his knockup. Denied his crowd control, Jarvan IV is left exposed in a prolonged melee trade where your Brittle procs easily out-damage his Martial Cadence as the game goes on.

summary: Jax's Counter Strike completely dodges all piercing bolts from Twitch's Spray and Pray, rendering Twitch's ultimate useless in teamfights.
howToPlay: Your primary goal is to shadow Twitch's position and save Counter Strike specifically for his ultimate. When a fight erupts, do not waste your E early. Use Leap Strike to close the distance once he reveals himself from Ambush. Wait for the distinct sound of Spray and Pray, then immediately activate your dodge. By positioning yourself directly between Twitch and your backline, you absorb and negate his entire ultimate while charging up your stun.
laneImpact: This interaction completely shifts the jungle dynamic in your favor during skirmishes and river fights. Twitch cannot contest objectives or secure crabs if you are nearby, as he cannot safely channel Ambush to escape your sticky pursuit. Any attempt by Twitch to force a gank or a duel backfires because your raw block potential prevents him from getting the burst required to execute you.
why: Jax completely neutralizes Twitch's entire offensive identity in teamfights. When Twitch activates Spray and Pray to pierce through your team, activating Counter Strike allows you to dodge every single one of those long-range bolts. Since Twitch relies entirely on landing these auto-attacks to stack Deadly Venom and detonate Contaminate, your defensive stance completely shuts down his damage output, turning his ultimate into a waste of cooldown.

summary: Swain's Demonic Ascension continues to drain Akali and heal him even while she is hidden inside Twilight Shroud.
howToPlay: Prioritize freezing the wave near your turret to deny him easy targets for Nevermove. If he steps forward to poke, use Shuriken Flip as a mobility tool to dodge sideways rather than committing to a fight. Once Swain triggers Demonic Ascension, immediately disengage using Perfect Execution or Twilight Shroud to run away until his ultimate expires. Only commit to an all-in when his ultimate is down and you have chipped him with short, clean trades.
laneImpact: Swain will constantly shove you under turret using Death's Hand, forcing you to use Five Point Strike defensively just to secure minion gold. If you get caught by Nevermove, he pulls you with Ravenous Flock for a massive health swing. This constant attrition ruins your recall timings, forcing you to choose between losing waves or staying with low health, which completely kills your map pressure.
why: This matchup hinges on a painful interaction: Swain's Demonic Ascension continues to drain your health and heal him even while you are completely hidden inside your Twilight Shroud. Since you cannot drop his aggro with invisibility, your shroud loses its primary defensive value during his ultimate. Combined with his constant healing from Ravenous Flock, you simply cannot burst him down before he out-sustains your energy pool.
